spots.name: Mokdong SBS
spots.desc: One of Korea's leading broadcasters. Located in Mok-dong. The clear glass allows you to watch radio broadcasts in real time. Also can see entertainers coming to work.

spots.name: DMZ
spots.desc: :The Panmunjeom article provides a more specific guide to the 'peace village' in the DMZ that many tourists will visit.

spots.name: Seoul National University
spots.desc: Seoul National University is the uncontested number one university in South Korea. Its main campus is under Gwanak Mountain. Attending Seoul National University is a dream for Korean middle high school students, and admission is extremely competitive. The university offers various campus tour programs like university student's mentor program and campus guide tour. Souvenirs are sold in the…

spots.name: Changdeokgung
spots.desc: Second only to Gyeongbokgung in historical importance, it was built in 1405 and was the seat of power between 1618 and 1896. The buildings have been restored to create a dazzling but still elegant effect that got the palace listed as a . The site is better preserved than Gyeongbokgung. Buildings of particular note include the blue-roofed Seonjeongjeon, which was the King's office, and the…

spots.name: Gyeongbokgung
spots.desc: This is Seoul's grandest Joseon Dynasty-era palace and the seat of power for centuries before it was razed in 1592 by a Japanese invasion (and again by the Japanese in 1910). This was the first palace used by the Joseon Dynasty and was constructed after King Taejo founded the Joseon Dynasty and moved the capital to Hanyang. Large parts have now been restored, and the vast grounds also house the…
spots.hours: Opens at 09:00, closes between 17:00 and 18:30 depending on the season, closed Tuesdays; last admission 1 hour before…

spots.name: Jongmyo Shrine
spots.desc: The royal ancestral temple during the Joseon Dynasty, this is where the kings would perform sacrificial rituals in honor of their ancestors. Certainly, the most famous shrine devoted to the royal family members of Korean dynasties. The grounds are a bit more walker-friendly than some of the palaces, admission is cheaper, and they also have some interactive equipment available to learn about the…
spots.hours: Wed-Mon: Feb-May/Sep-Oct: 09:00-18:00; Jun-Aug: 09:00-18:30; Nov-Jan: 09:00-17:30; closed Tue

spots.name: Panmunjeom
spots.desc: The location of unresolved peace talks. See the Panmunjeom article for details.

spots.name: Yuzu
spots.desc: It is a specialty of Geoje, a citrus fruit with a cultivation history of more than 400 years. Thanks to the mild maritime climate and abundant sunshine, Geoje’s yuzu is known for its rich aroma and well-balanced sweet and sour taste, as well as its high vitamin C content. It is most commonly enjoyed as yuzu tea made with honey or sugar, but is also used in dressings, sauces, jams, candies, and…

spots.name: Seokguram Grotto
spots.desc: A masterpiece of Silla Buddhist art, this grotto houses a majestic granite Buddha looking toward the East Sea. On the solstice, a ray of sun hits the Buddha's "third eye," a design meant to protect the kingdom. Although the Buddha is now behind a glass panel for preservation, the site offers spectacular views on clear days. Photography is strictly prohibited inside due to the sacred nature of the…

spots.name: Geumgang Mountain
spots.desc: It consists of numerous peaks with 40 km east-west, 60 km north-south, and 530 km² in total area, strange rocks and waterfalls caused by long-term geological activities and weathering, and areas covered with coniferous and broad-leaved forests.

spots.name: Hwaseong Fortress
spots.desc: A stunning fortress constructed between 1794 and 1796 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It features four main gates with the north and south (Janganmun and Paldalmun) being particularly impressive with their unique structures. In addition small sentry posts (Porus) and two command posts (Jangdaes) can be found dotted around the walls. The SeoJangdae outpost, found within the forested hills on the…

spots.name: Bulguksa Temple
spots.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage site and a masterpiece of Buddhist art from the 8th century. In front of the main prayer hall stand two iconic stone pagodas: Dabotap (Pagoda of Many Treasures), known for its highly decorative carvings, and Seokgatap (Pagoda of Buddha), admired for its simple and dignified design. Note: Entrance fees have been abolished since May 2023. Look for the "hidden stone pig"…

spots.name: Namdaemun Gate
spots.desc: The Great South Gate is an iconic symbol of Seoul and has been designated as National Treasure Number 1. Particularly beautiful when floodlit at night, and best combined with a visit to the adjacent Namdaemun Market. Much of the structure was destroyed by arson in 2008, although a faithful reconstruction was completed in 2013. Formally known as 'Sungnyemun' (숭례문, 崇禮門). The other city gates can be…

spots.name: National Museum of Korea
spots.hours: For class times, inquire in advance

spots.name: Haeinsa
spots.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage temple housing the Tripitaka Koreana, located in Gayasan National Park. Also, you can enjoy Haeinsa's Temple Stay

spots.name: Lotte World Tower
spots.desc: Enjoy the view from the fifth tallest building in the world. Be sure to check the weather before entry. The Lotte World Tower is a 555.7-metre (1,823 ft), 123-story skyscraper located in Sincheon-dong, Songpa District. It opened to the public in 2017, and is the tallest building in South Korea and the sixth tallest in the world.

spots.name: Namhansanseong Fortress
spots.desc: A mountain fortress city that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The fortress lies atop the mountain Namhansan and stretches 12 km in length. It served as an emergency capital city during the 1392–1910 Joseon period. The design is based on fortress architecture of East Asia, embodying aspects of four historical cultural styles: Joseon of Korea, the Azuchi-Momoyama Period of Japan, and Ming and Qing…
spots.price: Free admission to the fortress; Palace: adult (19-64), ₩2,000, youth (7-18) ₩1,000

spots.name: Korean International Grand Prix Circuit
spots.desc: The annual Formula 1 race used to be held here every year around October in the years 2010-2013. It has been removed from the F1 calendar due to quality of the venue considered too low, however.

spots.name: Replica turtle ship
spots.desc: A full-sized replica of one of Admiral Yi's famed turtle ships. You can have a wander around the inside which is stuffed to the brim with some decidedly seasick looking mannequins acting out their daily routine. Situated just south of Dolsan bridge.

spots.name: Cheonggye Stream
spots.desc: This stream has been restored to a verdant tourist attraction after long being covered by a busy freeway. You can walk many kilometers along its path through the very center of Seoul. Be cautious during the rainy day, because it may be flooded.

spots.name: World Cup Stadium
spots.desc: It was South Korea's main stadium in the 2002 World Cup and is home to FC Seoul.

spots.name: Deoksugung
spots.desc: Deoksu Palace vividly contrasts with the other nearby palaces like Changdeok Palace. Built during the mid-15th century, the architecture of the buildings inside are heavily influenced by Western designs. Hence, you will see a fusion of Korean and Western architecture. The stone-wall narrow way around the palace is a beautiful and famous path for the lovers, although there was a myth that they…
spots.price: Adults (19 to 64 years old): ₩1,000 (groups: ₩800), children (aged 7–18) and soldiers: ₩500 (groups: ₩400), children 6…

spots.name: N Seoul Tower
spots.desc: Once the tallest tower in Asia, it has the best panoramic view in all of Seoul. Many locals and visitors have visited the tower to catch a glimpse of the city’s landscape while enjoying the nature of Namsan Mountain and a host of other attractive facilities. Owing to the tower's unique structure, the observatory section boasts spectacular views of the changing foliage throughout all seasons. The…

spots.name: Suwon World Cup Stadium
spots.desc: Also known as the Big Bird, Suwon's World Cup Stadium hosted one of the quarter-finals for the 2002 FIFA World Cup and is now home to the Suwon Blue Wings of the K-League.

spots.name: Sungkyunkwan Univ
spots.desc: Sungkyunkwan Univ is one of the best University in Korea. Also Sungkyunkwan was traditional school in Joseon Dynasty. So, People who want to see Korea University, It will be good choice to visit here.

spots.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory
spots.desc: The oldest existing observatory in the Far East, built during the reign of Queen Seonduk in 634.

spots.name: POSCO at night
spots.desc: At night POSCO turns the multicolored lights on, and the red-and-white-striped smokestacks turns into a show of all of the colors in the fluorescent rainbow.

spots.name: Ulsan Munsu Football Stadium
spots.desc: If you enjoy visiting random stadiums, then by all means, go to the Ulsan Sports Complex, although it seems like it only made the list because Koreans love soccer. Home to one of South Korea's many soccer teams.Ulsan Munsu Football Stadium’s exterior design looks like a crane, which represents the bird of Ulsan. The design of the roof and the pillars represents the youth and dynamics of the city.…

spots.name: 5-day Gimje market
spots.desc: A traditional market refers to a traditional market in which small merchants gather and sell various goods directly. Starting from regular markets held by people such as the 3-day market and the 5-day market, which have been handed down since the Joseon Dynasty, these days, permanent markets with a coalition structure of small merchants are the mainstream.

spots.name: Daejeon Citizen
spots.desc: The city's K-league soccer team. Daejeon, being a co-host of the 2002 FIFA World Cup, has a soccer stadium in Yuseong-gu on the north side of town (월드컵경기장 World cup kyeonggijang), quite literally and unbelievably plonked in the middle of a farm and now rather rusty in appearance. It's serviced by a dedicated subway station (listen for the old Korean World Cup theme song announcing the stop)…
spots.price: ₩10,000 and under from the team website

spots.name: Hanyang University
spots.desc: A private research university in Seoul and Ansan (ERICA campus). The university was founded in 1939 as an engineering school, and was the country's first college to offer engineering and architecture programs.

spots.name: Baengnyeong Island
spots.desc: It takes four hours to get to Baengnyeong Island. You may get seasick when the wind is strong, and the ship operation is not constant depending on the weather. It is a difficult island to access, but it has such amazing mysteries, scenic views, and many tourist attractions. It is often referred to as the jewel of the West Sea. It is also one of the top 100 tourist destinations in Korea selected…

spots.name: Incheon Munhak Stadium
spots.desc: The complex consists of a main stadium, a baseball stadium (Incheon SK Happy Dream Park), an auxiliary stadium, a swimming pool, a football field, a square, an x-game field, a camping ground, and an artificial rock wall. If you visit the Incheon Munhak Stadium, the home stadium of the SK Wyverns, you can experience the passionate cheering culture of baseball fans. There are many things to eat…

spots.name: Lotte World
spots.desc: This complex has a Lotte Department Store, a theatre which hosts the show Ballerina Who Loves a B-Boy, a Lotte luxury hotel, a large indoor ice skating rick, and a traditional Korean folk museum. However, what it is most famous for is one of the world's largest indoor theme park. Lots of rides. Atlantis rides, especially outdoors, are enough to make you have fun.Though it may seem attractive on a…
spots.price: All-day passes: ₩62,000 for adults, ₩54,000 youth; after 16:00 passes: ₩50,000 for adults, ₩43,000 for youth. For more…

spots.name: Changgyeonggung
spots.desc: It was built in 1104 as a summer palace for the Kings of the Goryeo Dynasty and became one of the main palaces during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace was used as a temporary home for the King during the time Gyeongbuk Palace was being built. Unlike other palaces that have a North-South orientation, Changgyeong Palace faces East-West. Also, this palace is known for connecting to Jongmyo Shrine, a…

spots.name: Sanggyesa temple
spots.desc: This is one of the major temples in Korea. You can take a bus from the Hadong Terminal.Bulil Falls, one of the 10 scenic spots in geography, is located near this temple, and during the cherry blossom season, the so-called Sipri Cherry Blossom Road from Hwagae Market below to Ssanggyesa Temple becomes a national attraction.

spots.name: Seoraksan National Park
spots.desc: Gangwon Province's famous mountain is in the Taebaek Mountains. It spans Sokcho-si, Yangyang-gun, Goseong-gun, and Inje-gun. It is 1,708 m high, the third highest mountain in South Korea after Hallasan Mountain and Jirisan Mountain. Rock rock and Ulsan rock are famous. If you look at the East Sea from Ulsan Rock, you can see the view of Sokcho City and the East Sea.

spots.name: Myeong-dong
spots.desc: Probably the best-known shopping area. It is definitely the most tourist-friendly fashion area. In spring and summer, fashion models/sidewalk promoters can be seen strolling the streets of Myeongdong promoting various cosmetics, stores or other fashion-related products. Many regular people also tend to catwalk their newest outfit on these streets. Rows of stores are available to look for that…

spots.name: Kyung Hee University
spots.desc: A private research university with campuses in Seoul and Suwon. Founded in 1949, it is widely regarded as one of the best universities in South Korea. Kyung Hee University offers comprehensive education from kindergarten through graduate school.

spots.name: Pusan National University
spots.desc: The area around the PNU is very lively. It is full of students, bars, cafes and fashion shops. You can try Korean student food specialties. Note that it retains the old spelling of 'Pusan'.

spots.name: Everland & Caribbean Bay
spots.price: One-day free pass ticket: adult ₩48,000, teenager ₩41,000, child and elderly ₩38,000

spots.name: Hantangang Milky Way Bridge
spots.desc: An asymmetric suspension bridge opened in 2020, stretching 180 meters over the basalt gorge. The center of the bridge features a glass floor for a thrilling view of the river below. It is a popular spot for night photography when the bridge is illuminated.

spots.name: Yangyang Airport
spots.desc: South Korea spent a great deal of money building airports all over the country. Yangyang airport is probably the best example of this, having an infamous reputation of being a fully functional international airport with hardly any flights at all.

spots.name: Gyeonghui-gung
spots.desc: It was built in the 17th century, and was burnt down twice in the 19th century. It was largely destroyed by the Japanese during colonial rule to build a school for Japanese children. It was finally restored in 1985 and opened to the public.

spots.name: Namsan Park
spots.desc: Namsan Park is a large park located in central Seoul, surrounding Namsan Mountain. Visitors can walk along the park's trails, enjoy views of the city, and observe plants and wildlife. The park is a popular place for walking and outdoor activities.

spots.name: Songdo International City
spots.desc: This is a multi-billion-dollar planned city in the Incheon Free Economic Zone has office and residential towers, shops, and hotels. Central Park has a gorgeous lake with boat rides, and deer.

spots.name: Seoraksan National Park
spots.desc: Seoraksan National Park (설악산국립공원), also spelled Soraksan, is a national park in Gangwon, South Korea.

spots.name: Yongpyong (Dragon Valley) Ski Resort
spots.desc: Yongpyong ski resort offers skiing in winter, and golf in the summer months. It is the largest ski and snowboard resort in Korea. The ski season runs from November to early April. It has 31 slopes, 15 different lift facilities, including one gondola at a length of 3.7 km, and Korea's largest ski house (Dragon Plaza). You can enjoy mountain activity called Mountain Coaster.

spots.name: Dongdaemun Gate
spots.desc: More formally known as Heunginjimun (흥인지문, 興仁之門), the old eastern gate of the city still stands. Though not as impressive architecturally as Namdaemun, the Dongdaemun market is infinitely more interesting than its counterpart.

spots.name: 63 Building
spots.desc: This striking building was the tallest outside North America when it opened in 1985 at 250 meters. It has an art gallery and observation deck on level 60 that allows you to see far and wide over the city. As featured in the computer games SimCity 3000 and SimCity 4.

spots.name: MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea)
spots.desc: MMCA is mainly located at the Gwacheon, near the Seoul Grand Park. MMCA Seoul opened in 2013. The site had been the Korean Armed Forces Capital Hospital and the Defense Security Command. MMCA Seoul has an art and culture complex equipped with exhibition and education buildings, a digital lab, a multi-project hall, and a theater. The building is unique and won Grand Prizes at the 2014 Korean…
spots.hours: Mon Tue Thu Fri Sun 10:00-18:00; Wed Sat 10:00-21:00 (18:00-21:00: free), closed on January 1st, Lunar New Year’s Day…
spots.price: ₩4,000. Free for ages under 24 or over 65, college students, and on the last Wednesday of each month

spots.name: Seoul City Wall
spots.desc: Detailed information and trail guidance on the eastern section of Hanyangdoseong and nearby traditional houses can be found on the Seoul Cultural Heritage website and the blog related to the visit to the city.

spots.name: Bukhansan
spots.desc: The highest peak in Seoul, at 836.5 m. Close to the summit, standing above Seoul, is one of the starkest nature/urban divides in the world. These hiking trails are the most visited of the world, with friendly local hikers.

spots.name: Alpensia Resort
spots.desc: Alpensia has six slopes for skiing and snowboarding, with runs up to long, for beginners and advanced skiers, and an area reserved for snowboarders. While the resort is open year-round, the off-season turns the bottom of the slopes into a wild flower garden covering about 100,000 m². All slopes are closed between 16:30-18:30 each day for piste-maintenance. Night skiing is available 18:30-20:00

spots.name: 롯데리아 안산한양대점
spots.desc: 롯데리아 안산한양대점 (Lotteria Ansan Hanyang University), 379 Gwangdeok 1-ro, Sangnok-gu, +82 31-501-7474. Daily 09:00-23:00. Korean fast-food restaurant serving burgers, fries, chicken and other quick meals. It is located near Hanyang University ERICA and is a convenient option for students looking for a quick meal. KakaoTalk Channel：롯데리아 공식 KakaoTalk 채널⁠

spots.name: Loveland
spots.desc: Jeju's most eccentric and internationally infamous attraction and almost a reason in itself to visit Jeju, this bizarre sculpture park was created by graduates of Seoul's Hongik University. Few of the more than 140 exhibits are generally shocking, and it makes for some interesting holiday snaps that you won't want to show your parents. Although you will likely see some Korean families in the…

spots.name: National Museum of Gyeongju
spots.desc: A museum with four exhibition buildings, it contains treasures such as the golden crown of Geumgwanchong, the pottery piece Gimainmulhyeongtogi (a mounted soldier from the kingdom of Gaya), King Michu's golden sword.

spots.name: Myeong-Dong Cathedral
spots.desc: Designed by a Coste priest, and build with financial support from the Paris Church Department, this was the house of Bum-Woo Kim and purchased by Marie Jean Gustave Blanc (under the Korean name Gamilro Kim). With a successful trade agreement in 1887, the cathedral was finally built in 1898. This building was the first church built with bricks. The height of the building proper is 23 m, but with…

spots.name: University of Seoul
spots.desc: A municipal public university that is famous in South Korea for a very large number of alumni working as national or municipal government officials. UOS is specialized in urban science and has top-tier programs environmental engineering, taxation, transportation engineering, urban planning and design, landscape architecture, and urban administration.

spots.name: Namsadang Baudeogi Festival
spots.desc: Namsadang Baudeogi Festival is one of the representative cultural festivals in Korea held in the fall in Anseong, and is a representative festival in Gyeonggi-do. The festival is usually held in October. It has been designated as an official festival of CIOFF by UNESCO's official advisory cooperation organization since 2006.

spots.name: Beomeosa Temple
spots.desc: One of Korea's great temples, this large complex is located up in the mountains and feels further away from the city than the few kilometers that it really is. The buildings have been destroyed and rebuilt many times since they were founded back in 678, yet they are still atmospheric. The temple does get packed with worshippers, hikers and tourists on weekends. The road from the metro station to…

spots.name: United Nations Memorial Cemetery
spots.desc: The only official United Nations cemetery in the world, it serves to honor the memory of soldiers from 16 nations who fought and died for the freedom of South Korea. This location is very far away from the DMZ on the south coast of the nation.
spots.addr: 93, UNpyeonghwa-ro, Nam-gu, Busan 부산광역시 남구 유엔평화로 93

spots.name: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond
spots.desc: The artificial Anapji pond was created by King Munmu in 674. The pavilions on its banks were destroyed by fire and fell into the pond in 935. Archeological finds from the pond can be seen in the National Museum today. The pond is covered from late July to early August with blooming lotus flowers. In the middle stands a pavilion, which can be reached via steps. This place is popular with wedding…

spots.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
spots.desc: is one of the most famous tourist attractions in Jeju Island and is a good place to climb. It also gives a similar feeling to Hallasan Baeknokdam. It lies at the end of Seongsan Peninsula, which protrudes to the east of Jeju. Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak is a water-based volcano created by magma erupting from the water, unlike other oreum on Jeju Island. As the hot magma emitted during volcanic…

spots.name: Hallasan National Park
spots.desc: Hallasan National Park is on Jeju island to the south of the South Korean mainland. Hallasan (한라산 / 漢拏山) is the highest mountain in South Korea, standing at 1,950 meters (6,400 ft).

spots.name: Seodaemun Prison
spots.desc: The prison was built in 1908, and became infamous during the Japanese occupation when it was used to torture, starve and execute Korean political prisoners. Actual prison cells, wax figures and videos are used to demonstrate the shocking brutality experienced there. Most signs are in Korean although volunteer guides can describe the sights in English. The content may not be suitable for those of…

spots.name: Hwangnyongsa
spots.desc: Located east of downtown, these temple ruins of 66,0002 are among the largest in Asia. In 553 King Jinheung planned to build a palace here, however as he heard rumors that a yellow dragon had been seen there, he decided to make a temple here. It was completed in 645. The most important things here were a nine-level wooden pagoda and a golden five meter high statue of Jangnyuksang. The temple was…
spots.hours: 09:00 to 18:00 (11:00-19:00 on weekends/public holidays during peak April-October)

spots.name: Gwanghwamun Plaza
spots.desc: A center of Seoul. The name came from the main gate of the Gyeongbokgung. The site was a location of the Six Ministries during the Joseon dynasty and was a large motorway since then. In 2009, the middle of the road was opened to the public as a renovation project. It's now home to festivals and events. There are two statues in the plaza: Admiral Yi Sun-sin (a legendary admiral who won numerous…

spots.name: Olympic Park
spots.desc: Built for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Seoul Olympics. A lake, a large field covered with the grass, and a square with sculptures are very popular among visitors. It is frequently visited by brides and grooms to take their wedding pictures. There are a couple of courses that are ideal for jogging or walking. In addition, the outdoor stage and the six stadiums are often used for concerts and…

spots.name: Haeundae Beach
spots.desc: One of the most popular summer destinations in South Korea. Haeundae beach attracts tourists from all around the country and gets really overcrowded in late July and early August. Deck chairs and parasols are available to rent for ₩10,000. Hotels including international chains are nearby, and the Busan Aquarium is on the beach front. On a clear day, Tsushima Island (Japan) can be seen. In winter…

spots.name: Jirisan National Park
spots.desc: Jirisan National Park (지리산국립공원) is in South Gyeongsang, South Korea.

spots.name: Gocheok Sky Dome
spots.desc: South Korea's first domed baseball stadium and the home stadium of the Kiwoom Heroes. It also hosts concerts, awards ceremonies, and other large-scale events. Public transportation is recommended because traffic and parking can be crowded on event days.

spots.name: Daejeon Station
spots.desc: A walk around the alleyways straight across from the station will offer Ginseng (인삼 insam) and traditional medicine stores. Across the street from the market, see the Buy section of this article.

spots.name: Gwangju Biennale & Design Biennale
spots.desc: Gwangju Biennale is one of the famed art exhibitions in the world. The city celebrates art every second year with international pieces on varying themes. The exhibition runs in even-numbered years. The sister festival to this is the Gwangju Design Festival which runs in odd numbered years and focuses on interior and exterior design elements. Even if you are not interested in the arts, you may be…

spots.name: Hanwha Eagles
spots.desc: The city's professional baseball team. Baseball games are held at the baseball field of Hanbat Sports Complex ex (한밭 운동장 Hanbat undongjang). Express bus #2 passes by it, or it can be walked within 15-20 min from Jungangno station. Various teams play including the local professional team and those of the local universities sometimes on Friday nights. Despite tickets being rather inexpensive, many…

spots.name: E-Mart
spots.desc: e-mart (Hangul: 이마트) is the largest retailer in South Korea. E-mart offers everything from food to clothes to diapers, and provides a very large variety of merchandise.

spots.name: Chungjuho
spots.desc: Chungjuho has the largest multipurpose dam in South Korea which holds the largest body of fresh water, linking Chungju, Jecheon, and Danyang in Chungcheongbuk do. There are Mt. Wolaksan National Park, Mt. Geumsusan, Gudambong Peak, etc. around the lake, so you can enjoy the beauty of nature harmonizing with the blue water. They run a tourist ship from Chungju to Sin Danyang (53km).

spots.name: Tongdosa Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple stay and museum. One of seven Korean mountain monasteries inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018.
spots.addr: 108, Tongdosa-ro, Habuk-myeon, Yangsan-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Republic of Korea

spots.name: Mt. Gaya
spots.desc: Mt. Gaya, at the southwest border of Seongju, is designated as a national park. The main peak is Chilbulbong (1,433 m) and with Udubong, Namsan, Danjibong, Namsan 1-bong, Maehwasan etc, which are around 1,000 m in height, Mt. Gaya is renowned for its outstanding scenery and diverse ridgelines. Follow the Circular Road from Suryun-myeon to Mt. Gaya, and you’ll be able to find dark-red cliffs…

spots.name: Ansan Sihwaho Tidal Power Plant
spots.desc: A tidal power plant that is located in Ansan, and the largest tidal power plant in the world.

spots.name: Silmi Island
spots.desc: This island is accessible from Muuido at low tide. It is an uninhabited island with a number of small beaches.

spots.name: Beopjusa Temple
spots.desc: Constructed in 553, is a head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism on the slopes of Songnisan. Visitors can spend time here in a temple stay. The temple is one out of 7 to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018.
spots.addr: 405 Beopjusa-ro Boeun-gun, 충청북도 보은군 속리사면 법주사로 405

spots.name: Dorasan Korail Station
spots.desc: Just outside of the DMZ near Paju is a fully operational rail station connected to the South Korean and North Korean rail network. No train to North Korea has run since 2008: it is completely symbolic as the former tourist trains from Seoul were terminated in 2023. However, it is intended to be a connection between the capital cities of Seoul and Pyongyang.

spots.name: Third Infiltration Tunnel
spots.desc: A tunnel that was secretly dug by the North Koreans into South Korean territory; there are suspicions that there are others. The tunnels are an interesting visit but if you are tall, they will be extremely uncomfortable to walk along the full distance allowed.

spots.name: Yeongjong island
spots.desc: It is the place where Incheon International Airport is and Eulwangri Beach is famous. There are also historic mountains and temples. An island with an area of 125.7 km² in Jung-gu, Incheon. It is South Korea's sixth-largest island and is home to a large-scale reclamation project to build Incheon International Airport. Half of the island's total area is the site of Incheon International Airport.…

spots.name: Bangudae
spots.desc: Petroglyphs of Bangudae Terrace in Daegok-ri, Ulju-gun are estimated to have been drawn over several periods since the New Stone Age so you can discover the differences in styles among various ages. Primary objects that were popularly carved include sea animals, land animals, humans and tools and, as our prehistoric ancestors actively engaged in hunting, the hope of abundance in game is believed…

spots.name: Korean Folk Village
spots.desc: A massive living museum showcasing traditional Joseon-era Korean culture. Features relocated historic houses from across the peninsula, daily traditional performances, folk games, and seasonal festivals. Accessible via feeder buses from Giheung or Suwon Station.

spots.name: National War Memorial
spots.desc: A museum about Korean military history and the Korean War. It starts with the ancient and Middle Ages, explaining the wars at that time and showing the weaponry of the time. Then the second-floor deals with the Korean War, both focusing on the Korean and UN forces. Outside of the memorial, there are several fighter, bomber, and trainer aircraft displayed that were used during the Korean War.

spots.name: Mireuksa Temple Site
spots.desc: This UNESCO Heritage Site was the largest Buddhist temple in Baekje, and was established in 6th century by King Mu of the Baekje. The temple is believed to be destroyed during the late Joseon Dynasty, but west and east pagoda and cornerstones still exist. West pagoda is the largest stone pagoda in East Asia, and shows the transition of materials from wood to stone. Pagoda was very unstable even…

spots.name: Yonggungsa Temple
spots.desc: This remarkable Buddhist temple complex is situated on top of a large rock along the ocean. Since most Korean temples are in the mountains this is an unusual location with sweeping ocean views. You need to walk through a market from the car park to the complex itself.

spots.name: Gwangan Grand Bridge
spots.desc: Driving (or taking the bus) across Gwangan Bridge is a great way to see the view, especially at nighttime. Viewed from the town it has an impressive light display at night. It featured in the Marvel movie 'Black Panther'.

spots.name: Gwanaksan
spots.desc: Gwanaksan (Korean for Mt. Gwanak; 632 m) is a small mountain in southern Seoul, South Korea. Portions lie in the Gwanak-gu and Geumcheon-gu districts of Seoul; other portions lie in the neighboring cities of Anyang and Gwacheon.

spots.name: National Memorial cemetery
spots.desc: National Memorial Cemetery is reserved for Korean veterans, including those who died in the Korean independence movement, Korean War, and Vietnam War. Four South Korean presidents are buried in the cemetery. It is not only opened for mourners. Anyone can enter the Cemetery. There are large park that you can play even badminton. Especially, in the Spring, the flowers are awesome
spots.addr: Seoul National Memorial Board 210, Hyeonchung-ro, Dingjak-gu

spots.name: Bongeunsa
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple with a long history that was once located on the rural outskirts of Seoul. The surrounding area was transformed during the rapid development of Gangnam from the 1980s, and the temple is now surrounded by high-rise buildings and commercial districts. The grounds contain several Buddhist buildings and sculptures.

spots.name: Bunhwangsa Temple
spots.desc: The only pagoda built during the reign of Queen Seondeok from 634 remains in this temple. It is thus Korea's oldest pagoda and a special feature is that it was built with bricks. Originally it had nine levels, but today only three remain. There are also a few stone figures.

spots.name: Gyeongju National Park
spots.desc: Either take a bus or taxi to get to the park. Once there, hiking trails lead up into the mountains. At first the signs are in both Korean and English but soon they become Korean only. Make sure you take a map or even better a Korean!

spots.name: Magoksa Temple
spots.desc: Magoksa is a head temple of the Jogye Order located on the eastern slope of Taehwasan in Gongju. The temple was first established in 640 by the Vinaya Master Jajang. Its compounds are uniquely divided by a stream running through them, with a northern worship area and a southern meditation zone. Among its notable features are a five-story stone pagoda with a bronze-tipped top and several halls…

spots.name: Jogyesa Temple
spots.desc: The chief temple of the Jogye order of Buddhism, the dominant branch of Buddhism in Korea. As such, it is one of the most important modern Buddhist temples in the country. That being said, Jogyesa Temple is rather small, and if time permits, Bongeunsa in Gangnam is a larger and more interesting Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Seoul City Hall
spots.desc: The old city hall was built under Japanese rule and it was renovated to a public library. In back of the old hall, the huge new city hall was built. In the basement, there is Citizen Hall, where musical performances and exhibitions are held for citizens. City Hall Square, in front of the hall, is open to public and political demonstrations. Every winter, Ice rink opens at the Square.

spots.name: Daebu Island
spots.desc: Daebudo is also known as 'the Hawaii of Ansan.' Daebudo is connected to the Sihwa seawalls, so it has become a land of Ansan. However, it still has the romance and lyricism of an island in various places.

spots.name: Mui island
spots.desc: The scenery of the island where you climb the mountains that stretch across Mui Island is lush and beautiful. You can feel the mood of Mui island through water play at Silmi Beach (Silmi island). The sand is fine and the water is clean. Unlike the Sea of Japan, the slope is gentle, making it ideal for families to play. There are bungalows suitable for summer vacations, many foreigners visit.

spots.name: COEX
spots.desc: This state-of-the-art complex combines a massive underground mall, luxury hotels, office towers, convention center, and international trade center. Parts of the mall have aged considerably since its debut, but it still features mid-to-upscale shopping, entertainment, and Korean and Western food options. Popular attractions here include Starfield Library with its towering bookshelves in central…

spots.name: Seoul Art Center
spots.desc: 700 Seocho-dong, Gangnam-gu, (line 3 Nambu Bus Terminal stn). This arts complex contains multiple performing arts and museum exhibition spaces, showcasing Korean traditional art as well as modern works.

spots.name: Manjanggul Cave
spots.desc: Manjanggul Cave is a famous lava tube and a UNESCO-listed world natural heritage site. There are numerous lava caves all over the world, but it is said that it is difficult to find a place like Manjanggul Cave that has well-preserved shape and topography even though it is hundreds of thousands of years old. The interior, which looks like an underground palace, has a magnificent and profound…

spots.name: Oedo Island
spots.desc: Typically included in cruises to Haegumgang, this is Korea's first privately owned island and host to the Oedo Botanica. It's somewhat of a cross between a botanical garden and one of East Asia's infamous "country-themed theme parks" and designed to make you think you're somewhere in the Mediterranean. Beautifully landscaped and covered with Greco-Roman statues. It's a bit prettier than the…

spots.name: Museum Kimchikan
spots.desc: A museum (previously known as Kimchi Field Museum) about all things kimchi. Includes a lot of interactive exhibits and comes with a free audio guide in English. There are also hands-on kimchi-making programs, only on reservation, however.

spots.name: Tapgol ("Pagoda") Park
spots.desc: A small park frequented by the elderly and the footsore traveler, just to the east of Jongmyo Shrine. Contains a 500-year-old namesake pagoda under protective glass and a nice large gazebo to get out of the sun. This is where the Korean constitution was first read aloud by the public during the 20th century. Acts as a navigation landmark when moving between Myeong-dong, Jong-no, and Insa-dong…

spots.name: Namdaemun Market
spots.desc: The largest traditional street market in Korea. This market is in the center of Seoul and is a famous shopping place for tourists. Clothing for children and accessories are the most-commonly sold goods in this market, but there's lots of food as well and many outdoor eating options, especially in the evening. There is also a huge digital camera market in this area.

spots.name: Yeungnam University Love Road
spots.desc: Yeungnam University’s “Love Road” is a scenic 700-m tree‑lined walkway on the campus in Gyeongsan, famous for its cherry blossoms each spring. It’s often described as a romantic space where the name “Love Road” reflects the path’s symbolic association with youthful affection. The cherry-blossom tunnel transforms the road every spring, creating one of the most romantic and photogenic spots in the…

spots.name: Statue of Peace
spots.desc: A Statue of peace was made to solve the problem of Japanese military sexual slavery victims. It has held regular protests every Wednesday since 1992 and Statue of Peace was first built in front of the Japanese Embassy in central Seoul on Dec. 14, 2011, the 1,000th anniversary of the demand rally. There are 129 statues in the country and several in other countries. The statue in Cheonan is one of…

spots.name: Juwangsan National Park
spots.desc: It is famous for its dramatic scenery featuring towering limestone rock cliffs and deep, picturesque gorges carved by water. Despite being one of South Korea's smaller national parks, it boasts breathtaking views, particularly along the valley trails that lead to several beautiful waterfalls. The park is also home to historical sites like Daejeonsa Temple and is particularly popular in Autumn…

spots.name: Gwangalli Beach
spots.desc: Best experienced at night when the impressive Gwangan Grand Bridge is illuminated. The area is similar to Haeundae but smaller and less upscale. There are plenty of local restaurants, bars and shops in the area. In summer the crowds are slightly less than in Haeundae Beach. This is also the premier location for new year's ever firework/drone shows.

spots.name: Dobongsan
spots.desc: This is a stone mountain. Many professional hikers visit the mountain and it is quite famous among the mountains of Korea.

spots.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
spots.desc: This is possibly Korea's most famous fish market with a large selection of seafood there. You will have to opportunity to eat squid that is still wriggling when you eat it! Try to come very early to see the activity around the fish being landed. It is walking distance from the Nampo Lotte Department store or the Jagalchi station on the Busan Metro Line 1.

spots.name: Sea Life COEX, Seoul Aquarium
spots.desc: There are various kinds of living things and indoor aquariums that are good to come with family or lovers

spots.name: Jeondong Cathedral
spots.desc: This mix of Romanesque and Byzantine style cathedral was constructed in 1914, and is in the same place where many Christians were martyred.

spots.name: Daecheong Dam
spots.desc: The observation deck of Daecheong Dam is located in Sangdang-gu, Cheongju-si, North Chungcheong Province. When you climb to the observation deck, you can see clear Daecheong Lake, and when you enter the water promotion center, there is a video facility where you can see data on water and the construction of the dam and various financial resources, which serves as a learning center for water…
spots.addr: Hyeonamjeong Rest Area, 206 Daecheong Hoban-ro, Munmun-myeon, Sangdang-gu

spots.name: Seoul Grand Park
spots.desc: A large park complex at the foot of Cheonggyesan, with Seoul Zoo, a botanical garden, a theme garden and walking routes. The surrounding area also includes Seoul Land, MMCA Gwacheon and a campsite. Allow several hours for the zoo alone. The lakeside walking route is an alternative to the ticketed attractions.
spots.hours: Zoo and Theme Garden: Mar–Apr and Sep–Oct 09:00–18:00; May–Aug 09:00–19:00; Nov–Feb 09:00–17:00. Last admission one…
spots.price: Zoo: adults ₩5,000, teenagers ₩3,000, children ₩2,000. Theme Garden and transport cost extra

spots.name: Unhyeongung
spots.desc: A museum in the former palace of a Joseon Dynasty archduke Heungseon, who was the father of the second last king of Joseon. It has several mannequins depicting the costumes of the yangban or noble class during the Joseon Dynasty. The palace buildings themselves represent the style of the Joseon noble class' mansion well.

spots.name: Seoul Museum of History
spots.desc: Seoul has been the capital of Korea since 1392, and this museum focuses on its history during Joseon Dynasty, the Japanese annexation period, and modern development.

spots.name: Busan Cinema Center
spots.desc: The Busan International Film Festival has had this impressive open cinema built for the October 2011 festival. Go at night time to appreciate the light show displayed on the ceiling. To get there take the subway/bus to Centum City. The building is behind Shinsigae Centum City.

spots.name: Tancheon Stadium
spots.desc: Seongnam City has its own local football team, Seongnam FC. It won the league seven times, and has enthusiastic fans. At this stadium, you can see the team's play.

spots.name: Seomjin River
spots.desc: Seomjin Cheongryu. To be exact, the Seomjin River, which means this tourist attraction, means the Seomjin River overlooking Jirisan. Or, paradoxically, it also means the Seomjin River, which flows with Jirisan as the background seen around the Seomjin River. In the local area, this attraction is called Seomjin Cheongryu (blue flowing Seomjin). Since the Seomjin River flows through Gurye-gun in…

spots.name: Hwaeomsa temple
spots.desc: This is the of the bus leaving from Gurye. Use it to explain your destination to reach the national park. This temple built in AD 544. It is located at the southwest foot of Nogodan. There is a hiking course that goes through this place. It is also a traditional temple with many national treasures of Korea and the largest temple in Jirisan. You can see beautiful temples and red plum blossoms.…

spots.name: Odaesan National Park
spots.desc: Odaesan National Park (오대산국립공원, 五臺山國立公園) is in the Pyeongchang county of Gangwon province in South Korea.

spots.name: Seoul Forest
spots.desc: Seoul's own Central Park, at the northern bank of Han. It's composed of five smaller parks, the culture & art park, the natural ecology forest, the natural hands-on experience learning garden, the ecological wetland garden and the Han river waterfront park as well as an outdoor stage and a big playground.

spots.name: Dongdaemun
spots.desc: An enormous fashion shopping district with 24 large department store-like buildings such as Doota, Migliore, and APM, each with 2-17 stories of trendy shops and stalls grouped together so customers can shop efficiently and save time. This market is of equal historical significance to Namdaemun market, with the obvious difference being Dongdaemun's modernity. Historically, Dongdaemun was a…

spots.name: Hyperion Towers
spots.desc: Three residential skyscrapers. Tower A, the tallest of them, is with 256 meters the second tallest building in Seoul. The bottom floors are made up of the Hyundai department store.

spots.name: Korean National Assembly Building
spots.desc: The seat of the South Korean government and a work of contemporary architecture.

spots.name: The Daejeon Museum of Art
spots.desc: An art museum established in 1998 and focused on the convergence of art and technology. Numerous exhibitions on contemporary art have been held here.

spots.name: Home Plus
spots.desc: Homeplus (Hangul: 홈플러스) is a Korean discount store retail chain. It is the second largest retailer in South Korea.

spots.name: Ho-Am Art Museum
spots.desc: A private art museum established by Samsung group founder Lee Byung-chull. Displays traditional Korean art alongside modern exhibitions. The surrounding traditional Korean garden, 'Heewon', is renowned for its cherry blossoms and autumn foliage.

spots.name: Gongju National Museum
spots.desc: Museum housing many of the actual artefacts recovered from King Muryeong's tomb. The treasures are unusual in that they are primarily metalcrafts, including pottery, swords, jewelry crafted from gold, silver and burnt-wood and some excruciatingly uncomfortable looking pairs of bronze shoes. Upstairs a second exhibit focuses on the ancient culture of South Chungcheong Province.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat Sun holidays 09:00-19:00 with some extended Sat hours during vacation periods
spots.price: Admission requires a ticket, but tickets are free

spots.name: Gyeryongsan National Park
spots.desc: This park takes up the far south-eastern portion of Gongju-si. Access to the extensive hiking trails is most convenient via Kap-sa Temple or Shinwon-sa Hermitage. Donghak-sa Temple on the east side of the range also provides access but requires a commute around the entire national park unless coming from Daejeon.

spots.name: Jinju National Museum
spots.desc: At the west end of the fortress. A small but well-presented branch of the National Museum specializing in the Imjin War. The museum also has a large collection of materials on exchanges between South Korea and Japan. Labeling in English is a little spotty but mostly sufficient. An interesting (if rather propagandistic) 3D film on the First Battle of Jinju is shown hourly for free.

spots.name: Musical Fountain
spots.desc: This fountain is a must-see for any visitor to Jinju. An impressive water and light show is put on by the fountain in time to a selection of songs ranging from classical to popular music. Shows are at regular intervals beginning after dark (exact times depend on the season). This is a popular gathering place for couples and families in the summer.

spots.name: Buram Mountain
spots.desc: It is a relatively low mountain about 400 meters above sea level, and there are trails and hiking trails that even beginners can climb without difficulty.

spots.name: Sukjeongmun Gate
spots.addr: San 25-22, Samcheong-dong 서울 성북구 성북동 산 25-22

spots.name: Peace Dam
spots.desc: known as Hwacheon Dam, is a large dam, completed in 2005. Bimokpark and Mulmunhall are to the left of the power plant entrance. Mulmunhall promotes the importance of water resources and has been operating a restaurant and other facilities. Biompark promotes the natural environment.
spots.addr: 145-145, Bisugumi-gil, Hwacheon-eup, Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province, South Korea

spots.name: Buyeo National Museum
spots.desc: The Buyeo National Museum preserves the heritage of the Baekje Kingdom during its Sabi-era capital (538–660). The collection includes over 13,000 artifacts excavated in the region, such as pottery, gilt-bronze statues, stone pagodas, and everyday objects. The most prestigious artifact in this museum is the Gilt-bronze Incense Burner from the Baekje Kingdom, found in 1993. It is credited as one of…
spots.hours: Nov-Mar: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat Sun 09:00-19:00; Apr-Oct: Sat Sun 09:00-21:00

spots.name: Dongbaek Island (Dongbaekseom)
spots.desc: Dongbaekseom is not a real island, but a forested area with Camellia and pine trees past the Westin hotel. It offers a pleasant and short coastal walk, and the APEC Conference Center (with great views of the Gwangali area in Busan) can be visited here as well.
spots.addr: Haeundae Beach, next to Westin Hotel

spots.name: Namhae Bridge
spots.desc: You will most likely cross this bridge when traveling to the island. The red, suspension bridge is beautiful in itself, but also offers great view of the surrounding landscape.

spots.name: Woljeongsa Temple
spots.desc: A head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, was founded in 643 by the Silla monk Jajang and located on the eastern slopes of Odaesan mountain.

spots.name: Mount Gwanggyo
spots.desc: Gwanggyosan is a 582-m mountain on the border of Suwon and Yongin in Gyeonggi Province, South Korea. It is part of a larger range touching Uiwang, Gwacheon, Seongnam, offering gentle ridges covered in forest, ideal for hiking and nature walks.

spots.name: Noryangjin Fish Market
spots.desc: The floors may be dank and wet, but this is undoubtedly the freshest seafood in Seoul, with live octopuses, spiky sea urchins, giant king crabs swimming about in water tanks, buckets and bags. Buy some fresh fish (try bargaining if you can), and head to the restaurants in the back row, where they'll prepare your food as requested. There's a wholesale auction at 02:00, where fishmongers bid for…

spots.name: Songnisan National Park
spots.desc: Songnisan National Park (속리산국립공원, /soŋɾisankukɾipkoŋwʌn/) is in the landlocked province of North Chungcheong in South Korea.

spots.name: Gamcheon Cultural Village
spots.desc: Gamcheon village was a Korean war refugee camp, and backwater outside of the city center. In 2008 it attracted the attention of local university students who began painting murals throughout the village as part of their social service activities. Today it has become a cultural center with photography and graffiti galleries, small museums, cafés and restaurants.

spots.name: Korea International Exhibition Center
spots.desc: The country's largest exhibition center, with 10 main exhibition halls and many conference rooms. There are also several restaurants and cafes.

spots.name: Incheon Munhak Stadium
spots.desc: Munhak Stadium consists of a main stadium, a baseball field, an auxiliary stadium, a swimming pool, a football stadium, a square, an x-game field, a camping ground and an artificial rock wall. Incheon. The closest station is Munhak Stadium on Incheon Subway Line No. 1, named after the stadium.

spots.name: Wolseong
spots.desc: This was a palace of the Silla kingdom, and is today a lovely park with some ruins. It contains the 'Seokbinggo' or 'Stone Ice House' built in 1738 for the preservation of food. It looks something like a grave mound (of which there are many in the area).

spots.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
spots.desc: This traditional village is home to around 700 hanok buildings, making it the largest traditional hanok village in Korea. Most of the Hanok were constructed in Joseon period (1392-1910). Here you can experience a variety of traditional Korean culture such as making traditional Korean paper (Hanji) or trying Korean liquor.

spots.name: National Science Museum
spots.desc: Showcases both permanent and special exhibitions.It also features free outdoor exhibits of aircraft and rockets, plus an astronomical observatory offering public viewing on weekends by prior reservation.
spots.price: ₩1,000 for exhibitions and another ₩1,000 for planetarium; half price for under-20s

spots.name: Gwangju National Museum
spots.desc: Built in the traditional Korean style, Gwangju National Museum includes exhibition halls and storage space for artifacts, as well as a garden that serves as a venue for outdoor exhibitions. On display are prehistoric remains from the surrounding Honam region; Buddhist art, pottery and ceramics from the Baekje Kingdom, Unified Silla Kingdom, and the Goryeo and Joseon periods; and undersea remains…

spots.name: OK Financial Group Okman
spots.desc: A professional volleyball team that plays in the Korea Volleyball Federation (KOVO). Their home arena is Sangnoksu Gymnasium. They were known as OK Savings Bank Rush & Cash until 2020. You can buy tickets by online (the website is in Korean only) or ticket box on site.

spots.name: Chiak Mountain
spots.desc: Chiaksan Mountain, which extends north and south around Birobong Peak at 1,288 m above sea level, has 1,000 m of high peaks, including Namdaebong Peak (1,181 m) and Maehwasan Mountain (1,085 m), and steep valleys and mountains (Guryongsa Temple, Sangwonsa Temple, Seokgyeongsa Temple, Gukgyeongsa Temple, Ipseoksa Temple) and historical sites are scattered everywhere.

spots.name: Sanbang Mountain
spots.desc: A remarkable dome-shaped mountain surrounded by green and yellow fields. Visit the temples on the mountain for incredible views of the surrounding countryside and beaches. Shops nearby.

spots.name: Gimhae National Museum
spots.desc: Historical exhibits about the ancient Gaya kingdom. Gimhae, which was the capital of Geumgwan Gaya, the leading Gaya Confederation, is displayed mainly in Gaya relics. The museum offers a permanent exhibition hall, a special exhibition hall, and an outdoor display area. It is an excellent place to learn about the history of the Gaya Confederacy and the ancient culture of the Gimhae region.

spots.name: Anyang University
spots.desc: a four-year comprehensive private university.

spots.name: Seoul Land
spots.desc: An amusement park with rides and family attractions. Check the operating calendar before planning an evening visit and the restrictions for individual rides when travelling with children.
spots.hours: Varies by date; check the daily calendar

spots.name: Bank of Korea Money Museum
spots.desc: You can find out about 20,000 rare domestic and foreign currencies held by the Bank of Korea and the money manufacturing process and the country's economic process.

spots.name: Leeum Museum of Art
spots.desc: The Leeum Museum of Art, located in Yongsan, Seoul, is a renowned museum showcasing both traditional Korean art and contemporary works, offering a unique cultural experience for visitors.

spots.name: Yongsan Electronics Market
spots.desc: Yongsan Station is in IMall which is another huge shopping mall with two storeys full of electronics. Without negotiating you can have cheaper prices than amazon.com. Yongsan is one option in Seoul if you are looking for electronics goods. Made up of over 20 buildings housing 5,000 stores, you can find appliances, stereos, computers and peripherals, office equipment, telephones, lighting…

spots.name: Byeonsan-Bando National Park
spots.desc: Byeonsanbando National Park is located in Buan-gun, Jeollabuk-do, and is the only peninsula-shaped national park in Korea that harmonizes both mountains and sea. It is divided into Naebyeonsan and Oebyeonsan. It is particularly famous for its beautiful sunset over the West Sea.

spots.name: Jeongnimsaji Temple and Museum
spots.desc: A complex with the ruins of the lotus pond, Buddha statue and a 1,500 years old five-storied pagoda, with a museum on-site showing some of the history of the Baekje Dynasty in Buyeo. There is an impressive 65% scale model of the temple grounds surrounded by a gate and perimeter walls, located inside the museum. It appears that they are undergoing excavation of the site, and possibly rebuilding…

spots.name: Hwangmaesan
spots.desc: It is a beautiful place to be called Geumgangsan Mountain because it is formed of rocky cliffs in the southeast, including Hwangmaebong Peak, which is located nearby. When you climb to the top, the surrounding scenery resembles the shape of plum petals, giving you a mysterious feeling as if floating alone in plum blossoms. In particular, the beautiful bright red azalea flowers on a plateau of…

spots.name: Daeheungsa
spots.desc: A Buddhist monastery on Mt Duryunsan, believed to be founded in 514 CE, during the time of the Baekje nation, by the monk Adohwasang. One of the main temples of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, it was one of seven to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018. Today, it can be reached by a hike through some of the oldest forests in the country. It features a central courtyard, a…

spots.name: KBS Hall
spots.desc: Home of KBS Philharmonic Orchestra and KBS Traditional Music Orchestra.

spots.name: Taejongdae Park
spots.desc: Named after King Taejong Muyul (654-661) of the Silla Dynasty who practiced archery here after unifying the Three Kingdoms. During the Joseon period, King Taejong (1400-1418) is reputed to have visited here for recreation and pleasure. The magistrate of Dongnae also came here during a major drought to offer prayers for rain. Taejongdae is a famous tourist attraction in Busan, with its white…

spots.name: Horim museum
spots.desc: The Horim Museum was opened in Daechi-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, based on the relics and funds presented by Horim Yoon Jang-seop. Then, in March 1996, the museum was expanded and built in Sillim-dong, Gwanak-gu, Seoul, and reopened in May 1999. There are more than 15,000 relics, 60 of which are designated as national cultural assets (8 national treasures and 52 treasures). It is recognized for its…

spots.name: Noryangjin
spots.desc: Plenty of stalls selling fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, squid, clams, and other seafood straight from the farm/trawler. Not exactly tourist-friendly, this market is definitely targeted towards a local audience, but if you're interested in seeing an off-the-beaten-track destination and really exploring the nitty-gritty of Korean daily life, definitely worth a look.

spots.name: Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs
spots.desc: Tranquil park in the middle of Gangnam with the burial mounds of two kings and a queen from the Joseon dynasty.

spots.name: Suwon KT Wiz Park
spots.desc: Home stadium of the Korean professional baseball team KT WIZ. The park functions as a venue for baseball games and as a complex cultural space for entertainment, leisure, and educational activities.

spots.name: Jeju National Museum
spots.desc: A history museum of Jeju Island’s historical and cultural assets. It houses various remains excavated from ruins, including meaningful relics from the prehistoric age through to the Joseon dynasty.

spots.name: Samseonghyeol
spots.desc: A revered site featuring three mythical holes, believed to be the origin of Jeju island's mythical founders.

spots.name: Golgulsa Temple
spots.desc: 20 km east of the ancient Silla Dynasty capital city of Gyeongju in Southeastern Korea. In the Golgulsa temple area can be found the oldest historical Buddhist ruins on Mt. Hamwol and the only cave temple in Korea. The original temple was built out of solid rock during the 6th century by Saint Kwang Yoo and his companions, Buddhist monks from India. This temple contains a sculptured Maya…

spots.name: Jeonju National Museum
spots.desc: It has 40,000 important cultural assets related to Jeollabuk-do, including historical materials, calligraphy, ceramics, and craft arts, as well as archaeological relics excavated and excavated in Jeollabuk-do. Among them, representative cultural assets are selected and displayed, and special exhibitions on various topics are also held.

spots.name: Jeongbang waterfall
spots.desc: With Seopeom and Beomseom island in front, the Jeongbang Waterfall is right at the edge of the ocean. Apparently the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly into the sea and one of the "three famous waterfalls of Jeju".

spots.name: Gongsan Fortress
spots.desc: A 1,500-year-old mountain-top fortress looming over the Geumgang River. You might need a decent amount of imagination to get the most out of this place, as much of the fortress is a series fenced off grassy rectangles marking the estimated site of the ancient Baekje Royal Palace and associated structures. A decent amount of information is provided around the various sites in both Korean and…

spots.name: Jebudo
spots.desc: A coastal island with a beach, tidal flats, a red lighthouse and seaside walking routes. The road from the mainland is submerged at high tide. Check the official road-opening schedule for the date of your visit, including the return journey. Weather can affect the predicted opening times. The phone number is for the Jebudo management office. See Jebudo for the island's travel guide.

spots.name: Oeam-ri Folk Village
spots.desc: A 500-year old site. Numerous films have been shot there.
spots.price: Adults ₩2,000, youth or soldier ₩1,000, children ₩1,000, group discounts offered

spots.name: Soyosan Mountain
spots.desc: A mountain spanning Dongducheon-si and Sinbuk-myeon, Pocheon-si, Gyeonggi-do. The main peak, Uisangdae Peak, is 587 m high, and although it is a low mountain, it takes more than four hours to go around all the peaks.
spots.price: Individual: adult ₩2,000, youth ₩600, child ₩300; group: adult ₩900, youth ₩500

spots.name: National Gwangneung Arboretum
spots.desc: A representative natural space where you can meet fresh air and green trees. It has 6,251 different kinds of plants, and visitors can see a specialized exhibition center, two greenhouses, and a forest museum.

spots.name: Seoullo 7017
spots.desc: A former motorway turned into pedestrian walkway. Opened in 2017, it offers a unique view above the cars and rails, with gardens and cafes along the path. Night view with car lights and neon signs is especially beautiful.

spots.name: Gwaneumdo
spots.desc: It is an annexed island about 100m away from Ulleungdo Island.

spots.name: Eunhaesa Temple
spots.desc: Literally meaning "Temple of the Silver Sea", the interior is as beautiful as its name. Eunhaesa was built in 809 during the reign of the Silla Kingdom.

spots.name: Sinheungsa Temple
spots.desc: Jajangyulsa, a high Buddhist monk, under the king’s command during the Silla Kingdom, constructed Sinheungsa Temple in 652. Within the temple is a nine-level stone pagoda that contains some of Buddha's ashes. It took 11 years to build the bronze sitting-Buddha in front of the Iljumun Gate, which is 14.6 meters high. At Jwadae there are 16 stone sculptures delicately carved in hopes of the…

spots.name: Garak Market
spots.desc: This is an enormous farmers' and fish market. It is a good place to visit because the amenities are well-equipped.

spots.name: BEXCO
spots.desc: BEXCO is a large exhibition center with many halls, and although most of the events are rather dry (i.e. Industrial Marine technology) there may be something of interest whilst you're in town such as computer gaming or coffee making expositions. Check out the schedule on the website. Many cafes in Busan have promotional leaflets for upcoming events held in BEXCO and sometimes offer a discount.…

spots.name: Jugeumsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain between Okcheon-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do and Seorak-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, and is 862 m high.

spots.name: Sudeoksa Temple
spots.desc: The temple stands at the foot of Deoksungsan Mountain. Its Daeungjeon Hall dates from 1308 and is one of Korea's oldest surviving wooden buildings.

spots.name: Yongdusan Park and Busan Tower
spots.desc: This pleasant little park is home to Busan's one true tourist attraction, the 118-meter-tall Busan Tower. This is the fourth tallest tower in South Korea, although it is over 100 meters shorter than the Namsan Tower in Seoul. There are some decent views even without going up the tower, and you can buy some corn to feed the resident population of ravenous pigeons. The fences surrounding Busan…

spots.name: Busan Modern History Museum
spots.desc: This building housing the Busan Modern History Museum was used as the Busan Branch of the Oriental Development Company during the Japanese occupation and as the Busan USIS Cultural Center (a CIA post) following the Korean war. The exhibition consists of the modern history of Busan during the Japanese occupation, Busan's role in the Korean war and the history of the relationship between Korea and…

spots.name: Nakseongdae Park
spots.desc: The park surrounding the Seoul National University, continuing on outside the city borders. Interesting points here include the Anguksa Shrine built in honor of the 10th-century general Gang Gam-chan

spots.name: Jejin Railway Station
spots.desc: A railway station in the South that could one day be connected back to the North.

spots.name: Daegwallyeong
spots.desc: Daegwallyeong is a mountain pass in the Taebaek Mountains of eastern South Korea. At a height of 832 m, it is between Hoenggye-ri, Pyeongchang-gun and seongsan-myeon, Gangneung-si.

spots.name: Independence Memorial Hall
spots.desc: This was built to celebrate Korea's independence from Japan. There are a monument of General MacArthur and several other statues that symbolize the country's independence.

spots.name: Dosan Park
spots.desc: This park was created to commemorate Ahn Chang-ho's patriotism and educational spirit, and opened on November 9, 1973, the 95th anniversary of Ahn Chang-ho's birth.

spots.name: Seorae Village
spots.desc: Seorae Village is a small France in Seoul, where many French people live here, there are French cafes and bakeries, and there are many atmospheric restaurants.

spots.name: Nexon Computer Museum
spots.desc: Apparently Korea's first dedicated computer museum, housing over 4,000 working examples of antique computers and video games.

spots.name: Gyeongju World
spots.desc: An amusement park with a Ferris wheel, a roller coaster and other rides. It also incorporates several smaller theme parks such as the water park California Beach, the Kiddy Land and the Children's Animal Ranch.

spots.name: Seongjusa Temple
spots.desc: Impressive temple complex with many buildings in a picturesque setting. Paved roads the entire way there - no hiking necessary (though hiking trails do lead to and from the temple area).

spots.name: Mudeungsan National Park
spots.desc: For a mountain over 1,000 meters tall to be located close to a population center of over 1 million people is a rare occurrence not only in Korea but also in the world. Furthermore, it takes only 10 minutes by car from the urban area to the mountain. An unparalleled landmark of Gwangju, it appears to enfold the city in grandeur. It is a common occurrence to see photos of Mudeungsan in many stores…

spots.name: Wolmido Island
spots.desc: Wolmido Island is a lively waterfront destination in Incheon, known for its seaside boardwalk, amusement parks, and fresh seafood restaurants. Visitors can enjoy scenic walks, thrilling rides at Wolmi Theme Park, and panoramic views of the city and ocean from Mount Wolmi. The island is easily accessible from downtown Incheon and offers a relaxing escape with cultural attractions, cruises, and…

spots.name: Anyang Sports Complex
spots.desc: It is a sports facility in the city of Anyang. Opened on June 30, 1986, the main stadium is a stadium equipped with natural turf fields and urethane tracks. It also consists of a multi-purpose gymnasium, ice rink, auxiliary stadium, tennis court, ssireum court, and swimming pool.

spots.name: Jungmun·Daepo Coast Jusangjeolli Cliff
spots.desc: A hexagonal rock formed by reducing its volume in the process of solidifying liquid lava like a turtle's back, and is designated as Natural Monument No. 443 and protected.

spots.name: Yungneung and Geolleung Royal Tombs
spots.desc: Two Joseon royal tombs in wooded grounds. Yungneung contains Crown Prince Sado, later honoured as King Jangjo, and Lady Hyegyeong. Geolleung contains their son King Jeongjo and his wife Queen Hyoui. Follow the designated paths between the tomb areas.
spots.hours: Feb–May and Sep–Oct 09:00–18:00; Jun–Aug 09:00–18:30; Nov–Jan 09:00–17:30. Last admission one hour before closing.…
spots.price: ₩1,000 for Korean visitors aged 25–64 and foreign visitors aged 19–64; younger visitors and those aged 65 or older…

spots.name: Seonyudo Island
spots.desc: One of the most popular island destinations in the Gogunsan Archipelago. Connected by bridges to neighboring islands like Munyeodo and Jangjado, making it easy to explore on foot, by bike, or via electric vehicles. Features scenic beaches and dramatic coastal peaks like Mangjubong.
spots.price: Free access to island (ferry or local transport fees apply)

spots.name: Yakcheonsa
spots.desc: The largest temple in Asia.

spots.name: Seoul Museum of Art
spots.desc: Renovated from an old court building, it mainly exhibits contemporary art works. You can see installments and video arts as well as paintings and sculptures. A cafe is with a souvenir shop on the first floor.

spots.name: National Hangul Museum
spots.desc: With a big permanent exhibition hall divided in three: The Creation of Hangeul, Before the Invention of Hangeul, The principle behind the creation of Hangeul; and a small one for the special temporary topics (relating to Hangeul and other linguistic characters of the world), this place is a must-see to understand why the Koreans are so proud about their language.

spots.name: Kim Gu Memorial Hall
spots.desc: It is a memorial hall left to remember and record the history left by Kim Gu.

spots.name: Yeonghyeon-ri Rock-carved Buddha Triad
spots.desc: National Treasure No. 84. It is noted for its mysterious smile that changes according to the direction of light.

spots.name: Woljeong-ri Station
spots.desc: This was a through-station before the division of the two Koreas, but now is the northernmost terminal station near the southern boundary of the DMZ. A large sign says The train wants to run, symbolizing the tragedy of national division.

spots.name: Baekmagoji Memorial
spots.desc: A memorial site dedicated to the fierce Battle of White Horse, one of the bloodiest high-altitude conflicts of the Korean War. The site includes a birch forest path leading to a memorial tower and a museum honoring the fallen soldiers.

spots.name: Jangneung
spots.desc: Even though most of the royal tombs of Joseon Dynasty are in Seoul and Gyeonggi-do, Jangneung for King Danjong is in Yeongwol, because the young king was ​murdered here. Yeongwol registants hold an annual festival, Yeongwol Danjong Festival to commemorate him.

spots.name: Jamsil Sports Complex
spots.desc: This large sports complex centered around Jamsil Olympic Stadium, built in 1976 and host to most of the competitions in the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Though its heady Olympic heydays are long past, this sports complex is still very much active and frequently hosts various cultural and sporting events, most frequently concerts and baseball games. At Jamsil Baseball Stadium, Doosan Bears and LG Twins…

spots.name: Busan Aquarium
spots.desc: This is the largest aquarium in Korea with great facilities and excellent displays. There is also a 3D ride that is worth checking out. There are larger aquariums in Asia, and outside the facility looks rather underwhelming, but inside the displays are high quality and the tanks well maintained. Easy to spend a couple of hours with kids. The price is ₩23,000 but you can get various discount like…

spots.name: Nogodan
spots.desc: The highest peak on the west side of Jirisan Mountain's main ridge. You can see a spectacular view of clouds made from the Namhae Sea and Seomjingang River flowing between the ridges. The harmony of azaleas living on peaks and clouds is worth seeing.The sea of clouds seen from here is famous. Nogodan Unhae is one of the 10 scenic views of Jiri, and it is also called Nogounhae.

spots.name: Yeongdo Bridge
spots.desc: This is a famous lifting bridge that was built in 1934. It was a meeting point for missing families during the Korean War. The current bridge was rebuilt in 2013, and the bridge lifts up at 14:00 for 15 minutes on every Saturday.

spots.name: Busan Museum
spots.desc: Discover the history of Busan from the Prehistoric period to the present day.

spots.name: Geumjeong Fortress North Gate
spots.desc: Offers commanding views over the city of Busan. It can be reached via a relatively steep 2-km climb of the mountain behind the Beomeosa Temple.

spots.name: Children's Grand Park
spots.desc: Neung-dong, Gwangjin-gu. The park was opened in 1973. The park has a zoo, amusement facilities and restaurants. To get there, simply take the subway to Children's Grand Park on line 7. Avoid the weekends as it can get very crowded.

spots.name: Cheungwan Mountain Provincial Park
spots.desc: This mountain park is known for its jagged rock formations and views of the South Sea islands. Its primary attraction is the vast silver grass fields near the 723m summit, which peak every October. The park grounds also house the historic Cheongwansa Temple, a natural recreation forest with camping and cabin facilities, and a literature park featuring stone monuments dedicated to local authors.

spots.name: Incheon Grand Park
spots.desc: A large park in the eastern inland area of Incheon. It has various facilities including a children's zoo, a botanical garden, an arboretum, a sledding area, etc. There are so many cherry blossom trees that the scenery is very nice during the cherry blossom season. As it is surrounded by Mt. Gwanmosan and Mt. Sanga, the hiking course is included inside the park. It is 160 meters tall and 150…

spots.name: Yangjae Citizen's Forest
spots.desc: On the southern end of Gangnam Street is this large public park featuring playgrounds, performance spaces, sculpture gardens, memorial monuments for the victims of the Sampoong Department Store disaster and the bombing of Korean Air flight 858, and over 106,600 trees. It's a very popular picnic spot for young students and photographers. A little out of the way, but accessible by commuter rail…

spots.name: Sevit Island
spots.desc: It is a beautiful place in the Han River. There is a floating island called Sebit Dongdongseom Island, where you can enjoy various activities such as eating and boat experience.

spots.name: Daerungwon Burial Mound
spots.desc: This tumuli park is the main attraction of the region and consists of 30 burial mounds in the central part of the city. In the Grave of the Heavenly Horse (Cheonmachong, 천마총, Grave #155) there is an entrance that allows you to take an inside look. In addition to the grave, replicas of artefacts found in the grave are displayed. Among these the most valuable item is a golden crown (national…

spots.name: Woljeonggyo Bridge
spots.desc: Scenic bridge reconstructed in Silla style near Gyeongju National Museum and Gyochon Traditional Village. It is a popular place for its night view

spots.name: Kamŭnsa
spots.desc: This temple which is close to the sea in the east has only the foundations and two 13-m-high stone pagodas remaining. The building was begun by King Munmu and completed by his son, Shinmun, in 682. The temple hall was to serve as a resting place of King Munmu's reincarnation as a sea dragon, and therefore Shinmun built a water path from the sea to this temple. This should not be confused with…

spots.name: Girimsa Temple
spots.desc: At the foot of Hamwolsan mountain, this temple was founded in 643 in the twelfth year of the rule of King Seondeok. The relatively large compound comprises of 16 buildings. The main highlights are the three floor pagoda (Samcheung Seoktap), the Daejeokgwangjeon hall and the golden sitting Buddha statue of Geonchilbosal Jwasang. This temple is much quieter than the one in nearby Bulguksa.

spots.name: Tomb of Kim Yu-sin
spots.desc: Not just kings were buried in the mounds, but prominent persons like general Kim Yushin (595-673) as well. He was a son of Kimsuo, the last king of the Geumgwangaya Kingdom. At the age of 15 he started serving the kingdom of Silla and played a decisive role in the conquest of Goguryeo and Baekje, wherefore he was elevated to the highest rank under King Munmu. According to a legend, the general…

spots.name: Poseokjeong
spots.desc: There are not much left of the site where the Silla kings held their ceremonies. The most visible part is a narrow passage called yusanggoksuyeon, 22 m in length and built for a game called goksugeo where the player had to recite a poem while a glass ball was rolling down the passage. Not far away there is a site called Najeong of which there are just the foundations left. This is the site where…

spots.name: Sikjangsan Mountain Forest
spots.desc: Open all year round, no parking facilities. The site provides extensive walking trails and temple visits.

spots.name: Expo Park
spots.desc: Commemorate the Deajeon Expo held in 1993 and committed to understanding the role of science and technology. Closed every Monday. Entrance ₩2,500 per person. Parking for 100 cars, small ₩1,500-large ₩2,000. Image simulation hall, dome image hall, energy hall, electric energy hall, and science hall science/exhibition, science academy, robot class, handicraft class, body world, dinosaur festival…
spots.addr: Deajeon Expo Science Park Local Corporation 3-1 Doryongdong, Yusunggu

spots.name: Naewonam Valley of Mt Daeun
spots.desc: The tranquil valley is filled with pools of water and waterfalls next to large stones. The Naewonam Temple is also located in the valley amidst the mountain scenery.

spots.name: Muhaksan
spots.desc: Hike up Muhaksan, a 700-m mountain near Masan's city center. In particular, the Seowongok Valley in the east is a lush tree landscape, making it a favorite resting place for Changwon citizens. Hakbong, at the top, blends azaleas blooming in the mountains, creating a superb view in spring.

spots.name: Mt Gaji
spots.desc: Selected as one of the 100 Most Beautiful Mountains in Korea, Mt Gaji is the tallest mountain in Ulsan. There are well marked hiking trails up the mountain and are accessible from Seongnamsa Temple.

spots.name: Yongjusa
spots.desc: Historic Buddhist temple with an elaborate, colorful interior, storied bells & tranquil grounds.

spots.name: Dora Observatory
spots.desc: Located at the top of mountain "Dora". Visitors can see the DMZ (demilitarized zone) and North Korea.

spots.name: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall
spots.desc: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall is one of the "three famous waterfalls of Jeju". Cheonjiyeon (meaning a waterfall connecting the sky (ch'eon) and land (ji)) receives a large number of tourists to get their picture taken with the falls in the background. Although there is one main area where water falls over the cliff, depending on how much rain has fallen recently, the stream may spread and cascade down at…

spots.name: Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls
spots.desc: A three-tier waterfall, one of the three famous waterfalls of Jeju.

spots.name: Jikjisa Temple
spots.desc: Constructed in the year 418 at the foot of Mount Hwangaksan, Jikjisa temple claims to be the oldest in Korea. Temple stays are offered.
