Within the temple grounds are cultural properties such as the Gilt-bronze Reliquary from the Stupa of the Three Honored Ones at Dorisa Temple (National Treasure No. 208), the Painting of the Assembly of Sakyamuni Buddha and Two Bodhisattvas at Jikjisa Temple…

spots.name: Royal Tomb of King Suro
spots.desc: Legend has it that in AD48, Princess Suriratna of the Ayutah Kingdom in the city of Ayodhya in India was sent to Korea at the age of 16 to marry King Suro, and became Queen Heo Hwangok. Although it is not certain that these events happened, Korean historians believe that if true, the subsequent Kim clan can claim to have as many as 10% of Koreans as her descendants. It has been relatively rare in…

spots.name: Mt. Seowoon
spots.desc: Mt. Seowoon (547.4 m), one of the eight scenic views of Anseong, is located on the border between Anseong City in Gyeonggi Province and Jincheon County in North Chungcheong Province. It is said to be Mt. Seowoon because you saw a blue dragon climb down Seowoon-myeon. The ridge is smooth and the mountain has a gentle slope. From the top of Mt. Seowoon, you can see Anseong City such as Gongdo-eup…

spots.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
spots.desc: Since its independence from Japan, Korea has experienced a series of political events during a short period. You can see exhibitions that show war, dictatorships, uprisings against dictatorships, and industrialization that happened in South Korea.

spots.name: Oido Fishing Village
spots.desc: Here, you can experience the natural mudflats and dig for clams. Enjoy grilled clams and kalguksu nearby.

spots.name: Hike Cheonggyesan
spots.desc: Well-known hiking area on the Seoul–Gyeonggi boundary with multiple trailheads. Routes range from easy to steep; check current trail notices and the best access point in a live route planner before you go.

spots.name: Gamaksan
spots.desc: It is a mountain between Paju-si, Yangju-si, and Yeoncheon-gun, Gyeonggi-do, and is 674.9 m high. Since ancient times, it has been called Gamak (紺岳), or navy rock, because black and blue light flow through the rocks at the same time.

spots.name: Godalsa
spots.desc: It was a Buddhist temple located in Sanggyo-ri, Buknae-myeon, but only the site remains. It was designated as a Historic Site in 1993.

spots.name: Woraksan Mountain
spots.desc: It was designated as the 17th national park in 1984 and has an area of 288 k㎡. It is located in the middle of Baekdudaegan Mountain, which passes through Sobaeksan Mountain and connects to Songnisan Mountain. Wolaksan Mountain has a rugged mountain due to the soaring rocky cliffs and has been regarded as a spiritual mountain since ancient times, so the main peak is called Yeongbong Peak (1,097…
spots.hours: 04:00-14:00 every day from April to October, available time for entry 05:00 - 13:00 every day from November to March of…

spots.name: National Iksan Museum
spots.desc: This museum used to be known as Mireuksaji Museum, and was reopened as national museum in 2020. It stores many treasures from Mireuksaji Temple and Baekje artifacts from Iksan and Gunsan region.

spots.name: Palbong Mountain
spots.desc: It is 362 meters tall. Located in Palbong-myeon, Seosan-si, South Chungcheong Province, it belongs to the Geumbuk jeongmaek, and according to Hosanrok, the name of the mountain is derived from the line of eight rocky peaks. Originally, there were nine peaks, but they are usually called eight peaks except for the smallest ones. For this reason, a legend goes that one peak that was excluded did not…

spots.name: Eungbongsan
spots.desc: Scattered with numerous waterfalls and deep cows, the valley is known for being a highly adventurous hiking destination for amateur climbers. The scenery is great, but the hiking trail is rugged.

spots.name: Wonsando (Wonsan Island)
spots.desc: Jeodu, the entrance of Wonsando (Wonsan Island), is a 30 minutes from Daecheon port by ferry. People in the village named this island Wonsando, because the geographical features of the island looked like a wild boar. This island is very famous for the shipping spot. You can reach Seonchon, the biggest village in the Wonsando, when you take a walk for 10 minutes from Jeodu.

spots.name: Ami Mountain
spots.desc: It is 349 m high. Amisan Mountain means a beautiful mountain like a beauty's eyebrows, and it was also called Soyisan Mountain or Somisan Mountain in the past. It is the highest mountain in Dangjin-si, and forms a watershed between the north and south, and Dabulsan Mountain extends southwest from the top.

spots.name: Naksansa Temple
spots.desc: This temple is in Naksan where the Buddhist Goddess is said to reside. Ui-sang Daesa built the temple in 676 during the unified Silla era. After studying in Tang Dynasty China, Ui-sang encountered the Buddhist Goddess in prayer, and she pointed out where Mt. Naksan should be built.

spots.name: Seoul Baekje Museum.
spots.desc: Seoul Baekje Museum (Korean: 한성백제박물관) is a museum in South Korea. Based on the natural silhouette of the nearby Mongchontoseong, the appearance of Seoul Baekje Museum was shaped a ship of Baekje in honor of Baekje. Seoul Baekje Museum is a civic lifelong education center with an emphasis on the educational role. There are a variety of Baekje artifacts and vividly embodied materials on ancient…

spots.name: Buso Mountain Fortress
spots.desc: Busosanseong is a park showcasing the ancient fortresses through wooden-covered paths around the park. Some of the prime sights are: Samchungsa Temple (where they honour three servants from China), Yeongillu Pavilion, Soldiers' Huts, Banwolli Pavilion (with the best sights of the town of Buyeo below), Gungnyeosa Shrine, Sajaru Pavilion, Nakwaam Rock (where legends have it that 3,000 women threw…

spots.name: Baekje Cultural Land
spots.desc: It is a historical theme park built in Buyeo-gun, South Chungcheong Province, for about 17 years from 1994 to 2010 to promote the excellence of Baekje's historical culture to the world. The palace of Baekje, Sabi Palace, was recreated as it was in the Three Kingdoms period in the past, and not only the palace, but also Neungsa Temple, Ancient Tombs Park, Wirye Castle, and Living Culture Village…

spots.name: Five storied stone pagoda of Jeongnimsa Temple site
spots.desc: It is a stone pagoda of the late Sabi Baekje, a unique Baekje-era stone pagoda that exists along with the Mireuksa Temple Pagoda in Iksan. It is not known when the stone pagoda was built because there is no record of the background of the establishment of the five-story stone pagoda of Jeongnimsaji Temple Site in Buyeo, but it is estimated that the stone pagoda was established in the mid-6th…

spots.name: Chilgapsan Provincial Park
spots.desc: The mountain that gives the county its name and is considered to embody the "seven origins of creation." A popular hiking route runs from Hantigogae pass down to Janggoksa Temple, taking about 3 hours. Trailheads are also accessible from Daechi Tunnel, Cheonjangho, Dorimsaji, and Kkachine Recreation Area.
spots.hours: weather-dependent, may be closed during dry season for fire prevention
spots.price: free (parking free at Janggoksa, Chilgapsan, Jicheon, Cheonjangho areas)

spots.name: Sorokdo
spots.desc: The island is called Sorokdo because it looks like a deer from a distance. It is a popular destination for volunteers. The story of the Austrian sisters Marianne and Margaret, who were suffering from Hansen's disease, is inspiring. The island is rich in cultural and natural attractions, including a pristine environment, beautiful scenery, dense pine forests, and historical monuments.

spots.name: Naeso Temple
spots.desc: Founded in 633 CE, rebuilt in 1633.

spots.name: Banyabong Peak
spots.desc: The second highest peak (1732m) in Jirisan, is located on the west side of Jirisan, so it is a better to see the sunset than the sunrise. Watching the sunset from Banyabong Peak and watching Banyabong Peak & Sunset together on other nearby hiking trails are all included in 'Banya Sunset'. For the second case, it is recommended to reserve and watch accommodation at the hiking route with a shelter.…

spots.name: Worldcup Park
spots.desc: Worldcup Park has several sections. Sky Park is the most popular for the Silver Grass Festival. The park used to be a waste landfill.

spots.name: Anyangcheon
spots.desc: It is a river that joins the Han River, Seongsan Bridge, passing through Geumcheon-gu and Yeongdeungpo-gu, Guro-gu, Yangcheon-gu. The place name means that the river flows to Anyang. This river is connected to the Han River. The park is long along the river.

spots.name: 40 Steps
spots.desc: A few streets of a grubby district have been 'restored' to their condition in the post-Korean War 1960s, with wooden lamppost and bronze figures illustrating scenes of hardscrabble street life. Also easy walking distance to Yongdusan Park.

spots.name: Sangwonsa Temple
spots.desc: A Jogye Order temple built in 742.

spots.name: Byeolmangseong Fortress
spots.desc: It is a coastal fortress built of stones by connecting two shallow mountain peaks on the beach to prevent Japanese pirates from invading the coast through Namyang Bay in the early Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Jeju Old Government Offices
spots.desc: A comparably nice set of Joseon-era historical buildings in central downtown Jeju City. What's unusual is the existence of a nicely landscaped square pond in the complex, and its tumultuous history of getting built in lieu of a well, destroyed due to an irrational hatred of noisy frogs and ultimately rebuilt.
spots.price: ₩1500, free if wearing Korean traditional dress

spots.name: Hyeopjae Beach (협재해수욕장)
spots.desc: A popular white sand beach on Jeju's west coast, known for its shallow, clear cobalt-colored water and stunning views of Biyangdo Island just offshore. The sand's distinctive silvery shimmer comes from crushed seashells mixed in with it, and the beach's gentle slope with no sudden drop-offs makes it a favorite among families with young children and novice swimmers. Shaded evergreen groves border…

spots.name: Tomb of King Muyeol
spots.desc: King Muyeol is considered as a great unifier of Korea, having conquered the Kingdom of Baekje in the seventh century. His power is symbolized by a turtle, a statue of which can be seen near the tomb's entrance.

spots.name: Tomb of Munmu of Silla
spots.desc: The ashes of King Munmu, 30th ruler (661-681) of Silla, are supposed to be placed in an underwater tomb, next to some rocks 200m from the coast. Archaeologists have found no signs of a royal grave there, so visitors can just look at the rocks and wonder if the legend is true or not. You may not explore the area yourself - access to the rocks is prohibited. There is a beach close to the rocks…

spots.name: Oreung Tomb's Park
spots.desc: The site of five burial mounds, but there are different theories about how many persons in reality have been buried here. According to one story only the founder of the Silla Kingdom, Park Hyeokgeose and his wife Aryeong. As they were buried, a giant snake appeared and interrupted the ceremony. The snake divided the corpses into five parts and buried them at five different locations, wherefore…

spots.name: Mount Bomunsan
spots.desc: Observatory, recreation facilities, and cable cars. Also 20 springs, one every 20 m and each supplies drinkable water. 10 trail routes are available including the Sirubong, Mupilbon, and Sansunggil trails. Important historical sites are located on the top of the mountain. Open year round. A few access ways are available, but the most popular one is via Bomunsan Park Jct.

spots.name: Yuseong Spa
spots.desc: Wounded soldiers of the Baekje Dynasty are said to have been healed after taking a bath in these springs. Kings and presidents including the first King of the Josun Dynasty, have reposed here.

spots.name: Mount Gyejoksan
spots.desc: Bike and walking trails. Site of the Yongwal thermal power plant, and Gyejok Mountain Fortress. Open year round. No parking facilities.

spots.name: Sungsimdang
spots.desc: It is a famous bakery that ranks first in sales among non-franchise bakery nationwide. It is one of the most famous places in Daejeon and is the most famous among the three major bakeries in the country. It is considered one of the representatives and best practices of local self-employed businesses, with six restaurants in Eunhaeng-dong dramatically revived after losing competition with the…

spots.name: Oegosan Pottery Village
spots.desc: Oegosan Onggi Village was established when earthenware master Heo Deok-man settled in the area in 1975. The village today showcases a massive collection of various earthenware products, which creates a unique sight. Over 50% of the country's earthenware products are crafted at this village. The village also features several attractions for visitors to enjoy, such as the Ulsan Onggi Museum, which…

spots.name: Pung Island
spots.desc: It takes about 2 hours and 30 minutes from Incheon to Pung Island by passenger ship.

spots.name: Ilsan Lake Park
spots.desc: Ilsan Lake Park has been loved by countless visitors including people from Goyang since its opening on May 4, 1996. It is manmade, and has a grand, peaceful lake and round park around it so people can take walks around the lake along the parkway. In the corner is the famous Musical Fountain. It was built in 2004 and it beams beautiful lights and pumps water with the music. Sit on the ground and…
spots.hours: Open all day, but most lights go out around 01:00

spots.name: Sunrise at Ganjeolgot
spots.desc: Ganjeolgot Cape is a famous sunrise-viewing spot on Korea’s east coast, located in Ulju, Ulsan. It is celebrated as the first place in Korea (and one of the earliest in East Asia) to see the sunrise due to its geographical position. The site features a lighthouse, a large mailbox symbolizing hope and good fortune, and landscaped walking areas overlooking the East Sea. Every New Year’s Day…

spots.name: Ulsan Museum
spots.desc: A museum covering Ulsan's history and industrial development, with permanent and special exhibitions.

spots.name: Asia Culture Center
spots.desc: You can see art exhibitions and musical performances at this national art complex. It's one of the largest museums in South Korea, but most of the facilities are built in the basement. Old South Jeolla Provincial Hall, where the Gwangju Uprising started in 1980, is involved in this area. You can also buy Korean-style souvenirs here.It is a place with a very beautiful night view. For this reason…

spots.name: Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art
spots.price: Adult ₩4,000; elementary school child, teenager, soldier ₩2,000; preschool child ₩1,000; child (under age four) free

spots.name: Sungkyul University
spots.desc: A private university of Korean Protestant descent. On September 20, 1962, it was opened in Chungjeong-ro, Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, as a seminary directly managed by the Jesuit Korean Congregation Church (abbreviated as Yesung).

spots.name: Daerim University
spots.desc: It is a junior college established by Daelim Academy as Daelim Technical College in June 1977. It was reorganized into Daelim Technical College in 1979, and the school name was changed to Daelim Technical College in 1990 and Daelim University in 1998.

spots.name: Seongeup Folklore Village
spots.desc: The "folklore" is a bit misleading, this is actually an authentic traditional Jeju village in which (some) people actually live. While there is a bit of signage in English, to really appreciate and understand this place requires a tour guide or book.

spots.name: Gunsan Impi Station
spots.desc: One of Korea's oldest stations, built in 1912 but no longer used as a railway station. It is a rail museum and sculpture gallery.

spots.name: Yudalsan Park
spots.desc: Yudalsan is well worth a visit for the commanding view from its summit of the bustling city and the many scenic islands. On your walk up, be sure to visit the noon gun, installed during the Japanese occupation, and two beautiful "Buddhist rock carvings". You can also enter with your dog.

spots.name: AK Plaza
spots.desc: Opened in 2012, with 5 basement stories and 7 above ground stories.

spots.name: Gyeongin National University of Education Gyeonggi Campus
spots.desc: Gyeongin University of Education is a four-year university of education in the metropolitan area of Korea located in Gyeonggi-do and Incheon Metropolitan City. It is the largest educational university in Korea, covering both Gyeonggi and Incheon areas with a population of 17 million, and has the only dual campus system among educational universities nationwide. It has a Gyeonggi Campus in…

spots.name: Nam June Paik Art Center
spots.price: Adults ₩4,000, elementary student, teenager or soldier ₩2,000, under age 7 free, over age 65 free

spots.name: Neungnae Station
spots.desc: Train station which was closed in December 2008, and Ungilsan Station was newly established in place of this station. It is now a closed station where trains do not travel, but it has been remodeled and is used as an exhibition hall. The waiting room and railroad tracks are well-preserved, and vintage props such as wooden chairs, ticket offices, and art photographs make it a popular photo spot.

spots.name: Bongseonsa
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple near Gwangneung Forest. Lotus flowers bloom around the temple grounds in summer, and the complex includes traditional halls and forested walking areas.

spots.name: Seoul Animation Center
spots.desc: Seoul Animation Center (48, Sogong-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea) is a space where you can read over 30,000 comic books and animations for free, and is comprised of a 1st and 1.5-story duplex. Except for Mondays and other designated closed days, ‘Comics Cafe’ on the first floor is open from 10:00 to 20:00, and the admission fee is free. ‘Ani Picnic’ on the 2nd floor is open from 10:00 to…

spots.name: Democracy and Human Rights Memorial Hall
spots.desc: History buffs may heard of the notorious "Seobinggo hotel" used by Chun Doo-hwan's Defense Security Command, but dissidents were more likely to be sent to anti-communist branches like Namyeong-dong before South Korea became a democracy. The branch, which functioned as an interrogation and torture chamber, was built in 1977. This is where university student Bak Jong-cheol was tortured to death…

spots.name: Dokdo Museum
spots.desc: To mark the 50th anniversary of liberation in 1995, Ulleung-gun provided the site, and the Samsung Cultural Foundation built the building was based on data collected and donated by Lee Jong-hak at home and abroad for more than 30 years. It was opened as the only territorial museum in Korea on August 8, 1997 by adding materials such as the remains of the late leader Hong Soon-chil and the Dokdo…

spots.name: Donam Seowon
spots.desc: This seowon was built to honor the academic achievements of Kim Jang-saeng and was designated as Historic Site No. 383 on October 18, 1993. It was also listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on July 10, 2019.

spots.name: Haeamieupseong
spots.desc: This flatland fortress, designated Historic Site No. 116, was constructed in the early Joseon Dynasty. Visitors can walk along the 1.8 km wall. The site carries deep historical significance as a persecution ground for Catholic believers in the late Joseon era. Reconstructed government offices and a prison are located inside the walls. The fortress hosts seasonal traditional performances and…

spots.name: Eoreumgol
spots.desc: A valley referred to as the 'Ice Valley' that is unusually cold. There is trekking around the valley, and you can see ice at the top all year round. (There isn't much at the height of summer, but it is there.)

spots.name: Abai Village
spots.desc: A small village of North Korean expats. Located just off the main street, a hand drawn (called Gaetbae and only ₩200) ferry will take you across the river to this charming village. You can even pull the boat across as a kind of "exercise." There isn't much to see in the village itself, but it served as scenery for the TV drama "Autumn in My Heart" and serves excellent Abai Sundae, a local…

spots.name: Silhak Museum
spots.desc: It is the first and only museum with the theme of 'Practical Learning'. Since Gyeonggi-do is the place with the largest amount of cultural heritage related to practical learning, Silhak museum collects, preserves, researches, exchanges, and exhibits tangible and intangible materials and information related to practical learning and provides knowledge and information to visitors through various…

spots.name: Imun Seolnongtang
spots.desc: The oldest extant restaurant in South Korea, founded around 1904. Serves seolleongtang (beef stew).

spots.name: Punch Bowl
spots.desc: A valley by 400-to-500-meter-above-sea-level highlands near the coast of Yanggu-gun. American reporters dubbed the basin the punch bowl. From Dolsanryeong that is between the east side and coasts in Yanggu-gun, visitors can view the beautiful panorama of the sea of fog that often hangs around the punch bowl.

spots.name: Seokchon Lake
spots.desc: Actually two lakes divided by a road, surrounded by park with several playgrounds. This park is something of an oasis in the middle of the skyscraper landscape. There is also a bar inside Seokchon Lake, so you can enjoy beer with the lake in the background.

spots.name: Seonunsa
spots.desc: A head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. It stands on the slopes of Dosolsan in Asan-myeon, Gochang County, near the Yellow Sea coast in western Jeollabuk-do province. Seonunsa Temple was established by Seon Master Geomdan in 577 CE.

spots.name: Nakhwaam
spots.desc: A rock related to King Uija of Baekje in the Three Kingdoms period. Originally named Tasaam, it was later transformed into a court lady, and later the court lady was compared to a flower, and the name was given to beautify it.

spots.name: Ssanggyesa Temple
spots.desc: An 8th-century Buddhist temple nestled in the southern foothills of Jirisan. Founded in 722, Ssanggyesa is famous for its historical relics, scenic valley location, and a 6 km cherry blossom avenue connecting it to Hwagae Market. Visitors can explore centuries-old stone pagodas, wooden halls, and a tranquil mountain atmosphere. It’s one of the most beloved cultural and natural landmarks in Hadong.

spots.name: Soswaewon Garden
spots.desc: Passing through a bamboo forest, you can see water in the valley flowing below the wall. Crossing the valley, you can look around the pavilions there.

spots.name: Naksan Beach
spots.desc: Yangyang's main beach with swimming opportunities and parasol rental. Located 16 kilometers south of Sokcho (束草), it is considered one of the most popular beaches in the East Coast region along with Gyeongpodae Beach. It has a 4-km white sand beach against a dense pine forest, and Namdaecheon Stream flowing from 雪嶽 Mountain forms a large lake in the estuary, which is also rich in fresh water. As…

spots.name: Yeongdong Grape & Wine Festival
spots.desc: Annual late-summer festival celebrating the county’s grapes and wines with parades, tastings and hands-on picking.

spots.name: Oseosan Mountain
spots.desc: The mountain is located on the border of Cheonghwa-myeon and Cheongna-myeon in Boryeong-si, Chungcheongnam-do, Hwaseong-myeon in Cheongyang-gun, and Gwangcheon-eup in Hongseong-gun. It is 790m high, the highest peak of the Geumbuk jeongmaek.

spots.name: Samseonggung
spots.desc: Samseonggung is a unique cultural and spiritual complex located about 1.5 km up a mountain trail in Cheonghak-dong, Cheongam-myeon, at an altitude of around 850 m on Jirisan. Founded in 1983 by Master Hanpul, it was built as a shrine dedicated to Korea’s founding figures — Hwanin, Hwanung, and Dangun — and as a center for the practice of Korea’s traditional spiritual path known as Sundo. The…
spots.price: Adult ₩8,000, youth (middle/high school student) ₩5,000, child (elementary school and under) ₩4,000, concessions…

spots.name: Mihwangsa
spots.desc: A temple on Mt Dalmasan. It is nearly 1,300 years old, founded in 749 CE during the Shilla Dynasty, which had by then conquered Baekje lands. Positioned amidst a dense forest and jagged peaks, it features a monochrome roof rather than the usual colorful Buddhist decorations, as well as carvings of sea creatures such as turtles and crabs.

spots.name: Duryunsan
spots.desc: The orchid evergreen broad-leaved and temperate deciduous broad-leaved trees form a forest.

spots.name: Pangyo techno valley
spots.desc: Pangyo techno valley, a research and development complex, is a place where businesses research institutes related to ICT (Information Communication Technology), BT (Bio Technology), Content Technology (CT), and Nano Technology (NT) are gathered to seek convergence between technologies. Pangyo Station after stepping off for 15-20 minutes on foot to techno Belley get there. Parking is available for…

spots.name: Buyongdong Garden-(Yun Seon-do Garden) (부용동 정원)
spots.desc: Bogildo Yun Seon-do Wollim (Garden) is a Scenic Site designated as a National Heritage of South Korea, and it was where Gosan Yun Seon-do (1587–1671), a Joseon-era scholar-official, poet, and scholar, spent the rest of his life. Gosan gave names to the island's most scenic spots and, as he moved between them, composed exquisite classical Korean poems, including Eobusasisa ("The Fisherman's Four…

spots.name: Galleria Department Store Gwanggyo Branch
spots.desc: An eye-catching architectural landmark with a shimmering glass facade, offering luxury and designer brands, gourmet groceries and stylish dining floors.

spots.name: Moran folk market
spots.desc: The most popular items on the market are chili peppers and dogs. The most popular and controversial thing in Moran Market is dog meat. It accounted for more than 50 percent of the Korean's dog meat distribution at Moran Market, and there were dog slaughterhouses within the market. Thus, the Moran Folk Market was criticized and protested by the World Association for the Protection of Animals and…
spots.hours: Open every five days, on days that end in either "4" or "9" of each month

spots.name: Seodaemun Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: At this museum you can learn more about geology, archeology and biology. Plenty of fossils on display, interactive exhibitions and various activities for kids.

spots.name: Seoul National University Museum of Art
spots.desc: Contemporary art gallery on the premises of the university. The Museum's main gate was designed by Rem Koolhaas, a famous architect from the Netherlands. Since its reconstruction in 2005, it has been opened with the goal of communication between the university and the community. 3 floors above ground and 3 floors below ground with a total area of 4,486 m², there are no entrances between the…

spots.name: Jeongok Prehistory Museum
spots.desc: It is a prehistoric museum built at the Jeongok-ri Paleolithic site where East Asia’s first Acheulean hand axe was discovered. The permanent exhibitions introduce human evolution, Paleolithic stone tools, and the natural environment through excavated artifacts, life-size models, and reconstructed shelters. The building has a curved, metallic exterior inspired by natural forms, and inside there…

spots.name: Wolmyeongdong
spots.desc: Wolmyeongdong Park is in South Chungcheong, South Korea.

spots.name: Ansan Reed Marsh Park
spots.desc: South Korea's first large-scale artificial wetland created for eco-water treatment. Features extensive wooden boardwalks over reed beds, a bird observation deck, and an environmental education center.

spots.name: Haengju Sanseong
spots.desc: A typical earthen walled mountain fortification from the Three Kingdom/Joseon dynasty. Chungjang Shrine where a portrait and a statue of deceased general Kwon Yul is - kept, 3 monuments commemorating the victory and a victory memorial etc. are located in the compound

spots.name: GangHwa mountain fortress
spots.desc: It was built in Goryeo period. The path of the fortress along the ridges is full of green. When you climb Namsan Mountain, where Namjangdae is located, Ganghwa under the mountain unfolds like a picture. If you can see the sea behind Ganghwa and the weather is good, you can see Songak Mountain in North Korea behind the sea. When you walk along the walls with calm scenery, you will find a tranquil…

spots.name: Gyeyang mountain
spots.desc: Mt. Gyeyang, which is 395 m above sea level, is the highest mountain in Incheon, except for Ganghwa Island. In spring, azaleas color the whole mountain red. Surrounding islands such as Yeongjong Island and Ganghwa Island are visible at the west, Gimpo airport and Seoul at the east, Goyang city to the north, and Incheon metropolitan city to the south. It is attractive to be able to meet many…

spots.name: Samsan World Gymnasium
spots.desc: Samsan World Gymnasium is an indoor general stadium in Samsan-dong, Bupyeong-gu. The stadium has 7,500 seats, and is the largest indoor stadium in the Incheon metropolitan government. It has a swimming pool, auxiliary gymnasium, living and sports facilities, performance facilities and convention centers. There is also an artificial turf soccer stadium outside next to the gym.

spots.name: Haewoojae Museum
spots.desc: It is a museum where you can learn about Korea's history through poop. From the past to the present, we can see the culture of Korean bowel movements. You can also learn about not only Korea but also the culture of bowel movements in the world.
spots.hours: Summer: 10:00–18:00; winter: 10:00–17:00 (closed Mondays, January 1, New Year's Day holiday and Chuseok holiday)

spots.name: Jeju April 3rd Peace Park
spots.desc: This museum is about the mass murder of Jeju islanders by government forces on 3 April 1948. This was part the 1948-49 Jeju Uprising, during which the government wiped out 30,000 people, 10% of Jeju's population.

spots.name: Jeju Stone Park
spots.desc: A museum and ecological park that shows the whole body and systematic stone culture of Jeju Island, the hometown of stones. It is so large that all the stone statues of Jeju Island are displayed, and the entire park is built under the theme of Seolmundae Halmang and 500 General, the birth myth of Jeju Island, so it is a perfect place to feel the quiet atmosphere of Jeju mountains. Jeju Island has…

spots.name: Myeonghwalsanseong Fortress
spots.desc: This fortress used to extend for 6 kilometers to protect the country from Japanese attacks. Today only a few stone foundations and a temple remain.

spots.name: The Gwoereung Tomb of King Wonseong
spots.desc: The burial mound of King Wonseong, 38th king of Silla, lies close to Bulguksa. In 780, Wonseong and his friend Kim Yangsang fought the rebel Kim Ji-jeong. As King Hyegong died in the rebellion, Kim Yangsang took over the throne as the King Seondeok. His successor was Wonseong in the year 785. In 787 he let his title be known to the Chinese emperor, through the sending of tributes. A tradition…

spots.name: Gyochon Traditional Village
spots.desc: A traditional Hanok village that was the center of Silla education and the seat of the famous Gyeongju Choi Clan (rich family) for 12 generations. Visitors can experience traditional Korean crafts, taste the famous 'Kyochon Gimbap', and see the well-preserved aristocratic architecture.

spots.name: Jeonju Hyanggyo
spots.desc: This building is a Confucian school from the Joseon Dynasty. It is less crowded, because it is located on the outskirts of the Jeonju Hanok Village. You can see a well-organized architecture and feel a simple yet elegant atmosphere.

spots.name: Mount Gubongsan
spots.desc: Open all year round, no parking facilities. This mountain has 9 peaks and walking trails.

spots.name: Government Complex Sejong Rooftop Garden
spots.desc: With an area about 3.6 km long and the size of 12 football fields, it is the world's largest rooftop garden that connects 15 government buildings. The rooftop garden has 1.44 million plants of 310 species, and space by plant theme, with a variety of tree species.

spots.name: Sejong Lake Park
spots.desc: It is the largest artificial lake park in Korea with an average depth of 3 meters. There are five artificial islands decorated by themes, and trails and bicycle paths are created along the lake.

spots.name: Daewangam Songnim
spots.desc: Daewangam Park is a seaside park located on the east coast. The park has a walking trail that passes by a forest of pine, cherry blossom trees, magnolias, camellias, apricots, and forsythia. This park is located at the end of the southeasternmost point facing the East Sea, and has a lighthouse that serves as a marker for fisherman and sailors out on the sea. The park is also home to Daewangam…

spots.name: Jangsaengpo Whale Museum
spots.desc: The Jangsaengpo Whale Museum opened on May 31, 2005 is the first and only whale museum in Korea and stands on what used to be a central area for the Korean whaling industry. After whaling was banned in 1986, 250 artifacts from whalers and the whaling industry were collected and put on display. Visitors can enjoy experience zones such as the Whale Belly Road or the Underwater Adventure Zone.…

spots.name: Dangganji in Geunhwa-dong, Chuncheon
spots.desc: Designated as Korea's Treasure No. 75 in recognition of its historical and cultural value, it was a structure that served as a pedestal for a pillar where a flag called Dang (幢) was hung at the entrance of the temple, and was mainly used to promote Buddhist rituals or events.

spots.name: Chuncheon International Marathon
spots.desc: This marathon circles Uiamho Lake, famous for its beautiful scenery. This is considered the optimal marathon in terms of scenery, difficulty and weather. There is a full course of 42 km and short courses of 5 and 10 km. Here is an international marathon that anyone can enjoy, running with world-famous marathoners.

spots.name: Memorial Hall for Incheon Landing Operation
spots.desc: Museum about the landing of 70,000 troops led by General MacArthur in 1950 during the Korean War. The museum has some landing craft and missiles from the war, and a memorial statue.

spots.name: Manseok Park
spots.desc: It covers 355,800 m². The park was constructed in 1998 and is centered on a reservoir called Manseokgeo. Manseokgeo is a reservoir built by people who moved in nearby areas while building Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon in 1795. The reservoir was built and 10,000 more rice were produced, so it was called a full seat. But now it is called the Japanese Imperial Reservoir or Gyopjeongbangjuk. The name…

spots.name: Aqua Planet Gwanggyo
spots.desc: It is an aquarium where people can meet 30,000 marine creatures of 210 species, including sand tiger sharks, small toenail otters and penguins.
spots.addr: 1st basement floor of 300 Galleria Gwanggyo Passage, Gwanggyo Lake Park-ro, Yeongtong-gu

spots.name: Yongduam Rock and Yongyeon Pond
spots.desc: A large piece of volcanic rock said to be the solidified remains of Yimugi, a water dragon. Whilst the legends behind just how he got himself turned to stone in that position vary, it hasn't diminshed his influence, as the surrounding suburb is called Yongdam by extension: literally "Dragon's Head Rock". Just about 100 m to the east you can find the lesser known, but probably prettier Yongyeon…

spots.name: Hangpaduri Hangmong (Anti-Mongolian) Historical Site
spots.desc: A special defense unit of the Goryeo kingdom rebelled against the invading Mongolian army in 1270, and eventually retreated to Jeju Island for a last stand. They held off the Mongolian forces here for 2 years before they were all killed at a fortress built here.

spots.name: Suwolbong Peak
spots.desc: A view peak in the western part of Jeju, 77 m above sea level, and the scenery from the top cools the chest. In particular, the coastal cliff of Suwolbong Peak, which seems to be carved, extends up to 2 km to the east. This coastal cliff is called "Ungal," and spring water rises throughout the cliff, and it is widely known as a mineral spring called "melting water." Under Suwolbong Peak, there is…

spots.name: Gyeongju Folk Craft Village
spots.desc: A few replicas of the surrounding sights, some performances by artisans and several stores selling every imaginable type of souvenirs. In short: a tourist trap, that however is part of almost all tours and widely advertised.

spots.name: Hwangnidan-gil
spots.desc: Hwanglidan-gil is a street full of delicious restaurants, cafes, shopping, and small shops in Gyeongju. It's a gathering place for young people traveling to and from the race, and many of the shops here are converted hanoks or single-family homes. Hwangnidan-gil is located in the core area of Gyeongju.

spots.name: 5.18 Memorial Park
spots.desc: Gwangju's claim to fame is for its own Gwangju uprising, May 18, 1980. There are two memorials for this moment in its history. The main one is found in the beautiful 5.18 Park, in central Sangmu district. There is an exhibition hall there that enlightens visitors to the events that exemplify South Koreans' struggle against authoritarian regimes and their fight for democracy. While there, follow…

spots.name: Daechon-dong Countryside
spots.desc: Daechon-dong (Daechon district) is a rural community which is located on the outskirts of Gwangju, southwest of the city. Daechon-dong village has preserved the rice-farming cultures in Korea well. Some interesting places for experience and understanding it is operating, such as Gwangju Ceramic Culture Center, Daechon Folk Culture Experience Hall (Bitgoeul Craft), Gwangju Bean Center, Gossaum…

spots.name: Sasechungyeolmun
spots.desc: It is Gyeonggi-do Cultural Property number 8.

spots.name: Hanbat Arboretum
spots.desc: If coming by taxi, be sure to use the Korean name.

spots.name: Guryongsa Temple
spots.desc: Guryongsa Temple is intertwined with an interesting legend that in the Silla dynasty, the year 666, nine dragons filled up a pond and built the temple atop. The splendid golden single-story building inside Daeungjeon and Daeungjeon itself were built in the representative architecture of the Joseon dynasty. Korea's largest straw mat is another attraction at Guryongsa Temple.

spots.name: Heungbeopsaji
spots.desc: It was designated as a cultural heritage site for Gangwon State on June 2, 1984. It had the Yeomgeohwat Pagoda (National Treasure No. 104), the Great Vacuum Pagoda and the Seokgwan (Treasure No. 365), which were forcibly taken out by the Japanese in 1931, and are now kept by the National Museum of Korea.

spots.name: Anyang 1st street
spots.desc: This is a busy street built around Anyang Station. Some restaurants in Anyang Central Market, which is adjacent to Anyang 1st Street, and tripe alley in the central market are famous among the locals. The ground floor is not small, but the underground shopping mall of Anyang Station is built on a huge scale to cover most of Anyang 1st Street.

spots.name: Jangneung Royal Tomb
spots.desc: It is a royal tomb where King Wonjong of Chujon, the parents of King Injo of the 16th King of Joseon, and his wife Queen Inheon Gu are buried. It has been designated as a Korean historical site.

spots.name: Seogwipo Olle Market
spots.desc: A traditional market famous for street food, fresh seafood, and local produce. A must-visit for trying Jeju's iconic black pork skewers, fresh hallabong juice, and various snacks.
spots.price: Varies by stall. Street food typically ranges from ₩3,000 to ₩15,000

spots.name: Sangdangsanseong
spots.desc: Sangdang Mountain Fortress lies on the slopes of Mt. Uam within the city limits. The fortress is comprised mainly of a 3- to 4-meter-high wall that stretches over 4.2 km in circumference. The present walls date to the 1716 restoration of the site. Within the walls there is a small tourist village that has several restaurants.

spots.name: Heungdeok Temple Site
spots.desc: Home to the Early Printing Museum, and is purported to be the site of the printing of Jikji, the oldest existent book printed using movable metal type. The museum itself contains exhibits related to the art of printing through the ages.

spots.name: Cheongnamdae
spots.desc: Cheongnamdae Presidential Villa, literally meaning “Cheong Wa Dae in a warm southern land”, was originally used as a private retreat for former Presidents of South Korea. Cheongnamdae is not only a historical site with traces of affection for the people and agony for the development of the country, but also a place where offers views of Daecheong Lake.

spots.name: Wolmyeong Park
spots.desc: It is connected to Wolmyeong Mountain, which is a symbol of Gunsan City, as well as Changgye Mountain, Seollim Mountain, Mubangbang Mountain, and Mt. If you go up the park along the promenade between the ridge and valley, you can see the Gunsan city area, Geumgang Hagduk, West Sea, Outer Harbor, Airfield and Janghang Smelter. The park is well landscaped, and its mature wisteria and cherry trees…

spots.name: Jinju Fortress
spots.desc: Originally, the castle was made of clay, but later the stone was turned into material. Most sights in Jinju are located on the grounds here, at the west end of the north bank. General Kim Si-min fought here when the Imjin War broke out. Jinju's moment of glory came in 1592 during the Imjin War, when a force of just 3,800 Koreans held off an invading army of 20,000 Japanese. The Japanese came back…
spots.price: Admission to the fortress grounds costs ₩1000. Parking is available in front of the fortress, at ₩500 per 30 minutes…

spots.name: Hyangiram Hermitage
spots.desc: A beautiful temple-like hermitage with views of the sea and the scattered islands that make up Yeosu Peninsula. The hermitage itself is located up the sides of a cliff and the entire complex is connected by a series of very thin trails winding their way through tight caves and under twisted evergreen foliage. Rather claustrophobic, but unique making it one of Yeosu's must-see attractions. The…
spots.price: Adult: ₩2,500 / Youth and Military Police: ₩1,500 / Children: ₩1,000 / 65 years of age or older, National Meritorious…

spots.name: Jinnamgwan
spots.desc: Korea's largest single-storey wooden pavilion. Has a small museum attached.

spots.name: Dolsan bridge
spots.desc: A beautiful bridge with changing lights at night and lots of seafood restaurants and romantic cafes around the area. Good place to see Yeosu's famed nightview. For even more striking nightview, climb up to Dolsan Park (돌산공원) when you cross the bridge.

spots.name: Gamak Mountain
spots.desc: Wildflowers in spring, cool valleys in summer, autumn leaves in autumn, snow-covered snow mountains and snowflakes in winter, making it suitable for four seasons of hiking. During the forest fire watch period, the mountain is controlled to prevent forest fires.

spots.name: Eo Island
spots.desc: The majority of the residents were engaged in both agriculture and fisheries because large-scale fishing grounds were established around the island, along with nearby Masanpo, until it was connected to the land through the reclamation project in the Sihwa district in 1994. However, after the reclamation project, the island has been transformed into a grape orchard, a guest house, and a sashimi…

spots.name: Heyri Art Valley
spots.desc: An arts village with galleries, museums, studios, shops and cafés. Check the opening days of any particular exhibition or venue before visiting, especially on a Monday.
spots.hours: The village is accessible at any time; museums, galleries, shops and cafés set their own hours. Many venues close on…
spots.price: No admission fee for the village; individual venues may charge.

spots.name: Gapsa Temple
spots.desc: Gapsa Temple, which was founded during the Baekje period and became one of the top 10 temples of the Huayan School, is the Malsa Temple of Magoksa Temple. Gapsa, which means the best or the first, is called Gyeryong Gapsa Temple after the mountain at the end of the 18th century, and there are 15 Buddhist temples, Buddhist temples, annexes, and pavilions in the compound, and there are hermitages…

spots.name: Gatbawi
spots.desc: Big rocks with a strange shape, illuminated at night.

spots.name: Korea Railroad Museum
spots.desc: Railway museum with indoor exhibitions and outdoor rolling-stock displays. Verify opening days/hours and ticketing on the official website.

spots.name: Yeongneung (King Sejong)
spots.desc: King Sejong's tomb, where he and his wife, Queen Soheon, are enshrined.

spots.name: Cheongpung Cultural Properties
spots.desc: It is a place where the natural scenery was beautiful and the culture flourished, and it is a place where you can see many cultural relics of Jecheon, including Cheongpung Palyeongru, Muntae-ri Stone Standing Statue, Yeonriji and Yeonrimok, Hwangseok-ri Overpass, Natural Learning Center, and Geumnamru.

spots.name: Gatbawi Buddha of Palgongsan Mountain
spots.desc: Gatbawi, officially known as Gwanbong Seokjo Yeorae Jwasang, is a stone seated Buddha located at the top of Palgongsan Mountain in Gyeongsan, South Korea.It is famous for the flat stone hat (gat) on its head and is believed by many pilgrims to grant one sincere wish. The rewarding hike combined with the chance to see one of Korea’s most iconic stone Buddhas—believed to grant wishes—makes it both…

spots.name: Jewelry Museum
spots.desc: Iksan Jewelry Museum houses 119,000 rare jewels and fossils. The Jewel Museum provides tourists with a complex culture and exhibition where history and culture coexist, allowing tourists to enjoy the benefits of various cultures.

spots.name: Banyasa
spots.desc: The Banyasa is located mid-river, leaning against a slope resembling a lotus peak.

spots.name: Dongpirang Mural Village
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see murals painted on the walls.

spots.name: Tongyeong Cable Car
spots.desc: It is a place where we can ride a cable car while looking at the scenery of Tongyeong.
spots.price: Adult: round trip ₩14,000, one-way ₩10,500; child: round trip ₩10,000, one-way ₩8,000

spots.name: Suncheon Bay National Garden
spots.desc: A large park with Korean and international themed gardens. Check the official website for seasonal opening hours.

spots.name: Hakrim Dabang
spots.desc: Opened in 1956, this is the oldest extant coffee shop (in Korean, 다방; dabang) in Seoul. Known for its vintage charm, cozy wooden interiors, and retro vibe, Hakrim Dabang offers a nostalgic experience reminiscent of the old Seoul. It’s particularly famous for its hand-drip coffee, tea, and classic menu items like the "Vienna coffee," served with a generous topping of whipped cream. The café is a…

spots.name: Bulgoksan
spots.desc: Bulgoksan Mountain (470 m) near Yangju City Hall protects Yangju City. It is the mountain that forms the boundary between Yuyang-dong and Baekseok-eup in Yangju City, and is also called Bulguksan Mountain. It is a small mountain that is not very high, but you can enjoy hiking with many rocky outcrops and ridges.

spots.name: Sangju Bicycle Museum
spots.desc: It is the only bicycle museum in Korea. The bicycle exhibition hall, "The Meeting Place," features some 60 bicycles showing the history. There is an experience room, "The Place of Experience," "The Place of Empathy," which introduces bicycle culture, "The Place of Festival," which introduces the Sangju Bicycle Festival, and "The Place of Failure," which sells bicycle-related products.

spots.name: Baekhwa Mountain
spots.desc: At around 933 m above sea level, it is mainly located in inland areas of North Gyeongsang Province. The name Baehwa Mountain is known to have been given because the stones near the top of the mountain are white. The mountain has excellent natural scenery with its lush forests and strange rocks, just like other mountains on the Korean Peninsula.

spots.name: Gapjang Mountain
spots.desc: It is 806 meters high. Baekdudaegan is one of the stems of the Sobaeksan Range, which rises to the granite mountain range of Jurassic. Near the top are Naongbawi Rock, Baekgilbawi Rock, and Sirubong Peak. You can see Baekdudaegan, Nakdonggang River and Sangju Plain, which bend from Deogyusan to Sobaeksan.

spots.name: Topjeongho Waterfront Ecological Park
spots.desc: This reservoir, the second largest in South Chungcheong Province, includes a lotus and wildflower complex, silver grass by the water, observation trails, landscape lighting, rest areas, and parking facilities. A deck road leads to the Tapjeongho Suspension Bridge.

spots.name: Yeonsan Station Railway Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: This cultural center, transformed from a Saemaul train, offers multiple platforms with distinct features: a cafe, a history exhibit on Yeonsan Station, a children's library, and a train-themed playground.

spots.name: Labor Party Building
spots.desc: Built in 1946 under fund-raising and labor forced by the North Korean government, the shelled-out carcass of a building is in Soviet-type architecture with concrete building. For security reasons, only devoted communist partisans were allowed to work within the building.

spots.name: G-Tower
spots.desc: A large 33-story building that houses the Incheon Free economic Zone Authority (IFEZ) and the UN. There is a public observation on the 33rd floor with great 360-degree views of Songdo. There is also a small museum dedicated to the history of the IFEZ, which has been under construction since 1994.

spots.name: Gyeongdeok Royal Tomb
spots.desc: A tomb believed to belong to King Gyeongdeok of Jomunguk, an ancient tribal state that once existed in the Uiseong area. The tomb is surrounded by pine trees and features a stone monument and other traditional stone structures.

spots.name: Goongnamji
spots.desc: It is an alluvial plain located in the lower part of the Geumgang River and was formed by the rise of sea level during the post-ice period. And the ruins of Gungnamji are located in the back marsh of the Gungnam Plain. In addition to the floodplain, Haandan-gu and Jeogureung are typically distributed in the survey area, so it can be widely used as a terrain learning center.

spots.name: Buyeo Seongheung Mountain Fortress
spots.desc: It is a Teme-style fortress (a fortress built for defense around the top of the mountain) built along the top and ridge of Seongheungsan Mountain at about 260m above sea level.

spots.name: Goseong Dinosaur Museum
spots.desc: Korea's first museum dedicated to dinosaurs, built around the fossilized dinosaur footprints found along the nearby coastline. The four-story building houses five exhibition halls and a video room covering the region's paleontological history.
spots.hours: 09:00-18:00 (Mar-Oct), 09:00-17:00 (Nov-Feb); ticket sales end 1 hour before closing; closed Mondays (except when a…
spots.price: ₩3,000 adults (19-64), ₩2,000 teenagers/military, ₩1,500 children (3-12); free for Goseong residents, seniors 65+, and…

spots.name: Juknokwon
spots.desc: It is a bamboo garden built by Damyang-gun while building bamboo forests around Seonginsan Mountain. Bamboo trees where you can enjoy bamboo forest bathing are planted, and you can enjoy a walk along the bamboo forest path. The bamboo trees grow green and look like are spread out fresh, so you can enjoy bamboo forest bathing, and many tourists visit.
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000, Youth (middle and high school students) & Soldier ₩1,500, Elementary school student ₩1,000 elementary…

spots.name: Geogeumdaegyo
spots.desc: Geogeumdaegyo Bridge is the bridge that connects Geogeumdo Island, the tenth largest island in Korea, to the mainland, and is one of the three major bridges representing Goheung. This bridge connecting Geogeumdo and Sorodo Islands is nicknamed Geumbitdaegyo, meaning “Golden Bridge,” because it sparkles in gold. The bridge, which turns golden at dusk, is truly a spectacular sight.

spots.name: Gajeong Station
spots.desc: A former railway station along the Seomjingang River and a stop on the steam-train route from Seomjingang Train Village. The station is a convenient place to enjoy views of the river and surrounding countryside.

spots.name: Ohsan Saseongam Temple
spots.desc: This temple is renowned for its unique architectural features and breathtaking views. The temple is situated on a 20-meter-high cliff, with the Yaksa-jeon Hall built using distinctive construction techniques. Inside the Yaksa-jeon, a stone-carved Buddha statue is etched into the cliff, with a legend suggesting that the revered monk Wonhyo carved it with his fingernail. From the temple's summit…

spots.name: Dopiansa Temple
spots.desc: Founded in 865 during the Unified Silla period, this quiet temple houses the Iron Seated Vairocana Buddha (National Treasure No. 63). The temple's name literally means "Reaching the Other Shore (Enlightenment)."

spots.name: Paroho Observatory
spots.desc: It is an observation deck where you can see the picturesque scenery of Paro Lake at a glance

spots.name: Seokjeong Literary Museum
spots.desc: A memorial hall built to honor Shin Seok Jeong's literary spirit. Shin Seok-jeong, who was born in Buan, was an idyllic and participating poet. Seokjeong Literary Museum exhibits a collection of his poems and autograph manuscripts.

spots.name: Imsil Cheese Village
spots.desc: A rural village where visitors can experience Imsil's cheese-making traditions. Activities include cheese-making, dairy farming experiences and other rural programs. A local food shop sells cheese and other dairy products.

spots.name: Songjeong Beach
spots.desc: Further along the coast, Songjeong is a 1.2km-long stretch of golden sand in a sheltered cove. There are many hotels and restaurants directly on the beach or within an easy walk. Since it is less crowded, this beach is a better option than Haeundae beach in summer. The water is very shallow and is fully patrolled in summer. Umbrellas and day-beds are available to rent during peak season (₩8,500).…

spots.name: Neunggasa
spots.desc: A thousand-year-old temple where you can feel the magnificent energy of Palyeongsan Mountain.This place is known as a historic temple built by Adohwasa named Bohyeonsa Temple during the reign of King Nulji of Silla in 417. Unfortunately, it was all burned down during the Imjin War, but was reborn as today's "Nungsa Temple" when it was reconstructed by Great Byeokcheon Temple in 1644.Daeungjeon…
spots.price: - Temple stay 1. Same-day type: daily / ₩20,000 (adult, student), ₩10,000 (school-aged) - Temple stay 2. Experience…

spots.name: Seomjingang Train Village
spots.desc: A railway-themed attraction built around the old Gokseong Station. Visitors can explore the former railway facilities and ride a replica steam train along a 10 km section of the old railway line to Gajeong Station.

spots.name: Jarasum International Jazz Festival
spots.desc: Early to mid-October.

spots.name: Gaeam Temple
spots.desc: Founded in 643 CE, rebuilt in 1314.
spots.addr: at the foot of Byeonsan Mountain in Gamgyo-ri, Sangseo-myeon

spots.name: Seongnam Art Center
spots.desc: Musicals and pop music concerts as well as classic music concerts are performed in the opera house. They sometimes exhibit art works created by local artists.

spots.name: Gwanggyo Lake Park
spots.desc: Gwanggyo Lake Park is the centerpiece of the city, offering a serene escape from urban life. The park surrounds a picturesque lake and features walking trails, picnic areas, and a footbridge. It's a popular spot for both locals and tourists to relax and enjoy the natural beauty.

spots.name: Songdo Beach
spots.desc: Songdo beach was apparently the first official beach in Korea and the main attraction in Busan for many years until Haeundae became the main tourist center. Today the beach is small (450 meters) and quiet with some charm, surrounded by low key restaurants and cafes. It is also in easy reach of Jagalchi fish market. (Jagalchi Station - Subway Line 1, Exit 2. Turn left at the corner, go straight…

spots.name: Borimsa Temple
spots.desc: Borimsa Temple is located in Bongdeok. Borimsa Temple is the birthplace of Silla's Seonmun, and is the center of the Gajisan School, which later opened the Seonmun Gate. Since 澄 Chejing (804-880), a subsidiary prehistoric man, moved here in the 4th year of King Heonan (860), Borimsa Temple has become the centerpiece of the Gajisan Gate, which uses Chejing, a subsidiary state, as its third…

spots.name: Cheongpyeong Lake
spots.desc: An artificial lake created by the construction of Cheongpyeong Dam. Surrounded by mountains, the lake is known for its scenic views and is popular for water sports and recreation, especially during summer.

spots.name: Trickeye Museum
spots.desc: Trickeye Museum features optical illusion paintings and installations. Divided into six themed galleries, visitors can freely touch, step inside 3D exhibits and take photos.

spots.name: Centre Pompidou Hanwha
spots.desc: A modern and contemporary art museum operated through a partnership between the Centre Pompidou in Paris and the Hanwha Foundation of Culture. It opened in 2026 and presents exhibitions drawn from the Centre Pompidou collection as well as contemporary art programs. Check the current exhibition schedule before visiting, as galleries may close between exhibitions.
spots.hours: Tu Th F Su 10:00-18:00, W Sa 10:00-21:00; closed M

spots.name: Arts Centre
spots.desc: An arts and entertainment venue in Guwol-dong (with which it is loosely synonymous). There are several large department stores, cinemas, designer shops, restaurants, and a central square named Rodeo Street. Sporting events are sometimes shown on a screen in the central square. Also, the place has a couple of stadiums for professional baseball and soccer games.

spots.name: Hwaseong Haenggung
spots.desc: It was a temporary place where King Jeongjo stayed when he visited the tomb. It used to be used as a place where the vice-president or Yoo Soo used to work. It was built on the eastern foot of Paldalsan Mountain in 1789 (the 13th year of King Jeongjo's reign) after the construction of a new town in Suwon. It has 567 square cars, the largest size of Korean royal palaces. Japanese occupation…
spots.price: Free (admission is free; separate tickets apply for special night tours)

spots.name: Paldalmun
spots.desc: It was designated as Treasure No. 402 on September 3, 1964. It was built in 1794 (the 18th year of King Jeongjo's reign) and has five squares on the front and two squares on the side of the gate and a medium-class right-winged roof. On the Hongye-mun Gate of the stone pillars, a middle-class structure was built with four sides of the gate, a half-moon shape, and a traditional Korean structure was…

spots.name: Banghwasuryujeong
spots.desc: The pavilion in the northeast of Hwaseon, built in the late Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Mileukdang
spots.desc: It was renovated in 1959 as a house where Miseol Buddha, believed to be the patron deity, was renamed to "Hwaghwadang." It is a small building made of bricks of 1 square and 3.1 m³. Maitreya is only exposed in the upper body and the lower body is almost sunk. The height of the upper body section is only 244 cm, chest width 107 cm, head height 114 cm and made of granite. In general, it is known to…

spots.name: Hwaseomun
spots.desc: It was built in 1796 (the 20th year of King Jeongjo's reign) and opened Hongye-mun Gate on the stone pillars leading from side to side to side. On the front, the fortress was also built with semi-circular foreshadows. The architecture was a typical two-wing house, with its exterior covered with a flower bed on top of a window room. In addition, there is a chungryang across the side posts from the…

spots.name: Northwest Gongsimdon
spots.desc: Treasure No. 1701. Money means a tall watchtower that monitors what happens inside and outside the sanctuary, and public money is an empty structure. The interior can be divided into layers and climbed up and down through a ladder, and many holes can be drilled up and down to look at the movements outside and attack the enemy with arrows or guns. In Hwaseong, Suwon, there are three public funds —…

spots.name: Daejeon Philharmonic Orchestra
spots.desc: Performs in Daejeon Culture and Arts Center and other local venues. It has undertaken several international tours, including visits to the United States and Japan.

spots.name: Sejong National Arboretum
spots.desc: National Arboretum of Sejong is an organization established to preserve and utilize forest biological resources in the temperate central region. Consisting of 22 gardens, 4548 plant species are preserved. A variety cultural events are also held throughout the seasons.
spots.hours: 09:00-18:00 in Summer season (Mar-Oct), 09:00-17:00 in winter season (Nov-Feb), closed on Mon
spots.price: ₩5000 for adult, ₩4000 for youth, ₩3000 for child

spots.name: Ulsan Petroglyph Museum
spots.desc: Ulsan Petroglyph Museum was established on May 30, 2008 at the entrance to Petroglyphs of Bangudae Terrace (National Treasure No. 285) in Ulju-gun. The museum displays 311 exhibit materials and has an exhibition hall, a storage room, a research lab, and an audiovisual room. The exhibition hall presents models of petroglyphs of Bangudae and petroglyphs of Cheonjeon-ri (National Treasure No. 147)…

spots.name: Jeungsimsa Temple
spots.desc: Jeungsimsa Temple, one of Gwangju’s main Buddhist temples, is located at the western foot of Mudeungsan Mountain. Important cultural artifacts are preserved on the grounds. Climbing up the temple is quite easy. You can walk along the trail with an atmosphere in a quiet stillness. Jeungsimsa operates temple stay programs for tourists.

spots.name: Animation Museum
spots.desc: This animation museum in Chuncheon is worth a visit of a few hours or more. The museum sits directly next to an animation studio. Patrons may also purchase tickets to view a screening of animated Korean short films for ₩4,000. The subject matter mainly pertains to the history of Korean animation, the anime production process, but also highlights animation from other parts of the world, including…
spots.price: ₩ 7000 with toy robot studio next building

spots.name: Ansan Arts Center
spots.desc: There are music concerts, art exhibitions, contemporary dances, etc.

spots.name: Incheon Metropolitan City Museum
spots.desc: It is a cultural complex that collects, preserves and exhibits cultural heritages in the Incheon area, and citizens learn and enjoy together.

spots.name: Starfield Suwon
spots.desc: Starfield is a department store owned by a company called Shinsegae. You can experience or purchase a variety of restaurants, activities, and clothes and accessories from a variety of luxury brands.

spots.name: Iho Tewoo Beach
spots.desc: It is close to Jeju Airport, and it is enough distance to ride a bicycle. There are white and red pony lighthouses, the slope of the beach is gentle, and there is a pine forest nearby, so it is a good place to enjoy the scenery and take a walk.

spots.name: Sori Arts Center of Jeollabuk-do
spots.desc: It is a complex cultural and artistic space that represents the art and culture of North Jeolla Province. It consists of various performance halls, especially the largest Moakdang, which is capable of performing in various genres.

spots.name: Ppuri Park
spots.desc: A family-oriented park on the far southern outskirts of town. Down by a smallish dam, there are the usual swan boats and the like, but the odd drawcard is the hill covered in stone statues representing local family lineages. Local Koreans no doubt have a great time pouring over these, tracing their roots (ppuri), but to the casual observer it's just a curious, if unusual, collection of modern…

spots.name: Jakgwaecheon
spots.desc: Formed by many years of water erosion, the river runs straight past a temple. The rocks are engraved with Korean characters and is an excellent place for photography.

spots.name: May 18 Archives
spots.desc: The 5.18 Archives systematically preserve and manage photos and images related to the May 18 Democratic Movement, which was listed in the UNESCO Memory of the World on July 27, 2011. The archive is located at the former Gwangju Catholic Center building on Geumnam-ro Street, where the pro-democracy demonstration took place. The collection includes photographs, films, and videos.

spots.name: Gwangju National Science Museum
spots.desc: It was opened on October 15, 2013 to lead the popularization of science and technology in the Honam region and to contribute to fostering scientific talents and spreading science and culture in the region. In connection with local industries, the main themes are 'light, art, and science'.

spots.name: K Pop Museum
spots.hours: Wed to Sun 10:00 – 18:00 (last admission 17:00), closed on Mon and Tue
spots.price: Adult ₩15,000; youth ₩10,000; child ₩8,000; discounts for seniors, welfare/disabled, military ₩8,000; free for children…

spots.name: Shrine Hall of the Guesthouse of the Anseong Local Government
spots.desc: 'Shrine Hall of the Guesthouse of the Anseong Local Government' is a Guesthouse built before 1363. Among existing Guesthouse, it is the only Guesthouse built during the Goryeo Dynasty and is the oldest Guesthouse building. Guesthouse is a government office or object installed in each village in the Goryeo and Joseon periods, and it was an accommodation where envoys stayed when they came and went.

spots.name: Cheonjinam Rock
spots.desc: Cheonjiam Rock is the sacred place where the Catholic philosophy was developed into a religion. It enshrines the tombs of the five founders of the Catholic Church and houses a monument, Korea Catholic Research Center, St. Mary Hall, Gwangam Church, and Korea Catholic Museum. Cheonjinam Grant Cathedral is under construction for a 100-year project, and constantly attracts many Catholic believers.

spots.name: South African War Memorial
spots.desc: Unveiled in 1975 in memory of the 37 South African Air Force members who served during the Korean War.

spots.name: Archaeological Site in Seokjang-ri, Gongju
spots.desc: Along with the museum nearby, there are many reproductions of the Paleolithic huts at that time, and various Paleolithic-style Paleolithic huts have been created next to them.

spots.name: Haegeumgang
spots.desc: Designated "Korean National Scenic Site #2, this is a must-see location. Essentially just a locally famed island consisting of tall cliffs. However, the ferry cruise around the island will thread its way through the extremely thin cliffs leading into the island into a sea cave before backing out and departing through different route. Spectacular. Round-trip 3-hour cruises including both…
spots.price: ₩28,000 for an adult and ₩20,000 for a child. A ₩1000 discount applies in the off-peak season. Admittance on to Oedo…

spots.name: Bunsan Fortress
spots.desc: Built in the Gaya Period and demolished after the Japanese Invasion in 1592. It has been reconstructed and is a popular hiking stop.

spots.name: Mokpo Modern History Museum – Hall No. 1
spots.desc: It is a museum dedicated to modern history, located in Yudal-dong, Mokpo, Jeollanam-do. The main building was used as the Japanese Consulate in Mokpo, and the building of the Oriental Development Company’s Mokpo branch is also part of the museum complex. It is well known as a filming location for television dramas. Built in the neoclassical architectural style, the building has preserved much of…

spots.name: Chiljangsa
spots.desc: It is said that 'Chiljangsa' was founded by Jajilyulsa in the 5th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla, and Hyeso State Temple was promoted as the king's name in the 5th year of King Hyeonjong (1014) of the Goryeo Dynasty, and +82 31the names Chiljangsa and Chilhyeonsan Mountain originated from the story that Hyeso State Temple stayed here and educated seven musicians to make them wise.In the 9th year…

spots.name: Pyeongchon Central Park
spots.desc: Many festivals such as Anyang Youth Festival and Anyang Dance Festival are held here, and it is a good park for families to enjoy.

spots.name: Gyeongan Marsh Ecological Park
spots.desc: A wetland park formed after low-lying farmland was submerged following the construction of Paldang Dam. Reeds and aquatic plants provide habitat for migratory and resident birds, making the park useful for birdwatching and nature observation. A trail around the wetland is suitable for walking and cycling.

spots.name: Gungpyeonghang
spots.desc: Gungpyeong Port is a fishing port with a fish market, fishing pier, and waterfront walking areas. The west-facing pier is also a well-known spot for watching the sunset over the Yellow Sea. Visitors can buy seafood at the market or fish from the pier.

spots.name: Geondal Mountain
spots.desc: The mountain is relatively low at 205 meters above sea level. When you reach the top of the mountain, visitors can see the whole area of Hwaseong.

spots.name: Ippa Island
spots.desc: It is 40 km away from the sea southwest of Incheon and takes about an hour by boat from Maehyang-ri, Ujeong-eup, Hwaseong-si. Most of the island is hilly below 50m above sea level, gentle to the east and west, and has a cliff coast in the north and south. The red rock formations on the coast are considered one of the eight scenic views of Hwaseong City.

spots.name: Seolbong Park and Lake
spots.desc: Found at the base of Seolbongsan mountain, the park is a medium size space that also plays host to the city's many traditional festivals. Year round there are some small ceramic based exhibitions, two museums and a sculpture garden to meander through. The park itself is 20 minutes walk from the town center or an even less demanding 5-minute cab ride. Entrance is free although the museums will…

spots.name: Mangwol Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple founded in 639 on Dobongsan Mountain. The temple complex contains historic buildings and is accessible from hiking trails in the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Seopjikoji
spots.desc: Koji means a cape in Jeju dialect. It consists of the bow shaped Gojaut Koji near the sea and Jeongji Koji near the beach. It was a filming place of the Korean drama "All In" So a lot of Korean sightseers visit. Walking along the sea, you may feel like you are in the ocean.

spots.name: Songaksan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a good path to walk while looking at the scenery as the mountains and the sea are harmonized. You can see "Brothers Island, Gapado Island, and Marado Island" the closest, and it is a great place to walk along the promenade while enjoying rape flowers in spring and reeds in autumn. The slope of the road is gentle, and there is also an artificial cave, which can lead to interesting steps.

spots.name: Yukgeori Market
spots.desc: Near downtown Cheongju, Yukgeori market is the cities biggest marketplace. Here you'll find a variety of fish, meat and produce, as well as a selection of home wares and nick knacks.

spots.name: Daeseong-dong Tombs Museum
spots.desc: Relics excavated from a nearby ancient tomb in Daeseong-dong, Gimhae, are being stored and displayed. Daeseong-dong Tombs, which surrounds the museum, is one of the UNESCO World Heritage sites in Korea.

spots.name: Anyang Museum
spots.desc: It is a museum where many planning exhibition is held.

spots.name: Yeonseong University
spots.desc: a private junior college.

spots.name: Chuam Candle Rock
spots.desc: A slender pillar of rock rising from the sea among smaller rock formations, at the southern edge of the city. The sunrise behind it appears at the start of the national anthem on Korean television, and it is a popular place to watch the sun come up. In the Joseon era the official Han Myeong-hoe was so taken with this stretch of coast that he named it Neungpadae. A 72-m suspension bridge over the…

spots.name: Mureung Valley
spots.desc: This is a fantastic valley with several hikes of varying difficulties. You can hike to waterfalls, temples or up mountains. Admission to the valley is ₩1,500 for adults. The valley can be reached by taking any of the city buses numbered 12-something (e.g. 12-4.) The bus fare is ₩1,000.

spots.name: Jusearu
spots.desc: It has long been known as a scenic spot because of its outstanding scenery. It was also designated as Korea's National Treasure No. 213 in 1963. It is designated as the eight scenic views of Kanto.

spots.name: Pocheon Art Valley
spots.desc: A former granite quarry converted into a cultural and arts complex. Its main feature is a green-water lake surrounded by steep quarry cliffs. The site also has exhibition and performance spaces, walking areas, and an astronomical observatory.

spots.name: Baegun Lake
spots.desc: Reservoir with lakeside walking paths and nearby commercial strips. Exact walking routes and access points vary; check the map on arrival.

spots.name: Olleung Royal Tomb
spots.desc: It is the tomb of Queen Dankyeong, the first queen of King Jungjong, the 11th king of Joseon.

spots.name: Yeongneung (King Hyojong)
spots.desc: The royal tomb of King Hyojong and his wife, Queen Inseon. It is designated as Historic Site No. 195 with King Sejong's tomb.

spots.name: House of Empress Myeongseong
spots.desc: The Birthplace of Empress Myeongseong is the house where Empress Myeongseong, the wife of Emperor Gojong who took part in state affairs during the late Joseon modernization period, was born and lived until the age of eight. She was assassinated during the Eulmi Incident in 1895.

spots.name: Bangokji Pond
spots.desc: This small and beautiful lake is surrounded by well-maintained walking trails, with flowers and trees that bloom differently each season. The serene lakeside and picturesque tree-lined path create a charming atmosphere, perfect for a relaxing stroll or taking beautiful landscape photos in any season.

spots.name: Gyeonhwonsanseong Fortress
spots.desc: On December 19, 1984, it was designated as Gyeongsangbuk-do Monument No. 53. It is said that the name became Gyeonhwon Fortress because Gyeonhwon used it as a base when he moved to Dong to defend and attack Silla and Goryeo.

spots.name: Iksan Soil Castle
spots.desc: It is a fortress with a circumference of about 714 m and is a theme-type earthen castle built using both soil and stone. Facilities such as south gate, water polo, and building sites remain in the earthen castle.

spots.name: Gwanchoksa
spots.desc: This temple was founded by Hyemyeong in the 19th year of King Gwangjong's reign (968) during the Goryeo Dynasty. It serves as the affiliated temple of Magoksa Temple, the headquarters of the 6th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The Standing Stone Mireuk-bosal Statue of Maitreya Buddha, which is over 18 meters tall and also dates from the Goryeo period, is the main attraction. It…

spots.name: Ssanggyesa
spots.desc: At the entrance of the temple are the Budo-gun and Junggunbi, both of which are designated as cultural assets of Chungcheongnam-do.

spots.name: Nonsan Gwanchoksa Temple Stone Standing Maitreya Bodhisattva

spots.name: Mt. Goseong
spots.desc: Mt. Goseong (298 m) has a beautiful hiking course from 'Manse Pass' to 'Unsuam'. 'Unsuam' is a temple that was built in the 26th year of King Yeongjo's reign in the Joseon Dynasty. When you reach the top of Mt. Goseong, you can see the wide field of the Anseong Yangseong area and the plain that extends to Pyeongtaek.

spots.name: Agricultural Cooperative Economic Holdings Anseong Farmland
spots.desc: Anseong Farmland is an experience ranch where you can directly touch and feed livestock such as bulls, sheep, geese, pigs, and donkeys, and have a pleasant experience.

spots.name: Kimjungeop Architecture Museum
spots.desc: It is a place that contains Kim jungeop's architectural and artistic history.

spots.name: Byeongmokan Civil Park
spots.desc: It is a park built on the site of a waste quarry that collected gravel for railroads from 1930 to the 1980s, and includes a central square, an artificial waterfall, a fitness center, a four-season garden, a lawn square, and a complex children's play facility.

spots.name: Ujeoseowon Confucian Academy
spots.desc: It is the shrine of Jo Heon who was a disciple of Yulgok Yi I.

spots.name: Aengjabong Peak
spots.desc: Aengjabong Peak looks like a Chinese oriole hatching eggs. You can see Mt. Yangja to the east and Mt. Mugap to the west from the peak. The mountain is only 667 m high, but it is such a great hiding place that the Catholic believers hid there to escape persecution during the 1801 Persecution. Cheonjinam Rock, the origin of Korea's Catholic church, is located here, attracting many Catholic…

spots.name: Mt. Mugap
spots.desc: A 578-m mountain with hiking trails through forested slopes. The summit has open views toward Paldang Lake and the surrounding area. Korean rosebay blooms in spring, while the mountain is also known for autumn foliage and snow-covered scenery in winter

spots.name: Konjiam Resort Ski Slope
spots.desc: There are various leisure activities throughout the year, such as skiing and snowboarding in winter and golfing and hiking in summer.

spots.name: Jeongok Port
spots.desc: It is a port facing Jebudo and Nue Island. According to the West Coast Tourism Belt Development Plan linked to Jebudo, Gungpyeong Port, and Hwaseong Lake, it was selected as a pilot area for leisure fishing for the first time in the country and was created as a multifunctional themed fishing port. A breakwater connecting Sinseo-myeon and Daebu in Ansan City is built right next to the port, so…

spots.name: Wuum Island
spots.desc: It became land due to the construction of the Sihwa Seawall in 1994, and now, Songsan Green City is being created under the leadership of the Korea Water Resources Corporation, and the administrative district has been changed to Saesol-dong. When it was an island, the total area was 0.42 ㎢, and it was a small island with a population of about 100 people.

spots.name: Osancheon
spots.desc: It is a river that passes through Yeongcheon-dong and Osan-si in Hwaseong-si, Gyeonggi-do, and joins Jinwi-cheon Stream from Jeokbong-ri, Seotan-myeon, Pyeongtaek-si. The total length is about 22 km, of which about 15 km is designated as a national river.

spots.name: Muryangsa temple
spots.desc: The Muryangsa Temple was greatly expanded by Monk Bowon after 1986. As an independent temple aiming to be a center for spiritual practice, its grounds include a stone pagoda, the Geungnakbojeon (Hall of Supreme Bliss), an Iljumun (One Pillar Gate), a Cheonwangmun (Gate of the Heavenly Kings), and a Sansingak (Mountain Spirit Shrine). The temple is also famous as the 'Golden Temple' because it is…

spots.name: Seolbong Seowon
spots.desc: Seolbong Seowon is a restored Neo-Confucian academy from the Joseon Dynasty that honors four prominent scholars, including Seo Hui. Today, it serves as a cultural center offering programs on traditional etiquette and Confucian teachings.

spots.name: Baekjok mountain
spots.desc: The mountain where the name Baekjok (百足, 白足) originated from a centipede legend. As the guardian mountain of Janghowon-eup, there is a "Centipede Cave" at its 402-meter peak where a centipede with a hundred feet is said to have lived. The name Baekjok is said to have originated from this centipede legend.

spots.name: Odusan Unification Observatory
spots.desc: An observatory overlooking the confluence of the Han and Imjin rivers and, when visibility permits, territory across the border in North Korea. Indoor exhibitions cover the division of Korea. Check the opening schedule before travelling.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 09:30–17:30 (last admission 17:00); Nov–Feb 10:00–17:00 (last admission 16:30). Closed Mon, or the following…

spots.name: Midongsan Arboretum
