spots.desc: It is a public arboretum operated by the Chungbuk Forest Environment Research Institute, featuring 11 themed gardens and over 870 plant species. Educational and experiential facilities such as the Forest Science Museum and the Wood Culture Experience Center are also operated within the site.

spots.name: Gimcheon Culture & Art Center
spots.desc: The Gimcheon Culture & Art Center was established in 2000 in Gimcheon, Gyeongsangbuk-do, with the aim of contributing to the development of local culture and the arts.
spots.price: It depends on the type of performance or exhibition.(add range))

spots.name: Geumgang Migratory Bird Observatory
spots.desc: Geumgang Migratory Bird Observatory is an eco-friendly park, where you can enjoy the nature of Geumgang estuary bank. Gunsan citizen can enter here by half of price.

spots.name: Catholic Stork Rock Pilgrimage Site
spots.desc: It is named because it is a place where many storks live because pine trees are stretched over the rock, and in one theory, it is also called the "Annex Rock" because sinners were dragged to the front of the rock by wearing anti-locks (a sword put on their necks) and executed. It is the place where Catholics who were tortured during the persecution of Catholics in the late Joseon Dynasty but did…

spots.name: Great Victory Park
spots.desc: A war memorial for the 1592-1593 naval battle against the Japanese. Next door lies a shrine to Admiral Yi who lead the Korean forces to victory, plus a small museum explaining the details of the war and Korean naval strategies. English explanations exist, although when browsing try to keep count of how often you read extremely biased language (answer: a lot).

spots.name: Windy Hill and Shinseondae
spots.desc: A picturesque cliff side hill with a windmill on one side and a bunch of purple-green cliffs you can climb down on to on the other side. There is also a Theme Museum here. The themes are "Korean modern life" and "European decorative art" (aka mannequins of pirates). The intercity buses to Tongyeong and Masan depart from here.

spots.name: Maemiseong
spots.desc: Maemiseong (Korean: 매미성, lit. Maemi Fortress) is a privately built stone fortress in Jangmok-myeon. It was created by a local resident, Park Myeong-jong, who began stacking stones after Typhoon Maemi struck the southern coast in 2003 and caused severe damage. The name of the structure derives from the typhoon itself.The fortress is notable for its resemblance to a medieval European castle…

spots.name: Geoje Art Center
spots.desc: It is a comprehensive cultural facility that opened in 2003 and serves as a hub for local arts and culture. Equipped with a grand theater, small theater, exhibition halls, and rehearsal rooms, it offers a wide range of programs including performances, exhibitions, and educational activities. The building’s design, inspired by a sailing ship overlooking Jangseungpo Port, reflects both regional…
spots.addr: Geoje Culture and Arts Center, 145 Jangseung-ro

spots.name: Gwanyangdong Bronze age Historic Site
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see the history of Anyang.

spots.name: Hantaek Botanical Garden
spots.price: Adults (age 19-65) ₩8,500, teenager (age 13-19) ₩6,000, child (age 3-13) ₩5,000, child under 36 months free, over age…

spots.name: Jeong Yak-yong's Historic site
spots.desc: A birthplace where Jeong Yak-yong's life is well-preserved. There is a memorial hall where the achievements and traces of pioneers ahead of his time are displayed, and a cultural center that re-examines Jeong Yak-yong from a modern perspective.

spots.name: Sanjeong Lake
spots.desc: Sanjeong Lake is one of the most famous tourist destinations in Pocheon. The surrounding small mountain peaks, such as Myeongseongsan, Mangbongsan, and Mangmubong, create a spectacular view when combined with the lake. Designated as a national tourist site in March 1977, many tourists visit, especially the night fog on the lake in spring and fall. The walking trail that circles Sanjeong Lake is a…

spots.name: Pocheon Auraji Baegae Yongam
spots.desc: Auraji refers to the estuary where two or more waterways meet, and Pillow Lava is a name given to the basalt because its shape resembles a round pillow. Pocheon Auraji Pillow Lava is a geological site located at the estuary where the Hantangang River and Yeongpyeongcheon River meet, and is a rock that solidified as high-temperature lava flows and cools rapidly when it meets cold water…

spots.name: Pocheon Banwolseong Fortress
spots.desc: The site of a castle in the Three Kingdoms period in Gueup-ri, Gunnae-myeon, Pocheon-si, Gyeonggi-do.

spots.name: Youngryeongdaekun Tomb and Shrine
spots.desc: Historic tomb/shrine site associated with the Joseon period. If access rules or visiting hours are posted on-site, follow them.

spots.name: Bulgulsa Temple
spots.desc: Bulgu-sa is a Buddhist temple on the slopes of Palgongsan Mountain in Gyeongsan. It is believed to have been founded by Monk Wonhyo during the Silla Dynasty. The temple is known for its Three-story Stone Pagoda, designated as a Treasure, and the Jeokmyeolbogung Hall, which enshrines a sacred relic of the Buddha. It offers a peaceful atmosphere harmonized with traditional Korean architecture and…

spots.name: Sangju Hyanggyo Daesungjeon
spots.desc: It was built in the 8th year of King Sejong's reign (1426) and then rebuilt in the 11th year of King Gwanghaegun (1619) due to the Imjin War (1592). The area around Namsan Middle School was originally the area of Hyanggyo, but some of it has been used as a school since 1949.

spots.name: Sangju Yangjindang
spots.desc: It was designated as Korea's Treasure No. 1568 on July 10, 2008. This building, which belongs to the so-called high-rise residence, shows the diversity of residential types during the Joseon Dynasty in that the floor of the building was placed more than 1 meter above the ground and spheres, which are rare in high-rise residences, were installed.

spots.name: Okdongseowon
spots.desc: On November 10, 2015, it was promoted and designated as Korea's Historic Site No. 532. In addition to the main buildings such as shrines and auditoriums, there are the Jeonsa Office, where offerings are prepared, and the Gosa, Hwajiksa, and Myojiksa, where the seowon managers reside.

spots.name: Bongnae Falls
spots.desc: 25 metres high, it is the only source of drinking water for the island. Next to it is Punghyeol, natural air vents that blow cool subterranean air.

spots.name: cheon-an seongbulsa seogjobosaljwasang
spots.desc: It is a stone bodhisattva statue owned by Seongbulsa Temple in Cheonan. It is a Buddhist statue found during the dredging work of Daeseongcheon in Yeonggi-gun Jochiwon. The statue is 67cm high, 34.5 cm shoulder width and 54.5 cm knee width. The upper part of the boat is broken and pasted, and the part of the right knee is broken, and it is partially filled with long thin cracks from the knee to…

spots.name: Gaetaesa
spots.desc: Designated as Monument No. 44 of South Chungcheong Province on September 29, 1983, this site is associated with a legend in which soldiers are said to have fought the Japanese after eating rice cooked in the cauldron here.

spots.name: Jukrim Seowon
spots.desc: Every spring and fall, a memorial ceremony is held at this site to honor the academic contributions of Jeong Ji-woong and Jeong Yu-gil. Jukrim Seowon was also used for academic research and education, contributing to the development of local scholarship.

spots.name: Hyoam Seowon
spots.desc: On May 17, 1984, it was designated as Cultural Heritage Material No. 87 of South Chungcheong Province. This seowon was built in Duwol-ri to honor Kang Eung-jeong, and was named Galsansa Temple. It was burned down during the Japanese invasion of Korea, and was rebuilt on its current site in the 39th year of King Sukjong (1713) and was called Hyoam Seowon.

spots.name: Chunggok Seowonji
spots.desc: This seowon was built to honor the sayuksin and was designated as Monument No. 12 of South Chungcheong Province on October 4, 1976.

spots.name: Noseonghyanggyo
spots.desc: This site was designated as Monument No. 118 of Chungcheongnam-do on December 23, 1997. It was established in 1878 to honor Confucian scholars and educate local residents.

spots.name: Yeonsanhyanggyo
spots.desc: Designated as Monument No. 119 of Chungcheongnam-do on December 23, 1997, this site includes various ritual and educational spaces such as Daeseongjeon Hall, Myeongryundang, and student dormitories.

spots.name: Kyunhwon Royal Tomb
spots.desc: Gyeonhwon Royal Tomb is now designated as Monument No. 92 of Jeollabuk-do. The tomb and its surrounding stone monuments are well preserved, and there are additional historic sites nearby.

spots.name: Tomb of Seongsammun
spots.desc: It was designated as Cultural Heritage Material No. 81 of South Chungcheong Province on May 17, 1984. It is a tattoo from the early Joseon Dynasty and is the tomb of Seongsammun (1418-1456), one of the breeding gods.

spots.name: Jonghakdang
spots.desc: This educational facility was established for the children of the Papyeong Yoon family and their relatives. It was designated as Tangible Cultural Property No. 152 of Chungcheongnam-do on December 23, 1997.

spots.name: Seosan Abandoned Room House
spots.desc: In addition to the daffodil landscape period, you can visit the pine forest, as well as pretty flowers and old houses that lead to green cherry blossoms, aliums, Shastadage, yellow rose tunnel, pearlescent flowers, camellia flowers, and cosmos.

spots.name: Ganworam Hermitage
spots.desc: At low tide, it is connected to shore; on the other hand, at high tide, it becomes an island.

spots.name: Geumseonggwan Pavilion
spots.desc: Geumseonggwan is historic government guesthouse from the Joseon Dynasty located in Naju.

spots.name: Eodal Port
spots.desc: A small fishing harbor, developed from 1984 and home to about 70 boats. You can walk out along the breakwaters to the lighthouses at either end, past tetrapods painted in bright colors. Anglers fish for flounder from the breakwater or on small charter boats, and seafood restaurants line the road behind the port.

spots.name: Donghae Mureung Festival
spots.desc: Donghae's main annual festival, organized by the city and the Donghae Culture and Tourism Foundation; 2026 was its 39th edition. The program changes each year, but the 2026 festival included a harvest ritual (pungnyeonje), folk games, children's activity zones, stalls run by local restaurants and evening concerts on a large outdoor stage. Some events take place at the nearby Donghae Culture and…
spots.hours: Four days each autumn (17–20 Sep in 2026)

spots.name: Miin Falls
spots.desc: When river water originating from the Shimpori Ubosan Valley flows and there are few water droplets hitting a cliff, it is like a fountain, and the big one is a waterfall that reminds people of snow mountain. There is also a legend about waterfalls.

spots.name: Samcheok City Museum
spots.desc: It is a museum that exhibits cultural relics and folk cultural materials of Samcheok and other southern Gangwon-do, and opened on March 29, 2000.

spots.name: Galnam Port
spots.desc: There are abundant seafood, numerous sea rocks, and clear sea water.

spots.name: Deoksan Port
spots.desc: The coastline is severely curved, and it is the departure point for Volak boat fishing in winter, and many flounder can be caught in the sand fields (Northern Farage) south of Sadong Village.

spots.name: Haemang Mountain
spots.desc: It is adjacent to Samcheok Port, so visitors can enjoy the view of the coastline. At the top of the mountain, there is a pavilion called Haemangjeong Pavilion.

spots.name: Joon-gyeong Grave
spots.desc: It is located in Neunggok-ri, Juvenile-ri, and is the tomb of General Lee Yang-moo, the 5th ancestor of King Taejo Lee Seong-gye of the Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Dodeok Mountain
spots.desc: It is 183.1 meters tall on the border between Gwangmyeong-dong and Cheolsan-dong and Haan-dong in Gwangmyeong-si, Gyeonggi-do.

spots.name: Gureum Mountain
spots.desc: Gureumsan Mountain is the highest mountain in Gwangmyeong-si, Korea, with a height of 237m, and is also called 'Abangsan Mountain'. It is a forested mountain that Gwangmyeong citizens like to visit. In May 2010, the upper line of the Gureumsan Tunnel, a six-lane twin cave system, was opened.

spots.name: Moran Museum
spots.desc: An art museum where visitors can enjoy contemporary Korean and foreign art. Works by famous Korean sculptors are on permanent display at the outdoor sculpture park, and several three-dimensional works centered on flat works are displayed in the indoor exhibition room. There are about 350 items, and in addition to the exhibition facilities, a spacious outdoor stage and sufficient rest areas are…

spots.name: Herb Island Light Fairytale Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival related to herb flowers with an outdoor garden featuring a beautiful light feast and the story of Santa's Village in a fairy tale.

spots.name: National Museum of Buddhism
spots.desc: This place works as a museum at the center of Korean Buddhism, it holds a meaningful special exhibition every year and can feel the traditional culture closer Prepare education.

spots.name: Yongsan Museum of History
spots.desc: It is a museum where you can see the history of Yongsan, and there is a garden on the third floor.

spots.name: Itaewon Foreign Bookstore
spots.desc: Probably the best place for English-language books, new or used, in Korea.

spots.name: Gwangokji
spots.desc: Gwangokji Pond, located in Hajung-dong, is a pond dating back to the reign of King Sejo of the Joseon Dynasty. It is privately managed by the family of Kwon Man-hyeong (an inspector of the Office of the Inspector General), the son-in-law of Kang Hui-maeng. The pond measures 23 meters wide and 18.5 meters long. It is said that Kang Hui-maeng (1424-1483), a civil servant and agricultural scholar of…

spots.name: Wangsong Lake
spots.desc: Lake with perimeter paths and nearby wetlands. Route conditions vary by season (mud/ice after rain or in winter).

spots.name: Gyeongsan Municipal Museum
spots.desc: A museum of local culture to promote citizens' cultural nostalgia. It introduces the history and culture of Gyeongsan from prehistoric times to modern times. It preserves the cultural heritage of Gyeongsan from ancient times to modern times. It has two permanent exhibition rooms and consists of an ancient culture room and a historical culture room. In addition, there are a special exhibition…

spots.name: the Royal Tomb of the Jeonsabeol
spots.desc: It was designated as a monument in North Gyeongsang Province on Dec. 29, 1977. This tomb is passed down to the royal tomb of the Sabeolguk.

spots.name: a confession of faith in the Catholic Church in Sangju
spots.desc: On December 28, 2009, it was designated as Cultural Heritage Material No. 562 in Gyeongsangbuk-do. Initially, it was hidden by trees to avoid persecution, but after liberation in 1945, it appeared and a clear testimony was made in 1984 about the monument to confess faith, and it is now a pilgrimage site for Catholics.

spots.name: Yeongcheon National Cemetery
spots.desc: As Korea’s first national memorial park, it was established to honor the sacrifices and contributions of national veterans and to foster a spirit of patriotism. In addition to the Memorial Tower, this place features outdoor exhibits and a relaxation area, attracting many visitors.

spots.name: Imgoseowon Confucian Academy
spots.desc: Imgo Seowon is a Confucian academy built to commemorate Jeong Mong-ju, one of Korea’s most prominent historical figures. "Seowon" was one of the educational institutions established during the Joseon Dynasty to teach Confucian values. Designated as Gyeongsangbuk-do Monument No. 62 on October 15, 1985, this site is well preserved as a former educational institution from the Joseon Dynasty. Since…

spots.name: Wanggung-ri Relics Museum
spots.desc: It is a relic presumed to be a royal palace. It was used as a palace during the Baekje period, but it is presumed that it was changed to a temple in later generations, and then the temple was destroyed and turned into a ruin over the years.

spots.name: Gijisi Juldarigi Museum
spots.desc: It is a traditional folk game museum and was established to inform and preserve the Korean-style tug-of-war handed down in the region.

spots.name: Dangjin Hapdeok Irrigation Folk Museum
spots.desc: It was built to commemorate Hapdeokje, one of the three major reservoirs of Joseon, and to allow residents and tourists to experience the value of Suri (water 利) and its past agricultural culture and the wisdom of their ancestors.

spots.name: Yeongrangsa
spots.desc: It is a quiet traditional temple in the arms of Yeongpasan Mountain (Samseonsan Mountain), which is said to block the waves of the West Sea.

spots.name: Anguk Temple Site
spots.desc: On the front of the Anguk Temple site, there is a stone embankment, and there are three main stones and foundations left in the site. On one side of the site, there is a small Ongdalsaem, and pieces of tile are scattered here and there behind it

spots.name: Oknyeobong Park
spots.desc: This is the place that located on a low mountain called Oknyeobong Peak, and there is a walking trail where visitors can enjoy walking and light hiking.

spots.name: Yeongamsa
spots.desc: It is known to have been built during the Baekje period. The temple has several buildings, including Daeungjeon and Yakjeon.

spots.name: Yongamsa
spots.desc: It is a temple influenced by the Zen sect and has Buddhist-related sculptures and monuments.

spots.name: Seokcheonam
spots.desc: It is a hermitage belonging to the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Seokcheonam Hermitage is located in a quiet mountain and is known as a place for meditation and practice in nature.

spots.name: Donam Seowon Eungdodang
spots.desc: It is an architecture that Joseon Dynasty building in Donams eowon. It was designated as Korea's Treasure No. 1569 on July 10, 2008. Eungdodang is the place where Confucian scholars studied and is arranged at right angles in the front.

spots.name: Five-layered Stone Pagoda at Gaetae Temple in Nonsan
spots.desc: This tower, designated as Cultural Heritage Material No. 274 of Chungcheongnam-do, is characterized by simple and elegant sculpting techniques. It is presumed to be from the Goryeo Dynasty.

spots.name: Songbulam Maitreya
spots.desc: This statue was designated as Cultural Heritage Material No. 83 of South Chungcheong Province on May 17, 1984. It features clothing with U-shaped lines and shallow carvings of the folds of the fabric.

spots.name: Ssanggyesa Daeungjeon
spots.desc: It was designated as Korea's National Treasure No. 408 on September 3, 1964. It was rebuilt in the 14th year of King Yeongjo's reign in the Joseon Dynasty (1738), and the pillars and beams were made of thick wood, and the scale was quite large.

spots.name: General Gyebaek Historic Site
spots.desc: This site was designated as Monument No. 74 of South Chungcheong Province on December 29, 1989.

spots.name: Nonsan Noseongsanseong
spots.desc: This site was designated as Historic Site No. 393 of South Korea. It is a stone Teme-type fortress located on top of Noseongsan Mountain.

spots.name: Nonsan Topjungri Stone Pagoda
spots.desc: This pagoda, in the form of a three-story pagoda, was built in the middle of Goryeo and is now designated as a tangible cultural asset in South Chungcheong Province. It follows the typical Goryeo Dynasty tower style and features a simple yet stable structure throughout.

spots.name: Water Tower of Yeonsan Station
spots.desc: It is a cultural asset located within the jurisdiction of Yeonsan Station. When railroad networks were built across the country in Japanese colonial era, locomotive supply facilities were installed at each of the major stations. In South Chungcheong Province, there were water towers at Seodaejeon and Ganggyeong stations, but now only Yeonsan Station remains here. It was made by trimming granite…

spots.name: Noseongguolisa
spots.desc: This building was designated as Monument No. 20 of South Chungcheong Province on December 30, 1978. It features a gabled roof and has a structure with three bays in the front and three bays on the side.

spots.name: Hyangjeok Mountain
spots.desc: This mountain is located northeast of Nonsan city, surrounded by hilly areas that support both rice paddy and field farming.

spots.name: Nosung Mountain
spots.desc: Composed of gneiss and granite, this area supports various tree species, including pine and broad-leaved trees.

spots.name: Wolseongbong
spots.desc: Nearby, there are historical sites such as Yeonsan-eupseong Fortress, so it is a place where visitors can explore cultural heritage and appreciate natural scenery at the same time. Various plant groups are native to the mountain, showing different landscapes from season to season.

spots.name: Nonsan Open Library
spots.desc: This facility offers a wide range of books and hosts programs such as reading discussions, author lectures, and cultural seminars.

spots.name: Buchun Mountain
spots.desc: Located in the center of Seosan City, it is a low mountain about 138 m above sea level, and you can easily enjoy a walk in the city center. When you reach the top of the mountain, you can see the panoramic view of Seosan City, and you can take a quiet rest with an open view. At the foot of the mountain is Buchunjeong, the Dongheon of Seosan Busa in the Joseon Dynasty, so it is a place where you…

spots.name: Golden Mountain
spots.desc: Golden Mountain is a great place to enjoy beautiful natural scenery and beaches on the west coast at the same time. It is a low mountain about 156m above sea level, and there is a trail where you can climb lightly overlooking the West Sea. In particular, when you reach the top, you can enjoy the panoramic scenery of the West Sea, the island, and the coastline.

spots.name: Ryubangtaek Science Museum
spots.desc: This place was built to commemorate Ryu Bang-taek, who was born in Seosan and completed a map of the sky in Joseon Dynasty. You can join in Ryu Bang-taek Star Festival every May.

spots.name: Pyochungsa Temple
spots.desc: This is a temple named by the state to honor the patriotic spirit of the great Buddhist monk Samyeongdaesa, who achieved significant merit during the Imjin War. While the temple was rebuilt in 1715 (the 41st year of King Sukjong's reign), all its buildings, except for the Eungjinjeon Hall, were destroyed in a fire in 1926. The temple was later reconstructed, and the buildings you see today are…

spots.name: Hyesan Seowon
spots.desc: Hyesan Seowon in Miryang is a tranquil Confucian academy where visitors can take part in traditional hanbok experience programs. Participants can choose from a variety of colorful hanbok, stroll through the serene academy grounds, and take memorable photos against the backdrop of the elegant buildings and scenic courtyard. The program may also include additional cultural activities such as…

spots.name: National Miryang Meteorological Science Museum
spots.desc: It opened in May 2020 and offers the largest tornado simulation experience in Korea. It is closed every Monday, on January 1st, and during major holiday periods. In addition to the tornado and climate phenomena experiences, the museum features various attractions such as the Ice Valley icicles, weather forecasting, and briefing sessions.

spots.name: Yonghwasa
spots.desc: Yonghwasa comprises eight buildings of Bogwawngjeon, Yonghwajeon, Jeongmukdang Halls, Haewollu Pavilion, Tamjindang Halls, Chilseongjeon and two buildings of Myeongbujeon and Yosa including a shrine of 145 pyong floor area and amongst these, Bogwawngjeon is appointed as one of the national tangible culture assets.

spots.name: Dal-a Park
spots.desc: Dal-a Park offers Korea’s best sunset. “Dal-a” was named after the geographical feature resembling to the back tooth of elephant and also means “ideal place to enjoy seeing the moon”. Tongyeong citizens also call it as “Dal-e.” The ring road, known as camellia road to natives, offers visitors spectacular views of Dadohae (Multi-island Sea).

spots.name: Yangsan Tower
spots.desc: Great views of the local area. At 160m tall, Yangsan Tower offers 360-degree panoramic views of the city and Nakdong River. It features a book cafe and exhibition hall on top, with free admission.

spots.name: Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City Forest Research Institute
spots.desc: The Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City Forest Research Institute is a forest environment research and forest healing space located in Sanpo-myeon, Naju City, Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City. With a metasequoia path and walking trail, it is highly popular as a healing travel destination.
spots.hours: Summer season - Mar to Oct 09:00-17:00 Winter season - Nov to Feb 09:00-16:00

spots.name: Naju Sports Park
spots.desc: It is a place where many cherry blossoms and marathon competitions are often held.

spots.name: Geumryongsa Temple
spots.desc: a temple located in Pocheon

spots.name: Jiktang Falls
spots.desc: Known as the "Niagara of Korea," this waterfall spans 80 meters across the entire width of the Hantan River. Although only 3 meters high, the sight of water pouring over the basalt columnar joints is unique and impressive.

spots.name: Cheorwon Hantangang Jusangjeolli Path
spots.desc: A 3.6-km cliffside walkway (Zando) suspended high over the Hantan River. It offers an unparalleled close-up view of the basalt columnar joints and the canyon's geological diversity.

spots.name: Imcheonhyanggyo
spots.desc: It was designated as a monument in Chungcheongnam-do on December 23, 1997. It was built in Gugyo-ri, Imcheon-myeon, and was rebuilt in 1688 by Jeong Seok-jing, the county governor.

spots.name: Jeongchungsa Temple
spots.desc: It is a temple that symbolizes loyalty and loyalty. This temple is a place to honor the righteous spirit of our ancestors, and it is especially related to Korean history. Jeongchungsa Temple is a historic temple that is frequently visited by those who want to honor the righteous spirit along with its historical significance.

spots.name: Goseong Songhak-dong Tumuli
spots.desc: Grassy burial mounds of the rulers of Sogaya, one of the Gaya states, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2023 as part of the Gaya Tumuli. The neighboring Goseong Museum displays objects excavated here.

spots.name: Okcheonsa Temple
spots.desc: Founded in 670 by the monk Uisang, this temple sits on the northern slope of Mt. Yeonhwa inside Yeonhwasan Provincial Park. Its main hall (Daeungjeon) is a Gyeongsangnam-do Tangible Cultural Heritage.

spots.name: Goseong Jangsan Forest
spots.desc: A small grove of old zelkova and other broadleaf trees around a pond, planted in the Joseon era to shelter the village. Now a provincial monument, it makes a shady spot for a short stroll.

spots.name: Haman Mujinjung
spots.desc: Mujinjeong Pavilion is a historic pavilion built in 1567 during the Joseon Dynasty. It was named after scholar Mujin, who served as a government official in various regions. The pavilion has a simple wooden structure with three rooms in the front and two on the side, showing the style of early Joseon pavilions. It was reconstructed in 1929. Every spring, the local festival Haman Nakhwa Nori is…

spots.name: Myeonangjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Myeonangjeong Pavilion is a pavilion where Song Soon (1493-1582) of Myeonangjeong left his office in the 28th year of King Jungjong's reign and spent the rest of his life teaching scholars, and discussed his studies with Toegye Yi Hwang and other celebrities. Myeonangjeong Pavilion is a simple building, but it has great historical value.

spots.name: Tombstone of Myeongnyang Battle
spots.desc: The monument was erected to commemorate Yi Sun-shin's contribution to the victory of the Battle of Myeongnyang (1597), during the Japanese invasion of Korea. What was moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace during the Japanese colonial rule was relocated to the coastal area of Haenam in 1947 (1186-7, Hakdong-ri, Munnae-myeon), and relocated to its current location in March 2011.

spots.name: Daeheungsa Daewoongbojeon
spots.desc: This building houses Sakyamuni Buddha. Here, "Daewoong" symbolizes the greatness and benevolence of Sakyamuni, and Daewoongbojeon means the Buddhist temple of Sakyamuni Buddha.

spots.name: Jindo Island Jinseong Fortress
spots.desc: It is a castle from the Three Kingdoms period in Namdong-ri, Imhoe-myeon, Jindo-gun, Jeollanam-do.

spots.name: Jindo Geumgolsan Five-story Stone Pagoda
spots.desc: The stylobate and one-story pagoda body appear to follow the style of the three-story stone pagoda in Eunseon-ri, Jeongeup, Jeollabuk-do, and it is interpreted that the Baekje style has spread to this place. It is said that there has been a temple called Haewolsa Temple since the Goryeo Dynasty, so the stone pagoda is also presumed to have been built around that time.

spots.name: Sikyeongjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Built in 1630 by scholar Hanho Im Yeon, Sikyeongjeong Pavilion served as a place for study, writing, and scholarly discussions. The name “Sikyeongjeong” means “a place where shadows rest for a moment,” reflecting the owner’s appreciation for tranquility and leisure. Surrounded by scenic views of the Yeongsan River, the pavilion became a gathering place for poets and scholars of the Joseon period.…

spots.name: Sundam Valley
spots.desc: A picturesque valley featuring white sands, clear water, and dramatic rock formations. It serves as the main hub for white-water rafting in summer and is the starting point for various winter trekking courses.

spots.name: Seungilgyo Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge that North and South Korea built together - the North completed the basic construction and two piers while the remaining parts were completely by the South. The name of the bridge is Seungilgyo after 'Seung' of the late President Rhee Seung Man, and 'Il' of President Kim Il Sung so as to commemorate the ironic construction process.

spots.name: Hajodae Scenic Point
spots.desc: The Hajodae Dulle-gil is a few steps away from the Hajodae Observatory, which is good for men and women of all ages. Visitors can see the glass floor and the transparent window, and you can see the waves hitting the rock and the horizontal line in the distance.
spots.hours: the summer season 06:00-20:00, the winter season 07:00-18:00

spots.name: Yecheon Astronomical Space Center
spots.desc: a theme park on the theme of stars and space, including astronomical observations

spots.name: Subukjeong
spots.desc: It was designated as a cultural heritage site in South Chungcheong Province on May 17, 1984. It is a hipped-and-gabled house with 3 bays in the front and 2 bays in the side. Built by Kim Heung-guk during the reign of King Gwanghaegun in the Joseon Dynasty, the pavilion is named after his lake.

spots.name: Usanseong
spots.desc: A Baekje-period fortress, designated Chungcheongnam-do Monument No. 81, whose walls run about 965 m along the ridges and valleys of Usan Mountain. The site includes a stone standing Buddha triad (Treasure No. 197) and a three-story stone pagoda.

spots.name: Yongbongsan Mountain Natural Recreation Fores
spots.desc: There are amenities such as a forest bath, a rest area, an observation deck, a walking trail, a hiking trail, a nature observation trail, a children's playground, and physical fitness facility, as well as educational facilities such as outdoor classrooms and forest classes.
spots.addr: Yongbongsan Natural Recreation Forest, 87, Yongbongsan 2-gil, Hongbuk-eup

spots.name: Bongsusan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain 482m above sea level, and the ruins of Bongsudae remain at the top of the mountain.

spots.name: Gosansa Temple
spots.desc: It is a temple located on a high mountain. This temple is a place where you can practice in nature, and many people visit to find tranquility through forest bathing and meditation. Gosansa Temple is also a center of Buddhist rituals and prayers, known as a place where various religious activities and events are held. The characteristic of this temple is its unique atmosphere that blends with the…

spots.name: Yongbongsa Temple
spots.desc: It contains the symbolic presence of dragons and phoenixes in its name. The temple is mainly engaged in activities related to Buddhist culture and meditation, and is especially popular with those seeking purification and enlightenment. Yongbongsa Temple is also famous for its magnificent compound and iconic architecture.

spots.name: Chollipo Arboretum
spots.desc: An arboretum on the coast near Sowon-myeon, founded by Carl Ferris Miller (Min Byeong-gal), with one of Korea's largest plant collections.

spots.name: Hwangnyeongsan Mountain
spots.desc: This mountain offers one of the best panoramic views of Busan, including Gwangalli Beach, the Gwangan Grand Bridge, and the cityscape. The view is especially breathtaking at night. The peak features an observation deck and a beacon fire station.

spots.name: Goseong Mask Museum
spots.desc: Opened in 2005 and registered as a specialized museum in 2014, this museum displays over 300 traditional Korean masks from across the country, alongside special exhibits on Goseong Ogwangdae, the local mask-dance drama recognized as a National Intangible Heritage. A hands-on experience room lets visitors try mask-making.
spots.hours: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00, Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00 (last entry 30 min before closing); closed Mondays (Tue if Monday is a…

spots.name: Yeonhwasan Provincial Park
spots.desc: Forest trails and deep valleys lead to the peaks of Mt. Yeonhwa (524 m), named for its resemblance to a lotus flower. Trails start near Okcheonsa Temple; free parking.
spots.hours: Open year-round (may close in bad weather)

spots.name: Haman Museum
spots.desc: As of Sep 2025, access is controlled due to remodeling work and exhibition reorganization. It has relics from different eras, such as Anra history, the Paleolithic Age, and the Neolithic Age. Haman Museum is largely divided into Exhibition Hall 1, Exhibition Hall 2, Malisan Ancient Tombs Exhibition Hall. 1st Floor Children's Experience Room, Book Cafe, 2nd Floor Exhibition Hall 1 - Prehistoric…
spots.hours: March to October: Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00, November to February: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00; Mon, New Year's Day and Chuseok…

spots.name: Nogudang
spots.desc: Nogudang is a part of Haenam Yun Clan Nogudang surrounding a house from the Joseon Dynasty in Yeondong-ri, Haenam-eup, and was designated as Historic Site No. 167 on December 19, 1968. It is the head family house of Eocho Eungong faction of the Haenam Yun clan, and there is the Gosan Yun Seon-do Museum nearby.

spots.name: The Great Battle of Myeongnyang Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival held in the Uldolmok area by Haenam-gun and Jindo-gun in Jeollanam-do to commemorate the Battle of Myeongnyang during the Japanese invasions of Korea. The Battle of Myeongnyang was a battle in which Admiral Lee Sun-sin led 13 Joseon naval fleets against 133 Japanese naval ships at Uldolmok on September 16, 1597, and defeated 31 of them. Haenam-gun held an event in 1997 to…

spots.name: Unlim Mountain Room
spots.desc: The title of the studio where painter He Yu (1807-1892), from the late Joseon Dynasty, lived in his later years.

spots.name: The Birthplace of Cho Eui Seon Sa
spots.desc: Cho Eui Seon Sa, a Buddhist monk from the Joseon Dynasty, is widely regarded as the “tea master” of Korea. He played a major role in developing Korea’s traditional tea culture and Buddhist tea rituals. The site is geographically closer to Mokpo. It features a small memorial hall, traditional-style pavilions, and a peaceful garden where visitors can learn about Korean tea history and Cho’s life.

spots.name: Seungdal Mountain
spots.desc: Seungdal Mountain, rising 332.5 meters above sea level, stretches across Cheonggye-myeon and Mongtan-myeon and forms the southwestern tip of Korea’s Baekdudaegan mountain range. Although not very high, its location near the coast offers sweeping views of the Dadohae archipelago and the western sea. The mountain is famous for its mild climate, allowing visitors to enjoy pleasant hiking conditions…

spots.name: Oryongsan
spots.desc: A 228-m-high mountain on the boundary between Imseong-ri and Yongpo-ri in Samhyang-eup. According to Muan Gunji, the ridge descends about 3.9 km from Guksabong Peak, while its name “Oryong” (Five Dragons) derives from the shape of five dragons playing with a pearl. The summit was once said to feature a small iron sculpture of a heavenly horse.

spots.name: Dongchun Circus
spots.desc: One of the most traditional Circus in South Korea. It started in Mokpo city, 1929 with more than 90 years.
spots.price: Adult ₩25,000,child ₩16,000, discount for more than 4 people
spots.addr: 1849-31, Daebubuk-dong, Danwon-gu, in front of Hyundai gas station

spots.name: Cheonwangbong peak
spots.desc: A peak with a beautiful sunrise. The sunrise seen from Cheonwangbong Peak at 1,915m, which is open on all sides, is special. It is a famous place where the sun rises through the cold air of the clouds on the eastern horizon. There are many days when clouds are in the way, so the panorama of this beautiful sunrise is not easily observed. But it's definitely beautiful.On a clear day, you can see…

spots.name: Piagol
spots.desc: From mid-October every year, Piagol Valley, the largest hardwood forest in Jirisan, is colored with autumn leaves. Unlike most other mountains, the color of autumn leaves here is subtle.

spots.name: Byeoksoryeong
spots.desc: It is a place name given because the moonlight rising above the green forest looks very blue beyond white.Byeoksoryeong Shelter, a national park shelter, is located in Byeoksoryeong, so you can stay there. Thanks to this, you don't have to go hiking at night to see Byeokso Myeongwol. In addition, Byeoksoryeong Pass is one of the major hubs of Jirisan Mountain's Jongju, so you can meet…

spots.name: Cheoneunsa Temple
spots.desc: Built in 828 and reconstructed in 1774, this Buddhist temple is often overshadowed by its neighbor Hwaeomsa. It does, however, hold the unique honor of being one of the last places in South Korea where the endangered wild pigeon is still common, with visitors to the temple being very likely to see one.At the time of reconstruction, a large serpent frequently appeared near the spring of Gamnosa…

spots.name: Cheondong Cave
spots.desc: This cave has many ups and downs along with twisty narrow passages. It is perfect for nimble athletic folk. There are some excellent stalactites, stalagmites, fins, and soda straws to be seen.

spots.name: Samsan-ri Machilus Thunbergii
spots.desc: This tree is a designated Natural Monument of South Korea. It is about 400 years old and is known for its beautiful, broad canopy that forms a perfect dome shape. Historically, local villagers have used the area under its shade as a community gathering spot and for traditional rituals. It is a peaceful stop located in Samsan-ri, offering a glimpse into the region's natural heritage.

spots.name: Gwanggyo Modern library
spots.desc: The Gwanggyo Modern Library is an architectural marvel. Its striking design features a large central atrium and plenty of natural light. Even if you're not a bookworm, the library is worth visiting just for its innovative design.

spots.name: Naksaeng high school (Naksaeng myeon office 3.1 Resistance from Japan)
spots.desc: It now looks like an ordinary high school, but it was the place where on March 1, 1919, people protested against Japanese rule.

spots.name: Herdsman indoor ice rink
spots.desc: Indoor ice arena in Yangcheon-gu, Seoul. The main stadium is on the ground, the secondary stadium is a stadium in the basement. Opening on December 1, 1989, the capacity is 5,000 people.
spots.hours: Sat Sun public holidays 12:00-18:00 (closed on Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok), Mon-Fri 14:00-18:00

spots.name: Korean Peninsula Unification Future Center
spots.desc: It is a unification experience and training facility operated by the Ministry of Unification, providing opportunities to reflect on division and unification through various programs and hands-on activities. The center is equipped with modern facilities such as the Unification Future Experience Hall, dormitories, a gymnasium, a family village, and outdoor activity areas.

spots.name: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car)
spots.desc: This marine cable car connects Songdo Beach to Amnam Park. It offers spectacular views as it glides over the sea. For a more thrilling experience, you can choose the Crystal Cabin with a transparent floor. On a clear day, you can see as far as Yeongdo, the Namhangdaegyo Bridge, and even Haeundae.

spots.name: GangHwa Hyanggyo
spots.desc: Hyanggyo is the Confucian temple and school to teach local students in the Joseon Dynasty period.

spots.name: Ganghwa mudflat center
spots.desc: Ganghwa mud flat is the world's top five mudflat and one of the largest mudflat in Korea. This refers to the mudflats from Ganghwado Island to Sihwa Embankment in the south, centered on Yeongjongdo Island in Incheon. It is well preserved and its economic value is very high.
spots.addr: Incheon Ganghwa, on the west coast

spots.name: Sorae bridge
spots.desc: It is an attraction where visitors can see the cool sea, parks, lakes, and exhibitions all at once. You can also see the long night view bridge.

spots.name: Asiad Central Park
spots.desc: The 17th Asian Games were held in Incheon Metropolitan City from September 19 to October 4, 2014. 36 events were held. It is a plaza to celebrate this. The night view park and the ecological park are pretty. There is a nearby hotel, and it is easy to move around because it is in the center of Incheon.

spots.name: Soraepogu Fishery Market
spots.desc: Large enough to represent the Republic of Korea and has a deep history. It sells a wide variety of seafood like the Incheon Fishery Market.

spots.name: Bijarim Forest
spots.desc: A beautiful forest of old-growth nutmeg trees, accessed by flat, gravel walking paths. In the center of the forest stands a Japanese Torreya tree that is more than 800 years old, the oldest tree on Jeju. There are two connected walking paths: a short trail takes about 30 minutes and the longer loop perhaps double that.

spots.name: The Hands of Harmony
spots.desc: Well beyond POSCO lies a small fishing village called Homigot. While the beaches in this town are too rocky to be considered viable for swimming, there is a work of art worth seeing; The Hands of Living Mutually or Hands of Harmony. This is a massive bronze sculpture of a hand stretching up from the water in a small cove. A second bronze hand of equal proportion stretches up from dry land on the…

spots.name: New Millennium Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The Millennium Memorial Hall is located near Homigot and was built to commemorate the hosting of the sunrise event and to pray for the unification of Korea.

spots.name: Iga-ri Anchor observatory
spots.desc: An anchor-shaped observatory facing Dokdo. The direct distance to Dokdo is about 251 km, which contains the people's desire to protect Dokdo. It is 102 m long and 10 m high, and is famous for its sunrise. It is near Igari Beach.

spots.name: Imjingak
spots.desc: A four-storey museum and observatory 7 km south of the DMZ, with views across the Imjin River towards the DMZ and North Korea. The train line to Pyongyang passes nearby. This is the closest you can get to the DMZ without security clearance and there are regular scheduled regional trains to and from Seoul, however with only 2-4 trains per day with most of the line terminating 7 km earlier in Paju…

spots.name: Odusan Unification Observatory
spots.desc: The Odusan Unification Observatory near Paju gives visitors a clear of North Korea. Products from North Korea are also sold here. The observatory is closed for the months of December and January but is opened the rest of the year.
spots.addr: 659, Seongdong-ri, Tanhyeon-myeon, Paju-si, Gyeonggi-do, 경기도 파주시 탄현면 필승로 367

spots.name: Goseokjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: This two-story tower was established under King Jinpyeong of the Silla Kingdom. Goseokjeong Pavilion was built above a valley, surrounded by cliffs and clear, blue waters. The battlefield conservation office here is the starting point for DMZ tours.

spots.name: Woljeong-ri Station and Cheorui Samgakji observatory
spots.desc: This was a through-station before the division of the two Koreas, but now is the northernmost terminal station near the southern boundary of the DMZ. A large sign says: "The train wants to run", symbolizing the tragedy of national division. The observatory next to it has the capacity for 300 people at once. Through eight sets of high-quality binoculars visitors can view the DMZ, the Pyeonggang…

spots.name: The Second Infiltration Tunnel
spots.desc: Discovered in 1975, the Second Underground Tunnel is wide enough to allow 30,000 soldiers an hour to pass and even large armored vehicles. The tunnel has been developed into a tourist site so that visitors can tour the tunnel.

spots.name: Labor Party Building
spots.desc: Built in 1946 under fund-raising and labor forced by the North Korean government, the shelled-out carcass of a building is in Soviet-type architecture with concrete building. For security reasons, only devoted communist partisans were allowed to work within the building.

spots.name: Seungilgyo Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge that North and South Korea built together - the North completed the basic construction and two piers while the remaining parts were completely by the South. The name of the bridge is Seungilgyo after 'Seung' of the first South Korean President Syngman Rhee and 'Il' of the first North Korean President Kim Il Sung so as to commemorate the construction process.

spots.name: Punch Bowl
spots.desc: A valley in 400-500 m highlands near the coast of Yanggu-gun. American reporters dubbed this basin the punch bowl. From Dolsanryeong (between the east side and coasts in Yanggu-gun), visitors can view the beautiful panorama of the sea of fog that often hangs around the punch bowl.

spots.name: The Fourth Infiltration Tunnel
spots.desc: This is the only tunnel dug by North Korea to be discovered with motorized vehicles inside. The water flowing out from the tunnel has filtered through mountain rock, and is considered healthy enough to drink.

spots.name: Eulji Observatory Tower
spots.desc: 1,049 m above sea level, it is one of the most bitter battlegrounds of the Korean War. From the tower, visitors can see the checkpoint and farms in North Korea and four peaks including Birobong, the highest in the Geumgangsan Diamond Mountains.
spots.addr: Hyeon2-ri, Haean-myeon, Yanggu-gun, Gangwon-do, 강원 양구군 해안면 땅꿀로

spots.name: Goseong Unification Observatory
spots.desc: As the observatory closest to North Korea and the northernmost point of South Korea, more than one million people visit this area on an annual basis. Visitors can see the Geumgangsan (Diamond Mountains) and the Haegeumgang in North Korea, with the naked eye, and unlike many other observatories, photographs are allowed everywhere. In the observatory North Korean food products are for sale, and the…
spots.addr: 457, Tongiljeonmangdae-ro, Hyeonnae-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do 강원도 고성군 현내면 통일전망대로 457

spots.name: Maritime Museum
spots.desc: At the entrance of Hwajinpo Beach, the Maritime Museum exhibits 40,000 articles of 1,500 types of shellfish, corals and fossils, some of which are very rare.

spots.name: Summerhouse of Kim Il Sung
spots.desc: The house is embedded in a cliff where you can have a bird's eye view of the beautiful Hwajinpo beach. There is an exhibition of Kim Il Sung's personal belongings including furniture. On the stairs up to the summerhouse, photos are displayed of Kim Jeong-il during his early days.

spots.name: The War Memorial of Korea
spots.desc: The original headquarters of the South Korean infantry, this is now a large museum dedicated to the Korean War over 8 exhibits.
spots.addr: 29 Itaewon-ro, Yongsan-gu, Seoul 서울특별시 용산구 이태원로 29 (용산동1가)

spots.name: DMZ Jangdankong Cafe
spots.desc: (6 of 15 Coffee & Tea Spots) Security tourism is possible by calling the restaurant in Unification Village a day before on the premise of visiting the restaurant and obtaining prior permission through 'Yetong'. (notifying the military in advance) You must bring your resident registration card and foreigner passport to pass through the military area.

spots.name: Daemyung Resort Seorak Aqua World
spots.desc: Daemyung Resort Sorak’s most recognizable facility is the 1.6 Hot Spring Theme Park. It has various hot spring baths, including a high-tech bath that provides different massages with different flows of hot spring water, an outdoor bath, a Jasmine bath, a pine tree bath (Hinoki bath), and others. Sorak Aqua World also provides special attractions, such as an outdoor recreational pool surrounded by…

spots.name: Seorak Pine Resort
spots.desc: Garden Spa, an outdoor bath of Seorak Pine Resort, is equipped with various hot spring baths, high-tech sauna and massage rooms, and a world-class indoor pool. It is well-known for hot spring baths that use various herbs, such as green tea, angelica, mint, and many more, a “lover’s bath” scented with lemon, and a waterfall bath that provides massages under natural waterfalls.

spots.name: Yeongwol Danjong Festival
spots.desc: The Ministry of Culture and Tourism gave a special designation to the Yeongwol Danjong Festival. It is held to console the spirits of King Danjong, whose life ended in a tragedy after exile by King Sejo, the sixth king of the Joseon Dynasty, and his followers who sacrificed their lives. The festival starts with a commemorative funeral followed by a parade honoring King Danjong's life, and a…

spots.name: Hoengseong Hanu Festival
spots.desc: Hoengseong is famous for Korean beef (Hanu), made from cattle who are easy to breed in this climate. You can enjoy the taste of Hanu and also buy it. There are also many other thing to do at the festival. For example, you can wear traditional Korean costumes and enjoy a foot bath.

spots.name: Oakvalley ski resort
spots.desc: Ski and golf resort with three types of slope. There are 2 slopes of beginner level, 5 slopes of normal level and 2 slopes of expert level. Oakvalley resort manages ski school and snow board school. Thare is also Sledding slope for children, woh can not do ski or snow board.

spots.name: Alpensia Resort
spots.desc: Open year-round. You can enjoy ski slopes as well as a golf course and an indoor water park, staying in luxurious accommodation. It hosts skiing events for the 2018 Winter Olympic Games.

spots.name: Chuncheon National Museum
spots.desc: It exhibits and preserves heritage from the region that encompasses epochs from the prehistoric era to modern times.

spots.name: Gangwon Provincial Arboretum
spots.desc: Includes Four seasons botanical garden Forest museum with Korean and partly English texts.

spots.name: Chuncheon International Mime Festival
spots.desc: A globally renowned art performance festival in Korea. The main event consists of performances of international and domestic mime groups, and there are special events such as street performances, mime lessons, body painting shows, and mime concerts throughout the festival period.
spots.hours: Starts Wed of the fourth week in May and lasts for five days

spots.name: Nami Island
spots.desc: A moon-shaped island of 4 km in diameter, resulting from the construction of a dam in 1944. Great nature, with metasequoias. You can enter this island by boat, taking less 10 min. If you enter the island, you can see huge nut pines along the both paths. It is full of green, very nice for holiday spot. You can also hire a bicycle or tandem for 30 min or more, it is good way to get around whole…

spots.name: Jangjeolgongshin Sungkyum General Tomb Station
spots.desc: This is the site of the tomb of General Shin Sung-gyeom, who contributed to the reunification of the Later Three Kingdoms by helping King Taejo of the Goryeo Dynasty. Along with the general's tomb, the tombstone and monuments honoring his achievements are included.

spots.name: Statue of Lady Soyanggang
spots.desc: It was built in the 1970s to celebrate the popular song 'Soyanggang Maiden.' The statue is a sculpture of the main character of the song, 'Soyanggang Maiden.'

spots.name: Soyang River Dam Completion Memorial Tower
spots.desc: Completed in 1973, it is the nation's largest sandstone dam. It was built for flood control, water supply, and hydroelectric power in the Han River basin.

spots.name: Uiamhryu Inseok Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The facility was established to commemorate the life and achievements of Ryu In-seok (Yoo In-seok), the commander of the righteous army in the late Joseon Dynasty. It displays Ryu In-seok's relics and materials related to his activities and is used as an educational space to convey the meaning and spirit of the independence movement he left behind.

spots.name: Statues of Mermaids in Uiamho Lake
spots.desc: A sculpture built around Uiam Lake, the statue was installed to add to the local symbolism and tourist attraction. It symbolizes the connection between water and nature.

spots.name: Soyang River Skywalk
spots.desc: The total length is 174m, and the floor is 156m long with transparent tempered glass. A circular square is formed at the end of the bridge, and the floor is made of transparent glass in the center of the circular square. There is an observation deck on both sides of the square that extends like wings, and if you stand in the center of the end of the square, you can see the statue of the mandarin…

spots.name: Legoland Korea Resort
spots.desc: The first Legoland theme park in South Korea (and the 2nd largest in Asia behind Legoland Malaysia Resort), Legoland Korea features eight themed areas with over 75 interactive rides, shows, and attractions, all built with more than 85 million Lego bricks. The resort's Miniland, a signature Legoland attraction globally, features Lego replicas of various urban landscapes, historical landmarks and…

spots.name: Jungdo (Island)
spots.desc: A large island on the Soyang River. A ferry runs to the island every half hour. Fare is ₩5,500 per adult. The island makes a great day trip or picnic. You can hike around and see ancient Korean huts, or rent bikes and ride a paved trail that goes around one side of the island. Bike rental is approximately ₩10,000 per hour. Surrey bikes and four wheelers are also available to rent. The island has…

spots.name: Soyang Dam
spots.desc: At the head of the Soyang river. Built in 1973, Soyang Dam is Asia's largest gravel dam. Soyang Lake was formed while the dam was being constructed and lies across Chuncheon, Yanggu and Inje. It is called the "ocean within the land", and forms an ideal driving course for its open panorama and beautiful scenery. There is a ferryboat trip to Yanggu, a popular dating course. Boat rides are available…

spots.name: Hiking
spots.desc: Chuncheon sits in a valley surrounded by mountains. Bong Ui Mountain is a famous peak just north of Myongdong (Downtown Chuncheon) and sits just south of the Soyang river. Trails lead to the top from all sides of the mountain, and there is exercise equipment on top. It is not a very tall peak, but makes for a good hike. Its elevation is approximately 280 m (925 ft), next to the Soyang River which…

spots.name: Statue Park
spots.desc: A park with many marble statues and a building which contains and replica of an ancient Korean water clock. A small store provides bike rentals and across the street are docks where you can rent paddle boats on the river. The river feeds into the Soyang and from there you can see Jungdo island. The Ethiopian war memorial is adjacent to this park.

spots.name: Gangchon Ski Resort
spots.desc: It is approximately 30 minutes drive from downtown Chuncheon. A free shuttle runs from Chuncheon to the ski resort.

spots.name: Cheongpyeong-sa Temple
spots.desc: Cheongpyeong Temple is South Korea's National Treasure No. 164 is a Buddhist temple dating back to reign of King Gwang-Jong (949-975). Tucked away in a valley between two mountains, it sits at the southern ridge of Mount Bong. The walk up to Cheongpyong Temple is one of Korea's most beautiful walks. Surrounded by woods, clean air and a beautiful stream with many waterfalls, the walk up to the…
spots.price: Adults ₩5,000, youth ₩5,000, children ₩3,000 including ferry charge
spots.addr: The ferry leaves from Soyang Dam

spots.name: Chuncheon Myeongdong Street
spots.desc: A small street, splendid for shopping. There are stores on both sides of the lane. It is dubbed the "street of the young people" since you can always find clothes and culture that are in fashion.

spots.name: Chuncheon Barbecue Spicy Chicken Street
spots.desc: Chuncheon barbecue spicy chicken is almost better known than Chuncheon itself. Many chicken restaurants each boasting to be the original. The savory smell of the cuisine attracts passers-by.

spots.name: University Street
spots.desc: A 900-meter street at the back of Gangwon University in the "city of education," Chuncheon. Many interesting stores and cafes.

spots.name: Chuncheon Underground Shopping Complex
spots.desc: A huge underground shopping complex under City Hall. This is a one-stop shopping mall where you can compare prices and get a nice bargain.

spots.name: Gangchon
spots.desc: A popular membership-training site for college students. Gangchon is called the heaven for bike trekking. It is very close from Seoul, 40 minutes by train, a favorite weekend vacation spot because of the amusement parks, hostels and the new Gangchon resort.

spots.name: Gongjicheon
spots.desc: A favorite resort spot for citizens of Chuncheon; it is said that spring has come to Chuncheon when the ice of Gongjicheon melts and boat lovers come out. You can enjoy biking and boating on the weekends. Covered wagons in the vicinity are full of people until late at night.

spots.name: Emart
spots.desc: The closest thing to a Walmart equivalent, Emart is a large shopping center with most everything you might need. The lower level is a food court and grocery center, the second level a department store and additional levels for parking. Emart is located on the south side of Chuncheon.

spots.name: GS Mart
spots.desc: A bit smaller than Emart, GS mart provides much of the same in terms of product and pricing. GS Mart also has a food court upstairs that includes a McDonald's. Some local Koreans seem to prefer GS Mart due to its "cleaner" and less crowded nature, but it doesn't offer as large of a selection of groceries and household goods as Emart. GS Mart can be found in Seoksadong on the east side of…

spots.name: Home Plus
spots.desc: It's E-mart's major competitor throughout Korea. It is, for the most part, exactly like Wal-mart or E-mart. It has all essentials you could ever need packed into one, four story building. Produce, groceries, electronics, hardware, homeware, kitchenware, beauty products, cleaning supplies...obviously the list goes on. If you live in Toegye-dong it's the best and probably closest mart you can get…

spots.name: Hajukol
spots.desc: This upscale restaurant in the far eastern part of Chuncheon's urban area serves lunch for around ₩18,000 per person. The set meal comes with many courses, appealing visually as well as taste-wise.

spots.name: Peace of Mind Bakery and Book Cafe
spots.desc: This cafe is filled with so many books, it can be considered a library. They serve bread as side dishes and offer steak, Italian food, and special teas. Before one leaves, the customer has the option to purchase baked snacks to go (like cookies) and special teas. In the background soothing music is played from a satellite service. The owner of the shop is a gentleman who speaks fluent English and…

spots.name: Vips
spots.desc: A Western-style buffet with a Korean twist. Here the customer can order steak, an all-you-can-eat salad bar (with free drinks included), tacos, fried chicken, and more. In the background, American music plays.

spots.name: Chuncheon log house dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken)
spots.desc: You need to wait for a good restaurant up to the third store. Dakgalbi makguksu is also delicious.

spots.name: EARTH17
spots.desc: Located along the Soyang River in Sinbuk-eup, Chuncheon, this large-scale café features a spacious outdoor lawn with scenic river views. The facility offers outdoor beanbag seating as well as a second-floor music-listening lounge designated as an adult-only zone. While providing distinct riverside views and outdoor spaces, the menu items and desserts are relatively high-priced.

spots.name: Gamzabatt
spots.desc: Located near Earth17 along the Soyang River in Chuncheon, this popular bakery café is famous for its signature potato-shaped bread (Gamja-ppang). The venue features a rustic, pet-friendly outdoor garden alongside indoor seating and sells various themed merchandise alongside its baked goods.

spots.name: Potatoflower studio
spots.desc: In the village of Pyeongchang, Gangwon Province, a small village in Pyeongchang, Gangwon Province, a flower village called it was built to repair a small school called Nosan school, which was enclosed in the middle of a beautiful mountain village. The school has turned into an exhibition hall, a library, a museum, and a dining room.

spots.name: Pyeongchang Freshwater Fish Museum
spots.desc: After a plan for building a dam in Dong River was canceled, it was established in 2009 to promote the region. You can learn about fishes living in the river.

spots.name: Lee Seung-bok Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The Lee Seung-bok Memorial Hall is in Nodong-ri, Yongpyeong-myeon to memorialize Lee Seung-bok who was a South Korean boy murdered by North Korean commandos in 1968. It was established in 1982, with building a memorial statue for Lee. Lee's house was restored in 2000.

spots.name: Jeonggangwon
spots.local: Traditional Korea Cuisine Experience Center (한국전통음식 문화체험관)
spots.desc: Jeonggangwon was established with the aim of doing research on the value and excellence of Korea's traditional food culture, distributing and publicizing the Korean traditional food culture into the world. It is operated to make it possible for visitors to learn and experience the Korean traditional food culture, and Jeonggangwon is the place where visitors can feel the beauty native to Korea…

spots.name: Eoreumchi Village
spots.desc: The township in the clean nature is beautiful with mountain scenery and valley made up of the meandering river and rock stratum. You can enjoy various water sports such as rafting, kayaking, skyline, etc., and you can enjoy stunning stalagmites in Baekryong Cave, Natural Monument 260, a limestone cave.

spots.name: Hyoseok Cultural Town
spots.desc: The town is a tourist attraction as the background of the novel, When Bucketwheet Flowers Blossom (1967). Each year the festival will be held here in late summer, late August early September. (cf. 2016 Hyoseok Cultural Festival).

spots.name: Pyeongchang Hyoseok Culture Festival
spots.desc: Lee Hyoseok, one of the greatest authors of modern Korean literature, holds the festival at Pyeongchang, the actual stage of the story, When the Buckwheat Flowers Bloom. During the festival, visitors can also enjoy the special ambiance created by the prolific buckwheat flowers.

spots.name: Fun Ski Festival
spots.desc: A ski festival for foreign visitors in Yongpyeong Resort, the heart of Korean skiing. For three nights and four days, participants enjoy ski lessons, dinners and various events. On the last day, all participants take part in a ski competition. Many foreigners participate in this romantic winter festival every year to enjoy the snow, skiing and parties.
spots.hours: Early December to early March, around seven times

spots.name: Pyeongchang Trout Festival
spots.desc: Every year, Pyeongchang hosts the trout festival from the end of December to the end of January. Trout are considered to be a speciality of PyeongChang because they are the first fish to be farmed. At the festival, visitors can experience the fishing tent, ice fishing, and catching trout bare-handed. Fishing equipment and convenience tools can be purchased at the site. It also offers a variety of…

spots.name: Daegwalryeong Snow Festival
spots.desc: This celebrates the region's snow with fireworks, an ice art contest, ice-fishing, and an international marathon.

spots.name: Daegwallyeong Sky ranch
spots.desc: Sky Ranch is a representative ranch of the Daegwallyeong composed in 1974.
spots.price: Admission fee: child ₩ 4,000, adults ₩ 5,000 + additional charges

spots.name: Daegwallyeong Sheep Farm
spots.desc: This ranch is the only place where sheep are raised, although there are many ranches in the region. Visitors can see the sheep along a circular walkway, or give a hay to them.

spots.name: Herbnara Tourist Farm
spots.desc: This is a famous dating course. More than 100 types of herbs thrive in the garden and herb restaurants here serve tasty and healthy food.
spots.addr: 291-42, Heungjeonggyegok-gil, Bongpyeong-myeon, Pyeongchang, 강원 평창군 봉평면 흥정계곡길 291-42

spots.name: Korea Botanic Garden
spots.desc: Widely varying flowers and plants can be seen in the Korea Botanic Garden. Flowers bloom from spring to autumn in the wild flower community, a perfect place to take a photograph.
spots.addr: 405-2, Byeongnae-ri, Daegwallyeong-myeon, Pyeongchang 강원도 평창군 대관령면 비안길 159-4 (대관령면)

spots.name: Pyeongchang Olympic Market
spots.desc: Pyeongchang Olympic Market has been in business since 1955. It is in southern Pyeongchang. It is famous for buckwheat fry dish which over the past 40 years has been made the traditional way by directly grinding buckwheat.

spots.name: Bongpyung Traditional Market
spots.desc: Bongpyeongjang is the 5-day market which is open on the 2nd and 7th days. Buckwheat noodles, buckwheat pancakes, buckwheat muk, potato rice cakes, Tadpole noodles are sold in Bongpyung Traditional Market.

spots.name: Jinbu Market
spots.desc: Jinbu Market will be held in the 3rd and 8th days of the old bus terminal. Junbu Market is the biggest figure in the Pyeongchang. they sell alpine vegetables, various kinds of Seasoned vegetables in mountain, medicinal herbs.

spots.name: Bongpyeongwon
spots.desc: Buckwheat store in Pyeongchang, Bongpyeongwon sell buckwheat flour, buckwheat rice, buckwheat noodles, buckwheat tea, buckwheat cookies and buckwheat fried flour.

spots.name: Pyeongchang Farm
spots.desc: Pc Farm sells excellent agricultural products. You can buy seasoned vegetables, deodeok, kimchis, potatoes, etc.

spots.name: Youngchun garden
spots.desc: A famous restaurant for own growing Korean traditional chicken and Korean ogol chicken cuisine (Hangul:오골계, Korean traditional black chicken). also famous for a stewed chicken with oriental medicinal herbs. ₩20,000 per person and more.
spots.addr: 3591-10 chang ri, seo-dong ro, mee-tan myeon, Pyeongchang, gangwon

spots.name: Paldo Myeon Ga
spots.desc: A Korean traditional restaurant, that opened in 1980. Located nearby the Olympic market. A Buckwheat (Hangul: 막국수, Makgooksu), Spicy Stir-fried Chicken, a broiled eels are famous. Avoiding the artificial seasoning, only using a Korean traditional seasoning, natural herbs, local speciality. ₩10,000 per person and more.

spots.name: Ansan Olympic Museum
spots.desc: There is a fitness center. Many local people work out in the gym.

spots.name: Glass Island
spots.desc: This island is famous for the Daebudo Glass Island Museum, which includes a glass art gallery, showcase and outdoor sculpture park.

spots.name: Seongpo Arts Park
spots.desc: Seongpo Arts Park adjoins a residential area, so it is a good resting place for locals.

spots.name: Starlight Village Photo Land
spots.desc: A place full of colorful light exhibitions, you can take various photos of memories.

spots.name: Damunhwa street
spots.desc: One of Ansan's most vibrant urban centers, where you can experience a unique atmosphere of diverse cultures. The street was naturally formed as foreign workers and immigrants from countries such as China, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, and Thailand began to settle here in the late 1990s.

spots.name: Tando Fishing Village
spots.desc: A place where you can catch various creatures such as crabs and conch in the tidal flat.

spots.name: Sunset observatory
spots.desc: A place where you can see the red sunset with the beautiful sea..

spots.name: Paper art museum
spots.desc: It is the first paper-making art museum in Korea. It has a children's art museum, a traditional play experience center, a hanok experience center, and a craft making experience center.

spots.name: Gyeonggi Maritime Safety Experience Center
spots.desc: A place where people can experience various experiences related to marine safety.

spots.name: Ansan World Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: Experience center where you can feel the culture of various countries

spots.name: Ansan Industrial History Museum
spots.desc: Ansan Industrial History Museum (Gyeonggi-do Registered Cultural Property Recognized for Value)
spots.addr: Ansan Industrial History Museum, 265, Hwarang-ro, Danwon-gu

spots.name: Wol-pi Art Library
spots.desc: On the first floor, there is an art lounge, children's archives, silver bookshelf; on the second floor, art, comprehensive archives, digital corners; and on the third floor, there is a club room and lounge.

spots.name: Ansan Yeoremio Festival
spots.desc: A representative summer festival. Various participatory programs such as music concerts are provided.

spots.name: Daebu Grape Festival
spots.desc: A biennial festival, usually held in September in every other year. You can make wine and participate in a photographic contest.

spots.name: Moonlight Festival in Wol-pi
spots.desc: It is a representative festival in Wolpi-dong that everyone enjoys based on harmony and communication among local residents. It is a rich festival full of food, things to see and enjoy by operating various experience booths and food booths such as work presentations, exhibitions, magic, and balloon art.

spots.name: Urban Regeneration Street Culture Festival
spots.desc: Urban Regeneration Street Culture Festival is a street culture festival specializing in public design. You can enjoy busking, performances, and various experience booths.

spots.name: Flying
spots.desc: Due to Ansan's location along the sea and the surrounding islands, there are a number of companies that offer test flights in light and ultra-light airplanes for an hour or so, including views of most of the nearby islands. These usually cost somewhere around ₩80,000 depending on the duration of the flight.

spots.name: Biking
spots.desc: Bike paths exist throughout Ansan, making it more bicycle friendly than the average city. Bicycles can be hired from Gojan and Jungang stations. Bicycle stations are gradually increasing. There is a dedicated cycle road with picnic benches beyond the Lake Park that run alongside the river and terminates at Ansan Waterfowl park. Ansan's public bike service is called 'Pedalro'.

spots.name: Ansan Lake Park
spots.desc: It has various facilities such as nature learning center, soccer field, basketball court, volleyball court, inline skating link and so on. Especially, reed marsh and waterside square is good for walking. At the center of the square, you can see outdoor performances. Also, Ansan Lake Park has theme spaces such as wild flower garden and lilac hill.

spots.name: Ansan Slide Park
spots.desc: In summer season, water sled slope is open. Besides, there are some water pools to have fun and have an air slide. In winter season, snow sled slope is open. It has a main slope, slope for children and a hand sled area. The hand sled area is for children. The sled is drawn by their parents whereas other sled slide from high. Moving walkway is available just in winter season.

spots.name: Wadong park
spots.desc: This urban neighborhood park is also known as Wadong Sports Park. Wadong Park houses an indoor gymnasium, which is used as the exclusive stadium for the Ansan Shinhan Bank basketball team.

spots.name: Starlight Park
spots.desc: Starlight Park is a small, natural park with well-maintained walking trails.

spots.name: Mega Box Ansan Jungang
spots.desc: 6 screens and 371 of seating capacity. All seats are recliner.

spots.name: Lotte Mart Ansan
spots.desc: This is a large supermarket that includes a variety of facilities such as a food court and various beauty stores.

spots.name: Ansan Multicultural Food Street
spots.desc: A vibrant dining area featuring authentic dishes from over 20 countries, including Vietnamese pho, Chinese lamb skewers (양꼬치), Indonesian rendang, Russian bakery items, and Uzbek plov.

spots.name: New York Burger
spots.desc: Although the restaurant is called “New York Burger,” the flavors are actually more suited to Korean tastes, giving the burgers a Korean take on the classic New York-style burger.It’s a popular spot among students at Hanyang University ERICA, especially for grabbing a quick burger after class. One burger alone might not be enough for a full meal, so adding fries or a drink can make it more filling.

spots.name: Sanduri Bibim-guksu, Ansan Branch (산두리비빔국수 안산점)
spots.desc: A place where you can enjoy spicy bibim-guksu served in a refreshing mulhoe-style broth.

spots.name: Meal PlanB
spots.desc: This restaurant is in front of Hanyang University. It is famous for Mexican food, especially burritos.

spots.name: DosMas
spots.desc: This restaurant is in front of Hanyang University. It serves Mexican food, especially burritos. Customers can add different ingredients to their burritos.

spots.name: Lotteria
spots.desc: Korean fast food restaurant at the station.Lotteria is like a Korean McDonald's or Burger King. There are dozens of other Lotteria outlets in the town.

spots.name: Alchon
spots.desc: One of the busiest restaurants in front of the Hanyang University. If you order, the food you ordered comes out very quickly, so you can enjoy your meal even if you don't have enough time to eat something. The dish of Alchon is relatively cheaper than other restaurants nearby the Hanyang University.

spots.name: Warm Table
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant serving set meals, including spicy pork with rolled omelet (jeyuk and gyeran-mari jeongsik) and beef seaweed soup (soegogi miyeokguk). Meals are served with rice and side dishes.

spots.name: Sigol Hongdukke Kalguksu
spots.desc: This is a kalguksu restaurant in Ansan where you can enjoy a hearty meal at an affordable price. It has the atmosphere of an old-established restaurant and is very popular with the local residents nearby. Before the meal, barley rice and various kinds of kimchi are served, so you can make and eat a simple bibimbap. If you want to try local food at a long-established Korean restaurant at an…

spots.name: Ansan bulgogi house
spots.desc: This is a Korean-style barbecued beef restaurant. It also serves a lot of delicious chicken.

spots.name: Kantipur
spots.desc: It's an Indian cuisine restaurant. This restaurant is found across the street from Ansan Station, in Asia Town. Once across the street, walk 3 blocks further, directly away from the station, and look to your right. It is on the second floor, above a shoe shop and cell phone store. A variety of Indian and Nepalese dishes are served. The curries start at ₩7,000 and 4 samosas make up an order.

spots.name: Shinsun Seolnongtang
spots.desc: Seolleongtang is Korea traditional soup which is boiled from ox’s bones.

spots.name: Namwol
spots.desc: This restaurant is found across the street from Hanyang University. This is a Vietnamese restaurant. The popular Vietnamse dish, pho, is very delicious.

spots.name: Yellow Chicken
spots.desc: This restaurant sells roasted chicken and beer. It tastes pretty good.

spots.name: Earthen wall cheonggukjang boiled barley
spots.desc: This restaurant sells traditional Korean food like cheonggukjang (fast-fermented bean paste) boiled barley, and bulgogi (barbecued beef).

spots.name: Pizzeria
spots.desc: Delicious pizza at reasonable prices, Russian menus and guides are also available.

spots.name: Jelly Factory
spots.desc: You can enjoy JokBal (Korean dish of pig's trotters cooked with soy sauce). There are several JokBal like Jokbal, Jelly Jokbal (which is softer than original Jokbal), Spiced Jokbal.

spots.name: Pepperoni Button
spots.desc: Pizza specialized restaurant. It serves various kind of pizza and is famous for pepperoni pizza.

spots.name: Dokebiking
spots.desc: This is the only pork back bone stew restaurant in front of Hanyang University at Ansan. It does not close except for holidays. It is always crowded with many people visiting even at late hours. It's best to call ahead and ask for a table, as there may not be any available in the evening.

spots.name: HwaJungLi Makguksu
spots.desc: A restaurant that sells cold buckwheat noodles. It also appeared on TV in Korea

spots.name: Son Mi-myeong Tae Hang Gu
spots.desc: It is famous for its delicious braised pollack soy sauce and grilled fish.

spots.name: Sarangbang
spots.desc: It is famous for its own butchered beef restaurant. Not only beef, but other menus are also delicious.

spots.name: In the Viet
spots.desc: A Vietnamese restaurant specializing in pho. In addition to the typical soup-based pho, you can also enjoy a variety of other Vietnamese dishes, such as Banh Xeo, Bun Cha, and fried pho.

spots.name: Gangneung Original Gyodong Jjamppong
spots.desc: A Korean-Chinese restaurant serving jjamppong (seafood noodle soup) and gan-jjajang (stir-fried black bean noodles).

spots.name: Yonghodong Nakji NC Gojan Branch
spots.desc: It serves Korean seafood dishes, including nakgopsae (octopus with intestine and shrimp), jianhae (fresh octopus stew), and hot-plate octopus with rice.

spots.name: Sushi Tenkai
spots.desc: A conveyor-belt sushi restaurant serving a variety of sushi. Diners can take plates from the belt or order special rolls and sashimi from the chefs.

spots.name: Chef Cha Sung-jin's ChaCha Sushi
spots.desc: A sushi restaurant. The restaurant offers set menus at lunchtime with a choice of udon or soba. A self-serve bar provides tea, plum drinks, salad, and seaweed porridge.

spots.name: Onsen
spots.desc: A Japanese-style casual restaurant serving donburi (rice bowls) and tempura dishes. Menu items include onsen tamago don, tendon, and katsudon.

spots.name: Gyukatsu Jeong
spots.desc: A Japanese-style restaurant specializing in gyukatsu, a breaded beef cutlet served rare inside. Set meals include rice, miso soup, and side dishes, and the meat can be grilled on personal hot plates.

spots.name: Mentsuru
spots.desc: A Japanese noodle restaurant serving abura soba (soupless oil noodles) and tsukemen (dipping noodles).

spots.name: Mirak restaurant
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant serving dwaeji duruchigi (spicy stir-fried pork), bulnak jeongol (beef and octopus hot pot), kimchi jjigae(kimchi stew), and doenjang jjigae(soybean paste stew).

spots.name: Hwinichiro
spots.desc: A Japanese-style ramen restaurant serving tonkotsu ramen, tsukemen, gyoza, and mini rice bowls such as gyudon and butadon.

spots.name: Yeongwolae gondre
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant serving stir-fried spicy pork, grilled mackerel, seasoned cockles, and gondre rice. Additional side dishes and desserts such as sikhye, plum tea, and barley bread are available at a self-serve bar.

spots.name: Danwon Korean Table d'hote
