spots.desc: You can enjoy Aruncus dioicus from Ulleungdo Island, bamboo shoot from Damyang, soybean paste from Sunchang and so on.

spots.name: Matchandeul Wang Sogeum Gui Ansan Jungang Branch
spots.desc: A Korean barbecue restaurant serving thick-cut pork belly grilled over charcoal with coarse salt.

spots.name: Chonggak Super
spots.desc: A Korean barbecue restaurant serving thinly sliced frozen pork belly (naengdong samgyeopsal) made from Jeju pork. Side dishes include cheonggukjang, minari, and fried rice cooked on the same pan.

spots.name: sushi juyeon
spots.desc: It offers a variety of menus, such as the main omakase assortment and lunch set, especially the lunch set is highly cost-effective and is recommended as a lunch spot. Inside, there are about 10 seats in the form of counter seats, and you can enjoy your meal in a neat and comfortable atmosphere.

spots.name: eccentric tripe
spots.desc: It is a famous restaurant that offers a variety of grilled menus such as gopchang, makchang, and yeotong. There are also high-end menus such as Korean beef tripe, Korean beef tripe, and raw beef, and you can enjoy various parts at once with assorted grilled meat.

spots.name: The taste of the four seasons
spots.desc: It is a good restaurant where you can taste fresh seafood such as natural croaker and extra-large yellowtail. blue crab bibimbap and briquette-grilled bulgogi are also popular menus, especially briquette-grilled bulgogi, which has a lively taste of fire, making it good to enjoy with rice. With its spacious interior and room facilities, it is suitable for family gatherings or group dinners, and…

spots.name: Mongmame (몽마메)
spots.desc: Bistro serving pasta, steak, salads and small plates, with wine and beer. Reservations and queueing via the Catch Table app. Free 2-hour parking in the Polytown garage. Located in the side street between Polytown buildings A and B.
spots.addr: 10, A-dong, Polytown, 130 Gwangdeok-daero, Danwon-gu, Ansan-si, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea (In the side street between Polytown buildings A and B. The…

spots.name: Jungang Station area
spots.desc: The Jungang Station area features many traditional Korean restaurants as well as many familiar chains such as Mr Pizza, Viking, VIPS, Kraze Burger, Papa Johns, Krispe Kreme, Baskin Robbins, Coldstone etc.

spots.name: Radio
spots.desc: Regular holidays are every Thursday, A cafe with a pretty view over the park

spots.name: To Presso
spots.desc: To presso is a dessert cafe near by the Hanyang University. To presso sells a variety of drinks and ice flakes with syrup.

spots.name: Fashion Design Cafe
spots.desc: Delicious coffee and comfortable sofa. It consists of 1st floor, 2nd floor, and rooftop.

spots.name: Momo Coffee
spots.desc: You can enjoy coffee and other drink as ice-tea, be able to drink at a relatively low price

spots.name: Caesar Coffee
spots.desc: Many students visit to work on assignments and study. A menu called "Ice Age" is the Caesar coffee's signature menu.

spots.name: PROSCONS
spots.desc: There is a large space in the basement of the cafe where students come to study or work on team projects (assignments).

spots.name: Baek Geumdang
spots.desc: -Cafe with delicious soufflé pancakes -Free parking, kids welcome, all menu items made in store -For more information, please call the store.

spots.name: Village Shop Life
spots.desc: Sell books, flowers, and coffee. They also sell used goods on consignment. In addition, they plan and run programs for the local community.

spots.name: AP coffee&bakery
spots.desc: This is a bakery cafe that sells bagels. There are many desks that are easy to study. It is also a space where cultural activities such as books, LPs, music, and lectures are conducted.

spots.name: Proscons west
spots.desc: A cafe near Hanyang University ERICA serving bread, coffee, and other drinks.

spots.name: Blooming Day
spots.desc: It is a cafe that sells delicious drinks and macarons. The interior with a comfortable atmosphere stands out.

spots.name: Cafe of the Day
spots.desc: Delicious drinks, desserts, and comfortable interiors stand out.

spots.name: Cafe Maru
spots.desc: It is about 100 m away from the front gate of Hanyang University's Erica Campus toward Seokho Shopping Center.

spots.name: Mel coffee Ansan Jungang
spots.desc: This is a hands-on cafe where you can enjoy drinks and desserts while painting. When you order a drink, you receive a palette, brushes, and a water cup, which you can use to color a postcard with your desired design. They offer a variety of drinks, including strawberry lattes, Earl Grey chocolate lattes, and homemade lemonade, as well as seasonal dessert menus.

spots.name: HOWDY
spots.desc: A café in central Ansan serving homemade cakes, lattes, and kaymak, a creamy milk spread.

spots.name: Cuore Espresso
spots.desc: A coffee shop serving espresso-based drinks, including espresso, flat white, and hand-drip coffee. The menu also includes desserts such as ice-cream croffle.

spots.name: Cafe P&P
spots.desc: A café serving drinks such as black-sesame cream latte and cinnamon latte, along with seasonal desserts.

spots.name: Rim Coffee
spots.desc: A café serving coffee and handcrafted beverages. Seasonal desserts and pastries are also available.

spots.name: 5: am milktea
spots.desc: A place to experience Chinese-style milk tea in Korea, with indoor seating and a selection of Chinese-style desserts available in addition to drinks.

spots.name: Koino Coffee
spots.desc: The café offers several choices of coffee beans, including fruity and nutty blends, as well as a decaffeinated option. Hand-drip coffee, espresso-based drinks, signature beverages, and desserts are available. Roasted coffee beans can also be purchased.

spots.name: Full House
spots.desc: Full House is a cozy cafe located in Gojan-dong. At this cafe, you can enjoy a variety of parfaits that change every season. However, some reviews mention that compared to the expensive price of 8,000 won, the taste of the parfait is not particularly special. In addition, menu prices, including drinks, are generally on the higher side. While there is a wide variety of bakery items including whole…

spots.name: Goyang Aram Nuri Arts Center
spots.desc: Meaning a large and beautiful world in Korean, Aram Nuri features Aram Playhouse, Aram Concert Hall, Saerasae Theater, Norumok Outdoor Theater, Aram Art Gallery and a library that offer best quality facilities and services for cultural events.

spots.name: Goyang Oulim Nuri Arts Center
spots.desc: As the largest culture/sports center in the Seoul metropolitan area, Goyang Oulim Nuri offers various cultural experience at its playhouse, theater and art gallery. The center also offers various sports facilities, including a main stadium built to international standards, an ice rink and an indoor swimming pool.

spots.name: Lafesta
spots.desc: A complex commercial district in Goyang-si Ilsan. Sector A, B, C, D, E, F are connected each other. There are a lot of stores, cafe, restaurants, theater, and offices. Lafesta forms a central commercial district in Goyang-si. Also it is close to the Lake Park, KINTEX so it is convenient to get around.

spots.name: Goyang Stadium
spots.desc: A multi-purpose stadium with a capacity of 41,311 people in Goyang City. It is the home stadium of the Goyang Citizens' Soccer Team, but they also held game of the Korean national soccer team and several artists concerts.

spots.name: Hanwha aqua planet Ilsan
spots.desc: It is a 4,300-ton large aquarium located in Ilsan. It is the largest aquarium near Seoul and the first structure to combine an aquarium and an indoor zoo in Korea. In total, it can see 325 kinds of marine and land animals.

spots.name: Goyang International Flower Festival
spots.desc: Goyang International Flower Festival is one of the largest flower festivals in South Korea. It is held every year around May. This Flower Festival is considered as good model for local culture festivals, in which various foreign flower farmers participate.

spots.name: Baedagol Theme Park
spots.desc: Baedagol is a theme park focused on lotus and colored carp purifying water and maintaining ecological balance. You can experience traditional handicraft culture of our ancestors being forgotten, taking a sniff at earth. Activities –Making carp necklace, wooden carp, experiencing doctor fish, ecological experience.

spots.name: Seonyurang Village Farm Experience
spots.desc: The village surrounded by ranges of Mt. Bukhan like a folding screen is 600 years old and boasts of beautiful scenery as indicated by its name meaning ‘a place where Taoist hermits relax’. Activities – getting your feet soaked in water in a rice paddy containing red clay, making pressed flowers, making ddeok or Korean rice cake and historical experience etc.

spots.name: Ilsan Children’s observatory
spots.desc: People can observe through high-resolution astronomical telescope stars and planets shining in the night sky

spots.name: Kimchi School
spots.desc: This place is for foreigners only to experience Kimchi. The facility has a photo zone where foreigners can wear traditional Korean garments and have them photographed. A place where they can make Kimchi and pack it is also made available. They also can buy various souvenirs here and the place has become one of the hottest tourist attractions. Activities – Making Kimchi, Wearing traditional…

spots.name: Heunguksa Temple Stay
spots.desc: About 1,300 years ago during the reign of King Munmu of Shilla, Weonhyo, the Buddhist monk of highest virtue established the Heungseongam (a small temple or hermitage). After that, the temple was renamed Heungguksa Temple during the reign of King Yeongjo of Joseon in 18th century. Guests at home and from abroad can stay at the temple experiencing Korean Buddhism.

spots.name: Haengjusanseong Fortress Sun Rise Festival
spots.desc: On new year’s day each year, a splendid festival is thrown at Haengju Sanseong to welcome the new year’s day sunrise. The Sweeping Victory Gate is opened from 04:30 on the day of the event. Admission and parking are free.
spots.hours: 05:00-09:00 on new year’s day each year

spots.name: The Great Battle of Haengju Festival
spots.desc: The event is held to commemorate the most sweeping victory in our history (14 March) at Haengju Sanseong. Elementary school kids and their parents from the neighborhood can watch memorial service for patriotic martyrs of the nation and learn about the history of Haengju Sanseong. There’s a saying that you can see as much as you know. Get yourself primed with information about Haengju Sanseong and…

spots.name: Goyang Haengju Cultural Festival
spots.desc: The event is one of the major traditional cultural festivals held to commemorate the sweeping victory at Haengju, one of the 3 greatest victories won by Koreans during Japanese Invasion in 1592, and revive the noble mind of the deceased general Kwon Yul and other patriotic martyrs of the nation to properly inherit it. The festival is designed to be a traditional cultural event shared with…

spots.name: Goyang Lake Art Festival
spots.desc: Held at various locations around the Lake Park. Imagination and wits of artists getting out of the constraints imposed by stages fill the streets with vigor and romantic mood. Various performing arts including jazz, mime, dance, drama and installation arts decking out the venue with colorful decorations to add glamour, passionate performance by famous theatrical companies from around the world…

spots.name: The Lafesta
spots.desc: It is a street style entertainment center called ‘Myeong dong in Ilsan,’ housing over 150 stores, a broadcasting station (KMTV), and movie theaters. Music concerts are held every Wednesday and on special holidays such as Christmas, Easter, Thanksgivings and New Year’s Day, there are many sales and events. In Lafesta, there are dozens of shopping stores, restaurants, game centers, and a movie…

spots.name: Western Dorm
spots.desc: Popular sites in Ilsan with Lafesta. It's open street shopping mall. It has Multiplex cinema with IMAX screen. Besides, it has MBC Dream Center.

spots.name: Deogi-dong Fashion Town
spots.desc: Located at Deoki-dong, Ilsan Seo-gu. About 230 famous brand shops of the outlet sell various clothess at discounted prices every year.

spots.name: Hwajeong Rodeo Street
spots.desc: Lots of famous brands have shops here and sell at prices discounted. People come here for shopping not only from Ilsan but also from Seoul. Because it's close to Seoul. It is very convenient to shop here as you can find what you want no matter how old you are. They sell new products at prices lower than those offered by other shops.

spots.name: Ilsan Traditional Market
spots.desc: A traditional market. The marketplace is recorded in ancient documents as ‘Sapojang’ There are everything at the market place. Fresh vegetables just picked out of vegetable garden, fruits, fish, cloths, shoes, medicinal herbs, various foodstuffs, household goods, puppies, rabbits, ducks and goats are just eye-catching. The market is full of vigor with stalls packed with goods, buyers haggling…

spots.name: Furniture Store Complex
spots.desc: The largest shopping center for furniture in Korea offers a complete selection of furniture from designers’ to imported goods to meet everyone’s taste and needs.

spots.name: Baedari Korean Traditional Wine Museum
spots.desc: Part of the Baedari Brewery, now in its fifth generation, famous as the source of the makgeoli favored by President Park Chung-hee (ruled 1961-79, father of former President Park Geun-hye), and since then considered by many as the best variety of makgeoli.

spots.name: Goyang Onemount
spots.desc: It is the largest theme park in this city. They have Water Park, Snow Park and Shopping Mall. This Shopping Center has around 127 brand line, also other facilities like cafes, restaurants. In the middle of center, sometimes you can enjoy small performances.

spots.name: Starfield Goyang
spots.desc: A large six-story indoor mall (two of whose stories are underground). It has 560 entry brands, about 100 entry restaurants, and convenience facilities such as hypermarkets, movie theaters, indoor sports centers, and swimming pools.

spots.name: Pung-dong Anygol
spots.desc: Taverns where they played guitar and live music were once clustered in an area in front of Baekma Station. All these places had to relocate to anigol in the vicinity due to urban development and formed a food alley of unique cafes reminding you of old memories and as many as 80 plus large restaurants boasting of distinctive flavors. You can enjoy diverse cuisines and classy meals in a spacious…

spots.name: Lafesta & WesternDom Restaurant Alley
spots.desc: Large shopping malls like LaFesta and Western Dome are clustered in this area creating more food alleys than anywhere else. The food alleys are full of vigor of the youth. Restaurants satisfying various tastes of their customers are always crowded with people, like Shinchon or the neighborhood around Hongik University in Seoul, whether it is weekdays or weekends. Reasonable prices, comfortable…

spots.name: Bamgasi Food District
spots.desc: Neighbourhood filled with quaint restaurants and cafes. Increasingly popular among locals.

spots.name: Daehwa-dong Food Street
spots.desc: The area covering the four-way intersection of Daejin High School in Daehwa-dong and 6 subdivision of Munchonmaeul has the food street with great atmosphere and tasty foods.

spots.name: Haengju-dong Food Street
spots.desc: The district located near the Haengjusanseong Fortress offers various restaurants that specialize in eels, seafood and spicy fish soups. Especially, the clear scenic view of Hangang River and clean atmosphere add to the taste of foods.

spots.name: Yeonan Pier (연안부두)
spots.desc: The terminal is the gateway to more than 100 islands in the West Sea, offering ferries to destinations like Palmi-do, Deokjeok-do, and even China. It features the bustling Incheon Fish Market, famous for affordable fresh seafood, as well as waterside parks, boat tours, and the St. Petersburg Square, which commemorates friendship with Russia. Visitors can enjoy authentic local cuisine, coastal…

spots.name: Jeondeungsa Daeungjeon
spots.desc: The Daeungjeon Hall is the main worship hall of Jeondeungsa Temple, located on Ganghwa Island. Designated as Korean Treasure No. 178, this beautifully preserved structure dates back to the mid-Joseon Dynasty (17th century) and is known for its detailed wooden carvings. A distinctive feature is the small, nude female figure carved under one of the corner eaves, which is connected to a popular…

spots.name: Incheon government office building
spots.desc: It was the first to be declared a tangible cultural property in Incheon. The buildings across the street from Munhak Stadium are reproductions, not tangible cultural properties.

spots.name: Gachon Museum
spots.desc: Gachon Museum is a private museum in Incheon founded by Dr. Lee Gil-ya, specializing in the preservation and exhibition of historical and medical artifacts. The museum holds a significant collection of Korean traditional medicine materials, ancient books, and cultural relics. It is a valuable destination for those interested in the history of medicine in Korea, housing several designated National…

spots.name: GangHwa Daesan-ry dolmen distant view
spots.desc: It is appointed in 1995. This cultural property is related to brazen age.

spots.name: Ara tower
spots.desc: It is tower of Gyeongin Ara canal. On the first floor of Ara tower, there are information, lobby, exhibition space, video theater, and cafe.

spots.name: Ganghwa Peace Observatory
spots.desc: The Ganghwa Peace Observatory is a place for displaced people who wished for peaceful unification and left their hometowns, and is the building ranges from one basement to four floors above ground. The first basement level and the fourth floor of the ground are military facilities, which restrict civilian access. The first floor is a restaurant, a Ganghwa Specialty and a special-product market…

spots.name: Baedari (pontoon bridge)
spots.desc: It is named after a long time ago that a small boat traveled under the iron bridge through the channel where the seawater flowed in. It refers to the area of Geumchang-dong and Songhyeon-dong, Dong-gu, Incheon. This is famous for secondhand bookstore street. There are only five bookstores left on the old bookstore streets created in the 1960s and 1970s. There is a space beam opposite the old…

spots.name: Ganghwa Hwamunseok Village
spots.desc: Ganghwa Hwamunseok Village is a traditional rural theme village. Visitors can enjoy various cultural and traditional experiences that follow from the village. Hwamunseok is a flower mat made out of flower patterns. It is widely used in summer and has a great decorative effect because of its beautiful patterns. The village runs a Hwamunseok weaving experience program, which is also a specialty…

spots.name: Museum of Korean Immigration history
spots.desc: The Museum of Korean Immigration history was built in 2003 to honor the pioneer life of ancestors and convey its footsteps to descendants.

spots.name: Incheon Art Platform
spots.desc: It is a multicultural art space. It is used as a creative studio, studio, exhibition hall, and performance hall. It is carrying out various cultural events and creative support projects for writers.

spots.name: National Museum of Biological Resources
spots.desc: It is on the exquisite border between the city and the countryside. It is equipped with the largest water burial facility in the East, which can hold more than 11 million biological samples, and is operating an advanced management system that can permanently preserve biological samples. Exhibitions and education centers also display 4,600 specimens of 985 native plants on the Korean Peninsula. It…

spots.name: Incheon Islands
spots.desc: There are several islands accessible by ferries. Most islands provide comfortable environments with fresh air and various cuisines that allow visitors to stay away from city life for a while. Also, the islands have great hiking roads and beaches. Here are several islands people can easily visit: Daecheongdo, Yeonpyeongdo, Ganghwado, Yeongjongdo, Muuido, and Deokjeokdo.

spots.name: Eulwang-ri Beach
spots.desc: It is a beach in Eulwang-dong, Jung-gu, Incheon, and was designated as a national tourist destination in 1986 as it is also called Neulmok or Eolhang. The length of the white sand beach is about 700 m and the average depth is 1.5 m, which is relatively large.

spots.name: Incheon culture & arts center
spots.desc: The Incheon Culture & Arts Center has served as the home of culture and the arts in Incheon.

spots.name: Haughty Cat
spots.desc: It is a cat café where you can drink some coffee and enjoy with cats.

spots.name: Fairy-tale town
spots.desc: This town is designed to show like fairy tales. The murals here are three-dimensional, so it's a great place to take commemorative pictures with family or lover. There are souvenir shops, experience facility and food shops.

spots.name: Gyeongin Arabat Road
spots.desc: Gyeongin Arabat-road that connects the waters off Incheon with the Han River, is the first canal in Korea and is an 18-km water route linking the West Sea and the Han River. A pleasant bicycle road and a park have been built on both sides of the Arabat Road, making it a popular resting place for residents. The Arabat Road bike path is connected to the Han river bike road, which allows you to ride…

spots.name: Ganghwa Trail
spots.desc: It will pass through history and culture, including the World Heritage site in Ganghwa. From the old history of the Korean Peninsula, you can see old and modern history. It covers 20 sections of 19 courses and 310.5 kilometers. It is divided according to the subject, so you can choose your route as you like. Visitors can meet the dolmen of the prehistoric age, royal tombs and buildings of the…

spots.name: Sorae Wetland Ecological Park
spots.desc: It is a park in Nonhyeon-dong, Namdong-district. The entire area is about 3.5 million m² in size. In August–September, you can observe the production of salt from the salt farms, and you can also experience harvesting it. There is also an ecological exhibition hall, and there is also a mud flat experience area where you can observe the living things such as crabs and shellfish.

spots.name: Liberty Park
spots.desc: Liberty Park is next to Chinatown. It is the first modern park in Korea. For most Incheon citizens, the park is well known for General MacArthur's statue and the memorial of the Centennial Anniversary of U.S.-South Korean relations. If you go to Liberty Park in April, you can see the full bloom of cherry blossoms. This place is a resting place for citizens who can see Incheon's downtown area, the…

spots.name: Songdo-Beer Festival
spots.desc: The Super Beer & Music Festival is held in the park, where the green grass is shining cool! Asia's largest stage and the venue of more than 30,000 simultaneous inmates will feature the most delicious beer, food, joyful live concerts, fireworks and EDM parties.

spots.name: Sorae-port festival
spots.desc: The Incheon Soraepo Construction System is a festival based on the basic concept of being the only traditional fishing port in the metropolitan area. The Incheon Soraepo Construction System offers a variety of attractions, as well as rich participation events, including various events, to help visitors and residents become one. Various salted fish, discount sales of local agricultural and…

spots.name: Koryo Mountain azalea Festival
spots.desc: Every April, a festival is held near Mt. Koryo in Ganghwa, where azalea blossoms bloom. It is by far considered the best spring flower festival in Incheon. Although the mountain is rather high at 400 meters above sea level, many people climb the mountain to see azalea flowers. When you climb the mountain, you can enjoy not only azaleas but also various landscapes of Ganghwa. During the festival…

spots.name: Bupyeong Pungmul Festival
spots.desc: Annual autumn festival of pungmul (Korean farmers' percussion music), first held in 1997. Troupes from Bupyeong's neighbourhoods, other regions and abroad perform, and on the weekend the main road is closed for a street parade where visitors can join in. The 30th edition ran 2–4 October 2026.

spots.name: Incheon SK Happy Dream Park
spots.desc: It is the home stadium for the SK Wyverns in the Korean professional baseball league.

spots.name: Incheon Football Stadium
spots.desc: Incheon Football Stadium is a soccer-only stadium in Incheon, South Korea. Incheon United FC has been using it as a home stadium since the 2012 season, and it is also where the Haiti match, an exhibition game for the Korean national soccer team, was held on Sep 6, 2013. As the distance between the stadium and the stands is only one meter, the stadium is considered the closest to the stadium in…

spots.name: Gyeyang Gymnasium
spots.desc: Gyeyang Gymnasium is an indoor gymnasium in Seo-dong, Gyeyang-gu. The V-League's Incheon Korean Air Jumbo and Incheon Heungkuk Life Pink Spiders use it as their home stadium. Badminton and airlift were played here in the 2014 Asian Games.

spots.name: Incheon Complex Fish Market
spots.desc: The country's largest seafood distribution market, which distributes seafood sent directly to the Seoul metropolitan area. Fresh seafood and raw fish can be bought at a low price, and fresh raw fish can be eaten if you pay extra for the restaurant.

spots.name: Sinpo International Market
spots.desc: A representative market in Incheon with more than 100 years of history. This place is a market with a variety of delicious foods, and the most famous food is chicken Gangjeong.

spots.name: Moraenae market
spots.desc: Moraenae market is a traditional market. It was first formed in 1982. It is a comprehensive market where various products are sold.

spots.name: Yonghyeon market
spots.desc: Around 400 stores including a grocery store, food, fisheries and livestock products, fruit, clothing, accessories. This market has a ‘Music box’: music broadcasts are held every Monday and Saturday from 14:00-16:00 with the application song of merchants and customers. You can listen to the story of the market merchant's life through the broadcast, and you can listen to the songs you applied for…

spots.name: Jungseojin-jungang traditional market
spots.desc: Jungseojin Jungang Traditional Market is developing into a traditional cultural and cultural market with a theme by actively applying the tourism elements of Junggamjin which is beautiful in the sunset and cultural elements of the region. The commercial building-type medium-sized market offers a wide range of items, including vegetables, livestock, fisheries, clothing, and vegetable and many…

spots.name: Ganghwa Pungmul Market
spots.desc: The market originated from merchants opening stalls around Ganghwa Market, which has turned into a shopping mall, and traditional five-day markets are held together on the 2nd and 7th.
spots.hours: 08:00-20:00, Closed on the first and third Mondays

spots.name: Singi Market
spots.desc: More than 120 stores are in operation, and the Singi Tokens, which are only used in the Singi Market, adds to the fun.

spots.name: Daeryong Market
spots.desc: Youth Bravo's Puppy-shaped Rice Cake is famous, and there are things to see such as Gyodong Barber Hall, Gyodong Theater, and Farmers Market.

spots.name: Bupyeong Market
spots.desc: It consists of Bupyeong Station Underground Shopping Center, which sells clothing and IT devices, Bupyeong Kkang Market, which sells fruits and fisheries products, and Bupyeong Comprehensive Market, which mainly sells agricultural products, dried fish, and miscellaneous goods.

spots.name: Gajwa Market
spots.desc: It is a market formed in the early 1970s and has more than 140 stores.

spots.name: Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center
spots.desc: Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center is 1.8 km from Bupyeong Station to the Bupyeong cultural street. There are 1408 stores . Boasting the largest number of stores in a single area, it was certified as a world record in 2015.

spots.name: Duty Free at Incheon Airport
spots.desc: Duty free shops at Incheon airport before your exit flight is always a good idea. You can find them both at terminal 1 & 2, so just arrive a little bit ahead of time!

spots.name: New York Banjeom
spots.desc: New York Banjeom is a contemporary Korean-Chinese restaurant in Incheon that puts a modern and fusion twist on traditional Chinese cuisine. While they serve high-quality classics like Jajangmyeon and Jjamppong, they are particularly known for unique fusion dishes, such as their creamy, pasta-style seafood Jjamppong.

spots.name: Jeongdeun Dakbal
spots.desc: Jeongdeun Dakbal is a popular casual Korean eatery specializing in Dakbal (spicy chicken feet), a famous local drinking snack. Their most popular menu item is the fiery Boneless Spicy Chicken Feet, which is often served alongside Jumeokbap (rice balls) and soft Gyeranjjim (steamed egg) to balance the intense heat. It’s an ideal place to experience genuine Korean late-night Hof (drinking place)…

spots.name: Yeongyeong
spots.desc: One of the most popular and long-standing Chinese restaurants in Incheon Chinatown. It is famous for its unique signature dish, White Jajangmyeon (Baek Jajangmyeon), which is prepared with a clear, savory sauce instead of the traditional black bean paste. They also offer excellent standard Jajangmyeon and various dim sum options. Expect long waiting lines, especially on weekends.

spots.name: Sinpo Dakgangjeong
spots.desc: Sinpo Dakgangjeong is famous nationwide for its unique sweet and spicy flavor. Unlike typical fried chicken, this dakgangjeong has a crispy texture even after being tossed in the sauce. Be warned: the basic flavor is quite spicy for some foreigners, so be ready for the kick.

spots.name: Samgang Seolleongtang
spots.desc: This restaurant serves seolleongtang, a stock soup of bone and stew meat. This restaurant boasts of a tradition that goes back 60 years.

spots.name: Granada Guwol
spots.desc: A well-regarded Spanish-style restaurant in the Guwol-dong area, specializing in fusion tapas, pasta, and gratins. The restaurant is popular as a date spot, offering a pleasant atmosphere and often providing free parking for up to two hours. Dishes like Gambas al Ajillo (garlic shrimp) and various pasta are highly rated.
spots.price: Main dishes (Pasta, Gratin, Tapas platters) typically range from ₩14,000 to ₩25,000 per plate

spots.name: Sushiway (Bupyeong Branch)
spots.desc: A well-regarded Japanese restaurant specializing in fresh sushi and sashimi. It is popular for its various course and set menus, which offer high-quality selections of seafood and appetizers.
spots.price: Lunch course sets range from ₩25,000 to ₩35,000, and dinner course menus typically range from ₩35,000 to ₩50,000 per…

spots.name: Myeongdong Boribap
spots.desc: A traditional Korean restaurant with over 40 years of history specializing in Boribap (Barley and Rice). The signature dish, Boribap Jeongshik, is served with a variety of fresh seasonal vegetables and Cheonggukjang (a robustly flavored soybean paste stew). It is an excellent choice for travelers looking for a hearty and healthy traditional Korean meal.

spots.name: Eat's
spots.desc: A popular casual Western restaurant specializing in Italian-style cuisine such as steak, pasta, and risotto. It is known for its large portions and excellent value, making it a favorite for family dining. The atmosphere is bright and modern.
spots.price: Pasta and Risotto dishes typically range from ₩15,000 to ₩22,000

spots.name: Wonjo Halmeoni Naengmyeon
spots.desc: A cold noodles bowl of ‘Hwapyeong-dong Washbowl Cold Noodles Street’ is as big as a washbowl, and very cheap compared to the quantity. The types of cold noodles are water-cold noodles and Bibim-cold noodles, and the characteristic of it is that it contains Yeolmu Kimchi.

spots.name: England Pork cutlet
spots.desc: A restaurant with a 30-year history. The atmosphere of the restaurant is retro, and the food maintains the recipes from 30 years ago. It became famous for its many appearances on TV and dramas. The price is also relatively low.

spots.name: Mandabok
spots.desc: This restaurant is a little way from the center of the town, and there is a parking lot in the back of the store, but only a few cars can be parked, so it is hard to park easily. If possible, it would be better to park at the public parking lot and walk. Mandabok literally recreates jjajangmyeon that was made 100 years ago when there was no chemical seasoning. This place is decorated with Chinese…

spots.name: Myungwoljip
spots.desc: Myeongwoljip is a Korean restaurant specializing in home meals and has been open for nearly 50 years. Eleven side dishes are served. And you can refill it. The main dish here is Kimchi stew.

spots.name: Taeyang Sikdang (Solar restaurant)
spots.desc: Taeyang Sikdang is a popular, unpretentious, and affordable local eatery in Incheon, known for its authentic, home-style Korean stews and nostalgic atmosphere. Its signature dish is the rich and deeply flavored Tuna Kimchi Jjigae (참치 김치찌개), which is served with generous portions and a variety of side dishes. This restaurant is a great spot to experience genuine Korean comfort food at a low price.

spots.name: Inha's House (Inhaui jip)
spots.desc: Inha's House is a pub, with a parking lot nearby so you can park easily. A variety of snacks are available, and the price is low. Nice to go when you want to drink simply enjoying Korean snacks.

spots.name: Cheongsil Hongsil
spots.desc: Famous for dumplings and buckwheat noodles (soba), Cheongsil Hongshil started out in 1979. And in 1983, the current head office - the store in front of the Rotary Outdoor Stage in Sinpo-dong - was put on a signboard for Clean Room. There are branch stores in Sinpo-dong, Juan, Bupyeong, Yeonsu, and Nonhyeon. Some say the house is 'the most visited restaurant in Incheon.' Cooking and serving speed…

spots.name: Gyeongin Myeonok
spots.desc: Incheon's Pyeongyang naengmyeon opened in 1883. People from all over Paldo gathered in Incheon in the hope of "Incheon Dream," and Pyeongan-do people opened a restaurant in Incheon and made and sold Pyeongyang naengmyeon. Unlike the history of the tile-roofed house, the building is now on the first and second floors of the modern building, but you can read more than half a century of history from…

spots.name: Bupyeong Hwami Pork Belly
spots.desc: It is popular for a variety of Korean food items such as aged pork belly, pork neck, budae jjigae, and soybean paste stew. Pork belly and pork neck have excellent savory tastes.

spots.name: Jincheon native sundae
spots.desc: It is a place where you can enjoy various Korean dishes such as sundae soup, freshwater snail and loach soup, and gopchang hot pot, and the taste of spicy soup is excellent.

spots.name: Moja Ondal
spots.desc: A highly popular local pub specializing in charcoal-grilled spicy chicken feet (Dakbal), known for its strong smoky flavor and fiery kick. The Boneless Chicken Feet (Mubbyeo Dakbal) are highly recommended for first-timers. This is a favorite spot for locals to pair spicy food with Soju or beer.

spots.name: Panino Gusto
spots.desc: An authentic Italian restaurant in Guwol-dong specializing in Neapolitan pizza, baked in a 485°C wood-fired oven (참나무 화덕). It offers a wide menu of pasta, risotto, and pizza (like the popular Margherita con Bufala and Gorgonzola). It is known for its excellent value, especially during lunchtime specials, making it a reliable spot for Italian dining.
spots.price: Main dishes (Pasta, Pizza, Risotto) are generally ₩15,000 to ₩20,000

spots.name: Bbuldabang
spots.desc: This is a dessert cafe operated by photographer Kim Yeon-yong. His photo essay, "The Sea of Father," which depicts a touching true story with his blind father, was also introduced to Heo Young-man's cartoonist and KBS' human theater program, and I can see the photos and photo equipment that he took from all over the world, looking around the world for the scenery of Seonjae Island, filling the…

spots.name: Mealwoo
spots.desc: A small dessert café specializing in a variety of cakes, including cheesecakes and Victoria cakes. Baked goods such as scones and pound cakes are also available.

spots.name: Hangang Citizen's Park
spots.desc: Alongside the Han River through 13 districts: Gwangnaru, Jamsil, Gangdong, Ttukseom, Jamwon, Banpo, Ichon, Yeouido, Yanghwa, Mangwon, Seonyudo, Nanji, and Gangseojigu. You can see many people strolling or jogging along the trail paths, as well as in-line skaters, bicyclists, and soccer fields or basketball courts. Yeouido, Jamsil, and Ttukseom districts are especially popular because of the…

spots.name: Shinsegae Department Store Gangnam Branch
spots.desc: It is a popular shopping spot in Seoul that often hosts famous pop-up stores, always offering new experiences. It is a great place for gourmets as there are many delicious desserts and various restaurants. In addition, you can enjoy high-end brands, lifestyle products, and even cultural experiences in one place. However, as it is a department store, the price is rather high. It is easily…

spots.name: World Comic Convention
spots.desc: Roughly every other month, the SETEC convention center hosts Seoul's World Comic con Festival. Admission is ₩4,000 but the inside is rather bland unless you are extremely familiar with Japanese and Korean anime. Your best bet is to go during convention hours and mingle with the crowds of Korean teenagers in elaborate cosplay costumes dressed as their favorite anime characters. Most are excited to…

spots.name: Shiroco
spots.desc: This cafe is a breezy coastal viewpoint cafe near Jeju airport where low-flying airplanes pass close overhead every few minutes. Signature menu items feature specialty drip/espresso coffee, refreshing ade beverages, and simple-paired bakery/dessert items. Reviewers highlight the unique plane-spotting vantage point, open ocean views toward Yongdam coast, and relaxed pet-friendly neighborhood vibe.

spots.name: Haenyeo Museum
spots.desc: Museum dedicated to the Haenyeo (female divers). Small but interesting. Nice views from the top.

spots.name: Gimnyeong Snake Cave
spots.desc: The Gimnyeong Snake cave is a 700-meter-long S-shaped lava tube. It is also called snake cave for its internal shape. The entrance of the cave bulges like a head of a snake and it becomes thin as you go deeper into the cave.

spots.name: Gold Cave
spots.desc: The gold cave is a rare lava tube that remains its original shape. It's blocked off from the public.

spots.name: Hallim Park
spots.desc: The park is divided into 16 gardens, including a tropical garden, garden of Washington palms, a garden of foliage plants, and a bonsai gardens with bonsai trees that are over 150 years old. Also has a Folk Village.

spots.name: Jeju Jeolmul Recreational Forest
spots.desc: The forest opened on July 23, 1997, it's comprised of both a natural Japanese cedar forest and a man-made forest. It has a promenade, waterfall, pond, grass square, wood-crafting studio, and more. There are forest cabins available for lodging.

spots.name: Halla Arboretum
spots.desc: Home to nearly 1,100 species of plants, including native Jeju flora and exotic subtropical species.

spots.name: Jeju Folklore and Natural History Museum
spots.desc: The museum is divided into four exhibition halls: natural history, folklore, special resources, and an audio-visual room. It contains natural history of the island as well as relics, animals and plants that are found around the island. The stuffed animals are popular among children.

spots.name: Lava tubes and other volcanic sights
spots.desc: Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes is a UNESCO World Heritage site in the "nature" category. Mount Halla (Hallasan) dominating the island is a dormant volcano and there are underground caves with lava tubes to explore on Geomeunoreum. Seongsan Ilchulbong is a tuff cone crater in Seogwipo. All three are very popular attractions and accessible.

spots.name: Mysterious Road
spots.desc: Called the Mysterious Road or the Goblin Road, this is a strange place where if you park your car on a downhill road, the car that has to go down does not go down, but rather steps back toward the uphill. In fact, the side where the uphill road is visible is a downhill road with a slope of about 3 degrees, so it seems to be going up by a simple optical illusion. Due to this phenomenon, Dokkaebi…

spots.name: Kimnyeong Miro Park
spots.desc: It is Korea's first maze park built in 1987 The mazes symbolise the history and geography of Jeju Island, surrounded by green Ralandi trees and Jeju pine trees. About 50 cats live here too, and are part of the attraction.

spots.name: Glass Castle
spots.desc: One of Jeju's two theme parks specialising in glass sculptures. Also offers an optional hands-on studio experience where visitors can craft their own works.

spots.name: Kimyoung Maze
spots.desc: A Jeju-shaped hedge maze which is interestingly complex and fun to walk through. The hedges are evergreen so it runs all year round. The maze claims fewer than 5% of visitors complete it in under 5 minutes, and the layout tends not to favor blind-luck too heavily so try timing yourself.

spots.name: Jeongwol Daeboreum Fire Festival
spots.desc: The Jeongwol Daeboreum Fire Festival originates from the traditional harvesting of the grasses found in the local domestic farm animal pastures, which were annually set in fire each winter by the villagers as a way to exterminate harmful insects. It has been held annually since 1997. It is held during the holiday of Daeboreum (which is the 15th day of the first lunar month of the year, typically…
spots.addr: Saebyeol Oreum area on Route 95, Bongseong-ri, Aewol-eup, Bukjeju-gun

spots.name: Halla Arboretum
spots.desc: Take a stroll through some botanical gardens. This is actually one of the nicest arboretums in all of South Korea, as it is both well-established and located up on the lower flanks of Mt Halla at the back of Jeju city. The gardens wind themselves over the foothills, giving tantalising views of the coast and Mt Halla through the trees. The ~2km walk from the arboretum to the rear entrance at the…

spots.name: Yesodam
spots.desc: It sells famous meat noodles in Jeju Island. It has a strong soup and is recommended by Jeju residents.

spots.name: Donsadon
spots.desc: Famous Jeju black-pork (Heukdwaeji) barbecue restaurant well-known among locals and tourists. Known for high-quality cuts grilled over charcoal and traditional Jeju-style side dishes.

spots.name: Myeongjin Jeonbok
spots.desc: Long-established abalone (jeonbok) specialty restaurant on Jeju’s northern coast. Famous for fresh grilled abalone, abalone porridge (jeonbokjuk), and abalone stone pot rice. Very popular among locals and tourists alike.

spots.name: Neulbom Heukdwaeji
spots.desc: Popular black pork barbecue house and one of Jeju’s well-known franchise-style locations. Offers high-quality Jeju black pork grilled over charcoal with traditional accompaniments. Often recommended for first-time visitors seeking authentic Jeju pork flavor.

spots.name: Dombaedon
spots.desc: Local black pork restaurant located on Jeju’s Black Pork Street. Famous for its tender, flavorful Jeju pork (heukdwaeji) grilled over charcoal. A favorite among both locals and tourists looking for authentic island-style barbecue.

spots.name: Baekgane Jeju Korean Food
spots.desc: Traditional Korean restaurant serving Jeju-style full-course meals (hanjeongsik) made with fresh local ingredients. Offers a variety of seafood, black pork, and vegetable dishes. Popular among visitors staying in the Hamdeok area for breakfast or dinner.

spots.name: Crab Jack
spots.desc: Ocean-view seafood restaurant featuring fresh crab dishes and Western-style seafood platters. Known for its scenic seaside atmosphere and large glass windows overlooking the Aewol coastline — a popular stop for lunch or sunset dining.

spots.name: Doldam Black Pork Jeju
spots.desc: Late-night Jeju black pork restaurant offering premium cuts grilled over charcoal. Popular among locals and tourists alike for its tender pork belly and friendly service. Convenient location for evening meals near Jeju city center.

spots.name: Gozipdol Ureok (Jeju Airport Branch)
spots.desc: Popular seafood restaurant specializing in ureok (rockfish) and Jeju-style stone pot dishes. The Jeju Airport branch offers quick, high-quality local meals in a modern setting — ideal for visitors catching a flight. Closes early if ingredients run out.

spots.name: Sinjeju Bomal Kalguksu Jeju Main Branch (신제주보말칼국수 제주본점)
spots.desc: A specialty restaurant serving rich and savory bomal (sea snail) kalguksu made with fresh sea snails from the Jeju ocean and chewy noodles. Known for its clean and comforting broth, it is a popular spot for a hearty breakfast or hangover cure, complemented by delicious side dishes.

spots.name: Kkotdam Handmade Burger Seongsan
spots.desc: Handmade burger restaurant featuring black pork patties and local ingredients near Seongsan Ilchulbong.

spots.name: Dongbaek Kitchen
spots.desc: Casual Western dining restaurant in Hanrim-eup serving pasta, risotto, and pork cutlet in a cozy, quiet atmosphere.

spots.name: Burger Carrot
spots.desc: Their slogan is "love carrot, love Jeju". I'm not sure what that means but their burgers, topped with carrot, are indeed easy to love. Dine in or take-away. Has the dubious honour of being the only place in the area open early in the morning, and closes pretty early too.

spots.name: The Green Cafe
spots.desc: A good choice if you're craving some vegetables. Baked goods and made-to-order sandwiches. True to its name, the interior of the cafe is full of beautiful plants.

spots.name: Modu-modu
spots.desc: A rather large and upmarket Korean restaurant. The restaurant is built in the oddball "mushroom" style with outdoor dining in summer. The food (and the interior design alike) is a modern fusion of Chinese and Korea styles. Mostly serves large expensive group dining platters and course meals, but has an extensive lunch special range for under ₩10,000. Featured in a 2010 SBS K-drama.

spots.name: Sehwa Picnic
spots.desc: Tiny, made-to-order pizza place run by a friendly couple. English spoken.

spots.name: The tree inhabited by the Samshin-goddess
spots.desc: Walk around it three times, and write your wish on a tag. Peace or reuinification seem to be common answers if stumped. The sight alone of all the aging tags hung off such an ancient tree is worth a peek.

spots.name: Byongdae cliff
spots.desc: The view from atop showcases the entire village and is rather spectacular. Take the little wooden ferry from down by the pine forest, it's pretty cheap and return is included. Those feeling adventurous can note that its actually possible to descend or ascend the cliff not only by taking the main trail beside Okyeon Pavilion, but also by a lesser marked one that goes via Gyeomam Pavilion…

spots.name: Andong International Mask Dance Festival
spots.desc: In every October, you can also visit the Andong International Mask Dance Festival, showcasing not only Korean Mask Dance, but also various traditional dances of countries round the world. The festival is split into two halves.Typically tourists only visit the main event in Andong city itself, by the river (~2 blocks south of the bus and train terminals). It is interesting, but dance acts on the…

spots.name: Andeok Apple Village
spots.desc: Famous for producing honey-sweet apples with a savory crunchiness. It is a beautiful and quaint village located between the cities of Pohang and Andong.Numerous apple farms to be appreciated. Just walk around the village and you will see them. Spend a day walking around and appreciating the beauty. Maybe the locals will offer apples to foreigners when they are in season around October.

spots.name: Yeoni nangja (natural dyed goods)
spots.desc: Graceful and beautiful natural herb & grass dyed goods. Dresses are nice and becoming to everybody.

spots.name: The Diner
spots.desc: This is the only cafe in town where you can eat some kinds of brunch. They have 6 brunch menus - chicken, vegetable egg, basic type, pancake, quiche, vegan pasta and extra orders (of sausage, toast, bacon, pancakes, etc.) are possible. There are 5 kinds of hand-dripped coffee - from Kenya, Indonesia, Ethiopia, Colombia and Brazil — and sometimes they can serve specialty coffee (but there is no…

spots.name: Andong Jjimdak Jongson
spots.desc: Andong Old Market, or Jjimdak Golmok, is crammed with Andong jjimdak restaurants. All the food is cooked in booths out front of the restaurant, so you can tour around and choose a favourite. Andong Jjimdak Jongson stands out because its menu contains a variety of different styles of Andong jjimdak.

spots.name: Kkachi Gumeong Jib
spots.desc: Kkachi Gumeong Jib, or Magpie Hole House, specialises in heotjesabap (₩9,000), which is a local variation of bibimbap flavoured with soy sauce instead of hot pepper sauce. If you get the Yangban Meal (₩15,000) you get a variety of dishes including fish and some very excellent shark meat. All food is served in heavy bronze tableware.

spots.name: Andong Godunga
spots.desc: This restaurant specialises in salted mackerel, and many locations can be found across Andong. As well, they run a mail-order system for sending out Andong mackerel. The restaurant serves mackerel roasted or in a very mild (but spicy looking) soup.

spots.name: Mammoth Bakery
spots.desc: You can taste European style bread&goods. Mammoth bakery always use well-roasted coffee beans so all of their espresso drinks are very good and reasonable. "Mammoth Bakery is just off the main square in downtown Andong, a short walk northward from the bus terminal, near the Pizza Hut. Baked goods start from ₩1,000, with cakes starting in the ₩15,000 range, sandwiches around ₩3,500, and espresso…

spots.name: Nodongri and Noseori grave parks
spots.desc: Here are two small parks next to each other with many burial mounds. The western park, Noseori, has 14 graves of different sizes where Geumwanchong, Geumnyeongchong, Seobongchong, Houchong, Ssangsangchong and Machong are buried. The eastern park, Nodongri, has graves from the 4th to 6th centuries.

spots.name: Hwangnyongsa History and Culture Center
spots.desc: This center features a 1/10 scale model of the legendary nine-story wooden pagoda and a 3D theater showing its history. A great place to understand the scale of the original temple.

spots.name: Songdae horse lighthouse
spots.desc: Songdae Horse Lighthouse is one of South Korea's snorkeling hotspots. The water is clear enough that you can see the bottom even if you don't go in, and there's a place to grab a bite to eat in front. However, it's not an official beach, so you'll need to bring your own supplies, as the facilities aren't very well equipped.

spots.name: Bomun Mulebanga Water Wheel
spots.desc: A large water wheel with 108 channels (a holy number in Buddhism).

spots.name: Gyeongju World Culture Expo
spots.desc: Since 1998 the resort hosts culture festivals, centered around the 82m high Gyeongju Tower and the Expo Culture Center. The event includes exhibitions, concerts, video shows and other performances.

spots.name: Sonje Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.desc: Permanent exhibition consisting of pictures, sculptures and media installations. Also differently themed temporary exhibitions.

spots.name: Sungdeokjeon
spots.desc: A shrine south of Oreung, built in the 11th century under King Sejong. Later destroyed by the Japanese, it was rebuilt by King Sunjo. In the shrine there is a monument telling the stories of the kings Park Hyeokgeose and Sundeokjeong.

spots.name: Nangsan
spots.desc: The holy hill Nangsan looks more like a burial mount than a hill, being just 108 m high. In 413 CE, King Silseong saw a cloud reminiscent of a pavilion above the hill. He believed that it was the house of the gods and declared the hill holy. The Sillas performed shamanic rites on the hill. Nowadays you can find the remains of the Buddhist temple Sacheonwangsaji there. It was built in 679 to…

spots.name: Samneunggol
spots.desc: Also known as Naenggol, Cold Valley due to its cold weather around the year. Into the valley's walls several Buddha figures have been sculpted. The first one you will encounter is Seokjoseokga yeoraejwasang, a Buddha sitting with crossed legs with a missing hand. After this Maaegwaneum Bodhisattva, a standing Buddha with a Lamp of Pureness (jeongbyeong) in the hand. It is especially beautiful at…

spots.name: Baeri Samneung Tombs
spots.desc: These three burial mounds are located at the entrance to the Samneunggol valley. The kings Gyeongmyeong, Sindeok and Adala are buried here. In the temple there are three standing Buddha statues — the Baeri Seokbul Statues.

spots.name: Gyerim Forest
spots.desc: Located between the Cheomseongdae observatory and the National Museum, some of the trees here are over 2000 years old. According to a legend King Talhae heard a rooster in the forest in the middle of the night. The next morning a baby was found in the forest. The king adopted him, named him Kim Alji and he would eventually become the founder of Gyeongju. The forest was named Gyerim which…

spots.name: Lake Bomun
spots.desc: A getaway for the locals both in the spring for the cherry blossom and in the summer for canoeing and seeing open air concerts and theater performances. Several restaurants, stores and activities. Very busy in the summer, remarkably less so outside the season.

spots.name: Korean Traditional Liquor and Cake Festival
spots.desc: Events include traditional music and dance performances, as well as opportunities to learn traditional Korean arts and crafts. However, the highlight of the festival is the rice cakes, traditional tea, and rice wines.
spots.hours: An annual festival held during March and April

spots.name: Namsan mountain
spots.desc: This historically and spiritually significant mountain only 5min south of the central city is littered with historical Buddha reliefs carved into its rocks and boulders as well as dotted with ancient pagodas and temples. A hike up the mountain (466 m) through its western valley from the Samneung tomb site is recommended.

spots.name: Wolseong Park
spots.desc: Wolseong Park, also called Banwolseong or “Half-Moon Fortress,” is the former site of the Silla royal palace in Gyeongju. Although the earthen fortress walls remain, the area is now a large grassy park featuring historical relics and scenic walking paths. Archaeological excavations have uncovered palace foundations, ponds, and artifacts from the Silla Dynasty, providing valuable insight into…

spots.name: California Beach
spots.desc: California Beach is a large water park located in Gyeongju’s Bomun Tourist Complex. Inspired by California’s beaches, the park features wave pools, water slides, lazy rivers, and kid-friendly play zones. It is designed as a family-friendly summer destination and is connected to Gyeongju World amusement park, allowing visitors to enjoy both attractions. With seasonal events and various leisure…

spots.name: Silla Millenium Park
spots.desc: Silla Millennium Park is a large theme park in Gyeongju dedicated to recreating the culture and history of the Silla Dynasty. The park features life-sized replicas of Silla palaces, traditional craft workshops, and live performances such as historical reenactments and martial arts shows. Visitors can explore cultural exhibits, enjoy family-friendly attractions, and experience interactive programs…

spots.name: Outdoor activities
spots.desc: The region is ideal for hiking. There are hiking paths along the forested hills and between the sights. The tourist office can provide you with information about hiking itineraries. On Lake Bomun you can rent small or big boats, with or without a motor. Bomunho Resort and Hotel Kolon have golf courses. If you would like to swim, most larger hotels have pools that are also open to non-guests, in…

spots.name: Kangdong Waterpark
spots.desc: It consists of 2,000 pyeong indoors, 8,500 pyeong outdoors, and 1,500 pyeong of customer convenience facilities, and is equipped with various water play facilities and convenience facilities.
spots.price: High Season Weekday: Adult ₩50000, Child ₩40000, Weekend: Adult ₩55000 Child ₩45000

spots.name: Gyeongju Gyo-chon Traditional Village
spots.desc: Gyeongju Gyo-chon Traditional Village has been newly restored and preserves the original form of the cultural heritage. Woljeonggyo Bridge, the largest wooden bridge in Korea, has been newly restored, and colorful lighting can be seen at night.

spots.name: Dori Village Ginkgo Tree Forest
spots.desc: Numerous ginkgo trees form a forest, and there is something for villagers to enjoy by operating food and specialty markets.

spots.name: Seongdong Covered Market
spots.desc: A classic example of the modern Korean market with lots of fresh seafood, food stands and some textiles.

spots.name: Bomun Shopping Center
spots.desc: The shopping mall at Bomunho Resort caters to tourists: it has stores with souvenirs and local specialties as well as traditional restaurants.

spots.name: Gyeongju Jungang Market
spots.desc: It is the market with the longest history among urban markets, and stores in commercial buildings operate every day and the five-day market enters around the commercial building every day ending on the 2nd and 7th.

spots.name: Angang Market
spots.desc: It is the largest traditional market in the northern part of Gyeongju, with more than 400 stores. On the 4th and 9th of every month, a five-day market enters around the commercial building.

spots.name: Gampo Public Market
spots.desc: It is a market in the center of Gampo Port, Gyeongju's largest fishing port, and the 5-day market enters the area around the commercial building every day ending on the 3rd and 8th of each month.

spots.name: Bae-li-dang
spots.desc: A popular souvenir shop in Hwangnidan-gil specializing in Gyeongju-themed goods. They are famous for their unique "Neung" (Royal Tomb) shaped candles and various stationery items designed with Silla cultural heritage motifs.

spots.name: Gyeongju Simsang
spots.desc: An independent bookstore and gift shop that offers a curated selection of books, postcards, and locally made crafts. It is a great place to find artistic and high-quality souvenirs that capture the quiet atmosphere of the city.

spots.name: Dosol Maeul
spots.desc: You can experience a Korean traditional meal of Gyeongbuk area here. Located next to the Sarangchae accommodation. The building is a one-hundred-year-old traditional Korean house.
spots.price: ₩13,000 per head base, plus extra main dishes at ₩10,000 each

spots.name: Sukyeong Sikdang
spots.desc: Korean cuisine in a traditional Korean building. Famous for its barley rice, you can also find items and dishes like Hwangnam ppang, bibimbap and pajeon on the menu.

spots.name: Kisoya
spots.desc: A range of Japanese dishes, including bento boxes, sashimi and noodle soups, with a Korean twist.

spots.name: Hwangnam Ppang
spots.desc: The bakery where the namesake bread, or rather pastry, was invented in 1939. They are sold in packages of 20 or 30.

spots.name: Metdol Sundubu
spots.desc: Korean cuisine, specializing in different soups including sundubu jjigae (tofu soup/stew).

spots.name: Pyeongyang Naengmyeon
spots.desc: Traditional Korean food, for instance bulgogi (Korean barbeque) and naengmyeon (noodles). The restaurant is in a backyard, accessed through a small gate from the Wonhyoro street opposite to a movie theater.

spots.name: Toobbul Korean BBQ
spots.desc: Korean BBQ house, specializing in beef from the Korean hanu cattle. During lunch hour, they reportedly have 35% discounts.
spots.price: meats around ₩16,000-21,000, sets with small dishes ₩10,000

spots.name: With Gusto
spots.desc: Italian restaurant with a Korean twist, serving pastas and omelettes among other things.

spots.name: Julie's
spots.desc: Eclectic menu (Indian, Italian, Korean) and most dishes can be made vegetarian or vegan

spots.name: Gyeongju Cheonnyeon Hanu Bomun
spots.desc: A BBQ restaurant, also specializing in hanu beef. You get to choose your meat at the butcher shop, and as usually with Korean barbecue, it's barbecued on your table. The price includes all-you-can-eat side dishes.

spots.name: Yosokkoong
spots.desc: Located in the house of a local aristocratic family, the Choi family. The dishes are from the Korean royal cuisine and are works of art just like the building. Dining there is a memorable experience, justifying the high price. Reservation is mandatory.

spots.name: Hwangnam Dagwa-jeom
spots.desc: A trendy dessert cafe in a renovated Hanok. Famous for its financiers and traditional tea, offering a perfect blend of old Gyeongju atmosphere and modern dessert culture.

spots.name: Hwangnam Gyeongju Ten-Won Bread
spots.desc: The original shop for the famous '10-won bread'. The bread is shaped like a 10-won coin and filled with melting mozzarella cheese. It has become a viral street food icon of Gyeongju.

spots.name: Ryoko
spots.desc: A popular fusion Japanese restaurant specializing in Tonkatsu (pork cutlet) and Ryoko-style fried rice. Known for its minimalist Hanok interior and high-quality plating.

spots.name: Oncheonjip
spots.desc: A visually stunning restaurant famous for its Hanok-style hot pot (Shabu-shabu). It features a beautiful interior courtyard with a traditional hot spring pond theme, making it one of the most Instagrammable spots in Gyeongju.

spots.name: Hyanghwa-jeong
spots.desc: Specializes in Gyeongju-style cockle bibimbap (Kkomak-bibimbap) and Yukhoe-mulhoe (raw beef spicy cold soup). It is highly popular for its generous portions and traditional taste served in a modern Hanok setting.

spots.name: Sol-Sot
spots.desc: Known for its premium Korean pot rice (Sotbap) with various toppings like steak, sea bream, and eel. It offers a comforting and healthy meal that reflects the modern interpretation of Korean traditional dining.

spots.name: Schuman and Clara
spots.desc: A coffee house, reportedly with one of the best baristas in Korea.

spots.name: Nahbi Brunch Cafe & Books
spots.desc: Cosy cafe and brunch restaurant, also featuring a bookstore. They have different sandwiches and coffees and it's one of the few Western-style cafés in the city.

spots.name: Cafe Araeheon
spots.desc: It is the most crowded time from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m., and the bakery is delicious, so if you go to Gyeongju, it is a good place to visit.

spots.name: Guryongpo Gwamegi Culture Museum
spots.desc: At the Gurongpo Gwamegi Cultural Museum, you can learn about Gwamegi, a specialty of Pohang, such as the process of making Gwamegi and the Gwamegi industry. In addition to writing, you can actively feel Guryongpo Gwamegi as an exhibition and experience type.
spots.addr: 경북 포항시 남구 구룡포읍 구룡포길117번길 28-8 과메기문화관

spots.name: Key-Chungsan Botanical Garden
spots.desc: A botanical garden that can be enjoyed outdoors; a place where endangered plants are preserved and multiplied.

spots.name: Deokdong Culture Village
spots.desc: A 300-year-old village where you can experience old games and enjoy the scenery of old Korean villages. Deokdong Folklore Exhibition Hall, which displays relics used in the past, is located inside. Between the village's reservoir and the valley, there is a pine forest designated and managed as a "beautiful village forest.". Experiences such as Seodang Education, Tea Ceremony, Hanok Accommodation…

spots.name: Duksil Village
spots.desc: Duksil Village is a historic village in Heunghae-eup, Pohang, known as the childhood home of former President Lee Myung-bak. The village has preserved old Korean rural architecture, wide yards, and signage/exhibits explaining his early life. It offers a peaceful, nostalgic stroll through village life and insight into modern Korean history.

spots.name: Bogyeongsa Temple
spots.desc: Bogyeongsa Temple in Pohang is an old temple located in Naeyeonsan Mountain. It is beautiful because there is a valley around.

spots.name: Sabang Memorial Park
spots.desc: A place to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the start of modern sabang projects in Korea. Sabang project refers to construction carried out to prevent natural disasters. There are three exhibition rooms that collect various materials and technical changes of the Sabang project, a multi-purpose video room, and outdoor facilities that reproduce the actual construction site.

spots.name: Saemaul Memorial Hall
spots.desc: It is an exhibition hall created to re-examine the achievements of the Saemaul Movement and promote the history of the Saemaul Movement. It is a place where many domestic and foreign officials visit every year to learn and check the contents of the Saemaul Movement. There are various events where you can experience Saemaul Movement here. If you want information about the event, please go to the…

spots.name: Hwanho Park
spots.desc: Completed in 2001. The park is divided into several themes, including high-tech science, marine culture, and sports. Landscape facilities such as a science museum, an outdoor park, and an artificial waterfall are established.

spots.name: Space walk
spots.desc: Hwanho Park's night view attraction. It is located near Yeongildae Beach. It is one of Pohang's landmarks. It is a work of architectural structures by German Heike Mutter and Ulrich Gentz. The track length is 333 m and the number of stairs is 717. The maximum number of people to experience is 150 at the same time. You can't use it if you're less than 110 cm tall. Access is restricted during…

spots.name: Yeongil Folk History Museum
spots.desc: The Yeongil Folk Museum uses Jenamheon, a building from the Joseon Dynasty, as an exhibition room. It was built in 1835 and designated as a cultural property. In the exhibition room of Jenamheon, old agricultural equipment, ancient books, and earthenware are displayed, so you can look at the lives of the people in the past.

spots.name: Botanical Garden of Gyeongsangbukdo
spots.desc: There are 22 arboretums, which are largely divided into professional arboretum, theme garden, changpo garden, spire garden, and broadleaf garden. The theme garden is a place where flowers are planted in groups separated from each season so that flowers can be seen in four seasons. In Changpo Garden, Coniferous Garden, and Broad Leaf Garden, there are plants that fit each name. Free.

spots.name: Yangdong Folk Village
spots.desc: Yangdong should in no case be confused with the tourist trap "Gyeongju Folk Village". The village consists of estates and houses from the 15th and 16th century. The about 150 buildings are to a large part still inhabited. The main sights include the estates of Yi Hui-Tae (1733), Simsujeong (1560) and Hyangdam (1543). From Gyeongju there are many bus lines to Yangdong (more precise information…

spots.name: Oksan Seowon
spots.desc: Established in 1572, Oksan Seowon was one of Korea's most important Confucian schools. Contrary to many other Confucian schools it was spared the destruction of the 1860s, but not a fire in the early 19th century that left just 14 buildings standing. In the summer people are camping at the nearby river bank and bathing at the waterfall. One of the nine components of the world heritage site…

spots.name: The tomb of King Heungdok
spots.desc: One of the last tombs built by the Silla dynasty and the one furthest away from Gyeongju. It is 4 km north of Angangri, about halfway between Oksan Seowon and Yangdong Folk Village.

spots.name: Songdo Beach
spots.desc: Located in Songdo-dong, Songdo Beach sits directly across a small inlet from POSCO's steel mill. Though not popular for swimming, it often attracts windsurfers.

spots.name: Bukbu Beach
spots.desc: Located just north of downtown Pohang and across the bay from POSCO, Bukbu Beach is a popular (i.e. often crowded) summertime hangout. It is more popular than Songdo Beach for swimming, though the brown color and its proximity to POSCO keep many people out of the water. The International Fireworks Festival December 2020 is held here every year in July.

spots.name: Chilpo Beach
spots.desc: About 10 km north of the city. Clean water and good waves. Inner tubes are for rent (₩10,000).

spots.name: Wolpo Beach
spots.desc: 4 km north of Chilpo Beach, Wolpo Beach is often less crowded. Inner tubes are for rent (₩10,000).

spots.name: Guryongpo Beach
spots.desc: Guryongpo Beach is about 10 km east of the city. Though small, Guryongpo Beach has clear blue water that attracts snorkelers, and fishermen.

spots.name: Yeongildae Beach
spots.desc: It is the largest beach on the east coast. be famous for the sunrise There are Yeongilgyo Bridge, a sea bridge, and Yeongildae, a sea pavilion. You can use the free beach parking lot to park. It provides facilities and services such as shower rooms, changing rooms, toilets, water supply stands, canteens and parasols. You can also experience marine leisure activities.

spots.name: Pohang Steel Art Festival
spots.desc: This is a festival that combines the cultural codes of iron across the time and space of Pohang history with art and cultural activities, from the Yeonorang SeoNyeo Ilwol myth to POSCO's success myth. It is the world's only steel festival and consists of exhibitions of steel art works, experience programs, tour programs, and performance programs. Admission is free, but the experience program is…

spots.name: Chilpo Jazz Festival
spots.desc: It is a symbolic cultural festival in Pohang that started in 2007 and is held every year. Various jazz music stages such as swing, bebop, cool, free jazz, and rock jazz will be held. It is held on the outdoor special stage of Chilpo Beach, and the bathroom is located in the concert hall. The booth and fence are used to distinguish the outside from the concert hall. Wheelchairs are available. It…

spots.name: Pohang Rose Bread
spots.desc: Inspired by roses designated as urbanization in Pohang. It is about 4.5cm in diameter and is shaped like a rose. It contains various kinds of nuts, seeds, and cheese. It is a bread made by kneading glutinous rice and milk without using flour. It can be stored at room temperature for about three days. Alternatively, it can be stored in a freezer and eaten by heating it in a natural defrosting or…

spots.name: Hwan-yeo Sashimi restaurant
spots.desc: Cold raw fish soup and spicy fish stew are delicious. It is near Yeongildae. Parking is available in front of the restaurant (paid) or in front of the Heian Cafe (free)/Yeongildae 2 parking lot (paid). You can order as to go.

spots.name: Yurim Restaurant
spots.desc: It is famous for Mori noodles. It consists of two types: standing and sitting, and you cannot order one serving. Break time from 15:00-16:00. Mori-noodles: It is a local food of Guryongpo-eup in Pohang. It originated from spicy noodles eaten by fishermen in Guryongpo-eup. It is seafood kalguksu boiled with fish, seafood, and bean sprouts. Generally, fish put anglerfish.

spots.name: Jukdo Market
spots.desc: It is the largest traditional market in Pohang. It sells a variety of items such as marine products, dried fish, vegetables, fruits, clothing, and furniture. It is composed of various alleys such as a fish market area, agricultural product street, food alley, and rice cake restaurant alley. Parking is available in the nearby public parking lot. It is ₩5,000 for 20 minutes, and ₩200 will be added…

spots.name: Gaeksa Building
spots.desc: This building was built around 1471 and was used to accommodate important visitors. Rituals to honour the king were also held here. It's a meeting place for many as well as a hangout location for many old men. The downtown area surrounding is also referred to as Gaeksa.

spots.name: Hansol Paper Museum
spots.desc: The Hansol Paper Museum was established in Jeonju in 1997 as the first paper museum in Korea with the mission of "Paper is a container of culture."It has a total of 12 cultural assets, including National Treasure No. 277 Daebanggwangbulhwamgyeong, and Treasure No. 1222-1 Haengnokjeolyo Byeongpisa, and has been relocated to Wonju Museum SAN.

spots.name: Jeonju Traditional Wine Museum
spots.desc: Opened in the Hanok Village in 2002, this museum aims to promote Korea's tradition of home brewing. Besides displays, there are classes and hands-on programs. They are reportedly eager to assist anyone wishing to brew Korea's traditional drinks for themselves. There are small fees for the programs: interestingly, teens get a discount on the "Local Wine-Drinking Rituals" class!

spots.name: Ohmockdae
spots.desc: A small hill with a traditional house on top. The best thing about this spot is the night view of the city.

spots.name: National Intangible Heritage Center
spots.desc: The National Intangible Heritage Center (NIHC) in Jeonju is a crucial institution dedicated to the preservation, transmission, and promotion of Korea's rich and diverse Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), including traditional skills, performing arts, and craftsmanship. This modern complex features a state-of-the-art museum, archives, performance halls, and educational facilities, allowing…

spots.name: Jeolla Gamyeong
spots.desc: The restored headquarters of Jeolla Province during the Joseon period. The complex offers visitors a look at the administrative history and traditional architecture of the region.

spots.name: Veteran
spots.desc: A noodle restaurant with a limited but worthwhile menu. It is always busy.

spots.name: Taste of bumpkin
spots.desc: It sells meatballs on a stick. Meatballs is made grilled Short Rib Patties.

spots.name: Gyodong croquette
spots.desc: It is a croquette store. It serves many different types of croquette.
spots.price: Cream cheese croquette: 2,500won, Jeonju bibimbap croquette: 2,500won, Potato croquette: 2,000won

spots.name: Daurang
spots.desc: It is a dumpling store. It serves many different types of dumpling. Shrimp pan-fried dumpling is one of the most popular food in this store.
spots.price: Shrimp pan-fried dumplings: 1ea-2,000won/1package-8,000won, Shrimp dumplings: 1package-5,000won, King-sized Dumplings…

spots.name: two aunts (Duimo)
spots.desc: This café is famous for a bibimbap waffle. And it serves various homemade juices.

spots.name: Jeondong Korean pancake
spots.desc: It serves Korean pancake that is baked in a firepot. Korean pancake is chewy and mild.
spots.price: Soybean milk honey Korean pancake: 2,000won, Cream cheese Korean pancake: 2,500won, Garlic Korean pancake: 2,500won…

spots.name: Sushi Mirai
spots.desc: You can eat many kinds of sushi, and if you go alone, you can eat at the bar table. However, you may have to wait because the restaurant is rather small.

spots.name: Jamae Galbijjeongol
spots.desc: Jamae Galbijjeongol is one of Jeonju's most celebrated local dining experiences, famous for its signature spicy short rib stew served in a traditional hot pot (Jjeongol). The dish features tender, marinated short ribs cooked with various vegetables and spices in a rich, flavorful broth, often finished with chewy noodles or rice. This iconic restaurant is a must-visit for travelers seeking an…

spots.name: Moila Café
spots.desc: Popular dessert & brunch café near Jeonju Hanok Village area, with minimalist interior and signature berry-cheesecake.

spots.name: GT Cafe Jeonju Innovation Branch
spots.desc: Modern café in Jeonju Innovation City, first floor, known for brunch and speciality coffee.

spots.name: Jeonmang Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe and guesthouse famous for its stunning rooftop view of the Hanok Village.

spots.name: Cafe Ireuri
spots.desc: A spacious and elegant traditional Hanok cafe with a beautiful inner courtyard.

spots.name: WORKERBEE Jeonju
spots.desc: A modern cafe specializing in various honey-based beverages and desserts.

spots.name: Cafe 16 Hours
spots.desc: A bakery cafe famous for its unique baked goods and desserts.

spots.name: Cafe In od
spots.desc: A spacious cafe with a garden, often used as an event venue.

spots.name: PNB Choco Pie Cafe
spots.desc: The main PNB bakery in Jeonju, offering its signature Choco Pie and coffee.

spots.name: Bichui Anbu
spots.desc: Bichui Anbu is an aesthetically striking cultural space and cafe located conveniently close to Jeonju Hanok Village. This popular destination distinguishes itself by seamlessly integrating traditional Korean Hanok architecture with a distinctly modern, minimalist interior and specialized lighting design, offering visitors a unique and serene environment where they can enjoy drinks amidst a…

spots.name: On-the-go
spots.desc: A modern cafe serving grab-and-go desserts and beverages, including a selection of sweet treats and signature drinks. The cafe is designed for takeaway or short visits rather than long sit-down meals.

spots.name: Kape Dalgeom
spots.desc: A cafe near Jeonju Hanok Village serving Korean-inspired baked goods, desserts, and signature beverages.

spots.name: National Cemetery
spots.desc: National cemetery for Korea's war heroes and patriots. It's quite beautifully landscaped and surrounded by a ring walking trail. Dress standards apply.

spots.name: Dunsan Prehistoric Settlement Site
spots.desc: When excavating for Dunsan new town in the early 1990s, a bunch of "stone-age" relics were discovered. Prior to the discovery, it was widely believed the region had a rather recent history. At a glance, the site is essentially a very hilly grassy park with scattered reproduction 'prehistoric huts' built over it. However the site provides extensive historical information for visitors. It is open…

spots.name: Daejeon Expo Aquarium
spots.desc: It is a complex cultural space where you can enjoy various sea creatures and contents through media art as well as living creatures.
spots.addr: Basement 1, Daejeon Shinsegae Art & Science, 1 Expo-ro, Yuseong-gu

spots.name: Daejeon Aquarium
spots.desc: It is the first and largest freshwater fish aquarium in Korea, where you can see various freshwater fish from other countries and decorated fish by theme.

spots.name: Daejeon Modern History Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: Along with viewing the building, you can see many events in modern and contemporary history of Daejeon and special exhibitions in various fields such as history, architecture, urban planning, design, and popular culture.

spots.name: Euneungjeongi Cultural Street
spots.desc: Euneungjeongi Cultural Street is known for its vibrant LED media facade and various cultural performances.

spots.name: Daejeon Observatory
spots.desc: Here you can observe the sun during the day or any number of celestial bodies at night. Located west of Expo Park, take the 604 bus to the observatory stop.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 14:00-22:00, closed Mondays and the day following a national holiday

spots.name: Daejeon Art Center
spots.desc: Small art gallery in old downtown showcasing modern art works of young artists. The exhibits rotate every 1-2 months exhibiting to an often unusual theme, individual pieces regularly are quite involved, taking up an entire room.

spots.name: Donghak-sa Temple
spots.desc: A picturesque temple outside of Daejeon in the adjacent city of Gongju, but linked in on the Daejeon bus routes. In addition to the temple, the valley contains restaurants, hotels and saunas (including a fair few of the funky "hobbit mushroom" styled ones) and a fairly dramatic waterfall, albeit dry much of the year.
