spots.name: Wakeboarding
spots.desc: *Wakeboarding If you drive into Chungju, take the first left after the bus terminal intersection, heading south towards the river. You will go under the railway, then see a park on your left. Drive into the riverside park and walk 100m to a wakeboard floating house on the river. Prices are cheaper than Seoul. Only ₩17,000 for outboard engine each time (in the 2008 season).

spots.name: Apples
spots.desc: Chungju is famous for apples. A giant apple sculpture greets you as you drive into town. Apples are a lot cheaper here than in the rest of Korea.

spots.name: Wonjo Jungangtap Makguksu
spots.desc: This is a very popular spot for makguksu (buckwheat noodles) known for its quick service. It's a great choice for both cold broth noodles and spicy mixed noodles.

spots.name: Bon-ga Seokgalbi Jungangtap
spots.desc: A great option for seokgalbi (grilled marinated short ribs). The meat is pre-grilled on a hot stone plate, allowing for a clean and delicious dining experience without the smoky smell.

spots.name: Ssamjeong Myeonok
spots.desc: This restaurant is famous for its Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles). It's praised for its light and clean beef broth, a refreshing alternative.

spots.name: Cheongpoong Garden
spots.desc: Known for its traditional Korean dishes, especially its doeji galbi (pork ribs). The restaurant has a rustic, cozy atmosphere.

spots.name: Gamnamujip
spots.desc: A restaurant specializing in pheasant dishes, a local delicacy in the Suanbo area. They offer a full course of pheasant cuisine, including sashimi, dumplings, and bulgogi.

spots.name: Maensil Village Restaurant
spots.desc: A local gem known for its hearty sundubu-jjigae (soft tofu stew). The broth is rich and spicy, and the tofu is incredibly soft. It's a great comfort food option.

spots.name: Gangbaksa Seolleongtang Hamheung Naengmyeon
spots.desc: This restaurant is well-regarded for its Hamheung naengmyeon (spicy cold noodles) and also serves seolleongtang (ox bone soup). It has been operating for over 30 years and is a local favorite.

spots.name: Chungju Boktteokjip
spots.desc: A popular spot for traditional Korean rice cakes (tteok). It's a great place to buy a souvenir or try some local sweets. Their pumpkin rice cake is especially well-known.

spots.name: Mu-hak Market Sundae Alley
spots.desc: An alley of stalls specializing in sundae (Korean blood sausage) and sundae gukbap (sundae soup with rice). The unique taste comes from the use of bean paste and dried radish greens in the broth.

spots.name: Daega-jip Korean Beef
spots.desc: This restaurant serves high-quality Korean beef (hanu), with a reputation for its tender and flavorful cuts. It's a great place to experience premium Korean barbecue.

spots.name: Yeonhwaji
spots.desc: Yeonhwaji Pond is an artificial pond located in Gyodong, Gimcheon. In spring, cherry blossoms bloom around the pond and along the walking trail, and in summer the water is covered with lotus flowers. The pond is open year-round with no admission fee, and a walking path with benches and rest areas makes it suitable for light exercise and family visits. At night, the area is illuminated, and…

spots.name: National Center for Forest Therapy, Gimcheon
spots.desc: The National Center for Forest Therapy in Gimcheon is located in a dense birch forest on the slopes of Sudosan Mountain in North Gyeongsang Province. It offers a variety of forest therapy programs that make use of the rich natural environment along scenic forest trails. One of the main programs is the thermal therapy course designed to promote blood circulation. It consists of a half-bath and…

spots.name: Gimcheon Green Future Science Museum
spots.desc: The Gimcheon Green Future Science Museum is a science exhibition and experience facility themed around climate change, renewable energy, and the green future. The exhibitions are organized into the Climate Change Hall, Green Energy Hall, and Green Future Hall, featuring interactive displays related to these topics. The 4D Full-Dome Theater offers stereoscopic video screenings, and outdoor…
spots.hours: 09:30 - 18:00. Closed on Mondays, January 1, and the day of Lunar New Year & Chuseok.

spots.name: Bangchojeong Pavilion
spots.desc: A historic pavilion built during the Joseon Dynasty, located near Jikjisa Temple. Surrounded by a landscaped garden with lotus ponds and stone walls, it offers a glimpse into traditional Korean architecture and a tranquil place to rest.

spots.name: Buhang Dam
spots.desc: A large multipurpose dam completed in 2011, surrounded by scenic mountains. The area features a suspension bridge, observatory, and eco-park, making it a popular spot for walking, cycling, and enjoying views of the reservoir and nature.

spots.name: Gimcheon World Ceramic Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to traditional and contemporary ceramics from Korea and around the world. The collection includes Korean celadon, porcelain, and folk pottery, as well as international works. The museum also hosts special exhibitions and hands-on programs for visitors.

spots.name: Riverside Park
spots.desc: A riverside park along the Gamcheon River, popular with locals for walking, jogging, and family outings. The park features landscaped trails, seasonal flowerbeds, and open spaces for relaxation. Festivals and cultural events are occasionally held here.

spots.name: Gimcheon Stadium
spots.desc: A multi-purpose stadium mainly used for football matches and home to Gimcheon Sangmu FC of the K League. The venue hosts domestic league games as well as athletic events and other public gatherings.
spots.hours: Event hours vary; generally open on match or event days.
spots.price: Varies depending on event (football match tickets usually ₩10,000–20,000)

spots.name: Jeungsan Sudo Valley Camping Resort
spots.desc: A scenic valley campground set along a clear mountain stream, offering 27 deck-style auto-camping sites. Surrounded by forested hills and near natural attractions like Muhul Gugo (Nine Bends), it’s ideal for campers seeking tranquility, water play, and nature walking.

spots.name: Gimcheon Sky Park
spots.desc: An adventure and leisure complex near Buhang Dam featuring Korea’s longest glass skywalk, zipline, and paragliding experience. Offers panoramic views of surrounding mountains and the dam lake. Great spot for photography and outdoor activities.

spots.name: Buhang Dam Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: A suspension footbridge crossing above the surface of Buhang Dam reservoir, offering visitors a thrilling walk with scenic views of the lake and surrounding hills. At 256 m in length, it is one of the longest suspension bridges on water in Korea.

spots.name: Gimcheon Plum Picking Experience
spots.desc: Experience picking fresh plums in the orchards of Gimcheon during summer. Participating farms offer guided picking, tasting, and sometimes crafts or puzzles (e.g. plum-clay activities) as part of the program. The city also organizes a plum distribution / picking event around mid-July using agricultural and theme-park venues.
spots.hours: Generally during plum harvest season (June ~ July) – by reservation
spots.price: Varies by farm – contact farm for details

spots.name: Gimcheon Gagok Festival
spots.desc: An annual choral and art song concert mostly organized by the Gimcheon City Choir. The program often revolves around “Gimcheon” as a theme: local poets’ works set to music by Korean composers. The festival aims to promote community spirit and regional cultural identity.
spots.hours: ypically evening performances (e.g. around 19:30) depending on year

spots.name: Gimcheon Gimbap Festival
spots.desc: An annual food festival held at Jikji Culture Park and Samyeongdaesa Park. It features gimbap-themed food stalls, performances, exhibitions, games, and hands-on activities such as making and tasting gimbap.

spots.name: Pyeonghwa Market
spots.desc: Gimcheon’s main traditional market, Pyeonghwa Market, offers a glimpse of everyday local life. It features stalls selling fresh produce, handmade snacks, clothing, and kitchenware. Visitors can try local street foods such as hotteok and tteokbokki while browsing through the lively aisles.
spots.hours: 08:00–20:00 (closed on the first and third Mondays of each month)

spots.name: Jungang Market
spots.desc: Jungang Market is one of Gimcheon’s oldest traditional markets, located right next to Pyeonghwa Market. It features various small shops selling fruits, vegetables, seafood, and household items. The narrow alleys and local vendors offer a lively and authentic glimpse into everyday life in a Korean provincial city.
spots.hours: 08:00–20:00 (closed on the first and third Mondays)

spots.name: Hwanggeum Market
spots.desc: A small neighborhood market located in Hwanggeum-dong, south of downtown Gimcheon. Hwanggeum Market mainly serves local residents, offering fresh produce, side dishes, and daily essentials. Its friendly vendors and relaxed atmosphere make it a good stop for travelers wanting a look at local life outside the city center.
spots.hours: 08:00–20:00 (closed on the first and third Mondays)

spots.name: E-Mart Gimcheon Branch
spots.desc: A large supermarket operated by Shinsegae Group, E-Mart Gimcheon offers groceries, Korean snacks, cosmetics, electronics, and travel necessities all in one place. It is a convenient stop for travelers to pick up local products and daily goods before leaving the city. Tax-refund service is available for foreign visitors.

spots.name: Lotte Mart Gimcheon Branch
spots.desc: A large retail store operated by Lotte Group, offering groceries, fashion items, cosmetics, and household goods. The mart also has a food court and bakery. It is a convenient one-stop shopping destination for both locals and travelers. Tax-refund service is available for foreign visitors.

spots.name: Nonghyup Hanaro Mart Gimcheon Branch
spots.desc: Operated by the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (Nonghyup), Hanaro Mart offers locally sourced produce, Korean food products, and household goods. It is a convenient stop to buy regional specialties such as Gimcheon plums, rice, and honey at fair prices.

spots.name: Gimcheon Nonghyup Hanaro Mart Local Food Direct Store
spots.desc: Operated by the Gimcheon Agricultural Cooperative (Nonghyup), this local food store directly connects local farmers with consumers. It offers fresh agricultural products from the Gimcheon region, including fruits, vegetables, grains, and processed goods. The store aims to promote regional produce and provide reliable, locally sourced foods to residents and visitors.
spots.hours: 09:00 – 21:00 (may vary slightly depending on season or events)

spots.name: Buil Sanchae Restaurant
spots.desc: A long-standing Korean restaurant near Jikjisa Temple, Buil Sanchae Restaurant specializes in traditional mountain vegetable dishes such as sanchae set meals, deodeok-gui (grilled deodeok root), and acorn jelly salad. Popular with temple visitors and hikers, the restaurant is known for its fresh seasonal ingredients, generous portions, and welcoming service. Free parking is available nearby.

spots.name: Ulsan Restaurant
spots.desc: Ulsan Restaurant is a well-known traditional Korean restaurant near Jikjisa Temple, specializing in mountain vegetable set meals, doenjang stew, and various side dishes made with local produce. The restaurant is appreciated for its homestyle cooking, hearty portions, and friendly service, making it a popular stop for temple visitors and families traveling in the area. Parking is available near…

spots.name: Cheongsan Goeul Restaurant
spots.desc: Cheongsan Goeul is a traditional Korean restaurant famous for grilled deodeok, bulgogi, and mountain herb set meals. Featured on national television programs such as KBS 6 O’Clock My Hometown, it is known for its rustic interior and authentic countryside flavors. Visitors enjoy locally sourced ingredients, neatly presented side dishes, and outdoor seating with scenic views of Mount Hwangak. Free…

spots.name: Dansan Garden
spots.desc: Dansan Garden is a countryside-style restaurant specializing in Korean dishes such as bulgogi, soybean paste stew, and freshwater snails with vegetables (ureong ssambap). Known for its spacious interior and group seating, the restaurant is a popular stop for families and hiking groups visiting Jikjisa Temple. Customers appreciate its clean setting, generous portions, and traditional side dishes…

spots.name: Giwajip Ssambap Restaurant
spots.desc: Giwajip Ssambap is a traditional Korean restaurant offering ssambap (rice wrapped in leafy vegetables) served with grilled pork and soybean paste. The restaurant emphasizes healthy home-style dishes prepared with local produce and fermented sauces. With its tiled roof design and rustic ambiance, it provides an authentic countryside dining experience for temple visitors and hikers. Parking space…

spots.name: Moran Hoegwan (Moran Restaurant)
spots.desc: Moran Hoegwan is a Korean barbecue restaurant in the Innovation City area specializing in frozen samgyeopsal (pork belly). The menu is quite focused, with the main dish being 냉동삼겹살 (frozen pork belly), supplemented by side items like ramen, fried rice, and sauces. The place has a retro aesthetic and is popular among local residents and visitors seeking a relaxed grill-style meal. According to…
spots.addr: 15, Hyeoksin-ro 3, Yulgok Square 6, 1st Floor, Room 121, Yulgok-dong

spots.name: Andong Hwangso Sikyuk Restaurant
spots.desc: Andong Hwangso Sikyuk Restaurant is a beef specialty restaurant in Gimcheon’s Innovation City. They serve premium Korean beef including various cuts like ribeye, sirloin, and tenderloin, along with dishes like beef soup and yukhoe bibimbap. The restaurant is known for its spacious layout with private rooms, a children’s play area, and a large parking lot (capacity ~200 cars)
spots.addr: 1st Floor, Units 112–119, Yulgok Technovalley, 5 Hyeoksin-ro 8, Yulgok-dong

spots.name: Haru Myeonok
spots.desc: Haru Myeonok is a noodle restaurant in Gimcheon’s Innovation City known for its Pyeongyang cold noodles and stir-fried noodles. The restaurant has been featured on TV programs and is popular locally for its clean flavors and generous portions.

spots.name: Uri Bansang Siwol
spots.desc: Uri Bansang Siwol is a Korean set-meal (bansang) restaurant located in the Innovation City area.

spots.name: ShowJinz Malatang Innovation Branch
spots.desc: This is a malatang / mala xiang guo style restaurant (spicy Chinese hotpot / spicy soup) popular in Innovation City. You pick ingredients, then they cook with your choice of heat level. It’s noted for being accessible to students and locals, offering a variety of vegetables, meats, and side options. It has a self-service sauce bar and uses a kiosk ordering system for convenience. Parking is…

spots.name: Marine Monument
spots.desc: Monument placed where South Korean marines held the line against overwhelming communist forces during the Korean War.

spots.name: Chae Man-Sik Literature Museum
spots.desc: A museum to the famous Korean satirical writer during the Japanese occupation.

spots.name: Gunsan Modern Architecture Museum
spots.desc: Formerly the Gunsan branch of Joseon Bank built during the Japanese colonial period, this museum now displays the architectural history and modern heritage of Gunsan.
spots.hours: Mar-Oct: Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00; Nov-Feb: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00 (Closed Mondays and Jan 1)

spots.name: Chowon Photo Studio
spots.desc: This studio is a film set of Christmas in August. This is not a real studio.

spots.name: Saemangeum New Year Festival
spots.desc: The Gunsan sea wall is the world's longest, and every January 1st there is a festival to celebrate the new year here.

spots.name: Gunsan TimeTravelFestival
spots.desc: This festival is held every October in Gunsan-si, using modern architectural heritage. The three-day street, where the Time Travel Festival takes place, features a rickshaw stamp tour to explore modern heritage facilities with a bicycle rickshaw, a Jangdol banger play yard, an experience yard for Japanese martyrdom, a street magic, an art performance, an amateur saxophone performance contest and…

spots.name: Ggongdang Barley Festival
spots.desc: This festival is held every May to promote regional specialty 'white rice barley'. This consists of 7 parts, ggongdang barley madam contest and recreation ground, performance ground, experience ground, marketplace ground, rest ground, and walk ground.

spots.name: Gunsan Insect Experience Learning Farm
spots.desc: An educational farm offering hands-on experiences with insects for children and families. Visitors can learn about beetle life cycles, touch various specimens, and purchase live beetles or caterpillars.

spots.name: Gunsan Oldam Public Market
spots.desc: Gunsan Public Market is the most famous traditional market in Gunsan, which was opened in 1918. You can buy various items such as agricultural products or marine products.

spots.name: NoBrand
spots.desc: A convenience store. Also, you can not use cash, so you must pay by credit or check cards only.

spots.name: Ilhaeog
spots.desc: Classic Korean restaurant. This restaurant is famous for Kong-namul-gukbap (bean sprout and rice soup), and it costs ₩6,000.

spots.name: Lee Sung Dang
spots.desc: This is a famous bakery in Gunsan, and it is known as the oldest bakery in Korea. It traces its roots back to the 1920s when it was founded by a Japanese person under the name 'Izumoya', but it was renamed Leesungdang after Korea's independence in 1945. Their signature bread is danpatppang (단팥빵), which is bread filled with red bean paste, but other flavors such as vegetable bread (야채빵…

spots.name: Sweet India
spots.desc: This place has some pretty good Indian food if you are looking for anything besides Korean.

spots.name: Mulgogi Jari
spots.desc: This is a seafood restaurant. And it is in front of the sea, so the landscape is great. The price of sashimi is little bit expensive.

spots.name: Hansoggeum
spots.desc: This restaurant is famous for Seafood Stew in a Hot Pot. And there are lots of seafood dishes. But price is little bit expensive.

spots.name: Wangsan Chinese Dishes
spots.desc: This is the most famous Chinese restaurant in the Gunsan-si. The price of hot-jjamppong (Chinese-style noodles with vegetables and seafood) and baek-jjamppong (not spicy jjampong) is ₩9,000. But you may have to wait because of lots of people.

spots.name: Jirinseong
spots.desc: This Chinese restaurant is famous for hot pepper jajangmyeon (black-bean-sauce noodles). But you should be careful. This one is really really rellay spicy.

spots.name: Hanilok
spots.desc: This is a restaurant of Korean-style dishes. Beef radish soup and Beef Tartare Bibimbap is the most famous.

spots.name: Bokseongru
spots.desc: 1. jajangmyeon (black bean sauce noodles): ₩6,000. 2. jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle noodle soup): ₩9,000. 3. jjamppong bap (spicy seafood noodle soup with rice): ₩9,000. 4. fried rice: ₩9,000. 5. japchae bap (rice with stir-fried glass noodles and vegetables): ₩10,000.

spots.name: Onyang Folk Museum
spots.desc: The largest folklore museum in Korea, the Onyang includes architectural installations of Korean traditional homes and housewares, and experience hands-on activities such as fishing, farming, and witness traditional wedding ceremonies.
spots.price: Adults ₩8,000, youth ₩5,000, children ₩4,000, seniors ₩3,000, disabled ₩1,000, group discounts offered

spots.name: SinJung-ho
spots.desc: Sinjeongho is an artificial lake created in 1926 and a scenic resort destination throughout all four seasons. On weekends, music events and various cultural performances are held. If you visit during the summer season, you can also use the outdoor pool facilities.

spots.name: Hyeonchungsa Gokgyo Ginkgo Tree Road
spots.desc: Hyeonchungsa Gokgyo Ginkgo Tree Road is a landmark selected as one of the 'Top 10 Most Beautiful Tree-Lined Streets in the Nation.' Along the 2.2-kilometer road from Chungmugyo Bridge over Gokgyocheon to the entrance of Hyeonchungsa, about 350 ginkgo trees have been planted. In autumn, ginkgo trees create a stunning scene, and in spring, canola flowers offer a different kind of beauty.

spots.name: Hyeonchungsa Shrine
spots.desc: Shrine commemorating Admiral Yi Sun-sin, first established in 1706. The grounds include a memorial museum with exhibits about Yi and the Imjin War.
spots.hours: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00 (last admission 17:00); Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00 (last admission 16:00); closed Mon

spots.name: Bonggoksa Temple
spots.desc: It is a tranquil temple with a history of more than 1,300 years, and a combination of dense forests and clear valleys provides a tranquil nature. With a legend related to the Silla Uisang Temple, it is an important attraction that preserved Buddhist cultural properties and traditional architectural styles.

spots.name: Sesimsa Temple
spots.desc: As its name implies, it is known as a place to wash and purify the mind. Sesimsa Temple is said to have been built during the Silla Dynasty, and thereafter, several reconstructions and repairs were made. The temple is located deep in the mountains, creating a calm and peaceful atmosphere, especially Daeungjeon Hall and various Buddha statues are protected as important cultural properties.

spots.name: Songamsa Temple
spots.desc: The name is said to have originated from the 'pine rock'. The temple was built during the Silla Dynasty and has since been rebuilt several times. The main buildings of the temple include Daeungjeon Hall and a number of Buddha statues, and it is a place that preserves the traditions and historical values of Buddhism.

spots.name: Hyemyeongsa
spots.desc: The temple is said to have been built during the Goryeo Dynasty, and 'Hyemyeong' means 'life of wisdom'. Located deep in the mountains, Hyemyeongsa Temple is known as a place of meditation and practice where you can find peace of mind in harmony with nature.

spots.name: Suamsa Temple
spots.desc: The temple is said to have been built during the Silla Dynasty, and Suam means "a mind that has become as solid as a rock through training." Suamsa Temple is particularly scenic, and Daeungjeon Hall and various Buddhist relics are protected as important cultural properties.

spots.name: Mahavihara Buddhist Temple
spots.desc: Mahavihara Temple is the first Sri Lankan-style Buddhist temple built in Korea. You can tour the Southern Buddhist-style temple buildings and the indoor greenhouse. We also offer meditation programs to help manage stress.

spots.name: Asan Spavis
spots.desc: A contemporary hot spring that focuses on sports treatment and family experiences. They even offer snow sledding and traditional spa treatments.
spots.price: Spa & sauna range from ₩24,000-29,000 for children and ₩33,000-40,000 for adults, sauna only ranges from ₩6,000-8,000

spots.name: Onyang Hot Spring
spots.desc: Onyang Hot Spring is the oldest hot spring in Korea, with a history dating back from the Three Kingdoms period to the Joseon Dynasty. It is available at Onyang Hot Spring Hotel and The Cheil Hotel Onyang.

spots.name: Paradise Spa Dogo
spots.desc: Paradise Spa Dogo is a resort where you can enjoy the charm of nature and a healthy relaxation experience. Enjoy mineral-rich hot spring water, a variety of indoor and outdoor pools, and a large public bath.
spots.price: Spa prices vary by season, but they usually range from ₩40,000-₩60,000. Adding the hot spring costs an additional…

spots.name: Yeonginsan Azalea Festival
spots.desc: This festival is held annually in April on Yeonginsan Mountain. In 2025, it was held on April 19th. Various hands-on activities, such as woodworking and crafts, as well as recreational sports, are available.

spots.name: Asan Admiral Yi Sun-sin Festival
spots.desc: The Asan Admiral Yi Sun-sin Festival is a representative festival of Asan, Chungnam, held annually around the birthday of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, April 28. This is an interactive cultural tourism festival that offers a variety of attractions and activities, including experience events and parades themed around General Yi Sun-sin, as well as academic seminars and talk concerts to help visitors learn…

spots.name: Onyang Oncheon Market
spots.desc: It is a traditional market where you can buy food, agricultural and fishery products, side dishes, fruits, butchers, rice cakes, and bread.

spots.name: Ongi
spots.desc: This restaurant serves fresh pasta along with a variety of Western-style dishes. You can make a reservation and enjoy a comfortable meal in the dining area.

spots.name: Hongdukkye Kalguksu
spots.desc: A restaurant where you can enjoy traditional Korean noodles at affordable prices. Despite the low price, it’s a local favorite among nearby residents because of its great taste.

spots.name: Nampo-dong Jikhwa Jjukkumi Sinjeongho Branch
spots.desc: This is a restaurant serving spicy webfoot octopus where you can enjoy your meal while overlooking Lake Sinjung. A favorite among locals, it is characterized by its spicy flavor and deep smoky taste. Spiciness can be adjusted to suit your taste.
spots.price: Teppan hot pot (￦48,000-￦50,000), Lunch Special (￦37,000), Single-serving menu (￦14,000-￦20,000)

spots.name: Cafe Annak
spots.desc: Large café in Asan offering a spacious and relaxing atmosphere, known for its bakery items, desserts, and comfortable seating areas.

spots.name: Eondeok
spots.desc: Café in Asan serving siphon-brewed coffee in a quiet and relaxed setting, offering visitors a distinctive specialty coffee experience.

spots.name: Cafe Brick
spots.desc: Café in Asan known for its fresh fruit-based beverages and desserts.

spots.name: Leepresso
spots.desc: Rooftop café in Asan offering scenic views of rice fields and countryside landscapes, known for its relaxing atmosphere and specialty coffee.

spots.name: Crossway
spots.desc: Specialty café in Asan known for its in-house coffee roasting, offering carefully crafted coffee and desserts in a comfortable setting.

spots.name: Inju Cafe Hanok Branch
spots.desc: It is a café with a beautiful traditional hanok interior. They sell traditional Korean drinks and traditional desserts here. They also offer menus that reinterpret traditional foods in a modern way.

spots.name: Inju Cafe Field Branch
spots.desc: This café features a lotus garden where you can enjoy coffee and various desserts while admiring the lotus flowers. The outdoor garden spans about 2,000 pyeong, making it a great place for a day out. Many customers say the coffee tastes great because it is roasted by an international coffee assessor.

spots.name: Magaret
spots.desc: A café with handmade Greek yogurt, granola, brunch, and desserts.

spots.name: Changing of the Guards
spots.desc: A show held every Saturday and Sunday in April, May, June, September and October each year.

spots.name: Songsan-ri Burial Mounds
spots.desc: A series of 7 tombs, 6 of which were discovered and suibsequently looted during the 1910-1945 Japanese occupation and as such their owners remain unknown. The 7th however, the Tomb of King Muryeong (Muryeong wangreung, 무령왕릉), was accidentally discovered by a Korean historian in 1971 and as such both the relics within, and the identity of the tombs owner were recovered and thus making it the star…

spots.name: Jeongjisan Relic Site
spots.desc: The only relics you'll find here are the traces of local residents having foraged for medicinal plants to sell at the markets, as the hill itself, deemed the likely site of Binjeon Hall — a hall where the body of King Muryeong and his queen had been placed for 27 months prior to the funeral — actually stands empty and bare. Regardless, the hill provides quite possibly the best view of…

spots.name: Hannok Village
spots.desc: A new estate has been built between the Songsan-ri Burial Mounds and the Gongju National Museum in the traditional wooden hannok style, a true rarity in modern-day Korea. Makes for an interesting and convenient detour.

spots.name: Gyeryong Reservoir
spots.desc: Gyeryong Reservoir is an irrigation reservoir located in Hadae-ri, Gyeryong-myeon, Gongju, in South Chungcheong Province. It was constructed between 1954 and 1964 to supply agricultural water for the surrounding region. The reservoir is known for its clean water and natural surroundings, with walking trails linking it to nearby Gyeryongsan sites. It is also a popular spot for freshwater fishing…

spots.name: Princess Metasequire Road in Gongju
spots.desc: The park was established in 2011. Since then, it has become a green tourist attraction in Gongju, attracting many tourists. There are 192 Metasequire trees in every 500 meter section.

spots.name: Mir Island
spots.desc: Mir Island is a scenic islet in the Geum River within Gongju, known for its riverside vegetation and seasonal photo spots. In autumn, the island is especially famous for pink muhly grass and reeds that adorn its banks. Visitors can stroll along paths connecting the riverbank and enjoy vistas of Gongsanseong Fortress across the water. The island serves both as a peaceful nature spot and as part of…

spots.name: Donghaksa Valley
spots.desc: It runs about 3.5 kilometers from Hakbawi Rock to Gwaneumbong Pass. If you walk through the stream like a god at the entrance of the valley, visitors can reach Donghaksa Temple, where Gangwon-do of the nuns is located, and right underneath there is a temple dedicated to the founder of Silla and Park Jae-sang, the loyalist.

spots.name: Gongju Gomanaru
spots.desc: Gomanaru is a historic ferry dock and riverside scenic area located in Ungjin-dong, Gongju. It served as a key river port during the Baekje period when Gongju was known as Ungjin. The site features pine groves, river views, and walking trails along the Geum River. Local legends tell of a bear that fell in love with a human, adding folklore depth to the place. Visitors enjoy strolling the…

spots.name: Doryeongseodang
spots.desc: It is a traditional hanok seodang experience space where visitors can experience the old educational culture of Korea. It reproduces the seodang culture of the Joseon Dynasty so that visitors can experience Chinese literature education such as Cheonjamun, Saja Sohak, and Myeongsim Bogam.

spots.name: Seonhwadang
spots.desc: Seonhwadang was the administrative hall where the provincial governor (Chungcheong-do magistrate) of the Joseon era carried out official duties. It is a traditional wooden government building reconstructed near the Gongju National Museum area. The building is fronted with eight bays and four bays in depth, in the style of traditional Korean official architecture. Over time, it was relocated and…

spots.name: Gongju Forest Recreation Village
spots.desc: It is a recreational forest in clean nature located in Gongju Forest Ecological Village. The surrounding facilities include wood culture experience center, Geumhak Ecological Park, and water source The native botanical gardens and campsites are under construction.

spots.name: Geumhak Ecological Park
spots.desc: Geumhak Ecological Park is a resting place with beautiful nature, clean water, ecological wetlands, ecological observation facilities and trails, and outdoor performance halls.

spots.name: Korean Natural History Museum
spots.desc: The Korean Museum of Natural History is the largest museum in Korea at the foot of Gyeryongsan Mountain. There are three theme museums: the world of dinosaurs 150 million years ago, the land of life, the earth, nature, and humans.

spots.name: Gongju Folk Drama Museum
spots.desc: As a museum with the most research data on Korean folk plays, it exhibits regional mask play characteristics, masks and costumes, and folk drama materials from around the world, as well as exhibitions of daily folk farming equipment and various household items such as chestnut dyeing.

spots.name: Baekje Cultural Festival
spots.desc: Advertised as one of Korea's three national festivals (the other two representing the Silla and Goguryeo Dynasties), this is held in both Gongju city and adjacent Buyeo annually from mid-September to mid-October. The Gomanaru National Drama Contest is held at a similar time.
spots.addr: Baekje Folk Village Land in Gongsan Fortress

spots.name: Archery
spots.desc: There's an archery range between the Hannok village and Gongju National Museum.

spots.name: Gongju Sanseong Market
spots.desc: Gongju Sanseong Market was relocated to Gongju, the central market in Gongju, due to flood damage in the riverside, and was opened as a private market. It is large, and is loved by many tourists and nearby residents for its market outing linked to the Baekje Cultural Heritage site.
spots.hours: A five-day market held on days ending in 1 and 6 each month

spots.name: Gomgol Sikdang
spots.desc: Gomgol Sikdang is a Korean restaurant specializing in Gongju's Korean food, and Spicy Pork Bulgogi and Braised Cutlassfish are popular menus.

spots.name: Sotttukkeong Maeuntang
spots.desc: It is a Spicy Catfish Stew restaurant located near Magoksa Temple.

spots.name: Yuga Kalguksu
spots.desc: It's a Seafood Noodle Soup restaurant located in Geumhak-dong.

spots.name: Jeontong Gungjung Kalguksu
spots.desc: Traditional palace kalguksu is a restaurant with a long tradition, and there are two menus: kalguksu and suyuk.

spots.name: Camellia Island
spots.desc: It is also called Dongbaek Island because camellia trees occupy 60-70% of the island's total area. It is located 6km east of Jiseong Island. During the reign of King Hyeonjong in the Joseon Dynasty, 15 generations of residents migrated and lived, and during the Japanese colonial period, a Japanese company was stationed as a military fortress until just before liberation. From a distance, it…

spots.name: Gujora and Wahyeon Beaches
spots.desc: A pair of large sand beaches overlooking some pine-covered islets. Gujora town is rather interesting too as the locals have undertaken a project to paint art on every wall in the town yielding rather pretty results.

spots.name: Inje-ro
spots.desc: The stretch of Inje-ro from the light rail northward to Bunseong-ro is popular in September when its plots of red spider lilies bloom, and in October, when festive lanterns are hung to line the walking trail.

spots.name: Gujibong Peak
spots.desc: Aa place related to the founding myth of Gaya. It was designated as Historic Site No. 429 in 2001. According to the Garak Flag of the Three Kingdoms, King Suro came down to Gujibong Peak in 42 AD, and the name Gujibong Peak came out because the shape of the mountain resembles a turtle. At that time, when the chief and the people who ruled the area gathered here and sang Gujiga and danced a golden…

spots.name: Archaeological Site in Bonghwang-dong
spots.desc: It is a relic of Geumgwan Gaya during the Bronze Age from the 1st to 4th centuries. It was designated as Historic Site No. 2 in 1963. Historic Site No. 2 used to be the Shell Mound in Hoehyeon-ri, Gimhae. Next to it was the Bonghwangdae Ruins (formerly Gyeongsangnam-do Cultural Heritage Material No. 87) and it has been pointed out that these two ruins are related to each other, and in 2003, they…

spots.name: Tomb of King Suro
spots.desc: Historic Site No. 73. According to legend, King Suro, the owner of this tomb, is the first king of Garakguk and the founder of Gimhae Kim. It is a circular mound tomb with a height of 5 m. The surrounding area of 18,000 pyeong was designated as Royal Tomb Park. Within a 20-minute walk, there are Surowangbirung, Gimhae National Museum, and Gimhae Passenger Terminal. Since ancient times, it has…

spots.name: Jillye-myeon
spots.desc: This village, nestled in the plains of a valley, is famous for showcasing the area's history and for making all types of pottery and clay pieces. An encouraged short trip "off the beaten path" is to walk the main street and shop the numerous pottery and craft stores. Also in Jillye-myeon is the Clayarch Gimhae Museum, which exhibits many works of art by local and regional artists, as well as some…

spots.name: suson jjajang
spots.desc: It is a Korean-style Chinese restaurant. Japchaebap and sweet and sour pork are delicious.

spots.name: Samil Dwitgogi
spots.desc: It sells a regional variation of Korean barbecue, called 'Dwitgogi', using unusual cuts of pork, such as jowl. 'Dwitgogi' means meat from behind, named because the cuts used to be traded unofficially from butchers, but such cuts are now legally traded and very popular among citizens.

spots.name: Dohyeongmin Restaurant
spots.desc: The main dishes of the restaurant inside and outside Gimhae, which is also famous for its Gimhae rice restaurant, include beef steak, pasta, and salad.

spots.name: Jangwonjeong
spots.desc: Jangwonjeong, a famous restaurant in Gimhae, is where you can enjoy hot pot rice and meat together. In particular, if you order hot pot rice, you can enjoy a generous amount of 7 side dishes made with homegrown ingredients, pork bulgogi, and grilled fish at Jangwonjeong.

spots.name: Haeru sushi
spots.desc: Harusushi is a rotating sushi restaurant located in Nae-dong, Gimhae, and is famous for its fresh ingredients and various kinds of sushi.

spots.name: bonghwang1935
spots.desc: A cafe with comfortable seats and delicious coffee. The atmosphere is so good. Quiet conversation in a sedentary room.

spots.name: Cafe Dahlia
spots.desc: It is a cafe building that won the Grand Prize in architecture. You can enjoy tea, coffee, and bread while looking at the mountain scenery.

spots.name: Poven
spots.desc: Poven is a specialty bakery cafe baked by Gyeongsangnam-do masters.

spots.name: Fruits Forest
spots.desc: The main branch of Fruit Forest is a cafe in Gimhae that offers a variety of desserts and drinks using fresh fruits.

spots.name: Chokseongnu Pavilion
spots.desc: Chokseongnu is in Jinju-seong. CNN ranked one of the 50 best places to hear if you visit Korea. The command base during the battles of Jinju, this beautiful pavilion is next to the cliff with commanding views across the river. During days of peace, civil service exams were held here.

spots.name: Nongae Shrine
spots.desc: Commemorates the gisaeng (courtesan) Nongae, who seduced a Japanese general after their victory in the second battle, and with her arms wrapped around him plunged from the cliff to her — and his — death. The yearly Nongae Festival commemorates the event.

spots.name: Eunyeolsa Shrine
spots.desc: The birthplace of Confucian scholar Gang Mincheom, the shrine is small but picture-perfect.

spots.name: Jinyang river
spots.desc: Jinyang Lake is an artificial lake and a lake where the Gyeong-ho River flowing from Sancheong-gun, Gyeong-sang namdo and Deokcheon River flowing from Jinju-si, Gyeong-sangnamdo meet. In spring, many cherry trees bloom near lakes and zoos, attracting many tourists from both families and lovers.
spots.price: Free for lake. Zoo: adults individual ₩1,000, group ₩800; youths, military police individual ₩800, group ₩600; children…

spots.name: Jinju Bronze Age Culture Museum
spots.desc: You can see the prosperous Daepyeong Village during the Bronze Age.

spots.name: Land and Housing Museum
spots.desc: The Land and Housing Museum is a specialized museum with the theme of Korean residential architecture culture and civil engineering construction technology. It first opened in Bundang, Gyeonggi-do in 1997, and was relocated to Jinju in 2015 and renovated.
spots.addr: Korea Land and Housing Corporation 19 Chungui-ro

spots.name: Jinju Children's Museum
spots.desc: It is a museum where children can touch and experience what is on display.
spots.hours: Tue-Sat 09:00-18:00 (Break Time: 12:00-13:00, closed Sun and Mon)
spots.price: 3-13 years old ₩13,000, 14 years old~adult ₩6,000, less than 3 years old free

spots.name: Nongae Festival
spots.desc: The Nongae Festival commemorates and celebrates the sacrifice of the beautiful and patriotic gisaeng (professional Korean entertainer) Nongae's suicide-assassination of a Japanese general together with the 70,000 Koreans who lost their lives in the battle of Jinju Castle during the Imjin War. The festival features an emotional reenactment of Nongae's suicidal drowning of a Japanese general from…

spots.name: Jinju National Bullfighting Contest
spots.desc: The Jinju National Bullfighting Contest is recognized as Korea's oldest bullfighting event and spectators can witness a test of strength at this bullfighting contest.
spots.hours: held at a purpose-built traditional Korean sports arena near Jinyang lake in August.

spots.name: Gaecheon Arts Festival
spots.desc: The entire city turns to the streets for celebration at Korea's first provincial culture art festival, which awakens the artistic spirit of the Korean people. The festival falls around Gaecheonjeol (National Foundation Day) and is widely regarded as one of Korea's finest.

spots.name: Jinju Namgang Lantern Festival
spots.desc: This nationally designated cultural tourism festival, found only in Jinju, features a spectacle of lanterns floating on the Nam River to commemorate the patriotic spirit of the 70,000 militia corps and government troops who died for their country defending Jinju from the Japanese forces during the Imjin War (1592–1598).
spots.hours: held in October for approximately ten days

spots.name: Kwan Namgaek Sikdang
spots.desc: Coffee, drinks and pretty decent bibimbap sets (₩5000). There's a bizarre collection of totem poles outside to stare at while you wait for your order.

spots.name: Yujeongjangeo
spots.desc: Specializes in amazing grilled eel. No English sign but easily spotted (it's the ornate traditional house). ₩22,000 for a saltwater Anguilla eel and the works, ₩27,000 for freshwater Conger eel, each set is designed to serves two if you order rice on the side (an extra ₩1,000). They'll halve the eel you get if you go in alone, but don't expect a discount. Open late which is good for festival…

spots.name: Subok Bread Restaurant
spots.desc: Subok Bread Restaurant is a traditional bakery located in Jinju Central Market in Gyeongsangnam-do, and steamed buns, honey bread, and patbingsu are popular. Steamed buns are soft with a lot of red bean paste, and honey bread is a combination of crispy outside and sweet inside. We recommend you to visit Open Run because waiting can occur on weekends.

spots.name: Ha Yeonok Ha Daedong Branch
spots.desc: When you order a meal, you'll get a fresh salad and hot seonjiguk. Jinju Mulnaengmyeon is served with cucumbers, egg garnish, beef jeon, and threaded red pepper. Dolpan beef chamgalbi is a premium grilled rib served with good ribs and delicious seasoning and grilled on charcoal.

spots.name: Ryo Ci
spots.desc: It is a restaurant where various Japanese menus are popular. Okonomiyaki and jirashisushi are especially popular. There are also a variety of sushi and rice bowls on the menu. It's perfect for dates or small gatherings, and we recommend you visit in time for opening on weekends because there may be waiting.

spots.name: Song Hwa-han set meal
spots.desc: It is a place where you can taste Jinju's unique Korean food. Private dining is possible because it consists of individual rooms, and special dishes such as deep-fried mushrooms with sweet and sour sauce, royal tteokbokki, and vegetable pancakes are especially impressive. Parking is available in the public parking lot in front of the store, and it is convenient to provide free parking when paying.

spots.name: Emperor's Restaurant
spots.desc: The Emperor's Restaurant is a Nopo restaurant with a tradition of more than 100 years located in the Jinju Central Market. The popular menu, beef tartare bibimbap, is a harmonious combination of fresh raw beef, sesame oil, herbs, and secret sauce. Also, grilled bulgogi and Korean beef jeon are popular menus, with group seats and seating areas, making them suitable for family gatherings and…

spots.name: Cafe. Born in September
spots.desc: There is a quiet cafe located in front of the university, a cafe mascot dog.

spots.name: Cafe Daylight
spots.desc: There are a lot of fun board games. After you give cookies and caramel and drink all the drinks, you can get a refill of iced Americano for ₩1,000.

spots.name: Here
spots.desc: Seasonal-varying granita and signature matcha latte are popular menus. Inside the cafe, warm lighting and neat interior make it a good place to visit alone or heal with friends. There are various seats, including group seats and sofa seats, so you can stay comfortably.

spots.name: Caped Pearl
spots.desc: You can enjoy a special coffee menu such as de Perlatte along with a variety of dessert menus such as salt bread and sculpture cake. It is popular with visitors because it is convenient to move by car due to its wide parking lot, and you can enjoy the beautiful natural scenery of Jinyang Lake together.

spots.name: Market Jinyang Lake
spots.desc: Market Jinyangho is a large cafe located in Jinju, with plenty of parking space and a picnic-like atmosphere with outdoor tables and plants. Various imported organic drinks and unique menus such as Dutch coffee and almond lattes are popular. It also sells organic snacks and imported snacks, making it good to visit with children, and you can accompany your dog.

spots.name: Sihwa
spots.desc: Tiny old streets on a hill side, with artistic paintings. Be quiet as people live in these small colorful houses. It was made famous by the drama Love and Ambition. At the top is a small resting area. The best place to spend an hour while waiting for your ferry.

spots.name: Gatbawi Literature Hall
spots.desc: Featuring information about famous writers from Mokpo. No English available.

spots.name: Mokpo Peace Plaza
spots.desc: It is the representative square of Mokpo, and it is a place where you can relax. You can enjoy the sea scenery during the day and the night view of Mokpo in the evening.

spots.name: Mokpo National Maritime University
spots.desc: The university comprises two colleges: the Maritime College, which trains merchant marine officers, and the College of Marine Engineering, which cultivates talent specialized in shipbuilding and maritime affairs. It also has a corps that selects officers for the Navy and Marine Corps. Since its founding, many alumni have gone on to work in shipping companies, shipyards, and government agencies…

spots.name: Gohado
spots.desc: Gohado Island is named after Yudalsan Mountain, Mokpo's highest mountain. Standing as if embracing the Mokpo coastline, the island clusters together and was strategically used by Admiral Yi Sun-sin's navy during the Imjin War to block enemy advances.

spots.name: Samhakdo
spots.desc: Three peaks rose from the spot where three cranes fell, giving rise to the current name Samhakdo. It was an island until the late 1960s, when reclamation of the waters off Mokpo transformed it into land. As of 2020, it has been transformed into a lake, offering a beautiful nighttime view.

spots.name: Mokpo Maritime Museum
spots.desc: This is the Mokpo Maritime Museum operated by the National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage. The Institute is the only national organization in Korea dedicated to excavating and researching underwater cultural heritage, as well as exhibiting its findings.The museum consists of four permanent exhibition halls, one special exhibition hall, an outdoor exhibition area, and a…

spots.name: Mokpo Natural History Museum
spots.desc: The Mokpo Natural History Museum features modern exhibits on the 4.6-billion-year history of the Earth, with displays of dinosaur fossils, minerals, insects, birds, and marine life. It also presents materials representing the history and culture of Korea’s southwestern region.
spots.hours: closed Mon; open 9:00-18:00; last entry 1 hour before closing.
spots.price: Adults: ₩3,000 Teenagers / Soldiers: ₩2,000 Elementary school students: ₩1,000 Preschoolers: ₩500

spots.name: Mokpo Marine Cable Car North Port Station
spots.desc: The Mokpo Marine Cable Car serves as a new hub of marine tourism, leisure, and cultural sightseeing, offering a panoramic view of Mokpo’s old downtown—the historic center of Slow City Mokpo—along with North Port, Yudalsan Mountain, and the beautiful scenery of the Dadohae, including Gohado Island. Taking into account the topography and outstanding landscape of Yudalsan, the cable car spans 3.23…

spots.name: Mokpo Peace Plaza Marine Leisure Experience Classroom
spots.desc: This activity allows you to experience marine leisure sports in the waters off Mokpo Peace Plaza. You can try kayaking, paddleboating, and jet boating. It operates annually from September to October, and you should check the website for detailed schedules. Admission is free, but reservations for activities must be made online.

spots.name: Samhakdo Cruise
spots.desc: You can enjoy the Mokpo coastline aboard a cruise that can accommodate up to 890 passengers. Each cruise lasts approximately 1 hour and 20 minutes. It departs from Samhakdo Island and passes 14 locations, including Mokpo Bridge, before returning. The route may change depending on weather conditions.
spots.price: Fireworks Busking Cruise: ₩35,000 (adult) ₩22.000 (minor) / Samhakdo Cruise: ₩20,000 (adult), ₩12,000 (minor) / Sunset…

spots.name: Mokpo Harbor Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival held around October every year at Mokpo Port and Samhakdo Island. In the year 25, it took place from Sept. 26 to Sept. 28. The timing of the festival may vary every year, so please refer to the linked site. The festival allows visitors to enjoy the traditions of Mokpo. You can cook seasonal seafood purchased through an auction on the spot.

spots.name: Mokpo World Madang Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival where artists from eight countries, including Laos and China, participate in overseas guest performances and parties where you can experience free markets, food trucks, and beer.

spots.name: Myeongin House
spots.desc: Myeongin House is known for its braised dishes such as braised hairtail, fresh cod soup, and braised butterfish. Both soy sauce marinated crab and spicy marinated crab are also considered local delicacies. Visitors can enjoy a variety of traditional southern Korean dishes.

spots.name: Manseongri Black Sand Beach
spots.desc: As the only black sand beach in Korea, Manseongri is the liveliest beach in Yeosu with lots of restaurants and cafes along the beach. Along the coast line between Manseongri and Yeosu train station is located Marae Tunnel, the only natural rock tunnel in Korea.
