spots.name: Milyang Pork Soup
spots.desc: Warm Pork Soup.

spots.name: gaya milmyeon
spots.desc: Delicious Wheat Noodles. Warm pork dumplings.

spots.name: Tin Shui Restaurant
spots.desc: They sell yukhoe and lime bulgogi.

spots.name: Jasan Park
spots.desc: View of Yeosu. Statue of Yi Sun Shin.

spots.name: Rotary Restaurant
spots.desc: ₩10,000, clean taste and side dishes can be refilled.

spots.name: Parks
spots.desc: Gwangmyeong has several large parks. A Hyeonchung Neighborhood Park is 34,586 m². This park is also called Hyeonchung Pagoda Park. One of the neighborhood parks in Gwangmyeong-si, located across from Cheolsan Complex 20. It was built on a mountain 50 m high. The trails are well polished up the mountain. At the top of the mountain, a memorial tower is erected, and around the tower there are sports…

spots.name: National Folk Museum Children's Museum
spots.desc: This place provides various experiences and services for children in areas such as exhibitions, education, research, and exchange.

spots.name: Seoul Museum of Education
spots.desc: The Seoul Education Museum opened on June 15, 1995, by displaying relics and photographs on educational systems, curriculum, educational contents, educational institutions, and educational activities to establish the status of Seoul education and present a bright future for future generations in the 21st century.

spots.name: Samcheong Sujaebi
spots.desc: Canteen style ambiance, renowned for serving good Sujaebi - a mild soup where the noodles are flattened and torn into sheets. Always packed with people so be prepared for a queue.

spots.name: Uiwang Rail Park
spots.desc: Visitor facility around Wangsong Lake with rail-bike-related attractions. Check the official website for operating dates/hours (weather and season can affect service).

spots.name: Uirimji Irrigation Reservoir and the Woods on the Bank in Jecheon
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see reservoirs and willow forests from the Three Kingdoms period in Mosan-dong, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do.

spots.name: Gwanghallu Gardens
spots.desc: It is a garden built in the early Joseon Dynasty, and there is Gwangallu Pavilion where Chunhyang and Lee Do-ryeong met in Korean classical literature, and the garden where the Gwangallu Pavilion is located is collectively called Gwangalluwon (廣寒樓園).

spots.name: Daejin Beach
spots.desc: A small beach beside Daejin fishing port. The water is shallow and the waves are moderate, which makes it popular for surfing. There is free parking for about 50 cars.

spots.name: Dojjaebigol Haerang Observatory
spots.desc: A footbridge that runs out over the sea, with sections of glass and steel-mesh floor so you can watch the waves break beneath your feet. It stays closed in bad weather.

spots.name: Kkamak Rock
spots.desc: A black rock just offshore, named for the crows (kkamagwi) said to have nested on it; it is also said to lie due east of Namdaemun gate in Seoul. According to local legend, a village headman of the Joseon era was reborn as an octopus to drive off Japanese pirates and still lives in a cave beneath the rock. An octopus statue on the shore marks the story.

spots.name: Mukho Byeolbit Village Observatory
spots.desc: A viewing platform above Mukho Port, built between 2016 and 2021 as part of a project to renew the hillside neighborhood. The houses on the way up have brightly painted roofs and walls, and the platform looks straight down over the harbor.

spots.name: Mukho Lighthouse
spots.desc: First lit in 1963, the lighthouse stands on a hill 67 m above the sea and looks down on Mukho Port. The present 24-m tower, rebuilt in 2007, has an observation deck just below the lantern, and its light can be seen up to 48 km out at sea. The plaza in front has a small exhibition on lighthouses and a monument to the 1968 film Miwodo Dasi Hanbeon, which was shot here.

spots.name: Nongoldam-gil
spots.desc: Four steep lanes (Deungdaeoreum-gil and Nongol 1-, 2- and 3-gil) climb from the harbor to Mukho Lighthouse through a fishing village where people still live. The walls are covered in murals and short poems about life in the port in its busier days. There is no parking in the lanes, and they are not suitable for wheelchairs.

spots.name: Pencil Museum
spots.desc: Billed as Korea's first pencil museum. Exhibits show how graphite becomes a pencil, and the collection of more than 3,000 pencils, gathered by the curator in over 100 cities around the world, includes some you can pick up and try.

spots.name: Mangsang beach
spots.desc: Popular beach area 8 km north of the town. Very crowded in the summer, with a very small amusement park area with a batting cage and a few rides.

spots.name: Chuam Beach
spots.desc: A less popular but more picturesque beach a few km south of town.

spots.name: Hansom Beach
spots.desc: There is a 2.2km sea path, so you can walk while looking at the sea. There is also a photo zone where you can take pictures in the Hanseom Light Tunnel.

spots.name: Yuchunji by Mureung
spots.desc: You can enjoy sightseeing by riding various experience facilities (Sky Glider, Alpine Coaster, etc.) and trains by Mureung.
spots.price: Adults ₩6,000 (June–September), ₩4000 (October–May) Senior citizens, people with disabilities, and national merit…
spots.addr: Igi-ro 97 Ie-ro, 2nd parking lot of Yucheonji by Mureung

spots.name: Dojjaebigol Sky Valley
spots.desc: A recreation area near Mukho Lighthouse with a skywalk, Sky Cycle and Giant Slide. The skywalk has a transparent glass floor overlooking the sea. The Sky Cycle is a bicycle ride along a cable above the valley and is open only to riders at least 140 cm tall. The Giant Slide descends about 27 m down a cylindrical slide.
spots.hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 (Apr–Oct), 10:00–17:00 (Nov–Mar); closed Mon (or the following business day when Mon is a public…
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000; teenagers and children ₩2,000; free for children aged 6 and under; Giant Slide ₩3,000; Sky Cycle ₩15,000

spots.name: Eodal Beach
spots.desc: A small beach with a 300-m-long and 20–30-m-wide shoreline. It has fine sand, a gentle slope and shallow water averaging about 1 m deep.

spots.name: Haeparang Trail Course 34
spots.desc: A 14.5-km section of the Haeparang Trail that takes about 5 hours to walk and is rated easy. Starting near Mukho Station, the route passes Mukho Lighthouse Park, Daejin Port and Mangsang Beach before continuing into Okgye, Gangneung. The route combines coastal paths, fishing villages and a forested valley section. call 1588-7417

spots.name: Chuam Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: A 72-m-long suspension bridge over the sea at Chuam Beach, opened in June 2019. It offers views of the surrounding coastline and Chotdaebawi Rock. It may be closed in rain, snow or strong winds. Free parking is available, and the bridge is wheelchair-accessible.

spots.name: E-MART
spots.desc: The only big chain retailer in town. They offer everything from food to clothes and electronics (think wal-mart). Apart from them, there are a number of shops in the downtown area offering your usual services. English will be limited however and bargaining is not too common in the retail stores.

spots.name: Mukho Port Live Fish Market
spots.desc: Seafood market with around 70 stalls selling live and fresh fish and seafood, including squid, flounder, octopus and snow crab depending on the season. Fish bought here can be prepared as hoe (Korean-style raw fish) and eaten at nearby restaurants for an additional charge.

spots.name: Janjanhage
spots.desc: A travel bookshop in Mukho, a 3-minute walk from Mukho Station. Parking is available nearby, and pets are welcome.

spots.name: Mukoya
spots.desc: A small souvenir shop near Mukho Lighthouse selling Mukho-themed gifts.

spots.name: Ottogi Restaurant
spots.desc: Spicy noodle soup and dumpling soup are typical dishes, and visitors can experience what the locals eat.

spots.name: Hosan Bakery
spots.desc: Breads like glutinous rice doughnuts and twisted bread stick are a favorite and relatively inexpensive.

spots.name: Cafe Hyunsangso
spots.desc: It has an antique look with a European vibe and outdoor tables to enjoy the natural scenery. And almost everywhere is a photo spot.

spots.name: Dongnam Hoejip
spots.desc: A plain local seafood restaurant known for flounder mulhoe (cold raw fish soup) and boneless flounder hoe. It also serves pufferfish soup (bokjiri).

spots.name: Mukho Gimbap
spots.desc: A small takeout shop whose gimbap is packed with egg, popular for a cheap lunch or a snack before a train. Also sells fish-cake bars, tteokbokki and fried snacks.

spots.name: Geodong Tangsuyuk
spots.desc: Korean-Chinese restaurant whose tangsuyuk (sweet-and-sour fried pork) has cubes of octopus inside the pork loin, in original or spicy versions. Also serves octopus jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup) and jajangmyeon. Waits of an hour or more are common (waiting list via the Catch Table app), last orders are 40 minutes before closing, and there is no parking.

spots.name: 103LAB
spots.desc: A small cafe on the mural lanes with window seats looking over the harbor. The owners look after local street cats, so you may share the room with one.

spots.name: Hwanseon Cave
spots.desc: You can reach the entrance of Hwanseon Cave after passing the ticket office, several traditional houses, a bridge, waterfall, and 398 iron stairs. 448 wild plants grow around the cave. It is also possible to take a monorail ride after the ticket office (return ticket ₩5,000, one-way ₩3,000), but this is not really worth it, and if busy will take longer than walking (walk is about 30 minutes from…

spots.name: Daegeum Cave
spots.desc: Daegeum begins with a monorail ride uphill. The Daegeum monorail offers a seven minute journey. Daegeumgul Cave’s monorail carries visitors into a hidden underworld, passing beautiful stalactites and rock formations on the way. Be sure to book this in advance, as in high season it might be fully booked. Booking can be done at the Tourist information booth outside the bus station.

spots.name: Haesindang Park
spots.desc: It is a place where people can take a walk along the pine tree trail along the park. In addition, there is an exhibition hall where people can feel the life of fishing villages.

spots.name: Jangho Beach
spots.desc: There is Yonghwa Beach in between, so it is also called Yonghwa Jangho Beach, and there is Jangho Port on the right, so you can enjoy fresh seafood at a cheap price.

spots.name: Yonghwa Beach
spots.desc: There is Jangho Port nearby, so you can buy fresh seafood at a low price, and you can also tour the cave by cruise ship. Wolmido Island, which is composed of three large rock islands in front of the beach, has many fish, so you can enjoy fishing.

spots.name: Maengbang Beach
spots.desc: It is called Samcheok's first beach due to its wide white sand beach, shallow water, and gentle slope, and it is well equipped with convenience facilities compared to other beaches.

spots.name: Samcheok Monorail
spots.desc: It started operating in April 2010. So, it became easier to see the Hwanseonggul Cave and the Daegeumgul Cave.
spots.price: Round trip (adult, adolescent) ₩7000, one-way (adult, adolescent) ₩4000, round trip (elementary school students) ₩3000…

spots.name: Samcheok Beach
spots.desc: Behind the beach, pine forests are dense, and there are sushi restaurants, guest houses, and hotels nearby. On the southern beach, there is a small scale of Hujin Beach, where you can enjoy swimming and fishing at the same time.

spots.name: Beach Sculpture Park
spots.desc: One of the main attractions along the Millennium Coastal Road is the octagonal pavilion after passing through a dense pine forest, where visitors can enjoy sea views and the Millennium Road. Small concert halls located by the sea sometimes hold performances.

spots.name: Samcheok Vitality Healing Forest
spots.desc: It is a forest created to provide forest healing services to the people by utilizing the phytoncide, anion, landscape, and sound of the forest.

spots.name: Leesabusaja Park
spots.desc: The space was created to commemorate the achievements of General Isabu during the Shilla Dynasty. Inside the park, you can feel the history while walking along various sculptures and trails. Also, you can enjoy a beautiful view of the sea off Samcheok.

spots.name: Mugeon-ri Moss Falls
spots.desc: It features a view of a waterfall that flows coolly with moss-covered rocks in a dense forest.

spots.name: Dogye Wood World
spots.desc: A variety of attractions and experience programs are prepared to help you understand trees more interestingly and informally

spots.name: Bunam Beach
spots.desc: The natural environment is well preserved, and visitors can do not only bathing but also fishing on the rocks of the seashore.

spots.name: Jeungsan Beach
spots.desc: Adjacent to Chuam Beach located in Donghae-si, visitors can see the sunrise of Chuam Chotdaebawi Rock at a glance, and there is a winter sea harmonized with a flock of seagulls.

spots.name: Wonpyeong Beach
spots.desc: There is a dense pine forest in the back, and a marine rail bike passes by. It was selected as one of the 50 quiet beaches selected by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

spots.name: Sinnam Beach
spots.desc: It is a small beach facing National Route 7, 30km south of Samcheok. The length of the beach is about 100 m, which is small and compact, with a sand field of about 100m, and there are many seashores beyond it.

spots.name: Shinum Mountain
spots.desc: Autumn leaves and wild flowers bloom in spring. There are also shelters and observation decks around.

spots.name: Samcheok Rose Park
spots.desc: A total of 218 types of 10 million roses are the world's largest single-scale park. It is a cultural and recreational space with various recreational and convenient facilities such as walking paths and photo zones, rose tunnels, event gardens, floor fountains, grass squares, barefoot parks, inline skating rinks, trails, and bicycle paths.

spots.name: Gungchon Beach
spots.desc: It consists of shallow waters, beaches, and dense pine forests, and has amenities such as a campground and parking lot. The beach opens from July 10 to Aug. 20.

spots.name: Dogye Glass Village
spots.desc: It is a village that promotes industrialization of the national core period and future knowledge base by converting it to eco-friendly and high value-added industries by developing new materials using local waste resources and glass products using waste. It is an experience village where you can experience glass crafts, and mine coal obtained from coal mines, which are waste resources in the…

spots.name: Samcheok Central Market
spots.desc: It sells a variety of agricultural products, marine products, and local specialties. Local residents and visitors can buy fresh ingredients and household items, and enjoy various foods in the market.

spots.name: Flea Market
spots.desc: Seafood, agricultural products, and various household items can be purchased here at low prices. In particular, a variety of specialties produced in Samcheok are sold, so you can experience local food and culture.

spots.name: Sol Beach Samcheok Ocean Play
spots.desc: It is a water park within the resort. It has various water play facilities against the backdrop of the sea, and offers indoor and outdoor swimming pools, running water pools, and amusement facilities for children.

spots.name: Gagok sulfur Bath Experience Center
spots.desc: It offers a foot bath experience using sulfur hot spring water. It has sulfur water that naturally rises from the underground, so visitors can take care of your health and rest at the same time.

spots.name: Maengbang Yuchae Flower Village
spots.desc: The canola flower festival is held in April every year, and it is a place where visitors can experience strawberries farming and seasonal farming.

spots.name: Sea of Japan
spots.desc: See the Sea of Japan. The beaches are not the most beautiful in the world but at night you might get to see a lot of Korean groups burning fireworks at the beach. There are numerous pagodas and observation areas for sunsets with fishing ships in the foreground. Also, the Lighthouse Observatory offers a better-than-average view of the sea.

spots.name: Sokcho Expo Tower
spots.desc: You can get to the 15th floor and have an amazing view of the city.

spots.name: Sokcho Beach
spots.desc: The length of the white sand beach is 2 km long, including Cheongho-dong, Joyang-dong, and Daepo-dong, and the opening is 1 km and 75 m wide, reaching 29,752 m (about 9,000 pyeong), and the quality of the sand is good as well as clean water and pine forests, making parks, flower roads, and trails popular among Sokcho citizens. In addition, along with Seoraksan Mountain, Cheoksan Hot Spring…

spots.name: Biking
spots.desc: Take a bike ride around Yeongnangho Lake The lake funnels into the East Sea and takes about an hour on bike to get fully around the lake. Some stops along the way include Bombawi, a rock shaped like a crouched tiger which offers views of downtown, pagodas and temples.

spots.name: Seorak Hanwha Waterpia
spots.desc: Korea's largest hot springs theme park with huge hot springs facilities such as modern facilities using natural spring water that comes out of the ground at 49 °C, outdoor leisure spa facilities, pulp wood baths and warm water baths at 8 °C. Visitors can enjoy various types of spas against the background of the ulsan stones that stand out like folding screens - the landmark of Gangwon-do.

spots.name: Sokcho Sea Boat
spots.desc: It is the only cable ferry in the country that can only be found in Sokcho. Now, Cheongho Bridge and Seorak Bridge have been opened, so it is easy to cross the sea, but Sokcho-si designated the seashore as a tourist product and maintained it for tourists' experience.

spots.name: Sokcho Tourist & Fishery Market
spots.desc: A big seafood market worth visiting. It contains different sections catering to fresh seafood, fresh vegetables, household goods and finally cooked foods. There are many stalls selling battered / tempura style seafood such as crab legs, squid and prawns. There are also takeaway steamed crab stalls which offer a more affordable way of trying the local crab than many of the crab restaurants in the…

spots.name: Wangshiprigoihanmadang
spots.desc: For ₩13,000 (₩12,000 if you buy a drink) you can eat an unlimited amount of meat, octopus, fish, and mandu. All of the standard types of pork are available, and they even have chicken marinated in some yellow stuff. Many foreigners staying at the House Hostel go there because the proprietor duly recommends it to everyone. There are also stray cats that lurk around which are fun to feed the fish…

spots.name: Mansuk Sweet and Sour Chicken
spots.desc: As the name gives away, this chain restaurant is popular for its chicken dishes.

spots.name: Hang-A-Ri Mulhoe in Sokcho
spots.desc: Sashimi dish where you scoop the flesh of flatfish, sea bream, fish, and shellfish, cut them finely, season them, mix them with soy sauce, and pour cold water.

spots.name: sokcho_gobuk_e
spots.desc: It is a bar around Sokcho Beach where various snacks are prepared.

spots.name: Café GID
spots.desc: Modern hill-view café overlooking Ulsanbawi Mountain; peaceful and scenic.

spots.name: Café Badamada
spots.desc: Multi-floor ocean-view café near Yeongnang Lake; famous for desserts and rooftop views.

spots.name: Café BaeTago
spots.desc: Ocean-view café above Sokcho Central Market; picnic-set rental and sea breeze terrace.

spots.name: Café Hindajeong
spots.desc: Minimalist white-tone café offering handcrafted drinks and calm seating.

spots.name: Café SiDNua
spots.desc: Plant-filled space with high ceilings and panoramic windows; pet-friendly.

spots.name: Café One Fine Day
spots.desc: Trendy dessert café by the coast; popular for “corn latte” and wide sea view.

spots.name: Café Shelter
spots.desc: Rooftop café right on the seafront; excellent sunrise view and coffee blends.

spots.name: Café Another Blue
spots.desc: Roastery-style café on Jangsa Beach with sea breeze and signature bakery.

spots.name: Café Chodang Coffee Mill
spots.desc: Rustic café themed after an old coffee mill; famous for espresso tonic.

spots.name: Café Hide
spots.desc: Sea-view café near Daepo Harbor; glass façade with modern seating and brunch menu.

spots.name: Taebaeksan National Park (태백산국립공원)
spots.desc: The city’s crown jewel. The 1,567-m Taebaeksan is sacred in Korean mythology and offers sweeping views, ancient Yew forests, and the famous Cheonjedan altar at the summit. Popular in winter for snow-covered landscapes.

spots.name: Hwangji Pond
spots.desc: Located in the city center, this pond is the legendary source of the 510-km-long Nakdong River. About 5,000 tons of water gush out daily from this spring, which is surrounded by a small public park.

spots.name: Yongyeon Cave
spots.desc: It was designated as a Gangwon State monument on February 26, 1980, as a limestone cave created by the gradual dissolution of limestone deposited in the ancient Ordovician period in the past hundreds of years in rainwater and groundwater. It is about 843m in length and has a large square with a width of 50 m and a height of 30 m inside the cave. The temperature inside the cave is 9 to 11 °C, and…

spots.name: Gumunso
spots.desc: A unique geological formation where the Hwangji-cheon stream has pierced through a massive limestone rock over millions of years, creating a natural stone gate and waterfall. It is a major Paleozoic site with various fossils visible in the area.

spots.name: Maebongsan Windy Hill
spots.desc: A vast highland area at 1,303m above sea level covered with cabbage fields and giant wind turbines. It offers panoramic views of the Baekdudaegan mountain range.
spots.hours: Open 24 hours (Shuttle buses operate during summer)

spots.name: Manggyeonsa Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple atop Taebaek-san. There is a store selling snacks and (non-alcoholic) drinks for hikers.

spots.name: Taebaek Coal Museum
spots.desc: One of the largest coal museums in the world. It provides a comprehensive look at the history of the coal industry, mining techniques, and the daily lives of miners through realistic dioramas and an experience tunnel.

spots.name: Taebaek Paleozoic Museum
spots.desc: Located next to Gumunso, this museum focuses on the Paleozoic era. It features an extensive collection of fossils, including trilobites and orthocones found in the surrounding limestone layers.

spots.name: Chujeon Station
spots.desc: The highest railway station in South Korea, located at an elevation of 855m. While regular passenger trains no longer stop here frequently, it remains a popular photo spot for its symbolic altitude and snowy winter scenery.

spots.name: Aurora Park
spots.desc: Built on the site of the former Tongni Station, this theme park features scale models of five famous high-altitude railway stations from around the world, including Switzerland's Jungfraujoch and the USA's Pikes Peak. It features a 32-meter-high observation tower that offers panoramic views of the mountain terrain and the historic switchback railway tracks.

spots.name: Mountain climbing
spots.desc: Climbing Taebaek-san is the main attraction in Taebaek city. Mt. Taebaek is one of the higher peaks of Korea and the area around the mountain has been designed a provincial park. The peak is criss-crossed with numerous hiking trails but none of them overly strenuous. At a reasonable rate a hiker can expect to reach the summit in about two hours. From the Taebaek Bus Station (located across the…

spots.name: Hiking to Cheonjedan
spots.desc: The most iconic activity in Taebaek. The trail from Yuilsa to the summit (Cheonjedan) is relatively gentle and takes about 3–4 hours round trip. It is world-famous for its "frost flowers" (rime ice) on the yew trees during winter.

spots.name: Stargazing at Windy Hill
spots.desc: Thanks to the high altitude and minimal light pollution, Maebongsan Windy Hill is a premier spot for stargazing and photographing the Milky Way. Visitors often visit late at night to see the stars above the giant wind turbines.

spots.name: Coal Mine Tunnel Tour
spots.desc: Some former mines offer guided tours into retired tunnels — an atmospheric look into Taebaek’s past.

spots.name: 365 Safe Town
spots.desc: A world-class safety-themed experience park. It features 4D simulations of natural disasters (earthquakes, wildfires, floods), a hero experience center, and outdoor activities like ziplining and cable cars. Most of the entrance fee is returned as a local voucher to spend within the city.
spots.price: ₩22,000 (includes a ₩20,000 Taebaek Love Gift Certificate back)

spots.name: O2 Resort Sledding Park
spots.desc: During the winter, O2 Resort operates one of the longest sledding slopes in the region. It is a popular family activity for those who find skiing too difficult but still want to enjoy the snow.

spots.name: Taebaeksan Mountain Snow Festival
spots.desc: Held every January in Taebaeksan National Park and downtown. Features large snow sculptures, sledding, night illuminations, and local food stalls. The festival attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors who come to see the majestic white landscape of the city.

spots.name: Taebaek Sunflower Festival
spots.desc: Held in Guwau Village, this festival features a sea of over a million sunflowers. Visitors can walk through the fields, visit small art exhibitions, and enjoy the cool summer breeze of the highlands.

spots.name: Hwangji Free Market
spots.desc: The largest and most central traditional market in the city. It is the best place to buy dried mountain herbs, fresh local vegetables, and traditional snacks. There are also many small eateries hidden in the alleys of the market.

spots.name: Tongni 5-Day Market
spots.desc: A massive open-air market that only opens on dates ending in 5. It has a long history and offers a raw, authentic market atmosphere. You can find everything from livestock and farming tools to regional delicacies. It is located near the Tongni Station area.

spots.name: Nonghyup Hanaro Mart (Taebaek Branch)
spots.desc: The primary local supermarket for residents. It is a reliable place to buy certified Taebaek Hanu (beef) and packaged local agricultural products (like dried thistle) with clear pricing and quality assurance.

spots.name: Hyundai Silbi
spots.desc: A historic beef restaurant that has been serving locals for decades. They use charcoal fires to grill high-grade Hanu. Their "Galbisal" (rib meat) is highly recommended for its marbling and tenderness.

spots.name: Taebaek Hanu Silbi
spots.desc: Located slightly away from the main market area, this place is renowned for its fresh, thick-cut beef and delicious side dishes. The "Kkot-dungsim" (ribeye) is a standout here.

spots.name: Taebaek Dakgalbi
spots.desc: Perhaps the most famous spot in town, featured on various Korean food shows including "Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef." It is known for its generous use of wild greens (naengi) which adds a unique aroma to the spicy broth. Be sure to order fried rice (bokkeumbap) at the end.

spots.name: Kim Seo-bang-ne Dakgalbi
spots.desc: A highly-regarded local alternative to the more tourist-heavy spots. The broth is deep and flavorful, and many locals prefer this location for its consistent quality and generous portions of noodles and vegetables.

spots.name: Sanchae Sikdang
spots.desc: A well-established restaurant located right at the entrance of Taebaeksan National Park (Danggol area). It specializes in Sanchae-bibimbap made with fresh mountain herbs and various wild greens. It is a classic choice for hikers descending from the mountain.

spots.name: Sarang-bang
spots.desc: Famous for its Gondre-namul-bap (thistle rice), another mountain specialty of the Gangwon region. The rice is steamed with seasoned thistle and served with various side dishes, offering a healthy and earthy flavor.

spots.name: Mong-to-rang Goat Farm Cafe
spots.desc: Located on a high-altitude ranch at 800m above sea level, this cafe offers a spectacular view of the entire Taebaek city. It is famous for its fresh goat milk, goat milk yogurt, and soft-serve ice cream. Visitors can enjoy their drinks on the outdoor terrace while watching goats roam freely.

spots.name: Cafe Geonneol-mok
spots.desc: A must-visit themed cafe located right next to the railway tracks. It is world-famous for its Yeontan-ppang (bread shaped like a coal briquette) and Yeontan Latte, paying tribute to Taebaek's mining history. The interior is spacious and decorated with vintage mining artifacts.

spots.name: Tapdong Valley
spots.desc: A 6-km-long valley running between Wangbangsan Mountain, 7 km east of Dongducheon City, and Guksabong Peak. Gwangam-dong and Wangbang Village are located in the area, and it was selected as a local heritage of Gyeonggi-do. The name 'Tap-dong' of 'Tapdong Valley' comes from the fact that there was a three-story stone pagoda that was built around the end of the Goryeo period. However, the…
spots.addr: 5 km from City Hall to Pocheon, Local Road No. 364

spots.name: Do Dream Music Center
spots.desc: The Dudream Music Center was launched in October 2017 through the K-Rock Village Project as part of the balanced regional development project in Gyeonggi-do. The first floor contains a concert hall, the second an exhibition hall, and the third recording and practice rooms. It is a concert hall with a practice room and a recording room, and you can use it.

spots.name: Freedom Protection Peace Museum
spots.desc: It is a museum built to honor the will of those who sacrificed to protect their understanding of the forgotten Korean War and to promote friendship with U.N. participants. The museum is located in Soyosan Mountain, well known as the Salt River in Gyeonggi Province in Gyeonggi Province, where visitors can enjoy sightseeing and hiking.

spots.name: North Gyeonggi Children's Museum
spots.desc: The Gyeonggi Northern Children's Museum is a provincial museum with exhibitions designed for children. In addition, performances, experiences, and seminars for children are held.

spots.name: Dongducheon Local History Museum
spots.desc: It has about 1,000 items, including local relics and household items from Dongducheon, as exhibits.

spots.name: Dongducheon Rock Festival
spots.desc: It was born as a historical background of the city, which was responsible for the creation of Western culture with the presence of the 2nd U.S. Division at the end of the Korean War. It is also the longest-running music festival in the country since the first Dongducheon Rock Festival was held in 1999 based on the historical assets of the region, the birthplace of Korean rock.

spots.name: Soyo Maple Culture Festival
spots.desc: It is one of the representative festivals of Dongducheon, which began in 1986 to promote the beauty of autumn leaves and is held throughout Dongducheon-si and Soyosan Mountain at the end of October every year.

spots.name: Dongducheon Arts Festival
spots.desc: Every November, eight affiliated organizations (Korean traditional music, literature, art, entertainment, music, theater, photographers, and filmmakers' associations) participate jointly, and various events such as various cultural and artistic performances and exhibitions are held.

spots.name: Dongducheon Constellation Science Festival
spots.desc: The Dongducheon Constellation Science Festival, hosted by Dongducheon City and organized by the social organization Eosoo Association, is held annually at the Dongducheon Sports Complex at the end of September. It is divided into competitive fields, experience and exhibition fields, and science exploration fields to instill great dreams and hopes for science to teenagers.

spots.name: Dongducheon Jungang Market
spots.desc: Dongducheon Jungang Market was established in 1967 when the market moved from Dongducheon-dong to Saengyeon-dong. The center of Dongducheon-si, to Saengyeon-dong, and the market was formed mainly for daily foods, primary foods, and processed foods.

spots.name: Dongducheon Jeil Market
spots.desc: Jeil Market has been opened since 1960 by coexisting with a nearby large market, and mainly deals with clothing, and stores such as furniture and shoes have been opened.

spots.name: Dongducheon Keun Market
spots.desc: The Keun Market has been opened naturally since 1960 by bartering food produced by farmers in nearby areas, and up to five days of wholesale and retail trade and barter of agricultural and livestock products have been in operation.

spots.name: Dongducheon Yankee Market
spots.desc: The Yankee Market in Dongducheon is full of unique clothes, hats, and equipment worn by special forces personnel in movies, and it is an interesting market just to look around. In the 1960s, when the local economy of Dongducheon was revitalized around the 2nd Infantry Division, stores and entertainment establishments that mainly sold supplies and imports of U.S. troops were concentrated around…

spots.name: Se-A Plaza
spots.desc: Se-A Plaza Market was opened in March 1993 and is adjacent to the large market as a residential and commercial complex with cooling and heating facilities.

spots.name: Lake Restaurant Main Store
spots.desc: It was introduced in "The Three Great Kings of Jongwon Baek, Budaejjigae".
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00 - 21:30, closed on the 2nd and 4th Sundays every month

spots.name: Pyeongnam Myeonok
spots.desc: Pyeongnam Myeonok, a cold noodle restaurant that serves buckwheat and dongchimi. You can enjoy the same menu in all four seasons, including Pyongyang-style cold noodles with 40 years of tradition, spicy seasoned spicy cold noodles, seasoned field that you can't eat anywhere, and Pyeonyuk boiled with rice straw and juicy.

spots.name: Songwolgwan
spots.desc: Songwolgwan is a 100-year-old store that has been loved by customers for more than 30 years, and has been officially certified by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups for its excellence and growth potential.

spots.name: Pine Hill Coffee House
spots.desc: The quiet natural scenery and relaxation with professional barista coffee, British scone by professional patissier, French Black Tea, and cake macaroons in the garden of 66,116 m².

spots.name: Oreum
spots.desc: 'Oreum' is a brunch cafe. You can enjoy a variety of brunch menus such as drinks, pasta, pizza, and risotto.

spots.name: Wangbangjigi
spots.desc: It is a cafe with a valley in front of Dongducheon Natural Recreation Forest.

spots.name: Cafe Authentic
spots.desc: A healing cafe with a vintage atmosphere that blends three attractive spaces and a wide outdoor area. Dark and fragrant coffee, carefully made homemade drinks, and various desserts go well together. It has been in the same place in Dongducheon for a long time, providing comfort with an interior that is not seen anywhere.

spots.name: Bugeun-ri Dolmen
spots.desc: A prehistoric burial site listed as a , the largest stone here is 2.6×7.1×5.5 meters in size and weighs somewhere between 150 and 225 tons. Hourly buses from Ganghwa-eup. There is another cluster of dolmen at Gocheon-ri (고천리).

spots.name: Ganghwa Stone Water Gate
spots.desc: The floodgates of the Joseon Dynasty in Sinmun-ri, Ganghwa-eup. It is Incheon Metropolitan City Tangible Cultural Property No. 30.

spots.name: Ganghwa Gapgotdon
spots.desc: Gapgot Dondae is an important fortress where Goryeo moved its capital to Ganghwa Island from 1232 to 1270, protecting the Ganghwa Strait in the war against Mongolia,.

spots.name: Bomunsa (보문사)
spots.desc: High up on Seokmodo Island, this temple is located in a scenic grotto with rock carvings and is famous as a place for women to pray for sons. Getting there is half the fun: take a bus from Ganghwa-eup to Oepo-ri (30 min, every 30 min), cross by ferry to Seokmodo (W2000; 10 min, every 30 min), and then take a shuttle bus (W1000) to the temple.

spots.name: Ganwha Chamsungdan
spots.desc: Ganghwa Chamseongdan is an altar located at the top of Mani Mountain, Heungwang-ri, Hwado-myeon. It is known that Dangun (檀君) was built during the ancient period, and on July 11, 1964, it was designated as Korea's Historic Site No. 136.

spots.name: The Amoene Cafe
spots.desc: A coffeeshop with a most peculiar slanted architecture, including some slanted elements inside. It stands close to another peculiar house: the Upside-down House, which offers overnight stays.

spots.name: Gwacheon National Science Museum
spots.desc: Indoor exhibitions introduce science, technology and natural history, with interactive displays and outdoor exhibits. A useful option for families or a rainy day. Check the museum website for programme bookings and any separate charges.
spots.hours: 09:30–17:30; ticket sales close at 16:30. Closed Mondays, January 1, Seollal and Chuseok; if Monday is a public…

spots.name: Gwanaksan
spots.desc: The mountain on Gwacheon's western side. Trails lead towards Yeonjuam and the rocky summit area at Yeonjudae. The route from Gwacheon Hyanggyo is one way to approach the mountain; see the hiking advice below.

spots.name: Yeonjudae
spots.desc: A small cliffside Buddhist site near the Gwanaksan summit, with Nahanjeon Hall set among the rocks. It is a separate site from Yeonjuam, a short distance to the south. Take care on the rocky paths near the summit.
spots.hours: Visiting hours are not published; hike in daylight and check trail conditions

spots.name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Gwacheon
spots.desc: Modern and contemporary art exhibitions and an outdoor sculpture garden. Nam June Paik's large video installation, The More, the Better (Dadaikseon), is here; check notices if you want to see it operating. A separate art bus connects MMCA Seoul and Gwacheon on selected weekdays; consult the latest route notice before using it.
spots.price: ₩3,000 for all exhibitions; free for visitors aged 24 or younger, those aged 65 or older and undergraduate students…

spots.name: Gwacheon Hyanggyo
spots.desc: A Joseon-era Confucian school and shrine. The institution was founded in 1398 and moved to its present site in 1690. It can be combined with a walk towards Gwanaksan. Respect any ceremonies or restrictions on entering the buildings.

spots.name: Ononsa
spots.desc: A historic guesthouse building associated with Gwacheon's Joseon-era local administration. Such guesthouses accommodated travelling officials and also had ceremonial functions. It offers a look at the city's history beyond its modern museums and parks.

spots.name: Chusa Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the calligrapher and scholar Kim Jeong-hui, known by his pen name Chusa, who spent his final years in Gwacheon. It is away from the Grand Park cluster; plan the journey separately.
spots.hours: 09:00–18:00; ticket sales close at 17:00. Closed Mondays (Tuesday if Monday is a public holiday), January 1, and the…

spots.name: Seoul Grand Park walking trails
spots.desc: The park has a lakeside route of about 2.8 km, a zoo-perimeter route of about 4.5 km and a forest-bathing route of about 7 km. These are separate routes with different starting points. Check the park map and notices for access and closures; do not confuse the forest route with a short walk around the lake.

spots.name: LetsRun Park Seoul
spots.desc: Gwacheon's racecourse, operated by the Korea Racing Authority. Telephone within South Korea: 1566-3333. Consult the calendar for race days and public events rather than assuming racing or tours are available every day.
spots.hours: Check the race and event calendar

spots.name: Gwanmun Sports Park
spots.desc: A park with green space and sports facilities, suitable for a walk or a break from sightseeing.

spots.name: Gwacheon Civic Center
spots.desc: A venue for theatre, musicals and concerts, with sports facilities including an ice rink. Check the relevant programme and public-session arrangements before visiting.

spots.name: Munwon Sports Park
spots.desc: A neighbourhood sports park with a football pitch, basketball and tennis courts, gateball courts, an inline-skating area and a floor fountain. Check availability and booking requirements before planning to use a court or pitch. The map marker points to the football pitch within the park.
spots.hours: Sports facilities daily 06:00–22:00; seasonal facilities have separate schedules

spots.name: Hike Gwanaksan from Gwacheon Hyanggyo
spots.desc: Follow the mountain trail towards Yeonjuam and Yeonjudae. The upper sections are steep and rocky, so wear suitable shoes, carry water and allow time to descend before dark. Check the route and weather before starting.
spots.hours: Use the trail in daylight and check for closures

spots.name: MMCA Shop Gwacheon
spots.desc: Sells exhibition catalogues, art-related goods, crafts and museum merchandise.

spots.name: Hang-ari Sujebi

spots.name: eunji yeongyangsundae
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that many local people visit to eat sundaeguk.

spots.name: Jwamaura

spots.name: chunhyanggolnamwon Loachsoup
spots.desc: Serves chueotang, a Korean loach soup. The restaurant is near Government Complex Gwacheon Station.

spots.name: From the Earth
spots.desc: A cafe with a large seating area, serving bread and desserts.

spots.name: Ki Hyeong-do Literature Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the poet Ki Hyeong-do. Exhibitions explore his life and writing through personal belongings, handwritten diaries and manuscripts, and photographs. The adjoining Ki Hyeong-do Culture Park has walking paths, poetry displays and places to sit.

spots.name: Gwangmyeong Cave
spots.desc: it was developed in 1912 during the Japanese occupation. It retains the painful history of Korea during the Japanese colonial rule. More than 1 million people visit annually. Tunnel length: 7.8 km (2 km open) Total depth: 275 m.

spots.name: Ante Ecological Park
spots.desc: Ante Eco Park is not only designated as an urban wetland and an ecological preservation district, but also has good location and is used as a resting place and ecological learning center for Gwangmyeong citizens. It is inhabited by a variety of wildlife.

spots.name: Chunghyeon Museum
spots.desc: Chunghyun Museum preserves the ruins and relics of Lee Won-ik and his immediate descendants. In the exhibition hall (Chunghyungwan), various materials of the four generations, including artifacts and materials related to Lee Won-ik and folk life products of Jongga, are displayed.

spots.name: Lee Won-ik House and Gwangamdang (이원익집과관감당)
spots.desc: This is the closing price of Lee Won-ik, a duck who served as a royal family member during the Joseon Dynasty (1567-1608) and King Injo (1623-1649) and was known as Cheongbaek-ri. In the eighth year of King Injo's reign (1630), when rain broke out on the teacher's house, which was two square kilometers away, the king granted him a new house. In the ninth year of King Hyojong's reign (1658), a…

spots.name: Gwangmyeong City Volunteer Festival
spots.desc: This event is held every year to comfort volunteers and promote harmony among volunteers, supporters and beneficiaries.

spots.name: Gureum-san Art Festival
spots.desc: Gureum-san Mountain appears in Gwangmyeong weather and regularity in the Citizen's Charter and the Song of the Citizens.

spots.name: Gwangmyeong Wine Festival
spots.desc: The Gwangmyeong Cave Korea Wine Festival is a festival held at Gwangmyeong Cave in Gyeonggi Province. It has become the only mecca of Korea's wine industry. Each year, it approaches different topics differently, and you can feel the charm of Korean wine with various hands-on events and programs.

spots.name: Gwangmyeong Traditional Market
spots.desc: A traditional market selling groceries and prepared foods such as jokbal, tteokbokki, chicken gangjeong, hotteok, and pretzels. Many stalls sell ready-to-eat snacks.

spots.name: Gwangmyeong Speedom
spots.desc: It is a large-scale racetrack with a total floor area of 74,000444㎡ on the 1st basement and 5th floors, and can accommodate up to 30,000 people. It is the world's largest domed racecourse. It has a complex leisure and cultural space. Admission and operating hours are different for each space, so you should check and go.

spots.name: Lotte Cinema Gwangmyeong Outlet
spots.desc: There is a place where you can watch movies and do shopping downstairs.

spots.name: Gwangmyeong Hanjeongsik Gyeongbok Palace

spots.name: Soha Gotaek

spots.name: Papadcujin
spots.desc: This restaurant serves the best foods such as pasta and pizza in Gwangmyeong. The price isn't too burdensome, so you can get in touch with it.

spots.name: Dwae Ji Jip

spots.name: Tteokppokttang (떡볶당)

spots.name: Chieutsiotdigd (ㅊㅅㄷ)
spots.desc: Pudding and coffee are delicious cafe treats here. Also, inside the cafe is very pretty, which is perfect for someone who likes a cute place. Also, it is quiet around.

spots.name: Glory coffee
spots.desc: It is a cafe in the trade center. The pride of the Icafé is its scones. Of course, coffee is delicious, but they make their own scones and boast fantastic taste.

spots.name: Remember 1910, Lee Seok-Young Plaza
spots.desc: A historical plaza commemorating Lee Seok-Young, who sold his property and went into exile in Manchuria to support the Korean independence movement. He helped establish the Shinheung Military Academy, which trained independence activists.

spots.name: Dasan Ecological Park
spots.desc: Dasan Ecological Park is a water environment ecological space that combines ecology, history, and culture. It is a waterside park where various plants are created. There is also an ecological interpreter who provides information about the various plants living in the park and tells the life story of Jeong Yak-yong, who loved the Han River.

spots.name: Namyangju Museum
spots.desc: Place where you can see Namyangju's history and traditional culture and the permanent exhibition room displays Paleolithic artifacts excavated from Namyangju, as well as Joseon and modern folk relics. In the special exhibition room, various exhibitions with new themes every year are displayed. Educational programs for infants, school organizations, and families are also in operation.

spots.name: Praum the Musical Instrument Museum
spots.desc: It is the first Western musical instrument museum in Korea, a cultural space designed for listening, touching, feeling, and communicating with music. The museum has various special exhibitions, educational programs, and experience programs so that visitors can directly experience instruments.

spots.name: Miho Museum
spots.desc: Based on the content of natural history, Miho Museum performs the functions of a museum such as collection, conservation, education, exhibition, and research of authentic fossils, traces of past life forms, minerals, rocks, stuffed animals, and insect specimens. Furthermore, it has a space for rest and leisure activities.
spots.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat,Sun 10:00-19:00 (closed Wed)

spots.name: Garden of Water
spots.desc: Garden of Water is an eco-friendly relaxation space. When you cross a sea Bridge, the symbolic bridge of the Water Garden, a large flower complex has been created along the riverside promenade, where visitors can enjoy poppies in May and yellow cosmos in September. Bukhan River and Chohwa Complex come together.

spots.name: DreamWave Water Lesiure
spots.desc: A seasonal water sports facility where visitors can try activities such as water skiing, wakeboarding, motorboat rides, and surfing during the warmer months.

spots.name: Ahtti strawberry farm experience
spots.desc: The main purpose is for families with young children to experience strawberry picking, and visitors can also experience making strawberry jam and strawberry pizza with strawberries they pick themselves.

spots.name: Sosori Farm
spots.desc: The activities vary depending on the season. The natural ecology experience takes place between April and June. Activities include collecting wild flowers, interacting with animals in Sosori Farm, observing and collecting tadpoles, planting rice, observing freshwater fish, making tofu with organic beans grown at Sosori Farm, experiencing vegetable garden, and searching for fertilized eggs. In…

spots.name: Andersen Garden
spots.desc: Visitors can experience different activities for each month. From March to April, making edible flower Korean pancake and strawberry jam are available, from April to May, planting plants in pots, and making cucumber pickles, from May to June cherry and plum picking, in July, harvest and take edible flowers and assorted vegetables, from August to October, grape and apple picking, from October to…

spots.name: Eco Green Farmer's School
spots.desc: It is an ecological experience farm that provides crop harvesting experience, traditional culture experience, curriculum-related learning program, and farmhouse service. It is an eco-friendly rural experience farm that provides a variety of rural tourism services.

spots.name: Jeong Yak-yong Cultural Festival
spots.desc: Jeong Yak-yong Cultural Festival is a representative cultural festival in Namyangju, which has modernly inherited the spirit of Jeong Yak-yong, a UNESCO-designated world memorial. It is held at the Jeong Yak-yong Historic Site and Dasan Ecological Park, and you can experience programs such as literary contests, musicals, and many others. It takes place mostly in October.

spots.name: Gwangneung Forest Festival
spots.desc: The Gwangneung Forest Festival is held in Gwangneung Forest, and it is selected as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. It is open only once a year during the festival, so visitors can feel the importance of nature by walking along the forest path where numerous flowers, wild grass and rare trees are breathing in a very special space that they cannot enter normally, and various cultural events such as…

spots.name: Wangsukcheon Cultural Festival
spots.desc: You can enjoy various experiences such as folklore experience, and walking competition, and you can also enjoy various food, flea market, and performances. It takes place mostly in October.

spots.name: Bongseonsa Lotus Festival
spots.desc: The Bongseonsa Lotus Festival aims to realize a Buddhist culture that is united through communication and harmony by showing the atmosphere and culture that can be felt in the mountain temple of Bongseonsa, a representative temple in Gyeonggi-do. It takes place mostly in August.

spots.name: Bukhan River Festival
spots.desc: Every visitor to Bukhan River outdoor concert hall can enjoy exciting cultural and artistic performances by popular artists.

spots.name: RockandPinetree
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in traditional Korean style food and red bean porridge.

spots.name: IlsimBonga Bean Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in bean dishes, especially abalone soft tofu soup.

spots.name: Stubborn Octopus Noodle Soup
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in noodle soup with seafood such as octopus, squid, and clams.

spots.name: Baekwoon Valley
spots.desc: It is a valley about 10 km long that stretches from Gwangdeoksan Mountain to Baekunsan Mountain. There are tourist attractions such as Seonyudam and Geumgwang Falls. The pond and strangely shaped rocks come together to create beauty. There is Heungnyongsa Temple, a temple where the handwriting of King Sejong of Joseon is kept. There are also scenic drives that begin in this valley.

spots.name: Pocheon Banwol Art Hall
spots.desc: Pocheon Banwol Art Hall is a place created for Pocheon citizens to realize civic cultural welfare through the creation of a cultural and artistic foundation. Here, you can see various artistic activities such as plays, musicals, and art exhibitions.

spots.name: Sinbuk Spa (Resort)
spots.desc: Sinbuk Hot Springs Resort is the largest natural hot spring in Korea, using natural Sinbuk Water, the best water in the country.

spots.name: Suwon Mountain Observatory
spots.desc: As an observatory modeled after the shape of Suwon Mountain, you can see the scenery of Suwon Mountain at a glance. It also serves as a resting place for citizens.

spots.name: Korea National Arboretum
spots.desc: Korea National Arboretum has 3,344 plant species, 15 specialized arboretums, a forest bath, and 15 rare animal wildlife zoos as well as a forest museum.

spots.name: Bidulginangpokpo Falls
spots.desc: Hundreds of mountain pigeons inhabit this place in winter, so it was called a Bidulginangpokpo. The waterfall along the Hantan River retreated due to erosion for hundreds of thousands of years, forming a cozy home with a deep valley.

spots.name: Pyunggang Land
spots.desc: It consists of four-season theme park Pyeonggang Land, dog playground, and Adventure Kids Park.

spots.name: Cobu World Coin Museum
spots.desc: Various cultural musical instruments and costumes experience, fake money identification experience, kidult cafeteria with Lego and Gundam, seminar room, book cafe, photo zone, and in-depth content through QR code are prepared.
spots.price: ₩6000 for out-of-area visitors, ₩5000 for local visitors

spots.name: Seowoon Park
spots.desc: There is a beautiful theme garden with 50,000 pyeong of landscaping and forests built for 40 years under Jukyeopsan Mountain. In addition, there are a well-cultivated garden, a children's experience center, various amenities, play facilities and accommodation facilities next to the beautiful Gwangneung forest, so you can enjoy relaxation and leisure together.

spots.name: Wangsan Temple
spots.desc: Wangbangsan Mountain, called Pocheon's Jinsan Mountain, is home to Wangsan Temple, which has a thousand-year history.

spots.name: Jain Temple
spots.desc: It is a traditional temple at the foot of Myeongseongsan Mountain that connects Pocheon-si, Gyeonggi-do and Cheorwon-gun, Gangwon State.

spots.name: Cheonjusa Temple
spots.desc: Many people visit the temple located next to Pocheon Art Valley.

spots.name: Pocheon Shen-eup Market
spots.desc: It is a large traditional market held every five days in the center of Pocheon City. You can eat traditional Korean snacks and foods, and purchase various tools and items.

spots.name: Pocheon Uncheon Traditional Market
spots.desc: Uncheon Traditional Market is a traditional market representing Yeongbuk-myeon, which is relatively large among the markets in Pocheon, and has many visitors. The main items handled here are fruits, electronics, agricultural products, marine products, and livestock products, and it is a medium-sized market with 160 stores.

spots.name: Pocheon Songwoo Market
spots.desc: Songu Market is a market with 85 stalls. It is not that big of a scale.

spots.name: The Pocheon Garden

spots.desc: It is a place where you can drink various beverages with delicious bread.

spots.name: Hyehwa Moon

spots.name: Seoul Craft Museum
spots.desc: The Seoul Craft Museum can experience the technical, practical, artistic, and cultural values of crafts by studying and sharing not only crafts but also knowledge, records, people, and the environment surrounding crafts.

spots.name: Police Museum
spots.desc: The Police Museum, which opened in 2005, is a space where you can preserve the history of the police and experience the activities of the police.

spots.name: Hanyangdoseong Museum
spots.desc: Hanyangdoseong Museum is a museum that contains the history and culture of Hanyangdoseong from the Joseon Dynasty to the present. It is a cultural space with a permanent exhibition room, special exhibition room, data room, and study room.

spots.name: Seoul Our Sound Museum
spots.desc: A unique museum where you can see and hear traditional culture.

spots.name: Newspaper Museum
spots.desc: The Newspaper Museum offers a panoramic view of the 130-year history of Korean newspapers since the first modern newspaper in Korea, Hanseong Sunbo (1883).
spots.price: Adult ₩4000, elementary school students~ university students ₩3000, free for older than 65 years old

spots.name: National Weather Museum
spots.desc: The National Weather Museum can see the development of modern weather technology from the history of weather observation to the current day world of supercomputers.

spots.name: Bukchon Oriental Culture Museum
spots.desc: You can see various exhibitions of the museum, and there is an observatory where you can see Seoul City Wall and Gyeongbokgung Palace.

spots.name: World Museum of Decorations
spots.desc: It is a space where you can learn the history, culture, society, and art of various ethnic groups through ornaments.

spots.name: PKM gallery
spots.desc: Established in 2001, PKM Gallery is known for its sleek, modern architecture and thoughtfully curated exhibitions that span painting, sculpture, multimedia, and installation art. The gallery actively participates in global art fairs and supports emerging and established artists alike, making it a significant player in South Korea's contemporary art scene. It offers visitors an immersive cultural…

spots.name: Whanki Museum
spots.desc: The Whanki Museum, nestled in the serene hills of Buam-dong in Seoul, is dedicated to the life and work of renowned Korean abstract artist Kim Whanki. Opened in 1992, this museum showcases Kim's distinctive abstract works that blend traditional Korean themes with modern abstract forms, creating a unique visual language. The museum’s architecture harmonizes with its natural surroundings, offering…

spots.name: Cheong Wa Dae
spots.desc: Also known in English as the Blue House, it was the residence of the President of the Republic of Korea from 1948-2022. It's next to the grounds of Gyeongbokgung, and can be easily recognized by its blue roof tiles and its unique fusion of modern and traditional Korean architectural styles. It is now open to the public, but only allows a limited number of visitors per day, so be sure to reserve…

spots.name: Sungkyunkwan
spots.desc: Sungkyunkwan was the highest educational institution during the Joseon dynasty since 1398. Students, including the royal family, studied Confucianism and other courses in Sungkyunkwan and became government officials and scholars. Munmyo was a Confucian shrine in Sungkyunkwan, and a ceremonial rite called 'Seokjeon Daeje' is performed twice a year. The current Sungkyunkwan University is a modern…

spots.name: Cheonggyecheon
spots.desc: It is a trail where you can take a walk along the river. The stream is a popular recreational area with walking paths, small waterfalls, and over 20 bridges, providing a peaceful escape in the heart of the city. Cheonggyecheon is also illuminated at night, making it a scenic spot for visitors to enjoy both the natural and urban landscapes. It’s especially popular during seasonal festivals, like…

spots.name: Bukchon Observatory
spots.desc: Provides a sweeping view of Bukchon Village and the greater Seoul cityscape, with Lotte Tower and the palace both clearly visible. It’s humble: clearly a converted apartment, and so tucked away its easy to miss, but it’s a great place to rest and take in the views, with beverage (tea, coffee) included as part of admission.

spots.name: Bukak palgakjung
spots.desc: You can see the night view of Seoul from the observation deck located on Mt. Bukak.

spots.name: Hongik University Daehakro Art Center

spots.name: Naksan Park
spots.desc: It is a park that runs from Dongdaemun to Hyehwa-dong. From the top of the park, you can see the night view of Seoul.

spots.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
spots.desc: The collective name of the few tiny suburbs ("dong") wedged between Gyeongbuk Palace and the Secret Garden, just north of Insadong and Anguk Station. This area was where relatives of the royal family, high public officials, and other important families lived for over 500 years as they serviced the nearby palaces. Today, some 900 of their traditional Korean "hanok" houses remain, making this area…

spots.name: Inwangsan Mountain

To get there, take Exit 2 and start climbing uphill following the "Inwang Temple" signs, through the huge construction site, and up through the temple gate. You'll see a map board and several paths. Take the left staircase upward, past the bronze bell of Bongwonsa, and…

spots.name: Hyehwa
