spots.desc: Performing arts center. Many small theaters with live dramatic and comedic performances lining every street. This district is filled with life and street commerce past midnight. The name came after the Seoul National University, which was located here before it moved to Gwanak-gu. SNU Hospital and Seoul National University School of Medicine one of the best in the country, is still here.

spots.name: Sejong Center for Performing Arts
spots.desc: Oldest and one of the largest multi-purpose theatres in downtown Seoul and home of Seoul Philharmonic. The biggest pipe organ in East Asia is in its Great Auditorium, and several video art pieces from Nam June Paik are in the entrance of the auditorium.

spots.name: Institute of Korean Royal Cuisine
spots.desc: As the name implies, you learn how to prepare royal cuisine, as well as rice cakes and hangwa (Korean cookies).
spots.hours: For class times, inquire in advance

spots.name: O'ngo Food Communications
spots.desc: Learn to make authentic Korean dishes in English or Japanese from Korean chefs. O'ngo Food Communications offers classes to make bulgogi and kimchi, Korean barbecue, and Vegan Temple Cuisine. You get a tour of a traditional Korean Market after the classes to see Korean ingredients and people.
spots.hours: For class times, inquire in advance

spots.name: The lantern light festival
spots.desc: Every November, the lantern light festival takes place at Cheonggye Creek. At the festival, you can see many lanterns made by Korean and foreign artists. Some of the lanterns are in traditional Korean style, and there are also many character lanterns and company mascot lanterns.

spots.name: Rent Korean Traditional Clothes
spots.desc: When you visit Gyeongbokgung (경복궁), Changdeokgung (창덕궁), or any palace near Jongno you can rent traditional Korean clothes and enter for a free visit. You will be able to embrace Korean culture and make great memories in Seoul. You can rent traditional Korean clothes for around ₩20,000, get a traditional Korean hairstyle for women and keep it for 2 hours.

spots.name: Aruto Small Theater
spots.desc: Located in the Daehak-ro district, Aruto Small Theater is known for staging romantic comedies. Since 2023, the theater is showcasing the play "De-minus Back to Fall in Love," a lighthearted romantic comedy. This small venue offers a cozy setting for audiences to enjoy live theater in an informal atmosphere.

spots.name: LOL Park
spots.desc: It is the place where League of Legends matches take place, and there are many PC rooms in the same building, so there are many things to enjoy

spots.name: Dongdaemun Market
spots.desc: Though not as impressive architecturally as Namdaemun, the Dongdaemun market is infinitely more interesting than its counterpart.

spots.name: Gwangjang Market
spots.desc: Famous traditional market in Seoul. It was one of the first permanent markets in Korea, and it is always crowded. It has a variety of silk, linen, and other traditional items. Street food is really excellent as well, especially bindaetteok(Mung Bean Pancakes).

spots.name: Insadong
spots.desc: Insadong is an area known for its art galleries and shops and is possibly the most touristy place in South Korea. It is a great place to buy cultural souvenirs. There are also a few stores that offer interesting vintage toys and various kitsch. Insadong also contains many traditional tea and coffee shops. It is one of the few places where vegetarian restaurants can be found.

spots.name: Ssamziegil
spots.desc: Ssamziegil is a shopping complex that opened in 2004. It has the form of a rectangular spiral on three floors and includes about a hundred craft shops (clothing, jewelry, leather, etc.), restaurants, and cafes, also make-your-own crafts like candles, pottery, etc.

spots.name: The store from Tong-In
spots.desc: Occupying four floors, this store offers high-quality items, including pottery, inlaid, and lacquered objects, as well as jewelry, postcards, etc. Not necessarily cheap, but the quality is good. It is located a little further than Ssamziegil on the same side as Insadong-gil.

spots.name: Kyobo Book Store
spots.desc: Kyobo is the largest chain of bookstores in South Korea, and this flagship store is located in the center of Seoul. It is completely invisible from the outside because it is underground. It is accessed directly from the Gwanghwamun subway station or at the intersection of Sejongno and Jongno. There is a huge selection of books, CDs, DVDs, stationery items, cardmaking, and a bunch of other…

spots.name: Sadongmyenok
spots.desc: Justly famous for its manduguk, a soup of gargantuan homemade dumplings stuffed with meat and veggies and served with side dishes for ₩5,000. English menu available.

spots.name: Gung
spots.desc: Specialty restaurant for mandu (Korean dumplings) from the nearby Kaesong region in North Korea. The chickpea patties are also very good. This restaurant has been passed down from mother to daughter for three generations.

spots.name: Everest
spots.desc: Nepali restaurant featuring dozens of delectable dishes ranging from mutton curry to butter naan. Bollywood music videos are free.

spots.name: Tosokchon
spots.desc: Reverently referenced in most local guides as the place for Ginseng chicken soup and variations on that theme.

spots.name: Jung Don
spots.desc: This restaurant serves Japanese-style pork cutlets. It's so popular that it's been featured on a popular Korean food program.

spots.name: Local Village(토속촌)
spots.desc: It sells samgyetang, a traditional Korean dish, and ginseng liquor.

spots.name: Pitzeriao
spots.desc: This is the place to go for wood-fired pizza. They serve pasta and pizza, so if you're looking for a western restaurant, this is the place to go.

spots.name: Yukhoe Sisterhood(육회자매집)
spots.desc: In Korea, lean cuts of beef with less fat are cut into small pieces, seasoned, and eaten as sashimi. It tastes great when paired with the fruit pear and egg yolk. However, be careful when eating sashimi with octopus, also known 'San Naggi (산낙지)', as it can be offensive. Of course, the octopus is trimmed after it dies, but its nerves are still alive and it can wiggle.

spots.name: Manson Hoff
spots.desc: It's known for its cold draft beer, nogari, and chicken. It's especially popular in the fall when the weather is nice and in the summer when it's hot.

spots.name: Tteoksang
spots.desc: This restaurant offers a fusion of Korean tteokbokki (rice cakes) in a hanok charming setting.

spots.name: Pungnyeon Ssal Nongsan
spots.desc: cheap snack places. noodle sausage, fried stuff, fried rice cake...

spots.name: Jin A Chun
spots.desc: The second oldest operating restaurant in Seoul, having been founded in 1925. Serves Korean Chinese cuisine.

spots.name: Yukmian
spots.desc: Yukmian is a restaurant that offers beef noodle dishes, located near Daehak-ro. The menu features various cuts of beef served with noodles in a broth. The restaurant is known for its focus on quality ingredients and simple preparation. Due to its popularity, reservations may be required during busy hours.

spots.name: a buckwheat-flavored restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in dishes made from buckwheat, offering a variety of traditional Korean meals. Located in the Daehak-ro area, it provides a menu that highlights buckwheat as a key ingredient, including noodles and pancakes. The simple setting and focus on buckwheat-based dishes attract those seeking a unique dining experience.

spots.name: UjauKimchi Tteokbokki
spots.desc: Yuja Yoo Tteokbokki is a restaurant that specializes in tteokbokki, a popular Korean dish made from rice cakes. The restaurant offers a variety of tteokbokki options with different levels of spice and flavors.

spots.name: Hyehwa Dodam
spots.desc: It is a famous restaurant for Korean traditional foods such as kimchi stew and pajeon. They also sell Korean traditional makgeolli.

spots.name: Hyehwa Gopchang
spots.desc: It is a restaurant where you can eat assorted tripe at a low price.

spots.name: Uyeonhwa
spots.desc: The Hanok-style restaurant in Ikseon-dong blends modern sensibilities and traditional atmosphere. It features Hamburg steak made with 100 percent Korean beef and is served with hot pot rice.

spots.name: Sinrajemyeon Anguk Branch
spots.desc: It is a kalguksu specialty store that originated in Gyeongju, and is located in Anguk Station in Seoul. It features a traditional Korean interior with a luxurious atmosphere.

spots.name: Chwiyabeolguksi
spots.desc: Dumpling hot pot is a particularly famous noodle restaurant. Dumpling hot pot here boasts a deep and cool taste of soup with a combination of large dumplings and fresh vegetables.

spots.name: Eomyongbaek pork soup
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that serves Busan style pork and rice soup in a tranquil hanok atmosphere. The main menu here is pork and rice soup in two styles, clear and thick, and kimchi and kkakdugi, served as basic side dishes, go well with gukbap.

spots.name: GwanghwamunMijin
spots.desc: As a traditional buckwheat specialty, cold buckwheat noodles and handmade pork cutlet are the main dishes. The restaurant is spacious and quick-rotating, and the Yeolmu Kimchi and pickled radish served as standard side dishes are delicious.

spots.name: Dooly snack
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that sells snacks in Hyehwa-dong. It sells a variety of menus at low prices. You can only pay in cash.

spots.name: Beonteu Seoul
spots.desc: Located between Cheonggyecheon and Jongno, it is a three-story large bakery cafe that features a large space and a variety of bakery menus. In particular, it offers a leisurely atmosphere where people can share coffee and bread while enjoying the view of Cheonggyecheon.

spots.name: Artist Bakery
spots.desc: It is a bakery specializing in various kinds of salt bread, featuring a savory and salty taste.

spots.name: Coffee one
spots.desc: Located in Gwanghwamun, it is famous for its fat sandwiches and various puddings.

spots.name: Sseolgeuregori Stroop waffle
spots.desc: This cafe specializes in Stroop waffle, an authentic Dutch dessert, and serves fresh waffles that are made on the fly.

spots.name: T.um
spots.desc: The future of technology can often be seen today in South Korea, and SK Telecom have created a museum dedicated to it! Exhibits change frequently due to the rapid pace of technology being shown. Preschoolers not allowed. Online pre-registration necessary, make sure to reserve early as its gets full weeks in advance.

spots.name: Culture Station Seoul 284
spots.desc: A culture center at the old Seoul Station. It was built in 1925 during the Japanese Colonial period, and the center of the Korean railway until 2004 when the current building for KTX opened. It reopened in 2011 as a culture center, and it hosts many exhibitions. The pre-modern architecture inspired by the Lucerene station (which has burnt down) offers unique sight among the glassy buildings of…

spots.name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
spots.desc: A central cathedral of the Diocese of Seoul. It was first built in 1920s and has a blended architecture of neo romanesque style with Korean traditional components.

spots.name: Korea Financial History Museum
spots.desc: It is a space where you can see Korea's financial development.

spots.name: Stamp Museum
spots.desc: It is a space where you can see the process of mail change and various stamps of the world.

spots.name: Rice Museum
spots.desc: It is a space where you can learn about the history of rice.

spots.name: Agricultural Museum
spots.desc: It is a space where you can see various exhibitions on agriculture and traditional agricultural culture.

spots.name: Seoul National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Deoksu Palace
spots.desc: Various artworks are displayed differently from time to time. You have to pay an additional exhibition admission fee in addition to the entrance fee to Deoksugung Palace.

spots.name: Seven Luck Casino
spots.desc: The casino is only accessible to foreigners (it is illegal for Korean citizens to gamble), so remember to bring your passport. Various card tables and slots are available to play. There is a bar and cafe that serve food and drinks, although expensive.

spots.name: Sparex 24
spots.desc: This jjimjilbang or Korean sauna occupies two levels of mall basements. B3 is the entrance, big luggage store near reception, valuables storage at reception, shoes locker, separate showers and bath for men and women (with another larger locker, shared key with shoes locker, missing ventilation so if got wet clothes because of rain, let them out else won’t dry; bar soap) and an extra sleeping room…
spots.price: Day arrival (5:00-20:00) ₩ 12,000 (child 7000), night arrival ₩ 15,000 (8000), out ticket ₩ 20,000. Food court meals ₩…
spots.addr: 247 Jangchungdan-ro, Jung District, Seoul, Corée du Sud

spots.name: Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center
spots.desc: Located within Myeong-dong, the Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center contains the largest number of shops specializing in Korean and world numismatics for both local and international numismatists.

spots.name: Lotte Young Plaza
spots.desc: *In renewal until Dec.31 2025* Just across the street from Avatar department store, this department store is oriented towards a younger, upscale clientele, and in addition to the usual Korean brands and international brands, the top floor of the space features an assortment of quality eating establishments to replenish your shopping energy. The wine bar is recommended. Sometimes art installations…

spots.name: Migliore
spots.desc: One of the biggest fashion buildings in Seoul. It has 17 floors above ground and 7 basement floors. Information boards in Migliore are written in Korean as well as English, Japanese and Chinese for foreign tourists. US credit cards are often accepted, but ask before haggling if you aren't sure. The outside stage features a "talent show" of local dance groups (mostly high school or college student…

spots.name: Shinsegae
spots.desc: The oldest department store on the Korean peninsula. The original building was refurbished in 2008 and became a high-street boutique. Accepts major credit/debit cards, including Amex and JCB.

spots.name: Jeonju Jungang Hoegwan
spots.desc: This Korean restaurant specializes in the Jeonju variety of bibimbap, which features different ingredients and spices than other bibimbap dishes. Delicious and healthy.

spots.name: Samarkand
spots.desc: In the heart of "Central Asian Town", which has Russian, Mongolian, Uzbek, and Central Asian restaurants. Wander around and discover the area a bit - you'll be rewarded with delicious food and an exotic experience.

spots.name: Nampomyeonok
spots.desc: This is a restaurant specializing in cold buckwheat-based noodles (Pyongyang’s cold noodles). This is a place visited by former presidents such as Moon Jae-in, Lee Myung-bak and Yoon Seok-yeol. This restaurant is located in a lively narrow alley in an area dense with office buildings, and consists of a room with table-style seating and cushion-style tables.

spots.name: Myeongdong Korean BBQ Mongvely
spots.desc: A popular all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ restaurant, offering unlimited premium pork and beef grilled over charcoal. With multilingual menus, a self-service buffet of fresh banchan, sauces, and a DIY ramen station, Mongvely combines local flavor with tourist-friendly service.

spots.name: Daeyeop Eulijoro Branch
spots.desc: Restaurant that specializes in Pyongyang naengmyeon and various Pyongyang food.

spots.name: Yeonhaejang
spots.desc: It is a restaurant specializing in pork small intestine hot pot that features a clean and modern interior, and is loved by many customers even if the waiting is long. They have gopchang hot pot with a variety of side menus, and the soup of the hot pot boasts a deep and thick taste and uses fresh gopchang without any odor. In addition, it is sold as a meal kit, so you can enjoy it easily at home.

spots.name: Gangsanok
spots.desc: Opened in 1958, the restaurant specializes in traditional soybean dishes that serve only soybean noodles in the summer and serve soybean meal for the rest of the year. It is open for only two and a half hours a day, and needs to be careful when visiting because it can be closed early when the ingredients are exhausted. It consists of thick and savory soybean soup and chewy noodles, and is served…

spots.name: Bakgane Bindaetteok Main Branch
spots.desc: It is the representative restaurant of Gwangjang Market, which has been around since 1966, and serves savory and crispy bindaetteok by grinding 100% green beans directly into a millstone. It is also popular with foreign tourists, has a variety of menus and friendly service.
spots.addr: jongrogu jongro32 street 7 gwangjang market 1st floor

spots.name: Hanwoojeong
spots.desc: Korean BBQ restaurant specializing in 1++ Korean Hanwoo beef, Korea’s highest-quality beef grade. Inspired by the elegance of a traditional hanok, Hanwoojeong provides refined Korean dining and a warm, sophisticated atmosphere. Guests can experience carefully selected cuts including sirloin, striploin, tenderloin and other premium specialties, complemented by Korean side dishes and classic…

spots.name: 2MOON Cafe & Pub
spots.desc: Low key, cozy cafe tucked away on the rooftop of a low building. Serves tea, coffee, drinks and cocktails. Quiet and very atmospheric at night, great for conversations, popular with and seemingly known only to locals. Owner speaks fluent English, studied in Texas and is happy to chat. Some of the clothing made downstairs by indie designers is sold here too.

spots.name: Jaehaeseok
spots.desc: It is a pudding specialty cafe that boasts a unique vintage interior and cozy atomosphere.

spots.name: Asoto Bakery
spots.desc: It is a bakery with a cute atmosphere where you can feel the Japanese Kitsaten sensibility.

spots.name: Gonggangap
spots.desc: It is a dessert cafe located in Euljiro, especially famous for pudding bingsu and various cakes

spots.name: Ling Ling
spots.desc: It is a space famous for its Y2K sensibility and kitschy interior. It offers a variety of desserts and drinks, and cakes and jelly sodas are especially popular. The interior of the store is cozy and has many photo zones, making it a great place to take pictures. Also, cute props and goods are on sale, so it entertains visitors.

spots.name: Museum of Colonial History
spots.desc: It is the first history museum specializing in Japanese colonial era.

spots.name: Namsan Outdoor Botanical Garden
spots.desc: You can see various trees and plants, and there is a way to take a walk.

spots.name: IPARKMALL Yongsan
spots.desc: A complex commercial facility that includes a shopping mall, convenience facilities, and stores. It consists of a building with 3 floors underground and 9 floors above ground. It is divided into The Center, Taste Park, Living Park, and Fashion Park, and has various stores including E Mart, LOTTE HIMART, CGV, and Young Poong Bookstore.

spots.name: Yongsan Children's Garden
spots.desc: Yongsan Children's Garden is a public park located on the former site of a United States military base. The park features green spaces, walking paths, and recreational areas, offering visitors a place to relax and enjoy the outdoors. It also provides an opportunity to learn about the history of the former military base.

spots.name: The Spa Grand Hyatt Seoul
spots.desc: The spa features a variety of massage treatments including a Korean massage, aromatherapy, and aroma stone treatment.

spots.name: Great Korean Beer Festival
spots.desc: The Great Korean Beer Festival is held annually at the Younsan station: I-Park Mall.

spots.name: Dinermate Yongsan Branch
spots.desc: It is a dining bar where you can enjoy brunch cafes during the day and wine and bourbon in the evening. It is also a good place for dates and gatherings, as you can enjoy carefully prepared brunch menus, desserts, and various alcoholic beverages together in a modern and comfortable atmosphere.

spots.name: Ueno
spots.desc: This is a Japanese home-style restaurant, and it is a place that contains a simple but deep taste and warmth like a hidden restaurant in a small alley in Japan.

spots.name: Siok
spots.desc: Shiok is a Singaporean restaurant that reproduces the local taste of Singapore, meaning "delicious" and "cool." It combines the sensual interior of the designer who makes the local atmosphere at a reasonable price with the food made with recipes that have been eaten and learned in Singapore for many years.

spots.name: Oilje
spots.desc: The oilseed is freshly ground koshihikari rice. It is served with fresh rice, salted octopus, and GatKimchi. The oilseed seaweed soup is made of Geogeumdo-san young seaweed. You can dip seaweed in a special sauce and taste it stronger.

spots.name: BaekGyeong restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant is where you can feel the savory charm of juicy pork belly. It is a popular restaurant among residents.

spots.name: Muswi
spots.desc: The natural light and wood-tone interior that come through the barrel create a warm atmosphere. There are different menus such as mushroom hamburger steak, tomato burrata pasta, and green onion pizza, and there is a lot of wine, so it is good to enjoy with food.

spots.name: Beomyuda Samgakji
spots.desc: This restaurant is a Mexican, Western-based fusion restaurant where you can enjoy various kinds of alcohol and fusion Mexican food that you have never eaten anywhere.

spots.name: Sam Sam Sam
spots.desc: It is a San Francisco restaurant that contains the sentiment of the U.S. mainland. It is loved as a Yongsan restaurant that combines authentic Italian menus in your own style. It is a place where authentic San Francisco sensibility meets Yongsan's sophisticated atmosphere.

spots.name: PPS
spots.desc: It is a handmade burger shop representing Yongsan, starting in 2021.PPS is a place where you experience the deep taste of hamburgers with fresh ingredients and sophisticated recipes.

spots.name: KkeoGeo
spots.desc: This is a conceptual restaurant with Hong Kong cuisine, not just ordinary Chinese food. This place has unflattering dishes and great alcoholic beverages to go with.

spots.name: JeongSeong Son Kalguksu
spots.desc: This place is a hidden kalguksu restaurant near Yongsan Station.It offers a variety of menus such as noodles and bibimbap, especially chewy noodles and thick soup.

spots.name: Jacoby's
spots.desc: Offers a wide variety of burgers, arguably the best for the value, in Seoul. In an area often known as the foreigner ghetto, a popular area for expats who live just west of Itaewon.

spots.name: Pattaya
spots.desc: Thai restaurant, and perhaps the best in Seoul. With a menu featuring nearly 100 different items, you're bound to find your favorite dishes and make some new ones, too.
spots.price: Stir-fried rice and noodle dishes cost ₩13,000-18,000, while curry pots and stews can run over ₩30,000

spots.name: Zelen
spots.desc: Fantastic Bulgarian restaurant featuring lots of stuffed everything - from tomatoes to mushrooms, peppers and chicken breasts. Well-worth it as it is unique to the dining landscape in Seoul.

spots.name: Don Charly
spots.desc: Not a Tex-Mex place: the front of the menu is a Spanish-language rant on that issue. This little "hole in the wall" will be something different for a lot of people. Portions are small, but that enables you to try a wider variety. Huge tequila menu; the Agavero is strongly recommended for dessert.
spots.hours: dinner hours, sometimes closed for lunch

spots.name: Oido Red Lighthouse
spots.desc: The Oido Red Lighthouse is a marine tourism facility built in 2005 as part of a fishing village experience tourism project. Its striking red hue makes it a popular date spot for couples and a popular spot for photography enthusiasts.

spots.name: Yongdo Arboretum
spots.desc: Located in Maehwa-dong, Yongdo Arboretum is a nature-based experiential learning center. Featuring a wildflower garden of over 100 species, a botanical garden filled with diverse plants, a herb village filled with the fragrant scent of grass, a water playground suitable for children, a year-round sledding hill, and more, it offers a unique experience for children and a beautiful retreat where the…

spots.name: Farm Farm Land
spots.desc: Farm Farm Land (팜팜랜드) is a seasonal outdoor activity venue in Siheung. It has offered winter sledding activities for families. Check its official announcements for current operating dates, available activities, and admission details before visiting.

spots.name: English space
spots.desc: Enjoy relaxation and experiences at Younggle Space, a multi-cultural space with a panoramic view of the Oido ocean. Younggle Space is a multi-cultural space where you can experience Oido through your senses.

spots.name: Tayo Strawberry and Tangerine Farm
spots.desc: The farm offers strawberry, golden fragrance, and natural fragrance experiences and sales.

spots.name: Sangol Arboretum
spots.desc: This is "Sumok," a cafe at Siheung Mulwang Reservoir. An arboretum, cafe, and bakery, this space offers healing in the forest. We hope you'll enjoy nature during the day and the nighttime views. Thank you for visiting. :)

spots.name: Paradive
spots.desc: Paradive 35, a 35-m-deep diving pool! Parasurf, indoor surfing all year round! Paraloop, a retreat in the heart of the city!

spots.name: Mulwang Lake
spots.desc: The other name for Mulwang Lake, the largest lake in Siheung City, is Heungbu Reservoir. At the time of its construction in 1945, the administrative districts were Siheung-gun and Bucheon-gun, so the name was taken from Heung of Siheung and Bu of Bucheon-gun.

spots.name: On-Animal Experience Farm
spots.desc: Parental accompaniment is required. All experiences must be conducted under parental supervision. Parents must always be present with children in the animal zone, especially in the animal zone. Be careful when interacting with animals!

spots.name: Tree of Life Observatory
spots.desc: Oido, located on the southwestern coast of Siheung City, is home to a variety of seafood and is a significant historical site, designated National Historic Site No. 441, thanks to numerous excavations revealing relics from various periods. The Tree of Life, located on Oido's Stork Rock Trail, is a popular sunset and nighttime attraction. The Tree of Life Observatory was built to revive the…

spots.name: Soraesan Forest Bathing Area
spots.desc: Soraesan Forest Bathing Area was established by Siheung City in 1992 to promote health and emotional well-being for its citizens. The existing 5-km walking path from the entrance of Naewonsa Temple to the summit has been renovated and redesigned to include acupressure paths, exercise facilities, a reading forest, a green pine forest playground, a strength-building forest using log ropes, and a…

spots.name: Gomsolnuri Forest
spots.desc: A forest walking path lined with metasequoia trees, suitable for a leisurely walk.

spots.name: Siheung Oido Museum
spots.desc: Opened in July 2019, the Siheung Oido Museum is located on the Oido Historic Site (a nationally designated cultural property). Oido is home to the largest shell mound on the west coast and is recognized for its preservation value as a prehistoric coastal cultural heritage site, with numerous Neolithic artifacts unearthed. The museum aims to showcase not only the Oido Historic Site but also…

spots.name: Creation Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: The Museum of Natural History is an eco-friendly nature education and relaxation space located in the heart of the city, with hundreds of species of flowers and trees on a site of approximately 3,500 pyeong.

spots.name: Korea Craft Experience Museum
spots.desc: This is a complex cultural space where you can experience various exhibitions by resident artists and 16 types of craft experiences. Exhibition admission fee: Free Experience fee: ₩10,000-80,000 (optional) Docent reservation: ₩10,000 per person (please inquire for groups) Training for graduates: Certification course (one-day classes and instructor activities available, museum group class…

spots.name: Siheung City Insect Exhibition and Experience Center Bugsrium
spots.desc: Experience the future value of insects at the Bugsrium (Insect Exhibition Experience Center) with Siheung Heung-gon. Siheung is home to Heung-gon, a cute insect character famous along with Haerotoro. Bugsrium, which features Heung-gon, a character that embodies the characteristics of stag beetles and rhinoceros beetles, the most common insects in Siheung City, is an insect exhibition experience…

spots.name: Siheung City Agricultural Technology Center Astronomical Observatory
spots.desc: This planetarium is located within the Siheung City Agricultural Technology Center. Reservations can be made through the Siheung City Hall website (Integrated Reservation/Planetarium Reservation).
spots.addr: 3rd floor observatory, Siheung Agricultural Technology Center, 139 Gwangokji-ro

spots.name: Gaetgol Ecological Park
spots.desc: Gaetgol Ecological Park is a wetland formed by deep inland tidal flats on the site of a 1.5-hectare abandoned salt farm. Developed utilizing the natural ecological resources of the inland tidal flats and the cultural heritage of the former salt farms, it is a treasure trove of vibrant natural ecosystems and a haven for citizens, offering a haven of relaxation and an eco-friendly park where nature…

spots.name: Lotus Theme Park
spots.desc: To honor the symbolic and historical significance of Gwangokji Pond, Siheung City has created and operates a "Lotus Theme Park" on a 19.3-hectare rice paddy surrounding the pond. A walking and bicycle path has been constructed around the pond, encouraging citizens to visit. Lotus flowers begin blooming in mid-July, peaking in mid- to late-August, and remain in full bloom until mid- to…

spots.name: Neunggok Prehistoric Site Park
spots.desc: Neunggok Prehistoric Site Park is located in the Neunggok area of Siheung. Visitors interested in the city's historical sites can include the park when exploring this part of Siheung.

spots.name: Baegot Hanul Park
spots.desc: Hanul Park, located in Siheung, Gyeonggi Province, is a popular recreational space for locals and tourists alike, offering a wide range of amenities. The park stretches for approximately 4 km and is divided into five color-coded zones. Visitors can explore different sections of the park on foot, making it suitable for a longer walk rather than a brief stop.

spots.name: Okgu Park
spots.desc: Until early 1998, Okgu Island was a barren wasteland, off-limits to civilians due to coastal outposts. However, Siheung City utilized public service workers to create Okgu Park, a recreational space for local residents and visitors. The park, offering panoramic views of the West Sea from the island's summit, features hiking trails, a cooking area, an outdoor stage, a rose garden, and a Rose of…

spots.name: Pigeon Park
spots.desc: Pigeon Park is a neighborhood park in Eunhaeng-dong. It has various sports facilities, an outdoor stage, a rose garden, etc. in a wide space, providing convenience for users to improve their physical strength and enjoy cultural activities.

spots.name: Sosan Seowon
spots.desc: Sosan Seowon is a place in Sincheon-dong, Siheung-si, dedicated to Ha Yeon, a renowned minister during the reign of King Sejong of the Joseon Dynasty. At the entrance stands a stone monument inscribed with "Sosan Seowon" in Chinese characters.

spots.name: Gyesu Bam Farm
spots.desc: If you come in autumn, you can experience chestnut picking here. Operates only from early September to mid-October when the nights are ripe.

spots.name: Siheung Horseback Riding Healing Experience Center
spots.desc: This is a place where you can run around with your pet and experience horseback riding in a place with natural grass. You can also rent out the playground, so keep that in mind.

spots.name: Tayo Strawberry and Tangerine Farm
spots.desc: You can experience picking strawberries, tangerines, and cheonhyehyang. You can also buy strawberries and tangerines at low prices, and you can eat strawberry cakes and strawberry fondue from winter to spring.

spots.name: Saenggeumjip
spots.desc: What did the houses of wealthy farmers in the late Joseon Dynasty look like? spots.desc: It is a religious complex run by Huh Kyung-young, a former presidential candidate of South Korea.

spots.name: ASEAN National Recreation Forest
spots.desc: Located near Jangheung Amusement Park, ASEAN Natural Recreation Forest is the most accessible natural recreation forest in the Seoul metropolitan area within an hour from Seoul and Uijeongbu, Ilsan, Incheon. In addition, in order to promote friendship between Korea and ASEAN and induce social harmony among foreign workers and multicultural families, ASEAN traditional houses have been created…

spots.name: Sikkup
spots.desc: It is a pork restaurant that also offers special menus such as jukkumi.

spots.name: Sinreuksa Tourist Site
spots.desc: Silleuksa Temple, located at the foot of Bongmisan Mountain, is a representative Buddhist temple in Yeoju. It is noted for its long history, grand scale, and scenic beauty. The temple is a branch of Yongjusa, the head temple of the Jogye Order’s 2nd district, and has been designated as a traditional temple of Gyeonggi Province. Unlike most temples that are typically built deep in the mountains…

spots.name: Geumeunmorae Riverside Park
spots.desc: It is a natural park along the Namhan River in Yeoju. As the largest ecological park in South Korea, it stretches along the Namhan River, offering beautiful sunset views over the river in the evening.

spots.name: Hwanghaksan Arboretum
spots.desc: It features 14 themed gardens designed according to the ecology and functions of various plants. The park is also dedicated to the conservation and restoration of endangered insects while providing recreational services for visitors.

spots.name: Yeoju Museum
spots.desc: Established in 1977 as the Yeoju County Local History Museum, it is a museum founded to research, collect, exhibit, and educate visitors about the history and cultural artifacts of Yeoju.

spots.name: Yeoju Insect Museum
spots.desc: located in ythis insect museum exhibits a wide variety of insects and offers diverse programs, including emotional healing activities through interaction with insects and exhibitions on edible insect species.

spots.name: Art Museum Ryeo
spots.desc: It respond to the needs of Yeoju's artists and, through the integration of arts like exhibitions, education, and experiential programs, we foster communication and opportunities for cultural enjoyment between art and the public.
spots.addr: West Public Market of Yeoju Premium Outlet, 370 Myeongpum-ro

spots.name: Pasaseong Fortress
spots.desc: It is a mountain fortress located on Pasan Mountain in Daesin-myeon. It was designated as Historic Site No. 251 in 1977. It is said to have been constructed during the reign of King Pasa, the 5th king of Silla.

spots.name: Yeoju Mobile Museum
spots.desc: This public specialized museum. It exhibits the types and history of various telephones that have existed since the past.

spots.name: Yeoju Spa
spots.desc: Yeoju Hot Spring, located near the Yeoju Charcoal Village Campground, is the only hot spring resort in Yeoju, situated at the peak of Satgatbong. The hot spring water is of the highest quality, rich in various minerals that naturally spring up from 800 meters underground bedrock, and it is a medicinal spring that is safe to drink. The hot spring was discovered in 1995 and was designated as a Hot…

spots.name: Hwang posailing vessel
spots.desc: A chance to ride/sail a Joseon-era sailboat, a vessel that was a major form of transportation.

spots.name: Yeoju Ceramic Festival
spots.desc: This pottery culture festival is held annually in early May in Yeoju. It aims to inherit traditional ceramic techniques and artistry, as well as popularize and globalize ceramic culture. Visitors can enjoy various pottery-related experiences, including purchasing ceramics, watching demonstrations by potters, and experiencing traditional kilns.

spots.name: Yeoju OgokNaru Festival
spots.desc: A traditional culture festival that is based on the historical background of presenting Yeoju's excellent agricultural products, such as rice and sweet potatoes, to the king through Jopo Naru, one of the four major ferry ports of the Joseon Dynasty. Key programs include the Jinsang (tribute) Parade, Yeoju Rice Bibimbap in a large cauldron, Baked Sweet Potato Guinness, the Wish Paper Path, and…

spots.name: Yeoju Hangeul Day Anniversary Celebration
spots.desc: A cultural event held to celebrate King Sejong's creation of Hangeul, honor its historical value, and promote the originality and excellence of the Korean alphabet. A variety of content is prepared, including celebratory performances, Hangeul-related experiences, and viewing of related works.

spots.name: Yeoju Geumsa Korean Melon Festival
spots.desc: A event to promote Geumsa Oriental Melon, one of Yeoju's specialties, by offering various hands-on programs and content such as the Golden Melon picking experience and surprise melon auctions.

spots.name: Yeoju Heungcheon Namhan River Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: It takes place in the Gwi-baek-ri area of Heungcheon-myeon, along the cherry blossom road that blooms around the Namhangang River, which was historically called Yeoganggil. During the festival period, the area is closed to traffic, and the event operates with a cherry blossom theme, including a night starlight photo zone, special stage performances, hands-on experiences, and booths for local…

spots.name: Yeoju Premium Outlet
spots.desc: It is South Korea's first suburban-style premium outlet and the number one outlet store in sales. It also has the most luxury and international fashion brands among major premium outlets in Korea.

spots.name: Emart Yeoju Branch
spots.desc: One of South Korea's major hypermarket franchises, it sells a variety of daily necessities and groceries.

spots.name: Eungambonga
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant near Yeoju Premium Outlets. It serves a variety of dishes, including soy sauce marinated crab (ganjang-gejang), grilled eel, and grilled pork belly (samgyeopsal).

spots.name: Woojeong-ok
spots.desc: A famous restaurant known for its Hanu Gomtang (Korean beef bone soup) and spicy braised short ribs with beef small intestines. It offers a comfortable dining experience with a clean interior and ample parking space.

spots.name: Yeoju Ongsimi
spots.desc: A famous restaurant specializing in Ongsimi Kalguksu (potato dough ball soup with noodles). They make their own potato dough fresh every morning to serve fresh ongsimi and noodles.

spots.name: Yeojusotban
spots.desc: A Hanjeongsik restaurant popular for its premium dishes made with fresh ingredients, such as soy sauce marinated crab (Ganjang-gejang), dried yellow corvina (Bori-gulbi), and braised cutlassfish (Galchi-jorim).

spots.name: Cafe Mumoor
spots.desc: A large cafe located on the riverside of Yeoju. It offers a relaxing atmosphere with a spacious three-story layout and beautiful views visible through floor-to-ceiling windows.

spots.name: nard
spots.desc: A spacious and cozy cafe with a large outdoor garden with lush green scenery visible through the floor-to-ceiling windows.

spots.name: Woodymeong
spots.desc: Woody Meong is a pet-friendly brunch cafe combined with a woodworking workshop.

spots.name: Copper Nine Coffee
spots.desc: Copper Nine Coffee is a large cafe in Yeoju featuring a spacious and pleasant interior, an outdoor garden, and group seating, making it suitable for dates or family gatherings.

spots.name: Green Pond
spots.desc: Green Pond is a cafe featuring a botanical garden-like interior. It is pet-friendly, making it a great place to visit with your companion animals.

spots.name: Chungmin-sa
spots.desc: Chungminsa Temple is a small memorial shrine dedicated to those who lost their lives defending Yeonpyeong Island. It reflects the island's role as a frontline community and serves as a quiet place of remembrance rather than an active religious site. The shrine is modest in size and atmosphere, and visitors are short-visited. It provides a context for travelers to understand the modern history of…

spots.name: Yeonpyeong Peace Observatory
spots.desc: Yeonpyeong Peace Observatory where you can see North Korea using a telescope.

spots.name: Yeonpyeong Island Peace Park
spots.desc: Yeonpyeong Peace Park is a small memorial space dedicated to remembrance and peace. Established in 2010 to honor civilians and soldiers affected by shelling, it reflects the island's continued hope for regional stability and coexistence. The park is quiet and contemplative rather than scenic, with simple monuments and open spaces that overlook the surroundings. Visitors often visit Yeonpyeong…

spots.name: Manghyang Observatory
spots.desc: Across the barbed wire fence on the beach is Yeonpyeong Island in the north There are two telescopes at the observatory. It is 3 km away from the north, so you can see the houses of the residents and even the appearance of the residents. There is no toilet, you musthave an ID card, and wheelchair access is impaired by about 8 steps.

spots.name: Galgama restaurants
spots.desc: Stir-fried pork with rice, pork belly, Korean beef soup, short rib soup, chogye noodles

spots.name: Byeolmi restaurant
spots.desc: Porks, pig hocks, Barbecue Bossam, Soft Bean Curd Jjigae, Jeyuk bokkeum

spots.name: Bakdaljae Natural Recreational Forest
spots.desc: It is a natural recreation forest in Pyeongdong-ri, Baegun-myeon, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do.It was created in a natural environment where dense pine trees, mixed trees, strange rock formations, and clear and clean valleys are harmonized just under Bakdaljae Pass. There is a smooth hiking trail along the ridges and hills, and when you climb to the top of the mountain observation deck while…

spots.name: Cheongpungho Lake Observatory
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see Cheongpungho Lake in Jecheon at a glance from the observation deck on the mountain if you walk in the forest.

spots.name: Yongchu Falls Glass Observatory
spots.desc: The glass observatory installed above Yongchu Falls is a mixture of transparent and opaque glass at the bottom of the footbridge, and after passing through a sensor installed on an iron pillar, the opaque glass turns into transparent glass and overlooks the waterfall. It is a place where you can relieve stress by watching the cool water pouring under your feet, looking at the dizzying feeling of…

spots.name: Kumsusan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain that is 1016 m high. From a distance, the mountain ridge is called 'Minnyeobong Peak' because it resembles a beauty lying down.

spots.name: Gaeunsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain that spans Sangcheon-ri and Seongri, Susan-myeon, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, and is a place where you can see the scenery of Oksunbong Peak and Gudambong Peak of Cheongpung Lake.

spots.name: Bibongsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain in Yeongok-ri, Cheongpung-myeon. It is 531 meters high. It is sometimes called Maebong Peak because it looks like a hawk is flying no matter where you look at the mountain. Surrounded by Cheongpungho Lake, the view from the mountain is cool and beautiful.

spots.name: Solbat Park
spots.desc: It is a park with natural forests and grass, and was developed to be used as a resting place and picnic area.

spots.name: Yongdusan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain that spans between Pogeon-ri and Mosan-dong, Songhak-myeon. It is 871m high. It is Jinsan of Jecheon-si, where Seokgiamsan Mountain (906 m) and Gamaksan Mountain (920 m) are connected to the northwest, and the water flowing from the foot of the mountain forms Yongducheon, making it an Uirimji.

spots.name: Jageundongsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see Cheongpung Cultural Complex and the sea shooting site of the drama Taejo Wanggeon at a glance.

spots.name: Cave Site in Jecheon Jeommal
spots.desc: The Jeommal Cave in Jecheon is a cave site from the Paleolithic Era. It is also a cave that allowed people to know the age of relics from the Paleolithic Age in Korea with animal fossils such as bears and short-tailed monkeys excavated here.

spots.name: Deokjusansang Fortress
spots.desc: A mountain fortress surrounding Deokjugol and Songgye Valley with four layers of wall. The total circumference of the wall along the mountain stream is more than 15 km, and several layers of wall are built in Deokjugol, the deepest valley at the southern foot of Wolaksan Mountain.

spots.name: Oriental Ecological Forest Park
spots.desc: It is a forest park with a well-managed lawn around the hackberry tree, and it is good to take a walk when autumn leaves come out. Also, Biryongdam Reservoir is nearby, so it is good to visit.

spots.name: Taksajeong Pavillion
spots.desc: It is a Jecheon pavilion during the Japanese colonial period in Guhak-ri, Bongyang-eup.

spots.name: Jakseongsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain that spans Jeokseong-myeon of Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do and Geumseong-myeon, Jecheon-si. Located at the northern end of Kumsusan Mountain, it is famous for its summer mountains along with the Dongsan Mountain next door.

spots.name: The Buddha of Deokjusa Temple
spots.desc: It is located under the 1.6-km mountain of Jeongsan Mountain along the hiking trail next to Deokjusa Temple, and there is a Buddha statue engraved on a large rock. If you visit in autumn, you can feel the nature more as there are maple trees everywhere in the middle of climbing.

spots.name: Mokguram Rock
spots.desc: It is located in Bakdaljae. it can see Mokguram Rock made by carving the inside of the tree.

spots.name: Jecheon Hyanggyo
spots.desc: It is a hyanggyo in Gyodong, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, and was designated as a tangible cultural heritage in Chungcheongbuk-do in 1981.

spots.name: Cheongpung Lake Cable Car
spots.desc: It is a cable car of Cheongpung Lakeside Cable Car in Korea that runs a 2.3km section from Multae-ri, Cheongpung-myeon to the top of Bibongsan Mountain.

spots.name: Cheongpungho Lake Tourist Monorail
spots.desc: It is Jecheon's monorail, which takes 50 minutes to return and operates as a course with some steep sections.
spots.hours: 09:30-16:30, Mon regular closure, December, January and February winter closure

spots.name: Chungju Ho Cruise Cheongpungnaru
spots.desc: It is operated as a 90-minute trip between Janghoe in Danyang and Cheongpungho Lake in Jecheon on a large tourist cruise ship.

spots.name: Cheongpungho Lake cruise ship
spots.desc: It is a place where you can tour Jecheon-si in Cheongbuk-do by cruise ship.

spots.name: Oksunbong Suspension Bridge in Jecheon
spots.desc: It is a suspension bridge place where you can feel Oksunbong Peak, one of the 10 scenic views of Jecheon, on the surface of Cheongpung Lake.

spots.name: Uirimji Parkland
spots.desc: It is an amusement park located in Jecheon, Chungcheongbuk-do.

spots.name: Uirimji Historical Museum
spots.desc: A specialized museum where you can learn about the history, structure, irrigation methods, and ecology of Jecheon Uirimji, a reservoir built in ancient times.

spots.name: Cinema 360
spots.desc: Cinema 360 is a full-screen video theater that presents a new world and experience by combining 360-degree ultra-high-definition images and sounds.

spots.name: World Christian Museum
spots.desc: It is a World Christian Museum that displays various biblical objects.

spots.name: Jecheon Mountain Experience Center
spots.desc: It is a place where you can verify your personal abilities and experience virtual disaster escape in the forest. You can experience various experiences such as survival, sky jump, and climbing in one place.

spots.name: Into the cypress forest
spots.desc: It is a place where you can experience side white foot baths, side white soap, and side white shampoo using side white byproducts.

spots.name: Intellectual Museum
spots.desc: The Intellectual Museum is a museum that protects Dokdo, a Korean territory, according to the founding ideology of the Korean Territorial Seowon, and collects, manages, preserves, exhibits, educational, research, and public relations data on Korean territory such as Goto Gando, Daemado, and Primorsky Krai.

spots.name: Jecheon Oriental Medicine Bio Complex International Fermentation Museum
spots.desc: It is located in Jecheon Oriental Medicine Expo, and is a museum where you can enjoy experiences and attractions related to fermentation.

spots.name: Gyodong Folk Painting Village
spots.desc: It is a mural village, and it is a place where you can experience folk painting, food, and pottery.

spots.name: Cheongpungho Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: Held once every spring season for two weeks, this festival represents Jecheon City and is a festival where all generations can see and enjoy cherry blossoms blooming around Cheongpungho Lake.

spots.name: Park Dal Song Festival
spots.desc: The Park Dal Song Festival is a traditional national trot song festival held at the end of August every year since 1997, based on Jecheon's Banyawol composition and Kim Kyo-sung's popular song "Park Dal-jae is crying."

spots.name: A night trip to Jecheon's cultural heritage
spots.desc: Various performances, exhibitions, and experiences can be seen under eight themes, including a drone lighting show with beautifully embroidered Uirimji, Jecheon's representative cultural heritage. It is also a festival where you can enjoy food booths and food trucks. It is held once a year, and in 2024, it was held for two days in early August.

spots.name: Jecheon International Music Film Festival
spots.desc: It is the first music film festival in Korea that enjoys movies and music at the same time, held in Jecheon. This event has been held since 2005 and was held for 5 days in early September as of 2024.

spots.name: The head office below the mountain
spots.desc: It is a restaurant where you can eat Korean set meals located at the bottom of the mountain.

spots.name: A house with a garden
spots.desc: It is a seafood restaurant in Jecheon that sells assorted seafood paste, barley oysters, and soy sauce marinated crab.
spots.addr: a house with 176 garden in Hasocheon-gil

spots.name: Bokhyeon
spots.desc: It is a meat Korean restaurant that sells pork ribs and black pork belly.

spots.name: Cheongpung Golden Tteok-galbi
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant in Jecheon that sells hot pot rice and short rib patties.

spots.name: Cheongpung Golden Trout
spots.desc: It is a raw fish restaurant in Jecheon that sells trout and scented fish.

spots.name: A lakeside restaurant
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant in Jecheon that sells gondre, cheonggukjang, and soybean paste stew.

spots.name: Lysom Forest Headquarters
spots.desc: It is a meat restaurant in Jecheon that sells grilled ribs as its main menu.

spots.name: Cowboy Grill
spots.desc: It is a restaurant in Jecheon that sells traditional Texas barbecue.

spots.name: A small Western restaurant
spots.desc: It is a Western restaurant in Jecheon, where lasagna and steak are representative menus.

spots.name: A toad restaurant
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant that sells pork ribs and gondre rice.

spots.name: Kang Ho-don
spots.desc: It is Jecheon's representative meat restaurant that sells pork.

spots.name: Jecheon Sirakguk
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant that sells dried radish leaves-related food as its main menu.

spots.name: Yakchaeseong County
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant that sells bulgogi, grilled deodeok, and galbi set meals.
spots.addr: 14-71 Cheongpungho-ro 54-gil, Cheongpung-myeon, Yakchaerak Seonghyeon on the 1st floor

spots.name: Venus Myeonji Station
spots.desc: It is a ramen restaurant in Jecheon that sells Japanese ramen.

spots.name: Handmade Pork Cutlet
spots.desc: It is a pork cutlet restaurant in Jecheon that sells handmade king pork cutlet.

spots.name: Ongsimi's sesame buckwheat noodles
spots.desc: It is a restaurant in Jecheon that sells Ongsim and kalguksu as its main menu.

spots.name: Coffee lacquer
spots.desc: It is a cafe in Jecheon where you can see Cheongpungho Lake.

spots.name: Tea cafe chasen
spots.desc: Tea is the main menu and it is a tea cafe in Jecheon that is famous for matcha.

spots.name: Petit chandelier
spots.desc: It is a large cafe in Jecheon decorated with a fairy tale-inspired pink house.

spots.name: Cafe 1929
spots.desc: It is a cafe in Jecheon where you can feel the atmosphere of Hanok.

spots.name: Unmood
spots.desc: It is a large cafe in Jecheon where pets can be accompanied.

spots.name: A medicinal herb
spots.desc: It is a cafe in Jecheon where you can taste Korean desserts.

spots.name: A precinct
spots.desc: It is a place where the former Yongdu Police Station was remodeled and turned into a cafe.

spots.name: Cafe Pino
spots.desc: It is a cafe inside the Pot Garden Park of Uirimji in Jecheon.

spots.name: Cafe Tanjiri
spots.desc: It is a large cafe in Jecheon where you can see Chungjuho Lake.

spots.name: Cafe 322
spots.desc: It is a cafe in Jecheon where you can enjoy the mountain scenery and valley at the same time.

spots.name: Shooting cafe
spots.desc: It is a cafe where you can see the stars best and read books together.

spots.name: A seasonal walk
spots.desc: It is a cafe that can be accompanied by a dog and sells pudding.

spots.name: E-Mart Jecheon Branch
spots.desc: It is a large supermarket located in a distribution complex in Jejudo-dong, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do.

spots.name: Lotte Super Jangnak Branch
spots.desc: Lotte Super and Lotte Mart are the same company, but as a different mart, Lotte Super is a place that focuses more on selling ingredients.

spots.name: Jecheon Station Hanmaum Market
spots.desc: Located in front of Jecheon Station, it combines a permanent market and a regular market.

spots.name: Nammaeji Pond
spots.desc: Nammaeji is a small artificial pond located in Namsan-myeon, Gyeongsan. It is known for its beautiful scenery throughout the year, especially the cherry blossoms in spring and lotus flowers in summer. With surrounding walking trails and a traditional pavilion, it is a popular spot for relaxation and photography. The pond’s seasonal scenery—pink cherry blossoms, lush summer greens, and sunset…

spots.name: Samunghyeon Historical Cultural Museum
spots.desc: Samseonghyeon History and Culture Museum is a multifaceted exhibition space in Gyeongsan dedicated to the lives and achievements of the three local sages—Wonhyo, Seol Chong, and Il‑Yeon. It’s the best place to understand the cultural roots of Gyeongsan, offering engaging exhibits on three influential figures who shaped Korean Buddhist and Confucian traditions.

spots.name: Gyeongsan City Tour
spots.desc: This program introduces tourists to the city’s cultural heritage, natural landscapes, and traditional markets. Wish-Fulfillment Tour: Operates on the second Thursday of every month. Samseonghyeon Premium Tour: Operates on the fourth Saturday of every month. Operating hours: usually from 09:30 to 17:20 (may vary by course). Fee: ₩3,000 per person (experience programs and meals are not included).

spots.name: Noru Climbing
spots.desc: A bustling bouldering gym near Yeungnam University, popular among students and local climbers. It operates daily (12:00–23:00 on weekdays, and 12:00–19:00 on weekends/holidays) and maintains a lively atmosphere full of youthful energy.

spots.name: Otter's Home(이웃집 수달)
spots.desc: Meet YouTube stars Dolce, Latte, Mocha, Soo-hyung, and Dal-nuna at the Otter Lounge — the only zoo in Korea where you can meet otters up close! They offer souvenirs (goods), food, and drinks, and you can even meet different otter families separately if needed.However, since the place is relatively small and doesn’t have many different animals or experiences, it might feel a bit limited if you…
spots.hours: Closed on Thu, Mon–Wed Fri 13:00 – 18:00, Sat Sun 12:30 – 19:00

spots.name: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish-Fulfillment Festival
spots.desc: A representative local event that carries on the tradition of faith in the Gatbawi Buddha—believed to grant any single earnest wish—combining prayer, culture, experiences, and performances.

spots.name: Gyeongsan Jain Danoje Festival
spots.desc: A centuries-old traditional folk festival held in the Gyejeong Forest area, Jain-myeon. It features ritual ceremonies to honor “Han General,” processions, traditional dances such as Yeowonmu, mask dance performances (Pal-Gwangdae), folk games, and a grand Dano ritual — blending local history, faith, and community celebrations.

spots.name: Gyeongsan Café Festival
spots.desc: The Gyeongsan Café Festival, held in late June and early July, showcases about 20 local cafés across Gyeongsan, with a special focus on the region’s signature Sinbi peach. Visitors can enjoy themed drinks and desserts using peaches, attend exhibitions, performances, and hands-on workshops, and take part in free peach tastings and special discount offers. The festival aims to fuse café culture…

spots.name: Jujubes
spots.desc: Gyeongsan is well known for its sweet, high-quality jujubes grown around the Palgongsan area. They are often sold fresh or dried and make a popular local gift.

spots.name: Grapes
spots.desc: Local grapes are recognized for their rich flavor and are widely available during the harvest season in markets and roadside stalls.

spots.name: Nectarines
spots.desc: Gyeongsan’s nectarines are valued for their strong aroma and juicy sweetness, and they are commonly sold at local farms and summer fruit stands.

spots.name: Gyeongsan Traditional Public Market
spots.desc: Gyeongsan Public Market (Gyeongsan Gongseol Market), established in 1956, continues the legacy of traditional markets and serves around 10,000 visitors daily. Thanks to modernization efforts, it now features an arcade roof that makes shopping possible even in rain or snow. Visitors can enjoy authentic local foods, fresh produce, and traditional market energy that offers a glimpse into everyday…

spots.name: Don Ori Jeju Ogyeop
spots.desc: It’s a popular restaurant in Gyeongsan that specializes in various duck dishes, such as stewed or roasted duck.

spots.name: Dong Dong Kalguksu
spots.desc: A popular kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant in Gyeongsan that also serves dishes like pajeon (Korean scallion pancake).

spots.name: Baekjasan Sikyuk Restaurant
spots.desc: It’s a popular restaurant in Gyeongsan specializing in premium Korean beef (Hanwoo).

spots.name: Yongseong Eotang
spots.desc: It is a Korean restaurant specializing in eotang (spicy fish stew), with eotang-guksu (fish stew with noodles) and eotang-gukbap (fish stew with rice) as its most popular dishes.

spots.name: Janggun Jjimdak
spots.desc: It is a popular Korean restaurant located near Yeungnam University, offering dishes such as jjimdak (braised chicken), jeyuk (spicy pork), and osam bulgogi (stir-fried squid and pork) at reasonable prices.

spots.name: Hands Coffee Hayang
spots.desc: Hands Coffee Hayang Branch serves espresso drinks, waffles, frappés, and seasonal desserts.

spots.name: Chales Ano
spots.desc: Chales Ano is a Blue Ribbon-listed café in Gyeongsan, known for its spacious interior and open-air terrace.

spots.name: Coffee Myeongga
spots.desc: A café listed in the Blue Ribbon Guide for three consecutive years. It offers a variety of coffee and also hosts one-day hand-drip brewing classes.

spots.name: Mungyeong Spa
spots.desc: A huge hot spring complex that can accommodate up to 2,500 people at one time. Mungyeong Spa is one of the largest hot spring facilities in North Gyeongsang Province, featuring indoor and outdoor pools, sauna, and family-friendly relaxation zones. The water is rich in minerals known for their therapeutic effects.

spots.name: Patriot Park Yeol Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The size of memorial hall takes you by surprise. It contains detailed and interesting information about Korea's independence activists.

spots.name: Mungyeong Eco Rala & Coal Museum
spots.desc: A museum with a nostalgic theme, dedicated to the miners who once worked in the area.

spots.name: Mungyeong Coal Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to Korea’s coal mining history, located on the site of a former coal mine. Exhibits include mining equipment, life-size tunnel replicas, and multimedia displays showing the lives of coal miners and the industrial development of Korea. Visitors can walk through a reconstructed mine shaft and learn about the transformation of the area into the Eco Rala cultural complex.

spots.name: Daeyasan Mountain Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: A scenic forest retreat located in the foothills of Mt. Daeyasan, part of Woraksan National Park. The recreation forest features cabins, camping areas, and forest trails surrounded by dense pine and oak trees. It’s ideal for hiking, family camping, and summer valley swimming. In autumn, the forest offers stunning foliage views and cool mountain air.

spots.name: Mungyeongsaejae Provincial Park
spots.desc: Mungyeongsaejae is one of Korea’s most famous historical mountain passes, once serving as the main route between Seoul and Yeongnam during the Joseon Dynasty. The provincial park is home to well-preserved stone gates, traditional inn replicas, and scenic forest trails. The area also hosts the Mungyeongsaejae Drama Set, used for filming historical dramas. The 6.5 km trail through the pass offers…

spots.name: Jinnam Gyoban
spots.desc: Jinnam Gyoban, meaning “Bridge over the Valley of Truth,” is one of Mungyeong’s most picturesque spots, where a stone bridge spans the clear upper Namhan River beneath dramatic cliffs. The area is surrounded by pine forests and features several scenic viewpoints. It’s especially popular for autumn foliage and riverside walks, and nearby cafés and traditional restaurants make it a pleasant…

spots.name: Gwaneumsa Temple
spots.desc: A peaceful Buddhist temple located within Mungyeongsaejae Provincial Park. Founded during the Silla Dynasty, Gwaneumsa is dedicated to the Bodhisattva of Compassion, Avalokiteśvara (Gwaneum). The temple is known for its quiet mountain setting, stone pagoda, and panoramic views of the valley below. In spring and autumn, its surroundings are particularly beautiful with blooming azaleas and colorful…

spots.name: Mungyeong Grand Resort Water Sled Park
spots.desc: A seasonal water sled park operated by Mungyeong Grand Resort, located near the scenic Mungyeong Saejae area. It features long water slides, children’s pools, and inflatable play zones surrounded by mountain views. The park is family-friendly, with life jackets and rental tubes available. Open only in summer (usually June–August). Adjacent to the resort’s hotel, café, and spa facilities, making…
spots.price: ₩10,000–15,000 depending on time and ticket type

spots.name: Mungyeong Youth Training Center
spots.desc: A youth activity and education center operated by Mungyeong City, offering cultural, sports, and creative experience programs for local students and visitors. The facility includes a gymnasium, outdoor playground, seminar rooms, and a small library. Various youth camps and weekend classes are held throughout the year, and some spaces can be used for community events or group activities.

spots.name: Buljeong Recreational Forest
spots.desc: A forest recreation area nestled in the mountains north of Mungyeong Saejae. The park offers hiking trails, wooden lodges, campgrounds, and scenic picnic areas surrounded by dense pine and oak trees. It is a popular weekend getaway for families and groups looking for a quiet nature experience. In summer, the Buljeong Stream provides a cool place for wading and relaxation. Reservations for cabins…

spots.name: Mungyeong Paragliding Land
spots.desc: A paragliding site offering tandem and solo flight experiences over the scenic Buljeong and Mungyeong Saejae valleys. Certified instructors provide safety training and take-off assistance, making it suitable even for beginners. The landing field has panoramic mountain views and a small café for spectators. Reservations are recommended, as operations depend on wind and weather conditions.

spots.name: Mungyeong Rail Bike
spots.desc: A popular leisure attraction where visitors can pedal along an old railway line that once connected Mungyeong and Gaeun. The route passes through tunnels, bridges, and scenic countryside, offering great photo opportunities. Each rail bike can seat up to four people, making it ideal for families or couples. The ride lasts about 40 minutes one way, and shuttle buses return passengers to the…

spots.name: Mungyeong Shooting Range
spots.desc: A modern shooting range offering live-fire and clay shooting experiences in a safe and controlled environment. Visitors can try pistol, rifle, or clay target shooting under the supervision of certified instructors. Safety gear and ear protection are provided. The facility also includes a small café and viewing area. Suitable for beginners and groups looking for an exciting outdoor activity near…

spots.name: Mungyeong Traditional Tea Bowl Festival
spots.desc: An annual cultural festival celebrating Mungyeong’s long tradition of ceramic craftsmanship. The event features exhibitions by local potters, hands-on pottery workshops, tea ceremonies, traditional performances, and markets selling handmade tea bowls and crafts. Visitors can try making their own pottery or enjoy local tea in scenic surroundings at the foot of Mungyeong Saejae. The festival…
spots.hours: 09:00–18:00 (held for about 10 days in late April or early May)

spots.name: Mungyeong Omija Festival
spots.desc: A local harvest festival celebrating Mungyeong’s signature fruit, omija (Schisandra berries). Visitors can enjoy omija juice tasting, traditional food markets, live performances, and local craft stalls. The festival also offers hands-on programs such as omija jam making, tea blending, and cooking workshops. It’s held every autumn when the berries are harvested, making it one of the most colorful…

spots.name: Artiatti
spots.desc: A small design goods shop offering handmade stationery, keychains, postcards, and local crafts. Artiatti emphasizes creative, minimalistic designs inspired by Mungyeong’s culture, and serves as both a local creator hub and gift boutique.

spots.name: LORO
spots.desc: A local design and souvenir shop that features creative goods inspired by Mungyeong. LORO offers postcards, keyrings, eco-bags, mugs, and magnets made by local artists. It serves as a small cultural hub for travelers looking for modern interpretations of traditional Mungyeong themes.

spots.name: Horong Store
spots.desc: A small ceramic and souvenir shop located at the entrance of Mungyeong Saejae Provincial Park. The store offers handmade pottery, mugs, and locally inspired crafts. Visitors can browse unique items reflecting Mungyeong’s traditional ceramic culture, and occasionally watch the artisan at work.

spots.name: Mungyeong Agricultural & Specialty Products Market (Saejae Direct Sales Center)
spots.desc: This is the main direct sales center for agricultural and specialty products in Mungyeong, located in the Saejae area. The market features local produce such as omija (five-flavor berry) in various forms (juice, dried, extracts), premium shiitake mushrooms and related products, traditional food items, and regional gift sets. Visitors can sample or purchase fresh goods and artisanal food products…

spots.name: Eune Market
spots.desc: Eune Market is a dessert & gift shop specializing in products made with local ingredients like omija (five-flavor berry), apples, and regional flavors. Its product line includes omija breads, omija wafer sandwiches, jam-infused goods, and packaged gift sets. The store blends café-style ambiance with retail, often appealing to travelers seeking edible souvenirs of Mungyeong.

spots.name: Saejae Mall (Mungyeong Love Saejae Market)
spots.desc: A government-supported specialty market and online store operated by Mungyeong City and the Mungyeong Tourism Corporation. Saejae Mall sells a wide range of regional products such as omija (five-flavor berry) drinks, dried omija, apples, mushrooms, and traditional Korean snacks. Visitors can purchase authentic local goods in person or order them online for nationwide delivery.

spots.name: Omynara
spots.desc: A winery shop specializing in omija (five-flavor berry) wine and local specialty liquors. Visitors can purchase a range of bottled wines, liqueurs, and omija-based gift sets made from berries grown in Mungyeong. The on-site store offers limited editions and premium products that represent the region’s signature flavor.

spots.name: Homeplus Mungyeong
spots.desc: A large supermarket / hypermarket chain selling a full range of groceries, household goods, electronics, and local specialty products. Homeplus Mungyeong offers a one-stop shopping experience for both daily necessities and regional souvenirs, making it convenient for travelers wanting to pick up snacks, local produce, or packaged goods.

spots.name: No Brand Mungyeong Mojeon Branch
spots.desc: A discount supermarket branch of the No Brand chain, offering groceries, daily necessities, and a selection of packaged local products. It’s a convenient spot for larger shopping needs while visiting Mungyeong.

spots.name: No Brand Mungyeong Central Market Branch
spots.desc: A supermarket branch located within the central market district, offering a variety of grocery items, household goods, and packaged local products. It provides convenient access for both locals and tourists to shop for everyday needs and souvenirs while exploring the market.

spots.name: Minji Song-eojang
spots.desc: Minji Song-eojang is a trout restaurant located in Gaeun-eup, Mungyeong. They specialise in fresh trout dishes (sashimi, fry, cutlet, sushi, stew). It has its own trout farm, free parking, and is well-known to locals and travelers.
spots.price: Trout sashimi ~₩34,000; Trout fry ~₩34,000; Trout cutlet ~₩15,000; Trout sushi/roll ~₩15,000; Stew (Maeuntang) ~₩3,000…

spots.name: Mokryeon Garden
spots.desc: Mokryeon Garden is a Korean food restaurant in Mungyeong’s Saejae area, located at Entrance Parking Lot No.1 of Mungyeongsaejae Provincial Park. It offers traditional Korean dishes including grilled meats (석쇠구이), 산채비빔밥, 전골, 정식 한상 차림, 냉면 등. It opens early at 8:00, making it a good breakfast or early meal spot for tourists visiting the trail.
spots.price: Gochujang Grilled Set Meal is available for ₩15,000, Wild Vegetable Bibimbap for ₩10,000, and Freshwater Spicy Fish…

spots.name: HanGukGwan SikDang
spots.desc: Korean Gwan Sikdang is a traditional Korean restaurant offering meals with rice, soup, and various side dishes (banchan). It often features Korean BBQ, where diners grill meats like bulgogi or pork belly at the table. The restaurant provides a communal and flavorful dining experience reflecting Korean culinary traditions.
spots.price: Korean Gwan Sikdang offers traditional Korean dishes such as grilled meats, stews, and banchan, with prices ranging…

spots.name: Familia
spots.desc: Familia is a charming Italian-style restaurant set in a hanok-inspired building in 문경새재 area. The setting is picturesque, with a lovely garden and ample parking, making it a relaxing spot for lunch or dinner. The menu includes pasta, risotto, steak, pizza, and salads. Signature dishes such as “트러플 쑥 크림 파스타 (Truffle Mugwort Cream Pasta)”, “부채살 수비드 스테이크 (Flatiron Sous-Vide Steak)”, and “흑미 필라프…

spots.name: Songnaechon Sannamulbap
spots.desc: Songnaechon Sannamulbap is a rustic, homey Korean restaurant specializing in healthy 산나물 (mountain greens) dishes in a scenic village setting. The focus is on 자연산 나물 (wild mountain greens), minimal seasoning to let the ingredients’ own flavour shine, and balanced sides. Signature dishes include 산채육회비빔밥, 문경산신령비빔밥, 발효산나물밥, as well as 산나물전 (fried greens pancake) and 수육/발효수육. It’s good for…
spots.hours: 11:00-20:00 daily except Mon; break time 15:30-16:30; last order 19:00
spots.price: Most main dishes range between KRW 13,000 and 18,000. The signature “Mountain Vegetable Raw Beef Bibimbap” is about KRW…

spots.name: Café Seodeul
spots.desc: A modern café located in a quiet rural area of Maseong-myeon, about 20 minutes by car from central Mungyeong. The building features wide glass walls and terrace seating overlooking nearby mountains and a stream. The menu includes coffee, tea, and specialty drinks such as omija-based beverages and butterscotch lattes, along with a small selection of baked goods. The café has both indoor and…

spots.name: Café Gaeun Station
spots.desc: A café built inside the renovated Gaeun Station, which once served the Mungyeong railway line. The interior retains parts of the original platform and signage, combining historical elements with a modern coffeehouse atmosphere. It serves standard espresso-based drinks, teas, and desserts, and offers seating both inside the old station building and on the former platform area. The café is a short…

spots.name: Café Eune
spots.desc: A small café located in a quiet rural area near Buljeong Recreation Forest. The building has a simple modern design with large windows facing the surrounding forest. It offers coffee, tea, and homemade desserts, as well as omija-based seasonal drinks using local ingredients. Outdoor terrace seating provides views of nearby hills, and the area is often visited by hikers heading toward Buljeong…

spots.name: Nakdonggang River History Museum
spots.desc: The Nakdonggang River History Museum presents the natural and cultural history of the Nakdong River. Exhibits include displays on ecology, local traditions, and the river’s importance in Korean history. Visitors can explore interactive exhibits, dioramas, and multimedia presentations. The museum also hosts educational programs and special events for children and families. It is located near the…

spots.name: Sangju Museum
spots.desc: Sangju Museum showcases the rich cultural heritage and history of the Sangju region. The museum’s permanent collection includes archaeological artifacts, traditional crafts, and exhibits on local life. It also features special exhibitions that highlight both historical and contemporary themes. Educational programs and guided tours are available for students and visitors. Surrounded by natural…

spots.name: Seongjubong Recreational Forest
spots.desc: Seongjubong Recreational Forest is a popular destination for hiking, camping, and eco-friendly leisure activities. The forest is known for its clean air, dense pine trees, and scenic walking trails. Visitors can enjoy cabins, camping sites, and educational nature programs. It is also a habitat for diverse flora and fauna, making it a great spot for ecological exploration. The surrounding mountain…

spots.name: Janggak Falls
spots.desc: A stream starting from Cheonhwangbong Peak, the highest peak of Songnisan Mountain, winds through the Janggak-dong Valley. There is a waterfall that falls along a 6-meter-high cliff, and this is Janggak Falls. Geumranjeong Pavilion is erected on the rock formations above the waterfall, and there is an old pine forest around it, which further enhances the beauty. Stroller rental status impossible.

spots.name: Gyeongcheon Island Park
spots.desc: Around Gyeongcheon Island, there are many linked resources such as the National Nakdonggang River Biological Resource Center, the Sansangnaru Tourist Site, the Water Leisure Center, the Bicycle Museum, the International Horseback Riding Ground, and the Military Theme Park.

spots.name: Nagak Mountain
spots.desc: It is located on the eastern side of the Taebaek Mountains. The name of the mountain is known as one of Uljin's representative sea-level terrains.

spots.name: Namjangsa
spots.desc: It is one of the eight scenic spots in North Gyeongsang Province (八景). It was built in 1186 (the 16th year of King Myeongjong's reign) by King 覺圓 of 尙 in the Goryeo Dynasty and named it Namjangsa Temple.
spots.hours: Open daily — temple grounds generally accessible 00:00–24:00; main halls open during temple visiting hours

spots.name: Donamseowon
spots.desc: The memorial tablets of Jeong Mong-ju, Kim Goong-pil, Jeong Yeo-chang, Lee Eon-jeok, Lee Hwang, Roh So-soo, Ryu Seong-ryong, Jeong Gyeong-se, and Lee Jun are enshrined and held.

spots.name: Myeongju Museum
spots.desc: It displays the manufacturing process and history of silk, as well as various traditional clothing and textile crafts using silk fabrics.

spots.name: Maeak Mountain
spots.desc: The mountain's elevation is about 614m above sea level and its slope is gentle, making it relatively easy to climb. The Sangju Hyanggyo is located in the middle of the mountain, which is connected to the Sangju's cultural and historical heritage.

spots.name: Royal Tomb of King Taejo of Goryeong Gaya
spots.desc: The remains are passed down to the tomb of King Lee Jin-ashi, the founder of Gaya.

spots.name: Bukcheon Civic Park
spots.desc: As the park is built around Bukcheon Stream, which flows through Sangju City, it boasts a pleasant environment with natural scenery along the river. It has various amenities such as a walking trail, bicycle path, grass square, and sports facility.

spots.name: Sangju Gonggumji
spots.desc: Gonggeomji is an ancient reservoir located in Gonggeom-myeon, Sangju. It is believed to have been constructed during the Proto-Three Kingdoms period and later rebuilt in the Goryeo dynasty. The reservoir played a vital role in local agriculture and community life. Today it is designated as a protected wetland with ecological and cultural value. Visitors can enjoy both its historical significance…

spots.name: Otae Reservoir
spots.desc: It contributes to the development of local agriculture through the stable supply of agricultural water, while at the same time serving as a multi-purpose space for residents to enjoy leisure and relaxation. It supplies agricultural water.

spots.name: Ungee Mountain
spots.desc: It is a low mountain about 311 m above sea level. Its natural environment is well-preserved, so visitors can observe various plants and animals.

spots.name: Osong Falls
spots.desc: A 15-meter-high waterfall created by a mountain stream originating from the Sinseondae of Songnisan Mountain falls in five or seven tiers between cliffs. Water flowing between natural forests and rocks does not dry out even in drought.

spots.name: Moonjangdae
spots.desc: It is 1,054 meters high. It is also called Unjangdae because a large rock rises high in the sky and forms a superb view as if it were in contact with white clouds. There is an empty space on the mountain floor where about 50 people can sit, and you can enjoy the superb view of Songnisan at a glance.

spots.name: Myowbong
spots.desc: It is a mountain that boasts an altitude of about 922 meters above sea level. Myobong is part of the Wolaksan National Park, and it has a unique natural scenery with its rugged mountains and many strange rocks. The name 'Myobong' is said to have originated from the shape of the mountain's ridges that look as sleek as a cat.

spots.name: Daewonjongsa
spots.desc: Built in a relatively modern era, the temple is not large but serves as a place for Buddhist practice and meditation in the city center. Like many temples, a variety of Buddhist rituals and events are held here, providing a place for Buddhists to gather and perform joint rituals.

spots.name: Yongheungsa
