spots.desc: This temple belongs to the Korean Buddhist Jogye Order, and although its history is not long-standing, it has established itself as a center of Buddhist faith and practice. Buddhist rituals and events are held regularly, and it functions as a place for Buddhists to gather to offer or perform rituals.

spots.name: Munjangdae Terrace
spots.desc: A great hiking spot with beautiful 360° views once you reach the top. Remember to bring good hiking boots.

spots.name: Sangju International Equestrian Center
spots.desc: A place where children can experience horse riding for the first time. They have a range of pony sizes.

spots.name: Farmers' Room
spots.desc: It is a large cafe of 3,000 pyeong near Sangju, where visitors can enjoy coffee and drinks while appreciating various animals (horses, rabbits, sheep, goats) on farms, gardens, and ranches.
spots.hours: Mon Thu Fri 12:30-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-20:00, closed Wed

spots.name: Sangju International Riding Center
spots.desc: With its large-scale equestrian facilities, it is a hub that hosts national and international equestrian events and operates horseback riding-related programs. This equestrian center is one of the largest equestrian facilities in Korea, offering various equestrian activities and education.

spots.name: Modong Farm
spots.desc: It is a Farm where visitors can see and feed animals such as sheep, geese, rabbits, horses, and chickens.

spots.name: Ugong's Strawberry Garden
spots.desc: It is a place where visitors can experience picking strawberries in a cozy space such as a garden.

spots.name: Sangju Central Market
spots.desc: Sangju Central Market is a traditional market, famous for its three hundred villages, including rice, cocoons, and dried persimmons. It sells agricultural products, clothing, and miscellaneous goods, including dried persimmons, a special product.

spots.name: Sangju Dried Persimmon Distribution Center
spots.desc: The city’s main dried-persimmon (gotgam) trade center operated by a local producers’ cooperative. You’ll find premium gotgam, sliced dried persimmons, and assorted persimmon-based products, with seasonal gift sets available and nationwide shipping.

spots.name: Myeongsil-Sangju Central Market
spots.desc: The city’s largest traditional market, combining a permanent market and a periodic street bazaar held on the 2nd and 7th of each month. Visitors can browse fresh produce, local specialties, household goods, and traditional snacks. The inner section hosts youth-run craft shops and small cafés, giving the market a mix of old and new Sangju culture.

spots.name: Hamchang Market
spots.desc: A traditional five-day market serving the northern region of Sangju. It opens on the 1st and 6th of each month and features a variety of local farm produce, herbs, and household goods. The atmosphere is rustic and authentic, with farmers and villagers gathering to trade in the open-air stalls. It’s a good place to experience the rural charm of Sangju and sample regional specialties.

spots.name: Gongseong Market
spots.desc: A small traditional marketplace serving nearby farming villages. It opens twice a month—on the 1st and 6th days—and offers local vegetables, grains, and daily necessities. The atmosphere is relaxed and communal, with elderly vendors selling handmade goods and local snacks. Visitors can experience genuine rural market culture away from the city center.

spots.name: Pungmul Market
spots.desc: Pungmul Market, held alongside the main Central Market, is a traditional “pungmuljang” featuring folk goods, antiques, and local crafts. On market days (the 2nd and 7th), the surrounding streets fill with stalls selling traditional snacks, farming tools, and vintage household items. The atmosphere is lively and full of street music, offering a glimpse into Sangju’s community spirit and…

spots.name: Hwaryeong Market
spots.desc: A rural five-day market that opens on the 3rd and 8th of each month. It’s known for its friendly vendors and small-town charm. Local farmers sell freshly harvested vegetables, fruits, and homemade condiments. The market’s open-air layout and relaxed pace make it a pleasant stop for travelers seeking an authentic countryside experience in southern Sangju.

spots.name: Euncheok Market
spots.desc: Euncheok Market is a traditional five-day market held on the 4th and 9th of each month. It serves the farming community in northwestern Sangju and offers locally grown produce, herbs, and homemade goods. The market retains a classic rural charm, with open stalls and friendly interactions between merchants and visitors. It’s an ideal stop to experience a quiet, authentic slice of everyday life in…

spots.name: Sangju Jangteo Agricultural Cooperative
spots.desc: Sangju Jangteo is an agricultural cooperative that handles cultivation, processing, and direct sales of Sangju’s specialty crops. Products include dried persimmons (gotgam), omija extracts, and doraji (balloon flower) products. Locals and visitors can buy packaged local agricultural goods directly from the cooperative.

spots.name: Sangju Nonghyup Hanaro Mart
spots.desc: This is the main agricultural cooperative-affiliated supermarket in Sangju, offering a wide range of fresh produce, packaged goods, and daily necessities. Because it is operated under Nonghyup’s Hanaro Mart network, it often features local agricultural products prominently, making it a reliable place to pick up Sangju specialties along with everyday items.

spots.name: E-Mart Sangju
spots.desc: The major hypermart in Sangju provides a wide range of goods from groceries, fresh produce, household goods, clothing, electronics, and more. It often features local agricultural products as part of its selection. Free parking is available, and it serves as a convenient one-stop shop in Mansan-dong for both locals and visitors.

spots.name: sangju_space
spots.desc: You can come up along the uphill path of the public parking lot in Namsan Neighborhood Park located opposite Sangju City Hall. Charging electric vehicles and parking is available in the public parking lot in front of the store or before going up the uphill. Sangju City Hall is 3 minutes away on foot. Electric cars can be charged in the city hall.

spots.name: cafe_in_garden
spots.desc: Search "Sangju Baptist Church" or "Caffeine Garden" and you'll see it right away. 2023 GCA Hand Drip Championship 1st place, Golden Coffee Award Hand Drip Championship, Northern European Garden can enjoy brunch, coffee, organic homemade tea drinks and shaved ice (summer) and can be accompanied by do.

spots.name: sokurian
spots.desc: Please use the public parking lot (free) in Sangju Middle School for parking lots. It's a 2-minute walk from the parking lot.

spots.name: Myeongju Garden
spots.desc: When using public transportation: Sangju Hamchang or Mungyeong Jeomchon Intercity Bus Terminal. Take a taxi. When using your own vehicle: Resident (shambles).Get off at Andong IC, turn left, go straight through Rotary and find the sign of Myeongju Garden on the right. Myeongju Garden is located in Hamchang, located between Sangju and Mungyeong in Gyeongsangbuk-do.
spots.addr: Myeongju Garden, a cafe in 7 Saejam-gil, Hamchang-eup

spots.name: Goryeo Bunsik
spots.desc: Famous longtime market snack shop (broadcast-featured) — known for handmade tonkatsu, gimbap, jjolmyeon, dumplings; market atmosphere.

spots.name: 상주주막
spots.desc: Traditional-style tavern serving regional Korean dishes (haemul pajeon, bibimbap, gukbap) with riverside/old-house ambiance. Popular for local specialty dining.

spots.name: Hwawon Bakery
spots.desc: Station-front bakery & cafe offering daily-baked breads (salt bread, bagels), sandwiches and coffee; suitable for quick stops.

spots.name: Sangju Space
spots.desc: A multi-floor landmark café with rooftop views and photo spots near Sangju City Hall. Popular for large interior spaces and rooftop.

spots.name: Days
spots.desc: Dessert shop specializing in cream pudding, baked goods and custom cakes; popular for takeaways and special orders.

spots.name: Nari 'Bunji' Basin
spots.desc: Nari ‘Bunji’ Basin is the largest flat caldera basin on Ulleungdo, formed by volcanic collapse beneath Seonginbong. It is the only extensive plain on the island and supports settlements and cultivation of medicinal and other plants. Traditional “tumakjip” houses are still seen there, built in distinctive styles integrating local materials. The basin is surrounded by ridges and steep slopes…

spots.name: Jugam Mongdol Beach
spots.desc: Jugam Mongdol Beach is a pebble beach on Ulleungdo, where sand is absent and the shoreline is composed entirely of rounded stones. It spans roughly 500 m in length and about 20 m in width. The waves and rocky coastline have smoothed the pebbles over time, creating an aesthetic black pebble seashore. Nearby natural attractions include the Samseonam (Three Fairy Rocks) and views toward Gwaneumdo…

spots.name: Songgot-bong
spots.desc: Songgot-bong is a sharp, pointed peak on the northwestern coast of Ulleungdo known for its dramatic cliffside appearance. Its name literally means “awl peak,” reflecting its needle-like silhouette rising from the sea. The summit offers sweeping views of the East Sea and the island’s rugged coastline. Hikers often approach via coastal trails and paths that skirt cliffs and rock formations.…

spots.name: Tours
spots.desc: Ferry and bus tours are available. The bus tour costs around ₩15,000 and last about 4 hours. But the timetables vary depending on the company. Contact Ulleungdo Tourism at +82 54-791-0066 for more information. The high speed ferry takes about 2 hours to go around the island. There are two to four rides daily. For the exact times contact the Ferry Association at +82 54-791-4477.

spots.name: Yaksu Park
spots.desc: Directly translated, 'yak' means medicine and 'su' means water. The mineral spring is supposed to have healing properties. It is a short 10 minute walk from the ferry terminal and is also where you can find the Dokdo Museum and ride the cable car.

spots.name: Cable car ride
spots.desc: This is a must-do activity. From the car you can get a panoramic view of the island. It goes up to the nearby Manghyang Peak and on a clear day, you can see Dokdo.

spots.name: Seonginbong
spots.desc: The large mountain in the middle of the island. At the foot lies rare plants found only there. It is a good 5 to 6 hour (coming and going) hike from Dodong-ri or a similar 5 hour hike back to the Nari 'Bunji' Basin.

spots.name: Dodong Lighthouse
spots.desc: On a clear day you can see Dokdo from the top. You can have a leisurely one hour walk up a staircase from the ferry terminal.

spots.name: Dokdo Observation Platform
spots.desc: Here you'll get a great view of Dodong from above, and the southern parts of the island. The island of Dokdo is also visible on a clear day. You can see the platform when you arrive at Dodong harbor. To get here, take the cable car (₩7,000 return) from the Dokdo Museum.

spots.name: 99 Sikdang
spots.desc: Here you will find ojing-eo bulgogi (spicy grilled squid mixed with veggies) and another island specialty, taggaebibap (shellfish with rice).

spots.name: Bohyeonsan Dam Zip Wire
spots.desc: The Yeongcheon City Bohyeonsan Dam Zip Wire is a sport where you walk across the dam from a starting point on the mountain overlooking the dam to the destination, hanging onto a single wire and moving as if dropping. Ride the 1,411-meter distance in about 90 seconds and experience speeds up to 100 km/h. A mountain monorail takes you from the ticket office to the start of the zipline, and a…

spots.name: Hwarang Seolhwa Village
spots.desc: A Hwarang-themed cultural park featuring interactive exhibits, VR experiences, a 4D dome theater, traditional Korean archery, and outdoor attractions inspired by Silla-era Hwarang legends.

spots.name: Sudosa Temple
spots.desc: The monk’s temple is located near Chisan Valley on the slopes of Palgongsan Mountain and houses the Nodasanbul Gwaebultang, Treasure No. 1271.

spots.name: Dolhalmae Wishing Stone
spots.desc: Dolhalmae is a famous site made of mysterious granite with a history of about 350 years, where people make a single wish and fortune-telling. They lift an oval granite stone, about 25 cm in diameter and weighing around 10 kg, to make a wish. Here, there is a method for making wishes: first, empty your mind and lift the stone to feel its weight. After that, say your name, date of birth, and…

spots.name: Uroji Ecological Park(우로지생태공원)
spots.desc: A lakeside ecological park with walking paths and scenic views, suitable for a relaxing stroll and enjoying the surrounding natural landscape.

spots.name: Yeongcheon Bohyeon Mountain Starlight Festival
spots.desc: The Yeongcheon Bohyeonsan Starlight Festival will feature the opening of the Astronomy Center, astronomy lectures, and various hands-on programs. Using telescopes installed in the experience center, visitors can observe the sun during the day and various celestial bodies at night. In addition, the Bohyeonsan Observatory will be open only during the festival, allowing visitors to conduct…

spots.name: Let's Run Park Yeongcheon
spots.desc: Multi-purpose cultural space suited for families. Leisure activities and sports. Special horse races held every Sunday.

spots.name: Yeongcheon Wood Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: Forest culture experience space about forest ecology, education, and culture, for people of all ages, including toddlers and young children, who can create craft. Wide variety of programs; also just having a simple forest retreat is possible.

spots.name: Yeongcheon Public Market
spots.desc: A traditional Korean-style market selling fresh food, medicinal herbs, groceries as well as local arts and crafts. It is primarily for the locals so it is a challenge for English speakers to get by. Try the twisted bread sticks and gomtang soup.

spots.name: E-mart Yeongcheon
spots.desc: E-Mart Yeongcheon is a large supermarket. Also household goods and home appliances.

spots.name: Yeongcheon Uri Whole Foods Mart
spots.desc: Supermarket that stays open late. It has a well-stocked selection of meat, seafood, and produce.

spots.name: Pyeondaejang Yeonghwa Sikdang
spots.desc: Known for its light and refreshing Hanwoo beef yukhoe, tossed with fresh water dropwort, green onions, and sesame oil. The signature dishes are the yukhoe—made with thinly sliced, tender round steak that brings out the meat’s natural umami—and the yukhoe bibimbap.

spots.name: Hwapyung Daegun
spots.desc: Hwapyung Daegun is a restaurant specializing in beef. Their Hanwoo yukhoe, yukhoe bibimbap, and soju mulgogi are popular. When you order a meat dish, you get a free serving of doenjang jjigae.

spots.name: Pohang Halmae Jip
spots.desc: Beef soup restaurant that has been passed down through three generations since 1950. Famous for its beef head gomtang, made with beef head broth simmered for hours in a large cast-iron pot and generously loaded with beef head meat.

spots.name: Dew it
spots.desc: Dewit is a popular café in Yeongcheon City, with spacious interior. Group seating and sofa seating available. Menu items include the butternut squash and ricotta cheese sandwich, vanilla bean latte, and grapefruit ade. Parking is available in the lot in front of the store or at the Uroji Ecological Park public parking lot.

spots.name: Lake 410
spots.desc: Lake 410 is a spacious café with views of Uroji Lake in Yeongcheon. Try yje Teddy Cheese Cake and Chocolate Cake. Americano and cake set menu

spots.name: letter coffee
spots.desc: Specialty filter coffee shop Wide variety of coffee drinks, including decaf and oat lattes. Also desserts. Spacious interior. Dogs welcome.

spots.name: Buseok Temple
spots.desc: Renowned as one of the most beautiful temples in the area Buseoksa draws in the most visitors in the fall when leaves cover the area in color. The area has plenty of restaurants and is famous for apples. One of seven Korean mountain mountain monasteries to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2018.

spots.name: Sosu Seowan
spots.desc: Known to be the home of Joseon scholars and the first Confucian school. The entrance fee includes the ticket into Seonbichon Village (선비촌), a living museum depicting traditional, Seonbi life. It's one of nine components of the world heritage site "Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies".

spots.name: Seonbichon Village
spots.desc: This is where the cultural heritage of Korea’s classical scholars is preserved. It offers a variety of traditional activities for visitors: making Injeolmi rice cake, hanging wish lanterns, attending a traditional wedding ceremony or playing folk games such as yutnori or jegichagi. Traditional dining is available at Jeojatgeori Street. You can stay overnight in a traditional hanok house..

spots.name: Sobaeksan National Park
spots.desc: Hike the various trails in and around Sobaek Mountain. There are two main entrances accessible by public transport from Yeongju. The first is Sam-ga which is the shortest hike to the highest point. It takes around 3 hours from the trailhead.

spots.name: Heungbuga
spots.desc: There's a wait. Yukhoe bibimbap is delicious. The basic side dishes are full.

spots.name: Geumsansa
spots.desc: In fact, it is a temple that any Korean citizen must have heard at least once, because it was a place of misfortune where Gyeon Hwon, the king of Later Baekje, was forcibly detained by his eldest son, Shingum, in the late Three Kingdoms Period in the early Goryeo Dynasty.

spots.name: Arirang a museum of literature
spots.desc: The Arirang Literature Museum was built in the Byeokgolje Museum Complex in Gimje on May 16, 2003 to establish Gimje's identity as a place of literature and history in the epic novel Arirang by writer Cho Jung-rae (1943~) and to share the literary spirit and historical consciousness contained in Arirang with more people.

spots.name: Manghaesa Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple overlooking the Yellow Sea and the nearby islands. The temple has a long history dating back to the Silla period and was rebuilt several times during the Joseon dynasty. It is known for its coastal scenery and was designated a nationally recognized scenic site in 2024.

spots.name: Gwisinsa Temple
spots.desc: A historic Buddhist temple traditionally believed to have been founded by the monk Uisang in 676 during the Unified Silla period. Its grounds contain Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, a nationally designated Treasure, along with a three-story stone pagoda, a stupa and stone animal sculptures. The temple is situated in a quiet village near Moaksan Mountain.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 09:00–18:00; Nov–Feb 09:00–17:00; closed Mon and Jan 1

spots.name: Horizon Festival
spots.desc: Held late September and early October, this is a festival celebrating Korea's traditional farming culture.

spots.name: Earthenware Kiln of Bugeo-ri
spots.desc: It is a space where pottery was made during the Joseon Dynasty and is making efforts to make pottery again. Anyone can experience pottery, so let's try it.

spots.name: Guemsansa
spots.desc: It is a temple located at the southwest foot of Moaksan Mountain, Geumsan-ri, Geumsan-myeon, and is the headquarters of the 17th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.

spots.name: Daeheunggak
spots.desc: Daeheunggak, an old Chinese restaurant with a tradition of more than 40 years in Gimje. The traces of time can be seen throughout the store, including red-painted menus and antique chairs.

spots.name: Urim garden(유림가든)
spots.desc: This restaurant is a hidden restaurant. It might be hard to find it because it's in the countryside, but let's make sure to go. Menu: spicy chicken soup, shirimp soup, rice

spots.name: jo's sundae soup(조만영의 벌떡순대국)
spots.desc: You can taste a lot of sundae gukbap and Gimje rice. Recommended for big eaters. Menu: Sundae soup

spots.name: jo's sundae soup(원평지평선청보리한우촌)
spots.desc: It is a taste that even foreigners can easily like. Menu: raw meat(cow) Bibimbap

spots.name: Prison filming location
spots.desc: If you have ever watched a prison scene in a Korean film or drama, then chances are it was filmed here, in the country's only purpose built prison set.

spots.name: Garam Literature Museum
spots.desc: Garam Byung-gi Lee (Garam is his pen-name) is a scholar of Koran literature who established theory of Modern Korean Sijo (traditional three-verse Korean poem). This literature museum is founded to commemorate his achievement related Korean literature. (updated Sep 2019)

spots.name: Nabawi Cathedral
spots.desc: Nabawi Cathedral is a unique type of building that combines Korean and Western architecture. The front of the cathedral is decorated with a Gothic three-story vertical bell tower and an arched entrance, and the roof and walls maintain the traditional wooden hanok shape.

spots.name: Experiencing Prisoners in Prison
spots.desc: The set consists of the first and second floors, and the interior and exterior walls of the building are equipped with phrases necessary for edification. Although it is an experience, you will see how precious freedom is.

spots.name: Experience making red pepper paste
spots.desc: You can see more than 3,500 traditional jars on 20,000 pyeong, and you can experience making red pepper paste using only organic ingredients.

spots.name: Iksan Jewelry Festival
spots.desc: You can buy jewelry at reasonable prices as well as watch 60 jewelry companies' colorful jewelry and heartfelt works. In addition, there are various attractions such as the Royal Palace Jewel Theme Tourist Site and the Baekje Historic Site, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Chrysanthemum Festival
spots.desc: Various events will be held, including outdoor chrysanthemum exhibitions, promotion and sales of agricultural products, national chrysanthemum product contests, and cultural performances.

spots.name: Maeil Market
spots.desc: Iksan Maeil Market was selected as an excellent market among 1,600 traditional markets nationwide at the 2008 National Excellent Market Fair. It sells a lot of food and specialties.

spots.name: Spring Day 35
spots.desc: There is a greenhouse garden cafe, a cat. have a good view of the picture.

spots.name: Museong-seowon
spots.desc: A Confucian academy, one of nine to make up the world heritage site Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies.

spots.name: Jeongeupsa Culture Park
spots.desc: A cultural park dedicated to Jeongeupsa, a famous Baekje Gayo. The park features a statue of the heroine of Jeongeupsa, a shrine, a monument commemorating the poem, walking trails and cultural facilities.

spots.name: Jeongeup Gujeolcho Flower Festival
spots.desc: An annual autumn festival held at Gujeolcho Local Garden, featuring fields of white gujeolcho flowers among pine trees. The festival includes live performances, busking, hands-on activities, local food and specialty products.
spots.price: Adults ₩7,000; teenagers, military personnel and seniors ₩5,000; children ₩3,000

spots.name: Jeongeupsa Culture Festival
spots.desc: An annual cultural festival celebrating Jeongeupsa, an ancient Korean song from the Baekje period. Held at Jeongeupsa Park, the festival features cultural performances, ceremonies and programs highlighting Jeongeup's local history and heritage.

spots.name: Solnamu Tteokbangatgan
spots.desc: A traditional rice cake shop where visitors can buy locally made tteok, including sommeori-tteok.

spots.name: Chunhyang Theme Park
spots.desc: Paid park dedicated to Namwon's famous love story, Chunhyangge. It depicts various scenes from the story and also has a pottery museum on premises.

spots.name: Manin Memorial Tomb
spots.desc: A historic memorial site honoring the soldiers and civilians who died defending Namwon Fortress during the Japanese invasion of 1597. The site contains a collective burial mound and Chungnyeolsa Shrine, where the fallen are commemorated. Designated a national historic site in 1981, it offers visitors an opportunity to learn about the Battle of Namwon and the region's wartime history.

spots.name: Honbul Literary House
spots.desc: A literary museum dedicated to Choi Myeong-hee and her acclaimed novel Honbul, set in Nobong Village, which inspired the novel's setting. The traditional Korean-style museum displays the author's personal belongings, a recreation of her writing room, and exhibits about the novel and local history.
spots.hours: 09:00–18:00 (17:00 in winter). Closed Mondays and January 1.

spots.name: Silsangsa Temple
spots.desc: A historic Buddhist temple founded in 828 during the Silla period, located on flat farmland near Jirisan National Park. Unlike many Korean temples built on mountainsides, Silsangsa stands in a peaceful rural setting. Visitors can explore its ancient stone pagodas, stone lanterns, and other cultural treasures while enjoying the surrounding countryside.
spots.price: Admission fee: confirm with the temple before visiting

spots.name: Namwon City Kim Byeong-jong Art Museum
spots.desc: A public art museum dedicated to the work of Kim Byeong-jong, a painter and writer born in Namwon. Opened in 2018, the museum houses artworks and literary materials donated by the artist, alongside changing exhibitions. Surrounded by woodland, the museum combines contemporary architecture, art, and natural scenery.

spots.name: Add Namwon City Kim Byeong-jong Art Museum to See section
spots.desc: An ecological education museum introducing the Baekdudaegan mountain range, its wildlife, and the traditional culture of mountain villages. Exhibits include interactive displays, a 5D circular theater, and themed exhibitions about the region's natural environment. The complex also features outdoor spaces and an insect greenhouse.
spots.hours: 09:00–17:00. Closed Mondays, Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok.
spots.price: Adults ₩2,000; teenagers and military personnel ₩1,500; children ₩1,000

spots.name: Sanctuary of Korean Traditional Music
spots.desc: A museum and cultural complex dedicated to preserving Korean traditional music, especially pansori. Located near Jirisan Mountain, it features exhibitions of traditional instruments, displays about renowned singers, practice facilities and an outdoor performance area. Visitors can learn about the history of Korean music and may participate in traditional music activities when available.
spots.price: Free admission. Some activities may cost extra

spots.name: Fiorium
spots.desc: An immersive media art exhibition hall created by transforming a formerly unused facility into a cultural attraction. Its themed galleries combine light, sound, digital technology, and artistic interpretations of Namwon's cultural heritage. Visitors can experience interactive installations and explore exhibitions inspired by local art and nature.
spots.hours: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sun 10:00–19:00; Fri–Sat 10:00–21:00. Closed Tuesdays. Last admission 30 minutes before closing.
spots.price: Adults ₩12,000; teenagers ₩8,000; children ₩6,000. Discounts for Namwon residents

spots.name: Namwon Aerospace Observatory
spots.desc: A municipal science museum and observatory offering experiences in astronomy and aerospace science. Visitors can observe the Sun, Moon and planets through telescopes, watch immersive presentations in the planetarium, and explore aviation exhibits and flight simulation activities. Observation programs depend on weather conditions.
spots.hours: Apr–Oct 10:00–22:00 (last admission 21:00); Nov–Mar 10:00–21:00 (last admission 20:00). Break 12:00–13:00. Closed…

spots.name: Jirisan Herb Valley
spots.desc: A large herb-themed garden and ecological attraction at the foot of Baraebong Mountain in the Jirisan area. Visitors can explore herb gardens, seasonal flower displays and greenhouses, and enjoy walking paths surrounded by mountain scenery. Plant-related activities and guided tours are also offered, with advance reservations required for some programs.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:00); Nov–Feb 09:00–17:00 (last admission 16:00). Closed Mondays.
spots.price: Adults ₩4,000; teenagers and military personnel ₩2,000; children and seniors ₩1,500. Additional fees for some activities

spots.name: Gyoryongsanseong Fortress
spots.desc: A historic stone fortress built along the natural terrain of Gyoryongsan Mountain, approximately 518 m above sea level. Its walls extend for about 3.1 km and follow the mountain ridges. Visitors can explore the surviving stone walls and enjoy the surrounding forest scenery. Wear comfortable walking shoes, as the site is located on mountainous terrain.
spots.hours: Open-air historic site; visiting hours not specified.
spots.price: No admission fee listed; confirm locally

spots.name: Namgye-seowon
spots.desc: One of nine Confucian academies (seowon) to make up the world heritage site Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies.

spots.name: Daecheon Beach
spots.desc: This is the beach that represents Boryeong. Endlessly continuing beach with white sand, blue sea, small and big islands dotted along the horizon, colorful swimsuits looks, pine forest enough to keep the sunshine off, the sun dropping slowly behind the horizon.

spots.name: Mt. Seongju
spots.desc: In Boryeong, there is a place reminding the sentence, "When I got out of the tunnel, there was a snow country", which is the first sentence of Japanese author Kawabata Yasunari's novel Yukiguni. That is "Seongju" tunnel. Passing through the Seongju tunnel, which connects downtown and Seongju-Myeon, gives us novel feeling as if we step in totally different world.

spots.name: Coal mining museum
spots.desc: Both in and out door coal mining museum has a collection of 1,700 artifacts such as mining tools and mineral samples. Inside the museum six different halls present their unique collections. The Guiding Hall provides general information and has gift shop. The Research Hall shows developing of coal, the Discovery Hall presents samples of coal and other mineral and history of mining industry and the…
spots.price: \2000(Adult), \1500(Teenager), \1000(Child), Free(Under 6 years old, over 66 years old)

spots.name: Boryeong Lake
spots.desc: The surrounding scenery is beautiful, so you can enjoy a drive along Iseol-do, which surrounds Boryeong Lake, and there is Jungam Rock in Amisan Mountain around Boryeong Dam, and Yongam Yeongdang in Yanggaksan Mountain.

spots.name: Navy Headquarters of Chungcheong-do Province, Boryeong
spots.desc: Navy Headquarters of Chungcheong-do Province, Boryeong is a stone castle built high with stones to prevent external invasion into the West Sea. In the 4th year of King Jungjong's reign, Lee Jang-saeng, a Navy thief in the 4th year of King Jungjong's reign, built a 1,650-meter-long castle surrounding the outskirts of Suyeong, Chungcheong Province, and placed a chiseong or a gokseong on a high…

spots.name: Seongjusa Temple Site, Boryeong
spots.desc: The temple site includes the Jungmuncheo, Seokdeung, 5-story stone pagoda, Geumdang building, followed by the east and west three-story stone pagoda, the center three-story stone pagoda, and the west three-story stone pagoda, and the auditorium is located behind it. The Daenanghye Burnt Pagoda, one of Choi Chi-won's stillborn monuments, is also located in the northwest of the temple. Many relics…

spots.name: Boryeong Energy World
spots.desc: Boryeong Energy World is a public relations exhibition hall of Boryeong Thermal Power Headquarters, the largest thermal power generation complex in Korea, and is a comprehensive electric energy experience hall where you can learn how to use the electricity we use every day.

spots.name: Gaehwa Art Park
spots.desc: The Gaehwa Art Park is built on a scale of 50,000 pyeong, including auxiliary facilities located nearby. The Gaehwa Art Park, a large-scale art complex, is home to Herbland, Music Hall, Yukpilsi Park, Birim Park, and Mosan Art Museum in the art park.

spots.name: Boryeong Mugunghwa Arboretum
spots.desc: It was created as a story-themed arboretum by collecting, proliferation, preservation, management, and exhibition of tree genetic resources centered on Mugunghwa, and securing research infrastructure for its resource conversion.
spots.hours: the summer season 09:00-18:00, the winter season 09:00-17:00

spots.name: Boryeong Mud Festival at Daecheon Beach
spots.desc: This festival has been held at Daecheon beach every July since 1997. It's held on a unique shell-covered sand beach only found in the Far East. You may swim and massage with a mudpack at the same time. Furthermore, there are mud massage programs (self massage at the beach, ultra modern mud massage) and a mud experiential land program where mud powder made out of processed and filtered mud is…

spots.name: Sea fishing
spots.desc: There are five outports, Daecheon Port, Ocheon, Muchangpo, Jukdo and Songdo, for sea fishing in Boryeongcity that is famous for boat fishing in West Coast. In Daecheon Port, about 40 boats are ready for boat fishing.

spots.name: Mud from Boryeong
spots.desc: Mudpack that is claimed to be good for skin health and beauty.

spots.name: Nampo Inkstone
spots.desc: Inkstone that is one of the four precious things for study of scholars was once as essential as computers are nowadays. Inkstones made in Nampo out of natural stone from the Sungju mountain were considered the most precious. As modern society influences in our life, inkstone is not used much and 60% to 70% of inkstones that are produced in Korea is made in Boryeong. So Boryeong is the main area…

spots.name: Ungcheon Stone
spots.desc: Osuk produced in Ungcheon is glossy and black like a feather of crow and the quality is excellent. So it is used as the material for various epitaph, tomestones, etc. As you trim the stone more and more, the black color becomes distinguished, and as you carve, the white color comes forth. Especially Osuk from Sungju mountain area is famous as the best quality in Korea and is the indigenous…

spots.name: Marine products
spots.desc: Launce that is caught in the sea of Boryeong is regarded as having superior quality. Especially pickled launch that is caught in May and June, salted at the ratio of 8 to 2 and ripened has a unique taste. Due to the large tide in the area it takes longer time for oysters to grow and that allegedly gives them a better taste.

spots.name: Agricultural Products
spots.desc: Western mushrooms in Boryeong and other mushrooms that are grow above an underground closed mine taste excellent, but on the other hand they are not durable. Grapes that grow along No. 21 national road from Nampo to Ungcheon has superior sweet taste and best nutrition. Especially, Sahyung grape from the Nampo area is famous for its very sweet taste. Masan area produces various edible greens such…

spots.name: Sujeong Restaurant
spots.desc: Only in-store meals are available. It sells Korean dishes such as bibimbap and bibim-guksu.

spots.name: Cafe Blue Lake
spots.desc: The outdoor photo zone view is pretty, the interior of the cafe is small, and there is no space or peculiarity to take pictures.

spots.name: Gakwon Buddhist Temple
spots.desc: It's quite a big temple in Cheonan. The Buddhist temple has a very large sitting Buddha. A nice place to go hiking.

spots.name: ARARIO Small City
spots.desc: In 2007, ARARIO Small City was selected as the most beautiful square in Korea, for which it was awarded the Prime Minister Award. There are 28 contemporary installation artworks.

spots.name: ARARIO Gallery
spots.desc: For years ARARIO Gallery collected significant artworks which have been internationally acknowledged. It is also where BTS' RM visited.

spots.name: Byeongcheon Sundae Street
spots.desc: There is a famous sundae (Korean sausage) street situated near the Aunae (Byeongcheon) Market, where patriotic martyr Yu Gwan-sun led an independence movement. With the establishment of a ham manufacturing plant near Byeongcheon in the 1960s, people in the area began making sausages using vegetables and pork byproducts such as intestines and clotted blood, and a couple of sundae restaurants began…

spots.name: Cheonan Museum
spots.desc: The Cheonan museum presents artifacts and relics that sheds light on the history of Cheonan from the prehistoric times to the modern times through permanent exhibitions.

spots.name: Postal Museum
spots.desc: It is easy to get to the Postal Museum by bus. It's a good place for young children to see.

spots.name: Ligak Museum of Art
spots.desc: This is a contemporary art museum that honors the memory of sculptor Lee Jong-gak. There are many sculptures in the park.

spots.name: Memorial hall of Patriotic martyr Yu Gwan-sun
spots.desc: Yu Gwan-sun was a great Korean independence activist. Visitors are able to see the life story of Yu, Gwan-sun, from her birth to her entry into martyrdom, through exhibits, videos, and various different experiences.

spots.name: Cheonan Heungtaryeong Center
spots.desc: the theme of dance and liquor. You can experience traditional liquor and traditional dance.

spots.name: Jung-ang market
spots.desc: There are many delicious foods in the market. Hotteok store is especially famous. There is a store that closes after 18:00, but the food truck opens and you can eat something different from daytime.

spots.name: Cheonan Hong Dae-yong Science Museum
spots.desc: The Hong Dae-yong Science Museum was opened adjacent to the site of Mr. Hong Dae-yong’s birthplace to honor his great achievements. Dameon Hong Dae-yong was a leading thinker and practical scholar of the Joseon period who was the first to advocate the theories of the theory of terrestrial motion and the spherical earth. This is a place where visitors can experience the great scientific ideas of…
spots.hours: Exhibition Hall and Planetarium: 10:00-18:00, Observatory (by reservation only): 15:00-22:00

The current law building was newly built in 1970. It is 4 spaces on the front and 2 spaces on the side, and the roof is eight-roof roof. spots.desc: Two stone lion statues on both sides of the stairs leading to Gwangdeoksa Daeungjeon. Sculpture was made with a stone without placing the pedestal separately. The face looking up to the sky is almost horizontal and looks like a human face. The hair is clouded, and the mouth is slightly open with its teeth represented. Only the head is sculpted, the body is omitted.

spots.desc: It is a temple built by Doseon in the fourth year of Goryeo Dynasty (921), it is said to have built a Buddha statue and a 5-story pagoda, but it is not accurate. The statue of 164㎝ high is carved on the rock wall in the natural cave behind the temple. I lost my hair and made it new, but it feels a bit bigger than my body. The deeply engraved garment wrapped around the left shoulder, with the…

spots.desc: It is a place where the Memorial of Park Moon-soo (1691 ~ 1756), who left many anecdotes as a clue, is held. Park Moon-soo, who had been in Gyeongjong 3 years (1723) at the late Joseon Dynasty, went up to the bottle control hall and was dismissed when Noron came to power in 1724. In 1727, when Soron took office, he was re-used and went through the Yeongnam-am Hangeul History and Chungcheongdo-am…

spots.desc: Min Seung-se, who was the grandfather of Kyujanggak, was built directly down here. This house has an anchae, an anchae, and an annex, which has a slightly higher anchae and an annex than an annex. The main house is a wooden tile house, and the roof is an octopus roof. Min Ik-hyun, the owner of this house, whose buildings are old and have lived for six generations, is the fifth generation of Min…

spots.name: gwangdeogsa daeungjeon
spots.desc: Gwangdeoksa Temple was built by Queen Seondeok, 12 years old (643), and Jinsan was rebuilt during King Heungdeok. It was said to have been one of the biggest temples in Gyeonggi-do and Chungcheong-do provinces. The main court, Daeungjeon, was completely dismantled and restored in 1983 and was built larger than the first. The large headstone found at the time of demolition was the style of…

spots.name: Cheonan Hyanggyo (Confucian School)
spots.desc: A hyanggyo (local Confucian school) founded in the early Joseon period. Educational facility. Municipal (city)/provincial monument. Designated as a Chungcheongnam-do monument in 1997, during the Joseon Dynasty it received land, books, and slaves from the state so that one instructor could teach 30 students, but after the Gabo Reform and the implementation of the new educational system, its…

spots.name: Gakwonsa Temple
spots.desc: The temple has a large bronze seated Buddha, Daeungbojeon Hall, Chilseonggak Shrine, and a pond.

spots.name: cheon-ansanglog-akuapia
spots.desc: There is an indoor pool and an outdoor pool. The indoor pool has a variety of water facilities such as flowride, master blaster, wave pool and spa. The outdoor pool is much quieter and more comfortable than the indoor pool. Surrounding green environment is also good.

spots.name: Teddin Water Park
spots.desc: Teddin Water Park is a water park in summer and a spa in winter. There is an indoor pool and an outdoor pool, and there's plenty to eat inside so you can have fun with your family. There are facilities for family members such as therapy centers, healing shelters, kids zones and cafeterias.

spots.name: Dad's Love Farm Egg Experience
spots.desc: You can have a special experience by harvesting eggs yourself, bonding with the chicks, and feeding the chickens. You can also try various DIY activities, such as making egg sandwiches, egg bread, and egg soap.

spots.name: Heungtaryeong festival
spots.desc: It is held every September for four days. It is the biggest dance festival in Korea.

spots.name: Gwangdeok Walnut Festival
spots.desc: What comes to mind when it comes to Cheonan is a nutcracker. This is because good quality walnut is produced, and because of this history, walnut festivals are held.

spots.name: Cheonan Buk-myeon Wirye Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: The Wirye Cherry Blossom Festival is held for 2 days every April in Buk-myeon. The Buk-myeon Beokkotgil (cherry blossom street) stretching 15 km from Yeonchun-ri to Unyong-ri becomes surrounded by cherry blossoms.

spots.name: Ipjang Geobong Grape Festival
spots.desc: free tasting booths offering grapes and food made with grapes. This festival is held on a yearly basis in September.

spots.name: Ryu Gwansun Gymnasium
spots.desc: It is the home stadium of Hyundai Capital Skywalkers, a professional volleyball team.

spots.name: Cheonan Samgeori Park
spots.desc: As a family-oriented theme park, it is designed for outings and walks, featuring walking trails, a writing forest, a multipurpose plaza, a lawn, Onnuri Health Center, a musical fountain, a media wall, a water play area, and a mirror pond.

spots.name: E-Mart
spots.desc: It is located in the basement of Shinsegae Department Store.
spots.hours: Daily 10:00 - 22:00 closed on every Sun of 3rd week of the month

spots.name: Morumi Shop
spots.desc: Morumi Shop is a small accessory store where you can find cute and unique items all in one place.

spots.name: Soso Store
spots.desc: Soso Shop is a kidult and lifestyle curated shop that goes beyond simply selling accessories, offering trendy vibes and curating unique, rare products.

spots.name: Kyotori café

spots.name: Wondujip Cheonan Branch
spots.desc: This is a cafe that sells drip coffee bags and whole coffee beans. They offer a variety of beverages.

spots.name: Samseon Mountain Arboretum
spots.desc: It is a beautiful arboretum, an ecological learning center where you can enjoy nature and preserve and display various plant species. It is a good place to enjoy a walk while healing in nature, and it is a popular attraction for family visitors and nature lovers

spots.name: Waemok Village Beach
spots.desc: Waemok Village Beach is in the northernmost part of the Taean Peninsula in Dangjin-si, and has a unique topography that extends long and thin while dividing the West Sea. As the coast of the extended part faces the east, it is the only place in Korea where you can see sunrise, sunset, and moonrise. And thanks to the sandy beach and the seashore rock, you can enjoy beaching and seashore rock…

spots.name: Nanjido Beach
spots.desc: The white sand beach is 2.5 km long, 500 m wide, and the water temperature is 20 to 23 degrees, and it is located off the coast of Daeho Embankment in the north of the Taean Peninsula.

spots.name: Dangjin Sollmae Village Gim Daegeon Priest Remains
spots.desc: The remains of Father Kim Dae-geon in Solmoi Village, Dangjin, are the birthplace of Father Kim Dae-geon, the first Korean Catholic priest. Pilgrims continue to visit this place, and after Pope Francis visited on August 15, 2014, it became a popular shrine not only for domestic but also for overseas pilgrims.

spots.name: Site of Bishop St. Marie Nicolas Antoine Daveluy in Dangjin Sin-ri
spots.desc: It is a village where the largest number of Catholics lived in the late Joseon Dynasty, and is designated as a Catholic holy site.

spots.name: Pilgyeongsa
spots.desc: The house was designed and built by Sim Hoon, a Japanese colonial era poet and novelist, in 1934, and was designated as a monument in Chungcheongnam-do in 1997.

spots.name: Myeoncheoneupseong Walled Town
spots.desc: Myeoncheoneupseong Walled Town is a flatland walled town built in 1439 and the 21st year of King Sejong to protect the government and administrative districts from Japanese invasion, and is the main stage of many historical events.

spots.name: Dangsan Reservoir Eco Park
spots.desc: Dangsan Reservoir Eco Park offers a nature-friendly environment and is equipped with various facilities such as trails and exercise equipment.

spots.name: Seokmunsan Mountain
spots.desc: Seokmunsan Mountain is a low mountain about 100m above sea level, providing a beautiful view of the West Sea and Seokmun Seawall. Popular for gentle hiking trails, surrounding fishing and driving courses, it is a natural resort suitable for family visitors.

spots.name: Eunbongsan Mountain
spots.desc: At about 210 m above sea level, it is a mountain where you can see the West Sea and the surrounding natural scenery at a glance. The trail is a relatively gentle and accessible resting place loved by local residents and tourists. In particular, the scenery of Seokmunho Lake and the West Sea from the top is impressive.

spots.name: Korean Buddhist Jogye Order Yeongtapsa Temple
spots.desc: The temple was built by Doseon Guksa, a Buddhist monk from Unified Silla during the Northern and Southern dynasties, in Sangwangsan Mountain.

spots.name: Daehosa
spots.desc: Daehosa also serves as the general office of the parish of Taegojong in Chungnam. Buddhist monks and believers are engaged in activities to spread the Buddha of mercy, such as donating rice for underprivileged neighbors to each village in Daehoji-myeon.

spots.name: Marine Theme Experience Center
spots.desc: It is a facility that provides marine-related exhibitions and experiences. It is a space that provides various educational and fun experiences by utilizing Dangjin's marine resources and helps understand the marine environment and ecosystem

spots.name: Dangjin Traditional Market
spots.desc: It is a medium-sized market in the form of a commercial housing building opened in 1974.

spots.name: Observatory Fish Market
spots.desc: It is the Sapgyoho Observatory Fish Market, a landmark of the Sapgyoho Tourist Site.

spots.name: cheong-chun jogae pocha
spots.desc: It is one of the most famous franchise shellfish restaurant.

spots.name: Gyeryongsan National Park
spots.desc: One of South Korea's most celebrated national parks. Famous for its dramatic mountain ridges, lush forest valleys, and vibrant autumn foliage. While the main peak (Cheonwangbong) is inside a restricted military zone, nearby peaks like Gwaneumbong and Sambong offer rewarding views.

spots.name: Sagye Gotaek (Eumnongjae)
spots.desc: The historical residence of Sagye Kim Jang-saeng (1548–1631), a prominent Neo-Confucian scholar of the Joseon Dynasty. This beautifully restored traditional hanok house features quiet courtyards, traditional gardens, and seasonal cultural heritage workshops.

spots.name: Mt. Hyangjeoksan & Healing Forest
spots.desc: At 574 meters, Hyangjeoksan is the highest accessible peak in Gyeryong City. It features well-paved walking trails, wooden deck paths, a scenic observation deck overlooking Gyeryongdae, and a dedicated forest healing complex.

spots.name: Sindoan Historic Foundation Stones
spots.desc: Historical stone foundations left behind when King Taejo of Joseon halted the construction of his new capital city here in 1394. A fascinating stop for Korean history enthusiasts.

spots.name: Gyeryong Military Culture Festival
spots.desc: A major annual military festival co-hosted with the ROK Armed Forces. Features grand honor guard parades, international military band concerts, tank and armored vehicle exhibitions, street food stalls, and interactive military simulation experiences.

spots.name: Hiking the Mt. Hyangjeoksan Ridge
spots.desc: Enjoy a half-day hike along the ridge connecting Eomsa-ri to the Hyangjeoksan peak. Offers panoramic views of both Gyeryong city center and the surrounding national park.

spots.name: Eomsa Traditional Market
spots.desc: The main traditional market in Gyeryong. A great spot to browse fresh seasonal fruits, traditional Korean snacks (like gangjeong and tteok), fresh mountain vegetables, and daily goods.

spots.name: Homeplus Gyeryong Branch
spots.desc: Large multi-story supermarket offering groceries, clothing, electronics, and a food court near the city hall area.

spots.name: Cheongseokgol
spots.desc: A long-standing local favorite specializing in hearty Korean grilled pork (samgyeopsal), marinated pork ribs (galbi), and rich soybean paste stews served with abundant side dishes.

spots.name: Gyeryong Kalguksu
spots.desc: Popular eatery near Gyeryong Station famous for handmade knife-cut noodle soup (kalguksu) served in a savory clam broth, accompanied by spicy freshly made kimchi.

spots.name: Sindoan Tofu Restaurant
spots.desc: Known for healthy traditional Korean dishes made with locally produced soybeans, including freshly made soft tofu stew (sundubu-jjigae) and bean curd hotpots.

spots.name: Cafe Rest in Hyangjeoksan
spots.desc: A scenic nature cafe situated near the hiking trail. Features spacious outdoor garden seating, specialty drip coffee, and traditional Korean herbal teas.

spots.name: Twosome Place Gyeryong Geumam Branch
spots.desc: Modern coffee shop offering espresso drinks, desserts, and free Wi-Fi in the civic center district.

spots.name: Citizens' Family Park
spots.desc: The landscape features such as Byeokcheon Falls, Mirror Pond, and the Promenade are complemented by the small Silgaecheon Stream, which connects the upper and lower parts of the park. At night, LED lighting creates an illuminated atmosphere.

spots.name: Strawberryhyang Rural Theme Park
spots.desc: This theme park is focused on strawberries, a local specialty of Nonsan. It offers a variety of experience programs utilizing facilities such as a strawberry learning center, agricultural experience center, and cultivation greenhouses.

spots.name: Yeowull Farm
spots.desc: The farm is decorated with various plants and offers spaces with individual rooms where visitors can sit and relax.

spots.name: Hwangsan Guenrin Park
spots.desc: This park features a walking promenade, a large lawn, a children's playground, and various sports facilities for recreational use.

spots.name: Byeongam Amusement Park
spots.desc: There are other attractions near Byeongam Amusement Park, such as Topjeong Lake, so visitors can tour the surrounding attractions together after spending time there. It is also close to other attractions in Nonsan City.

spots.name: Yangchon-ri Sports Park
spots.desc: There are various sports facilities such as a soccer field, basketball court, and badminton court.

spots.name: Noseongsan Aehyang Park
spots.desc: There are recreational facilities such as a multi-purpose lawn yard and an outdoor stage, as well as an exercise yard, Pungryu Madang, Seonbi statue, suspension bridge, and deck circulation trails.

spots.name: Robot Museum
spots.desc: This space displays themed figures and classic toys, evoking a sense of nostalgia. (CLOSED DOWN?)

spots.name: Ganggyoeng History Museum
spots.desc: This cultural and historical exhibition space was established to promote and preserve the region's history and cultural heritage.

spots.name: Kangkyungsan Salt Literature Museum
spots.desc: This space introduces the literary and cultural heritage related to Korea's salt industry, showcasing the importance of salt production and its impact on literature.

spots.name: Ganggyeong Salted Seafood Exhibition Museum
spots.desc: It introduces the history and culture of salted fish, a local specialty. The exhibition hall displays the various types and manufacturing processes of salted fish traditionally produced in the Ganggyeong area, providing information on the historical background of salted fish and its importance to the local economy.

spots.name: Youngjusa
spots.desc: Traditional Buddhist structures such as Daeungjeon Hall, the Three-story Stone Pagoda, and Beomjonggak Pavilion are found within the grounds of Yeongju Temple.

spots.name: Bonghwangsa
spots.desc: It is said to have been built during the Baekje period. The name of the temple is said to have originated from the story that phoenixes came down from the sky and settled down, according to a legend.

spots.name: Yubongyeongdang
spots.desc: Yubongyeongdang (Seowon is a private educational institution and place to study Confucian thought and studies) built in honor of Lee Jeong-ik, a scholar of the late Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Banya Mountain
spots.desc: Located southeast of Nonsan city, this area is primarily urban, with paddy farming in the alluvial plains and fruit farming in the hilly regions.

spots.name: Daemyeong Mountain
spots.desc: It is a low mountain about 200 m above sea level. As it is close to Gwanchoksa in Nonsan, visitors can continue your cultural heritage tour after visiting Daemyeongsan Mountain.

spots.name: Taebong Mountain
spots.desc: It belongs to a relatively low mountain at an altitude of about 200 meters, and is used by the surrounding residents as a place for walking and light hiking. It is located close to downtown Nonsan.

spots.name: Cheonho Mountain
spots.desc: Gaetae Temple is located on the western foot of this mountain.

spots.name: Onbit Natural Recreation Forest

spots.name: Yangchon Natural Recreation Forest

spots.name: Surak Valley

spots.name: Surak Reservoir

spots.name: Yeonsancheon

spots.name: KT&G Sangsang Madang Nonsan

spots.name: Kim Jong-beom Photographic Culture Center

spots.name: Kim Hong-shin Literature Center

spots.name: Little Prince Literature Museum
spots.desc: It is a literary museum that stores the first English and French editions of the book 'The Little Prince' published in 1943, and the first translated book in Korea.

spots.name: Miseok Hangeul Literature Museum
spots.desc: The museum covers the creation and development of Hangeul, and the historical flow of literary works written in Hangeul, and aims to promote Hangeul's value. It also features lectures, educational programs, and hands-on activities on Hangeul literature.

spots.name: Waya-ri Mural Village

spots.name: Sunshine Land
