spots.name: Ulsan Rock
spots.desc: Ulsan is a set of six steep, rocky peaks rising 873m above sea level, some 4km in total girth, and very difficult to climb. Their imposing stature has made Ulsan the symbol of Seoraksan and Gangwon-do. Ulsan is sometimes compared with the similar Ayers Rock in Australia.

spots.name: Lotte World Ice Rink
spots.desc: The ice rink is located on the first floor of Lotte World. Even if you don't use Lotte World rides, you can use it separately. It's a great way to feel the atmosphere of Lotte World in a short time and at a reasonable price. There are many good restaurants around here, so you can enjoy delicious food after enjoying the ice rink. Resurfacing times: daily 12:50-13:10, 14:00-14:30, 16:00-16:30…

spots.name: Korea Bamboo Museum
spots.desc: It is a Korean bamboo museum with a space where you can perform comprehensive functions such as preserving, exhibiting, selling, and experiencing bamboo products. It was opened and operated in Damju-ri, Damyang-eup in 1981, and was expanded and relocated to Cheonbyeon-ri, Damyang-eup on March 12, 1998. In addition to exhibiting bamboo products, technical information on the production of bamboo…

spots.name: Jeollado Hanjeongsik
spots.desc: Haenam Hanjeongsik is an elaborate table setting prepared with generous use of quality ingredients when serving precious guests. Delicious rice cooked with Haenam rice is served with more than 20 side dishes, including grilled fish, japchae, pancakes, vegetables, soy sauce crab, bossam, and bean curd. The shape and color of the food are beautiful and neat.

spots.name: The Iron Triangle Zone / Cheorwon Peace Observatory
spots.desc: Located inside the DMZ Civilian Control Zone, this observatory offers panoramic views of the Pyeonggang highlands, a North Korean propaganda village, and Kim Il Sung's former vacation home through high-powered binoculars. Entry is only permitted via the official DMZ Peace Tour departing from Goseokjeong.

spots.name: Cheorwon Peace Observatory
spots.desc: Located at the northernmost point of the central front, this observatory offers a panoramic view of the DMZ and North Korean territory. Visitors can use a monorail to reach the summit and observe the Pyeonggang Plateau and North Korean propaganda villages through high-powered binoculars. Entry is only permitted via the official DMZ Peace Tour.

spots.name: The Second Underground Tunnel
spots.desc: Discovered on March 19, 1975, the Second Underground Tunnel is wide enough to pass 30,000 soldiers an hour and even large armored vehicles. The tunnel has been developed into a tourist site so that visitors can tour the tunnel.

spots.name: Goseokjeong
spots.desc: A scenic 15 m granite rock rising from the middle of the Hantan River, featuring a pavilion first built during the Silla dynasty. The site is part of the Hantan River UNESCO Global Geopark and is famously linked to the legend of the outlaw Im Kkeok-jeong.

spots.name: Saemtong Migratory Bird Sanctuary
spots.desc: A 5,000-square-meter natural spring pond that remains unfrozen throughout the winter. Located within the DMZ buffer zone, it serves as a critical winter sanctuary for endangered red-crowned and white-naped cranes.

spots.name: Sambuyeon Falls
spots.desc: A stunning 20-meter waterfall on Myeongseongsan Mountain that cascades through three distinct rocky basins. It was famously captured in paintings by the renowned Joseon artist Jeong Seon. The falls maintain a powerful flow even during dry seasons.

spots.name: Hantangang Columnar Jointing Path (Zando)
spots.desc: A 3.6 km cliffside boardwalk built along the dramatic basalt gorge of the Hantan River. It features skywalks and suspension bridges with stunning geological views. Shuttle buses run between Sundam and Deureuni gates on weekends.

spots.name: Cheorwon Hantangang River Rafting
spots.desc: Hantangang River, the Grand Canyon of Korea, takes pride in the mysterious cliffs and huge valleys and one-after-the-other scenic stretches that appear to be blessed by the heavens. The rafting course is 15 km long, divided according to the level of difficulty from beginner to advance.

spots.name: Hantan River Spa Hotel
spots.desc: Cheorwon Hot Spring is located at Goseokjeong Pavilion. The hot spring is a germanium-content volcanic spa with natural waters springing from 850 m deep. Known to be exceptionally effective for skin care for women, Cheorwon Hot Spring has sauna facilities and swimming pools. Visitors can enjoy the first-class pure natural waters while gazing at the beautiful vista of Hantangang River.

spots.name: Hantan River Ice Trekking Festival
spots.desc: A unique winter event where you can walk directly on the frozen river. The course stretches from Taebongdaegyo Bridge to Sundam Valley, offering close-up views of frozen waterfalls and columnar joints. Various snow-related activities and pop-up playgrounds are also available.

spots.name: Goseokjeong Flower Field
spots.desc: A former military firing range transformed into a sprawling garden. Depending on the season, you can find fields of poppies, rapeseed, zinnia, and pink muhly. The "Can Train" tour around the fields is a popular family activity.

spots.name: Soyisan Monorail
spots.desc: Take a monorail to the summit of Soyisan Mountain (362m) for an expansive view of the Cheorwon Plain and the DMZ. The peak features a former US military radar base and bunkers, reflecting the region's military history.

spots.name: DMZ Peace Train Music Festival
spots.desc: A unique music festival promoting peace through song and dance. Performances take place at symbolic locations like Goseokjeong and near the Labor Party Office, featuring both domestic and international indie musicians.

spots.name: Dongsong Traditional Market
spots.desc: The largest permanent market in the region and host to a five-day market on dates ending in 5 and 0. It is the best place to find fresh local produce such as paprika, tomatoes, and corn directly from farmers.

spots.name: Cheorwon Local Food Market (Today's Farmer)
spots.desc: A specialized shop featuring certified agricultural products and processed foods produced by local farmers. You can find unique items like Odae rice noodles, local rice bread, and high-quality packaged grains.

spots.name: Nonghyup Hanaro Mart (Dongsong Branch)
spots.desc: A reliable supermarket for purchasing certified Cheorwon Odae Rice in various sizes. It is also a good spot to stock up on basic supplies before heading to campsites or pensions.

spots.name: Samgyori Dongchimi Makguksu
spots.desc: Specializes in buckwheat noodles served with chilled radish kimchi broth (dongchimi) and savory potato pancakes, a popular local meal after trekking along the Hantan River.

spots.name: Cheorwon Makguksu
spots.desc: A local legend with over 60 years of history. This restaurant, housed in a cozy traditional Hanok, serves handmade buckwheat noodles pressed to order. Their cold noodles (Mul-makguksu) and spicy mixed noodles (Bibim-makguksu) are both highly recommended.

spots.name: Solhyanggi
spots.desc: Specializes in handmade dumpling hotpot (Mandu-jeongol). The dumplings are generously filled with kimchi, meat, and tofu, served in a rich beef bone broth. It is an ideal meal for warming up during Cheorwon's cold winters.

spots.name: Naedae-ri Makguksu
spots.desc: A hidden gem favored by locals and gourmets. Known for its rougher, more rustic buckwheat noodle texture and flavorful noodle water (myeon-su). The wait times can be long, but the authentic taste is worth the patience.

spots.name: Eunhasu Cafe
spots.desc: Located right next to the Hantangang Milky Way Bridge, this cafe features large glass windows that provide panoramic views of the basalt canyon. Their signature "Kissing" bread made with local Odae rice is a must-try.

spots.name: Cafe None
spots.desc: A trendy cafe offering a tranquil "paddy field view" that changes beautifully with the seasons. It specializes in unique desserts utilizing Cheorwon rice, providing a modern take on local flavors.

spots.name: Cafe Goseokjeong
spots.desc: Conveniently located within the Goseokjeong National Tourist Area. It serves as an excellent resting spot before or after taking the DMZ Peace Tour or exploring the riverside trails.

spots.name: Hwajinpo Beach
spots.desc: Surrounded by pine forests, Hwajinpo Beach with its white sand was a foreigner-exclusive summerhouse during the time of Japanese imperialism. The surrounding scenery is so beautiful that it was the summerhouse of Kim Il Sung and Rhee Seung Man after liberation from Japan.This area also became famous for filming the popular drama Autumn in my heart and now many fans come to Hwanjinpo to collect a…

spots.name: Summerhouse of Kim Il Sung
spots.desc: The house is embedded in a cliff where you can have a bird's eye view of the beautiful Hwajinpo beach. There is an exhibition of Kim Il Sung's personal belongings including furniture. On the stairs up to the summerhouse, photos are displayed of Kim Jeong-il during his early days.

spots.name: Unification Observatory
spots.desc: As the observatory closest to North Korea and the Northernmost point of the ROK, more than one million people visit this area on an annual basis. Visitors can see the Geumgangsan (Diamond Mountains) and the Haegeumgang in North Korea, with the naked eye, and unlike many other observatories, photographs are allowed everywhere. In the observatory North Korean food products are for sale, and the…

spots.name: Maritime Museum
spots.desc: This museum exhibits 40,000 articles of 1,500 types of shellfish, corals and fossils some very rare.

spots.name: Sutasa Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple at the foot of Mt. Gongjak, traditionally said to have been founded in 708 during the Silla period. Its main hall, Daejeokgwangjeon, is a designated Treasure of South Korea. The temple is beside Gongjaksan Eco-Forest and Suta Valley, so visitors can combine the temple with a walk.

spots.name: Mt. Palbong
spots.desc: Eight rocky peaks rise above a bend in the Hongcheon River. The ridge routes take about 2–3½ hours and include steep sections with ropes and ladders. Wear hiking shoes and gloves. The trail may close because of rain, snow or strong wind; check its opening status before travelling.
spots.hours: Hiking trail 07:00–18:00 during its opening season; last entry 15:00 or 15:30 depending on the month

spots.name: Hongcheon Ginkgo Forest
spots.desc: A private forest of about 2,000 ginkgo trees planted in neat rows. The owner began planting them in 1985, hoping the clean mountain air would help his sick wife. It has opened to the public every October since 2010, when the leaves turn bright yellow. It is closed for the rest of the year.

spots.name: Heumang-ri Three-story Stone Pagoda
spots.desc: A 2.45-m granite pagoda from the Goryeo period, designated Treasure No. 79. It stands in the garden of the Hongcheon-eup office. A Goryeo-era flagpole support (Treasure No. 80) is also in Heumang-ri.

spots.name: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha of Mulgeol-ri
spots.desc: A seated stone Buddha from the late Unified Silla period (Treasure No. 542). Its octagonal lotus pedestal is carved with musicians and offering figures. It is kept in a protective hall.

spots.name: Vivaldi Park
spots.desc: A large resort run by Sono Hotels & Resorts, opened in 1995. It has a ski resort (Ski World) in winter, the Ocean World water park, golf courses, and indoor games such as bowling and go-karts.

spots.name: Hongcheon River Rafting
spots.desc: Guided rafting trips on a 5.5–6 km stretch of the Hongcheon River, from the Hongcheon River resort area past Mt. Palbong to Bamboel resort area. A trip takes 1½ to 2 hours. The river here is calm, not whitewater, which makes it good for families and beginners. Guides let you flip the boat and jump in for a swim along the way. Life jackets, helmets and water shoes are provided, and there are…

spots.name: Alpaca World
spots.desc: A hillside animal park where visitors can see alpacas and other animals. Allow time for the sloping paths and check the official site for activity times. Public transport access is limited.
spots.hours: 10:00–18:00; last admission 16:30; closed on Seollal and Chuseok
spots.price: ₩18,000 for visitors aged 36 months and over; younger children free with proof of age. Alpaca walks cost extra.

spots.name: Garisan Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: A forest recreation area below Mt. Garisan, with walking trails, valleys and cabins for overnight stays. Check the official reservation site for current cabin availability, rates and temporary closures.

spots.name: Forest Amusementpark
spots.desc: Hongcheon Forest Adventure Park is a public children's facility located in Gaeun-ri, Yeongguimi-myeon, Hongcheon-gun, Gangwon-do. The park features outdoor play equipment such as net adventure zones and slides set within a natural pine forest environment.

spots.name: Hongcheon Hanwoo Sarangmal Restaurant
spots.desc: A popular farm-to-table cooperative direct market and barbecue restaurant offering high-quality Hongcheon Korean beef at great value. Visitors can pick pre-packaged cuts from the 1st-floor market to grill upstairs, or purchase gift and ice-packed sets to go.

spots.name: Gaboja Tosong Sundaegukbap Ppyeodawi Haejangguk
spots.desc: Gaboja Tosong Sundaegukbap Ppyeodawi Haejangguk is a local Korean restaurant located in Hongcheon-eup, Hongcheon-gun, Gangwon-do. The menu features traditional Korean soup dishes, specifically specializing in blood sausage soup (sundaegukbap) and pork bone hangover soup.It serves as a casual dining spot providing standard local meals in the area.

spots.name: Son-kalguksu Restaurant
spots.desc: Son-kalguksu is a traditional local restaurant located near the central market in Hongcheon-gun, Gangwon-do. The menu features handmade noodles and dumplings prepared in a traditional style. It operates as a casual, community-oriented dining spot primarily frequented by local residents.

spots.name: Jo Kyung-Chul Observatory
spots.desc: Jo Kyung-Chul Observatory features advanced telescopes that allow visitors to explore the night sky.It also hosts science programs and events to inspire interest in astronomy.

spots.name: Hwacheon Museum
spots.desc: Hwacheon Museum showcases the region’s history, culture, and traditions through various artifacts and exhibitions. It offers visitors interactive programs and seasonal events to experience local heritage.

spots.name: Lake Paroho
spots.desc: Lake Paroho is an artificial lake created by Hwacheon Dam in 1944. It is famous for fishing and its historical significance.

spots.name: Sancheoneo Coffee Museum
spots.desc: Features exhibits connected to the Sancheoneo Ice Festival and offers visitors a chance to taste freshly brewed coffee. A quiet and cozy spot to relax while learning about local culture.

spots.name: Sabanggori
spots.desc: It is a traditional rural intersection located in Sangseo-myeon, a quiet street with village trails and small shops.

spots.name: Georye-ri Sarang Tree
spots.desc: It is a 400-year-old protected tree located in the Arles Theme Arboretum created along the Han River, and is also called the 'alone tree'.

spots.name: Lotus Flower Garden
spots.desc: You can walk a 1-km walk while looking at the lotus flowers. They can be seen in full bloom in July and August

spots.name: Into the Forest Bridge
spots.desc: It is a place where you can walk on Salanggyo Bridge, a bridge, and the Bukhangang River flows below.

spots.name: Baegamsan Cable Car
spots.desc: Offers a scenic cable ride with wide views of Hwacheon’s lakes and surrounding mountains. Visitors appreciate the calm atmosphere and low fare, especially during autumn when the forest turns into brilliant shades of red and gold.

spots.name: Native Freshwater Fish Ecology Experience Center
spots.desc: An educational aquarium and experience center showcasing various freshwater fish species native to Korea.

spots.name: Sancheoneo Valley
spots.desc: You can experience catching Sancheoneo with your bare hands.

spots.name: Hwacheon Wood Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: It provides an experience place to make unique wooden products that only I can have by utilizing excellent wood produced in forests that account for 86% of Hwacheon-gun.

spots.name: Jjokbae Water Festival
spots.desc: Takes place in Hwacheon and ends at Bungeoseom island. Jjokbae is a kind of raft used in Korea and during this festival creative rafts with unique shapes decorate the lake of Bungeo seom island. There is a very famous song about a rabbit living on the moon crossing over the Milky Way by a raft. Many of the contestants have built their rafts themselves. The rules don't set any limits concerning…

spots.name: Tomato Festival
spots.desc: Tomato is Hwacheon's local specialty. Delightful experience programs of the tomato festival are prepared to offer a good time without spending a lot of money. For example, the tomato slide & tomato tail catching events. Spaghetti for 1,000 people is also provided during the festival. You can buy tomatoes at the festival for an inexpensive price if you want to buy fresh tomatoes of Hwacheon. When…

spots.name: Sancheoneo Ice Festival
spots.desc: Hwacheon's signature winter event, held every January along the frozen Hwacheoncheon stream. The event attracts over a million visitors every year. Programs are organized into four major categories, themed around ice and snow. The program relates to the fresh water fishes living in mountain lakes and creeks, especially sancheoneo - a fish which can only live in the best and clearest waters.…

spots.name: Tomato Sculpture Park
spots.desc: Hwacheon is the representative producer of tomatoes in Korea, and the tomato festival is held in July every year. This is a park that was created to celebrate the festival

spots.name: Ecological Media Center Water Theme Park
spots.desc: It is a park located next to Hwacheon Ecological Imaging Center, and the water playground is open in summer.

spots.name: Mullebang-a Park
spots.desc: Sancheoneo Festival A park located next to the World Winter City Plaza.

spots.name: Gamseong Theme Literature Park
spots.desc: A park where you can visit novelist Lee Oe-soo's literature museum.

spots.name: International Peace Art Park
spots.desc: It is right next to the Dam of Peace. A park was created by reconstructing it as a peace art using waste weapons, a symbol of war.

spots.name: Hwacheon Market
spots.desc: Located inside the intercity bus terminal, the market sells local specialties and fresh regional products.

spots.name: M Mart
spots.desc: There are various products. It is located in the main street

spots.name: Hanaro Mart Hwacheon Nonghyup Main Branch
spots.desc: Large supermarkets run by the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation. Have many visitors

spots.name: Yeongwon Supermarket
spots.desc: A mart that sells vegetables, fish, packaged meat, and miscellaneous goods at a discount

spots.name: Gangwon Namulbap Chaewon
spots.desc: It is a popular restaurant among visitors, as Hwacheon is famous for its mountain vegetables (san-namul).

spots.name: Bukhangang Hoetjip
spots.desc: This restaurant’s main menu features sancheoneo. The Sancheoneo Ice Festival is often held in front of the restaurant, and even without fishing, visitors can enjoy fresh trout here.

spots.name: Sanchaegol
spots.desc: It is a popular restaurant among locals, offering a wide variety of dishes and a spacious parking area.

spots.name: Dowon
spots.desc: A local restaurant known for its signature stir-fried udon, praised for rich flavor and generous portions.

spots.name: Byeolmichon
spots.desc: Sundae guk is the main menu, and it is popular with local residents for its good taste and comfortable mood.

spots.name: Hangari Butcher’s Restaurant
spots.desc: A cost-effective meat restaurant . You can eat meat as well as eel

spots.name: Hwacheon Yeolmu Noodles
spots.desc: Loved for its refreshing taste and affordable prices, especially during the summer season.

spots.name: Hwacheon Kodari
spots.desc: Steamed foods are representative and loved by local residents

spots.name: Hi Daily
spots.desc: It is a stylish café where visitors can enjoy fragrant tea and coffee, accompanied by savory bread.

spots.name: Chedo
spots.desc: It is a nice café to visit after seeing the Chilseong Observatory, and it is often frequented by soldiers. The coffee here is known for its good taste.

spots.name: Cafe Garden
spots.desc: Serves coffee and a wide range of brunch dishes in a cozy, quiet setting.

spots.name: Shato Green
spots.desc: Popular local cafe often described as one of the best in downtown Hwacheon.

spots.name: Jan Art Museum Cafe
spots.desc: A hidden cafe and small art gallery tucked away in a quiet valley

spots.name: Cafe Sanchaek
spots.desc: Located near the Chilseong Observatory, the bakery and latte are delicious

spots.name: Ppangker
spots.desc: They sell a variety of bread, including donuts, and there are also various jams

spots.name: Mountain Story
spots.desc: A cafe with a clear view of the mountain view. A quiet, neat atmosphere

spots.name: Fleroo
spots.desc: A neat cafe located behind the county office. There are many reviews that the staff is friendly.

spots.name: J Ahn Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe near Hwacheon County Office that makes homemade desserts

spots.name: Gwangdeokri 329
spots.desc: A cafe with various types of bread such as basil bread, tomato bread, and vegetable bread.

spots.name: Yongdam Cafe
spots.desc: A beautiful cafe on the way up to the cafe. You can enjoy coffee while enjoying the mountain view.

spots.name: Park In-hwan Literary Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the Korean modernist poet Park In-hwan (1926-1956), who was born in Inje and made a name for himself early in his age. However, at the age of 29, he passed away after four days of heavy drinking. Exhibitions include his personal items, letters, and literary works, as well as a recreation of Myeongdong in the 1940s where he ran a small bookshop and mingled with the poets of…

spots.name: Inje Mountain Village Folk Museum
spots.desc: Another museum beside Park In-hwan Literary Museum. Exhibitions mainly focus on the lifestyle of the villages in the mountains as well as agricultural history. There are farming tools, taxidermy of local animals, food models of local cuisine, and so on. Information boards mainly in Korean. Cool to check out both museums if you have some downtime in the town center.

spots.name: Wondae-ri Birch Forest
spots.desc: The birch grove is reached on foot from the visitor centre and car park; allow about 1–1½ hours to walk uphill to the forest, plus time to return. Wear suitable footwear, and check for weather-related trail closures before setting out. Winter conditions may require crampons.
spots.hours: May–Oct 09:00–18:00, last entry 15:00; Nov–Feb 09:00–17:00, last entry 14:00. Closed Mon and Tue; access restricted in…

spots.name: Yongdae-ri Hwangtae Village
spots.desc: Hwangtae is the Korean name for Alaska pollack, and Yongdae-ri is renowned for the tradition of drying these fishes on deokjang (traditional air-drying racks) by the batches outside their homes. Using the cold climate, the fishes undergo a natural freeze-drying process which gives them a chewy texture. It is no doubt the restaurants in this area specialize in all things pollack.

spots.name: Maebawi Artificial Waterfall
spots.desc: An artificial waterfall in Yongdae-ri that falls over a tall mountain rock, giving a majestic impression. In summer, people come here to cool down; in winter it freezes over, and ice climbing enthusiasts come here to train themselves.

spots.name: Gombae-ryeong
spots.desc: A mountain 1,164m above sea level. Average 3 hours to scale the mountain. There are well-built wooden paths for most parts. Due to the abundance of wild, rare flowers on a high altitude, it has earned the nickname of 'garden in the sky'. Different flowers blossom in different seasons other than winter: expect azaleas in spring, water lilies in summer, and mugworts in autumn. To protect the…

spots.name: Naerincheon Stream
spots.desc: The main stream of Inje. The 70-km stream starts from Mt. Odaesan National Park, winds around the steep mountains and valleys, and flows into the North Hangang River. It is one of the cleanest streams in Korea. When spring comes, the thick ice of the valleys starts to melt. The Lenok, which is a type of salmon, starts to swim upstream to lay eggs. When you notice scarlet royal azaleas blossom…

spots.name: Secret Garden
spots.desc: It is said that the site was called the "Secret Garden" because it was not accessible to the general public because it was a former military operation area. Previously, photos could not be taken because it was a military operation area, but now it is only allowed to take pictures on the side of the road. Early in the morning, you can see frosty and foggy images, all of which feel beautiful, and…

spots.name: 38 Park
spots.desc: 38 Park is located at the end of the 38th Bridge connecting Gwandae-ri and Namjeon-ri, Nam-myeon, Inje-gun, and is designed to discover and shape storytelling based on the 38th parallel in Inje-gun to provide forgotten historical value and build the 38th parallel as a tourism resource that can represent Inje-gun.

spots.name: Public Naeseorak Art Museum
spots.desc: Public Naeseorak Art Museum is a public art museum where artists who build their homes in Gyejeong-ri, Buk-myeon, Inje-gun or work in a workshop in Gyejeong-ri exhibit paintings born in the artist village. It fosters artists' active creative activities to create opportunities for local residents and tourists to experience creative works of culture and art and to inspire artists' creative…

spots.name: Inje Speedium
spots.desc: A world-class motorsports complex featuring an international grade racing circuit. Even when there isn't a race, visitors can tour the grandstands, visit the Classic Car Museum on-site, or simply admire the high-tech architecture integrated into the mountain landscape.

spots.name: Baekdamsa Temple
spots.desc: A historic temple that serves as a gateway to the Inner Seoraksan area. It is famous for the thousands of small stone towers (pagodas) built by visitors in the surrounding stream. The shuttle bus ride from the village to the temple offers a thrilling view of the rugged Baekdam Valley.

spots.name: Hangyeryeong Pass (Observatory)
spots.desc: A high mountain pass on the boundary between Inje and Yangyang. The observatory at the rest area provides one of the most iconic panoramic views of the jagged peaks of Seoraksan National Park. It is a legendary spot for driving enthusiasts and photographers alike.

spots.name: Circuit Taxi & Circuit Driving
spots.local: 서킷 택시 및 서킷 주행 체험
spots.desc: For motorsports fans, this is the ultimate experience. You can take a "Circuit Taxi" where a professional driver takes you around the technical corners of the Inje Speedium at high speeds, or even drive your own car on the track after a short safety briefing. It’s a rare opportunity to experience a Grade 2 FIA-certified circuit firsthand.

spots.name: White-water Rafting on Naerin-cheon
spots.desc: Inje is home to the most famous rafting course in Korea. The Naerin-cheon stream offers grade 3 and 4 rapids, providing a thrilling ride through narrow gorges and pristine nature. Most rafting centers are clustered along National Route 31 and offer combined packages with ATV and bungee jumping.

spots.name: Bungee Jumping at X-Game Resort
spots.desc: Test your courage at one of Korea’s highest bungee jump sites, standing 63 meters tall. The jump overlooks the beautiful Naerin-cheon river. The resort also offers other "X-games" like the "Slingshot" and "Power Fan" for adrenaline junkies.

spots.name: Photography at Whispering Birch Forest
spots.local: 원대리 자작나무 숲 트레킹 및 출사
spots.desc: A must-do for media students and photographers. The 3.2km trekking course to the heart of the forest is moderately challenging but rewards you with a surreal, silver-white landscape. It is a world-class location for capturing cinematic shots, especially when the white bark contrasts with the autumn leaves or winter snow.

spots.name: Hanaro Mart Inje Agricultural Co-operative
spots.desc: A supermarket right in the town center, where you can stock up on groceries. It has a variety of products, from food and beverages to toilet paper, perfect for last-minute shopping before going on a camping or hiking trip.

spots.name: Yongdae-ri Hwangtae Market
spots.desc: The best place to buy premium Hwangtae (dried pollack). You can find various forms of it, from whole dried fish to convenient shredded strips and even hwangtae-based snacks. The quality here is considered the best in Korea due to the unique freezing and thawing process in the local valley.

spots.name: Inje Traditional Market
spots.desc: A classic five-day market (opening on dates ending in 4 and 9). It is a great spot to find wild mountain herbs (namul), local honey, and seasonal fruits directly from the farmers of the Taebaek mountains.

spots.name: Birch Forest Souvenir Shop
spots.desc: Located at the entrance of the Birch Forest, this shop sells various items made from birch wood and bark, including postcards, small crafts, and local birch sap beverages.

spots.name: Inje Jaelaesik Sondubu
spots.desc: The name literally translates to 'Inje Traditional Handmade Tofu'. This restaurant gained popularity ever since it appeared on Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King, a famous Korean cooking-variety show. Beside the restaurant is a tofu factory, which directly supplies tofu to them. Hot-sellers include jeongol tofu (tofu stew), jjabak tofu (tofu braised in sesame oil), tofu hotpot, and grilled tofu in…

spots.name: Inje Makguksu
spots.desc: A down-to-earth Korean restaurant specializing in makguksu (buckwheat noodle), the specialty dish of Gangwon. You sit on the wooden floor and enjoy their makguksu on a short wooden table. Dishes include dongchimi makguksu (served in a soup with dongchimi kimchi), and bibim makguksu (served dry, you are supposed to mix it up just like bibimbap). For beverages, its either plain water for ₩2,000, or…

spots.name: Inje Sundaeguk
spots.desc: A restaurant specializing in sundae-guk (blood sausage soup), served with side dishes and rice. They also sell haejangguk (hangover soup). Beverages are either plain water or alcoholic drinks. Menu in Korean.

spots.name: Yongdae-ri Hwangtae-chon
spots.desc: Specializes in Hwangtae-haejang-guk (dried pollack hang-over soup). The broth is milky white and rich in flavor, served with local side dishes. It is a legendary breakfast spot for travelers heading to Seoraksan.

spots.name: Yet-nal Won-dae-ri Makguksu
spots.desc: Famous for its authentic buckwheat noodles (Makguksu) served with a tangy cold broth. It is located near the Birch Forest, making it a perfect post-trekking meal. Don't forget to try the boiled pork slices (Suyuk) with wild herbs.

spots.name: Champions Club (Inje Speedium)
spots.desc: Located within the Speedium complex, this restaurant offers a variety of Korean and Western dishes with a view of the racing circuit. It provides a unique atmosphere where you can dine while watching cars zoom past the track.

spots.name: Cafe Jajaknamu
spots.desc: A cozy cafe located right near the entrance of the Birch Forest. It offers various teas and coffees, but their signature birch sap tea (when in season) is a must-try for a true taste of Inje.

spots.name: The Bridge
spots.desc: A modern cafe overlooking the Naerin-cheon River. It’s a popular spot for people to watch the rafters go by while enjoying a refreshing iced Americano or a seasonal fruit ade.

spots.name: Namoo
spots.desc: Even in a small town with quite a small population, somehow there's a trendy cafe. The name is the Korean word for 'tree', and the cafe's decor emphasizes on nature, perfect for Instagram shots. Not only do they sell classics such as americano and cappuccino, but also creative ones like toffee nut latte and mango crush ade, and even alcohol. Do try out their croffle, which is croissant + waffle…

spots.name: Jeongamsa Temple
spots.desc: Established by Jajang the monk during the Silla Daynasty. Because the Sumand Pagoda in the temple stores Buddha's Śarīra, so no Buddharupa statue is seated in the main building Jeokmyeolbogung. The pagoda is the only treasure designated by the Korean government in the region.

spots.name: Jeongseon Arirang Festival
spots.desc: This festival is held annually to promote Korea's primal folk song — actually, set of folk songs — the Jeongseon Arirang. The festival starts with disguise parades and folk events followed by various sports and cultural events such as performances of Arirang.

spots.name: Hwaam Cave
spots.desc: A natural cave that was used to mind gold, Hwaamdonggul has been developed as a theme cave: The Meeting of Gold and Mother Nature. The total area is 1,803 m and it has five special exhibition rooms. Asia's largest golden stalactite wall stands here, 30 m high and 20 m wide, and stalactites in differing types and various sizes.

spots.name: Kangwonland Casino
spots.desc: Located above the town of Sabuk in southern Jeongseon county, this is the only casino where Koreans are allowed to gamble, and features blackjack, baccarat, roulette, tai-sai and big wheel, plus 480 slot machines. If you have a party of five or more foreigners you can, however, reserve a private table in advance. There is also a subterranean virtual-reality theme park, various performances by a…

spots.name: Rail biking
spots.desc: You can ride a rail bike and enjoy a valley along a 7.2 kilometer abandoned railway from Gujeol-ri to Auraji. You can take a free train when you return. At the starting point, a grasshopper-shaped cafe welcomes you. A 2-person bike and a 4-person bike are available.

spots.name: Five Day Market
spots.desc: Run on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, and 27th day of every month, this market sells mountain produce such as Korean red peppers, garlic, herbal medicine, mountain vegetables, corn rice wine and buckwheat paste.

spots.name: Gwongeumseong Fortress
spots.desc: 860m above sea level, Gwongeumseong Fortress is found near the south entrance of Sinheungsa Temple, located at the peak that reaches the heavens. The fortress is named after two generals - Kwon and Kim - who were said to have erected the wall in a day to block the Mongolian invasion (1253) during the Goryeo Dynasty. Seoraksan scenery seen from this Gwongeumseong Fortress is regarded to be the…

spots.name: Heundeulbawi Rock
spots.desc: One of the most famous attractions in Mt. Seoraksan. A small, round stone sitting on a bigger one, regardless of the number of people pushing it, rocks back and forth only 1530 cm.

spots.name: Jujeongol Valley
spots.desc: In the southern Seoraksan Osaek region, Jujeongol Valley is where the old yeopjeon coins were made during the Joseon Dynasty. As one might expect of a valley in which the national currency is produced, Jujeongol lies deep between high mountain ridges where the glorious tints of the autumn foliage are said by many to be the most beautiful in all the Seoraksan Mountains. The path leading to Osaek…

spots.name: Osaek Mineral Water and Osaek Hot Spring
spots.desc: Osaek means five different flavors that may be tasted in this special water. The water has strong iron content and is highly carbonated, which makes it difficult to drink it the first time. The water is so famous, though, that people from all over the country come to Mt. Seoraksan just for access to it. Osaek Hot Spring is called the beauty hot spring and does wonders for the skin.

spots.name: Naksan Provincial Park
spots.desc: It takes 15 minutes to Naksan Provincial Park from Yangyang International Airport, where visitors can enjoy a fine selection of facilities. There are many famous national monuments such as the Naksansa Temple, Hongryeonam, Uisangdae, and Hajodae; beaches with clean sand such as Naksan Beach and Hajodae Beach; theme parks, drive-in movie theaters, and sushi centers.

spots.name: Haesugwaneumsang
spots.desc: You can grasp the true essence of Korean Buddhist culture through this 16-m Buddhist statue. The grand scale of the statue along with the benevolent smile on its delicate expression is so beautiful that it moves anyone who sees it.

spots.name: Hongryeonam Shrine
spots.desc: Hongryeonam is a shrine within Naksansa Temple, too small to accommodate many people at once. However, this room is famous because Ui-sang Daesa is said to have met Gwaneumbosal where it stands. Many tourists come to see this little shrine, with a hole in the ground through which one can see the cliffs and the ocean.

spots.name: Uisangdae Pavilion
spots.desc: A six-sided pavilion built in honor of Ui-sang Daesa, the founder of Naksansa Temple, where he used to sit in meditation. The sunrise at Uisangdae is regarded as one of the most spectacular sights on the East Sea.

spots.name: Biryong Falls
spots.desc: Biryong Falls is at the center between Yukdam Falls and Towangseong Falls. The falling water of the loud and magnificent Biryong Fall looks very much like dragons flying up towards the sky, which is why it was named Biryong (flying dragon) Falls. The frozen waterfall in winter is another magnificent sight.

spots.name: Bisondae Rocks
spots.desc: Biseondae is about a 300-meter walk along the mountain stream from Waseondae Rock. The view is quite beautiful, and after rainfall water cascades down large boulders. The name ‘Biseondae’ derives from the legend of a fairy who flew up into the heavens while admiring the area’s beautiful scenery.

spots.name: Osaek Hot Spring
spots.desc: In Mt. Seoraksan National Park. This is a natural hot spring at about 600 m above sea level. There is a legend that the angels went to heaven after bathing in this very water. Osaek Hot Spring is famous for efficacy in treating neuralgia, muscle pains, arthritis, skin irritations, diabetes, blood circulation problem and digestive maladies. In particular, it is dubbed the 'Beauty Hot Springs' for…

spots.name: The Fourth Underground Tunnel
spots.desc: This is the only of the North-Korean-built tunnels discovered with motorized transport inside. The water flowing out from the tunnel have filtered through mountain rock and is considered healthy to drink.

spots.name: Eulji Observatory Tower
spots.desc: Eulji Observatory Tower is located 1,049 meters above sea level and one of the bitterest battlegrounds of the Korean War. From the tower, visitors can see the checkpoint and farms in North Korea and four peaks including Birobong, the highest in the Geumgangsan Diamond Mountains.

spots.name: Park SooKeun Museum
spots.desc: The Park SooKeun Museum conducts research, collects and exhibits works, and provides educational programs on the artistic spirit and body of work of Park SooKeun. It also offers various programs and activities, including a creative studio, the Park SooKeun Art Award, and a national landscape painting competition. The museum has five exhibition spaces: the Park SooKeun Memorial Exhibition Hall…
spots.hours: 10:00–18:00, last admission: 17:00, closed every Monday (open when Monday is a public holiday), January 1, and the…

spots.name: Yanggu Arboretum
spots.desc: Yanggu Arboretum is located at the foot of Daeamsan Mountain, about 450 meters above sea level. Visitors can see around 90 species of trees and shrubs, 170 species of flowering plants, six endangered plant species, 153 taxidermied animals, and around 1,500 bonsai trees. The DMZ Wildflower Bonsai Garden recreates natural landscapes in bonsai form to preserve and propagate northern plant species…
spots.hours: 09:00–18:00, closed every Monday and January 1. Open on public holidays that fall on a Monday, closed from May 11, 2026…

spots.name: National Center of Astronomy and Space Science
spots.desc: National Center of Astronomy and Space Science was opened in 2007 after an observatory was built near the geographical center of the Korean Peninsula, allowing visitors to look at the night sky from the center of the country. Visitors can observe stars directly through the observatory's guided exhibition programs and learn more about constellations and planets while touring the facility. The…
spots.price: Adults (20 and over): ₩6,000; military personnel, teenagers, and children: ₩3,000

spots.name: Gomchwi Festival
spots.desc: The Gomchwi Festival is held every May. A variety of foods made with gomchwi are available, along with various performances and events.

spots.name: Baekbeop Festival
spots.desc: The Baekkop Festival is held every August. It is a cultural and arts festival featuring water hybrid programs, a street parade, and a fireworks show.

spots.name: Punch Bowl Siraegi Apple Festival
spots.desc: Various agricultural products, local specialties, and foods produced in the Haean area are displayed and sold.

spots.name: Yangrok Festival
spots.desc: Held every October, the festival features a variety of performances by local military personnel, traditional folk games, and athletic events for everyone to enjoy.

spots.name: DMZ Marathon
spots.desc: This event offers a rare chance to run while taking in pristine, untouched natural scenery. Most of the course runs along unpaved roads, allowing runners to fully immerse themselves in nature. Side events include military band performances, aerobic dance shows, free food stalls, and local specialty booths.

spots.name: Naksansa
spots.desc: Possibly the main draw of Yangyang besides the ocean. Beautiful temple area with both mountain and ocean views.
spots.hours: every day 06:00 - 17:30 - Entrance/Pet is not allowed until 17:30 (No moving place, no dog car)

spots.name: Hajodae Beach
spots.desc: A 1.5-km-long beach with fine, white sand. It is a famous spot for snorkeling in Yangyang. It is 1.5km long, 100m wide, 7,562.5㎡ wide, and 0.5 to 1.5m deep, 12km south of Yangyang-gun and 1km north of the 38th parallel. Behind the beach, pine forests are dense, and in the pine forest, there is Hajodae, a hexagonal pavilion where Ha-ryun (河崙) and Jo-jo (趙浚), the founding contributors of the Joseon…

spots.name: Mulchi Beach
spots.desc: This is a simple beach. As it is at the entrance of Mt. Seorak, it is well-known as a place where many tourists stop by for a brief tour of the sea. Mulchi-ri Village is well-known as a place where many Seoraksan tourists stop by to see the sea for a while as it is at the entrance of Seoraksan Mountain. The Pine Mushroom Lighthouse at Mulchi Port next to the beach is a lighthouse shaped like pine…

spots.name: Namdaecheon River
spots.desc: In the upper reaches of Namdaecheon Stream in Yangyang, there are Beopsuchi Valley, Yongsogol Valley, Songcheon Valley, Naehyeon Valley, and Seorim Valley, and Songi Sculpture Park in the middle stream, and Salmon Ecological Park and Namdaecheon Ecological Observation Road in the lower stream.

spots.name: Daechongbong Peak, Seoraksan
spots.desc: Daecheongbong Peak is the third highest peak in Korea, and is considered a famous mountain with some 700 large and small peaks centering on Daecheongbong Peak. When you climb to Daecheongbong Peak, you can see the entire national park and the East Sea at a glance.

spots.name: Osaekryeong Pass
spots.desc: Osaekryeong Pass was a 1,004m-high pass that transported salt and daily necessities from Yangyang to Inje. In 1971, the number of tourists visiting Seoraksan Mountain and the east coast increased as National Route 44 was paved, and in 1981, the road from Inje-gun to Yangyang-gun and Sokcho-si was expanded and paved, making Osaekryeong Pass a deliberate visit to see the superb view.

spots.name: Osaek Jujeongol Valley
spots.desc: On the course from the Osaek Mineral Spring to the Yongso Falls, visitors can see large and small valleys located in the forest. The cool shade under the dense primeval forests is popular as a summer resort.
spots.hours: the summer season 03:00-17:30, the winter season 04:00-17:30

spots.name: Jukdojeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Jukdo was an island in the past, but now it is said to have been named Jukdo due to the dense pine porridge throughout the year. Jukdojeong Pavilion is a resting place completed in 1965 with the support of local administration and voluntarily raised by residents, and the tranquil space and sea scenery go well together.
spots.hours: the summer season 06:00-20:00, the winter season 07:00-18:00

spots.name: Namaehang Port
spots.desc: Namaehang Port, one of the three most beautiful ports in Gangwon State, is also the filming location for the hit movie "Whale Hunting" in the 1980s. The Namae Port Skywalk is not higher than other observation decks, so it is easy to walk and is divided into 1st and 2nd floors, so you can see the sea.

spots.name: Hyuhyuam
spots.desc: A serene coastal Buddhist hermitage known for its scenic ocean views, a giant Guanyin statue, and a flat seaside rock (Yeonhwadae) where visitors can feed swarms of dace fish in clear waters.

spots.name: Naksansa Temple Stay
spots.desc: It is located at the foot of Obongsan Mountain, one of the three famous mountains in Gwandong along with Geumgangsan Mountain and Seoraksan Mountain. In particular, Naksansa Temple is located in a place where you can see the East Sea at a glance. Temple Stay is a traditional cultural experience program that experiences the daily life of a practitioner in a mountain temple where the 1,700-year…

spots.name: Sol Beach Yangyang Ocean Play
spots.desc: It is a water park that uses seawater directly raised from the clean sea on the east coast. Outside, you can enjoy open-air bath, outdoor pool, and event bath while looking at the East Sea. It's operated by the resort, so you can even solve the accommodation.

spots.desc: Surfing is the main place. However, it is a hot place for young Koreans these days, such as food and famous photo zones in Korea. It's a unique thing to find in Korea because it's decorated in an exotic way.

spots.name: Yangyang board park
spots.desc: It is a place where you can skateboard. There are three skateboard lamps.

spots.name: Song-i Festival
spots.desc: Song-i mushrooms are known as the golden mushrooms, diamonds of the forest and mysterious spiritual beings. The Song-i Mushroom Festival is an opportunity to observe the habitat of song-i mushrooms that are strictly monitored. Anyone can enjoy the mysteriousness of these delicious pine mushrooms, but reservations should be made in advance.

spots.name: Yangyang Salmon Festival
spots.desc: This festival is held in the fresh waters of Namdaecheon, the biggest Korean river up which salmon swim. Apart from a good look at the natural ecosystem, there are various events such as catching salmon with bare hands, regular salmon fishing, and running with salmon.

spots.name: Yangyang market
spots.desc: If you want to feel Yangyang properly, you can visit traditional markets. Yangyang Traditional Market has the whole region and you can feel its unique vitality. If you visit Naksan Beach and Naksansa Temple, it is one of the courses you can stop by on your way. There are 64 stores and 100 stalls. It is a place where you can buy fresh local agricultural products at a low price, and you can enjoy…

spots.name: Stuff house
spots.desc: Stuff House is located in Yangridan-gil, Hot place, near Ingu Beach, and has many things to eat and play. It also sells a variety of surfing items including surfboards, clothing, and camping equipment for travelers.

spots.name: Pine Mushroom Village
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that has appeared in several Korean restaurant broadcasts, and is famous for shabu-shabu, bulgogi, and hot pot with pine mushrooms, a specialty of Yangyang.

spots.name: Sweet and sour pine chicken
spots.desc: It is Yangyang's sweet and sour chicken restaurant, selling mild, spicy, and fried chicken. It is located in Yangyang Traditional Market.

spots.name: Naksan Spicy Moray Eel Stew
spots.desc: It is a restaurant near the entrance of Naksansa Temple and is recommended by locals. You can enjoy a moray and cod soup. You can taste various Korean fish dishes such as soup and grilled fish.

spots.name: Samgyori Dongchimi Makguksu
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that sells makguksu that utilizes Dongchimi, a traditional Korean dish. Dongchimi is a type of water kimchi, which is made by putting various spices in salt water as the main ingredient of radish. With white kimchi, you shouldn't think of red kimchi. It also sells sashimi makguksu with sashimi.

spots.name: Ilbeonji Gamjatang Yangyang Branch
spots.desc: A restaurant known for its hearty portions of gamjatang served in large sharing-sized pots.

spots.name: Ondam

spots.name: In-Out Coffee
spots.desc: Café near Dongho Beach, known for its signature “corn coffee (옥수수커피)” — a local specialty. Great for beach-side coffee breaks or take-out before heading to the sea.

spots.name: Favorite Gelato & Coffee
spots.desc: Gelato-specialty café near Ingu Beach / coast — offers house-made gelato (various flavors), coffee, desserts; popular as a dessert stop after beach or coastal drive.

spots.name: Concentric Yangyang
spots.desc: those looking for a chill café vibe, coffee lovers, a quiet place to read/read/write, or couples/friends who want a relaxed café experience.

spots.name: Lighthouse Cafe
spots.desc: ocean‑view (sea & cliff) café, calm / relaxed vibe, also known for nice traditional‑tea / warm drinks & a quiet getaway spot.

spots.name: Badaview Bakery
spots.desc: Enjoy a wide variety of freshly baked bread made in-house every day while looking out at the open East Sea. Take a relaxing break with coffee and pastries alongside panoramic ocean views across each floor. The cafe features multiple scenic photo spots set against the beautiful backdrop of the sea.

spots.name: Dumunjin Port
spots.desc: If you take a cruise ship departing from Dumujin Port, you can enjoy the magnificent view of Baengnyeong Island for 40 minutes. Black cormorants fly around a lot, and on lucky days, you can see a natural monument, a spotted seal, as you pass through the elephant rock. As the sun sets, you can see the spectacular sight of the coastal cliffs of Baengnyeong Island turning red along with the red sun.

spots.name: Baengnyeong Sagot Sabin(Natural Airfield)
spots.desc: It is a geological topography. It was designated as Korea's Natural Monument No. 391 on December 30, 1997. The sand that forms the sand beach and the gap between the sand is very small, so the sand beach is forming a very hard layer of sand. The Sabin is hard like a concrete floor and was used as a natural airfield for the UN forces during the Korean War as well as for automobiles.Baengnyeong…

spots.name: Simcheong-Gak
spots.desc: Baengnyeongdo Island, the background stage of Simcheongjeon, a representative Korean traditional novel, is located in the place where you can see Indangsu, where Simcheong threw her body to open her father's eyes, and Yeonbong Rock, where she was reborn. To commemorate this, Simcheonggak Pavilion was built in a place overlooking Indangsu and Yeonbong Rock to discover and inherit traditional…

spots.name: Rock of seal
spots.desc: Endangered species spotted seals mainly live in areas adjacent to the NLL(Northern Limit Line). Baengnyeongdo Sealbawi Rock is their main resting place and moves to Balhae Bay, China in winter.

spots.name: Gamramam Rock Capture Site
spots.desc: It is a primitive topography. It was designated as Korea's Natural Monument No. 393 on December 30, 1997.

spots.name: Kongdol Beach(콩돌 해수욕장)
spots.desc: It is a beach made of round pebbles, and the stone is shaped like beans, so it was named kongdol (rock likes bean). There are seal rocks, which are the habitat of seals, and saury fishing grounds nearby. Because of this speciality, it is designated as Korea's Natural Monument No. 392. The average size of the gravel is between 1 and 2 inches and consists of various colors and patterns such as…

spots.name: Baenyeong Canola flower field(백령도 유채꽃단지)
spots.desc: Since it is located in the northernmost part of Korea, it is the last area where rape flowers bloom. You can see rape flowers in full bloom from early to mid-May, and there is also a walking trail. I hope you enjoy the rape flowers grown in the sea breeze. Originally, this was the sea, but it was converted into a reclaimed land. It is more fertile land because of. In autumn, it becomes full of…

spots.name: Joonhwadong church(중화동 장로교회)
spots.desc: This church is the second Presbyterian church in Korea. The gospel spread when Karl F.A. Gutzlaff, a Dutch missionary, entered Baengnyeong Island in 1865, and it was officially established in 1898. Throughout the Joseon Dynasty and Japanese colonial era, religious propagation was interrupted several times. Worship still takes place. Korea's first gospel spread right here. There is also a history…

spots.name: Baengnyeong dried sand lance
spots.desc: Usually, in Korea, people cook stir-fried anchovies a lot, and here is a side dish called stir-fried sand lance. It's a food that's not common. It is more savory and lighter than anchovies, and is excellent as a side dish for drinking.

spots.name: Baengnyeong dried seaweed
spots.desc: Seaweed is considered a healthy food in Korea. As Baengnyeong Island is far from the land, you can purchase better quality seaweed. In particular, it is recognized to the extent that exports are being made to foreign countries. You can make it with soup or side dishes, and it will be fun to find a recipe.

spots.name: Baengnyeong Semi-dried Rockfish
spots.desc: It is a semi-dried rockfish made by seasoning with Baengnyeong Island sea salt and then drying it in the sea breeze. Rockfish are regarded as high-quality fish worldwide. It's good to make with braised or steamed. It is often eaten as a side dish with mayonnaise on high heat.

spots.name: male crab in season
spots.desc: It lives in an area rich in plankton, where fresh water from the Imjin River is connected and fed by crabs. So crabs have a strong sweetness and hard skin. In Korea, it is usually used to make and eat marinated crab and soy sauce crab.

spots.name: Baengnyeong Island kimchi dumpling(백령도 김치떡)
spots.desc: Oysters and buckwheat, which are specialties in Baengnyeong Island Island, are the main ingredients of Baengnyeong Island kimchi dumpling. So it can be said to be a dumpling that shows regional characteristics well. It is also called Zanjideok (janzitteok). It is a food where you can feel the spicy taste of Korean kimchi and the smell of the sea that oysters contain.

spots.name: Jangbongdo Musan traditional laver(장봉도 햇김)
spots.desc: Jangbongdo laver is a sustainable cultivation method that is resistant to various diseases and insect pests, has a good scent, and has excellent taste and color. Jangbongdo Musan traditional laver is covered by sea ice due to cold weather, causing a lot of damage and taking a long time to grow laver, but you can eat delicious laver with strong scent and sweet taste because of the sincerity of…

spots.name: The Peace Institute, the Birthplace of Peace

It was designed and built as an education and training institute, a facility with accommodation and cooking facility, and was completed in 2014. The Peace Institute was designed to host guests for peace activities. It has served as a place of harmony for peace…

spots.name: Jarasum

People who walked along the waterfront trails, walked wild flowers, sports facilities, and recreational forests gradually began to recognize the beauty of Jarasum Island.

spots.name: Eobi Valley
spots.desc: During winter, the waterfall of the valley freezes over, creating a mesmerizing scenery. January-February is when most travelers arrive. There is a wooden bridge that you can take photos, and if you want to simply rest and enjoy the scenery, there is a traditional Korean pavilion beside it. Walking from the carpark to the waterfall takes about 10 minutes on an easy path. There is a shop at the…

spots.name: Water Sports
spots.desc: The river that runs past Gapyeong to Cheongpyeong has many opportunities for wake boarding, water skiing and tubing. You can enjoy many water sport like banana boat, flying boat, peanut boat, and bungee drop.

spots.name: Bungee Jumping

spots.name: Yoeninsan MTB Course

spots.name: Gangchon MTB Course
spots.desc: Through the mountains between Gapyeong and Gangchon is the Gangchon MTB course which also hosts an annual race. It is not as tough as the Yeoninsan course but it is still a great trail.

spots.name: Outdoor Market
