Since the late 1990s, the Incheon Metropolitan Government's strategy of combining five new cities by adding the business-port and leisure sectors to the triport with three elements: airport, port and information and communication base.Pentaport also refers to five different meanings that represent the spirit and philosophy…

spots.name: Incheon Songdo Fireworks Festival
spots.desc: The Incheon Songdo Fireworks Festival is a festival where lovers, family members and friends can enjoy various nightly lights, performances, and experience programs such as the beautiful world, lighting art zones, lighting shows with music, Christmas special zones, etc.

spots.name: Okryeon Market
spots.desc: Okryeon Market, which opened in 1996, has many small stores set up mainly for food.

spots.name: Bornga
spots.desc: Downtown. A Korean BBQ restaurant famous for its beef BBQ and the huge platter of vegetables that comes with it. They also serve the traditional pork BBQ known as samgyopsal. Try also the restaurant's other specialty, cha-dol jigae, a spicy fermented bean stew.

spots.name: Cafe Chosun
spots.desc: Downtown. A Korean BBQ restaurant serving samgyeopsal and seafood on a large stone grill. Delicious scallops and prawns.

spots.name: Newyork Bagel
spots.desc: Downtown, a famous bagel restaurant. There are different kinds of cream cheese.

spots.name: Triple Streets
spots.desc: Downtown. A complex shopping mall where you can find various kinds of restaurants and stores.

spots.name: Bapsang Pyeonji
spots.desc: A full set of Korean home-style dishes, including galbitang (beef short rib soup) and seasoned fish like grilled mackerel.

spots.name: Ching Ching China Songdo
spots.desc: Chinese dishes such as the popular samseon jjajangmyeon (seafood black bean noodles) and crispy sweet and sour pork.

spots.name: Caisson 24
spots.desc: A cultural complex cafe offering seasonal drinks with a view of the West Sea. It's a peaceful spot with outdoor seating and a photo zone, perfect for relaxing.Famous menus are Spring Cherry Blossom Latte, Passion Fruit Sweet Milk, Very Very Thank Cube Bread.

spots.name: Nordic Coffee Roasters
spots.desc: Known for its expertly roasted beans and cozy atmosphere, Nordic Coffee Roasters is perfect for coffee enthusiasts.

spots.name: Cafe Belle
spots.desc: A minimalist-style cafe known for its calm atmosphere and high-quality coffee, great for a quiet time in Songdo.

spots.name: Burgeroom 181
spots.desc: Gourmet burgers, especially the "Breakfast Room Burger" with a melted egg yolk. Don't miss the crispy bacon and chili cheese fries.

spots.name: Ushiya
spots.desc: Japanese-style yakiniku restaurant offering premium beef grilled at the table. Known for fresh cuts and private room dining.

spots.name: Seokam Saengsogeumgui (Songdo Time Space Branch)
spots.desc: A Korean barbecue restaurant. The meat is cooked on a hot stone grill and served with kimchi, garlic, and side dishes. Parking available in the basement.

spots.name: Oreumchae
spots.desc: A shabu-shabu and sukiyaki restaurant. The menu includes various broths (clear, spicy, sesame-seed), beef and pork, and finishing options such as noodle or porridge. The venue offers free parking for up to 5 hours.

spots.name: Samcheongdong Shabu
spots.desc: A shabu-shabu restaurant. The menu includes individual hot-pot servings, assorted vegetables, sliced beef or pork sets, and finishing options such as noodle or porridge. Solo diners is available. Free parking is available in the complex’s garage.

spots.name: Maum Coffee
spots.desc: A spacious cafe with a calm atmosphere, ideal for a work or leisure break. Known for high-quality coffee brewed to perfection.

spots.name: CinqVapeur
spots.desc: It is a cafe that sells bread made with natural fermentation, handmade sauce, and handmade jam.

spots.name: Café Comma – Songdo Branch
spots.desc: Quiet wood-toned café offering coffee, pastries and book-reading space; ideal for a restful break in Songdo.

spots.name: Café Poke
spots.desc: Trendy dessert café known for black sesame ice-cream and strawberry short-cake; short walk from Technopark Station and popular for photo-friendly interior.

spots.name: Forest Outings
spots.desc: Large, nature-inspired café known for spacious seating, brunch, and signature desserts. Ideal for photo spots and weekend gatherings.

spots.name: Ten Percent Coffee
spots.desc: Modern café chain serving hand-drip coffee and bakery items. A popular workspace spot near Songdo Techno Park.

spots.name: illy Caffē – Orakai Songdo Park Hotel
spots.desc: Hotel-lobby café offering premium illy coffee, brunch menu; convenient for mornings near Technopark Station.

spots.name: Kopi 101 Street – Technopark Branch
spots.desc: Café chain serving specialty coffee, handcrafted beverages and bakery items; located within walking distance of Technopark Station.

spots.name: Dumulmeori
spots.desc: Dumulmeori, the pure Korean word for Yangsu-ri, where the Namhangang River and the Bukhangang River meet and form one, is a favorite place for lovers. (It takes 15-20 minutes to walk from Yangsu Station) On September 18, 2016, the "Cultural Space Dumulmeori" was opened, which was created and operated by residents of Dumulmeori Village in Yangseo-myeon. In addition, in the cultural space, products…

spots.name: Namhan River Bike Road
spots.desc: It is a 26.8km bicycle-only road from Paldang Station in Namyangju City to Yanggeun Bridge in Yangpyeong-gun County, and is 4.5m wide, allowing two-way bicycles to pass through. The closed line section was used for 25.6km of the Paldang Station to Asin Station, and the Namhangang River bike path, which connects the Han River bike path, is characterized by beautiful surrounding scenery and the…

spots.name: Yangpyeong County Museum of Art
spots.desc: It is consists of exhibition halls, educational facilities, conference rooms, libraries, kid rooms, seminar rooms, and cafes.

spots.name: Gudun Station
spots.desc: A former train station that is no longer in service. It has become a popular filming location, famously featured in a music video by the renowned Korean singer IU, as well as in various Korean films.

spots.name: Semiwon
spots.desc: A riverside garden adjacent to Dumulmeori, themed around the philosophy of spiritual purification through nature. It is famous for its extensive lotus ponds which peak in summer. A unique pontoon bridge made of boats connects the garden directly to Dumulmeori.

spots.name: Yongmunsa Temple
spots.desc: A Silla-era temple famous for its 1,100-year-old ginkgo tree, the largest in Asia at 42m tall. This designated natural monument attracts massive crowds every autumn for its vibrant golden foliage.

spots.name: Sonagi Village
spots.desc: A literary park themed after the classic Korean short story 'Sonagi' (The Rain Shower). It features a recreation of the story's rural setting, where visitors can experience hiding from sudden showers just like the young protagonists.

spots.name: Yangpyeong Rail Bike
spots.desc: An active 6.4km round-trip course along a defunct railway. It offers a relaxing way to enjoy Yangpyeong’s pristine mountains and river views while pedaling through the countryside.

spots.name: Yangpyeong Sheep Ranch
spots.desc: A ranch featuring vast grasslands where visitors can feed and interact with sheep. It is an ideal spot for families and friends to create pleasant memories in a peaceful, rural setting.

spots.name: Jungmisan Observatory
spots.desc: Jungmisan Observatory is one of the best spots near Seoul for stargazing. Located at an altitude of 437 meters, it offers clear views of the night sky with professional telescopes and educational programs for visitors.

spots.name: Youth Museum
spots.desc: A nostalgic museum where visitors can rent 1970s school uniforms and explore replicas of vintage streets and classrooms. With numerous themed photo zones, it is an ideal spot for capturing unique memories in a retro atmosphere.

spots.name: Yangpyeong Mulmangeun Market
spots.desc: A central traditional market famous for its 5-day market (held on dates ending in 3 and 8). It is the perfect place to buy fresh local produce and sample authentic Korean street food.

spots.name: Yongmun 5-day Market
spots.desc: A traditional market located right in front of Yongmun Station, held every 5 days (on dates ending in 5 and 0). It is particularly well-known for fresh wild edible greens and herbs from the nearby mountains.

spots.name: Munhori River Market
spots.desc: A trendy riverside craft market featuring high-quality handmade goods, local artwork, and artisanal foods. It offers a unique shopping experience with a scenic view of the Bukhangang River.

spots.name: Dogabies spicy octopus
spots.desc: A popular restaurant specializing in spicy webfoot octopus with a distinct smoky aroma. The spice level can be adjusted to your preference. Each serving comes with rice and a variety of side dishes.

spots.name: Barley rice from Yongmun Mountain
spots.desc: A restaurant serving generous and healthy barley rice bowls. You can enjoy a nutritious and filling meal that comes with a savory stew and various side dishes.

spots.name: ddlanche
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant with the ambience of a traditional Korean house. You can enjoy a variety of authentic dishes, including seasoned acorn jelly (dotori-muchim), bibimbap, and wild herb pancakes (sanchae-jeon)
spots.addr: 6, Yongmunsan-ro 628beon-gil, Yongmun-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea

spots.name: Dreamy Camera Cafe
spots.desc: A unique cafe shaped like a giant vintage camera. It offers a sentimental experience where visitors can write down their personal dreams and take photos to preserve their memories.

spots.name: Concrete Jungle
spots.desc: A large café overlooking the Bukhan River, known for its scenic views and spacious interior.

spots.name: Chiquitito
spots.desc: A bakery offering a variety of financiers in different flavors and seasonal selections.

spots.name: SUSU Cafe
spots.desc: A riverside café featuring a spacious outdoor garden and views of the Bukhan River.

spots.name: Gangida
spots.desc: A café overlooking the Bukhan River, known for its outdoor seating areas and scenic riverside views.

spots.name: Marado Lighthouse(마라도 등대)
spots.desc: Marado Lighthouse is a prominent landmark located on Marado, South Korea's southernmost island. First lit in 1915, it has a long history of guiding ships in the treacherous waters around the island. The lighthouse continues to serve as a vital navigational aid for maritime traffic in the region.

spots.name: Marado Cheonyeo Dang Temple(마라도 천주교회)
spots.desc: Marado Catholic Church is a small and charming place of worship located on South Korea's southernmost island. As one of the country's most isolated religious sites, it provides a spiritual home for both the local community and visitors. Its unique and modest architecture, set against the beautiful coastal scenery, makes it a notable landmark.

spots.name: Janggun Rock(장군바위)
spots.desc: Janggun Rock, or "General Rock," is a distinct coastal rock formation on the island of Marado. The rock gets its name from its unique shape, which is said to resemble a general standing watch over the sea. It serves as a popular photo spot and is a notable landmark along the island's scenic walking path.

spots.name: Jeong Ji-yong Literature Museum
spots.desc: This museum dedicated to poet Jeong Ji-yong (정지용, 1902-1950) serves as Okcheon's cultural centerpiece. Jeong is celebrated as one of Korea's most important modernist poets, whose sensory imagery and refined language elevated Korean poetry to new artistic heights during the 1930s-1940s. His most famous works include "Nostalgia" (향수) and "Lake Gampo" (압록강), which remain essential reading in Korean…
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00; closed Mondays and major holidays (Lunar New Year, Chuseok)

spots.name: Jeong Ji-yong Birthplace
spots.desc: Jeong Ji-yong's restored birthplace stands as a tangible connection to the poet's early years. This traditional Korean house (한옥) exemplifies the modest yangban-class architecture of the early 20th century. The restoration preserves the original layout: a small courtyard (마당), main living quarters, and simple furnishings reflecting the period's domestic life. Walking through these spaces where…
spots.hours: Exterior viewable anytime; interior access may vary
spots.addr: Old-town area, Okcheon-eup (adjacent to the literature museum)

spots.name: Okcheon Traditional Market
spots.desc: Okcheon's traditional market embodies authentic local commerce unchanged by modern tourism. This is where county residents shop for fresh produce, seafood, meat, household goods, and prepared foods—providing visitors with genuine insight into everyday Okcheon life. The market comprises both permanent shops under covered arcades and seasonal outdoor stalls. The visual abundance is compelling: neat…
spots.hours: Market operates daily approximately 07:00-19:00; busiest mornings, especially days ending in 2 and 7 (장날, market days)…
spots.price: Free entry; bring cash for purchases

spots.name: Busodam-ak & Chusujeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Busodam-ak represents one of Okcheon's most dramatic natural features—a striking rock ridge rising from Daecheong Lake's waters. The formation emerged when the creation of Daecheong Dam in 1980 submerged the original valley, leaving these resistant rock outcrops as spectacular lake islands and cliffs. The jagged silhouette against the water creates scenes reminiscent of traditional Korean…
spots.hours: Accessible daylight hours; sunrise and late afternoon offer best light
spots.addr: Chuso-ri, Gunbuk-myeon (northwestern shore of Daecheong Lake)

spots.name: Dunjubong Observatory
spots.desc: Dunjubong Observatory offers one of Korea's most photographed natural phenomena: the Geum River forms a dramatic series of meanders that create a topographic shape remarkably resembling the Korean Peninsula. From this elevated viewpoint, the peninsula's characteristic "profile" is clearly visible—the river's curves outline the landmass with Jeju Island and Ulleungdo represented by small islands…
spots.hours: Accessible sunrise to sunset; autumn and winter mornings offer clearest views

spots.name: Janggye Tourist Site
spots.desc: Janggye Tourist Site serves as Okcheon's most developed lakeside recreation area, offering manicured grounds for relaxation and lake appreciation without demanding physical exertion. The site occupies a peninsula extending into Daecheong Lake, providing expansive water views in multiple directions. Facilities include paved walking paths, lakeside viewing decks, picnic areas with tables and…
spots.hours: Park area accessible 24 hours; facilities operate approximately 09:00-18:00

spots.name: Jangnyeongsan Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: Jangnyeongsan Natural Recreation Forest provides organized access to the mid-elevation mixed forests characteristic of Chungcheong Province's mountain ecosystems. The site serves both day visitors seeking short forest hikes and overnight guests using the forest lodge facilities. The trail system offers several options: Short interpretation trails (30-45 minutes, minimal elevation gain) introduce…
spots.hours: Recreation forest grounds accessible year-round; overnight accommodations require advance reservation
spots.price: Day use: ₩1,000 adults, ₩500 children; parking ₩3,000. Overnight forest lodges: ₩40,000-90,000 depending on facility…

spots.name: Yongamsa Temple & Rock-Carved Buddha
spots.desc: Yongamsa is a small mountain temple known for its rock-carved Buddha (마애불), a religious and artistic heritage site that predates the current temple structures. The carving represents Buddha's image created directly into natural rock faces, a sculptural tradition with deep roots in Korean Buddhist practice. While not as monumentally scaled as famous examples like Seokguram or the Gyeongju sites…
spots.hours: Temple grounds accessible during daylight hours; respect evening closure and meal times
spots.addr: Mountain temple site, Okcheon (specific location in temple mountain area)

spots.name: Jiyongje (Jeong Ji-yong Literature Festival)
spots.desc: Jiyongje stands as Okcheon County's signature cultural event, celebrating the life and work of poet Jeong Ji-yong while showcasing broader Korean literary culture. The festival transforms downtown Okcheon-eup into a celebration of Korean poetry, literature, and artistic expression. Programming typically includes: Poetry readings by established and emerging Korean poets, often held in atmospheric…
spots.hours: Typically held over a late spring weekend (May); specific dates vary annually—check with museum or county tourism office
spots.price: Most programs free; some workshops or special events may require minimal fees
spots.addr: Primary venues in Okcheon-eup; specific locations announced annually

spots.name: Okcheon Seedling Festival
spots.desc: The Okcheon Seedling Festival celebrates the county's status as one of Korea's primary nursery-tree production centers. Okcheon's nursery industry supplies ornamental trees, fruit tree seedlings, and landscape plants to gardens, orchards, and urban landscaping projects throughout Korea. The festival showcases this agricultural specialty while providing community entertainment. Festival activities…
spots.hours: Typically held over a spring weekend (late March or early April) when nursery industry activity peaks; exact dates…
spots.price: Festival entry free; purchases at market and activity fees vary
spots.addr: Iwon-myeon area; specific venue varies by year

spots.name: Lakeside walking along Daecheong Lake
spots.desc: Daecheong Lake's shoreline provides numerous opportunities for easy, scenic walking that emphasizes visual enjoyment and contemplative calm over physical challenge or specific destinations. The lake's indented coastline creates varied settings: wooded peninsulas, rocky promontories, quiet coves, and open lake vistas with distant mountain backgrounds. Developed access points like Janggye Tourist…
spots.hours: Accessible sunrise to sunset; early morning and late afternoon offer best light and temperatures in summer
spots.addr: Multiple access points around Daecheong Lake; Janggye Tourist Site provides the most developed starting point

spots.name: Hiking Jangnyeongsan
spots.desc: Jangnyeongsan offers typical mid-elevation Korean mountain hiking—mixed forests, modest peaks, and the satisfaction of upward progression through changing vegetation zones without extreme technical demands or massive elevation gain. The mountain suits half-day or full-day excursions depending on chosen routes and hiking pace. Primary trail options: Short interpretation loops (1-1.5 hours)…
spots.hours: Daylight hours; avoid evening/night hiking on unfamiliar trails
spots.price: Recreation forest day use fee: ₩1,000 adults
spots.addr: Jangnyeongsan Natural Recreation Forest serves as main trailhead

spots.name: Okcheon Byeolmi
spots.desc: Okcheon Byeolmi operates as one of the county's better-known local-style restaurants, serving Chungcheong regional dishes with attention to ingredient quality and traditional preparation methods. The menu emphasizes saengseon-guksu, various fish preparations, and seasonal specialties reflecting what's best from local producers. The restaurant's reputation among local residents validates its…
spots.hours: Typically 11:00-21:00; may vary seasonally—verify before visiting
spots.price: ₩8,000-15,000 per person for main dishes; set meals ₩12,000-18,000
spots.addr: Check website for current location details (Okcheon-eup area)

spots.name: Daebakjip (Dollyeobangbaeng)
spots.desc: Daebakjip specializes in the "dollyeobangbaeng" (돌려뱅뱅) style that has become popular in Chungcheong dining: a rotating tray at the table's center holds numerous dishes that diners turn to access—creating a visually impressive and practically efficient way to serve traditional Korean meal components. The style emphasizes variety, abundance, and sharing. This restaurant represents contemporary…
spots.hours: Typically 11:00-21:00; seasonal variations possible—confirm via website
spots.addr: Check website for current location (Okcheon area)

spots.name: Wollyubong Peak
spots.desc: Scenic rocky peak in the Hwanggan area, known for its sheer cliffs rising above the Geum River. Popular with hikers for its trails and panoramic views, especially at sunset. The site is also noted for its seasonal foliage in autumn.

spots.name: Okgye Falls
spots.desc: A 20m-high waterfall also known as the "Bak Yeon Falls," as the legendary musician is said to have played his flute here for inspiration. The falls are surrounded by lush forests and dramatic cliffs, making it a peaceful spot for meditation and photography.

spots.name: Mulhan Valley
spots.desc: Located at the foot of Mt. Minjujisan, this deep valley is famous for its crystal-clear water and cool temperatures even in the height of summer. It is home to several smaller falls like Hancheonso and Deungnyongso, and is a popular starting point for hikers.

spots.name: Minjujisan Mountain
spots.desc: A prominent peak (1,241m) in the Sobaek mountain range. It is unique for being the meeting point of three provinces (Chungcheong, Jeolla, and Gyeongsang). The ridge hike offers panoramic views of the inland heart of Korea, especially stunning during the winter frost or autumn foliage.

spots.name: Songho Tourist Site
spots.desc: One of the "Eight Scenic Spots of Yangsan." It features an ancient pine forest along the Geumgang River, providing a serene environment for camping and walking. The nearby Banamjeong Pavilion offers a picturesque view of the river's bend.

spots.name: Chupungnyeong Pass
spots.desc: A legendary mountain pass that historically served as the main gateway between the central and southern regions of the peninsula. Today, it features a memorial park and an observatory where visitors can overlook the historical route and the modern expressway snaking through the mountains.

spots.name: Songho Tourist Site (Geum River Trail)
spots.desc: River-side area by the Geum River, walking trails, scenic views, relaxing natural setting near 강선대.

spots.name: Yeongdong Wine Tunnel
spots.desc: A 420-m former railway tunnel converted into a themed wine exhibition space. Visitors can taste and buy local Yeongdong wines, explore displays on wine-making, and enjoy seasonal cultural events. The tunnel maintains a naturally cool temperature year-round, making it especially pleasant during the hot summer months.

spots.name: Nangye Gugak Museum
spots.desc: Dedicated to Nangye Park Yeon, a master musician of the Joseon Dynasty. The museum displays over 150 types of traditional Korean musical instruments and explains the history and theory of Gugak. It is part of a larger complex that includes a performance hall and Park Yeon's shrine.

spots.name: Gugak Experience Village & Cheongo
spots.desc: This cultural village allows visitors to hear and play various traditional instruments. It is home to Cheongo, officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the largest drum in the world, symbolizing the spirit and rhythm of the Korean people.

spots.name: Park Yeon's Birthplace
spots.desc: A restored traditional thatched-roof house where the musical genius Park Yeon was born. It provides a humble and authentic look into the early life of one of Korea's most significant cultural figures.

spots.name: Banamjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: A historic pavilion perched on a cliff overlooking the Geumgang River. It is considered one of the most beautiful spots in Yangsan-myeon, particularly during sunrise or when the river mist rolls in, reflecting the scholarly elegance of the Joseon era.

spots.name: Yeongguksa Temple
spots.desc: Historic Buddhist temple nestled in forested hills northeast of Yeongdong. The site is known for its serene walking paths, centuries-old stone pagodas, and mountain scenery. A peaceful stop for those interested in Korean temple architecture and quiet nature.

spots.name: Nogeunri Peace Park
spots.desc: A memorial park commemorating the tragic Nogeunri incident during the Korean War. The site combines reflective indoor exhibits, outdoor monuments, and peaceful natural surroundings. It serves as a place of remembrance and education about wartime history.

spots.name: Traditional Gugak Instrument Experience
spots.desc: At the Gugak Experience Village, visitors can learn to play traditional Korean instruments such as the Janggu (hourglass drum) or Gayageum (zither). Programs range from short 30-minute sessions to overnight stays where you can immerse yourself in the rhythms of Korea.

spots.name: Scenic Drive through Doma-ryeong Pass
spots.desc: A must-do for driving enthusiasts and photographers. This mountain pass features a series of 24 hairpin turns that snake up the Sobaek range. The drive offers a technical challenge and rewarding panoramic views from the summit observatory, especially during the autumn foliage season.

spots.name: Trek the Wollyu-bong Dulle-gil
spots.desc: A scenic 3.4km walking trail that follows the Chogang-cheon stream. The path is divided into three sections, offering different perspectives of the jagged Wollyu-bong cliffs and the surrounding countryside. It is well-paved and relatively flat, suitable for all fitness levels.

spots.name: Wine Tasting and Foot Bath
spots.desc: Visit the Yeongdong Wine Tunnel to sample various premium domestic wines produced by over 40 local wineries. After the tasting, you can enjoy a relaxing wine-infused foot bath, which is said to improve circulation and relieve fatigue after a day of exploration.

spots.name: Yeongdong Wine & Gugak Festival
spots.desc: The biggest annual event in the county, where traditional music performances and wine promotions happen simultaneously. Visitors can watch grand-scale Gugak orchestra performances and purchase local agricultural products at discounted prices.

spots.name: Hiking to the Summit of Mt. Minjujisan
spots.desc: Challenge yourself with a hike to the 1,241m summit. The most popular route starts from the Mulhan Valley. The peak is famous for its "Samdogbong" point, where the boundaries of three provinces meet. It provides one of the best vantage points for observing the "sea of clouds" in the early morning.

spots.name: Yeongdong Wine Tunnel Shop
spots.desc: The best place to browse and purchase over 40 different labels of locally produced wine. From sweet dessert wines to deep reds, visitors can taste before they buy. It is the most comprehensive collection of Yeongdong wines in one location.

spots.name: Yeongdong Traditional Market
spots.desc: A vibrant local market that comes alive during the five-day market dates (ending in 4 and 9). It is the ideal spot to buy high-quality Yeongdong walnuts and dried persimmons (gotgam) directly from local farmers.

spots.name: Hwanggan Walnut Specialty Shop
spots.desc: Located near Hwanggan Station, this shop specializes in locally grown walnuts, which are famous for their thin shells and rich flavor. They also sell various walnut-based snacks and gift sets.

spots.name: Local grape-fed specials
spots.desc: Small eateries around the market use seasonal grapes and local produce; ask for house wine pairings.

spots.name: Anseong Sikdang
spots.desc: A long-standing local favorite located right in front of Yeongdong Station. It is famous for its Olbaengi-guk, a savory and refreshing soup made with marsh snails and soybean paste. It’s a perfect breakfast or "hangover" meal for travelers.

spots.name: Deokseung-gwan
spots.desc: A historic Chinese restaurant in Hwanggan-myeon, famously featured on Korean food programs. It is renowned for its unique spicy black bean noodles (jjajangmyeon) and crispy sweet and sour pork (tangsuyuk).

spots.name: Gayeon
spots.desc: Located near the entrance of Wollyu-bong, this restaurant serves excellent Sanchae-bibimbap (wild herb mixed rice) and mushroom hotpot. It is a great spot to enjoy a traditional meal while overlooking the stunning river cliffs.

spots.name: Cafe Wollyu
spots.desc: A trendy cafe with a modern interior that offers an unobstructed view of the Wollyu-bong cliffs. It is a fantastic place to enjoy a specialized ade or coffee while watching the moon rise over the jagged rocks.

spots.name: Yeongdong Wine Cafe
spots.desc: Located within the Wine Tunnel complex, this cafe serves wine by the glass as well as non-alcoholic grape juices and coffee. It's a convenient spot to rest after exploring the underground tunnels.

spots.name: Unmunsa Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple founded during the Silla period. It is surrounded by pine and fir forests and is one of the major cultural attractions in Cheongdo.

spots.name: Cheongdo Museum
spots.desc: A local museum displaying archaeological and historical materials related to Cheongdo County.

spots.name: Saemaul Movement Birthplace Memorial Park
spots.desc: A memorial park introducing the history of the Saemaul Movement, which began in villages in the Cheongdo area.

spots.name: Cheongdo Seokbinggo
spots.desc: A historic stone ice-storage facility from the Joseon period, built partly underground to preserve ice through warmer months.

spots.name: Cheongdoeupseong Walled Town
spots.desc: Cheongdo Eupseong is a square-shaped flatland fortress located in the center of Cheongdo County, with a circumference of about 2 km and a height of 1.7 m, and is believed to have been built since the Goryeo period.During the Imjin War, the east, west, and north gates were destroyed and the fortress walls were dismantled; following the Japanese colonial era, the remaining walls were also damaged…

spots.name: Unmunsan National Recreational Forest
spots.desc: A national recreational forest on the slopes of Unmunsan Mountain. Visitors can explore wooded trails, streams and mountain scenery. The forest also has accommodation and camping facilities. Check admission fees, opening hours and accommodation availability before visiting.

spots.name: Cheongdo Namsan Valley
spots.desc: A scenic valley on the slopes of Namsan Mountain, known for its rocky landscape and flowing streams. The area contains rocks engraved with writings by scholars from earlier Korean dynasties and offers opportunities for short nature walks.

spots.name: Unmun Dam
spots.desc: A reservoir surrounded by mountains in eastern Cheongdo. The area around the reservoir offers scenic views and drives.

spots.name: Cheongdo Provence
spots.desc: A themed attraction known for its colorful buildings, photo zones and nighttime light displays.
spots.hours: M Tu Th F 15:00–21:30; Sa 14:00–22:00; Su & holidays 14:00–21:30; closed W

spots.name: Cheongdo Wine Tunnel
spots.desc: A former railway tunnel converted into a wine-themed attraction. The cool tunnel is used to store and display locally produced persimmon wine.

spots.name: Cheongdo Sin Hwarang Culture Village
spots.desc: A cultural complex introducing the traditions and values of the Hwarang, a group of young elites from the ancient Silla kingdom. The complex includes historical exhibitions, cultural experience facilities, a VR experience zone and a traditional archery range.
spots.hours: Tu-Su 09:00-18:00, closed M and selected public holidays

spots.name: Cheongdo Yongam Hot Spring
spots.desc: Bathe in natural hot spring water drawn from about 1,008 m underground. The complex has indoor and outdoor baths, saunas and a bade pool.
spots.price: Hot spring and bade pool from ₩7,000 for children; ₩15,000 for adults

spots.name: Cheongdo Bansi Festival
spots.desc: An annual autumn festival celebrating Cheongdo Bansi, the county's famous seedless persimmon. The festival features persimmon exhibitions, local food, live performances and hands-on activities. Check the official schedule for future dates.
spots.hours: Held annually in autumn; the 2026 festival was held on 16-18 October
spots.price: Free admission; some activities may require a fee

spots.name: Cheongdo World Comedy Art Festival
spots.desc: A comedy festival featuring live performances, street entertainment and family-friendly shows. It has been held alongside the Cheongdo Bansi Festival, allowing visitors to enjoy both events during the same trip. Confirm future dates and programmes before visiting.
spots.hours: Held annually in autumn; the 2026 festival was held on 16-18 October

spots.name: Watch Cheongdo bullfighting
spots.desc: Watch Cheongdo's traditional bullfighting matches, generally held on weekends.

spots.name: GoonPark Luge
spots.desc: Ride a gravity-powered luge cart along a 1.88-km winding downhill track. A lift takes visitors uphill before the ride. The attraction is near Cheongdo Bullfighting Stadium. Operating hours may change depending on the season and weather.

spots.name: Traditional archery at Cheongdo Sin Hwarang Culture Village
spots.desc: Try traditional Korean archery at the cultural village's archery range, inspired by the martial traditions of the Silla-era Hwarang. Ask about session times, age restrictions and availability before visiting.

spots.name: Comedy experiences at Korea Comedy Town
spots.desc: A comedy-themed cultural facility with interactive exhibits and performance spaces. Visitors can explore the history and culture of Korean comedy and check whether live shows or other programmes are scheduled during their visit.

spots.name: Hwarang VR Experience
spots.desc: Experience activities inspired by the Silla Hwarang through virtual reality. Visitors can choose from different themed simulations, subject to availability. This is part of Cheongdo Sin Hwarang Culture Village.

spots.name: Cheongdo Rail Bike
spots.desc: Pedal along a rail track through the countryside beside the Cheongdo Stream.

spots.name: Hike Unmunsan
spots.desc: Unmunsan is a mountain in the Yeongnam Alps, rising to approximately 1,188 m above sea level. Its forested trails and mountain ridges offer scenic views. Hiking routes are accessible from the Miryang side, including the area around Seokgolsa Temple. Some routes on the Cheongdo side have access restrictions, so visitors should check current trail conditions and entry regulations before hiking.
spots.addr: Unmunsan, on the border between Cheongdo County and Miryang

spots.name: Cheongdo Traditional Market
spots.desc: A traditional market selling fresh produce, meat, seafood, clothing and household goods. On market days, visitors can browse stalls selling regional agricultural products. Look for Cheongdo Bansi persimmons, dried persimmons and seasonal fruit. The market is within walking distance of Cheongdo Station.
spots.hours: Market days are the 4th, 9th, 14th, 19th, 24th and 29th of each month; individual shop hours vary

spots.name: Hanjae Cham Minari Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant specializing in grilled pork belly served with Hanjae minari (water parsley), one of Cheongdo's best-known local products.

spots.name: Yeokjeon Chueotang
spots.desc: A traditional Korean restaurant near Cheongdo Station specializing in Gyeongsang-style chueotang (loach soup). The soup is prepared by boiling and grinding loach, producing a rich broth. Fried loach is also available. The restaurant is within walking distance of the railway station.

spots.name: Ogyeong Tongdak
spots.desc: A restaurant near Cheongdo Traditional Market specializing in ongchigi, a local Cheongdo chicken dish. Chicken is simmered in a soy-based sauce, with mild and spicy versions available. The dish is served in portions suitable for sharing. Check opening hours before visiting, as the restaurant usually closes on Mondays.

spots.name: Coffee Myungga Cheongdo
spots.desc: A branch of the Korean coffee chain Coffee Myungga, offering coffee drinks and cafe seating. It is an option for a break while travelling through the Cheongdo-eup area.

spots.name: Verdant
spots.desc: A large bakery cafe with spacious indoor and outdoor seating. Its menu includes avocado coffee, sandwiches, baked goods and other beverages. Parking is available.

spots.name: Flower Place
spots.desc: A traditional-style tea house near Cheongdo Eupseong. It serves Korean teas, coffee and desserts, including persimmon-based refreshments. Visitors can relax in its garden seating area.

spots.name: Cheongsong Eoreumgol
spots.desc: Cheongsong Eoreumgol Valley is a gorge located on Juwangsan Mountain in Cheongsong. It is known for its warm winters and cool breezes in the summer, creating a mystical atmosphere. In May 2017, it was recognized for its geological value and certified as a UNESCO Global Geopark. During the summer, when the temperature exceeds 32 °C, ice forms in the valley, melting when the temperature drops below…

spots.name: Cheongsong Yasong Art Museum
spots.desc: It opened in 2005, was created by remodeling the former Sinchon Elementary School. With modern exhibition halls of various sizes and an art library, the museum offers a unique cultural space to experience creativity and contemporary art in Cheongsong. Free.

spots.name: Cheongsong County Seokgatdol Museum
spots.desc: This is a place exhibiting a diverse collection of scholar's stones and flower stones. It is housed in a traditional building, and visitors can enjoy a leisurely walk along scenic trails.

spots.name: Daejeonsa Temple
spots.desc: Daejeonsa Temple, founded in 672 during the Silla Dynasty, is a historic Buddhist temple located at the entrance to Juwangsan National Park. The temple is renowned for housing Bogwangjeon Hall, a mid-Joseon Dynasty wooden building designated as a national treasure, as well as several other traditional halls and relics. Surrounded by scenic forests and mountains, Daejeonsa offers visitors a…

spots.name: Hyeonbiam
spots.desc: This is a striking natural cliff along the Yongjeoncheon Stream in Cheongsong. Standing about 20 meters high, its dramatic rock formations and lush surrounding woods create an impressive landscape reflected in the clear stream below. The site is famous for legends tied to dragons and Queen Sohun, the wise consort of King Sejong, after whom the rock is named. Visitors can enjoy riverside walks…

spots.name: Jeolgol Gorge
spots.desc: Jeolgol Gorge is a dramatic valley in the Juwangsan mountain area, treasured for its steep rocky cliffs, dense forests, and clear mountain streams. The gorge offers scenic hiking opportunities, with paths winding through striking geological features carved by nature. Popular among nature lovers and photographers, Jeolgol Gorge reveals the wild and tranquil beauty of Cheongsong’s national park…

spots.name: Jusanji Pond
spots.desc: Jusanji Pond is a small reservoir located in Juwangsan National Park. It is a man-made pond that was dug out in August, 1720 and completed in October the year after. The pond has been used as a source of water for agricultural use as well as for drinking water. Even though it is small in size, about 200 meters long and 8 meters deep, the pond has never dried up from any drought. 150-year-old…

spots.name: Soheon Park
spots.desc: It is a resting area where the history, culture, and nature of Cheongsong, Gyeongsangbuk-do harmonize. The park is home to major cultural assets that attest to Cheongsong's long history, including Changgyeongnu Pavilion (찬경루) and Unbonggwan Hall (운봉관). Beyond its historical significance, Soheon Park is also a hub for cultural activities for both residents and visitors. Various concerts and events…

spots.name: Baekseoktangol Buri Area
spots.desc: It known for its scenic natural surroundings and cultural heritage. The area features the Baekseoktangol Buri Area Activation Center, which serves as a hub for local programs, community activities, and cultural events. Visitors can explore the region’s natural beauty, participate in hands-on experiences, and engage with local traditions.

spots.name: Cheongsong white porcelain
spots.desc: It offers visitors a chance to explore the beauty and tradition of Korean white porcelain, known as baekja. Located in Cheongsong, an area renowned for its pure natural environment, the center provides hands-on programs where participants can create their own porcelain works while learning about the history and craftsmanship behind this cultural heritage. It is a unique destination to experience…

spots.name: Sono belle cheongsong
spots.desc: This is a modern hot spring resort located in Cheongsong. Visitors can enjoy both indoor and outdoor hot springs amid pristine natural scenery, offering relaxation and wellness throughout the year. It is a place where families, couples, and travelers can stay comfortably and unwind while surrounded by nature.

spots.name: Sanso Cafe Cheongsong Jeongwon
spots.desc: It is the beautiful and largest flower park. It is famous for its massive flower fields, especially the largest Crape Myrtle (백일홍) garden in Korea that blooms vibrantly in Autumn. In Spring, you can see beautiful flowers like Poppies. It is a perfect healing spot to enjoy the fresh air and take stunning photos, with many great photo zones available. It’s often referred to as a "Healing Garden"…

spots.name: Cheongsong Apple Festival
spots.desc: It is the representative local festival held every autumn in Cheongsong County. Cheongsong is renowned nationwide for its apples, and during the festival, a variety of events are organized to celebrate the excellence of Cheongsong apples and the joy of a bountiful harvest. Visitors can enjoy apple-themed experience programs, parades, fireworks, apple sorting lotto, apple nanta performances, and…

spots.name: Cheongsong National Ice Climbing Championship
spots.desc: It is a world-class ice climbing competition held annually in Eoreumgol. Organized by the International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation (UIAA), about 110 athletes from 18 countries compete in difficulty and speed events. Alongside the competition, various cultural programs such as local product exhibitions and experience events are held, attracting many tourists.

spots.name: Juwangsan Sudalrae (Korean azalea) Flower Festival
spots.desc: It is held annually in early May when Korean azaleas (sudalrae) fully bloom along the Jubangcheon Stream at Juwangsan Mountain. The festival promotes Juwangsan National Park's stunning scenery and local tourism while praying for community unity and visitor safety. It offers diverse cultural events, including traditional rituals, flower petal floating, concerts, craft contests, exhibitions…

spots.name: UIAA Ice Climbing World Cup
spots.desc: It is a world-class international ice climbing competition held annually in Eoreumgol. Organized by the International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation (UIAA), athletes from around the world compete in lead and speed climbing events. Along with the stunning winter mountain scenery of Cheongsong, the event features traditional cultural programs, attracting many tourists and sports fans.

spots.name: Agricultural Cooperative Livestock Specialty Store Hanaro Mart
spots.desc: It specializes in selling Hanwoo beef raised in the clean environment of Cheongsong. The center focuses on providing fresh, high-quality products and introduces visitors to local agricultural practices. It offers insight into the regional livestock industry and Korean beef culture.

spots.name: Cheongsong NH Hanaro Mart
spots.desc: It is a supermarket run by Nonghyup, which sells groceries and household goods to local residents

spots.name: Jinbo Sikjajae Mart
spots.desc: It's a large supermarket specializing in food ingredients and supplies

spots.name: Juwangsan Hanwoo Charcoal Grilled Ribs
spots.desc: It offers grilled Korean beef ribs cooked over charcoal, a traditional cooking method that adds a unique smoky flavor. Visitors can enjoy high-quality Hanwoo beef known for its tenderness and rich taste.

spots.name: Juwangsan Songeo
spots.desc: Juwangsan Trout is a locally renowned restaurant specializing in freshwater trout dishes. Guests can enjoy a variety of trout—served raw, steamed, or grilled—with an array of fresh side dishes sourced from the region. The restaurant is known for its relaxed setting and friendly service, making it a comfortable stop for travelers after exploring Juwangsan National Park. It offers a taste of…

spots.name: Juwangsan Cheongsol Restaurant
spots.desc: It is popular for set menus centered on wild mountain herbs, grilled deodeok root, and traditional Korean tofu stew. The restaurant offers generous side dishes and a comfortable dining area, making it ideal for groups and solo travelers. Located near the entrance to Juwangsan National Park, it welcomes hikers and visitors seeking healthy, local flavors after exploring the mountains. Dishes…

spots.name: Minbakchon Restaurant
spots.desc: Minbakchon Restaurant is located near the entrance to Juwangsan National Park in Cheongsong. It has been run by the same family for two generations and offers traditional dishes such as herb bibimbap, chicken soup cooked with mineral water from Dalgisul, and grilled deodeok (Codonopsis lanceolata). The restaurant provides ample parking and a clean dining environment. It is a popular choice for…

spots.name: Mansoomugang
spots.desc: It is located near Juwangsan Mountain and Dalki Mineral Spring in Cheongsong. It offers dishes like herbal duck stew and grilled duck, featuring flavors passed down from ancestors.

spots.name: Palpal Restaurant
spots.desc: Palpal Sikdang is a local eatery known for its specialty chicken dishes, including steamed chicken, spicy chicken barbecue, and grilled chicken wings. The restaurant uses fresh ingredients and generous Korean side dishes to create hearty meals enjoyed by both locals and travelers. Its casual, welcoming atmosphere makes it a good choice for those seeking regional cuisine in Cheongsong.

spots.name: Sinchon Yaksu Restaurant
spots.desc: Sinchon Yaksu Restaurant is located near the Sinchon Yaksu mineral spring in Cheongsong. It specializes in chicken dishes such as spicy chicken soup, grilled chicken wings, and other local specialties prepared using the mineral spring water. The restaurant provides ample indoor seating and parking space. It is recognized for serving traditional regional cuisine popular with both locals and…

spots.name: Teotbatjigi
spots.desc: It offers traditional dishes such as herbal shabu-shabu, medicinal herbal chicken soup boiled in mineral water, and Korean beef bulgogi. It provides a quiet setting where visitors can experience local ingredients and food culture.

spots.name: 09 Sundaegukbap
spots.desc: It is a local eatery that serves traditional Korean dishes like sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup with rice). The restaurant provides a simple setting focused on home-style cooking. Visitors can experience authentic flavors typical of this region’s cuisine.

spots.name: Wangbeodeul Sikdang
spots.desc: It is a local restaurant in Cheongsong known for serving authentic regional cuisine. It specializes in hearty dishes made with local ingredients, most notably Medicinal Water Chicken Baeksuk (약수닭백숙) and Chicken Bulgogi (닭불고기), often prepared using spring water from the area. The restaurant typically opens early, making it a good place for tourists to enjoy a hearty meal before or after visiting…

spots.name: Apple & Coffee Story
spots.desc: Apple & Coffee Story is a bakery cafe situated near Juwangsan National Park. The cafe offers baked goods and drinks using local apples, and features comfortable seating on two floors with both table and window-side options. The atmosphere is casual, with views of fields and mountains, making it a pleasant stop for visitors exploring the Cheongsong region. Free parking is available.

spots.name: Bau
spots.desc: Bau is a spacious cafe known for its beautiful surroundings and a variety of baked goods made using the local specialty, apples. Visitors can enjoy fresh apple-flavored pastries in a relaxing atmosphere with lovely views, offering a pleasant stop for travelers exploring the region.

spots.name: Baekilhong
spots.desc: It is a traditional Korean-style cafe (Hanok cafe) located inside Songso Gotaek, a historic house. It's a place where you can enjoy tea and coffee while experiencing the beauty of traditional Korean architecture.

spots.name: Cafe Abad
spots.desc: It is a roastery cafe with a spacious indoor area and several separate tables suitable for groups and study. The menu includes standard espresso drinks, lattes, seasonal beverages, and cakes. There is a central table used as a study zone, while other tables are intended for casual conversation and rest. The interior is simple and clean, and self-service water and condiments are provided.

spots.name: Cafe Waterfall
spots.desc: Cafe Waterfall offers a quiet setting where guests can enjoy various coffee and tea beverages alongside baked goods. Through its large glass windows, visitors can admire the impressive ice waterfall and surrounding natural landscape. The cafe provides popular menu items such as the Waterfall Coffee and a variety of desserts.

spots.name: Kika Boni
spots.desc: It is a casual cafe offering coffee, non-coffee drinks, and simple desserts in a relaxed setting. Large windows provide a view of the ice wall, allowing visitors to enjoy the scenery while having their drinks. The cafe states that it uses organic products and focuses on bringing out the natural qualities of its ingredients.

spots.name: Kingdom coffee
spots.desc: It is a café serving as a comfortable resting place for both local residents and tourists. In addition to standard coffee options, the cafe is known for offering a variety of beverages and desserts, such as cup bingsu (shaved ice dessert). Some reviews mention that the space is opened up during the evening for a cool dining experience. Due to its proximity to resorts, it offers easy access for…

spots.name: Supullim
spots.desc: Supullim is a small, quiet cafe located at the entrance of Juwangsan National Park. The building, finished in white wood tones, blends naturally into the surrounding landscape, offering a calm view of Mount Juwang from its large glass windows. The interior features handcrafted rattan decor, creating a warm, natural atmosphere. The café serves coffee, herbal teas, and Korean-style desserts such as…

spots.name: Gasansanseong Mountain Fortress
spots.desc: The impressive castle was built during the Joseon Dynasty. It takes 2 hours to walk up the mountain from where you park.

spots.name: Dabudong War Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Dabudong War Memorial Museum commemorates the Battle of Dabudong, a fierce engagement during the Korean War. It displays artifacts used in combat, memorial slabs, and exhibits about the contributions of police and civilian volunteers. The museum is situated near the Nakdong River front line and serves as a local educational site about wartime history. Visitors can learn about the defensive…

spots.name: Songjeong Recreational Forest
spots.desc: A camping and picnic spot. Nice views of the mountains and forests though there is not much to do.

spots.name: Chilgok Patriots & Peace Memorial
spots.desc: Korean War museum focusing on the battles and incidents near the Nakdong river. Most of the exhibits are in Korean some of the major ones are also in English.

spots.name: Daegaya Museum
spots.desc: Daegaya Museum was established in Goryeong-gun to systematically investigate, research, exhibit, and preserve the history and culture of Daegaya and the Goryeong region.

spots.name: Jisan-dong Tumuli
spots.desc: A large group of ancient tombs associated with the ruling elite of Daegaya. The site overlooks Daegaya-eup and is one of the seven components of the Gaya Tumuli, which were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.

spots.name: Daegaya Living Village
spots.desc: A cultural attraction where visitors can explore reconstructed spaces inspired by the history and culture of Daegaya and take part in various hands-on activities. It is particularly suitable for families and visitors interested in learning about Daegaya culture.

spots.name: janggok Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: If you climb the steep hiking trail along the valley, there is Yongamji, a reservoir used by farmers for agricultural water in the old valley.
spots.addr: 195 Janggok Recreation Forest Road, Samguk Yusa-myeon, Gunwi-gun, Daegu

spots.name: Second Seokguram Rock
spots.desc: A place where you can see the greatness of the old ancestors who made caves on rocks and served Buddha

spots.name: Jeongane Farm
spots.desc: A farm offering hands-on rural experiences and educational programs. Visitors can participate in activities such as apple picking, making apple barley bread, and preparing apple cinnamon tea, as well as learning about healthy eating and experiencing eco-friendly rural life.

spots.name: Uiseong Traditional Market
spots.desc: A traditional market selling local agricultural and seafood products, including Uiseong's famous garlic, as well as onions, peppers, sesame, and other local goods.
spots.hours: Market days are held on the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, and 27th of each month.

spots.name: Uiseong Garlic Dak-galbi Restaurant
spots.desc: Uiseong Garlic Dak-galbi is a restaurant specializing in spicy chicken dishes made with garlic, the signature local ingredient of Uiseong. The menu offers a wide variety of choices, ranging from affordable single-person portions to the generous 'Emperor Set' served in hearty quantities. Visitors can enjoy tender chicken enhanced by the deep flavor of garlic-infused seasoning.

spots.name: Cafe Nine
spots.desc: A café near the Namdaecheon Stream in Uiseong, offering a variety of drinks and a relaxing place to take a break.

spots.name: Hyangchondang
spots.desc: Café in a former mill and cotton-fluffing shop, in a wooden building dating from the Japanese colonial period. Serves grain lattes (five-grain, black sesame), and sells sesame and perilla oil made from local grains. Parking in front.

spots.name: Cafe Sonamu
spots.desc: Café on the 2nd floor in Angye with a terrace decorated with potted plants and succulents. Serves coffee, ades and iced drinks.

spots.name: Gunchung-gil 17
spots.desc: Blue-painted café near the county office, named after its address. Known for its bingsu (shaved ice) in summer.

spots.name: Yetnal-ui Geu Jip
spots.desc: Quiet café in the former Gaeil rest area building on the road between Gunwi and Uiseong.

spots.name: Cafe US
spots.desc: Local-food café on the 2nd floor of Uiseong Food Village, serving drinks and desserts made with local produce.
spots.addr: 1858 Seobu-ro, Angye-myeon (2nd floor, Uiseong Food Village)

spots.name: Yecheon Jinho International Archery Field
spots.desc: It is the largest bow experience complex in Korea, where you can enjoy all bow-related experiences regardless of age.

spots.name: Insect Research Institute Ecological Experience Center
spots.desc: It is an insect-related experience, learning, and play space created and operated by Yecheon-gun, and opened in July 2007. It is divided into the Yecheon Insect Ecology Experience Center and Insect Ecology Center.

spots.name: Shilla Botanic Garden
spots.desc: If you visit the Shilla Botanic Garden, you can see the botanic garden and hear explanations about various plants.
spots.price: Depends on the price of the drink

spots.name: Hakgasan Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: It is a clean area with beautiful mountains and less human touch, and there are pine trees, Chamnanu trees, and Sanbut trees, so you can enjoy forest bathing.

spots.name: Seonmongdae
spots.desc: Seonmongdae is a pavilion established in 1563 by Lee Yeol-do, a student of Toegye Yi Hwang. In the front, you can see the wide white sand beach of Naeseongcheon Stream, and in the back, it is surrounded by pine forests, so the surrounding scenery is beautiful.

spots.name: Yecheon Wood Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: It operates a woodcraft experience center where all ages can participate. It provides an opportunity to learn how to use wood in daily life.

spots.name: Choganjeong
spots.desc: The Choganjeong, a separate house of the Choganjeong House of Yecheon Kwon Clan, refers to the detached house of Chogan Jongtaek, and was built together by Chogan Kwon Mun-hae in 1582 when he created a forest to live in his later years.

spots.name: Hwarongpyo
spots.desc: It is a place where you can enjoy the natural scenery with mountains and rivers in the shape of Taegeuk.

spots.name: Yecheon Bow Festival
spots.desc: The Yecheon Hwall Festival is a festival held at the Hancheon Sports Park. It is an experiential festival in which not only children but also adults can enjoy a variety of experiences related to archery, which can be interesting to participate in in Yecheon, the home of archery.
spots.hours: The festival takes place every year, but the dates may vary.

spots.name: Yecheon Insect Festival
spots.desc: With the theme of the Insect Ecology Center, the Yecheon Insect Festival provides children with time to return to their childhoods while arousing curiosity about living insects.
spots.hours: The festival takes place every year, but the dates may vary.

spots.name: Geumdangyahaeng
spots.desc: It is a night festival where you can enjoy the autumn night of the beautiful Geumdangsil Village with more dignity through various night programs.
spots.hours: The festival takes place every year, but the dates may vary.

spots.name: Yecheon Samgang Inn Ferry Festival
spots.desc: Representing the Chuseok holiday, this festival is a shelter for returning visitors to and from their hometowns. Various Yecheon's representative tourism resources, cultural and artistic performances, and Retro-Newtro coexist.
spots.hours: The festival takes place every year, but the dates may vary.

spots.name: Yecheon International Smartphone Film Festival
spots.desc: It is the only representative smartphone film festival in Korea. It conveys a new perspective by making a movie in accordance with the footsteps of the times with the smartphone that everyone has.
spots.hours: The festival takes place every year, but the dates may vary.

spots.desc: a complex store where you can buy a variety of daily necessities

spots.name: Samil Mature Society

spots.name: Bakdal Restaurant

spots.name: Yoon Hoon-sik Farm Ssambap

spots.name: a good-natured toadam
spots.desc: This restaurant is an ideal place to experience the local taste and culture. Mulberry leaf medicinal rice and grilled beef are the main menus.

spots.desc: The restaurant offers Korean beef menus such as beef bulgogi (grilled meat), raw beef ribs, and pork menus such as pork belly and seagull meat.

It is famous for 1,500 wooden stairs installed to the place where you can see the sunrise. In the middle of the wooden stairs, there are two…

spots.desc: It is a wind power complex built in Changpo-ri, which has a lot of wind throughout the four seasons because it is along the coast, and is built on the hill above Sunrise Park, a famous tourist destination in Yeongdeok. The power generation is 96,680 MWh per year, which can be used by about 20,000 households, which is the amount that all Yeongdeok-gun residents can use for a year. About 80-m-high…

In 2022, it was held 22-25 Dec. Venue: It will be held in Haeparang Park and Samsa Marine Park in Ganggu-myeon, Yeongdeok-gun.

spots.name: Yeongdeok Golden Fish Festival

As of…

spots.desc: A permanent market and a five-day market are also held every day.On the 4th and 9th of every month, 14th and 19th, 24th and 29th, peddlers gather like clouds.It deals with various kinds such as snow crab, which is a famous product of Yeongdeok, food for ancestral rites, vegetables, side dishes, and bowls, and customers are constantly visiting restaurants such as banquet noodles, barley rice, and…

spots.desc: Snow crab (market price/varying)Times (market price/varying)Cold Raw Fish Soup (₩20,000)Crab + Raw Fish + Raw Fish Soup + Crab Rice (₩160,000).

spots.name: Nabi Mountain Driver's Restaurant
spots.desc: It is a fish stew restaurant introduced as a famous restaurant in Yeongdeok-gun that the owner has cooked himself for more than 20 years. The menu may vary depending on the ingredients of the creature that comes in on the day. an order per person All foods can be ordered from 2 servings or more per menu. No delivery!
spots.addr: 10 Nabi Mountain Driver's Restaurant, Gangsan-ro, Ganggu-myeon

spots.name: Ssook Mulhoe in my hand, Sea Garden (내손에쏙물회,바다정원)
spots.desc: Representative menu:Mulhoe (₩17,000)Reification confidently carry your up-to-date portfolio in my hand (₩8,000)Hoedeopbap (₩17,000).
spots.hours: Mon Tue Thu Fri 10:30 to 18:30, Sat Sun 10:30 to 20:30, Wed closed

spots.name: Julpo Bay Sunset Garden
spots.local: 부안 줄포만 노을빛 정원; Julpo Bay Tidal Flat Ecological Park
spots.desc: A coastal ecological garden near Julpo Bay, formerly known as Julpo Bay Tidal Flat Ecological Park. The spacious grounds feature reed-lined walking paths, gardens and wetland scenery. Visitors can enjoy peaceful walks, observe the natural surroundings and visit an ecological exhibition hall introducing the plants and animals of the tidal flats. Some activities and facilities require separate…
spots.hours: Sunrise–sunset. Closed Mondays (or the following day if Monday is a public holiday), January 1, Seollal and Chuseok.
spots.price: Free admission to the garden. Separate fees apply to the ecological exhibition hall and some activities

spots.name: Buan Silkworm Town
spots.desc: An educational museum complex dedicated to silkworms, mulberry trees and traditional Korean sericulture. Visitors can explore the Silkworm and Insect Science Hall, learn about the life cycle of silkworms, and discover how silk is produced. The complex also features interactive exhibits, a hands-on learning hall and outdoor gardens. Some workshops require an additional fee.
spots.hours: Tue–Sun 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:00). Closed Mondays (or the following day if Monday is a public holiday)…
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000; teenagers ₩2,000; children ₩1,000. Some hands-on activities cost extra

spots.name: Baeksanseong Fortress
spots.desc: A historic fortress site on a low hill in Baeksan-myeon, closely associated with the Donghak Peasant Revolution of 1894. Peasant forces gathered here before advancing toward Jeonju. Although few visible remains of the original fortress survive, the site is important for understanding Korea's late Joseon history and the struggle for social reform. The hill also offers views over the surrounding…

spots.name: Buan Cheongnim Observatory
spots.desc: An astronomical observatory and educational facility opened in 2011 in the countryside of Buan. It features a 1,000-mm Nasmyth reflecting telescope housed in an eight-meter fully opening dome, along with smaller telescopes for observing celestial objects. Visitors can participate in astronomy programs and observe the Sun, Moon, planets and stars, depending on weather conditions and the…
spots.hours: Observation schedules vary by date. Check the official website for daytime and nighttime sessions and closure notices.
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000; ages 7–18 ₩2,000; free for children aged 6 and under and seniors aged 65 and over. Discounts available

spots.name: Gomso Port
spots.desc: A fishing port on Gomso Bay, known for its traditional salted seafood and locally produced sea salt. Visitors can watch fishing boats in the harbor, explore the surrounding seafood market and discover a variety of fermented seafood specialties. The waterfront also offers views of the tidal flats and the coastal landscape of western Buan.

spots.name: Woongyeon Jodae
spots.desc: This view captures the serene, peaceful outer coast at Gomso Bay. It highlights the traditional, picturesque scene of anglers fishing (jodae) against the backdrop of the calm sea and the unique salt flats, embodying the relaxed atmosphere of the western shore.

spots.name: Jikso Pokpo
spots.desc: The undisputed star of inner Byeonsan, this is the magnificent, 30-meter waterfall that plunges vertically into a deep, emerald pool called Jiksobo. The surrounding valley, complete with clear streams and the legendary Fairy's Bath (Seonnyeotang), makes it a true mountain sanctuary.

spots.name: Sosa mojong
spots.desc: The 3rd of the Eight Sights of Byeonsan. 'Sosa' is the former name of Naesosa Temple, and 'mojong' means 'evening bell.' It refers to the scenic beauty and the serene sound of the temple's Dharma bell echoing through the foothills of Naebyeonsan at dusk.

spots.name: Wolmyeong muae
spots.desc: The 4th of the Eight Sights of Byeonsan. This name means 'Misty Haze at Wolmyeong.' It refers to the ethereal and dreamlike view of the sea of clouds and mist surrounding the Naebyeonsan mountains, as seen from Wolmyeongam Hermitage, especially at dawn or after rain.

spots.name: Seohae Nakjo
spots.desc: The most celebrated of the Eight Sights of Byeonsan. This name means 'Sunset Glow over the West Sea,' referring to the grand and spectacular sight of the sun setting over the West Sea, dyeing the ocean red. The view of the sun sinking behind islands like Gogunsan Archipelago and Wido is magnificent. Sarang-ui Nakjo Park near Byeonsan Beach is the most renowned spot for viewing this sunset.

spots.name: Chaeseok Beomju
spots.desc: The 6th of the Eight Sights of Byeonsan. This name means 'Colored Cliff with Sailing Boats.' It refers to the dramatic scenery of Chaeseokgang Cliff and the fishing boats in the sea below. Best viewed at low tide when the cliff layers and sea caves are fully revealed

spots.name: Buan Celadon Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the history and craftsmanship of Goryeo celadon pottery, particularly the inlaid celadon produced in Buan during the 12th and 13th centuries. Visitors can explore galleries displaying historic ceramics, learn about traditional pottery-making techniques, and participate in hands-on ceramic workshops. The grounds also include historic kiln remains.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 10:00–18:00 (last admission 17:30); Nov–Feb 10:00–17:00 (last admission 16:30). Closed Mondays, January 1…
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000; teenagers ₩2,000; children ₩1,000. Discounts for groups of 20 or more

spots.name: National Saemangeum Reclamation Museum
spots.desc: A national museum exploring the history, technology and environmental significance of land reclamation in Korea and around the world. Its permanent galleries introduce traditional reclamation techniques, the development of the Saemangeum project and international examples. The museum also features special exhibitions, educational spaces for children and a rooftop garden overlooking the Saemangeum…
spots.hours: Tue–Sun 10:00–17:30 (last admission 17:00). Closed Mondays, January 1, Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok.

spots.name: Mohang Breakwater Fishing
spots.desc: A coastal fishing spot at the breakwater of Mohang Harbor, near Mohang Beach. Anglers can try shore fishing for rockfish, mullet and black porgy while enjoying views of the Yellow Sea. Check tide times, weather and local access restrictions before fishing, and keep clear of working fishing boats.
spots.hours: Access depends on weather, tides and any local restrictions.
spots.price: Free access reported; fishing equipment not included

spots.name: Swimming at Byeonsan Beach
spots.desc: One of the oldest established bathing beaches in Korea, opened in 1933. The long, gently sloping sandy beach is backed by pine trees and is a popular place for summer swimming and seaside walks. Its relatively shallow water makes it attractive to families, although visitors should check tides, weather and designated swimming zones before entering the sea.
spots.hours: Swimming is seasonal. Check the officially designated swimming period and lifeguard hours before entering the water.

spots.name: Hiking Byeonsan Masil Trail Course 1
spots.desc: An easy 4.5-km coastal walking route from the National Saemangeum Reclamation Museum to Byeonsan Beach, taking approximately one hour. The trail passes the Daehang-ri shell midden and Sarang-ui Nakjo Park, offering views of the Yellow Sea and surrounding coastal scenery. The coordinates mark the trailhead near the museum, not the entire route.
spots.hours: Best walked during daylight hours. Check weather and trail conditions.

spots.name: Gochang Mireuksaji Temple
spots.desc: This temple is a historically important place where you can see beautiful temple buildings and historical relics.

spots.name: Gochang World Heritage Dolmen Museum
spots.desc: Gochang World Heritage Dolmen Museum is a museum dedicated to the dolmen sites of Gochang, which are part of the UNESCO World Heritage–listed Gochang Dolmen Site. The museum provides exhibitions introducing the history, structure, and archaeological significance of dolmens, along with indoor displays and outdoor areas connected to the surrounding dolmen park.

spots.name: Ungok Ramsar Wetland
spots.desc: Ungok Ramsar Wetland is divided into three main visitor zone. The Obaegol Natural Restoration Wetland is the core zone of the site and can only be explored on foot via wooden boardwalks. Ungok Wetland Ecological Park, located between Obaegol and the reservoir, is an artificial park area accessible by walking or by a small exploration train. Ungok Reservoir, an artificial wetland, can also be…

spots.name: Dongho Beach
spots.desc: The beach stretches for about 4 km with fine sand and a gentle slope, making it suitable for swimming during the summer season. The beach officially opens to the public during the summer months.

spots.name: Dongnim Reservoir
spots.desc: Dongnim Reservoir is a freshwater reservoir in Gochang that is known as an important stopover site for migratory birds.

spots.name: Neoldeul Hakwon Farm
spots.desc: The farm is known for its seasonal landscapes, with green barley fields in spring and white buckwheat flower fields in autumn.

spots.name: Mujanghyeon Government Office
spots.desc: Mujanghyeon Government Office is a restored historical complex that served as the administrative center of Mujang-hyeon during the Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Sangha Farm
spots.desc: Sangha Farm is a large rural experience complex. It operates workshops, hands-on classes, and factory tours focused on food and agriculture.

spots.name: Yundojang
spots.desc: Yundojang is a traditional workshop associated with the making of yundo, a Korean geomantic compass.

spots.name: Gochang Cheongnongwon
spots.desc: Gochang Cheongnongwon is a farm attraction known for its open fields and seasonal rural scenery.

spots.name: Seokjeong Hot Springs
spots.desc: Seokjeong Hot Springs is a hot spring complex that uses naturally sourced germanium rich thermal water. The facility includes indoor and outdoor bathing areas, spa pools, and separate zones for adults and children.

spots.name: Gochang Tidal Flats
spots.desc: Gochang Tidal Flats are an extensive tidal flat area along Korea’s west coast, offering wide open coastal scenery shaped by large tidal changes. Visitors can explore the shoreline during low tide, observe coastal wildlife, and experience the natural landscape of Gomso Bay. The area is designated as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage site.

spots.name: Pansori Museum
spots.desc: Pansori Museum is a specialized museum dedicated to pansori, Korea’s traditional narrative music. The museum features permanent and special exhibitions displaying artifacts, recordings, and documents related to pansori and notable performers from the Gochang area. Visitors can explore multiple exhibition rooms, watch related audiovisual materials, and participate in basic hands on experiences…

spots.name: Seonunsan Provincial Park
spots.desc: Seonunsan Provincial Park is also known as Dosolsan, reflecting its long association with Buddhist practice. The park features forested valleys, distinctive rock formations, and Seonunsa Temple, a historic Buddhist temple complex with several hermitages and cultural properties. Visitors can follow well-marked trails to explore temples, rock carvings, viewpoints, and seasonal landscapes, making it…

spots.name: Munsusa Temple
spots.desc: Munsusa Temple is a Buddhist temple located on the mid slope of Mt. Munsusan, near the boundary between Gochang and Jangseong. Surrounded by forested valleys, the temple complex includes several designated cultural properties such as the main hall, shrine halls, stupas, and wooden Buddhist statues.

spots.name: Emart24 Gochang Park City Branch
spots.desc: Emart24 Gochang Park City Branch is a convenience store. The store provides basic groceries, snacks, drinks, and everyday necessities.

spots.name: Hanaro Mart Gochang Nonghyup
spots.desc: Hanaro Mart Gochang Nonghyup is a large local supermarket operated by the agricultural cooperative in Gochang-eup. The store sells groceries, fresh produce, local agricultural products, and daily necessities.

spots.name: Sinsun Food Materials Mart
spots.desc: Sinsun Food Materials Mart is a local grocery and food supply store. The store sells fresh ingredients, packaged foods, and daily necessities.

spots.name: CU Gochang Seonunsa Branch
spots.desc: CU Gochang Seonunsa Branch is a convenience store. The store provides snacks, drinks, ready-to-eat meals, and basic daily necessities.

spots.name: Daeseong Discount Mart
spots.desc: Daeseong Discount Mart is a large local supermarket. Compared to smaller neighborhood stores, it offers a wider range of groceries, household goods, and daily necessities.

spots.name: Uri Pungcheon Eel
spots.desc: Uri Pungcheon Eel is specializing in freshwater eel dishes. The menu includes grilled eel prepared with salt, eel soup served as a set or side dish, and simple accompaniments such as rice and scorched rice. The restaurant provides group seating and on site parking.

spots.name: Arirang Premium Chueotang
spots.desc: Arirang Premium Chueotang is a Korean restaurant specializing in chueotang. The menu includes chueotang served with either stone pot rice or regular rice, as well as side dishes such as fried loach, soybean paste stew with river snails, dumplings, and other accompanying items.

spots.name: Seongsong Hoegwan
spots.desc: Seongsong Hoegwan is a Korean restaurant offering a menu centered on dishes made with young barley along with meat and soup options. The menu includes barley based bibimbap with raw beef, bossam set meals, grilled pork, loach soup, seasonal cold noodles, and shared dishes such as boiled flatfish soup.

spots.name: Mokkoji Clam Cuisine
spots.desc: Mokkoji is a restaurant specializing in dishes made with clams(bajirak). The menu focuses on clam-based soups, stews, and shared dishes commonly served as Korean-style meals. Located within a commercial complex.

spots.name: Gunsan Agujjim
spots.desc: Gunsan Agujjim is a restaurant specializing in agujjim (braised monkfish). The menu focuses on monkfish dishes prepared in a shared-dining style, commonly ordered for group meals.

spots.name: Hyodo Jjinppang
spots.desc: Hyodo Jjinppang is a small local shop in traditional market area specializing in jjinppang (steamed buns). The shop focuses on freshly prepared steamed buns.

spots.name: Yeondawon Cafe
spots.desc: Yeondawon is a cafe located in a rural area of Gochang, surrounded by natural scenery. It focuses on drinks made with green tea and matcha.

spots.name: Thanks Duck Berber’s House
spots.desc: Thanks Duck – Berber’s House is a cafe featuring an Africa-inspired interior. The menu includes coffee, desserts, and bread sets served with kaymak (clotted cream).

spots.name: Old Downtown Joyangwan Cafe
spots.desc: Old Downtown Joyangwan Cafe set within a restored building in the old downtown area. The menu includes coffee, tea, and non coffee drinks, with bokbunja latte and bokbunja based beverages.

spots.name: Deulkkot Cafe Arboretum
spots.desc: Deulkkot Cafe Arboretum is a cafe located within the Goindol Wildflower Learning Garden. Visitors can enjoy drinks while walking through landscaped gardens featuring wildflowers and plants.

spots.name: Ylang Ylang Cafe
spots.desc: Ylang Ylang Cafe is located near the beach. The menu includes light meals such as baked egg dishes and French toast, along with desserts like cheesecake, brulee, and tarts. Drinks include coffee, grain-based lattes, and fruit based beverages, including bokbunja (Korean black raspberry) yogurt smoothies and lattes.

spots.name: Okjeongho Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: A 420-metre-long pedestrian suspension bridge connecting Yosan Park to Bungeoseom Island across Okjeongho Lake. The bridge offers views of the surrounding lake and mountains and provides access to Bungeoseom Ecological Park. Parking is available near the entrance.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:00); Nov–Feb 10:00–17:00 (last admission 16:00). Closed Mondays, except public…

spots.name: Bungeoseom Ecological Park
spots.desc: An island park in Okjeongho Lake, accessible via the 420-metre-long Okjeongho Suspension Bridge. The island is named for its fish-like shape when viewed from the surrounding mountains. Visitors can explore landscaped gardens, seasonal flower displays and walking paths overlooking the lake.
spots.hours: Mar–Oct 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:00); Nov–Feb 10:00–17:00 (last admission 16:00). Closed Mondays, except public…

spots.name: Pilbong Cultural Village
spots.desc: A cultural complex dedicated to preserving Pilbong Nongak, a traditional Korean folk performing art. Facilities include a traditional music exhibition hall, indoor and outdoor performance spaces, cultural experience facilities and hanok accommodation. Visitors can learn about Korean folk music and participate in traditional cultural programs by reservation.
spots.hours: Office and reservation inquiries: Tu–Sa 09:00–18:00. Performance and experience schedules vary.

spots.name: Saseondae
spots.desc: A scenic area along the Owoncheon stream, surrounded by rocky cliffs and forest. It features Unseojeong Pavilion and a sculpture park, and is especially popular for its seasonal scenery.

spots.name: Seongsusan
spots.desc: A forested mountain rising 876 m above sea level. It is known for its hiking trails, valleys and natural scenery, and offers panoramic views from the summit.

spots.name: Guksabong Observatory
spots.desc: An observation point overlooking Okjeongho Lake and its surrounding mountains. It is particularly known for panoramic views of the lake and the morning mist that forms over the water.

spots.name: Yongchu Valley
spots.desc: A natural valley between Yongchu Reservoir and Yongchu 2 Reservoir, originating from Baengnyeonsan Mountain. Yongchu Falls becomes particularly impressive after rainfall, and the area is also used as a starting point for hiking Baengnyeonsan.

spots.name: Osu Loyal Dog Park
spots.desc: A park commemorating the legendary loyal dog of Osu, which is said to have saved its owner from a fire. The park features dog statues, walking paths and green spaces.

spots.name: Imsil Hyanggyo
spots.desc: A traditional Confucian school founded in 1413 during the Joseon dynasty. Its historic buildings include Daeseongjeon Shrine and Myeongnyundang Hall. The site also features two centuries-old ginkgo trees.

spots.name: Jeonbuk 119 Safety Experience Center
spots.desc: Take part in hands-on safety programs covering fire prevention, earthquakes, typhoons, traffic safety, and emergency response. Some activities simulate disaster situations, while others teach practical skills such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Reservations and program availability should be checked in advance.

spots.name: Dohwaji Pottery Cultural Center
