spots.desc: Explore a pottery gallery and try making your own ceramics. Programs may include shaping clay, decorating cups and plates, and traditional craft activities. Contact the center in advance for current workshops, fees, and reservations.

spots.name: Seomjingang Dam Water Culture Center
spots.desc: Learn about the Seomjingang Dam and the surrounding area's water resources and history. Check the Imsil County tourism website for current visitor information and any available educational programs.

spots.name: Wood Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: Discover woodworking and the uses of timber through hands-on craft activities. Check with the county tourism office for current programs, age requirements, and reservations.

spots.name: Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province Shooting Range
spots.desc: Visit a public shooting range with facilities for clay target, rifle, and pistol shooting. Visitor access and participation depend on facility availability and eligibility requirements. Contact the range before visiting.

spots.name: Shangrila Country Club
spots.desc: Play a round of golf in the countryside around Imsil. Tee times, visitor access, and fees depend on availability; consult the golf club's official booking information before making plans.

spots.name: Deukgajeong Traditional Archery Range
spots.desc: Find out about traditional Korean archery at a local archery facility. Contact the operator or the county tourism office to confirm whether introductory sessions or visitor experiences are available.

spots.name: Survival Game Field
spots.desc: Try a team-based survival game as an outdoor group activity. Check the facility's current operating status, booking requirements, age restrictions, and fees before visiting.

spots.name: Haneulgureumgil Campground
spots.desc: Spend a night outdoors at a campground listed by the Imsil County tourism portal. Check current facilities, campsite availability, reservation procedures, and seasonal operating information before travelling.

spots.name: Sesim Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: Enjoy a nature getaway in a forest recreation area. Check the county tourism portal for current accommodation options, facilities, and reservation information.

spots.name: Gangbyeon Sari Campground
spots.desc: Go camping in the Gangbyeon Sari area near the Seomjingang River. Confirm the campground's current operating status, facilities, and booking arrangements before visiting.

spots.name: Banggil Fishing Campground
spots.desc: Combine an outdoor camping trip with fishing. Check current access conditions, fishing rules, campsite facilities, and reservations before setting out.

spots.name: Imsil National Sports Center Swimming Pool
spots.desc: Swim at the public pool inside Imsil National Sports Center. The county tourism portal lists weekday and Saturday opening hours, with a midday closure. Confirm the latest schedule and admission requirements before visiting.

spots.name: Cheese Valley Oak House
spots.desc: A restaurant near Imsil Cheese Theme Park specializing in cheese sundubu, a local dish combining soft tofu with Imsil cheese. The restaurant also serves seafood sundubu.

spots.name: Ilsongjeong Garden
spots.desc: A restaurant near Okjeongho Lake specializing in baeksuk, a traditional Korean dish of whole chicken simmered in broth. The restaurant offers lake views and serves locally sourced side dishes.

spots.name: Yeomunuri Hanwoo & Cheese
spots.desc: A Korean beef and cheese restaurant in Imsil Cheese Village, specializing in grilled hanwoo beef and dishes combining local cheese with traditional Korean cuisine. The menu includes sirloin, cheese yukhoe bibimbap and beef soup, with both open dining areas and private rooms.
spots.price: Hanwoo sirloin (200 g) ₩38,000; cheese yukhoe bibimbap ₩13,000; beef soup ₩9,000

spots.name: Daewon Driver's Restaurant
spots.desc: A local restaurant specializing in daseulgi-tang, a Korean soup made with freshwater snails, often served with hand-torn dough pieces. Other dishes include spicy stir-fried pork, kimchi stew and fermented soybean stew.
spots.price: Daseulgi-tang (freshwater snail soup) ₩12,000; spicy stir-fried pork ₩12,000; kimchi stew ₩10,000; cheonggukjang ₩9,000

spots.name: Imsil Cheese Village Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant operated by Imsil Cheese Village, serving dishes made with locally produced Imsil cheese. Specialties include cheese-filled pork cutlets, oven-baked cheese spaghetti and cheese rice. Group meals can be arranged in advance.
spots.hours: Wed-Sun 10:00-16:00 for individual diners; closed Mon-Tue. Group meals by reservation.
spots.price: Imsil cheese pork cutlet ₩12,000; cheese oven spaghetti ₩13,000; cheese rice pot ₩15,000

spots.name: Imsil Warehouse 1964
spots.desc: A bakery cafe converted from a former rice warehouse. It serves local specialties such as Imsil Gouda cheese coffee, cream cheese coffee and breads made with Imsil cheese. The renovated warehouse interior preserves traces of the building's original use and reflects Imsil's history as a cheese-producing region.

spots.name: GRANGGE Cafe
spots.desc: A lakeside cafe overlooking Okjeongho Lake, known for its panoramic views and European-style architecture. Visitors can enjoy signature drinks such as Grangge Latte, herbal teas, and freshly baked pastries. The second- and third-floor terraces offer scenic views of the lake, making it a popular stop for travelers exploring the area. Parking is available.

spots.name: Didier Cafe
spots.desc: A cheese-themed cafe in central Imsil where visitors can learn about the region's cheese-making history while enjoying drinks and desserts. The cafe displays traditional cheese-making equipment and features a cheese-aging cellar. Popular menu items include Cheddar Cheese White Milk, Camembert Chocolate Milk, and cheesecake. Free parking is available.

spots.name: Firefly Bridge
spots.desc: Located in the center of town, the bridge is decorated with colored tiles, artistic renditions of fireflies, and is covered by lights that change color. Unfortunately, predicting when the bridge will be lit is next to impossible, as it is solar powered and will only light up when the capacitors have charged (during special events, however, the bridge will always be lit).

spots.name: Deogyusan National Park
spots.desc: One of Korea's most beautiful national parks, famous for its high peaks and diverse flora. The highest peak, Hyangrobong (1,614m), can be reached via a scenic hike or a tourist gondola from the resort. It is particularly stunning in winter when the trees are covered in hoarfrost.

spots.name: Gucheon-dong Valley
spots.desc: A 28-km-long valley stretching from Seolcheon-myeon to the foot of Mt. Deogyusan. It is famous for the "33 Scenic Spots of Gucheon-dong," including various waterfalls, strangely shaped rocks, and deep pools nestled in a lush forest.

spots.name: Mt. Jeoksang
spots.desc: The mountain is open all the time, but the road to reach the top is quite steep, and may be impassable at rare times during the winter. At the summit, there's an enormous reservoir used to power the city and a Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Cheonillyeo Falls
spots.desc: A hidden waterfall on the slopes of Mt. Jeoksang. The name implies that the waterfall is "so high it touches the sky," and it provides a cooling mist and a refreshing view for those driving up the mountain road.

spots.name: Taekwondo Park
spots.desc: The park is in area covering 2.3 million m² and includes a Taekwondo Stadium, Exhibition Hall, Experience Hall and Accommodations. An observatory in the site of Taekwondo Park in Seolcheon-myeon, Muju-gun, draws Taekwondo lovers and tourists from around the world.

spots.name: Anguksa Temple
spots.desc: A peaceful temple located near the summit of Mt. Jeoksang. It was built to protect the royal archives of the Joseon Dynasty stored nearby. The temple offers a quiet atmosphere and great views of the mountain ridges.

spots.name: Baekryeonsa Temple
spots.desc: The gateway temple to the summit of Mt. Deogyusan. The walk from the park entrance to this temple is a gentle trekking course along the stream. The white lotuses (Baekryeon) that gave the temple its name are its symbolic feature.

spots.name: Jeoksangsanseong Fortress
spots.desc: A stone mountain fortress built during the Goryeo period. It was strategically important for guarding the Sagak (Royal Archives). Most of the fortress walls have been restored, allowing visitors to walk along parts of the historical defense line.

spots.name: Muju Hyanggyo
spots.desc: A local Confucian school established during the Joseon Dynasty. The traditional architecture is well-preserved, including the Daemyeong-ru gate and the main hall where ancestral rites were performed.

spots.name: Bandi Land
spots.desc: An eco-cultural park dedicated to fireflies (Bandi), which are a symbol of Muju's clean environment. The complex includes an insect museum, an astronomical observatory, and an ecological aquarium.

spots.name: Muju Insect Museum
spots.desc: Part of Bandi Land, this museum houses thousands of insect specimens from around the world. It features a 3D theater and a greenhouse with tropical plants, making it a favorite for families with children.

spots.name: Muju Meoru Wine Cave
spots.desc: A tunnel that was built for a hydroelectric power plant has been repurposed as a wine cellar. It stays naturally cool year-round and is used to age and sell wine made from local "Meoru" (wild grapes). Visitors can enjoy wine tasting and foot baths.

spots.name: Taekwondo Performance and Training at Taekwondowon
spots.desc: Watch professional Taekwondo demonstrations at the T1 Arena or participate in a basic training program. Visitors can learn fundamental kicks and forms under the guidance of certified masters.

spots.name: Muju Mountain Film Festival
spots.desc: Known as a "healing" film festival, this unique event features outdoor screenings of independent, classic, and international films in a relaxed mountain setting. It emphasizes a "slow" culture, where visitors can enjoy movies while camping or sitting on the grass under the stars. The festival also hosts various live music performances and talk sessions with filmmakers.

spots.name: Skiing and snowboarding at Muju Deogyusan Resort
spots.desc: One of the most famous ski resorts in Korea. It features the "Silk Road" slope, which is the longest in the country (6.1km), and the "Raiders" slope, known for its steep incline. Equipment rental and lessons are available for all skill levels.

spots.name: Muju Firefly Festival
spots.desc: A representative eco-friendly festival in Korea dedicated to fireflies, a natural monument and symbol of a clean environment. The festival offers firefly exploration tours, traditional performances, and a "falling fire" (Nakhwa-nori) show over the river.

spots.name: Ride the Tourist Gondola
spots.desc: Take a 15-minute gondola ride from the resort base to Seolcheonbong Peak (1,520m). From there, it is a gentle 20-minute walk on a wooden boardwalk to Hyangrobong, the highest peak of Mt. Deogyusan. It is especially popular in winter for viewing frost-covered trees.

spots.name: Stargazing at Bandi Observatory
spots.desc: Located within Bandi Land, this observatory features high-powered telescopes to observe planets, stars, and nebulae. It is an ideal spot for families to learn about astronomy in the clear, unpolluted night sky of Muju.

spots.name: Rafting on the Geumgang River
spots.desc: Enjoy a scenic rafting trip down the Geumgang River. The rapids here are relatively mild, making it suitable for families and beginners. It is a great way to see the riverside cliffs and rock formations from a different perspective.

spots.name: Muju Meoru Wine Cave Shop
spots.desc: The best place to purchase Muju's signature wild grape wine. Several local brands are available for tasting before purchase. The wine is known for its deep color and rich, sweet-tart flavor profile.

spots.name: Muju Traditional Market
spots.desc: A traditional five-day market that opens on dates ending in 1 and 6. It’s an excellent spot to find fresh local produce like walnuts, apples, and dried herbs directly from local farmers.

spots.name: Cheonma Specialized Shop
spots.desc: Specializes in products made from Cheonma (Gastrodia elata), a rare medicinal herb that thrives in Muju’s clean environment. You can find tea, extracts, and powdered forms of this health-boosting root.

spots.name: Geumgang Sikdang
spots.desc: A legendary restaurant famous for its authentic Eojuk (fish porridge). The dish is made by boiling freshwater fish for hours, then adding rice, noodles, and gochujang. It’s a hearty, spicy, and nutritious meal that is considered a local soul food.

spots.name: Byeolmaru
spots.desc: Located near the entrance of Deogyusan National Park, this restaurant specializes in Sanchae Bibimbap (wild herb mixed rice) and Deodeok-gui (grilled deodeok root). They use seasonal herbs harvested directly from the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Mujuhyang
spots.desc: A popular spot known for its buckwheat noodles and pork slices. It offers a clean, modern atmosphere and is a great place to have a light but satisfying meal after visiting Taekwondowon.

spots.name: Cafe Jinyori
spots.desc: A cozy and aesthetically pleasing cafe located near the Taekwondowon and Bandi Land. It is a popular spot for travelers to grab a high-quality coffee or a refreshing seasonal fruit juice. The interior is decorated with traditional touches, providing a relaxing atmosphere.

spots.name: Seodong Park
spots.desc: An interesting park where the grounds are mostly covered by pond water in lotus shape. One can walk on stone paths, or one of the numerous pathways around the pond with a pavilion in the centre, connected by a long wooden bridge. They claim that this was one of the first man-made parks in Korea. On a site to the east closer to the Hwaji Mountain, there is a monument dedicated to 5,000 military…

spots.name: Baekje Royal Tombs Park
spots.desc: Site with seven tombs of the Baekje Royal families. There is a Baekje Gobun Museum with exhibitions about the tombs.

spots.name: Donam-seowon
spots.desc: Confucian academy, one of nine to make up the world heritage site Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies.

spots.name: Buyeo Yeo Heungmin's House
spots.desc: It is a traditional hanok, a cultural heritage that shows the life of the Yangban family in the late Joseon Dynasty. This house has been inhabited and maintained by descendants of the Yeoheung Min family, providing a glimpse into the history and value of Korean traditional architecture.

spots.name: Miamsa Rice Rock
spots.desc: It is a huge rock located near Miamsa Temple, and the unique shape of its surface looks like a stack of rice grains, so it was named 'Salbawi'.

spots.name: YeonipDam
spots.desc: Yeon-ip-dam is a serene lotus pond in the Gungnamji Pond area in Buyeo, often considered the first artificial garden in Korea. It is especially famous in summer when thousands of lotus flowers bloom beautifully, offering a tranquil and historic atmosphere. This spot provides a perfect peaceful retreat, reflecting the ancient elegance of the Baekje Kingdom's capital.

spots.name: Jangwon Makguksu
spots.desc: Jangwon Makguksu is a highly popular local restaurant in Buyeo, renowned for its deliciously chewy and savory buckwheat noodles (Makguksu). The noodles are typically served cold with a rich, flavorful broth or spicy seasoning, often accompanied by their famous Pyeonyuk (sliced boiled pork). It’s considered a must-visit spot for an authentic and satisfying taste of local Korean cuisine.

spots.name: a piece of cloud
spots.desc: "Gureum Han Jogak" is a cozy and popular dessert cafe in Buyeo, well-known for its delicious handmade, seasonal fruit desserts and fresh egg tarts. They offer a variety of beverages, including hand-drip coffee and non-coffee drinks, making it a great place to relax. This charming spot is highly praised by locals and visitors for its quality treats and comfortable atmosphere.

spots.name: cafe IN
spots.desc: "Cafe IN" is a modern and stylish coffee shop in Buyeo known for its high-quality espresso drinks and inviting, aesthetically pleasing interior. It offers a spacious and relaxing environment perfect for taking a break or catching up with friends. Many visitors enjoy the cafe's meticulously prepared coffee and the peaceful atmosphere it provides.
spots.hours: 12:00-22:00 (Sun open until 18:00 and Mon is closed)

spots.name: Cheonjangho Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: A suspension bridge over Cheonjang Lake, one of Cheongyang's best-known landmarks, featuring a golden dragon sculpture tied to local legend.

spots.name: Chilgap Tower
spots.desc: A newer landmark (opened around early 2026) featuring a 102-m skywalk and observation deck over a lake, said to have drawn 100,000 visitors within its first four months.
spots.price: ₩2,000 toddlers (36 mo-6 yr), ₩3,000 children (7-12), ₩5,000 teens (13-18), ₩7,000 adults (19+); cash not accepted; no…

spots.name: Goun Botanical Garden
spots.desc: A botanical garden with around 10,000 plant species, designed to follow the natural contours of the mountain rather than artificial landscaping.
spots.price: ₩8,000 adults, ₩5,000 students (kindergarten-high school), ₩5,000 seniors(65+)/disabled; groups (30+): ₩7,000 adults…

spots.name: Chilgapsan Jangseung Park
spots.desc: A theme park opened in 1999 to preserve Korean totem pole (jangseung) culture, with two 11.5-m-tall main poles, Chilgapsan Daejanggun and Chilgapsan Yeojanggun, and jangseung from across the country.

spots.name: Chilgapsan Observatory
spots.desc: An astronomy science center open to the public, with a main observatory housing an APO 304 mm refracting telescope described as Korea's largest, a smaller dome observatory, a screening room, and a 12 m geodesic projection dome.

spots.name: National West Coast Climate and Atmospheric Center
spots.desc: An agency that studies and manages climate change and air pollution in the West Coast region

spots.name: Hongseong Sky Tower
spots.desc: It was established in 2005 on the shore of the coast of Hongseong on the coast of the sea in the middle of Eosa Port and Gungri. When you go up to the observatory, you can see Cheonsuman Bay at a glance, and there is a small island called Moseom right in front. In 2012, a photo zone of a boat model was installed through the creation of a scenic spot that is good for taking pictures, reminding you…

spots.name: Aurora Farm
spots.desc: It is a place where you can experience a farm. Depending on the season, you can experience harvesting strawberries, blueberries, cherries, and other fruits. The price varies between items.

spots.name: Baekwolsan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a mountain 394m above sea level, with a gentle slope and well-maintained hiking trails, making it easy for beginners to climb. From the top, it is characterized by a beautiful view of the west coast and a view of the mountains and fields around Hongseong.

spots.name: Cheolmasan Mountain
spots.desc: The mountain is 443m above sea level, providing relatively short hiking trails and various natural landscapes.

spots.name: Gwaneumsa Temple
spots.desc: This temple is known as a place related to the faith of the Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, and many people pay their respects in a calm and peaceful atmosphere.

spots.name: Yonghyeonsa Temple
spots.desc: Like its name, it is a place where there are legends related to dragons. The temple is mainly known as a place for Buddhist training and prayer, especially in the forest, and is famous for meditation and practice with nature.

spots.name: Wolgwangsa Temple
spots.desc: It is famous for its beautiful moonlight view. This temple is mostly visited by those who seek mental peace and stability, and is a quiet place where you can practice and meditate along the moonlight of the night sky. Especially if you visit at night, you can feel the mysterious atmosphere of Wolgwangsa Temple better.

spots.name: Jeongamsa Temple
spots.desc: Like the temple's name, Jeongamsa Temple is a place that feels similar to a quiet hermitage, providing a suitable environment for practice and meditation. Located in the mountains, it is a place where you can communicate with nature, and it is a popular place for people who want to practice in a peaceful atmosphere.

spots.name: Yongbongsan Campground
spots.desc: Located at the foot of Yongbongsan Mountain, Yongbongsan Campground is a camping site that provides nature and rest with pine forests. It is located in the middle of northwest Chungcheongnam-do, so it is connected to various tourist destinations within 20–30 minutes. Swimming pools, Wi-Fi, playgrounds, hands-on activities, and water slides are provided. For those who like eco-friendly activities…

spots.name: Hongseong Sol Wind Theme Park
spots.desc: It is a nature-friendly park with pine forests, walking trails, and open lawns. It offers playgrounds and activities for families throughout all seasons. It is easily accessible and popular among locals and tourists.

spots.name: Slow Sil Village Rural Experience
spots.desc: This is a rural village where you can enjoy nature and cultural experiences at the same time. It provides a variety of experience programs and comfortable rest areas that take advantage of local characteristics, and allows urban residents to feel the relaxation and fun of rural life.

spots.name: Namdang Port Net Adventure
spots.desc: It is a marine experience facility located in Namdang Port. It and offers play that can be enjoyed in the nets on the sea. It provides a safe and unique experience to family visitors and is good for connecting with marine tourism at Namdang Port.

spots.name: With Bugs
spots.desc: It is an educational space where you can directly observe and experience various insects as an insect experience learning center. It provides children and families with opportunities to learn and experience insect ecology, and operates in a nature-friendly environment. There is a program that combines learning and play, so you can enjoy ecological education and fun at the same time.

spots.name: N Mart Hongseong Branch
spots.desc: Under the slogan of "Frugal Price! Fresh Mart!", N Mart purchases selected foods and various foods from the mountain area to provide them at an affordable price and fresh taste. It is a shopping space that sells agricultural and fishery products, processed foods, daily necessities, and large-capacity food materials.

spots.name: Hongseong Traditional Market
spots.desc: Hongseong Market is a traditional market in the center of Hongseong, and is known for its long history as a place to purchase local specialties. In particular, it is a popular place for people looking for local specialties such as Hongseong Korean beef, kimchi, and salted fish.

spots.name: Gwangcheon Traditional Market
spots.desc: This traditional market offers fresh agricultural products, seafood, and a variety of local specialties to local residents and tourists. This market is especially famous for its mineral caves. Gwangcheongul Cave is an oyster grown in a clean area, and it is popular with people looking for fresh and delicious oysters.

spots.name: Chung-Mu-Jip
spots.desc: A restaurant known for soup with ox head meat (soup with beef head broth) and traditional Korean-style handmade noodle soup (kalguksu).

spots.name: The Hobong
spots.desc: A bakery where you can wake up early in the morning and taste new bread by kneading it.

spots.name: Hongseong Headquarters of Observatory Hoyeosusan Mountain
spots.desc: Located in Namdang Port, Observatory Hoesusan is a view restaurant that boasts fresh seafood dishes and a clean environment, and you can enjoy a romantic meal while enjoying the sunset. It has a public parking lot and a clean bathroom, and offers a variety of seafood such as prawns, gizzard, and webfoot octopus. It is famous for its 30-year tradition and media exposure, and is loved as…

spots.name: Gwangcheon Hanbat Restaurant
spots.desc: Located in Gwangcheon Traditional Market, it is close to walking from Gwangcheon Station and is a restaurant visited by many hikers after hiking Oseosan Mountain.

spots.name: Midang Hanwoo
spots.desc: It is a Hongseong Korean beef restaurant recognized as a 100-year store by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups. Raw galbi, which is sold only every day, is the signature.

spots.name: Dongbaeghoesusan
spots.desc: It is located in Namdang Port, Hongseong-gun, and has been selling prawns and clams for 30 years.

spots.name: Kkotji Beach
spots.desc: One of Taean's best-known beaches, famous for sunset views over its twin "Halmi-Harabae" rock formations.

spots.name: Mallipo Beach
spots.desc: A long, wide sand beach and one of Taean's most popular tourist beaches.

spots.name: Hagampo Beach
spots.desc: A quieter beach known for shellfish digging and coastal pine forest.

spots.name: Mongsanpo Beach
spots.desc: A beach known for its wide tidal flats, popular for family visits and mudflat activities; officially listed as one of the "Taean Eight Scenic Views".

spots.name: Taeanhaean National Park
spots.desc: A national park stretching along Taean's coastline, encompassing 26 beaches, coastal sand dunes, rock formations, and 72 islands.

spots.name: Sinduri Coastal Dune
spots.desc: A large coastal sand dune system designated as a Natural Monument of South Korea.

spots.name: Sinjindo
spots.desc: A small island connected to the mainland by bridge near Anheung, with fishing harbours and coastal views.

spots.name: National Taean Maritime Relics Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: A national museum displaying artifacts recovered from shipwrecks off Taean's coast, including Goryeo-era ceramics.

spots.name: Anheung-jinseong Fortress
spots.desc: A Joseon-era coastal military fortress, designated a national historic site (Sajeok).

spots.name: Gonam Shell Mound Museum
spots.desc: A museum on Anmyeondo about the Neolithic shell mounds of the area. It shows more than 470 prehistoric items, including Neolithic comb-pattern pottery and Bronze Age plain pottery. Opened in 2002.

spots.name: Oil Spill Recovery Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A memorial hall about the 2007 oil spill and the roughly 1.23 million volunteers who helped with the recovery. It opened in September 2017 and has an exhibition hall and a video experience room.

spots.name: Haebyeon Trail
spots.desc: A coastal walking trail in seven courses, from Hagampo in the north to Yeongmok Port in the south. The courses are Bara-gil (10.2 km, about 4 hours), Sowon-gil (22 km, about 8 hours), Pado-gil (9 km, about 3 hours), Solmoraet-gil (13 km, about 4 hours), Noeul-gil (12 km, about 3 hours 40 minutes), Saetbyeol-gil (13 km, about 4 hours), and Baram-gil (16 km, about 5 hours). Noeul-gil ends at Kkotji…

spots.name: Solhyanggi Trail
spots.desc: A coastal pine-forest trekking trail running along Taean's shoreline in several courses, popular for hiking.

spots.name: Sinduri Dune Ecological Trekking
spots.desc: Guided or self-guided walking trails through the protected Sinduri sand dune ecosystem, one of the "Taean Eight Scenic Views".

spots.name: Anmyeondo Recreational Forest Walk
spots.desc: Walking trails through a pine forest recreational area on Anmyeondo island.

spots.name: Mongsanpo Mudflat Experience
spots.desc: Guided tidal-flat (getbol) experience program for digging clams and observing coastal ecology.

spots.name: Jinsan-ri Fishing Village Shellfish Digging
spots.desc: A fishing-village experience center offering clam-digging programs for visitors.

spots.name: Eoeundol Beach Clam Digging
spots.desc: A tidal clam-digging activity near Mallipo, popular with families.

spots.name: Surfing at Mallipo Beach
spots.desc: Mallipo's open coastline and waves, nicknamed "Mallipornia", make it one of the west coast's only dedicated surfing spots.

spots.name: Taean Gadeuk (Taean Local Food Market)
spots.desc: An online market for Taean's farm products, seafood, meat, and processed foods. The website is in Korean.

spots.name: Solbat Garden
spots.desc: Blue crab stew (kkotgetang) is its listed specialty. Listed by Taean County as a model restaurant.

spots.name: Dami Hoetjip
spots.desc: Raw fish restaurant, with rockfish (ureok) as its listed specialty. Listed by Taean County as a model restaurant.

spots.name: Deungdae Hoetjip
spots.desc: Raw fish restaurant near Sinjin Port. Listed by Taean County as a model restaurant.

spots.name: Daeu Sikdang
spots.desc: Serves stone-pot rice (dolsotbap). Listed by Taean County as a model restaurant.

spots.name: Namunjeong
spots.desc: Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) restaurant in the county seat. Listed by Taean County as a model restaurant.

spots.name: Dalmaji Hill
spots.desc: This is regarded as Busan's 'romantic road', and climbs a hill overlooking the sea. It is often called the Montmartre of Busan by locals, although the two locations only share the attributes of being romantic and on a hill. The majority of visitors are couples of all ages looking for a romantic experience. Along the way there are many galleries and at the top there are viewing areas, cafes, as…

spots.name: MoonTan Road (문탠로드)
spots.desc: This is a nice forested walk along the sea coast on Dalmaji Hill with an impressive lookout in the middle. At night time the path is lit up.

spots.name: Busan Museum of Art
spots.desc: Contains three art galleries of modern art (one being for children). You can probably feel pretty good about spending 2-3 hours here and feel like you've seen it all. Closed every Monday and January 1st. In case Monday is a national holiday then the museum is closed on the next day instead.

spots.name: Sengbulsa Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple and monastery located up Jangsan mountain. Good scenic views over Haeundae.

spots.name: Cheongsapo Fishing Village
spots.desc: Although not particularly remarkable compared to Heaundae and Songjeong beaches on eigher side, this village is remote and away from the crowds with some cafes and restaurants by the sea. You can walk here either along the Moontan Road (hilly), along the disused rail tracks (flat) or the Number 2 Orange/Blue minibus outside Jangsan station.

spots.name: Johyun Gallery
spots.desc: Art gallery with exhibitions of works by Korean and international artists. Lovely views over the Korea Strait.

spots.name: Spaland Centum City
spots.desc: Part of the Shinsigae mall, this spa is probably the most friendly/accessible spa for foreigners in Busan. It is directly on the Centum City subway station, making it very easy to get to. Signs and an Instruction leaflet are also provided in English. Unlike many other spas, there is a time limit of 4 hours here after which you would need to pay again. The quality of the spa facilities as well as…

spots.name: Haeundae Cruise Boat
spots.desc: This boat trip starts off at Haeundae’s Mipo Ferry Terminal and heads towards Oryuk-do Islets and the Igidae area. The shores of Igidae are composed of breathtaking views of fantastically shaped cliffs. This 1-hour boat trip offers great views of Busan Harbor. The boat ride can be very bumpy and there is no way off, so check the weather conditions if you feel sea sick easily!

spots.name: Hiking up Jangsan Mountain
spots.desc: If you are near Haeundae, then Jangsan mountain can provide a good day's hiking. There are military bases at the summit complete with minefields (Clearly marked and fenced off), and great views over Busan and on a clear day to Japan. A hike to the summit and back should take 3-4 hours. Hiking trails are not really well marked, even if you can read Korean script.

spots.name: Club 101
spots.desc: A yachting club with a variety of boats for the public to try out, including tours with a yacht (₩60,000+), a dash around the harbor on a jet boat (₩40,000), Glass bottom boat (₩60,000) and jet skis (₩250,000+)

spots.name: Vesta Spa
spots.desc: Korean sauna with separate levels for men and women. Very nice water and views over Haeundae beach. Somewhat out of the way, but if you are visiting Dalmaji road anyway then worth visiting.

spots.name: Bay 101 Yacht
spots.desc: Provides trips around Gwangan Bridge and beach in the neighboring area.

spots.name: Haeundae Market
spots.desc: A pedestrian street full of fresh food to buy and small restaurants to try out.

spots.name: Shinsegae Department Store
spots.desc: A department store with an interesting (albeit expensive) food hall in the basement. It has two cinemas, an ice rink and a large public spa. It is also the biggest department store in the world according to the Guinness World Book of Records.

spots.name: Lotte Department Store
spots.desc: A smaller department store right next to the Shinsegae Department Store. Has a decent cinema as well as a small animal zoo (free) on the top floor. The Kyobo book store is very large and has a large variety of Korean and English books.

spots.name: Kim Hee-dae Halmae Wonjo Gamasot Gukbap (Granny Kim Hee-dae's Original Cauldron Gukbap)
spots.desc: Gukbap is a hot bowl of rice and broth, and available in many of the old style restaurants in Heaundae market.

spots.name: Happy Salad Club
spots.desc: A great option if you're craving vegetables. 5 salad choices and a fruit salad for dessert.

spots.name: Lee Jae-mo Pizza
spots.desc: Lee Jae-mo Pizza is known as one of Busan’s representative pizza restaurants, so tourists visiting Busan are encouraged to stop by and try the Lee Jae-mo crust pizza. It’s cheaper than other places, and the cheese flavor is excellent, so I highly recommend trying it.

spots.name: Subyeon Choe-go Pork Soup, Millak Main Branch
spots.desc: There are several chain branches of Subyeon Choegoe Pork Soup, but this is the main branch, so you should go there to enjoy it at its best. The most famous dish is the pork jowl soup with rice, so please be sure to try it.

spots.name: Korea Red Ginseng Samgyetang Galbitang
spots.desc: Hot broths with either chicken or beef cooked with rice and the special Korean ingredient of Ginseng.

spots.name: Fingers & Chat
spots.desc: Really good fish and chips with fresh batter that you can eat outside by the sea. Very long queues on weekends. Also good coffee and ice cream.

spots.name: Artista
spots.desc: Mexican restaurant with a good reputation. Slightly out of the way, but has vegetarian options as well.

spots.name: Busan Etteun Godeungeo – Haeundae Main Branch
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant specializing in wood-fired grilled fish, including grilled mackerel and seasoned grilled mackerel. The fish is cooked in a wood-fired oven heated to over 500°C, and the restaurant also offers a self-service bar with a variety of Korean side dishes.

spots.name: Ventanas Grill Steak and Seafood
spots.desc: Novotel Ambassador, Haeundae. Steak, fresh seafood, premier wine. Sephia style interior design, cozy atmosphere, and ocean view.

spots.name: Cola Mercato
spots.desc: Decent Italian restaurant at the top of Dalmaji Hill with views over the ocean.

spots.name: Wolfhound Irish Pub & Restaurant
spots.desc: A proper pub serving a large variety of premium draft beers and western food. Great place for a mid week dinner and pint or to party on the weekends. Good mix of Koreans and westerners.

spots.name: F1963
spots.desc: A unique cultural complex built in a former wire factory. It features a popular bookstore (Yes24), a local brewery (Praha Pub), a Starbucks, and various exhibition spaces. A great place to relax and enjoy the modern, artistic atmosphere.

spots.name: Suyeong-gu Cultural Center
spots.desc: A community hub that hosts various performances, exhibitions, and cultural classes. It's a great place to experience local arts and culture.

spots.name: Namcheon-dong Cherry Blossom Street
spots.desc: A famous street lined with cherry blossom trees, creating a beautiful pink canopy in the spring. It's one of Busan's most popular spots for enjoying the cherry blossom season.

spots.name: A.R.S Pocha
spots.desc: A unique restaurant known for its seafood dishes and lively atmosphere. It offers a great view of the beach and bridge, making it a popular spot for both locals and tourists.

spots.name: Suyeong History Park
spots.desc: Suyeong History Park preserves the remains of the former Suyeong-eupseong fortress from the Joseon Dynasty. Informational signs explain the historical significance of the site.

spots.name: Suyeong paldo Market
spots.desc: A local market offering fresh produce, street food, and daily necessities. It provides insight into everyday life in Suyeong and is popular with residents.

spots.name: Namcheon Catholic Church
spots.desc: A well-known Catholic church in the Namcheon area, recognized for its architecture and role as a local religious center.

spots.name: Suyeong Riverside Cycling Path
spots.desc: A paved cycling and walking route along the Suyeong River, frequently used by locals for exercise and commuting.

spots.name: Gwangalli Night Market
spots.desc: A temporary night market operating during peak tourist seasons, featuring street food, snacks, and small craft vendors along the beachfront.

spots.name: Suyeong Mural Streets
spots.desc: A small urban regeneration project featuring murals and street art painted on residential walls, offering casual photo opportunities and quiet walks.

spots.name: Gwangalli Public Performance Area
spots.desc: An open beachfront space used for public performances, cultural events, and seasonal festivals. Visitors may encounter street performances or small-scale concerts depending on the event schedule.

spots.name: Suyeong Community Culture Plaza
spots.desc: A neighborhood public space used for small exhibitions, community events, and outdoor gatherings. Primarily serves residents but is accessible to visitors.

spots.name: Suyeong Cultural Center
spots.desc: A public cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, and local cultural events that are open to residents and visitors.

spots.name: Suyeong Fortress Gate Site
spots.desc: Archaeological remains marking the original gate location of Suyeong-eupseong, with signage explaining its historical role during the Joseon period.

spots.name: Gwangalli Marine Leisure Zone
spots.desc: A designated area offering seasonal marine leisure activities such as kayaking and paddleboarding, popular with visitors during summer months.

spots.name: Mangmi-dong Ceramic Street
spots.desc: A small cluster of ceramic studios and craft shops known among visitors interested in local arts and handmade goods.

spots.name: Namcheon Beach Park
spots.desc: Namcheon Beach Park is a scenic coastal park located at the edge of Gwangalli Beach. It is widely considered the best vantage point to view the Gwangan Bridge (Diamond Bridge) up close from a front-facing angle. The park features a well-paved walking and cycling path that connects to the main Gwangalli strip. In the spring, it is famous for being adjacent to the Namcheon-dong cherry blossom…

spots.name: Gwangalli Hoe Festival
spots.desc: A raw fish festival held annually in October. The event, which takes place on the sandy expanse of Gwangalli Beach, is a lively celebration of Busan's seafood culture. Visitors can participate in a variety of activities, including making hoe bibimbap and sushi, and even a raw fish-eating contest. The festival also features live music, cultural performances, and a spectacular fireworks show over…

spots.name: Busan Fireworks Festival
spots.desc: The Busan Fireworks Festival takes place every October along Gwangalli Beach, transforming the city's iconic shoreline into a dazzling spectacle of light and sound. Drawing millions of spectators each year, it stands as one of South Korea's premier autumn events. The festival is renowned for its large-scale pyrotechnics, which are launched from barges and platforms in the sea, creating a stunning…

spots.name: Gwangan Bridge Walk
spots.desc: Each year, the Gwangan Bridge is opened to the public for a walking festival. This unique event allows you to walk or run across Busan’s most famous landmark, an opportunity not available at any other time of the year. The walk offers spectacular, unobstructed views of the city skyline, Gwangalli Beach, and the vast ocean. It's a popular event for locals and a truly memorable experience for…

spots.name: Gwangalli Eobang Festival
spots.desc: A traditional fishing culture festival recreating Joseon-era coastal life with performances, seafood events, and hands-on cultural programs for visitors.

spots.name: Gwangalli Beach Yoga Program
spots.desc: Seasonal outdoor yoga sessions organized along Gwangalli Beach, open to visitors looking for wellness-focused seaside activities.

spots.name: Namcheon-dong Seasonal Street Market
spots.desc: Temporary street markets featuring local food, crafts, and small performances, occasionally organized during seasonal events.

spots.name: Gwangalli Beach Media Art Zone
spots.desc: A designated beachfront zone where digital lighting and media installations are periodically displayed, creating a modern night-time atmosphere for visitors.

spots.name: SUP and Water Sports
spots.desc: Gwangalli Beach is a hub for water sports, with stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) being the most popular activity. You can easily rent equipment and get lessons from one of the many rental shops along the beach. Paddle out onto the calm waters to get a unique perspective of the Gwangan Bridge and the Busan skyline. It's a great way to stay active, especially during the summer months. Kayaking and…

spots.name: Suyeonggang River Cruise
spots.desc: Take a leisurely cruise along the Suyeonggang River, which flows through the heart of the district. The tour offers a different perspective of Suyeong's scenic beauty, passing by the APEC Naru Park and under a series of beautiful bridges. It's a peaceful and relaxing activity, ideal for those who want to escape the crowded beach area and enjoy some tranquility. The riverbanks are well-maintained…

spots.name: Gwangalli Beach Busking
spots.desc: As the sun sets, Gwangalli Beach transforms into an outdoor stage for talented buskers. You can find musicians, dancers, and artists performing along the boardwalk, creating a lively and energetic atmosphere. The busking culture is a major part of Gwangalli's appeal, offering free entertainment and a chance to experience the local arts scene. Grab a coffee or a beer from a nearby cafe, find a…

spots.name: Gwangalli M-Drone Show
spots.desc: A must-see attraction on Gwangalli Beach is the spectacular M-Drone Show. Every Saturday, hundreds of synchronized drones light up the night sky, creating intricate shapes and animations above the Gwangan Bridge. The show features a different theme each week, often related to holidays, seasonal events, or cultural topics. It’s a futuristic and visually stunning performance that draws large crowds…

spots.name: Bike along the Suyeonggang River
spots.desc: For a more active and scenic experience, rent a bike and cycle along the well-maintained paths of the Suyeonggang River. The path offers a peaceful escape from the crowded beach area, with beautiful views of the river, lush greenery, and the city skyline in the distance. It’s a great way to explore the local neighborhoods and get some exercise. Bike rentals are widely available at and around APEC…

spots.name: Relax at a Beach Cafe
spots.desc: The streets facing Gwangalli Beach are lined with a diverse selection of cafes, each offering a unique atmosphere and, most importantly, a prime view of the ocean and bridge. From trendy, minimalist cafes to cozy, themed spots, there's a place for every mood. It's a quintessential Gwangalli activity to grab a coffee or a drink, sit by the window, and simply watch the world go by.

spots.name: Prop Shops (소품샵)
spots.desc: Walk down the charming streets behind Gwangalli Beach, and you'll discover a collection of unique, independently owned prop shops. These stores are a treasure trove for anyone looking for special, handcrafted souvenirs, whimsical stationery, charming interior decor, and one-of-a-kind accessories. Popular spots include This is Gwangalli for its local-themed items and Pink House for cute…

spots.name: Millak The Market (밀락더마켓)
spots.desc: A modern, multi-story cultural complex on the water with a stunning view of the Gwangan Bridge. It is a popular hangout spot with small shops, art galleries, and pop-up stores. The ground floor offers a selection of trendy fashion items, unique lifestyle goods, and local snacks.

spots.name: Millak Raw Fish Market (민락회센터)
spots.desc: For an authentic and truly local experience. On the first floor, you can select fresh seafood directly from the vendors, who are eager to show off their catch of the day. Once you've made your choice, you can take your purchase upstairs to one of the many restaurants where they will prepare the fish for you on the spot. It's the best way to enjoy Busan's famous fresh fish and seafood at a…

spots.name: Busan Gwangalli Market (부산광안리상설시장)
spots.desc: A traditional market that offers a glimpse into local life. While not as large as other famous markets, it's a great place to find fresh produce, local street food, and everyday goods at affordable prices.

spots.name: E-mart Suyeong Branch (이마트 수영점)
spots.desc: A large supermarket where you can find everything from groceries to electronics and household items.
spots.hours: Daily 10:00-22:00 (Check website for alternating closed days)

spots.name: Suyeong Paldo Market
spots.desc: This traditional market is less touristy than others and provides a vibrant glimpse into daily life in Busan. You can find everything from fresh produce and seafood to delicious street food and household goods. It's a great spot to grab a cheap and authentic meal.

spots.name: Olive Young Gwangalli
spots.desc: A popular health and beauty store for Korean cosmetics and daily necessities.

spots.name: Daiso Gwangalli
spots.desc: A large discount store selling household items and travel essentials.

spots.name: ABC Mart Gwangalli
spots.desc: A footwear and sportswear store offering international brands.

spots.name: Cheongchun Jogae Pocha Gwangan
spots.desc: A beloved seafood restaurant and izakaya-style eatery specializing in clams, shellfish, and grilled seafood. It’s a local favorite for late-night dining with cold drinks and lively social atmosphere close to Gwangalli Beach.

spots.name: Seokhwayeon Korean BBQ
spots.desc: A highly rated Korean barbecue restaurant in the Gwangalli area, known for generous portions of grilled meats and quality side dishes. The lively atmosphere and beachside location make it an excellent dinner choice after sightseeing or beach activities.

spots.name: Salmon Brothers
spots.desc: A highly rated casual restaurant focused on salmon and seafood bowls, sushi, and creative fish dishes. Often recommended for seafood lovers looking for a more modern menu near the beach.

spots.name: Obok Pork Soup
spots.desc: A long-established local restaurant serving pork soup, a Busan specialty, often recommended to visitors seeking affordable and authentic regional food.

spots.name: Millak Town Raw Fish Center
spots.desc: Busan is famous for raw fish ('회 Hway'), which the Koreans eat in the same style as bulgogi, namely topped with kimchi and gochujang and wrapped in a lettuce leaf. One of the best places to sample this is in a large brown building at the northern end of Gwangalli Beach. The first floor is the actual fish market and the floors above are packed with nothing but restaurants serving it up. This can…

spots.name: Four Season Raw Fish
spots.desc: The owner, Mr. Jun, speaks English, and ordering here is easy: it's either set A, B or C. Even Set A is huge, while C is extremely large. This is as real as it gets and dishes will include still-moving octopus tentacles and other stuff most Westerners would not be familiar with.

spots.name: Samho Fish Restaurant
spots.desc: A local favorite for fresh sashimi and traditional Korean seafood stews. Known for its high quality and authentic flavors, often featuring seasonal catches.

spots.name: Suyeong Dwaeji Gukbap
spots.desc: A classic Busan-style pork and rice soup. This restaurant is in the Suyeong Gukbap alley and is known for its deep, flavorful broth.

spots.name: Gaemijip (Gwangalli Branch)
spots.desc: A famous Busan chain specializing in 'Nak-Gop-Sae' (spicy octopus, beef intestine, and shrimp casserole). A hearty and spicy meal, perfect for sharing.

spots.name: Choryang Milmyeon (Suyeong)
spots.desc: A branch of one of Busan's most famous 'milmyeon' (wheat noodle) restaurants. Offers refreshing cold noodles, both spicy (bibim) and non-spicy (mul).

spots.name: Millak Kalguksu
spots.desc: A humble restaurant near Millak Port serving delicious handmade noodle soup (kalguksu) and pajeon (green onion pancake).

spots.name: Gwang-an-jip Dwaeji Galbi
spots.desc: A long-standing local favorite for charcoal-grilled pork ribs (dwaeji galbi). The atmosphere is lively and often packed with locals.

spots.name: La Bella Citta
spots.desc: An upscale Italian restaurant with a direct view of the Gwangan Bridge. Specializes in pasta, risotto, and steak.

spots.name: HQ Bar
spots.desc: A popular expatriate-run bar with a friendly atmosphere. Serves excellent Western pub food, including burgers, wings, and fish and chips. Great selection of craft beers.

spots.name: Burger Shop
spots.desc: A popular gourmet burger joint. Known for its juicy, handcrafted patties and fresh ingredients. Often has a line.

spots.name: Pizza By The Slice
spots.desc: A casual New York-style pizzeria selling large slices. A perfect late-night snack to grab and eat by the beach.

spots.name: Ola!
spots.desc: A lively Spanish tapas bar serving authentic dishes like gambas al ajillo and paella. Great atmosphere with sangria and wine, plus a good view.

spots.name: SOL Taphouse
spots.desc: A casual pizza and pub-style restaurant serving pizzas, craft beers, and light dishes. With its beachfront proximity, it’s a popular evening gathering spot for travelers and locals.

spots.name: Tontaro
spots.desc: A cozy, authentic Japanese izakaya specializing in yakitori (grilled skewers) and various small dishes. Pairs well with sake or beer.

spots.name: Bangkok in Busan
spots.desc: Authentic Thai food restaurant run by a Thai chef. Popular for its Pad Thai and Tom Yum Goong.

spots.name: Hanoi Phở
spots.desc: A simple, no-frills Vietnamese restaurant serving excellent pho (beef noodle soup) and banh mi. Quick, delicious, and affordable.

spots.name: Little Aus Cafe
spots.desc: Australian-style cafe with variations on brunch and lunch classics.

spots.name: Cafe Lunar
spots.desc: A very popular cafe on the main beach road, famous for its multi-story glass windows offering unobstructed views of the bridge. Great for coffee and elaborate desserts.

spots.name: Byul-Swae Cafe
spots.desc: A "newtro" (new-retro) style cafe known for its quiet atmosphere and specialty hand-drip coffee.

spots.name: Namcheon-dong Bap-ppang
spots.desc: A bakery known for its savory breads (like onion or corn bread) and freshly baked goods. A local favorite for breakfast.

spots.name: Terarosa Coffee Gwangalli
spots.desc: A well-known specialty coffee café directly facing Gwangalli Beach, popular with tourists for high-quality coffee and clear views of Gwangan Bridge both during the day and at night.

spots.name: Paul Bassett Gwangalli
spots.desc: A premium café brand offering espresso-based drinks in a comfortable setting, often used by tourists as a rest stop while walking along the beachfront.

spots.name: Café Knotted Gwangalli
spots.desc: A popular dessert café known for its donuts and colorful interior, frequently visited by tourists and younger visitors walking along Gwangalli Beach.

spots.name: Sangjokam County Park
spots.desc: A coastal county park in Deokmyeong-ri, Hai-myeon, within Hallyeohaesang National Park. Dinosaur footprints are clearly visible in the flat rocks along the shore and can be seen on a walk along the coast. Namildae Beach is nearby.

spots.name: Danghangpo Tourist Site
spots.desc: Opened in 1987 on the bay where Admiral Yi Sun-sin won the Battle of Danghangpo, this waterfront park is the main venue of the Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo, Korea's first natural history expo. Facilities include marine leisure activities, pensions and an auto-camping site.

spots.name: Donghwa Fishery Village
spots.desc: A working fishing village where visitors can dig for clams on the tidal flats, join a torch-lit outing to catch octopus and live prawns, gather sea snails (godung), or go out on a small motorized fishing boat, in addition to walking a coastal trail. Nearby Mongdol Beach offers a range of marine life and views over Hallyeosudo (Hallyeo Waterway). In the middle of the village stand the remains of…

spots.name: Goseong Museum
spots.desc: The county museum, which grew out of the Sogaya Antiquities Exhibition Hall, covers the history and cultural heritage of Goseong, including objects excavated from the neighboring Songhak-dong Tumuli. It also holds special exhibitions.

spots.name: Hakdong Village Old Stone Walls
spots.desc: A village founded by the Choe clan around 1670, known for lanes lined with walls of thin flat stones layered with clay. Several old family houses survive, and bamboo groves surround the village. Free parking.

spots.name: Grace Garden
spots.desc: A private garden opened in June 2020 after some 15 years of planting, with a wide variety of trees. Keep your admission ticket — showing it at the on-site café gets you a free drink. A valid ID or other proof is required for any discounted or free admission (child, senior, disability, national merit, or Goseong-gun resident); without it, the standard rate applies.
spots.price: ₩6,000-10,000 (adults ₩10,000; teens, adult groups, seniors 65+, people with disabilities, and national merit…

spots.name: Manhwa Bangcho
spots.desc: A privately run garden with walking paths through flowerbeds and woodland, kept close to its natural state.

spots.name: Dino Ostrich Land
spots.desc: A large ranch where visitors can see and feed ostriches and other farm animals; popular with families.
spots.hours: Fri-Sun 10:00-18:00, also open on public holidays

spots.name: Goseong Ogwangdae Training Center
spots.desc: Home of Goseong Ogwangdae, a satirical masked dance drama recognized as a National Intangible Heritage. Performances and hands-on mask-dance programs are held here; contact the center for the current schedule. The Goseong Mask Museum is nearby.

spots.name: CGV Goseong
spots.desc: A small, county-operated cinema run on consignment with CGV — the only movie theater in Goseong-gun. Two screens, opened October 2020.

spots.name: Goseong Market
spots.desc: The county's main market, selling fresh seafood from the south coast along with local produce and Goseong rice. Busiest on market days.
spots.hours: Varies by shop; the traditional five-day market is held on dates ending in 1 and 6

spots.name: A very good restaurant
spots.desc: Home-style Korean set meals, with a menu that changes daily.

spots.name: Wang-chang-I
spots.desc: A family-run restaurant serving briquette-grilled gochujang (red pepper paste) bulgogi since the mid-1990s; good value.
spots.price: Hot red pepper paste bulgogi set cooked with briquettes: ₩12,000

spots.name: Dr. Jajang
spots.desc: A Korean-Chinese restaurant designated as a model restaurant (모범음식점). Jajangmyeon and jjamppong are the staples, and kkansho shrimp (sweet chili shrimp) is the specialty.

spots.name: Sura Korean table d'hote
spots.desc: A hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hôte) restaurant serving set meals with a wide spread of side dishes.
spots.price: Korean table d'hote ₩13,000, Sura Korean table d'hote ₩18,000, Sura Special Korean table d'hote ₩40,000

spots.name: Pungnyeonok
spots.desc: A local favorite for kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup), including versions with scallops or battered pan-fried meat, featured on KBS1's "Korean Table" (한국인의 밥상) in December 2021.

spots.name: A large mainland family
spots.desc: Set meals of soy-sauce-marinated crab (ganjang-gejang) and marinated scallops, made with local seafood.
spots.price: Soy Sauce Marinated Crab Set Menu ₩27,000, a scallop-jang set ₩17,000

spots.name: Dino-gogi Shrimp
spots.desc: Grilled shrimp sold by the kilogram at the daily market price, with domestic pork belly also on the menu.
spots.price: Shrimp at market price per kg; domestic pork belly ₩11,000 per 150 g

spots.name: Seomjin Freshwater Eel
spots.desc: Freshwater eel grilled with salt, with sauce, or with a deodeok (mountain root) seasoning.
spots.price: grilled salted freshwater eel ₩28,000, Freshwater eel with one sauce ₩33,000, Freshwater Eel Deodeok Seasoning Grilled…

spots.name: A spoonful of sunshine by the sea
spots.desc: A seaside restaurant serving pizza, pasta and steak, certified by the Naples Pizza Artisan Association.
spots.price: Grilled pork neck for grilled beef steak ₩24,000, Putanesca oil pasta ₩16,000, Basil Pesto Pasta ₩18,000, Sweet pumpkin…

spots.name: Dyunggari Cafe
spots.desc: A panoramic-view cafe inside the Goseong Dinosaur Museum complex overlooking Jaran Bay, accessible without paying museum admission. Try the dinosaur-shaped cookie or the waffle.

spots.name: Gogokjeong
spots.desc: A two-story hanok-style bakery cafe with ocean-view outdoor seating overlooking the coast, popular for photos. Serves coffee (including cream coffee, black sesame latte, matcha latte) and baked goods.
spots.hours: Tu-Sa 11:00-21:00 (last order 20:30); Su 11:00-19:00 (last order 18:30); closed Mo

spots.name: House of Choi Champan
spots.desc: A restored 19th-century manor featured in the epic Korean novel Toji (“The Land”) by Park Kyung-ni. The complex consists of over a dozen hanok buildings set above the vast rice fields of Pyeongsari Village. It recreates the lifestyle of a Joseon-era gentry family and also served as the filming location for the Toji TV drama. The site overlooks the Seomjin River, offering visitors a blend of…

spots.name: Hadong Wild Tea Museum
spots.desc: Located near the famous Hadong tea fields, this museum showcases Korea’s 1,200-year-old wild tea tradition. It offers exhibits on tea history and culture, along with hands-on experiences like roasting tea leaves and participating in a traditional tea ceremony. A relaxing and educational stop for tea enthusiasts exploring Hadong.

spots.name: Simni Cherry Blossom Road
spots.desc: A picturesque 4-km road lined with over 1,200 cherry trees, connecting Hwagae Market to Ssanggyesa Temple. Known as “Wedding Road,” it is one of Korea’s most romantic springtime destinations. During early April, the Hwagae Cherry Blossom Festival fills the area with food stalls, music, and photo spots under pink flower tunnels.
spots.addr: Road between Hwagae Market and Ssanggyesa Temple, Hwagae-myeon

spots.name: Haetteul Ranch
spots.desc: Haetteul Ranch is a family-friendly dairy farm in the foothills of Jirisan. Visitors can try feeding cows, bottle-feeding calves, milking, or making ice cream. Fresh milk and homemade dairy snacks are available on site, making it a hit with children and families.
spots.price: No admission fee; costs depend on the activities or snacks chosen

spots.name: Hwagae Market
spots.desc: A traditional market bridging Gyeongsang and Jeolla provinces, famous for green tea, persimmons, and folk culture. Immortalized in Korean songs and stories, Hwagae Market remains a living piece of regional heritage where visitors can still feel the charm of old Korea.

spots.name: Hadong Rail Bike
spots.desc: Pedal along a scenic rail track through Bukcheon-myeon, known for canola blossoms in spring and cosmos in autumn. The route offers calm countryside views and a fun activity for couples, friends, or families alike.

spots.name: Hadong Zipwire
spots.desc: Soar above the Seomjin River on one of Korea’s longest ziplines, offering stunning views and an adrenaline rush. Safety gear and staff guidance are provided, making it suitable even for beginners.
spots.price: Adults ₩45,000; youth ₩40,000; children ₩35,000 (half price for Hadong residents)

spots.name: Hadong Wild Tea Cultural Festival
spots.desc: Held every May in scenic Hwagae Valley, this signature event celebrates Korea’s oldest tea-growing region with tea-making, tastings, and traditional performances.

spots.name: Seomjingang Clam (Jaechup) Festival
spots.desc: Held in June, this summer festival highlights the Seomjin River’s famous freshwater clams with fishing events, live music, and water games.

spots.name: Bukcheon Cosmos & Buckwheat Flower Festival
spots.desc: In October, the fields of Bukcheon turn into a sea of pink and white as cosmos and buckwheat flowers bloom, drawing crowds of photographers and visitors from across Korea.

spots.name: Eat Hadong (Hadong Byeolmat) Festival
spots.desc: An autumn food festival featuring Hadong’s local specialties, markets, live performances, and creative dishes by regional chefs.

spots.name: Bamtoli Chestnuts
spots.desc: Hadong Bamtoli refers to premium-quality chestnuts grown in Hadong County, known for their large size, sweet flavor, and easy-to-peel shells. Cultivated in the clean natural environment near Jirisan Mountain and the Seomjin River, these chestnuts are widely appreciated across Korea. Visitors can buy fresh chestnuts directly from local markets or agricultural cooperatives, especially during the…
spots.price: The Chestnut Pie Set (6 pieces, ₩21,000), Chestnut Pie (₩3,600), and Chestnut Pie Set (9 pieces, ₩31,500) are popular…

spots.name: Hadong Honey Pear Liquor
spots.desc: Hadong Honey Pear Liquor is a traditional alcoholic beverage produced in Hadong. It is made from locally grown pears combined with natural honey, resulting in a mildly sweet flavor with a refreshing finish. The drink reflects the agricultural heritage of the region and is enjoyed both as a local specialty and as a souvenir for visitors.

spots.name: Hadong Green Tea
spots.desc: Hadong Green Tea is one of Korea’s most famous local specialties and a registered Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System by the FAO. The region’s tea fields along the Seomjin River have been cultivated for over 1,200 years using traditional hand-picking and pan-firing (deokkeum) methods. Visitors can buy premium loose-leaf teas ranging from high-end Ujeon to aromatic Sejak and enjoy tea…
spots.hours: Best enjoyed in spring harvest season (Apr–May)
spots.price: Varies by grade (Ujeon, Sejak, etc.) and by tea experience programs

spots.name: Hyesung Sikdang
spots.desc: A long-standing restaurant near Hwagae Market, well known for Seomjin River dishes like jaecheop-guk (clam soup) and chamge-tang (crab stew). Loved by travelers visiting Hwagae’s cherry blossom road and Ssanggyesa Temple.

spots.name: Jirisan Isima Shiitake Rice
spots.desc: Famous for rice cooked with locally grown shiitake mushrooms from Mt. Jiri. This restaurant emphasizes healthy, additive-free dishes and offers mushroom tea to guests. A peaceful place to enjoy traditional mountain food.

spots.name: Saebusan Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Located right by the water in Hadong’s Noryang area, Saebusan Hoetjip offers premium sashimi prepared from locally sourced seafood. It’s a popular stop for both travelers and residents, known for its friendly service, generous portions, and true taste of Korea’s southern coast.

spots.name: Seomjingang Fish Restaurant
spots.desc: A riverside restaurant specializing in freshwater fish and crab dishes from the Seomjin River. Popular for raw fish platters, chamge-tang (crab stew), and spicy stews enjoyed with scenic views of the river.

spots.name: Jangteo Gukbap
spots.desc: A countryside restaurant inside Pyeongsari Village known for sanchae-baekban (mountain-vegetable set meal) and grilled fish. Guests can dine overlooking rice fields and Jirisan’s foothills, making it perfect for those exploring Hadong’s literary and rural heritage.

spots.name: Haman Lotus Theme Park
spots.desc: Haman Lotus Theme Park is a nature-friendly theme park created by utilizing natural swamps of the old Gaya district. It was opened in 2013 to create an eco-friendly theme park that can attract tourists throughout the four seasons and improve the quality of life of the county by providing a unique resting place for Haman-gun residents and tourists visiting Haman. There is a story that goes back…

spots.name: Daepyeong Neup
spots.desc: A well-preserved natural freshwater wetland in Beopsu-myeon, known for its wide lotus fields, diverse aquatic plants, and tranquil scenery. The area is designated as Natural Monument No. 346 and serves as a habitat for migratory birds. A 1.9-km boardwalk trail allows visitors to explore the wetland up close without disturbing the ecosystem.

spots.name: Haman Bang-eosan Rock-carved Medicine Buddha Triad
spots.desc: The Bang-eosan Rock-carved Medicine Buddha Triad is a large rock-carved Buddhist sculpture created in 801 during the late Unified Silla period. Carved directly into a cliff on Mt. Bang-eo, the site features a central Medicine Buddha flanked by two attendant bodhisattvas.Unlike the idealized and highly dynamic Buddhist sculptures of the 8th century, this triad shows a more restrained and realistic…

spots.name: Goryeo-dong Archaeological Site
spots.desc: Goryeo-dong is a historic settlement where Yi O (李午), a jinsa (classical licentiate) of the Sungkyunkwan during the late Goryeo period, chose to reside after the fall of the Goryeo Dynasty and the establishment of the Joseon Dynasty, in order to remain loyal to the former state. From that time onward, his descendants have lived here continuously for generations.Yi O built a surrounding wall and…

spots.name: Aragaya Cultural Festival
spots.desc: The Haman Aragaya Cultural Festival showcases diverse historical and cultural content, re-examines the history and culture of Aragaya, and offers a rich festival experience with various themed performances and celebratory events. There is a history experience course where visitors can experience Aragaya firsthand, as well as horse-riding experiences, procession experiences, and various programs…

spots.name: Gangju Sunflower Festival
spots.desc: Free admission: Persons with disabilities, preschool children, seniors aged 70 and above, and residents of Beopsu-myeon. The festival features local agricultural product promotions, hands-on experience programs, and a variety of food stalls. A vast sunflower field of approximately 37,000 ㎡, created and maintained through the collective efforts of the residents of Gangju Village in Beopsu-myeon…

spots.name: Haman Persimmon Festival
spots.desc: Haman gotgam (dried persimmons) are rooted in the history of Ara Gaya and are widely known for their rich flavor and aroma. Throughout the Joseon Dynasty, they were presented as tribute to the royal court due to their exceptional quality. Held annually in mid-January. Among local varieties, Haman Susigam is relatively small in size compared to other persimmons, but when fully ripened its…

spots.name: Yeohangsan
spots.desc: Yeohangsan (770 m) is the main mountain of Haman. The name was given during the Joseon Dynasty by scholar Jeong Gu, who interpreted the mountain’s location in relation to the town from a geomantic perspective. The mountain has around seven major hiking routes, and it is visited throughout the year by both local and regional hikers.From the summit, there are wide views over Haman and, on clear…

spots.name: Haman Equestrian Park
spots.desc: Haman Equestrian Park is a public facility where visitors can experience horseback riding and interact with horses. The park offers beginner-friendly riding programs and hands-on activities, making it suitable for families and first-time riders.

spots.name: Haman Watermelon Festival
spots.desc: The festival marked its 31st edition in 2025.Exhibition events, including a promotional hall for outstanding local agricultural products and displays of entries from the 2nd National Watermelon CompetitionDirect sales market featuring watermelons, processed watermelon products, local agricultural specialties, and handicraftsHands-on activities such as watermelon-themed games, watermelon…

spots.name: Haman Bulppang Martin Bakery
spots.desc: Martin Bakery is known for producing Haman Bul-bbang, which won the Grand Prize at the Gyeongnam Tourism Souvenir Competition. The bakery also offers a "Hongsi Ade Making" experience, where visitors can try making a refreshing drink using ripe persimmons. It serves coffee and freshly baked bread, along with handmade juices and bakery items using local Haman specialties. Their signature item…

spots.name: Gaya Market
spots.desc: Haman’s largest traditional market. It operates as a permanent market, with regular market days on the 5th, 10th, 15th, 25th, and 30th of every month (and the 31st when applicable). The market first opened in 1974 and offers a wide range of goods, including fresh produce, seafood, processed foods, local snacks, clothing, and daily necessities.Public parking is available nearby.

spots.name: Urihanmadang
spots.desc: A really good duck restaurant that is popular with the locals. Really friendly owner too.

spots.name: OK Kukibwepe
spots.desc: This is a meat buffet kind of restaurant. Pick out the meat you want and grill it up. It's on the first floor below the duck restaurant.

spots.name: Konguinseongsik
spots.desc: This restaurant serves good side dishes with kimchi jjigae and dwenjang jjigae. They also have a nice fish soup. Bit nice if you don't want too much meat for a change.

spots.name: Daenamudong Samkeopsal
spots.desc: This is one of the best pork restaurants in town. They serve galbi tang (갈비탕) and yook gye jang (육게장) which is a spicy pork soup. Of course, their samgyeopsal is very good too.

spots.name: Daejang Bulgogi
spots.desc: Very popular restaurant in Gaya. Really good meat restaurant and has a nice Dwengajang jjigae.

spots.name: Modungi
spots.desc: The only place in Gaya that actually serves coffee and espresso. It is also a hof with pretty good side dishes.

spots.name: Hapcheon Video Theme Park
spots.desc: An outdoor film set recreating Korea from the 1920s to 1980s; popular for photography and filming locations. In the summer, it is operated as a ghost theme park, and many people dress up as ghosts and enjoy horror-themed events.

spots.name: Hapcheon Shin Soyang Sports Park
spots.desc: As a popular photo spot on SNS that many tourists visit every year, it is attracting attention as a representative tourist attraction in autumn. It is also a popular photo zone for many lovers as it is a place where you can take emotional photos as it is colored in deep pink every fall. You can see various autumn flowers such as yellow flower cosmos, Gujeolcho, and chrysanthemums, and run a pink…

spots.name: Hapcheon Garden Theme Park
spots.desc: You can see the set that makes the Blue House of the Republic of Korea the same. And you can ride a cable car from Hapcheon Video Theme Park. You can also see simple exhibits and take pictures as if you were at Cheong Wa Dae.

spots.name: Queen Hapcheon Market
spots.desc: With the traditional market feel, you can see and buy many kinds of food and goods. Also, the dates for the 3rd and 8th are called Jangnal, and there are more products and people.

spots.name: Forest of Life Park
spots.desc: It is a great place to take a walk with family or lovers. It is good to take a walk with the river breeze after eating at a nearby restaurant. There are also places for children to like, such as a playground and a basketball court, so it is good to visit for a family trip.

spots.name: Hapcheon Dam Water Culture Center
spots.desc: It provides information about the water and the role of Hapcheon Dam. And there is also an observation deck where you can see the beautiful view of Hapcheon Lake. It is a good place to go with your child.

spots.name: Tripitaka Koreana Theme Park
spots.desc: It is a theme park with the theme of the Palman Daejanggyeong of Haeinsa Temple, a World Heritage Site, and introduces the production and preservation process of Daejanggyeong through various exhibitions and experiences.There are 4D theaters, printing experience centers, and Janggyeong Panjeon models, so it is good to visit with children.There are souvenir shops and cafes near the ticket office…

spots.name: Safety Experience Center
spots.desc: Visitors can enjoy various hands-on education programs, exhibitions, and events ranging from disaster safety experiences such as earthquakes and storm and flood damage to first aid. Also, it vividly conveys experiences and examples of field activities that firefighters have experienced at various accident sites. It is a good place to go with children.

spots.name: Jeongyang Wetland Ecological Park
spots.desc: An ecological learning center, Jeongyang Wetland Life Path, and Observation Deck have been established in the ecological park, and the Jeongyang Wetland Ecological Learning Experience Center is operated. It has been reported as a wetland with excellent natural scenery, habitat for a variety of animals and plants, and very high biological and ecological preservation values. The Jeongyang Wetland…

spots.name: Hapcheon Museum
spots.desc: This place offers visitors a chance to learn about Hapcheon's history and traditional culture. The museum also includes life-sized tombs of Dara-guk, Dara-guk's capital city, miniature images and other video materials. It takes about one hour to watch.

spots.name: Hwanggye Falls
spots.desc: If you walk from the parking lot to the waterfall, you'll arrive in 5 minutes. It's a good place to heal while watching the waterfall. You don't have to walk a lot, so it's good to go with the elderly.

spots.name: Jeongyang Leports Park
spots.desc: In summer, there is a place where you can play in the water while enjoying the Hapcheon Vacation Festival at Hapcheon Jeongyang Leports Park. There are many cases where families come with children, and there is a water play where adults can also enjoy it lightly. In addition, there is a camping site, so it is good to play in the water during the day and have a barbecue party in the evening.

spots.name: Full Heaven Water World
spots.desc: Flyboat, hurricane, bandwagon, disco pang pang, peanut boat, pang pang, sightseeing boat, Marvel, banana boat, water skiing, and more. You can also use various and wide auxiliary facilities such as storage, dressing room, shower room, cafeteria, sunbed zone, and food court.

spots.name: Hapcheon Cherry Blossom Marathon
spots.desc: In March, the Hapcheon Marathon is held. There are usually about 3,000 participants and it is good to run while looking at the cherry blossoms. In the middle of the road, there are people who cheer and people who play traditional musical instruments.

spots.name: Big Korean Famous House Main Store
spots.desc: It is the healthiest and freshest Korean beef in Hapcheon, with ribs, sirloin, beef brisket, and juicy beef from special parts

spots.name: Sun grandmother's hand-cooked noodles
spots.desc: This kalguksu restaurant specializes in kalguksu, which only sells hand-pressed kalguksu. You can eat traditional kalguksu, noodle soup with perilla seeds, and Umnamu chicken kalguksu.

spots.name: BBanggu
spots.desc: It is a famous pork restaurant. During lunch time, you can eat kimchi stew with a lot of meat. The unique thing is that they give me pineapples to grill.

spots.name: The nengmyun with jjukkkumi (Cold buckwheat noodles)
