spots.name: A village of dried pollack
spots.desc: Spicy and sweet steamed pollack is a delicious restaurant. If you order a large size, it can be eaten by four people. Also, bean sprouts and tofu from steamed pollack are really delicious. Especially, it is best to add ramen noodles after you are done. But adding sauces is only possible on weekdays. After you finish eating, it is good to go for a walk there or to the cafe next door. It is right…

spots.name: Her delicious recipe
spots.desc: It is a Western restaurant that sells everything from snack food to pork cutlet and pasta. The main menu includes handmade pork cutlet, kimchi fried rice, cream pasta, tomato pasta, and gorgonzola pizza.

spots.name: yukmyeon
spots.desc: It usually sells naengmyeon and galbitang. Naengmyeon is delicious because it has meat pancakes on it. Besides that, you can also eat bulgogi.

spots.name: Braised Jumbo Codfish Head
spots.desc: Braised cod pollack is spicy and sweet and delicious with rice.
spots.price: Large size of cod pollack stew ₩50,000

spots.name: A central meat restaurant
spots.desc: It is cheap and delicious. Especially, the rice soup is very cheap, but it contains a lot of meat.

spots.name: Low pool
spots.desc: Hapcheon Dam View Low Pool Large Cafe. It has a pink exterior and a lake in front of it, so it's good to take pictures.

spots.name: Smilda
spots.desc: A small and cozy hanok house in the countryside alley, drinks, desserts, and small hobby classes. Rice latte, a popular menu, is popular for savory grain flavors and additional shot options, and various drinks such as matcha cream strawberry latte and ginger latte are available.

spots.name: Cafe on
spots.desc: Enjoy fresh coffee made with blended beans at Cafeon with mood music that gives you peace and rest in a comfortable sensual space like your own home. The interior is neat, so it's good to go.

spots.name: Cafe Flora
spots.desc: It is a cafe right next to the Hapcheon Dam and you can see the Hapcheon Dam inside the cafe. It is a good place to relax with calm music playing.

spots.name: Cafe Gdamae
spots.desc: It is in front of Hapcheon Jeongyang Leports Park and has a lawn yard. It has a view of the river running in the park right in front. It is recommended for families and couples as you can walk around the white sand and the park.

spots.name: DaeHan DaWon Boseong Green Tea Fields
spots.desc: Daehan Dawon is the largest green tea plantation in Boseong and a popular tourist attraction. Visitors can stroll through the picturesque tea fields, relax in traditional Korean pavilions, and enjoy tea tastings at the on-site tea houses.
spots.price: ₩4,000 adults; ₩3,000 seniors (65 and older), military personnel, ₩3,000 youth; free: children under 6 years old

spots.name: Yulpo Beach
spots.desc: For a change of scenery, head to Yulpo Beach, known for its scenic beauty and calm waters. It is a place where many people enjoy leisurely swimming or beach picnics. The nearby Yulpo Ocean Park offers additional recreational activities and a glimpse into the local fishing culture.

spots.name: Korean Tea Museum
spots.desc: The Korean Tea Museum, located in close proximity to the largest tea fields in Korea, which aim to promote the beautiful tea capital of Boseong, is the largest domestic tea museum in South Korea. It serves as a dedicated museum for all things related to tea, with rich content, and plays a central role in establishing, researching, and promoting tea culture correctly. The Korean Tea Museum is…

spots.name: Jeaam Mountain Nature Recreation Forest
spots.desc: The recreation forest features facilities such as forest cabins, a campground, outdoor classrooms, hiking trails, walking paths, fitness facilities, a youth square, grassy areas, a water play area, and a children's playground. Additionally, there are deer and wild boar breeding facilities in the vicinity known as the "Joosu Breeding Grounds." Nearby, you can also find the Yongchu Waterfall and an…

spots.name: Bibong Dinosaur Egg Fossil Site
spots.desc: This mineral from the Stone Age was designated as a natural monument on April 28, 2000. It's an ideal place for a seaside stroll, with Bibong Dinosaur Park and Bibong Dinosaur Museum a 6-minute drive away, making it a great destination for exploring both mineral and dinosaur-related attractions.

spots.name: Borimjeddah
spots.desc: Borim Jeddah offers a variety of different experiences including a tea making experience, 1-day branding tea making, green tea flower wine making, and tea ceremony experience programs. The green tea experience program, which has been held since 1998, has received a lot of love and interest as a customized experience program specialized not only for adults but also for students, children, and…

spots.name: Botjae
spots.desc: Botjae is closed every Monday, Lunar New Year and Chuseok, Botjae is a complex tourism facility, and a historical and cultural center where you can experience Boseong's history and culture is painted on the first floor, and a green market and cafeteria where you can buy specialties are drawn on the second floorOn the third floor, there is a museum emptying room where you can experience nature. It…

spots.name: Forest Garden Yun Jerim
spots.desc: Forest Garden Yun Jerim is a place where you can enjoy beautiful forest gardens, and it is especially famous for attractions where you can see hydrangeas from many countries. In addition, you can enjoy a variety of beautiful plants such as irises, willows, cypress forests, and pink muhly. At the forest healing center in the garden, various experiences such as foot baths and lower body baths are…
spots.price: ₩6,000 adult, ₩5,000 youth, ₩4,000 child (3-7 years old), ₩2,000 guest

spots.name: Healing Pack
spots.desc: Healing pack sells Boseong souvenirs related to various green tea, and operates a one-day class to experience it in person. Handmade souvenirs are also available.

spots.name: Bibong Dinosaur Park
spots.desc: Boseong Bibong Dinosaur Park is a dinosaur theme park in South Korea that opened in July 2017. The park has two floors, including a basement level, with a Dino Cafe and Dino Shop offering dinosaur souvenirs. The exhibition hall displays real dinosaur bone fossils from Boseong and provides information about geological periods and Asian dinosaur fossils. There are displays of Tyrannosaurus and…
spots.price: Weekend: ₩13,000 adult, ₩12,000 youth, ₩11,000 child; weekdays: ₩6,000 adult, ₩5,000 youth, ₩4,000 child

spots.name: Deukryang Station Memory Street
spots.desc: The Deukryang Station Memory Street is a place where Deukryang Station, which was on the verge of closure, has been transformed into a street of memories showcasing the old Korea through cultural tourism projects. You can explore everything from retro murals to props representing that era, old-style cafes, and even a supermarket filled with items from the past. Additionally, you can rent vintage…

spots.name: Green tea hotteok
spots.desc: A seed hotteok shop made with green tea. Due to its popularity, it sometimes closes due to the exhaustion of ingredients around 3-4.

spots.name: Boseong Green Tea Tteokgalbi Original
spots.desc: Soft green tea Tteokgalbi is famous. There are also waitings by appearing on various broadcast programs. assorted tteok-galbi.

spots.name: Mother Corkle
spots.desc: Mother Corkle is operated by an elderly couple as a home-style restaurant made by renovating a house. Pork cutlet and curry are prepared, and you can also eat cockle bibimbap during the cockle season.
spots.price: Cockle Bibimbap ₩13,000, Fresh Pork Cutlet ₩12,000, Today's Curry, ₩12,000

spots.name: Daewonjeong
spots.desc: Daewonjeong is known for its signature menu, the Cockle Set Meal. Included in the set meal is also the sashimi of flounder, which is another favorite among visitors.

spots.name: Green step
spots.desc: Green step is a spacious Western restaurant with a good atmosphere. There is a Western menu with a variety of green tea, such as green-don pasta and green-don pork cutlet.

spots.name: Mori's bakery
spots.desc: Mori's bakery is a bakery selling healthy bread. There are breads that come out by time, so if you want to buy fresh bread before it's sold out, you have to visit on time. Hongguk rice bread is famous.

spots.name: Chun-un Seo-ok
spots.desc: Chun-un Seo-ok is a forest hanok cafe with a good atmosphere, and there are seats in the cave next to the cafe. A wide variety of seats and desserts are prepared.

spots.name: Korea Gasa Literature Collection
spots.desc: The Korean History Literature Museum opened on November 11, 2000, in Gasa Literature-myeon, Damyang-gun, Jeollanam-do, and continues to hold various academic events for the transmission, preservation, and modern succession and development of cultural heritage related to Gasa Literature.
spots.hours: Nov-Feb: daily 09:00-17:00; May-Oct: daily 09:00-19:00; Mar Apr: daily 09:00-18:00

spots.name: Dambit Art Storage
spots.desc: This gallery was renovated from old grain storage. You can see and buy artworks created by young artists in Jeolla. A cafe is connected to this place, and you can listen to music played on a pipe organ made from bamboo here.

spots.name: Sigyeongjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Sikyeongjeong Pavilion was built by Kim Seong-won (1525-1597), Seohadang, in the 15th year of King Myeongjong of the Joseon Dynasty, and was named "Sikyeong" by his father-in-law Im Eok-ryeong (1496-1568). Here, Jeong Cheol (1536-1593) left Chinese poems, lyrics, and unit songs such as Seongsan Byeolgok and Sikyeongjeong 20yeong, and became the birthplace of Songgang Literature, and laid the…

spots.name: Songganjeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Songgangjeong Pavilion is a pavilion where Songgang Jeongcheol (1536-1593) stepped down from the court and stayed quiet for four years. It was designated as Jeollanam-do Monument No. 1 on January 29, 1972.

spots.name: Sangwoljeong Pavilion
spots.desc: Sangwoljeong Pavilion was built by Kim Ja-su in the third year of King Sejo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty and returned to his hometown. In the 8th year of King Sunjo (1808), Yeonjae and Chojeong were repaired, but in the 2nd year of King Cheoljong (1851), Ko Jae-jun and Ko Gwang-jo were repaired due to flood damage, and rafters and beams were repaired in the 9th year of King Cheoljong (1858). The…

spots.name: Gwaneojeong Pavilion
spots.desc: In the late Joseon Dynasty, the caretaker of Damyang built a pavilion here to enjoy the atmosphere and wind and moon. Since the water of Damyangriver Stream flows under the pavilion, you can sit here to fish or watch fish.

spots.name: Doksujeong Pavilion
spots.desc: The name Eaglejeong Pavilion is derived from the poem of Lee Tae-baek and contains the noble meaning of a scholar living in seclusion. The name Doksujeong Pavilion is derived from the poem of Lee Tae-baek and represents the noble meaning of a scholar who lives quietly.

spots.name: Myeongokhean Garden
spots.desc: It has a pavilion and an artificial pond. Zinnia trees surrounding the pond are famous.

spots.name: Damyang City Tour Bus
spots.desc: It is a bus tour that takes an electric bus to visit various tourist attractions in Damyang. There are three routes: Downtown course, Lyrics Literature Course (Take time: 1 hour and 50 minutes), Damyang Lake Course (Take time: 1 hour and 20 minutes).
spots.price: Adult ₩2,000, child and 65 years of age or older ₩1,000

spots.name: Chuwol Mountain Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: It is a cherry blossom festival held in April at Chuwol Mountain, a representative tourist destination in Damyang, and you can feel the scent of spring. [April, Biennial].

spots.name: Damyang Bamboo Festival
spots.desc: It is the only bamboo festival in Korea, and is Damyang's representative festival where unique exhibitions, experiences, performances, and sales take place to sympathize with the various values and uses of bamboo. [early May].

spots.name: Goseo Grape Festival
spots.desc: Various events are held, including various experiences of picking grapes in the vineyard, making wine, various performances, and tasting and purchasing grapes. [Held for three days in August, biennial].

spots.name: Damyang Hanu Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival that provides various foods such as tasting and selling Korean beef (Hanu) so that consumers can trust and find Damyang Korean beef, which is raised in a clean area of Damyang. [Held for three days in September or October].
spots.addr: Culture Plaza in front of Juknokwon

spots.name: Changpyeong Traditional Food Festival
spots.desc: It is a festival where you can taste traditional food in one place, and it is a special festival unique to Changpyeong, which is rich in food such as rice candy making experience, Korean sweets making experience. [for three days at the end of October, Biennial].

spots.name: Damyang Santa Festival
spots.desc: It is a winter festival where you can feel Damyang's Christmas atmosphere with Christmas-related experiences such as large trees, photo zones, night lighting, carol music, and busking performances. [December 23rd to 25th].

spots.name: Street Tree Love Concert
spots.desc: It is a festival that creates and preserves Metasequoia street and celebrates history. It is Damyang's October festival that plays music suitable for autumn to those who visit Metasequoia street.

spots.name: Changpyeong Traditional Market
spots.desc: Changpyeong Traditional Market (창평 전통 시장), 14-24, Sadong-gil, Changpyeong-myeon. Local agricultural products and traditional foods, such as Korean sweets and rice yeot, are mainly sold here.

spots.name: Damyang Burger
spots.desc: It is a fusion restaurant that sells burgers made with tteogalbi, a traditional Korean food.

spots.name: Nokdong Bada Jeongwon

When you cross the bridge and enter the garden, the first large deer statue welcomes you. The sculpture, which shines in the sun, creates an exotic scene of Nokdong Sea Garden Bay on the sea Fish sculptures located everywhere…

spots.desc: After looking around the seven beautiful trails of Geogeumdo Island, there is a place you must go. It is Geogeum Ecological Forest. Located in Cheongseok Village at the bottom of Daejeombong Peak, the pillar of Geogeumdo Island, the ecological forest consists of various orchid forests like 回轉, an entrance to a new dimension or a revolving door that allows you to enter a world that changes time.…

spots.name: Maboksan Wood Culture Experience Center
spots.desc: The Maboksan Wood Culture Experience Center is home to 12,000 natural stones, 18,000 plants and trees, and has a general experience center, a traditional house experience center, a pavilion tree shelter, a garden of love, and a parking lot. As a forest recreation space where visitors can enjoy various experiences such as cypress spa, traditional hanok, and wood processing as well as appreciation…

spots.desc: It is a popular animal experience center in Namyang, located at the entrance of Goheung, where you can experience feeding. You can freely play with animals in nature, and you can play with various animals such as sheep, horses, crucian donkeys, rabbits, mini pigs, flower deer, foals, and black cattle. The appearance of fluffy sheep running around in the meadow can experience a time of healing…

spots.name: Parrot Experience Center
spots.desc: It is the only parrot farm with a safe and exotic garden registered as a zoo in Goheung, a place where urban people's "rest" and "recovery" (healing) are located, and a rural education farm designated by the Rural Development Administration. It is a space enjoyed by all generations as it provides experiential education suitable for the curriculum through a work agreement with the Office of…

spots.name: UZZA
spots.desc: A famous cafe that sells a variety of citron drinks, desserts, and accessories with its handmade citron syrup. Citron smoothies are popular in hot weather, and citron scones are enjoyed by many people due to their soft texture. The interior of the store is also decorated with a yellow atmosphere to match the citron.

spots.name: Grilled sincere eel charcoal
spots.desc: The eel of the sincere eel charcoal grill boasts a deep taste that cannot be felt in ordinary restaurants and serves customers with a special taste. Many customers are coming from outside, and we are trying to serve delicious eel properly to those who come.

spots.name: Train Village Rose Park
spots.desc: A rose garden associated with Seomjingang Train Village. It is known for its rose displays and seasonal flowers, especially during the rose-blooming season.

spots.name: Simcheong Story Village
spots.desc: A themed village inspired by the Korean folktale of Simcheong. The grounds feature traditional-style houses, sculptures and walking areas connected with the story.

spots.name: Seomjingang Goblin Village
spots.desc: A folklore-themed attraction based on Korean goblin legends. The village introduces visitors to traditional storytelling and local folklore through exhibits and activities.

spots.name: Taeansa Temple
spots.desc: A historic Buddhist temple set in a wooded valley. The temple grounds contain historic Buddhist monuments and offer a quiet setting for exploring the area's religious heritage and natural scenery.

spots.name: Seomjingang Chimsil Wetland
spots.desc: A wetland along the Seomjingang River known for its reed beds, willow trees, wildlife and misty riverside scenery. It is a good place to observe the local wetland ecosystem and enjoy the natural landscape.

spots.name: Daehwanggang Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: A 185-m pedestrian suspension bridge crossing the Daehwanggang River. It offers views of the river and surrounding woodland and provides access to nearby walking routes.

spots.name: Amnok Recreation Area
spots.desc: A riverside recreation area near the confluence of the Seomjingang and Daehwanggang rivers. Its broad riverbank and surrounding scenery make it a popular place to enjoy the outdoors.

spots.name: Seomjingang Rail Bike
spots.desc: Ride a pedal-powered rail bike along the former Jeolla railway beside the Seomjingang River. The route runs from Gajeong Station to a turnaround point near Bongjo and covers approximately 3.6 km round trip. Two-, three- and four-person options are available.
spots.price: Paid; check the official website for current fares

spots.name: Train Village Rail Bike
spots.desc: Cycle on a rail bike around a roughly 1-km circular track inside Seomjingang Train Village. Each bike accommodates up to four people, and one circuit takes 10-15 minutes. Tickets are generally available on site, subject to availability.

spots.name: Gokseong Zipline
spots.desc: Experience a zipline ride above the Seomjingang riverside landscape. The attraction offers an aerial view of the river and surrounding natural scenery. Check operating conditions and restrictions before your visit.
spots.price: Check the official website for current fares

spots.name: National Gokseong Healing Forest
spots.desc: Take part in forest-based wellness activities in a wooded area near Dongaksan Mountain. The forest uses the surrounding woodland, streams and other natural features for activities intended to support relaxation and well-being. Advance arrangements may be necessary for some programs.
spots.hours: Check the official website for program availability

spots.name: Seomjingang Train Village Dream Land
spots.desc: Seomjingang Train Village Dream Land is an amusement area located within Seomjingang Train Village. Visitors can enjoy various rides and entertainment activities, making it a suitable place for families and visitors looking for a fun break.

spots.name: The Road to Jirisan
spots.desc: A pork cutlet restaurant offering handmade cheese and loin cutlets, with views of the Seomjingang River.

spots.name: Cafe The Log & Log Cabin
spots.desc: A riverside cafe overlooking the Seomjin River, with an outdoor terrace and freshly baked goods. Try local specialties such as green plum mojitos, strawberry lattes, and sweet persimmon desserts.

spots.name: Jirisan Garden
spots.desc: There is a wildflower-themed park and native plant garden where visitors can observe diverse vegetation throughout the four seasons, as well as an ecological forest, natural recreation forest, and arboretum. The forest lodges, which offer a healing experience surrounded by nature, are especially popular.
spots.hours: March to October: 09:00 – 18:00 November to February: 09:00 – 17:00
spots.price: Adult ₩2,000, youth or soldier ₩1,500, child ₩1,000; group (20 or more): adult ₩1,600, youth or soldier ₩1,200…

spots.name: Surak Waterfall
spots.desc: Surak Waterfall, with a height of 15 meters, cascades between rugged rocks and offers stunning surrounding scenery, making it one of the ten most scenic spots in Gurye.The waterfall is famous as a "water-hitting waterfall," traditionally visited by local residents after rice planting and weeding to relieve back pain and neuralgia. Word spread that it could help with conditions such as neuralgia…

spots.name: Gurye Cornelian Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: The Gurye Cornelian Cherry Blossom Festival is a representative spring flower festival in South Korea, offering a chance to experience the essence of early spring. Cornelian cherry blossoms bloom earlier than other flowers in March, heralding the arrival of spring. The festival, themed around the flower's meaning—"eternal and unchanging love"—features various hands-on programs and musical…

spots.name: Gurye 300-ri Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: The Gurye 300-ri Cherry Blossom Festival is held along the 129 km of the nation's longest cherry blossom road in Gurye, Jeollanam-do. This festival embodies the dreams and hopes of the Gurye community, celebrating the harmony of nature, people, history, and culture, while showcasing the beauty and value of Gurye.

spots.name: Jirisan Namak Festival
spots.desc: The Jirisan Namak Festival is a traditional folk cultural event held annually around April 20th in Gurye, Jeollanam-do. Rooted in the Jirisan Mountain Deity Ritual, it features a variety of cultural programs, including traditional rites, performances, exhibitions, and community activities. The festival aims to honor the mountain spirit and promote local heritage and unity.

spots.name: Jirisan Piagol Autumn Foliage Festival
spots.desc: The Jirisan Piagol Autumn Foliage Festival is a celebration of the breathtaking autumn colors in Piagol Valley, renowned as one of the most beautiful fall destinations in South Korea. The valley is famous for its "Three Reds"—red leaves on the mountains (산홍), reflected in the streams (수홍), and on the people (인홍)—creating a stunning natural spectacle. The festival features various events…

spots.name: Hanaro Mart Gurye Livestock Cooperative Main Branch
spots.desc: It is the largest mart in Gurye, where you can purchase various food ingredients and different kinds of meat (including beef, pork, and chicken).

spots.name: Gurye 5-Day Market
spots.desc: A traditional market in Gurye that opens every five days, offering local produce, handmade goods, and regional specialties.

spots.name: Jirisan Outing Market
spots.desc: A local market near Jirisan, offering fresh produce, regional specialties, and a variety of goods for both visitors and locals.

spots.name: Sannamul Bapsang
spots.desc: Situated among Gurye’s major tourist attractions, it is a famous restaurant specializing in Korean cuisine.

spots.name: Gurye Station Waiting Room
spots.desc: Situated behind the Sinwol-ri Police Substation on the left after crossing the bridge, in a red brick building. A Western-style restaurant near Gurye Station, famous for its black pork cutlet and freshwater snail pasta.

spots.name: Mokwol Bakery
spots.desc: One of Gurye’s representative bakeries, featured on multiple TV programs, known for its healthy bread made with Gurye wheat and natural yeast.

spots.name: Seomjingang Dasulgi Restaurant
spots.desc: Seomjingang Dasulgi Restaurant is a hidden gem in Gurye that showcases the finest freshwater snail (dasulgi) dishes. The rich flavors of the seasoned dasulgi and the refreshing taste of dasulgi sujebi (hand-pulled dough soup) are particularly impressive, and the side dishes, including seasoned mung bean sprouts and spicy chili paste pickles, are also delicious.

spots.name: Mannam Garden
spots.desc: It is one of Gurye’s premier restaurants offering healthy Korean cuisine, including wild pine mushroom hot pot, herbal chicken soup, and mountain vegetable set meals. With a spacious parking lot and seating for large groups, it is ideal for families and tour groups, and guests can enjoy a satisfying meal with a variety of neatly prepared side dishes.

spots.name: La Plata
spots.desc: La Plata is a café offering beautiful views of the Seomjin River, with a spacious parking lot and comfortable seating. Famous for its lattes and matcha lattes, it also serves chewy milk ice cream and a variety of beverages.

spots.name: Easywon Café Ro
spots.desc: Easywon Café Ro is a cozy café near Jirisan Oncheon in Gurye, offering spacious and separate areas ideal for group gatherings. Popular items include jujube tea and Ssanghwa tea, as well as freshly blended fruit juices and snacks for children.

spots.name: Café Guman
spots.desc: Café Guman is a large café boasting a spacious parking lot and a comfortable indoor space. Popular menu items include cream coffee and a variety of breads, especially fig campagne and salted baguette.

spots.name: Songho Beach
spots.desc: Songho was named because the beach is full of old pine trees, and the fine sand and clear, calm waves of the beach resemble a lake. In particular, Songho Beach has fine sand and shallow water, making it great for children and families to play, and is home to a forest of hundreds-year-old sea pine trees.

spots.name: Forest of Memory
spots.desc: In 2014, a passenger ferry Sewol from Incheon to Jeju sank near Paengmok harbor in Jindo. The forest was built to remember the Ferry Sewol disaster, commemorate the victims, and comfort the bereaved families.

spots.name: Sani Garden
spots.desc: It is a garden with various plants and flowers, and it is a place where you can appreciate the natural scenery that changes with the season.

spots.name: Biwon
spots.desc: The design that makes use of the beauty of the traditional Korean garden stands out, and you can enjoy various trees and beautiful scenery that changes from season to season.

spots.name: 4est Arboretum
spots.desc: It is a space where visitors can appreciate various plant species. There are gardens and trails with various themes.

spots.name: Ttangkkeut Observatory
spots.desc: Located in the southernmost part of the Korean Peninsula, it is an observatory where visitors can view the surrounding landscape, including the South Sea. When the weather is nice, visitors can observe the surrounding islands and seas at a glance.

spots.name: Doesolam
spots.desc: The hermitage is located in nature, especially on rocks, creating a unique atmosphere.

spots.name: Gosan Yoonseondo Historical site
spots.desc: There are Ginkgo Tree and Bijarim, Sarangchae, Nokudang, Anchae, Haengnangchae, Barn, Ansadang, Gosan Sadang, Eochoeun Sadang, Chuwondang, and Gosan Antiquities Exhibition Hall.

spots.name: Sagumi Beach
spots.desc: The slope is gentle and the water depth is shallow, and there is a forest of black pine trees behind the white sand beach.

spots.name: Osiano Beach
spots.desc: Pine trees planted at the time of opening grow around the beach to create shade, and a small park is also built to play ball. There is also a camping site nearby, so there are showers and repair facilities.

spots.name: Gocheonam Galdae Field
spots.desc: It is known as the most beautiful reed field among the reed fields in the country, and it is said that visitors can see the scenery around sunset from early November to the end of November

spots.name: Songpyeong Beach

spots.name: Imha Island

spots.name: Toppi of the Ttangkkeut Village
spots.desc: It represents the southernmost land end of the Korean Peninsula and was built to commemorate it. spots.name: Duryunsan Provincial Park

spots.name: Duryun Maze Park

On the first floor, there is a labyrinth history hall and a rest facility, a labyrinth cafe, and on the second floor, there is a labyrinth forest made of mirrors, dinosaur adventure, and a labyrinth experience hall with five themes of trick art zones.

spots.name: Ttangkkeut Hope Park
spots.desc: Located on the southern tip of the Korean Peninsula, the park symbolizes the geographical characteristics of the "land's edge." The park has been created as a place where people can pledge new hope and pray for their wishes at the end of the Korean Peninsula. With sculptures and trails, such as stairs of hope and the Tower of Hope, visitors can relax while enjoying the sea and coastal scenery.

spots.name: Haenam Minam Festival

spots.name: Ttangkkeut Monorail

spots.name: Duryun Mountain Cable Car

You can enjoy a variety of experiences such as making green tea pizza, tea meditation, tea making, and experiencing seasonal food.

spots.name: Ttangkkeut Marine Natural History Museum

spots.name: Mysterious Sea Road

spots.name: Mountain Hiking Trails

spots.desc: About 15 minutes west of downtown Muan, Topmeori Beach is one of the county’s most scenic seaside spots. It features a long, wide sandy shore that appears dramatically during low tide, creating a perfect environment for mudflat exploration and shellfish gathering. spots.name: Muan Octopus Park
spots.desc: Located along the tidal flats of Jogeumnaru Beach, Muan Octopus Park is a seaside camping park built to celebrate Muan’s famous local specialty—octopus. At the center of the park stands a 14-meter-tall octopus-shaped observatory, connected to a long slide bridge that both children and adults can enjoy. The park also features coastal walking trails, flower paths, and scenic sunset viewpoints…

spots.name: Muan Ecological Tidal Flat Land
spots.desc: Muan Hwangto Mudflat Land is an eco-park located along the coast of Muan, famous for its expansive tidal flats and unique yellow clay soil. The site offers educational exhibits about Korea’s mudflat ecosystem and provides hands-on experiences such as clam digging and barefoot mud walking. It’s a popular destination for families and tourists interested in nature, ecology, and healing activities.

spots.name: Military Theme Park
spots.desc: Military Theme Park is an interactive military museum and outdoor exhibition where visitors can see real combat aircraft, transport helicopters, training planes, tanks, and armored vehicles up close. The park recreates scenes that feel like stepping into a movie, allowing guests to climb inside large helicopters and explore military equipment firsthand. It’s especially popular with children and…

spots.name: White Lotus Festival
spots.desc: This representative summer festival held annually in Muan County. Taking place at Hoesan White Lotus Pond, the largest white lotus habitat in Korea, the festival attracts many visitors who come to enjoy the breathtaking scenery of blooming lotus flowers. During the festival, visitors can also participate in various cultural events and hands-on programs themed around the lotus.

spots.name: Muan Mudflat Octopus Festival

Visitors can find specialties such as Muan onions, sweet potatoes, and local octopus. Small eateries inside the market serve simple Jeolla-style meals.

Ansan Fishing Village Folk Museum
spots.desc: You can see the history of west coast foreshore and fishing village at Daebudo. You can directly experience the fishing industry culture and traditional folk in the fishing village of Ansan.

spots.name: Chungmunkyu Museum
spots.desc: The representative museum in Daebudo. You can enjoy exhibition and concert together.

spots.name: Daebudo Bada Hyanggi Theme Park
spots.desc: You can take a walk in Daebudo Bada Hynaggi Theme Park. The park is full of beauty of nature. The walk is about 4.3 km and water way and pond are nicely laid out. The five windmills, the landmark of Daebudo, are displayed in the park.

spots.name: Daebudo Bangameori Food Culture Street
spots.desc: This is the food culture street that is located at the north Daebudo. The most famous food is 'Bajilack noodle soup'. It is a noodle soup with clams. The Daebudo Bangameori Food Culture Street also known as 'Bajilack Noodle Soup Street'. You can enjoy sliced raw fish, a shellfish baked, Soy Sauce Marinated Crab, Soybean paste stew with clams and more.

spots.name: Gubongdo Sunset Observatory
spots.desc: A scenic coastal destination famous for its sunset view over the West Sea. Highlights include the iconic Grandmother and Grandfather Rocks (Halmae and Halbae Bawi) and the sculpture art at the tip of the walking trail.

spots.name: Gubongdo Sunset Observatory
spots.desc: Many visitors visit Gubongdo Sunset Observatory for enjoy sunset. It is located in Gubongdo. You can go through the Haesolgil.

spots.name: Nueseom Lighthouse Observatory
spots.desc: Only 4 hr with two times, it is possible to enter to the Nue island. Nue means silkworm in Korean. The shape of the island looks like a silkworm, so it is the name that has been given to the island.
spots.hours: March to October: 09:00–18:00, November to February: 09:00–17:00, Holiday on Mon

spots.name: Sihwaho Tidal Power Plant
spots.desc: Built in 2011, the world's biggest tidal power plant which can produce energy available for half a million a year. If you'd like to watch the view of this plant, you are recommended to go 'T-Light' park. There is Moon Observatory in this park, so you can enjoy sunset of the west coast. Admission free. The easiest way to get here is take bus 123 and get off at Sihwaho Tidal Power Plant.

spots.name: Tando Island
spots.desc: Tando is the fourth biggest island following the Daebudo, Sungam island, and Booldo. It is famous for the observatory at Nue island. There are many visitors who are fishing with family. It is not appropriate for playing or swimming in the sea. However, it is a great place for enjoying the quiet sea.

spots.name: Yukdo Island
spots.desc: Yukdo is the island that 6 small-sized island together. About 30 citizens live in Yukdo and most of them work in the fishing. You can visit Yukdo by boat. There are 2 ways for boat way, Daebudo to Yukdo and Incheon to Yukdo. It isn't that famous for travellers, so if you want quiet and relaxing travel, you can enjoy the sea of Yukdo.

spots.name: Metasequoire Road
spots.desc: 1,200 metasequoires are planted on both sides of the trail on a 3.5km section of the outer road of Daebu Sea Hyanggi Theme Park. You can take a walk or rent a bicycle, scooter, or electric cart.

spots.name: Bada Hyanggi Arboretum
spots.desc: A large coastal arboretum with around 1,000 species of plants and several themed gardens, including a rose garden, rock garden, greenhouse, and ecological ponds. Its hilltop observatory offers wide views of the West Sea and the surrounding islands.
spots.hours: Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00; Nov-Feb 09:00-17:00; closed Mon, Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok

spots.name: Glass Island Museum in Daebudo
spots.desc: [Facility Information]- Glass Island MuseumA space exhibiting contemporary glass works by glass artists as well as pieces created using various mixed media- Glass Art Demonstration RoomA venue equipped with a projector and sound system where visitors can experience the vibrant creative process of glass artists infused with artistic spirit- Glass Art Experience CenterThe workshop, where you can…

spots.name: Dongju Salt Field
spots.desc: There are 4 experiences on offer in the Dongju Salt Field: Education about the salt field, salt production experience, making colorful salt pillars, and making soap with bay salt.

spots.name: Jonghyeon Fishing Village
spots.desc: There are various experience in Jonghyeon Fishing Village, mud flat ecology education, sledding at mud flat, catching a mudfish with bare hands, fishing mudskipper, grape picking, making grape juice, making topiaries, planting grape trees, marine leports and more.

spots.name: Seongam Fishing Village
spots.desc: There are various experience in Seongam Fishing Village, shell gathering, fishing with a net, sledding at mud flat, grape picking, sweet potato picking experience, riding all-terrain vehicle, painball game, potato picking experience, and more.

spots.name: Ansan Daebu Grape Festival
spots.desc: Grape is well known local products in Daebudo. It is held in September every other year. In festival, you enjoy many kinds of special food with grape and other events like Miss Daebu grape contest, singing contest and quiz contest etc.

spots.name: Ansan M Valley Rock Festival
spots.desc: This is one of the biggest rock festivals in Korea. It is held every year around July, with many famous domestic and foreign artists.

spots.name: Daebu Mine Media Facade
spots.desc: The performance is held every September to October at Daebu Mine, a waste quarry in Ansan, where traces of the dinosaur era remain. Daebu Mine Media Facade is an immersive musical in which audiences walk around the mine to participate in the story.

spots.name: Daebudo Glass Island
spots.desc: The Daebudo Glass Island is also known as the Murano of Korea. The products that made from glass are exported to almost all countries in the world. There are glass-garden that display various arts, exhibition that display modern glass art creator, craft showcase and more. Also, there are various experience programs that you can make glass cup, glass accessories, key holder, aroma lamp and more…
spots.hours: Tue–Sun 09:00–19:00 in Apr–Oct, 09:30–18:30 in Nov–Mar, Mon is holiday
spots.price: Adult ₩10,000, teenager ₩9,000, child ₩8,000, under 7 years old free

spots.name: Gyeonggi Creation Center
spots.desc: The Gyeonggi Creation Center is run by Province Gyeonggi and support native and foreign artists to create and study. Various artists who are chosen by contest exhibition exhibit their arts. There are mentoring program, lecture from artists, seminar, workshops and more various programs. More information about exhibition will be updated on the official website.

spots.name: Sejong Pottery Center
spots.desc: The Sejong Pottery Center has built to give wider publicity to other people. This center can accommodate 600 people and it provide various programs that is systematically organized. You can participate the programs like salt pond experience, mud flat experience, etiquette lessons, or dye experience. Moreover, there are pottery programs that you can make your own pottery and color it. The programs…

spots.name: Daebudo Haesolgil
spots.desc: Haesolgil is the walking trail of Daebudo. There are 7 courses of trail and each course has different way to walk.

spots.name: Daebudo Bangameori seafood direct outlet
spots.desc: Daebudo has great quality of seafood. You can have fresh raw fishes and roasted clam caught that day. There are many restaurants in the outlet so you can buy some fishes and eat right away at the same time.

spots.name: Daebudo Bangameori Food Culture Street
spots.desc: A bustling street lined with seafood restaurants specializing in knife-cut clam noodle soup (bajirak kalguksu) and crispy seafood green onion pancakes (haemul pajeon), traditionally paired with local rice wine (makgeolli).

spots.name: Sodam spicy seafood soup with soft bean curd
spots.desc: Sodam spicy seafood soup with soft bean curd is a representative restaurant in Daebu-do, and spicy spicy seafood soup with soft bean curd and strong bagochi are popular menus. Samhap Kalguksu made with homemade secret broth combines the cool soup of clams, lilies and mussels with chewy noodles, and it is even better to eat with crispy seafood pajeon. Pets are allowed. High chairs and…

spots.name: Daebudo Badat Village Kalguksu
spots.desc: Daebudo Badat Village Kalguksu is a must-visit noodle soup with seafood restaurant when traveling to Daebudo Island. A sea noodle soup with seafood made of fresh seafood and shabu-shabu dumpling hot pot are popular menus, and basic side dishes such as kimchi and kkakdugi are also delicious. It is ideal for group gatherings or family dining out because parking is convenient and stores are large.

spots.name: American Muffin
spots.desc: A local bakery-cafe offering handmade muffins, cakes, and coffee.

spots.name: Hagenna
spots.desc: This cafe is located in along the seaside. You can enjoy beautiful scenery. Parking lot is available in front of cafe.

spots.name: Ruedecafe
spots.desc: Fancy cafe, pleasantly decorated in European style, serving many kinds of hand-drip coffee of high nice quality.

spots.name: Daebudo Grape Bread
spots.desc: Daebudo grape bread is a must-visit dessert spot when traveling to Daebu Island.Grape bread is characterized by a soft texture and a blend of non-sweet cream, and it goes well with drinks such as americano.

spots.name: Hanagae Beach
spots.desc: A large sandy beach on the southwest coast of Muuido Island, famous for its gentle waves, tidal flats at low tide, and sunsets over the Yellow Sea. There are showers, small shops, and seasonal food stands. Hanaggae Beach is a wonderful place for a laid-back weekend vacation. The entire island is quiet but beautiful, and easy to explore. Muuido is an ideal place to get away from Korea's noisy…

spots.name: Silmi Beach
spots.desc: A secluded beach in the north of Hanagae, a natural atmosphere. At low tide, you can see the mudflats spread toward Silmido Island.

spots.name: Silmi Island
spots.desc: An uninhabited island seen from the northwestern coast of Muuido Island. Accessible on foot only at low tide, visitors should check the tide time carefully as the route is quickly submerged. It is well known as a training ground for the 684th unit, and has also been the subject of movies.

spots.name: Guksa-bong
spots.desc: Guksabong Peak is 236 meters high and offers spectacular views of the Goeam Cliffs such as Whale Rock, Madang Rock, and Buddha Rock, and there is a legend that a memorial service was held to pray for the safety of the people when the country had a big event a long time ago, and the temple site remains about 200 meters south of the trail, proving its origin. Hundreds of tows, including gilt-bronze…

spots.name: Beach walking and tidal-flat exploration
spots.desc: Walking along Hanagae and Silmi Beach is especially popular at low tide when mudflats are exposed. While shellfish and small marine life can be observed, foraging may be limited in some areas.

spots.name: Light hiking
spots.desc: Several informal trails cross the island’s low hills, offering views of the coast and nearby Yeongjong Island. Trails are generally easy but can be muddy after rain.

spots.name: Seasonal beach activities
spots.desc: During summer, horseback riding and ATV rentals are sometimes available near the main beaches. Availability varies by season and weather.

spots.name: Ganghwa Leports Park
spots.desc: It has facilities such as zipline, adventure, and climbing. It is a leisure sport that anyone of all ages can enjoy after completing a simple safety rule training. You can feel the comfortable feeling of a natural recreational forest at the same time.

spots.name: 옥토끼우주센터
spots.desc: As Korea's first aerospace science theme park, it collects and preserves aerospace-related materials to provide exhibitions and education to help children and the general public understand aerospace science.

spots.name: Local seafood restaurants
spots.desc: Restaurants near the beaches serve grilled fish, shellfish, squid, and other standard Korean seafood dishes. Prices are generally higher than in the city, and many places close outside the summer season.

spots.name: Self-catering at the beach
spots.desc: Outdoor cooking areas near Hanagae Beach allow visitors to prepare their own meals. Supplies such as charcoal and ingredients must be brought in advance.

spots.name: Central Park
spots.desc: A beautiful place to stroll around. You can see an old Korean house as well, the last remaining house from the traditional village that existed in Bundang during the Joseon era.

spots.name: Yuldong Park
spots.desc: You can do bungee jumping here. You can take a walk while looking at the lake.

spots.name: Tancheon
spots.desc: The small river that runs through Bundang, has excellent walking and cycling paths along both banks. Additionally, there are basketball courts and grassy fields up and down the river, as well as a small golf course near Sunae station.

spots.name: Hyundai Department Store
spots.desc: You can shop from luxuries to fast fashion brands. It has a very large place for restaurants and cafes in the basement.

spots.name: AK Plaza
spots.desc: It's a central place in Seohyeon. It is directly connected to the subway station, and you can see many people waiting for someone in the lobby.

spots.name: Dai Hoshi
spots.desc: The restaurant serves kaisendon, a Japanese rice bowl made with a variety of seasonal seafood, and aged sashimi.

spots.name: Dansot (담솥)
spots.desc: It's made by cooking rice, a staple food in Korea, in a metal utensil called a sot. The menu varies depending on the ingredients that go on top, and after eating the rice, warm water is added to the bowl of rice and eaten as soongnyeong.

spots.name: Saemaeul Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant is a Korean BBQ chain run by Baek Jong-won, a famous chef and entrepreneur in South Korea. It is a franchise restaurant with over 100 stores in Korea. The restaurant's signature menu items are charcoal-grilled beef, salted pork, and 7-minute kimchi stew.

spots.name: Jin Udon
spots.desc: This is a Japanese restaurant serving hand-made udon. Its chewy noodles and deep broth give it a taste that sets it apart from other udon restaurants.

spots.name: The Jin Guk
spots.desc: We serve Korean-style pork soup. We also provide cold noodles

spots.name: Cat's Kitchen(고양이 부엌)
spots.desc: A cozy and charming restaurant famous for tabletop-cooked spicy rice cakes (jeukseok tteokbokki). Unlike conventional tteokbokki joints, its signature broth features baby clams and bean sprouts, creating a distinctly refreshing and savory soup. Diners can customize their meal by adding various toppings such as ramen noodles, cheese, and deep-fried seaweed rolls, and finishing with cheese fried…

spots.name: Paik's Coffee(빽다방)
spots.desc: A branch of the popular Korean coffee chain founded by celebrity chef Baek Jong-won. Well-known for its large portion sizes and affordable prices, it offers a wide range of beverages, including its signature extra-large iced Americano ("Wicked Americano"), rich sweet mixed coffee (Wongabang), milkshakes, and soft-serve ice cream desserts. Takeout is very popular among local commuters and office…

spots.name: Eurwangni Beach
spots.desc: Also spelled Ulwangli, this is most popular of the island's beaches, as the water doesn't recede as much here. Motels, restaurants, karaoke rooms and all you need for a Korean-style beach experience. There are fireworks at night on weekends.

spots.name: Unseo Sauna
spots.desc: Visitors to New Airport City wishing to enjoy a sauna may do so in the downtown area several blocks away from the subway station.

spots.name: BMW Driving Center
spots.desc: An automotive theme park on 240,000 square meters of land with six tracks. You can choose between BMW and Mini cars in driving courses that run from 10 minutes to 3 hours on diverse road conditions including off road, slippery, railroad and forest roads. Additionally there is a museum, showroom and a training center.

spots.name: Inspire Arena
spots.desc: Indoor arena opened in November 2023, built for concerts rather than sports. It seats up to 15,000 with a central 360-degree stage, or about 12,000 with a T-shaped stage. The schedule is mostly K-pop and other music concerts, along with esports, fashion shows and sporting events. Tickets are sold by each event's organiser, so check the schedule before making the trip.

spots.name: Cimer
spots.desc: Large spa in two zones. The aqua zone has indoor and outdoor pools, infinity pools and water slides (riders must be at least 1.3 m tall), and tattoos must be covered there, for example with a rash guard. The jjimjil zone is a Korean-style sauna area with a hot kiln room (bulgama, 80–85°C), salt and red-clay rooms and an ice room. The jjimjil ticket allows 4 hours in that zone, and the combined…
spots.hours: Aqua zone: M–F 10:00–19:00, Sa Su and holidays 10:00–21:00; jjimjil zone: daily 10:00–21:00; last entry 19:30
spots.price: Combined ticket ₩60,000 (₩70,000 in Jul–Aug and Dec–Feb); jjimjil zone only ₩40,000; children ₩10,000 less

spots.name: Cafe
spots.desc: There are many cafes in Yeonjong Island where many Koreans also visit. You can see beach and Wolmi island in many cafes.

spots.name: Eorimok
spots.desc: The 4.7-km-long walk up a forested valley is gentle and fairly consistent sloped. It is more than 1 km from the bus stop to the trail start. In winter, the trail is packed with children using the packed down snow for sledding downhill (bring an E-mart bag!) It has a rest house and basic shop at the trail start. Terminates at Witse Oreum.

spots.name: Yeongsil
spots.desc: The shortest path at 3.7 km (and 2.5 km from the carpark to the trail start). Weaves up a ridge along steep cliffs and past some waterfalls (frozen in winter) before a final flat stretch at the top. Has a decent restaurant and shop at the trail start. Terminates at Witse Oreum.

spots.name: Seobin Baeksa
spots.desc: A white sandy beach that's been a popular scene in many Korean dramas and films.

spots.name: Udobong Peak
spots.desc: At 132 m, it is the highest point on Udo island and offers great views of the national park.

spots.name: Bike Tours
spots.desc: Udo island is small enough that a 13-km bike ride will cover most of it.

spots.name: Lighthouse Park
spots.desc: This lighthouse is right in front of a dramatic sea view in the Udo Provincial Maritime Park. It was built by the Japanese during the occupation of Korea.

spots.name: Udo Museum
spots.desc: Exhibits of marine and insect life on the island of Udo, including a fossil collection.

spots.name: Yeondae-bong Peak (연대봉)
spots.desc: The highest point on Gadeok Island, offering panoramic views of the Busan-Geoje Fixed Link and the surrounding sea. The hike to the peak takes about 2-3 hours and is a popular activity for both locals and tourists.

spots.name: Gadeokdo Lighthouse (가덕도 등대)
spots.desc: A beautiful historical lighthouse built in 1909. It is one of the most iconic landmarks on the island and provides a glimpse into the island's maritime history. The lighthouse is part of the Gadeokdo Lighthouse Park, which is a great spot for photos.

spots.name: Gadeokdo Fortress (가덕도 왜성)
spots.desc: Ruins of a Japanese-style fortress from the late 16th century. It offers a historical perspective on the island's strategic military importance. Visitors can explore the stone walls and enjoy the views from the site.

spots.name: Daehang Port (대항항)
spots.desc: A small and charming fishing port on the southern side of the island. You can watch local fishermen and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere. Several seafood restaurants are located nearby.

spots.name: Haeoreum Jogaegui (해오름 조개구이)
spots.desc: A popular seafood restaurant known for its jogaegui (grilled clams). Many locals recommend it for its fresh ingredients and great ocean view.

spots.name: Bada Kalguksu (바다 칼국수)
spots.desc: A simple and cozy restaurant specializing in haemul-kalguksu (seafood noodle soup). A perfect place for a warm, comforting meal.

spots.name: Gadeokdo Galbi (가덕도 갈비)
spots.desc: A restaurant well-known for its delicious grilled pork ribs (galbi). It is a favorite among families.

spots.name: Gadeokdo Sikdang (가덕도 식당)
spots.desc: A simple, traditional Korean eatery that serves local dishes like miyeok-guk (seaweed soup) and doenjang-jjigae (soybean paste stew). It is a favorite among local residents.

spots.name: Hotteok Shop (호떡 가게)
spots.desc: A small street food stand that sells hotteok, a sweet pancake filled with brown sugar and nuts. It's a great snack on the go.

spots.name: Gadeokdo Dawon (가덕도 다원)
spots.desc: A cozy tea house with a great view of the sea, offering traditional Korean teas and desserts. It's a perfect place to relax after a hike.

spots.name: Haeinsa Temple
spots.desc: One of the Korea's Three Jewel Temples and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Haeinsa houses the Tripitaka Korea, a copy of Buddhist scripture carved onto 81,258 printing blocks.

spots.name: Se-seok flat
spots.desc: Se-seok. The habitat of the Royal Azaleas. This is one of the main habitats of royal azaleas, and you can see the wide stage of royal azaleas. The origin of the place name 'Seseok' is derived from the meaning of 'flat land with a lot of pebbles.' Seseok flat is a plateau of about 990,000 square meters located between Yeongsinbong Peak (1,652m) and Chotdaebong Peak (1,703m). This area is high…

spots.name: Yeonhabong Peak
spots.desc: Mossy strange rocks and bizarre stones are developed, and the forest of dead trees filled in between creates a mysterious beauty.

spots.name: chatnipmasul
spots.desc: High-end Korean restaurant operated on a reservation basis. Bibimbap without Gochujang is the main menu. It also provides green tea-applied foods such as pork belly in green tea sauce, green tea oil, green tea honey, and green tea wine.

spots.name: baekryeonsanbang
spots.desc: Lotus Leaf Rice and traditional Korean food restaurant. It also serves grilled bulgogi, yukgaejang, and grilled fish. There are many side dishes made of vegetables. This restaurant serve customers by reservation.
spots.hours: Closed on the 4th and 8th of every month

spots.name: dalgungsikdang
spots.desc: If you visit in the morning, you can order 'Soybean paste stew (Doenjang jjigae)' and 'Kimchi stew (Kimchi jjigae)', which are the basics of Korean home cooking. Other times, bibimbap or pork is the main menu. Or you can eat expensive chicken stew (Samgyetang, ₩60,000-100,000) with expensive herbs.

spots.name: Theroad101
spots.desc: Cafe in the green garden with a good view of Jirisan. This store sells various kinds of coffee roasted in this store. They have group seats, parking lot, free Wi-Fi, male/female toilets and can be to-go.

spots.name: Boriam Temple
spots.desc: Boriam Temple is located near the top of Geum Mountain, the tallest mountain on Namhae. It boasts great views of the island, including Sangju beach and the ocean beyond. Wander around on the numerous hiking trails surrounding the temple.

spots.name: Mulgeon-ri Bangjo-eobu-rim (Windbreak Forest)
spots.desc: Planted roughly 300 years ago by villagers to shield the town and its farmland from sea winds and storm surges, this crescent-shaped windbreak-and-fish-gathering forest stretches along the coast just below German Village. Hackberry, Aphananthe, sawtooth oak, zelkova, and evergreen machilus trees grow densely together, giving the grove an almost primeval feel. A walking path winds through the…

spots.name: Namhae Traditional Market
spots.desc: A lively, old-fashioned market selling fresh seafood, vegetables, clothing, and local snacks. Namhae's famous specialty, anchovies (myeolchi), are a highlight here — look for dried anchovies, anchovy sauce (myeolchi-jeot), and other anchovy products from the region's renowned bamboo-trap (jukbangnyeom) fisheries. It's also a good spot to try nostalgic street snacks like rice-ball porridge from…

spots.name: Aengang Market
spots.desc: Local food shop and tea café selling Namhae specialties such as dried anchovies, yuja preserves, seaweed and tea, plus souvenirs and crafts. It has a small tea room overlooking a garden.

spots.name: Namhae Jangsu Agujjim
spots.desc: A long-standing local favorite specializing in agujjim (spicy braised monkfish). The signature dish is the aged-kimchi agujjim, generously topped with well-fermented kimchi and steamed until spicy and tender; many diners note it's savory without being overly salty. Expect a wait during peak meal times.
spots.price: Agujjim (monkfish stew), medium/large ₩35,000-50,000; aged-kimchi agujjim (large) ₩57,000; suyuk (boiled meat, large)…
spots.addr: 266-4 Jijok-ri, Samdong-myeon, Namhae-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, South Korea

spots.name: Namhae Sigol Halmae Makgeolli
spots.desc: Known for its outdoor terrace overlooking Daraengi Village's terraced rice paddies and the sea beyond. The signature pairing is the seafood pancake with citron makgeolli, though the menu also features other Namhae specialties like anchovy lettuce-wrap rice and sea urchin bibimbap. Popular with tourists, so expect a wait on weekends and during peak season.
spots.price: Seafood pancake (haemul-pajeon) ₩15,000-20,000, anchovy lettuce-wrap rice (myeolchi ssambap) ₩12,000-15,000/person…

spots.name: Dongcheon Restaurant

spots.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace Visit
spots.desc: Gyeongbokgung Palace was the first and largest of the royal palaces built during the Joseon Dynasty. Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung Palace was located at the heart of the newly appointed capital of Seoul (then known as Hanyang) and represented the sovereignty of the Joseon Dynasty. The largest of the Five Grand Palaces (the others being Gyeonghuigung Palace, Deoksugung Palace, Changgyeonggung…

spots.name: Bike riding and walking in Hangang Park

spots.name: Traditional Crafts Experience Center

spots.name: Techno Mart (Gangbyeon)
spots.desc: There are two Techno Marts in Seoul: the original at Gangbyeon station, and the new store at Sindorim station. Both complexes house over 2,000 stores across eight floors that sell a variety of high-tech products. From electrical appliances to computers, you will find everything you need. The first floor has cosmetics, accessories, and stationeries. The second and third floors comprise Korean-made…

spots.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)

spots.name: SeMA Bunker
spots.desc: A rather mysterious former bunker built during the 1970s military government. It was discovered in 2005 during the bus transfer center construction, and was opened as a gallery in 2017. It is part of the Seoul Museum of Arts.

spots.name: Mullae Art Village
spots.desc: A former ironworks district that has developed into an artists' village with studios, workshops, murals, outdoor sculptures, cafés, and restaurants. The narrow alleys preserve traces of the area's industrial history while displaying contemporary art. Many ironworks close on weekends, making the artwork painted on their shutters easier to see.
spots.hours: Open area; individual studios and workshops have their own hours

spots.name: G Valley Industrial Museum
spots.desc: A museum documenting the history of the former Guro Industrial Complex and its transformation into today's Seoul Digital Industrial Complex. Exhibits include industrial products such as toys, televisions, radios, and other objects related to the area's manufacturing and labor history.

spots.name: Netmarble Game Museum
spots.desc: An interactive museum devoted to the history and culture of video games. Its exhibitions cover the development of games in Korea and abroad, game characters and music, and the cultural value of gaming. Visitors can also browse game-related materials and play classic arcade, console, and PC games.

spots.name: Tomb of Jeongseon Princess
spots.desc: A historic burial site associated with Jeongseon Princess, the seventh daughter of King Seonjo of the Joseon Dynasty. The site includes the graves of the princess, her husband Kwon Dae-im, and other members of the Andong Kwon clan. Its tombstones and epitaphs are valuable sources for understanding Joseon-period funerary practices.

spots.name: Ankara Park
spots.desc: A small park created to commemorate the sister-city relationship between Seoul and Ankara, the capital of Turkey. Opened in 1977, the park includes Ankara House, a traditional Turkish-style building, as well as sculptures and landscaped areas representing the friendship between the two cities.

spots.name: Seonyudo Park
spots.desc: This is a park with many gardens in the island of Seonyudo. The island was a site of water purification plant until 2000, and was converted to a park in 2002. Many of the sculptures and architectures are remnants of the previous plant, and won many awards such as Korean Architecture Institute Award and American Society of Landscape Architects Award. It is now a nice photo spot used by Seoul…

spots.name: Yeouido Park

There is a traditional Korean forest, and in many other places you can enjoy concerts, cycling, or taking walks. Hundreds of trees and flowers offer you shade and an opportunity to relax. There are nice ponds and basketball courts. For a nominal fee, one can also rent…

spots.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
spots.desc: One of Seoul's most popular riverside parks, with wide lawns and views of the Han River. It is popular for picnics, walking, and cycling, and bicycles can be rented nearby. The park is also a popular place to watch the sunset and hosts seasonal events, including the Seoul International Fireworks Festival. It is a good place to experience how Seoul residents spend their leisure time along the Han…

spots.name: Geobugi Upyeonso
spots.desc: Inspired by the slow, deliberate pace of a turtle, it offers a peaceful sanctuary where visitors can write "slow letters" that are delivered one year later and enjoy quiet moments.

spots.name: SEOULDAL
spots.desc: A tethered helium balloon that rises up to 130 m above Yeouido Park, offering panoramic views of the Han River and Seoul skyline. Each flight lasts about 15 minutes.
