spots.price: Adults ₩25,000, teens and seniors ₩20,000, children age 3-12 ₩15,000

spots.name: Pureun Arboretum
spots.desc: Seoul's first public arboretum, with themed gardens, wetlands, walking paths, a forest education center, and thousands of plant species. It is a quiet place for walking and nature viewing in southwestern Seoul.

spots.name: Guro Arts Valley Theater
spots.desc: A cultural arts complex with a 579-seat theater, gallery, small hall, education rooms, and other facilities. It hosts concerts, theater performances, exhibitions, and cultural programs throughout the year.

spots.name: D-Cube Link Arts Center
spots.desc: A large musical theater inside D-Cube City with 1,242 seats. It hosts major Korean productions of musicals and other stage performances, and is directly connected to Sindorim Station.

spots.name: Hangdong Railroad
spots.desc: A former freight railway that has become a popular walking route and photo spot. The single-track railway runs through a quiet green area and connects naturally with Pureun Arboretum, making it a pleasant place for a short walk.

spots.name: Anyangcheon Stream Walkway
spots.desc: A riverside walking and cycling route known for cherry blossoms in spring. The stream supports a variety of birds, fish, and plants, and the riverside also has recreational and sports areas. The Guro section is easily accessible from several subway stations.

spots.name: Guro Ollegil
spots.desc: A network of nine walking routes totaling 28.5 km across Guro-gu. The routes include forest trails through local hills, riverside paths along streams such as Anyangcheon, and urban walking routes. Visitors can choose individual sections rather than completing the entire trail.

spots.name: Yeongdeungpo Park
spots.desc: A neighborhood park built on the former site of an OB beer factory. One of its landmarks is a large copper brewing kettle that was actually used in beer production in the 1930s. The park also has lawns, a pond, sports courts, and other recreational facilities.

spots.name: Seoul Marina Club & Yacht
spots.desc: A marina on the Han River offering yacht rides and sailing experiences with views of the Seoul skyline. Professional crews operate the yachts, and evening rides are popular for views of the city lights along the river.
spots.hours: Daily 10:00-22:00; closed on Seollal and Chuseok

spots.name: E-Land Cruise – Yeouido Dock
spots.desc: Sightseeing cruises departing from Yeouido on the Han River. Programs include daytime sightseeing, sunset, night, music, and dinner cruises, with routes offering views of Seoul's riverside skyline and bridges. Passengers should check the current schedule before visiting, and adults should bring identification.
spots.hours: Daily 11:00-22:00; departure times vary by cruise

spots.name: Gocheok Neighborhood Park
spots.desc: One of Guro-gu's main neighborhood parks, with wooded walking paths, murals, sports facilities, and open recreation areas. It is a quiet place for a walk or light exercise away from the busier commercial areas of the district.

spots.name: YDP CULTURAL LOUNGE DADADA
spots.desc: A public cultural lounge in the Times Square plaza offering exhibitions, workshops, media art, and community programs. The space works with local artists and residents and can also be used as a place to rest while exploring the Yeongdeungpo area.

spots.name: Gungdong Reservoir Ecological Park
spots.desc: An ecological park built around a former reservoir, with walking trails, traditional Korean pavilions, exercise equipment, an outdoor stage, and areas for observing plants and wildlife. More than 25,000 plants grow around the reservoir, which is also home to around 100 koi fish.

spots.name: Cheonwangsan Family Camping Site
spots.desc: A family-oriented campground near Cheonwangsan Mountain and Pureun Arboretum. It has regular and automobile camping sites, shower facilities, washing areas, and equipment rentals. Reservations are required, and the surrounding trails provide easy access to nearby green spaces.

spots.name: Yeouinaru Station Runner Station
spots.desc: A facility for runners inside Yeouinaru Station, designed as a base for running along the Han River. It has changing rooms, lockers, powder rooms, shoe sanitizers, an InBody analyzer, and information on running routes and events. Running classes and other programs are also offered.

spots.name: Culture Train 959
spots.desc: A cultural arts space built inside Sindorim Station. It includes an art platform, gallery, and classrooms, and hosts exhibitions by resident artists as well as drawing, painting, photography, craft, and other cultural programs. Check the current program schedule before visiting.
spots.hours: Varies by exhibition, class, and program
spots.price: Exhibitions are generally free; classes and programs may charge a fee

spots.name: Yeouiseo-ro (Yunjung-ro) Cherry Blossom Road
spots.desc: A riverside road behind the National Assembly that is one of Seoul's best-known cherry blossom walking routes. In spring, the road is lined with cherry trees, azaleas, forsythias, and other flowers, and it hosts the annual Yeongdeungpo Yeouido Spring Flower Festival.
spots.hours: Open year-round; cherry blossom season is usually in early April

spots.name: Techno Mart (Sindorim)
spots.desc: The Techno Marts at Sindorim station.There are two Techno Marts in Seoul: the original at Gangbyeon station, and the new store at Sindorim station. Both complexes house over 2,000 stores across eight floors that sell a variety of high-tech products. Restaurants, a cinema and an arcade are on floors 9 & 10.

spots.name: Times Square
spots.desc: Yeongdeungpo Times Square is a new UELC-Urban Entertainment Lifestyle Center. It consists of more than 200 commercial, business, cultural, and leisure spaces, including department stores, various shopping brands, bookstores, and aquariums.

spots.name: The Hyundai Seoul
spots.desc: A large modern department store in the Parc.1 complex, known for its spacious interior, indoor garden, waterfall, fashion and lifestyle shops, restaurants, and frequently changing pop-up stores.

spots.name: No Brand Supermarket
spots.desc: No Brand is a chain supermarket in Seoul. It is Korea's equivalent of Aldi, except every single product has the same yellow "no brand" labelling. Their products are excellent quality and some are quite unusual. Recommended for self-catering or for snacks.

spots.name: Jinju-house
spots.desc: It is a famous restaurant for Korean traditional food, Kongguksu. Inside the Yeouido Department Store.

spots.name: Feel Damn Good Bakery
spots.desc: Unassuming bakery with a plethora of self-serve baked goods, coffee and fresh sandwiches made to order. English spoken.

spots.name: 김밥처럼 선유도역 본점
spots.desc: Great local snack bar. No English sign but cheap, delicious Korean food. Friendly staff. Order via touchpad at table.
spots.price: 10,000 Won for a few dishes to share

spots.name: JinJin's Dumpling
spots.desc: A Korean restaurant specializing in handmade dumplings, dumpling soup, and eobokjaengban, a traditional platter of boiled beef and vegetables.
spots.price: Around ₩89,000 for eobokjaengban; cheaper dumpling dishes are also available

spots.name: Jeongin Myeonok
spots.desc: A long-running restaurant specializing in Pyeongyang-style naengmyeon, known for its mild beef broth and buckwheat noodles. Dumplings, boiled beef, and eobokjaengban are also available.

spots.name: Itama-e
spots.desc: A 15-year-old Yeouido Japanese izakaya restaurant with authentic Japanese cuisine and side dishes based on raw fish aged with fresh sashimi

spots.name: Ijo Handmade Kalguksu
spots.desc: A 37-year-old soybean noodle restaurant, its signature menu includes soybean noodles made using Korean frosted beans and handmade king dumplings. It features a rich and savory soup and chewy noodles. Also, it is served with homemade kimchi and dongchimi to create a well-balanced taste.

spots.name: Grandma Pie
spots.desc: Located in Sindorim Station, the restaurant specializes in American-style pizza by the slice and focaccia. The dough is of high quality and the texture is impressive, and a variety of sauces and drinks that go with pizza are also gaining popularity. The interior of the store is decorated with a hip atmosphere that feels American.

spots.name: Masgihaeng four seasons Dangsan Branch
spots.desc: Located near Dangsan Station, the store specializes in seasonal dishes, especially Hamo shabu-shabu and clam shabu-shabu. Inside, it is spacious and offers private meals. In front of the store, there is an aquarium where you can check out fresh seafood yourself. In addition, braised pollack stew and raw octopus, served as basic side dishes, are also well received by many visitors.

spots.name: 103 Modern Chinese Food
spots.desc: As a bar serving fusion Chinese cuisine, it is an attractive place with a wide variety of menus and ambiance. In particular, signature yukhoe boasts a unique combination, served with avocado, chasai, and sriracha sauces. The interior is spacious and has many tables, making it suitable for group visits.

spots.name: Dangsan Red Jjukkumi
spots.desc: Known for its spicy webfoot octopus dishes, it is a restaurant that offers a wide variety of webfoot octopus menus. It is a perfect atmosphere for dinners or gatherings with friends, and the unique sauce combination using boiled eggs and tartare sauce served as a standard table setting is attractive. Fried rice is recommended as a must-have, and it can be enjoyed deliciously as it is well infused…

spots.name: Hanmaum Meat Restaurant
spots.desc: Hanmaum Meat Restaurant serves a wide variety of pork and beef dishes. You can grill fresh, high-quality meats right at your table and enjoy them with a diverse selection of side dishes that bring out the absolute best flavors.With spacious seating designed to comfortably accommodate large groups, it is an ideal spot for family gatherings.
spots.addr: 1F, 63 Dosin-ro, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul, 07366, Rep. of KOREA

spots.name: GOATT DELICATESSEN
spots.desc: Goat Deli Mullae is a cozy house-cured meat deli hidden on the second floor of a vintage alley building in Mullae-dong.The restaurant pairs warm wooden interiors and a classic European vibe with an artisanal selection of pastrami and jambon.Visitors can enjoy exceptional handcrafted sandwiches like the signature Jambon Beurre alongside highballs, craft beers, or coffee.
spots.addr: 2F, 14, Dorim-ro 139-gil, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea

spots.name: Home and Bread
spots.desc: A small bakery offering a variety of breads. One of its popular items is the Chocolat Cashew Nut, made with chocolate and nuts.

spots.name: Chiraendopeu Coffee Bar
spots.desc: Located in Dangsan Station, the cafe features LP music and sensuous interior design. Serving a wide range of drinks and desserts, croffles and signature coffees are especially popular. The atmosphere is good and suitable for working alone, and it is also suitable for dates and gatherings with friends.

spots.name: MAKON
spots.desc: It is a cafe with western American sensibility, and the combination of wood-tone interior and subtle lighting creates a cozy atmosphere. It offers a variety of desserts and coffee menus, especially the Aubero, a black sesame latte, is famous for its signature menu. Located in a quiet alley, it is the perfect place to work alone or talk to friends.

spots.name: FB Coffee Rosters
spots.desc: With a quiet and cozy atmosphere, it provides a good place to concentrate. You can enjoy roasted coffee and various desserts, especially salt bread and egg tarts. The interior of the cafe is industrial and comfortable, making it a perfect environment for working alone.

spots.name: Bae Bae Coffee Rosters
spots.desc: This is a cafe that roasts green beans, a special-class single origin from the representative coffee shop.

spots.name: Cafe Obom
spots.desc: Located on the second floor of a building along Dorim-ro in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul, this is a cozy local neighborhood café with a quiet atmosphere.It offers a selection of coffee, tea, beverages, and desserts, providing a comfortable space suitable for quiet conversations or individual work.

spots.name: Eastwood Dorim
spots.desc: The café offers a diverse selection of freshly baked financiers and pastries, alongside filter coffee and customizable milk options. Situated in a compact neighborhood space, seating is limited and dedicated parking is unavailable, so popular baked items may sell out early in the day.

spots.name: Cafe Arte
spots.desc: Located on Saemallo 16-gil in Guro-gu, Seoul, serving as a quiet local cafe space in the neighborhood. It provides a cozy and accessible indoor environment for visitors looking to grab a casual drink. The venue offers a comfortable spot to rest or meet locally away from the main commercial streets.

spots.name: Uijeongbu Budaejjigae street
spots.desc: Uijeongbu is a city famous for Budaejjigae, and there is Budaejjigae street and it is a popular attraction.

spots.name: Yeolsoe Observatory
spots.desc: Yeolsoe Observatory was established on April 11, 1998, by the Republic of Korea Army’s “Key Unit” to provide security education and to console displaced people who long for their hometowns in the North. From the observatory, visitors can view North Korea at a glance. The exhibition hall displays North Korean household items and military equipment, offering a glimpse into the reality of life in…

spots.name: Imjingang Ttepssari Garden
spots.desc: A seasonal garden near the Imjin River, known for its fields of kochia plants. The plants turn red and pink in autumn, creating a colorful landscape that is popular for walking and photography.

spots.name: Jeongok Nonghyup Hanaro Mart
spots.desc: Jeongok Nonghyup Hanaro Mart is a large supermarket specializing in fresh produce, groceries, and daily necessities in Yeoncheon. The mart features a local food section where visitors can find fresh agricultural products and processed foods directly from Yeoncheon’s farmers. The store’s spacious layout makes it convenient for travelers shopping for snacks, drinks, or supplies for camping or day…

spots.name: Eorak
spots.desc: Eorak is a restaurant specializing in grilled fish, offering a variety of Korean-style fish dishes cooked over a charcoal oven. Each plate is served with a selection of simple side dishes and freshly made rice. The atmosphere is casual and friendly, making it a suitable stop for anyone wanting to enjoy a straightforward, authentic grilled fish meal during their travels.

spots.name: Manghyang Bibimguksu
spots.desc: Manghyang Bibimguksu is a long-established noodle restaurant specializing in spicy bibim-guksu (mixed cold noodles) and simple noodle dishes. The bibim-guksu is served with thin wheat noodles, vegetables, and a sweet-and-spicy red pepper sauce, often accompanied by a light soup. The menu is straightforward, focusing mainly on noodles and a few side dishes, and orders are placed and paid for…

spots.name: Myungshin Banjeom
spots.desc: It is a long-established Chinese restaurant that has been in operation since 1972 and is now run by the second generation. The menu focuses on classic Korean-Chinese dishes such as jjajangmyeon, jjamppong, udon, and fried items. Many visitors mention the spicy gan-jjajang and tangsuyuk as notable options. The interior is simple, using both the first and second floors for seating, and mealtimes…

spots.name: C’est La Vie Hanok Cafe
spots.desc: C’est La Vie Hanok Cafe is a traditional Korean-style cafe. The café is set in a large hanok building and offers a calm atmosphere, with indoor seating and a broad courtyard. Visitors can enjoy coffee, teas, and simple house-made pastries while appreciating the classic architecture and quiet surroundings. The menu includes regional drinks such as barley sikhye and oat latte. The space provides a…

spots.name: Cafe Stone
spots.desc: It is a bakery cafe with a spacious, comfortable interior and distinctive design. The space is a remodeled brick factory that also includes a small exhibition area, offering visitors something to look around as well as a place to sit. Signature coffees and a variety of breads are available, with items such as “brick bread”, black brick pound cake, and salt bread mentioned frequently in reviews.…

spots.name: The Classic 10
spots.desc: It is an LP-themed cafe where visitors can drink coffee while listening to music played on a record player. The interior is furnished with simple tables and shelves of LP records, creating a quiet space for conversation or relaxed listening. The menu offers standard coffee drinks and a few non-coffee options, sometimes named after classical musicians. It is suitable for those who enjoy music and…

spots.name: Fishing
spots.desc: Chujado is highly regarded as a fishing destination by Koreans.

spots.name: Gapado Lookout
spots.desc: A lookout platform on the highest part of the island (still only about 20 metres above sea level). Easy to walk to with a nice view.

spots.name: Olle Trail Route 10-1
spots.desc: The island is part of the Jeju Olle trail, hosting route 10-1. This route has an S shape that cuts through the middle of the island as well as the coast. As it ends on the opposite side of the island, walkers will have to return to the ferry port. The walk could easily be done in an hour if walking fast, but it is best to enjoy the view.

spots.name: Seongmun Natural Arch
spots.desc: This scenic arch is located near the river. There is a large tourist parking and rest area nearby, with plenty of shops for food and drink.

spots.name: Danuri Aquarium
spots.desc: Eight scenic spots in Danyang-gun, including Jungseonam, Sainam, Oksunbong, and Dodamsambong, are reproduced as they are. You can see various freshwater fish at home and abroad in a large aquarium that is 8 m high

spots.name: Danyang Geumgul Cave Site
spots.desc: Cave ruins from the Stone Age and Bronze Age where Homo sapiens lived in Namhangang River, Dodam-ri, Danyang-eup, Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do. It was designated as a monument in Chungcheongbuk-do on Dec. 30, 1994.

spots.name: Suyanggae light tunnel
spots.desc: The Suyanggae Tunnel, constructed during the Japanese colonial period, is an underground structure located at San 24-2, Aegok-ri, Jeokseong-myeon. Measuring 200 meters in length and 5 meters in width, it had been abandoned for decades after its creation. Today, it has been reborn as a complex multimedia space that incorporates cutting-edge video, sound systems, and LED media facades.
spots.addr: 390, Suyanggae Yujeok-ro, Jeokseong-myeon, Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, Republic of Korea

spots.name: Bobaljae Viewpoint
spots.desc: It offers breathtaking panoramic views of Danyang’s mountains and valleys. It’s a perfect spot for photography and enjoying nature’s beauty.
spots.addr: San 14-2, Bobal-ri, Gagok-myeon, Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, Republic of Korea

spots.name: Darian Tourist Site
spots.desc: Darian Tourist Site is a good place to use as a hiking, recreation, and natural learning center for teenagers as various convenience facilities are established.

spots.name: Cheondong Tourist Site
spots.desc: It is a multi-purpose tourist complex with a garden, auto camping site, and cooking area around Cheondong Valley, where clear mooring and lush forest from Sobaeksan Valley exist.

spots.name: Danyang Paragliding
spots.desc: Paragliding is what this place does, and they do it well. If you look east from town, you can see an observatory on the hilltop. This shop will take you up there and do tandem jump, so it's perfect for people who want to try paragliding but have never done so before. Little English is spoken, but the people leading the jumps all know the important expressions for safely getting you off the ground…
spots.price: ₩100,000 for a basic jump; more for longer jumps

spots.name: Skywalk in the world
spots.desc: Zipwire is an extreme sport in which two fixed wire ropes of 980 m in length glide down as if they were non-powered. The skywalk offers panoramic views of the city and the Lotus Blossom Pedestal in Sobaeksan Mountain in the distance. The three-finger, 15-meter-long and 2-meter-wide high-intensity triple glass at the Manhakcheonbong Observatory in the form of a horseshoe-shaped observatory…

spots.name: Ondal Culture Festival
spots.desc: The Danyang-gun Ondal Culture Festival is a regional festival held in early October and is the only Goguryeo festival. In addition to traditional Goguryeo programs such as the operation of the Goguryeo theme zone and the Goguryeo costume experience, new programs such as the reproduction of Goguryeo Jeotgeori and Ondalsanseong Fortress were introduced to reinforce Goguryeo contents.

spots.name: POPS WORLD
spots.desc: Pops World Danyang is an experiential multi-complex with cutting-edge technology and diverse photo zones. Visitors can unleash creativity, tackle challenges, and gain new experiences while enjoying activities with family, friends, or partners.Four must-try spots include themed games and media photo zones, a new media space with video characters, colorful photo zones for perfect shots, and gallery…

spots.name: Sono Ocean Play Danyang
spots.desc: It is a water park located on a highland overlooking the Namhan River and Danyang city. Featuring both indoor and outdoor zones, it is a representative water park in the central inland region that can be enjoyed year-round.Designed as a spa-style water park using hot spring water, it focuses more on family-friendly activities and relaxation rather than extreme rides.

spots.name: Danyang Cruise
spots.desc: At Dodamsambong, a popular destination for family outings and dating, you can take a cruise boat that departs from the site and explore various scenic attractions across Korea.

spots.name: Danyanggang Jando Trail
spots.desc: On the Danyanggang Jando Trail, which is 1.12 km long, there is a Jando along the rock wall of the Namhangang River, so you can experience trekking. The Danyang River Jando offers a panoramic view of the Namhangang River.

spots.name: Danyang Shooting Theme Park
spots.desc: Previously, only clay shooting was possible, but now it has been transformed into a multi-shooting range where you can enjoy a total of five types of shooting sports by adding air pistols, air rifles, gunpowder pistols, and gunpowder rifles.
spots.hours: the summer season 09:00-18:00, the winter season 09:00-17:00

spots.name: Four Seasons Sledding Ground
spots.desc: The Danyang four season sledding ground can be used in spring, summer, autumn, winter, and all four seasons. During the peak summer season, it operates air bounces and pools.

spots.name: Cheondong Tourist Area Water Park
spots.desc: Cheondong Tourist Area Water Park, one of the facilities of Cheondong Tourist Site, opened in the summer of 2002 and operates separate adult and children pools, and there are also water swimming pools and high-slide pools.

spots.name: Danyang Nonghyup Hanaro Mart
spots.desc: It sells various items such as agricultural products, butchers, and marine products.

spots.name: Hanaro Mart Danyang Sobaek Agricultural Cooperative Headquarters
spots.desc: There are various items and various payment methods. Be able to park.
spots.addr: 48 Hanaro Mart Danyang Sobaek Agricultural Cooperative Headquarters, Ondalpyeonggang-ro, Yeongchun-myeon

spots.name: Danyang Gugyeong Market
spots.desc: This is Danyang's representative traditional market, offering delicious food and a variety of sights.

spots.name: Yeongyangilbeonga
spots.desc: The speciality here is yeongyangtang dog soup, but the chueotang minced fish soup with potatoes, mushrooms and rice cake is also quite tasty. No English menu.

spots.name: Jeonwon Hwagwan
spots.desc: Korean barbeque, offering the full range of beef and pork cuts and some pretty tasty cold noodles (naengmyon) to go with them. Some English and Russian spoken.

spots.name: Onnuri
spots.desc: This restaurant serves mostly vegetarian and spice fare. The set menus include a great variety of vegetable dishes, tons of garlic cooked in various ways, and a few meat dishes. Some staff members speak excellent English and can explain details of the food, though no English menu is available.

spots.name: Dodam Sambonga Cauldron Hand Tofu
spots.desc: It is a restaurant specializing in Korean food, and it mainly serves tofu dishes. There are many reviews that the view is good because it is a restaurant located within a tourist destination. Parking costs ₩3,000 per day.

spots.name: Ddanbbang Bakery
spots.desc: This is the representative famous eatery in Danyang Gugyeong Market, specializing in various garlic breads, including Cream Cheese Garlic Bread and Black Garlic Cream Cheese Bread. Please note that the market/store closes when ingredients are sold out.

spots.name: Danyang Black Garlic Nurungji Dakgangjeong
spots.desc: This is a popular eatery located inside Danyang Gugyeong Market, offering a unique Dakgangjeong (sweet and sour crispy chicken) that harmonizes the pungent flavor of black garlic with crunchy nurungji (scorched rice). The store may close early when ingredients are sold out.

spots.name: Black Garlic Salt Bread
spots.desc: You can purchase salt bread in various flavors, including black garlic, regular garlic, and streusel (soboro), individually or as a set. It is even more delicious when enjoyed with ice cream.

spots.name: Danyang Eogeupssogari Maeuntang Main Branch
spots.desc: Danyang Eogeupssogari is a popular restaurant favored even by locals. Their signature dishes include spicy and refreshing ssogari maeuntang (mandarin fish spicy stew) made with fresh ingredients, and the savory, light olgaengi haejangguk (freshwater snail hangover soup).

spots.name: Dawon
spots.desc: Dawon is a place where you can taste Garlic Tteokgalbi (marinated grilled short rib patties), Danyang's representative local food. It is conveniently located near Sono Belle Danyang.

spots.name: Namhangang Hoejip
spots.desc: Namhangang Hoejip is a raw fish restaurant beloved by Danyang locals. Fresh trout (songeo) and carp (hyangeo) raw fish and spicy fish stew (maeuntang) are the popular menu items. The interior of the restaurant is spacious and equipped with large tables, making it suitable for family gatherings or group meetings.

spots.name: Little Forest
spots.desc: It is a quiet cafe located in the mountains. People who are inexperienced in driving a car because they are in a remote area are advised not to bring a car.

spots.name: JB Coffee
spots.desc: They sell the signature menu, garlic-shaped bingsu, which is said to be famous.

spots.name: Cafe Dan & Dessert
spots.desc: Cafe Dan & Dessert is a spacious café located near Danyang Gugyeong Market. It features a multi-story layout and group seating, making it a comfortable place to relax and spend time.

spots.name: Goblin Café
spots.desc: This is a large café located atop the mountain in Gagok-myeon, Danyang, offering magnificent views near the paragliding launch site. The parking lot is spacious, making it convenient for visitors arriving by car, and pets are welcome.

spots.name: Moss Bakery
spots.desc: Moss Bakery is a café located in Danyang, characterized by its unique moss-themed interior and views of the Namhangang River.

spots.name: The bus terminal
spots.desc: The bus terminal is housed in a temple-style building at the bottom of the valley. Head up the hill from here to reach the temple itself.

spots.name: Four Heavenly Kings Gate
spots.desc: This gate marks the start of the temple proper. Climb up to the second story for a peek at the statues of the four heavenly kings inside.

spots.name: Storehouse Hall
spots.desc: Despite its impressive size, just a storehouse. Do check out the gift shop on the lower level.

spots.name: 5-Story Law Hall
spots.desc: Clamber up to the top floor to see the truly impressive gilded main altar of the Buddha Shakyamuni flanked by his attendants. No photos inside.

spots.name: Central courtyard
spots.desc: Cross under (or over) the bridges to reach the central courtyard, and check out the huge clay pots located on seemingly every available surface: these are the temple's storehouses of kimchi.

spots.name: Cafeteria Hall
spots.desc: This is where the contents of the pots are served up for breakfast, lunch and dinner, but for now, take the dark passageway just to the right and keep climbing those stairs. The next building, the most gigantic of the lot, is still under construction as of July 2009. Stairways lead past it both on the left and the right sides.

spots.name: Great Teacher Hall
spots.desc: A shrine erected in the memory of Sangwol Wongak, a large statue of whom can be found inside.

spots.name: Jeonju Sikdang
spots.desc: Does a good sanche bibimbap for ₩6,000 and sundubu tofu stew for ₩5000.

spots.name: Geunyeok Sacred Treasure Museum
spots.desc: Displays Buddhist cultural objects associated with Sudeoksa and its branch temples.
spots.hours: Tu-Su 10:00-16:00; closed 11:20-12:30 and Mondays; last admission 15:30

spots.name: Yedang Lake Sculpture Park
spots.desc: It is a harmonious place like Yedangho Lake, and you can enjoy various activities.

spots.name: Yedangho Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: This suspension bridge spans Yedang Lake, the largest reservoir in Korea.
spots.hours: It runs from March to November until 22:00 and other months until 20:00

spots.name: Naepo Bobusang Village
spots.desc: A cultural attraction about bobusang, Korea's itinerant merchants, with exhibitions and hands-on activities.
spots.hours: Tu-F 10:00-17:00, Sa Su and holidays 10:00-18:00; closed M; ticket sales end 1 hour before closing
spots.price: Adults ₩11,000; ages 13–18 ₩9,000; ages 3–12 and 65+ ₩7,000; some activities cost extra

spots.name: Bongsusan Natural Recreation Forest
spots.desc: It is a good natural recreational forest for a walk as it is located around Yedang Reservoir. There are various walking courses, so you can enjoy it in the style of hiking you want.

spots.name: Gayasan Mountain
spots.desc: It is a popular place to see the sunset, and it is a popular mountain among hikers. Especially, many people visit the peak.

spots.name: Deoksan Metasequoia Gil
spots.desc: It is a place that many people visit for a walk in autumn and winter. In particular, they choose the quiet Metasequoia Road because of the beautiful color of autumn leaves. This road has trees that extend straight into the sky on both sides, giving visitors comfort.

spots.name: Yun Bong-gil Memorial Hall
spots.desc: It is a place to take children and independence activist Yoon Bong-gil when studying, and it is a place where you can study and experience various history.

spots.name: Gwanghyeondang
spots.desc: It is a must-visit place to study Korean history because it is opposite the Yoon Bong-gil Memorial Hall and is a national heritage.

spots.name: House of Chusa
spots.desc: House of Chusa is a gate house, a detached house, anachae, and a shrine house, and there are various cultural relics that are closely related to Chusa Kim Jeong-hui, including the Tomb of Kim Jeong-hui.

spots.name: Yedang Lake Monorail
spots.desc: If you go on weekdays, you can ride a monorail without having to wait. And since you can accompany your dog, you can visit with your dog or cat.

spots.name: Yesan Stork Park
spots.desc: It is a special place where you can see the natural monument, the resident bird, and the stork. It is good to go on a family trip course
spots.hours: Mar-Oct: Tue-Sun until 18:00, Nov-Feb: Tue-Sun until 17:00

spots.name: Sapgyo Market Gopchang Street
spots.desc: This is a place where various tripe and rice soup shops are gathered.

spots.name: Yesan Market
spots.desc: There is a market-like old store, and various restaurants and bakery restaurants are gathered.

spots.name: Deoksan Hot Spring Sledding Site
spots.desc: It is a good place to visit when you want to go sledding with your children. It is a place to visit often because the price is low.

spots.name: Naepo Natural Playground
spots.desc: You can enjoy indoor play and performances using natural materials. It is operated by pre-reservation on the website.

spots.name: Eunseong Farm
spots.desc: It is a place where you can experience various things such as making apple pie, making apple wine, and harvesting apples.

spots.name: Muhancheon Sports Park
spots.desc: It has a large playground, so it is good for children to run and play, and it is good for sports activities.

spots.name: five-colored flower tea healing farm
spots.desc: It is a place where you can enjoy various hands-on activities such as making flower yams, collecting eco-bag flowers, making seasonal handmade jeans, and making flower vinegar.

spots.name: Friendly Brothers Park
spots.desc: It is a place created under the theme of the book, The Good Brothers. There are various hands-on activities and good courses for walking.

spots.name: Agroland Taeshin Farm
spots.desc: Agroland Taeshin Farm was certified as a "Dairy Experience Ranch" for the first time in Korea, and the ranch has been open since 2004 to experience it.
spots.hours: the summer season 09:00-18:00, the winter season 09:00-17:30

spots.name: Hongshi Office
spots.desc: There are cute interior accessories and clothes. If you go on the weekend, there are many people, so go on weekdays if possible.
spots.addr: Room 115, 1st floor, 217, Angels Tower, Government Complex-ro, Sapgyo-eup

spots.name: Soranseorim
spots.desc: There are various drinks and new books come in quickly, so it's a good place to read books. Also, it is a good place to buy various kinds of books

spots.name: Yesan Gopchang Street (예산 곱창거리)
spots.desc: A local street filled with restaurants specializing in grilled beef or pork intestines. Famous for crispy, well-seasoned gopchang and makchang dishes. Many shops have been open for decades.

spots.name: Deoksan Oncheon Sundae Gukbap (덕산온천 순대국밥)
spots.desc: This long-standing restaurant near the hot springs is known for its rich sundae soup and handmade blood sausage. It’s a favorite among locals after bathing in the onsen.

spots.name: Bakery Doldam (베이커리 돌담)
spots.desc: A popular bakery café using local butter and seasonal ingredients. Signature items include cream croissant and mugwort bread. Cozy atmosphere.

spots.name: Yedangho Coffee House (예당호커피하우스)
spots.desc: Overlooking Yedang Lake, this café offers coffee, tea, and desserts with a panoramic view.

spots.name: BIFF Square
spots.desc: As a symbolic location for the Busan International Film Festival, BIFF Square features handprints of famous film directors and actors. Once a district with a high concentration of theaters, it is now a representative street food destination in Busan with various food stalls. You can enjoy the festival atmosphere while trying out the street food.

spots.name: Chinatown
spots.desc: Home of Busan's Chinese community with cheap and delicious dumplings, though most of the Chinese have left the area, and it is today mainly home to Russians.

spots.name: Ibagu-gil and 168 Steps
spots.desc: This is an example of old, steep residential area of Busan that was formed after Korean War. Although you can walk the famous 168 steps, there is a free monorail that takes you uphill.

spots.name: Busan Citizen's Park
spots.desc: This was a US military base that was turned into a large park in 2014. The parks have large playground for kids and remnants of military base. The park museum has many artifacts about the history of the US military base and the lives around it.

spots.name: Busan Port Boat Tour
spots.desc: If you are interested in the industrial side of Busan then the Port tour is hard to beat. Passengers on board can see the port facilities of Busan Port, including the passenger terminal, general piers, and container terminals. You will learn about the port facilities, and their role as a transshipment hub. Specifically you will see: Coastal Passenger Terminal → International Passenger Terminal →…

spots.name: Samjung 'The Park' Zoo
spots.desc: In 2014 a new zoo opened in Busan, with a variety of animals (tigers, lions, bears, elephants, monkeys, etc.) It is very much targeted at children, and there is a very good activity center at the end, with climbing ropes and other activities.

spots.name: Ggangtong market
spots.desc: An old, easily overlooked market near Jagalchi Market in Nampo dong. There is nothing this market doesn’t sell. Since Busan has a big harbor, many foreigners have visited, so that it was quite early when citizens of Busan began to accept exotic culture and products. Ggangtong Market is a kind of evidence of that history. At the end of the Ggangtong market, there is a narrow street called Book…

spots.name: The markets of Gukje, Gwangbok-dong and Nampo-dong
spots.desc: Three major shopping districts connected to each other. Very much similar to Seoul's Namdaemun Market and Myeongdong shopping district. Various shops geared towards young and old people with many brand name stores and underground stores. You can bargain with the sellers. It also the setting for the Korean film Ode to My Father (2014).

spots.name: Lotte Department Store, Busan Main Branch
spots.desc: An over-the-top temple to consumerism (check out the fountains and statues at the basement entrance), this is Busan's second largest department store. It is the place to pick up some ₩500,000 ginseng or perhaps a Spam gift set for the folks back home. The basement has good food court, delicatessen and supermarket section.

spots.name: Lotte Department Store, Gwangbok Branch
spots.desc: This is a similar Lotte department store, and has an indoor vertical waterfall and rooftop observation deck which has a whole view of the harbor and bridges. With a sales area of 23,097 pyeong, it is the largest store in Busan and the third largest in terms of sales. In terms of overall size, it is a large store that enters the top 10 nationwide, and Lotte Department Store is connected to Lotte…

spots.name: Choryang Foreigner Shopping Area
spots.desc: A strange combination of a Chinatown and a Russian town with ornate Chinese gates and Russian shops selling pickles and vodka. The overall feeling is distinctly downmarket, and if you want to take the name literally there are ladies of many nationalities enticing sailors and other customers in the doorways. You may get more than you bargained for though, as the area is notorious for ripoffs and…

spots.name: Seomyeon Medical Street
spots.desc: Seomyeon Medical Street (서면메디컬스트리트) is an area with around 160 medical clinics providing all types of medical procedures, and is popular with foreigners who want to take advantage of low cost medical procedures. You can buy cosmetic surgery, dermatology, ophthalmology and dentistry procedures.

spots.name: Gimbap Cheongook
spots.desc: Serves up gimbap from ₩2000 and all sorts of noodles for ₩2500-4000. No English menu or sign, but if you can say it they'll make it, and it's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

spots.name: welly&food
spots.desc: This food court serves all the usual Korean favorites, with plastic food and English menus making ordering a snap.

spots.name: Amby's
spots.desc: European, North American, Russian, and SE Asian dishes; try the borscht stew. Popular with sailors and their lady companions, the best time to go is after midnight. A small shop offering a limited selection of dust-covered western goods is located in the front.

spots.name: Eva's
spots.desc: Turns into a bar, but they serve excellent Western food, and American-style breakfast until the afternoon. Open air bar. Thursday is ladies' bottomless drinks for ₩15000. In-Jung runs the bar and is a great hostess.

spots.name: Leegane Tteokbokki
spots.desc: Tteokbokki restaurant is inside the can market. Prices are reasonable at ₩5,000 for tteokbokki, ₩5,000 for fries, and ₩1,000 for a corn dog.

spots.name: Lee Jae Mo Pizza, Busan
spots.desc: This is the most famous pizza restaurant in Central Busan. On weekdays and weekends, a very large number of people line up to eat inside the restaurant. To solve this problem, a take-out only store has been opened across the street. Prices range from ₩20,000 to ₩40,000.

spots.name: Kkangdwaehu
spots.desc: This is a pork cutlet version of the Korean fried chicken called 'Pork Ribs Fried'. It is available in large, medium, and small sizes, with prices ranging from ₩13,000 to ₩23,000 depending on the size.

spots.name: Donghwa Chinese Restaurant
spots.desc: This Chinese restaurant in Busan, Jung-gu, is famous for its yuni-jjajang and sweet and sour pork. Noodles and fried rice are inexpensive at ₩6,000-8,000, but other dishes cost ₩20,000-30,000. Closed every Wednesday.

spots.name: Hongudan Nampo branch
spots.desc: It's a Chinese restaurant. Typically, there are regular course meals (₩37,000-85,000 ), lunch course meals (₩23,000-35,000), and couple course meals (₩39,000-49,000), with a 15:30 - 16:30 break.

spots.name: Dolswe Wood-fired grilling
spots.desc: A Korean barbecue restaurant with a single menu item: beef outside skirt It costs ₩13,000 per bowl and has sides such as Doenjangjjigae, rice, and Naengmyeon. Closed every Sunday and last order is at 21:00.

spots.name: Dongnae Eupseong History Plaza
spots.desc: An open historical plaza built around the remains of Dongnae Eupseong, allowing visitors to explore restored fortress walls, information panels, and surrounding heritage sites that explain Busan’s defensive history during the Joseon period.

spots.name: Bokcheon-dong Ancient Tombs
spots.desc: An archaeological site featuring ancient burial mounds from the Gaya and early Silla periods, offering visitors a rare opportunity to see excavated tomb structures within an urban residential area.

spots.name: Dongnae Hyanggyo
spots.desc: A Confucian academy from the Joseon Dynasty, historically used for education and ceremonial rites. Visitors can explore traditional architecture and gain insight into Korea’s classical education system in a quiet setting.

spots.name: Sajik Baseball Stadium
spots.desc: Busan’s main professional baseball stadium and home of the Lotte Giants, Sajik Baseball Stadium is known nationwide for its energetic atmosphere and passionate local fans. Even for visitors unfamiliar with Korean baseball, attending a game offers a memorable cultural experience featuring organized cheering, chants, and food culture unique to Korean sports venues. On non-game days, the stadium…

spots.name: Mandeok Gogae Pass
spots.desc: Famous for its stunning panoramic night views, this pass is a favorite spot for late-night drives and photography.

spots.name: Gupo Manse Street
spots.desc: A historical memorial street dedicated to the 1919 independence movement at Gupo Market, featuring murals and monuments.

spots.name: Hongbeopsa Temple
spots.desc: A quieter temple nestled in the foothills of Geumjeongsan, offering a peaceful cultural stop with traditional Buddhist architecture and surroundings emphasizing spiritual calm.

spots.name: Chungryeolsa Shrine
spots.desc: Take bus number 29, 29-1, 89 or 129 and walk for five minutes.

spots.name: Seokbulsa Temple
spots.desc: Another impressive temple is about 90 minutes' hike from the cable car station. It is often overlooked, but has magnificent statues carved into the mountain itself. Great views over Busan and very peaceful. From the South Gate (남문), the path indicated by the Mandeokchon (만덕촌) sign leads to a collection of restaurants and volleyball courts in Namman Village (남만 마을). At one point, the path stops at…

spots.name: Busan Al-Fatah Mosque
spots.desc: A distinctive Islamic place of worship and cultural site serving Busan’s Muslim community. Visitors can admire the Middle Eastern architectural style and explore cultural diversity in northern Busan.

spots.name: Busan Maritime Natural History Museum
spots.desc: South Korea's largest collection of sealife exhibits, with giant squid, whale sharks and oarfish.

spots.name: Busan Folk Art Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to traditional folk customs, crafts, and rituals of Busan and surrounding regions, helping visitors understand everyday life and seasonal traditions of Korea.

spots.name: Oryundae Korean Martyrs Museum
spots.desc: Roman Catholic museum dedicated to eight Christian martyrs who were killed for their faith in 1868.

spots.name: Geumjeong History Museum
spots.desc: A local history museum documenting the development of Geumjeong District, featuring archival materials, photographs, and exhibitions focused on urban and cultural change.

spots.name: Busan National University Museum
spots.desc: A university museum displaying archaeological artifacts, folk items, and regional history exhibits related to southeastern Korea.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Saengtae Museum
spots.desc: An educational facility introducing the Nakdong River ecosystem. Visitors can participate in interactive exhibits focused on environmental conservation.

spots.name: Sajik Baseball Stadium History Zone
spots.desc: A small exhibition area highlighting Busan’s baseball culture and the history of Sajik Stadium. It offers insight into one of the city’s most passionate local sports traditions.

spots.name: Geumjeong Local History Gallery
spots.desc: A small gallery preserving photographs and documents related to Geumjeong-gu’s urban development. Visitors can gain insight into how the district evolved alongside the university area.

spots.name: Nakdong River Estuary Eco Center
spots.desc: An ecological exhibition center introducing migratory birds and wetland ecosystems of the Nakdong River estuary, popular among visitors interested in nature conservation and environmental education.

spots.name: Geumgang Botanical Garden
spots.desc: A botanical garden featuring diverse flora native to Korea and abroad, located on the slopes of Geumjeongsan. Excellent for nature lovers and families exploring outdoor attractions.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Arboretum
spots.desc: A public arboretum featuring native Korean trees and plants, offering educational displays and seasonal scenery that attract visitors interested in nature and environmental learning.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Riverfront Picnic Zone
spots.desc: An open grass area along the Nakdong River suitable for casual picnics and relaxation. Visitors can observe local leisure culture in a spacious riverside environment.

spots.name: Dongnae Cultural Center
spots.desc: A public cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, and regional history programs, offering visitors insight into Dongnae’s traditional arts and contemporary cultural activities.

spots.name: Geumjeong Cultural Center
spots.desc: A public venue hosting performances, exhibitions, and cultural classes. Visitors can attend concerts or art events reflecting local culture.

spots.name: Geumjeong Mountain Forest Culture Center
spots.desc: An educational center introducing the natural environment and forest culture of Geumjeongsan. Exhibits and programs focus on conservation and local ecology, making it a useful stop for visitors before or after exploring nearby hiking trails.

spots.name: Dongnae Cultural Alley
spots.desc: A small cultural street connecting historic sites, galleries, and local workshops in Dongnae. Visitors can explore murals, exhibitions, and traditional architecture while gaining a sense of the district’s historical identity and everyday cultural life.

spots.name: Buk-gu Community Culture Classroom
spots.desc: A public classroom space hosting cultural and creative workshops. Travelers may participate in short programs or observe local community activities.

spots.name: Hurshimchung Spa
spots.desc: This massive hot spring complex claims to be the largest in Asia: Noboribetsu might disagree, but it certainly is huge, with hot, tepid, cold and strawberry milk-filled baths, saunas, pools, and an outdoor section. On the 3rd floor is a large jjimjilbang resting area, containing (among other things) a restaurant, a beauty salon, an oxygen room, and three 'igloos' heated to 81°C, 51°C and 0°C.…
spots.hours: The spa is closed in May for vacation and re-opens in June.
spots.price: Entry to the spa is ₩8000, plus ₩2,000 for the jjimjilbang

spots.name: Geumgang Park and Cable Car
spots.desc: Nice park at the foot of the mountains in North Busan. There are some small amusement rides for children as well. The highlight is the cable car that takes you to the top of the mountain near Namsam Gate. (Note that some signs call the cable car a 'rope way')

spots.name: Dongnae Oncheon Foot Bath
spots.desc: A public foot bath supplied with natural hot spring water from Dongnae Oncheon, allowing visitors to relax and experience the area’s traditional spa culture without entering a full bathhouse.

spots.name: Dongnae Traditional Archery Experience
spots.desc: A cultural experience allowing visitors to observe or participate in traditional Korean archery, offering insight into historic martial practices associated with Confucian values.

spots.name: Buk-gu Cultural Ice Rink
spots.desc: A public ice rink used for skating and events, often visited by families and tourists during winter months as part of Buk-gu’s recreational facilities.

spots.name: Bokcheon Museum Guided Tour Program
spots.desc: A guided tour program explaining archaeological findings from the Bokcheon-dong tombs, allowing visitors to gain deeper understanding of ancient burial customs and artifacts.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Ecological Education Center
spots.desc: An educational activity offering guided learning sessions about wetlands, migratory birds, and river ecosystems, designed for visitors interested in environmental conservation.

spots.name: Geumjeong Lifelong Learning Center
spots.desc: Short-term cultural and craft workshops open to the public, allowing visitors to participate in hands-on learning experiences related to Korean daily culture.

spots.name: Busan Science Education Center
spots.desc: Interactive science programs designed for visitors of all ages, featuring hands-on experiments and demonstrations that make science accessible and engaging.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Sports Complex
spots.desc: A multi-purpose sports facility near Hwamyeong Ecological Park offering open-access outdoor fields and courts for soccer, baseball, tennis, basketball, and other community sports. With scenic surroundings near the Nakdong River, the complex is often used by local teams and visitors for recreational play and events, providing a lively outdoor venue for physical activity and social interaction.

spots.name: Geumjeong Urban Farming Experience Site
spots.desc: A community-based urban farming site where visitors can learn about small-scale agriculture and sustainability practices. Occasionally hosting workshops and hands-on programs, it offers travelers a chance to observe local efforts toward eco-friendly living.

spots.name: Sajik Citizens Fitness Park
spots.desc: An outdoor fitness park equipped with exercise machines used by local residents. Visitors can casually join in physical activity while observing everyday recreational culture in Dongnae.

spots.name: Dongnae Traditional Music Practice Hall
spots.desc: A practice space for traditional Korean music groups. Visitors may observe rehearsals or attend small public sessions, offering exposure to regional performing arts.

spots.name: Geumjeong Fortress
spots.desc: A popular route is to take the subway to Oncheongjang, and then a short taxi ride to the cable car station. At the top of the mountain head towards the South Gate (Nammun) of Geumjeong Fortress and then through the North Gate (Bukmun) and down to Beomeosa Temple. This has a distance of 9 km (Taking between 3 and 4 hours).

spots.name: Geumjeongsan Main Ridge Trail
spots.desc: The main ridge trail of Geumjeongsan offers panoramic views over Busan and access to fortress remains. It is a popular by hikers and visitors seeking Busan’s mountain landscape frequently choose this route.

spots.name: Geumjeongsanseong Fortress Hiking Route
spots.desc: A historic hiking route following the walls of Geumjeongsanseong Fortress. Hikers can enjoy forest paths combined with cultural heritage, making it popular among history-oriented visitors.

spots.name: Dongnae Mountain Trail
spots.desc: A neighborhood mountain trail offering moderate hiking conditions and views over Dongnae district. Popular with locals for short but rewarding hikes.

spots.name: Geumgang Park Mountain Path
spots.desc: A forested mountain path inside Geumgang Park, suitable for light hiking combined with nature observation and city views.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Mountain Trail
spots.desc: A local hiking trail connecting low mountain ridges near Hwamyeong Ecological Park, often chosen by hikers seeking calm river-and-mountain scenery.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Ecological Park Riverside Trail
spots.desc: A long-distance hiking-friendly riverside trail allowing visitors to experience wetlands, bird habitats, and open landscapes along the Nakdong River.

spots.name: Hwamyeong Gichatgil
spots.desc: Hwamyeong Gichatgil is a 1.2-km-long forest trail created along the active Gyeongbu Line railway. What was once a neglected space next to the tracks has been transformed into a beautiful themed path filled with Metasequoia, pine, and various seasonal flowers.

spots.name: Daecheoncheon Eco-Trail
spots.desc: A peaceful ecological trail following the Daecheoncheon stream. It is a favorite local spot for birdwatching and enjoying the clear water flowing from Geumjeongsan Mountain.

spots.name: Geumgok-dong History Trail
spots.desc: A trekking path connecting ancient prehistoric dolmens and cultural heritage sites in the Geumgok area.

spots.name: Lotte Mart Dongnae
spots.desc: A large supermarket popular with visitors for purchasing Korean snacks, daily goods, and souvenirs. Conveniently located near Dongnae Station, making it accessible for travelers staying in northern Busan.

spots.name: Olive Young Dongnae
spots.desc: A health and beauty store offering popular Korean cosmetics, skincare products, and travel essentials, frequently visited by tourists seeking K-beauty items.

spots.name: NC Department Store Deokcheon
spots.desc: A mid-sized department store featuring fashion, cosmetics, and food courts, serving as a convenient shopping destination for visitors exploring the Buk-gu area.

spots.name: Seodong Maze Market
spots.desc: A traditional local market selling fresh produce, street food, and household goods, offering visitors a glimpse into everyday shopping culture in northern Busan.

spots.name: Daiso Hwamyeong
spots.desc: A large discount store selling household items, travel accessories, and daily necessities, often used by tourists staying near the Nakdong River area.

spots.name: Busan National University Bookstore
spots.desc: A campus bookstore selling books, stationery, and university-branded goods. Visitors often purchase souvenirs related to Busan National University.

spots.name: Dongnae Traditional Souvenir Shop
spots.desc: A small shop offering traditional crafts and regional souvenirs related to Dongnae history, often visited by tourists after museum visits.

spots.name: Oncheonjang Electronics Shops
spots.desc: Small electronics and accessory shops clustered near the hot spring district.

spots.name: Beomeosa Temple Souvenir Shop
spots.desc: A small shop selling temple-related souvenirs and traditional goods.

spots.name: Geumjeong Local Craft Shop
spots.desc: A small shop selling handmade goods produced by local artisans.

spots.name: Pusan National University
spots.desc: In the PNU area you can buy a lot of Korean student food specialties, such as Don Katsu and Croquette (Goroke - 고로케).

spots.name: Miryang Sundae Gukbap
spots.desc: A long-running local restaurant specializing in sundae gukbap. Popular among both residents and visitors for its rich broth and generous portions.

spots.name: Hapcheon Dwaeji Gukbap
spots.desc: A well-known local restaurant specializing in Busan-style pork soup, frequently recommended to visitors seeking an authentic and affordable regional dish.

spots.name: Subyeon Chueotang
spots.desc: A traditional Korean restaurant serving loach soup, popular among visitors interested in experiencing regional comfort food near the Nakdong River.

spots.name: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon
spots.desc: A famous restaurant serving Dongnae-style green onion pancakes, a regional specialty often introduced to tourists as a traditional local dish.

spots.name: Tonshou
spots.desc: A popular Japanese-style pork cutlet restaurant near Pusan National University. The menu includes loin, tenderloin, Berkshire K pork cutlets, and katsudon.

spots.name: Nakdong River Estuary Migratory Bird Sanctuary
spots.desc: The spot where the Nakdong River meets the South Sea has been declared a natural monument since 1966. Where the large mouth of the river forms, there are sand dunes and deltas and many small islands (including Ilung-do). It is now a bird sanctuary for migrating species that visit between October and March. There are over 150 different species (including many rare birds like white-naped cranes…

spots.name: Dadaepo Beach
spots.desc: This beach might be the least famous beach in Busan. It is right next to Nakdong river, so it has very soft sand and the water is very shallow. There are small park, fountains, locker room, and small benches for watching the sunset. Among the beaches of Busan, this beach is the only one that faces the west, making this place perfect for sunset. It also has a mudflat next to the beach, and you can…

spots.name: Janglim Harbor
spots.desc: Janglim Harbor (inlet) is surrounded by many colorful buildings and boats, a popular spot for strolling or taking pictures.

spots.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
spots.desc: A village with colorful houses built in a stair-step fashion on the foothills of a coastal mountain. It is known for its narrow alleys, art installations, and panoramic views.
spots.hours: Open all year, but most shops and galleries are open from 09:00 to 18:00
spots.price: Free to enter, but some experiences or workshops may have a fee

spots.name: Eulsukdo Ecological Park
spots.desc: A large park on an island at the mouth of the Nakdong River. It is a major migratory bird habitat and features walking trails, bike paths, and a bird-watching center.

spots.name: Molundae
spots.desc: A scenic rocky headland with walking trails and a dense forest. It's a great spot for a hike with views of the sea, Dadaepo Beach, and nearby islands.

spots.name: Dadaepo Sunset Fountain of Dreams
spots.desc: A spectacular musical fountain show with lights and water jets. It's a popular attraction, especially in the evening, as it's located right on Dadaepo Beach.
spots.hours: Show times vary by season. Check the official website for schedules.

spots.name: Amisan Observatory
spots.desc: An observatory offering a panoramic view of the Nakdong River Estuary, the sand dunes, and Dadaepo Beach. It's an excellent spot for photographers.

spots.name: Gukje Market
spots.desc: One of Busan's largest traditional markets, selling everything from clothes and household goods to street food. It's a bustling place with a rich history.

spots.name: Bosu-dong Book Street
spots.desc: A historic alley filled with secondhand bookstores, some of which have been around for generations. It’s a nostalgic and peaceful place for book lovers.

spots.name: Jagalchi Market
spots.desc: Korea's largest seafood market. You can see vendors selling fresh fish and seafood, and many restaurants on the upper floors will cook your selections on the spot.

spots.name: Yongdusan Park
spots.desc: A city park with the iconic Busan Tower at its center. It offers great views of the city and the harbor and features statues, flower beds, and a museum.

spots.name: Huinsnyeoul Culture Village
spots.desc: A village built along a cliff overlooking the sea. It's known for its scenic coastal path, art galleries, and cafes. It was also a filming location for a famous Korean movie.

spots.name: Swim at Dadaepo Beach
spots.desc: If it is not summer, walking along the coast and watching the mudflats and sunset is also fantastic. It is less crowded than other beaches in Busan, so you can quietly enjoy the ocean breeze. For information about the beach itself, please see the listing for Dadaepo Beach.

spots.name: Hapcheon Illyu Dwaeji Gukbap
spots.desc: A classic Dwaeji Gukbap, a pork soup mixed with rice restaurant.

spots.name: Haksun Milmyeon
spots.desc: Offers milmyeon (wheat noodles), a regional food item. Both cold noodles (mul milmyeon) and spicy mixed noodles (bibim milmyeon) are available.

spots.name: E-eun-ji Tteok-bokki
spots.desc: Sells tteok-bokki (spicy rice cakes) and eomuk (fish cakes). Provides a typical local street food experience.

spots.name: Songdo Haemul Bap
spots.desc: Serves seafood rice dishes and grilled fish options. The location provides views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car.

spots.name: Wonjo Halmae Nakji
spots.desc: Specializes in nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus) and nakgop-sae (octopus, tripe, and shrimp casserole). The dishes are noted for their high spice level.

spots.name: Sasang Pig's Feet Alley
spots.desc: A cluster of restaurants serving jokbal, a dish of marinated and boiled pig's feet. Various preparations, including cold sliced versions, are available.

spots.name: Gamcheon Culture Village Snack Corner
spots.desc: Several small vendors and cafes offering quick meals and snacks such as ramyeon (instant noodles), kimbap (seaweed rice rolls), and beverages for sightseers.

spots.name: Dadaepo Gwangyang Sashimi
spots.desc: Offers hoe (raw fish/sashimi) and seafood sets. The location provides a view of the ocean.

spots.name: Pyeonghwa Dwaeji Gukbap
spots.desc: Serves dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), a staple Busan dish. Noted for its rich, clear pork broth.

spots.name: Myeongji Jogae Changgo
spots.desc: An all-you-can-eat establishment focusing on grilled clams and shellfish (jogae gui).

spots.name: Dongdaeshin Kalguksu
spots.desc: Serves handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup). The broth is traditionally anchovy-based.

spots.name: Daejeo Byeolmi Nokdu
spots.desc: This establishment specializes in various Korean pancakes, notably the thick, savory nokdu jeon (mung bean pancake) and haemul pajeon (seafood green onion pancake). The dishes are made from freshly prepared ingredients.

spots.name: Sasang Milmyeon
spots.desc: A local eatery that serves milmyeon (wheat noodles), a food item associated with Busan. The restaurant offers both the chilled broth version (mul milmyeon) and the spicy mixed version (bibim milmyeon).

spots.name: Myeongji Jangeo Maeuntang
spots.desc: Specializes in jangeo maeuntang (spicy eel stew). The dish is served in a communal pot, combining fresh eel, vegetables, and spicy seasoning. It is a typical local favorite in the coastal region.

spots.name: Hyeopseong Tteokgalbi
spots.desc: Serves tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties), which are ground, seasoned, and grilled beef or pork. The meal typically includes rice and a set of traditional side dishes (banchan).

spots.name: Songdo Jogae House
spots.desc: A typical seafood restaurant in the area that offers jogae gui (grilled shellfish). Patrons select their seafood, which is then cooked at the table on a charcoal grill. Operating hours are generally geared toward the evening dining market.

spots.name: Molundae Seolleongtang
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in seolleongtang (ox bone soup), which is characterized by its white, milky broth from hours of slow cooking. The soup is usually served with rice and minimal seasoning, allowing diners to adjust the flavor themselves.

spots.name: Sasang Budae Jjigae
spots.desc: The main item served here is budae jjigae (army stew), a dish cooked at the table in a large pot. Ingredients typically include ham, sausage, baked beans, kimchi, and ramen noodles in a spicy broth.

spots.name: Joyeon-dong Haemul Kalguksu
spots.desc: A restaurant that focuses on haemul kalguksu (seafood knife-cut noodles). The noodles are typically hand-cut and served in a broth enriched by clams, mussels, and other seasonal seafood.

spots.name: Gangseo Hanwoo Center
spots.desc: Operates on a unique model where guests purchase fresh cuts of Hanwoo (premium Korean beef) directly from the butcher shop section and then cook the meat themselves at tables equipped with grills.

spots.name: Ami-dong Sundae Gukbap
spots.desc: Serves sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup with rice). The soup contains Korean-style blood sausage (sundae) and various pork offal in a dense, rich broth. It is open at all hours.

spots.name: Gupo Kalguksu
spots.desc: Specializes in kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), a dish traditionally associated with the Gupo area. The noodles are typically served in a clean, anchovy-based broth. This location is one of the long-standing original stores in the district.

spots.name: Sasang Chicken Foot Alley
spots.desc: This alley features multiple eateries specializing in dakbal (spicy chicken feet), a popular local late-night dish. Visitors can choose between boneless or bone-in versions, usually accompanied by alcoholic beverages.

spots.name: Songdo Haemul Tang
spots.desc: Serves haemul tang (spicy seafood stew). The stew is prepared with a variety of fresh seasonal seafood, crabs, and shellfish in a spicy broth, designed to be shared by several people.

spots.name: Gamcheon Donkey Steak
spots.desc: A small, themed eatery within the cultural village serving grilled meat skewers and simple rice dishes. It is primarily geared toward tourists looking for a quick and casual meal while sightseeing.

spots.name: Dadaepo Sundubu Jjigae
spots.desc: Specializes in sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew). The stew is served boiling hot and can be customized with seafood or meat, accompanied by traditional side dishes. Popular as a simple breakfast or lunch option.

spots.name: Jangeo Cheopbap (Eel Rice)
spots.desc: The primary dish is jangeo cheopbap (grilled eel on rice), often prepared in a Japanese style with a sweet glaze. It is considered a specialty meal in the area.

spots.name: Sasang Ttukbaegi Jjigae
spots.desc: Offers several varieties of traditional Korean stews (jjigae) served in individual earthenware pots (ttukbaegi). Options usually include kimchi jjigae, doenjang jjigae, and sundubu jjigae.

spots.name: Dongdaesin Bindaetteok
spots.desc: Specializes in bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), which are traditionally pan-fried until crispy. This dish is often paired with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) and is primarily open during evening hours.

spots.name: Myeongji Kalbi Jjim
spots.desc: Focuses on galbi jjim (braised short ribs), a traditional slow-cooked beef or pork dish. The meat is braised in a soy sauce-based marinade with vegetables and served in a hot pot.

spots.name: Songdo Fish BBQ
spots.desc: A typical seaside restaurant offering various grilled whole fish (saengseon gui), such as mackerel and hairtail. The dishes are usually served as a set with rice and several small side dishes (banchan).

spots.name: Gamcheon Culture Cafe Rooftop
spots.desc: A non-alcoholic cafe that offers coffee, tea, and juice. The main draw is the high vantage point providing panoramic views of the colorful Gamcheon village houses.

spots.name: Gudeok Traditional Tea House
spots.desc: Serves traditional Korean teas such as sanga-cha (twin citrus tea) and sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch). This spot provides a quiet setting away from the commercial areas, suitable for daytime relaxation.

spots.name: Somaemuldo Island Lighthouse
spots.desc: A famous setting in Korea, this lighthouse was built during the Japanese occupation on the smaller island of Deungdaesum.

spots.name: Miracle of Moses Waterway
spots.desc: Somaemuldo Island and Deungdaesum Islands are connected by a submerged gravel road. Twice a day the tides lower to allow people to walk across.

spots.name: Seyeonjeong (세연정)
spots.desc: Seyeonjeong was a space for leisure and pleasure. The name Seyeonjeong means "a place so clean and refreshing that the surrounding scenery looks as if washed by water," and according to the Gosan Yeonbo (Chronological Biography of Gosan), the garden was built when Gosan first arrived on Bogildo and discovered Buyongdong in 1637.
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000, youth and military personnel ₩2,500, children ₩2,000

spots.name: Yesong-ri Beach (예송리 해수욕장)
spots.desc: Dangsa, Yejak, Dalksseom, Giseom, and Chuja are islands that can easily be seen from Yesong-ri Beach. Visited by around 300,000 people annually, Yesong-ri Beach is a year-round resort destination, with its dark, rounded pebbles (cheonghwanseok) stretching along a shoreline about 50 meters wide and 2 kilometers long.

spots.name: Dongcheonseoksil (동천석실)
spots.desc: Dongcheonseoksil is a small pavilion site on the mountainside directly facing Naksseojae, offering a panoramic view of Buyongdong; in the philosophy of Neo-Confucianism, it was regarded as a realm where immortals dwell. It takes about five minutes by car from the ticket office of the Yun Seon-do Garden to the entrance of Dongcheonseoksil, followed by roughly a 20-minute hike up the mountain to…
spots.price: Adults ₩3,000, youth and military personnel ₩2,500, children ₩2,000

spots.name: Gosan Yun Seon-do Literature Experience Park (고산 윤선도 문학체험공원)
spots.desc: 40 display panels, each featuring a single poem from Eobusasisa (The Fisherman's Four Seasons) in both the original text and translation—have been installed along a walking path. The site includes a campfire area capable of accommodating around 50 people, a pond, and a pavilion, while a bamboo-lined path offers visitors the chance to enjoy a refreshing bamboo forest bath.

spots.name: Bo-ok-ri Dinosaur Egg Beach (보옥리 공룡알해변)
spots.desc: The name comes from the fact that the pebbles are large and rounded, resembling dinosaur eggs. Locally, it is also called the Pporaegi mudflat. Although it is not a beach, it is a great summer retreat where you can relax quietly while listening to the sound of dinosaur eggs by the camellia forest or on the shore, or even hike Bojuk Mountain.

spots.name: Manggeut Observatory (망끝전망대)
spots.desc: Manggeut Observatory is located on the outcrop at the tip of Mangwolbong, just before Bo-ok-ri, the westernmost point of Bogildo. Mangkkeut is the place where you can witness the most beautiful sunset in Korea, with its red-hued sea blending into the vast, refreshing West Sea. Along with Chuja Island, you can see the many islands of the Dadohae, such as Okmae, Gado, and Sangdo, as well as Jeju…

spots.name: Rock inscribed with Uam Song Si-yeol (송시열 글쓴바위)
spots.desc: During the reign of King Seonjo, the great Confucian scholar Song Si-yeol of the Sukjong era was stripped of his official rank over the issue of appointing a crown prince and exiled to Jeju; while resting here in this scenic location, he engraved his feelings of regret and longing for the king into poetry and carved it into a rock. Locally, it is called the 'Writer’s Rock' of Song Si-yeol. He…

spots.name: Nakseojae (낙서재)
spots.desc: Nakseojae is a historic site located beneath Byeongpung Rock in Buhang-ri. The word “Nakseojae” symbolizes the life of a scholar who enjoys reading while pursuing learning. Unlike Seyeonjeong, this is where the scholar Yun Seon-do lived, studied, and taught his disciples.

spots.name: Jeam Mountain
spots.desc: Known for its royal azalea blossoms in May. It offers well-maintained trails and panoramic views of the South Sea from the summit.

spots.name: Eokbul mountain
spots.desc: Located right behind the Cypress Forest Woodland. It features a "Mallegil" (boardwalk path) that is gentle enough for casual walkers and offers a great view of Jangheung.

spots.name: Jeongnam Jinmul Science Museum
spots.desc: It is a water-themed science museum. The building consists of four floors in total. There are an aquarium and a touch pool on the first floor, an aquarium on the second floor, a 4D video theater, and a hydrothermal promotion hall on the second floor, a subclass room on the third floor, and a dessert cafe on the fourth floor where you can relax. Inside, visitors can first meet various fish and…

spots.name: Jung Namjin Cypress Forest Woodland
spots.desc: One of its attractions is the Jeongnamjin Cypress Forest Woodland, created with cypress trees planted in the 40th year of reforestation projects. The woodland is located at the foot of Eokbulsan Mountain, overlooking Jangheung-eup. Facilities include a wood culture experience center, a pension complex, ecological architecture such as traditional hanok, the Jeonnam Woodcraft Center, a healing…

spots.name: Jeongnamjin Observatory
spots.desc: When you climb the stairs of the observatory, the Korean Peninsula-shaped floor fountain at Unification Square greets you with a cool stream of water. After passing the fountain at Unification Square, you will see the statue of Ahn Jung-geun facing the sea. In front of the observatory, a cute 12-gan sculpture welcomes visitors. The observatory tower is 45.9 meters high, with the upper layer…

spots.name: Chung Nam-jin, Mayor of Saturday
spots.desc: Every Saturday, a Saturday market is held at the marketplace in Jangheung-eup and various performance events are held.Performances with a traditional atmosphere continue, so you can enjoy fun, eat deliciously, and enjoy a substantial market trip to buy good things.The Saturday market is not just a market that was selected as one of the top 100 Korean tourism destinations in 2017-2018, but a…

spots.name: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival
spots.desc: The Jeongnamjin Jangheung Water Festival is held every summer in Jangheung. The festival makes use of local water resources such as the Tamjin River, Jangheung Dam, and Deukryang Bay.It is a regional festival where visitors can join various water-related programs and activities. The event was selected as a designated cultural tourism festival by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism in 2025.

spots.name: Sky Light Arboretum Tulip Festival
spots.desc: Hamjibong Peak in Jangheung, Jeongnamjin has a garden of about 100 m². The site contains around 300 types of trees and about 1,000 kinds of plants, including wildflowers and herbaceous flowers. A Sky Light Arboretum Tulip Festival is held every April. During the festival, tulips are planted along the cypress forest trail and other areas.The garden includes facilities for wedding conventions.…

spots.name: Yi Sun-shin Festival in Hoeryongpo, Jangheung
spots.desc: It is a historical experience festival held at Hoeryongpo, a historical place where Admiral Yi Sun-shin prepared for the miracle of the Battle of Myeongnyang by repairing 12 ships. The highlight of the festival is a maritime parade involving 12 Panok ships and a reenactment of the ceremony of the appointment of naval commanders. Visitors can participate in various hands-on activities such as…

spots.name: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Shell Festival
spots.desc: A local food festival using pen shells is held in Jangheung. Visitors can try dishes made with pen shells from the local clean waters.The festival program usually includes cultural performances such as guest singer stages, pungmul (traditional percussion) shows, sports dancing, and a singing contest for participants. A section for selling local products is also operated during the event. The…

spots.name: Jeamsan Mountain Azalea Festival
spots.desc: Held in May every year, the Jeamsan Royal Azalea Festival is a representative festival held in Jeamsan Mountain. It is held from May 1 to 15 every year, and various events and programs are held in time for the azaleas to be in full bloom. The Jeamsan Royal Azalea Festival is a popular festival among domestic and foreign tourists, and many people come to see the beautiful azaleas.

spots.name: Tamjin galbi
spots.desc: A spacious, family-oriented restaurant specializing in charcoal-grilled pork ribs (galbi). It is well-regarded for its clean interior and convenient facilities, including a large parking lot and a children's playroom. A notable feature is the use of table warmers to keep the meat hot throughout the meal. The restaurant offers a wide variety of side dishes and is known for its friendly service.

spots.name: Moon Soo-heon Jangheung Headquarters
spots.desc: Munsuheon Jangheung Main Store is a Korean restaurant that serves Jangheung Samhap Hot Pot and a variety of tteokgalbi menus. Juicy menus such as grilled Korean beef galbi patties, grilled pork galbi patties, and assorted tteokgalbi and deep-flavored samhap hot pot are popular. It is suitable for family gatherings and group visits due to its neat table setting and reasonable price, and it is…

spots.name: Yeongcheon Fisheries Corporation
spots.desc: Yeongcheon Fisheries is a freshwater eel restaurant where you can put pre-manipulated eels on the scale and taste them after payment. It features a large parking lot and a clean interior, and is convenient with self-baked eel, generous side dishes, and self-rice and soup.

spots.name: One and six
spots.desc: One and six cafe that sells cherry bingsu and various drinks and desserts.

spots.name: Ochai County
spots.desc: Ochai County is an atmospheric cafe located in Jangheung, offering a variety of drinks and desserts. Its popular menu, 'Finang Si' is popular with visitors, and its coffee menu, such as Creamy Flat, is also soft and delicious. The interior of the store is decorated with a different atmosphere from the exterior, and there is a large parking lot, making it convenient to visit by car.

spots.name: FOURROOM
spots.desc: It is a cafe in Jangheung where you can taste handmade cakes. It does not contain any preservatives, so you can feel the original taste. It is a cafe where handmade desserts and drinks are delicious.
